papers.title: Navigating grief in academia: ways to find balance
papers.abstract: Pamela Yeh found it hard to manage grief and the demands of her work. Here are some steps that helped her to ease the burden.

papers.title: Orangutans face bleak future after Indonesia’s devastating wildfires
papers.abstract: The super El Niño intensified Indonesian fires, which ravaged the habitat of the critically endangered Bornean orangutan.

papers.title: Learning beyond rigid manipulation with hybrid soft-rigid robots
papers.abstract: Rigid-soft robot hybrids promise to unite the precision and repeatability of rigid manipulators with the compliance and adaptability of soft structures. Yet, full-fledged rigid-soft manipulators remain largely unexplored, in part because the intelligence required to exploit this combination is still missing. Here, we introduce a hybrid robotic system obtained by the series interconnection of a rigid arm and a soft manipulator, and systematically examine its ability to perform both established and previously inaccessible manipulation tasks. We show that a tailored imitation learning algorithm–generally applicable to this class of hybrid systems–leverages the complementary roles of rigid precision and soft embodiment to acquire manipulation skills and generalize them in a single shot across task variations. As a result, the system matches or exceeds the performance of rigid robots in classical tasks such as stacking, while enabling qualitatively new behaviors, including grasping objects through narrow openings. Rigid robots are precise but struggle to adapt, while soft robots are flexible but less reliable. Here, the authors show that a hybrid soft-rigid robot can learn varied manipulation tasks from one demonstration, combining precision with adaptability.

papers.title: Impact-stiffening materials modulated by host–guest interactions in polypseudorotaxanes
papers.abstract: The development of high-performance impact-stiffening materials is critical for applications spanning personal protection to military defense. Conventional designs of such materials relying on strong noncovalent interactions often face a strength–toughness trade‑off. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a strategy that utilizes the dynamic threading–dethreading kinetics of host–guest complexes in polypseudorotaxanes to fabricate impact‑stiffening materials. Unlike binding‑strength‑governed designs, this approach is governed by kinetic mismatch between the dethreading time of the macrocycle and the external deformation time. This kinetic control decouples the static compliance from the dynamic stiffening threshold, enabling pronounced impact‑stiffening even with a modest solution‑phase binding constant. Under low shear rates, the macrocycles gradually slide from the polymer backbone, preserving flexibility. Upon high-speed impact, the dethreading of host–guest complexes cannot occur within the ultrashort loading window of deformation, kinetically freezing the network and increasing the storage modulus by 48‑fold (0.1–100 Hz, 25 °C). The material also exhibits self-healing, reprocessability, and strong adhesion. This work demonstrates rate-dependent host–guest disassembly as a design principle for adaptive impact-protective materials. “Designing impact-stiffening materials is critical for personal protective equipment, though it is challenging to optimize the strength-toughness trade-off using conventional methods. Here the authors design an impact stiffening material using host-guest polypseudorotaxanes.”

papers.title: Choline kinase α promotes glycolysis and tumor growth by phosphorylating and activating enolase 1
papers.abstract: Tumor cells exhibit aberrantly upregulated glycolysis, in which glycolytic enzyme enolase 1 (ENO1) plays a critical role. However, how ENO1 activity is dynamically regulated in tumor cells remains elusive. Here, we demonstrate that hypoxic stimulation promotes the binding of p38 MAP kinase to choline kinase α (CHKα). p38 phosphorylates CHKα at S114, subsequently leading to CHKα to interact with ENO1. Importantly, CHKα functions as a protein kinase and phosphorylates ENO1 Y44 thereby enhancing the metabolic activity of ENO1 to increase glycolysis. Knock-in expression of CHKα S114A or ENO1 Y44F inhibits brain tumor cell glycolysis and proliferation, blunts brain tumor growth in mice with inhibited lactate production, and prolongs mouse survival. In addition, CHKα S114 and ENO1 Y44 phosphorylation levels are positively correlated with each other and associated with poor prognosis in glioblastoma patients. These findings highlight the critical regulation of glycolysis by the noncanonical function of CHKα and underscore the potential to target the moonlighting function of CHKα for cancer treatment. Tumor cells rely on increased glycolysis for growth. Here, authors show that choline kinase α activates enolase 1 through phosphorylation, promoting glycolysis and tumor progression in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Disagreements in global urban growth projections amplify uncertainties in deforestation and carbon emissions
papers.abstract: Global urbanization is profoundly reshaping 21st-century land systems, yet its future trajectory remains highly uncertain. Existing projections exhibit divergent urban growth patterns even under identical socioeconomic scenarios. Here, by synthesizing six urban growth projections, we reveal substantial disagreements in the extent and location of urban growth by 2100. These disagreements are amplified by land-system feedbacks, driving cross-dataset variation in urban-induced deforestation (1.75–4.91 million km2) through direct forest conversion and indirect cropland displacement, assuming lost production is compensated by cropland expansion elsewhere. The associated emissions exhibit an absolute range of 29 to 76 GtCO2 by 2100. Across 100 countries, this range accounts for an average of 3% of unconditional Nationally Determined Contribution emission budgets, reaching 26% in specific countries. Our findings establish cross-dataset disagreement as an important source of uncertainty in land and climate assessments, highlighting the need for robust spatial planning across plausible urban futures. The study shows that disagreements among global urban growth projections can substantially affect future deforestation and carbon emissions estimates, revealing a key source of uncertainty in land and climate assessments.

papers.title: A bacteriocin from the commensal Streptococcus mitis prevents influenza infection-driven pneumococcal lung dissemination
papers.abstract: Streptococcus pneumoniae remains a major public health threat despite widespread use of vaccines and antibiotics. Its synergy with influenza A virus (IAV) often leads to secondary bacterial pneumonia, causing significant morbidity and mortality mainly in vulnerable populations such as children under 5 years old and adults over 65 years old. As pneumococcal pneumonia is preceded by nasopharyngeal colonization, preventing colonization represents a promising intervention strategy. While current interventions are somewhat effective, their impact is limited by serotype replacement and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show that colonization with the commensal S. mitis strain F22Ad significantly reduces pneumococcal density in the nasopharynx by day 10 post-infection and prevents dissemination to the lungs following IAV infection. This protective effect depends on bacteriocins encoded at the blp1 locus. Among these, Bac2v1 alone or in combination with Bac1 significantly reduces pneumococcal colonization. Notably, Bac2v1 exerts broad, serotype-independent inhibitory activity, impairing the growth of diverse epidemiologically relevant pneumococcal strains. These findings establish two precision-based, serotype-independent approaches to target pneumococcal colonization: using S. mitis F22Ad as a live biotherapeutic or administering a bacteriocin mixture produced by this strain. Both approaches have the potential to prevent pneumococcal disease and complement existing strategies. Here, the authors show that a specific strain of commensal Streptococcus mitis bacteria, and its bacteriocins, reduce S. pneumoniae asymptomatic colonization and lung dissemination after influenza infection.

papers.title: Dynamic B–OH intermediates enable photocatalytic conversion of CO<sub>2</sub> into formic acid
papers.abstract: Remediating of flue gas pollutants and the mitigation of carbon emissions represent two interconnected yet often conflicting challenges in environmental management. Here we report a borane-assisted photocatalytic system that achieves synergistic co-conversion of CO2, NOx, and SO2 from flue gas into valuable liquid products-formic, nitric, and sulfuric acids-with near-complete selectivity and high stability. Central to this process is the in situ generation of dynamic B-OH intermediates at the borane-catalyst interface, which serve as proton relays to activate water-derived protons for CO2 reduction while promoting reactive oxygen species for pollutant oxidation. This mechanism enables approximately 77.02% of the hydrogen in formic acid to originate from water. The system demonstrates broad applicability across diverse photocatalysts and borane reagents, and exhibits sustained performance under simulated flue gas conditions. Our work establishes a sustainable and economically viable pathway for integrated carbon and pollutant valorization, offering a scalable strategy toward circular carbon economies. Dynamic B–OH intermediates act as proton relays to harness water-derived protons for highly selective photocatalytic CO2 conversion to formic acid, enabling synergistic carbon mitigation and pollutant removal from flue.

papers.title: A quasi-particle theory for the dynamics of polycatenated architected materials
papers.abstract: Polycatenated architected materials (PAMs), composed of interlinked rigid units, exhibit complex frequency-dependent shear-thinning and shear-thickening behaviors that are not easily explained by traditional granular or continuum mechanics. Here, the authors develop a one-dimensional quasi-particle analytical model that captures the dynamic response of PAMs, successfully predicting their critical transition frequency and nonlinear rheological behaviors.

papers.title: Targeting chemotherapy-induced CD200 via a nucleoside-enhanced nanocarrier for cancer immunochemotherapy
papers.abstract: The efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade therapy is limited by the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here this group identifies the chemotherapy-induced CD200 upregulation as a resistance mechanism then develops a nanotechnology-based framework for spatially selective CD200 silencing, thereby reprogramming TME and enhancing antitumor efficacy.

papers.title: A long-read based haplotype panel enhances imputation and discovery of functional small and structural variants
papers.abstract: Here, the authors integrate long-read sequencing and statistical phasing to create the Han-SV panel, a comprehensive haplotype reference resource comprising 32.6 million SNVs, 3.2 million indels, and 172,569 structural variants from 943 Han Chinese individuals.

papers.title: Sustained changes to urban mobility after COVID-19 reinforced socioeconomic inequalities in Argentina, Chile and Colombia
papers.abstract: COVID-19 reinforced inequalities in Latin America. Two years later, everyday mobility remained below pre-pandemic levels in the high-income and densest areas of Argentina, Chile and Colombia, as they adapted to home working, unlike the most deprived.

papers.title: Development and clinical validation of a multimodal AI framework to predict persistent fever during antibiotic therapy in hospitalized patients with cancer
papers.abstract: Pucher et al. show that multimodal AI can predict whether fever will persist in hospitalized cancer patients 48 hours after starting antibiotics, potentially supporting risk stratification and targeted clinical decisions at this reassessment point.

papers.title: Author Correction: Learning reorganizes dendritic and stabilizes axon initial segment inhibitory synapses in CA1 pyramidal neurons
Retraction Note: NMDAR-mediated modulation of gap junction circuit regulates olfactory learning in C. elegans
Tunable diffusive memristor arrays for neuromorphic temporal computing
papers.abstract: The dynamic behaviour of diffusive memristors enables bio-realistic emulation of artificial neurons and synapses, yet scaling from individual devices to neuromorphic systems remains challenging. Stochasticity in ionic motion and filament evolution limits both the uniformity and tunability of these devices, hindering reliable system-level implementation. Here we present a framework for tailoring the relaxation dynamics of diffusive memristors via intrinsic and extrinsic tuning. Percolation in a thin platinum interfacial layer and grain boundaries in a polycrystalline hafnium oxide matrix spatially confine active metal-ion migration; this guided transport substantially improves device uniformity. Purpose-designed programming protocols enable tuning of relaxation time over two orders of magnitude. A prototype hardware system integrating a 28 × 14 array of tailored diffusive memristors and a memristive system-on-chip implements the hierarchy-of-time-surfaces algorithm, achieving 91.14% recognition accuracy on a downsampled neuromorphic-MNIST dataset. These results demonstrate a scalable approach towards robust and energy-efficient neuromorphic hardware for next-generation artificial intelligence. Scaling diffusive memristors from single devices to integrated systems has been hindered by stochastic ionic motion and filament evolution. Here confined metal-ion migration enables controlled relaxation dynamics, as demonstrated in a 28 × 14 array for neuromorphic computing.

papers.title: Accelerating inverse materials design using generative diffusion models with reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: Diffusion models promise to accelerate materials design by directly generating novel structures with desired properties, but existing approaches such as conditional generation typically require expensive and substantial labelled data (>10,000) and lack adaptability. Here we present MatInvent, a general and efficient reinforcement learning workflow that optimizes diffusion models for goal-directed crystal generation. By formulating equivariant denoising as a multistep decision-making problem, MatInvent leverages policy gradient with reward-weighted Kullback–Leibler regularization, including experience replay and diversity filters to enhance optimization efficiency and sample diversity. For single-objective designs, MatInvent rapidly converges to target values within 60 iterations (~1,000 property evaluations) across electronic, magnetic, mechanical, thermal and physicochemical properties. Furthermore, MatInvent achieves robust optimization in design tasks with multiple conflicting properties, successfully proposing low-supply-chain-risk magnets and high-κ dielectrics. Compared with state-of-the-art methods, MatInvent exhibits comparable or superior generation performance under specified property constraints while markedly reducing the demand for property computation. Compatible with diverse diffusion model architectures and property constraints, MatInvent could offer broad applicability in materials discovery. Chen et al. present MatInvent, a reinforcement learning workflow that fine-tunes diffusion models to design crystals meeting single or multiple property targets, with far fewer property calculations than previous methods.

papers.title: A measurement noise scaling law for cellular representation learning
papers.abstract: Large genomic and imaging datasets can be used to train models that learn meaningful representations of cellular systems. Across domains, model performance improves predictably with dataset size and compute budget, providing a basis for allocating data and computation. Scientific data, however, are also limited by noise arising from factors such as molecular undersampling, sequencing errors and image resolution. Here we introduce mutual information with auxiliary signals as a metric of representation model performance and study its scaling with noise. By fitting more than 2,000 representation learning models across three data modalities (gene expression, sequence and image data), we show that noise defines a distinct axis along which performance improves. Noise scaling follows a logarithmic law. We derive the law from a model of noise propagation, and use it to define noise sensitivity and model capacity as benchmarking metrics. We show that protein-sequence representations tolerate error rates in modern sequencing data, whereas single-cell transcriptomic models remain noise limited at current measurement signal-to-noise ratio levels. Within transcriptomic cell-state representation learning models, we find that transformer-based models are more noise robust but less performant than variational autoencoders. Noise scaling metrics may support future model evaluation and experimental design. Gowri et al. identify a simple mathematical relationship between the performance of a machine learning model and noise in its training data. The relationship might help to guide machine learning efforts in biology and other fields where data are noisy.

papers.title: Mitigating preferred orientation in cryo-EM with ultrasonic excitation during vitrification
papers.abstract: Preferred particle orientation remains a frequently encountered problem in cryo-electron microscopy that arises when proteins adsorb to the air–water interface in only a limited number of orientations. This issue can considerably increase the data acquisition time required to reach a desired resolution or even make it impossible to obtain a reconstruction altogether. Here we show that preferred orientation can be mitigated by continuously exciting the sample with ultrasonic waves during vitrification. Our experiments suggest that mechanical oscillations induced in the sample support continuously shake proteins loose from the air–water interface, thereby scrambling their orientations. The simple, physical nature of this mechanism should make it applicable to a wide range of proteins and implementable using existing vitrification devices. Exciting cryo-electron microscopy specimens with ultrasonic waves during vitrification helps mitigate the preferred particle orientation problem that plagues protein structure determination.

papers.title: Large-scale quantitative assessment of tissue preparation and staining conditions for robust multiplexed imaging of FFPE tissue samples
papers.abstract: Multiplexed protein imaging or spatial proteomics enables the simultaneous measurement of over 50 proteins in intact tissues at single-cell resolution, providing insights into tissue organization and cellular interactions. However, variation in tissue preparation and staining protocols remains a major source of technical variability, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies and platforms. Here we present a large-scale, multisite and multi-platform benchmarking study of tissue preparation conditions for formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues. We systematically evaluated 24 combinations of antigen retrieval and antibody staining conditions using a 27-marker immune panel and ranked performance using quantitative metrics that capture signal intensity, variability and marker failure. Tris–EDTA-based antigen retrieval combined with overnight antibody staining at 4 °C consistently achieved the highest performance, whereas several commonly used alternatives showed reduced robustness. Validation across additional academic and industry laboratories and multiple imaging technologies confirmed the generalizability of these findings across tissues and platforms. We further show that marker signal intensity correlated with greater spatial heterogeneity, improving the detection of diverse cell populations. Together, our results provide practical guidelines and a standardized benchmarking strategy to improve reproducibility, harmonize workflows and facilitate cross-study comparisons in spatial proteomics. This Registered Report quantitatively evaluates the impact of tissue preparation and staining conditions on imaging.

papers.title: Low thermal conductivity and high thermal durability in high-entropy zirconate coatings with dense screw dislocations
papers.abstract: High-performance thermal barrier coatings (TBCs) that simultaneously offer ultralow thermal conductivity and prolonged service life at extreme temperatures are urgently demanded for next-generation aircraft engines and gas turbines. Herein, we fabricate a double-ceramic-layer TBC systems consisting of a high-entropy (LaGdSmYbEr)2Zr2O7 top coat and an yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) intermediate layer, using electron beam-physical vapor deposition (EB-PVD). The high-entropy top coat retains a single-phase cubic pyrochlore structure and exhibits a coefficient of thermal expansion of 11.07×10−6·K−1 at 1500 °C, which significantly reduces the thermal expansion mismatch with the underlying metallic components. Owing to the ultra-dense screw dislocations (⁓1017·m−2), compositional complexity, and the characteristic columnar/feathery microstructure, the coating achieves a low thermal conductivity of 1.16 W·m−1·K−1 at 1000 °C, approximately 50% lower than that of conventional YSZ. Benefiting from the synergistic effects of the double-layer architecture and the enhanced strain tolerance, the (LaGdSmYbEr)2Zr2O7/YSZ TBCs demonstrates outstanding thermal durability, with thermal shock lifetimes of 14,333 cycles at 1100 °C and 5,666 cycles at 1300 °C–the latter being 14.4 times that of monolithic YSZ coatings. This work demonstrates that high-entropy engineering, combined with tailored microstructural design, provides a practical pathway to overcome the long-standing trade-off between thermal insulation and thermo-mechanical reliability in TBCs.

papers.title: Clip density and rebleeding after indirect clipping for colonic diverticular bleeding: an exploratory single-center cohort study
papers.abstract: Clip use and rebleeding after indirect clipping for colonic diverticular bleeding remain uncertain. We retrospectively studied 80 patients treated during 2014–2022 with follow-up through June 2023. Clips per treated diverticulum (CPD) was index-procedure clip count (IPC) divided by treated-diverticulum count; total cumulative clip count (TCC) included index and repeat-procedure clips through day 30. Continuous Cox analyses were primary; spline and post hoc categorical analyses were exploratory. Thirty first rebleeding events occurred, 15 within 30 days and 15 thereafter. Continuous CPD (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.80–1.42), IPC (HR, 1.11; 95% CI 0.92–1.34), and landmark TCC (HR, 1.06; 95% CI 0.96–1.17) were not linearly associated with their rebleeding outcomes. The continuous CPD model violated the proportional-hazards assumption. Three-knot restricted cubic splines suggested CPD nonlinearity (overall P = 0.014; nonlinearity P = 0.004), whereas fractional-polynomial testing did not support an overall association. Only eight patients had CPD < 2. Single-diverticulum sensitivity analysis was null (HR, 1.11; 95% CI 0.80–1.54; P = 0.536). The low-CPD signal arose mainly from late events, but the interaction was inconclusive and the sources of all four late CPD < 2 events were undetermined, providing limited support for failure at the clipped site. These findings are exploratory and do not establish a treatment threshold.

papers.title: A part affordance dataset for semantic segmentation based on diffusion model
papers.abstract: Fine-grained robotic manipulation requires part-level perception and affordance understanding, yet constructing large-scale part-level datasets remains challenging due to costly and ambiguous annotations. To address this issue, we propose a training-free diffusion-based framework for automatic part-level affordance dataset construction. The framework progressively refines diffusion attention through a Part-Guided Semantic Field, a Local Subject Constraint Field, and a Bootstrap Self-Relational Enhancement Field, followed by SAM-based refinement to generate semantic segmentation masks. Evaluation on a manually annotated subset demonstrates strong agreement with human annotations, achieving 86.34% mIoU, 75.61% bIoU, 91.47% Dice, 91.46% precision, and 93.72% recall. Ablation experiments demonstrate the overall effectiveness of progressive attention refinement and SAM-based mask generation. An image-to-image extension further explores zero-shot part segmentation on real images, achieving 28.44% mIoU and revealing challenges in cross-domain generalization. These results demonstrate the feasibility of diffusion-based part-level pseudo-annotation and its potential to reduce manual annotation requirements.

papers.title: Traditional Shaolin training hones millisecond motor control at material failure thresholds during needle piercing glass
papers.abstract: Across cultures, certain trained individuals perform feats that appear to exceed ordinary physical limits, yet how culturally sustained training enables such performance within physical constraints remains poorly understood. Using the Shaolin practice of needle piercing glass as a case study, this study investigates how highly specialized motor coordination interacts with material failure constraints during successful and unsuccessful attempts. By integrating fracture-mechanical analysis, three-dimensional motion capture synchronized with high-speed imaging, and practitioner-based training accounts, we characterized whole-body coordination, needle dynamics, and outcome-critical control parameters in an expert practitioner. Release speed was necessary but insufficient for successful penetration; penetration angle emerged as the critical determinant and was regulated within a narrow ~ 20 ms temporal window. These findings indicate that extreme performance can emerge not from exceptional strength or mystical forces, but from precisely regulated motor coordination shaped by long-term cultural training and constrained by material properties. Cultural concepts such as qi may function as training frameworks that scaffold refined motor solutions while obscuring their mechanistic basis. More broadly, this study illustrates how prolonged practice can drive ordinary neuromuscular systems toward highly specialized motor solutions at the limits imposed by physical constraints.

papers.title: Self-decontamination of simulated skin contamination using commonly available absorbent materials: implications for mass-casualty chemical incidents
papers.abstract: Mass casualty incidents resulting from accidental or intentional release of chemical substances require rapid responses from medical personnel to minimize the harmful effects of these substances on the human body. The main public health problem after a chemical incident is the protection of health and life. Self-decontamination plays a significant role in limiting the effects of chemical exposure. A practical solution could be the use of widely available absorbent materials. The aim of study was to preliminarily assess the suitability of commonly available absorbent materials for the removal of simulated liquid and solid contamination from the skin surface, identify practical self-decontamination methods, and develop simple instructions for self-decontamination that can be understood by people without previous training.

papers.title: JudgeLib as a lightweight online judge system for competitive programming education
papers.abstract: The increasing popularity of competitive programming (CP) as a means of computer science education has established a strong demand for robust and accessible online judging systems that facilitate skill-building as well as unbiased evaluation. This work presents an educationally centered solution to the design and implementation of such a system, illustrated by the development of JudgeLib. JudgeLib is a light, distributed, and highly versatile platform specifically designed with teaching environments in mind. Its design includes a Redis-backed job queue for horizontally scalable task execution, specialized worker services for running code in several languages (C++, Java, and Python) in managed sandbox environments, and a complete REST API with a complementing administration interface for monitoring and governance. Built with simplicity of deployment and streamlined resource consumption in mind, JudgeLib is especially suited to institutions that have limited technical infrastructures. Core functionalities are stable compilation and execution pipelines, auto-checked output, and process isolation through Node.js spawn() with custom protection. In addition to enabling precise and efficient code assessment, JudgeLib also serves as an efficient feedback mechanism, enhancing the learning experience in programming classes. The system is released as a reusable NPM package (lib-judge) and has been successfully deployed in a functional live coding platform, the details of which are formally documented and cited within the manuscript. This deployment demonstrates both its real-world applicability and its pedagogical benefits in educational environments.

papers.title: Active TSRI-based adaptive resilience control for INS-aided GNSS receivers under gradual spoofing
papers.abstract: Static INS-aided GNSS receivers are vulnerable to gradual spoofing because fixed coupling gains cannot adapt to evolving spoofing offsets. We transform the Topological Spoofing Resilience Index (TSRI) into a real-time feedback signal. A high-gain observer estimates the spoofing offset, and a precomputed three-dimensional lookup table provides TSRI and its gradient. A projected adaptive law adjusts INS gains and PLL bandwidth to keep TSRI above a safety threshold. Lyapunov analysis proves uniform ultimate boundedness (UUB). Monte Carlo simulations (50 runs) show the proposed controller improves the margin-loss time (first crossing of the safety threshold) by 82–135% (mean ≈ 115%) compared to static aiding in the reduced-order model, with the highest improvement in the low C/N0 scenario, while the success rate (lock retention) is 92–100%. It outperforms M-estimation and threshold-switching baselines in all tested scenarios, with near-deterministic response and low variance. The active TSRI framework significantly enhances resilience against gradual spoofing with modest computational load, suggesting potential applicability in safety-critical navigation components.

papers.title: Ultrasound-assisted extraction of lecithin-rich lipid fraction from fresh, boiled, and lyophilized hen egg yolk: process optimization and characterization
papers.abstract: Lecithin is a valuable natural emulsifier widely used in food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic formulations. However, extraction of lecithin-rich lipid fractions (LRLFs) from egg yolk remains challenging, and the influence of egg-yolk physical state on extraction performance has not been thoroughly investigated. Therefore, this study evaluated the extraction of LRLF from fresh, boiled, and lyophilized hen egg yolks using a one-step ethanol extraction process assisted by ultrasonication. Results indicated that maximum extraction yield (14.69%), LRLF content (1.469 g), surface free energy (68.2 mj/m2) and minimum contact angle (21.6 °) were obtained using lyophilized egg yolk. Optimization of the yolk powder to solvent ratio (10 to 40%) and ultrasonication time (10 to 50 min) on the responses indicated that, maximum extraction yield and surface energy, and minimum contact angle with values of 24.9% and 70.5 mJ/m2, and 12.2 ° were attained by powder to solvent ratio of 14% and ultrasonication time of 11 min. Further analyses including, TLC, FT-IR and HPLC were accomplished and results indicated that its LRLF content was 2.49 g with phospholipid and lecithin contents of 1.33 g and 1.29 g, respectively, which that indicated lecithin was the main component of the extracted lipid. The results demonstrate that lyophilization significantly enhances the recovery and functional properties of LRLF and provide insights for the development of more efficient extraction strategies for egg-yolk-derived phospholipid-rich ingredients.

papers.title: Platelet inflammasome-related changes and hypercoagulability are associated with retinal vein occlusion
papers.abstract: Retinal vein occlusion (RVO) is a thrombotic retinal vascular disorder classified into branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) and central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO). Here we examined platelet and coagulation changes associated with RVO in clinical samples. Thromboelastography showed a hypercoagulable profile in RVO patients, with a shorter reaction time and kinetics time and a higher α-angle in both BRVO and CRVO, and a higher maximum amplitude in CRVO. Platelets from RVO patients showed increased cytosolic ROS, increased NLRP3-ASC co-localization, and increased caspase-1 activity, which we interpret as inflammasome-related changes. Flow cytometry showed significantly increased platelet-neutrophil and platelet-monocyte aggregates in both RVO groups, with platelet-neutrophil aggregates higher in CRVO than in BRVO. Collectively, these findings show that oxidative stress, inflammasome-related changes in platelets and a hypercoagulable state are associated with RVO. As this cross-sectional study was performed after the occlusion had occurred, no causal relationship can be inferred, but the findings suggest that platelet-related pathways merit further investigation.

papers.title: An efficient deep learning architecture for classification of SARS-CoV-2 variants using spike protein sequences
papers.abstract: The rapid emergence of COVID-19 major variants like Alpha, Delta, Omicron has highlighted the critical requirement for robust computational approaches to classify viral sequences accurately and efficiently. Several machine learning techniques exist for alignment-free genomic sequence classification. However, these methods do not consider the contextual information present in sequences or relies on complex network architectures comprising of stacked layers. Consequently, an efficient deep learning method with proper hyperparameter tuning, can capture the contextual relationships present in sequence without parameter inflation, offering a possible alternative. In this work, Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), a sequential deep learning architecture, is proposed for categorizing the SARS-CoV-2 most prevailing variants using spike protein sequences. To capture the local contextual repetitions in sequences, raw amino acid sequences are converted into k-mers, which are then transformed into numerical representations using word2vec. Feature extraction is performed using a TCN model integrated with a location-weighted average pooling layer. The proposed model achieved 99.10% and 99.51% classification accuracy on testing and, entirely new samples respectively. Its training performance and runtime were benchmarked using two encoding schemes – integer and kmer, against convolutional network and, bi-directional long-short term memory model . Furthermore, an amino acid structural analysis is conducted to highlight highly mutational positions. To enhance model interpretability, its predictive capability is validated by mapping pooling layer outputs back to key amino acid positions. The results demonstrate that the Temporal Convolutional Network generalizes better across both training and new samples, making it a superior model for identifying SARS-CoV-2 variants.

papers.title: LDPF2-Net: dual-branch change detection network with local dynamic pooling and pixel-level feature flow learning
papers.abstract: Remote sensing image change detection plays a crucial role in dynamic surface monitoring. Existing change detection methods often overlook the key feature information in bi-temporal images as well as subtle variations between features, making it difficult for models to distinguish changes relevant to the target task from irrelevant changes. To address this issue, this paper designs a local dynamic pooling module (LDPM) and a pixel-level feature flow learning module (PF2M) based on an encoder-decoder architecture to learn key feature extraction from original images and detailed difference features, respectively. On this basis, a dual-branch change detection network based on local dynamic pooling and pixel-level feature flow learning, termed LDPF2-Net, is proposed. The network introduces the local dynamic pooling module (LDPM) into each branch of the dual-branch architecture to effectively capture key feature information from the original bi-temporal images. In addition, a pixel-level feature flow learning module (PF2M) is designed to learn detailed difference features between multi-level feature maps of the dual-branch network. Experimental results on three standard change detection datasets, namely LEVIR, SYSU, and WHU, demonstrate that LDPF2-Net significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods in terms of detection accuracy, achieving an F1-score/IoU/OA of 91.06%/83.54%/99.17% on LEVIR-CD, 82.57%/70.21%/92.52% on SYSU-CD, and 86.34%/77.37%/98.96% on WHU-CD with only 3.61M parameters and 5.84G FLOPs.

papers.title: An explainable machine-learning surrogate frameworûûk for multiparameter predictions of wideband substrate-integrated waveguide antenna
papers.abstract: The cost of repeated full-wave electromagnetic simulation dominates millimetre-wave antenna design. For rapid design and optimisation, this work reports a defected ground structure (DGS) loaded half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) antenna for the 24–44 GHz band. The antenna is developed in four verified stages: a multi-slot, stub-loaded patch bisected along the SIW virtual magnetic wall and etched with a periodic rectangular DGS in the ground plane; it yields a 20 GHz impedance bandwidth about a 31.5 GHz resonance, with 5.6 dBi gain and 54% radiation efficiency. A Latin hypercube sampled set of 1,202 valid samples from 1500 High frequency Structure Simulator (HFSS), spans sixteen geometric and via parameters. Nine standalone regressors and output-specific stacked ensembles are compared on a held-out test set: stacking is best for gain (coefficient of determination R² = 0.915, and a standalone Extra Trees model is best for bandwidth (R² = 0.961, with a mean absolute error, MAE, of 0.469 GHz). SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis recovers physically consistent bounded design rules, identifying slot length, cavity length and electrical aperture size as the important governing parameters. These findings indicate that hand-engineered physics features in this design space serve interpretability rather than raw accuracy.

papers.title: Acute warm-up effects on agility and lower-limb range of motion in elite female taekwondo athletes
papers.abstract: Evidence comparing the acute effects of foam rolling (FR), dynamic stretching (DS), and resistance-band exercises (TB) on taekwondo-specific performance is limited. In this randomized parallel-group study, 36 elite female taekwondo athletes (12 per group) completed one of three warm-up protocols. Agility and lower-limb range of motion (ROM) were assessed before and after intervention. A sensitivity analysis using conventional ANCOVA did not identify a significant between-group difference in agility (F(2, 32) = 2.780, p = 0.077). Quade’s rank-based ANCOVA indicated a nominal between-group difference in agility (F(2, 33) = 4.379, p = 0.021, η2 = 0.210), with a Bonferroni-adjusted comparison favoring FR over DS (p = 0.025). However, the agility finding was sensitive to the analytical method, and the overall result did not remain significant after Holm adjustment across six outcomes (adjusted p = 0.103). Knee flexion ROM differed between groups (F(2, 32) = 18.353, p < 0.001, partial η2 = 0.534); baseline-adjusted post-intervention means were 145.91° (FR), 150.74° (DS), and 152.77° (TB). No significant between-group differences were found for ankle or hip ROM. The findings suggest outcome-specific responses, but the absence of a general-warm-up-only control group precludes attributing within-group improvements solely to the interventions.

papers.title: Evaluating gradient-boosting machine learning methods for Q-matrix validation in cognitive diagnostic models
papers.abstract: This study evaluated two gradient-boosting algorithms, Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) and Categorical Boosting (CatBoost), for data-driven Q-matrix validation, framing it as a multiclass classification in which each item’s fit statistics (PVAF or McFadden pseudo-R²) predict its q-vector. Both were compared with random forest and the Hull and MLR-B methods across simulation conditions varying sample size, number of attributes, test length, item quality, and Q-matrix misspecification rate, and were applied to the PISA 2000 Reading assessment. No single method dominated. The method effect on Q-matrix recovery was small and the largest pairwise difference was 0.031. CatBoost-R had the highest mean q-matrix recovery but did not differ significantly from Hull or RF-R; MLR-B was weakest. Recovery declined as misspecification increased, and q-vector recovery remained low at K = 7 (maximum VRR = 0.400). XGBoost was more stable as K increased and yielded the lowest AIC in the empirical analysis, whereas RF-P yielded the lowest BIC. SHAP analyses showed that XGBoost relied more directly on class-matched fit-index features, and most boosting errors differed from the true q-vector by one entry. Gradient boosting is a viable complement to established validation procedures but should not replace expert review.

papers.title: Spatial governance and the evolution of green innovation networks across China’s five major urban agglomerations
papers.abstract: Green innovation increasingly depends on how innovation resources flow among cities, yet most network studies examine a single urban agglomeration and treat the conditions behind inter-city linkages as static. This study traces green innovation networks across China’s five major urban agglomerations from 2010 to 2021, combining entropy-weighted TOPSIS, a modified gravity model, social network analysis and QAP regression. The agglomerations differ persistently in connectivity and in the functional positions of their cities. The Yangtze River Delta and Pearl River Delta are polycentric, Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei remains organized around Beijing, and the Chengdu–Chongqing and Middle Reaches of the Yangtze River regions move from fragmented toward more cohesive and less hierarchical networks, largely after 2018. QAP regression reveals a consistent contrast: geographical adjacency and larger inter-city differences in human capital and income are positively associated with linkage formation, whereas differences in environmental regulation and industrial structure are negatively associated with it; the associations of urbanization and government regulation differences strengthen after 2017. These patterns are consistent with complementarity-driven exchange on one side and coordination costs on the other, although these processes are not tested directly. The findings reframe spatial governance as a relational, network-embedded process and support regionally adaptive, network-aware strategies for sustaining green innovation.

papers.title: A Bayesian neural network digital twin prototype trained on finite element and monitoring data for earthfill dam monitoring
papers.abstract: Interpreting dam monitoring records together with numerical models is difficult for earthfill dams, where seepage, deformation and seismic loading interact. This study develops a digital twin prototype for the Houzian Dam, western Iran, based on a Bayesian neural network (BNN) trained on finite element (FE) simulations and field monitoring records. The database combines 4,862 monitoring records (2013–2025) from five piezometers and three settlement gauges, cyclic triaxial test results and FE-generated responses. The calibrated FE model reached R2 of at least 0.95 and relative errors of at most 6.8% at the three representative piezometers. On a randomly partitioned test set, the BNN gave an RMSE of 0.087 and an R2 of 0.984 on normalised variables after sequential updating; before updating, the RMSE was 0.137, higher than that of a Transformer baseline (0.128). The updating status of the baselines is not reported. Sequential assimilation reduced the average predictive variance from 0.021 to 0.008 and the RMSE by 36.5%. Physical knowledge enters only through FE-generated data and laboratory-derived properties, not through governing-equation residuals. Seismic results are exploratory, and interval calibration and ablation analyses were not performed.

papers.title: Two year strength development and fracture response of high performance concrete with asymmetric hybrid fiber reinforcement
papers.abstract: This study investigates asymmetric hybrid-fiber architectures in high-performance concrete under a controlled constant-volume framework. Four hybrid systems combining hooked-end steel, polypropylene, basalt, and glass fibers were investigated at a fixed total fiber volume fraction of 3% and a fixed 2:1 hybrid ratio, together with corresponding single-fiber reference systems obtained within the same experimental program. The program included workability, 28-day and 730-day compressive strength and nominal peak splitting stress, 28-day displacement-controlled flexural response with independent CMOD measurement and post-cracking response including fracture energy, and non-destructive measurements at 730 days. Basalt-rich hybrids showed the greatest loss of workability, whereas steel–polypropylene and steel–glass systems remained flowable. The glass–steel hybrid developed the highest mean fracture energy among the hybrid systems, while the basalt–steel system showed the largest positive deviation from the adopted linear-additive reference. Representative hybrid load–CMOD curves were additionally approximated using continuous piecewise-linear and three-term multi-exponential functions. Complexity-adjusted comparison using adjusted R2, AIC, and BIC favored the multi-exponential formulation for all four representative curves. The specific contribution of the study is the controlled assessment of asymmetric 2:1 fiber allocation at constant total reinforcement volume, including its influence on processability, two-year strength development, and 28-day post-cracking response.

papers.title: PanoramicSplat: scaling 3D gaussian splatting for single-view large-scale outdoor reconstruction
papers.abstract: Although recent research on single-view 3D reconstruction has made substantial progress, accurately reconstructing complex, large-scale outdoor environments remains challenging. We present PanoramicSplat, a 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) framework for monocular large-scale scene reconstruction. The framework combines panoramic supervision, which distributes target-view supervision across four directional sectors to reduce directional sampling bias and improve reconstruction across wide viewpoint changes; semantic-aware depth regularization, which emphasizes foreground structures when matching relative depth and alleviates structural ambiguity in complex scenes; and a radially weighted photometric loss with Gaussian gating, which concentrates optimization on visually informative image regions while suppressing low-contribution primitives to preserve rendering detail. We also construct a dataset of large-scale outdoor scenes using Google Earth Studio, covering diverse urban landscapes and occluded structures. On the reported rendered-scene benchmark, PanoramicSplat achieves 19.28 PSNR, 0.4182 SSIM, and 0.4536 LPIPS, outperforming the evaluated retrained baselines.

papers.title: Assessment of central horizontal strain criterion in the Brazilian test for estimation of the tensile strength of brittle materials
papers.abstract: Accurate determination of tensile strength is critical for geo-engineering projects, given the prominent role of tensile cracks in brittle failure. The Brazilian Tensile Strength (BTS) test is the most common indirect method owing to its simplicity in specimen preparation and experimental procedure compared to the Direct Tensile Strength (DTS) test. However, significant discrepancies between BTS and DTS are often reported. This study evaluates a Strain-Based Tensile Strength (SBTS) method that identifies the true tensile strength at the onset of non-linearity in the central horizontal strain. A bonded particle model (BPM) calibrated for a typical brittle material was validated using analytical solutions, accurately reproducing the complex stress state in the Brazilian disc. Numerical simulations were performed for six jaw curvature ratios ($$\:\rho\:$$ = 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.57, 0.67, and 0.8) and material brittleness indices ranging from approximately 5 to 40. Unlike the conventional BTS, which overestimated strength by 10–25% and is highly sensitive to jaw curvature, the SBTS method agrees with DTS to within 5% across all loading configurations. This consistency arises because SBTS is independent of jaw curvature and material modulus. The method is robust for brittle rocks (brittleness index > 10), especially when using the ISRM-suggested curved jaws, where underestimation is below 5%. For less brittle materials, shear cracking causes greater underestimation. The study thus validates SBTS directly against DTS on identical material under controlled micromechanical conditions, removing the material mismatch inherent in experimental comparisons. Beyond this, the study isolates parameters that cannot be varied independently in physical testing, shows that the criterion corresponds to the crack damage stress, and defines the brittleness validation threshold. The results demonstrate that SBTS overcomes the key limitations of the conventional Brazilian test, offering a more accurate and reliable tensile strength estimation for brittle materials.

papers.title: Ultrasound radiomics-based prediction of central lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid carcinoma coexistent with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis
papers.abstract: To evaluate the clinical value of a machine learning model integrating ultrasound radiomics and clinical features for the preoperative prediction of central lymph node metastasis (CLNM) in patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) coexistent with Hashimoto’s thyroiditis (HT). This retrospective study included 324 patients with pathologically confirmed PTC in the context of HT at the Affiliated People’s Hospital of Jiangsu University between October 2010 and December 2025. Patients were randomly assigned to a training set (n = 226) and an internal validation set (n = 98) at a 7:3 ratio. Independent predictors of CLNM were screened using univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses. Ultrasound Radiomics features were extracted and selected. Three classifiers—logistic regression (LR), support vector machine (SVM), and random forest (RF)—were constructed and compared. Based on performance, the LR model was selected to compute the Radiomics score (Rad-score). A combined model was then developed by integrating the Rad-score with independent clinical predictors and was visualized via a nomogram. The predictive performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Age and maximum nodule diameter were identified as independent predictors of CLNM (P < 0.05). In the internal validation set, the combined model achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.817, which was significantly higher than that of the clinical model (AUC = 0.708; DeLong P = 0.017) and numerically higher than that of the radiomics model (AUC = 0.793; DeLong P = 0.324). Calibration curves and DCA showed that the combined model possessed good calibration consistency and clinical net benefit. A machine learning model combining ultrasound radiomics and clinical features showed potential for preoperative risk stratification of CLNM in patients with PTC coexistent with HT, pending external validation.

papers.title: Effects of quercetin on ovarian insulin signaling, mitochondrial dynamics, and oxidative stress in type 2 diabetic rats
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disorder characterized by hyperglycemia that disrupts metabolic and hormonal homeostasis and adversely affects multiple organs, including the female reproductive system. The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of quercetin, administered alone or in combination with gliclazide, on metabolic disturbances and reproductive alterations in a rat model of T2DM. Rats were randomly allocated into five groups: Control (C), Diabetes mellitus (DM), Gliclazide (G), Quercetin (Q), and Gliclazide + Quercetin (G + Q). T2DM was induced by intraperitoneal injection of nicotinamide (60 mg/kg) followed by streptozotocin (STZ; 70 mg/kg). The DM group exhibited elevated glycemic and lipid parameters accompanied by reduced insulin levels. Both treatments improved metabolic profiles, with the combined G + Q group showing the most pronounced improvement. The diabetes-associated decline in Anti-Müllerian hormone (AMH) levels was significantly reversed in the Q group. Furthermore, treatment attenuated the diabetes-induced irregularities in the estrous cycle. Ovarian oxidative stress was markedly elevated in the DM group, whereas treatment, particularly quercetin alone or in combination with gliclazide, improved antioxidant defense. Pronounced histopathological alterations in pancreatic, ovarian, and uterine tissues observed in diabetic rats were markedly ameliorated by treatment. In addition, diabetes-induced alterations in ovarian insulin signaling pathways, including insulin receptor substrate-1 (IRS-1), protein kinase B (AKT), forkhead box O3 (FOXO3), and mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) were regulated by treatment, particularly in the G and G + Q groups. Diabetes-induced dysregulation of ovarian mitochondrial function–related markers [Dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1), Mitofusin 2 (MFN2) and PTEN-induced putative kinase 1 (PINK1)] was alleviated by treatment in the Q and G + Q groups. These findings indicate that quercetin and gliclazide, administered alone or in combination, may mitigate T2DM-associated metabolic and hormonal dysregulation, oxidative stress, and histopathological alterations in the pancreas, ovary, and uterus, in association with modulation of ovarian insulin signaling.

papers.title: Climate-driven spatial reorganization of avocado ( Persea americana ) suitability in India: an integrated AHP–MCE GIS assessment
papers.abstract: Climate change is expected to substantially alter the geographical suitability of perennial horticultural crops, particularly those with narrow eco-physiological requirements such as avocado (Persea americana). This study employed an integrated Geographic Information System (GIS)-based Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and Multi-Criteria Evaluation (MCE) framework to assess current and future avocado suitability across India using Representative Concentration Pathways (RCP) 4.5 and 8.5 for 2050 and 2070. Ten environmental variables comprising dynamic climatic factors (Bio5, Bio6 and Bio17) and static soil, topographic and land-use variables were standardized using fuzzy membership functions and weighted through AHP. The pairwise comparison matrix showed excellent consistency (Consistency Ratio = 0.0155), confirming the reliability of the weighting scheme. Within the AHP framework, climatic variables received the highest parent weight (0.53). Among the evaluated variables, Bio5 (maximum temperature of the warmest month) and Bio17 (precipitation of the driest quarter) were assigned the highest global weights, reflecting their assumed importance based on expert judgment and published eco-physiological evidence. Under current conditions, optimum suitability occupies approximately 1.28 million km², concentrated mainly in southern India. Under the high-emission RCP 8.5 scenario, optimum habitat declines to 0.82 million km² by 2070, representing ~ 36% reduction, while the North-Eastern region shows ~ 32% increase in optimum suitability due to reduced frost limitation. State-level analysis identified Uttar Pradesh and Gujarat as the most climate-sensitive regions, with optimum suitability declining by ~ 74% under RCP 8.5 by 2070. Centroid analysis further revealed a south-westward shift of the optimum suitability zone by approximately 560 km, indicating progressive relocation of climatically favourable areas toward the Western Ghats. Overall, the modelling framework indicates that climatic variables exert greater influence on projected avocado suitability than static edaphic and land-use factors. Under the evaluated climate scenarios, the suitability projections suggest a gradual shift from traditional southern production zones toward relatively more suitable areas in the north-eastern region These findings provide a scientific basis for climate-resilient orchard planning, strategic relocation of cultivation, cultivar diversification and targeted irrigation management under future climate change.

papers.title: Synergistic stabilization of expansive soil using hybrid alkali-activated bagasse ash and rice husk ash for sustainable pavement subgrades
papers.abstract: Expansive black cotton soil poses significant challenges for pavement subgrades due to low strength, high swelling potential, and high moisture sensitivity. This study investigates a hybrid alkali-activated stabilization approach using agro-industrial wastes, namely Bagasse Ash (BA) and Rice Husk Ash (RHA), to improve soil performance. In the first phase, BA was used as the primary stabilizer and varied to determine its optimum content under constant sodium silicate activation. In the second phase, RHA was incorporated as a secondary pozzolanic additive to develop a hybrid stabilization system. Engineering performance was evaluated using unconfined compressive strength (UCS), soaked California Bearing Ratio (CBR), swelling characteristics, and compaction tests. Microstructural and chemical analyses, including XRD, FTIR, and SEM-EDS, were conducted at optimum stabilization levels to understand the governing mechanisms. Results show that BA enhances strength and reduces swelling up to an optimum of 12 wt%, beyond which performance declines due to unreacted ash. The hybrid system containing 12 wt% BA + 12 wt% RHA, activated with 8 wt% sodium silicate and cured for 7 days, achieved a UCS of 1350 kPa, soaked CBR of 18.5%, free swell index of 25%, and swell pressure of 40 kPa, demonstrating improved strength, bearing capacity, and swelling resistance. The combined XRD, FTIR, and SEM–EDS results indicate mineralogical, chemical-bond, and elemental changes associated with the development of a chemically bonded silica-rich matrix in the hybrid-stabilized soil.

papers.title: CoDiNet-ID: a confidence-aware dual-level ensemble framework with dynamic confidence fusion for network intrusion detection
papers.abstract: Network intrusion detection systems (IDS) increasingly rely on stacking ensembles that combine multiple classifiers. Most existing systems fuse classifier outputs using fixed rules. They do not account for how reliable each classifier is on a given sample. This limits their adaptability across different traffic conditions. This paper presents CoDiNet-ID, a confidence-aware dual-level ensemble for binary intrusion detection, distinguishing normal traffic from attack traffic. Four heterogeneous base classifiers are trained using a stratified out-of-fold procedure in which preprocessing and probability calibration are fitted within the training folds. Their output probabilities are calibrated through isotonic regression and combined into a 16-dimensional meta-representation. This representation captures prediction confidence, inter-classifier agreement, weighted consensus, and dispersion. A lightweight Convolutional Neural Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (CNN-GRU) meta-learner, containing only 7,553 trainable parameters, processes this representation with low computational overhead and fast inference. A Dynamic Confidence Fusion Layer then combines the meta-learner output with the ensemble consensus and the attack-vote fraction, using a blending weight and decision threshold tuned once per dataset. Over 10 runs on UNSW-NB15 it reaches 89.62% accuracy (95% confidence half-width 0.21) and an F1-score of 0.9111, which is 1.7 points above the best single base learner (95% confidence interval 1.4 to 1.9 points). On a stratified sample of CICIDS2017 it reaches 99.57% accuracy (half-width 0.02) and 0.9959 recall over 5 runs, a 0.02-point difference from the standalone Extra Trees that the McNemar test does not detect. The fusion layer is comparable with probability averaging, reliability-weighted consensus and learned gating under a common tuning protocol. Calibration quality is reported with Brier score, log loss and expected calibration error, and ablation, per-category, cross-dataset and computational-cost analyses are included. The limitations, including binary-only evaluation, benchmark artefacts and the limited cross-dataset evidence, are stated explicitly.

papers.title: Inflammatory signaling reshapes metabolic pathways in pediatric Crohn’s disease ileal organoids
papers.abstract: Metabolic changes in the mucosa occur during Crohn’s disease (CD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. The goal of our study was to mechanistically investigate the connection of metabolic pathways to cytokine signaling within intestinal epithelial cells. We used ileal patient derived organoids (PDOs) from individuals with CD and non-CD controls (N = 10, 5/5) and a combination of immunofluorescence, LC-MS, and in-vitro biochemical assays to characterize epithelial-specific metabolic responses under cytokine stimulation. GLUT1 protein levels increased in response to TNF-α/IFN-γ but intracellular ATP levels decreased. This effect on ATP was partially reversible with atorvastatin exposure, suggesting involvement of the mevalonate pathway during inflammation. Metabolic profiling suggested that glycolysis and amino acid metabolism were altered in CD PDOs at baseline and in response to TNF-α/IFN-γ exposure. Many of the CD-specific metabolic features were exemplified by non-CD PDOs when stimulated by TNF-α/IFN-γ. Secretory responses to TNF-α/IFN-γ measured in PDO conditioned media by Luminex were largely similar between CD and non-CD PDOs. However, using a computational assessment across experimental conditions, we detected subtle stoichiometric differences in secretome profiles and their association with metabolites at baseline and during TNF-α/IFN-γ stimulation. Taken together, we provide a framework for investigating metabolic changes in epithelial cells during CD.

papers.title: Multimodal fusion of visual and lesion features for mobile-based severity assessment of rice bacterial leaf blight
papers.abstract: This paper presents Paddy Pathologist, a field-deployable multimodal mobile framework for stage-wise severity assessment of rice Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). The study addresses the need for practical disease diagnosis under real field conditions, where variations in illumination, background, and symptom appearance affect model performance. The proposed pipeline uses a lightweight U-Net for rice leaf segmentation, followed by HSV-based lesion masking. A MobileNetV2 network enhanced with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM) is used to extract visual features, while six handcrafted descriptors representing lesion area, color, and texture are extracted from the lesion-masked images. The visual and description-based representations are fused at the feature level and used for five-stage BLB severity classification. Experiments were conducted using BLBVisionDB, with the data divided into training, validation, and test subsets before augmentation. The multimodal fusion model achieves an accuracy of 96.05% on the test set. A Grad-CAM analysis shows that the model is mainly focusing on lesion regions and not on background areas. The trained models were converted to TensorFlow Lite and integrated into the Paddy Pathologist Android application for on-device inference. The application provides multilingual support and additionally gives advisory through SMS, which makes it useful for both farmers and agricultural officers. Moreover, this work supports Sustainable Development Goal-2 by helping in early detection and proper management of rice diseases.

papers.title: Internet use, depression, and life satisfaction among older adults in China
papers.abstract: Based on the ecological theory of aging, this study examines whether the relationships between changes in Internet use status and depression and life satisfaction among Chinese adults aged 60 years or older vary across periods of Internet development. We construct three two-period panels from the China Family Panel Studies, covering 2010-2014, 2014-2016, and 2016-2018, and use ordinary least squares (OLS) and propensity score matching difference-in-differences (PSM-DID) models. The full-sample PSM-DID results show no statistically significant association between Internet entry or exit and depression in any of the three panels. The results for life satisfaction differ across the three periods. Compared with persistent nonuse, Internet entry is associated with a greater increase in life satisfaction in the first two panels but not in the third. In contrast, compared with continued use, Internet exit is associated with a greater decline in life satisfaction in the second panel, but with an increase in the third. Overall, the findings suggest that the associations between changes in Internet-use status and older adults’ well-being differ across periods of Internet development. These findings extend the competence-environmental press perspective by highlighting the role of the broader Internet environment in the relationship between Internet use and well-being.

papers.title: A hybrid question-generation framework integrates BoW-based concept extraction, Seq2Seq learning, and Bloom’s taxonomy
papers.abstract: This study presents an artificial intelligence–based framework for generating open-ended questions from Turkish educational content. The proposed system combines a template-based bag-of-words (BoW) approach with an attention-based sequence-to-sequence (Seq2Seq) model to identify salient concepts, model contextual relations, and generate questions at different Bloom cognitive levels. The framework was evaluated on two complementary resources: TQuADv1, a structured Turkish question-answering dataset, and a newly constructed Fruit-Orchard Maintenance Question-Generation Dataset containing 654 context–question instances derived from open course material. Automatic metric performance was assessed using Jaccard similarity, cosine similarity, BLEU-4, METEOR, ROUGE-L, morphological analyzability, and Bloom-level alignment, while broader question acceptability was examined through multidimensional expert evaluation. These indicators were aggregated through Shannon entropy weighting and complemented by four-expert evaluation per domain across seven linguistic, semantic, and structural criteria. On TQuADv1, Seq2Seq achieved a higher automated composite score than BoW (0.872 vs. 0.377), with METEOR and ROUGE-L scores of 0.871 and 0.906, respectively. It also received the highest expert rating (3.812/5). On the fruit-orchard dataset, BoW outperformed Seq2Seq in both automated composite scores (0.356 vs. 0.245) and expert ratings (3.779/5 vs. 1.273/5). Although the dataset-level rankings of the two methods were consistent between automated and expert evaluations, discrepancies in question-level assessments highlight the limitations of relying exclusively on automatic metrics to evaluate linguistic and educational quality. The findings show that automatic overlap and cognitive-level metrics capture only part of question quality and should be interpreted jointly with multidimensional expert judgement. The main contribution is an interpretable evaluation framework integrating entropy-weighted automatic metrics with human-centred assessment.

papers.title: Metaheuristic-optimized graph neuro-fuzzy temporal transformer capsule network for multiclass arrhythmia classification from heart rate variability
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of cardiac rhythm abnormalities from electrocardiogram (ECG) signals remains challenging because of nonlinear physiological dependencies, temporal variability, signal noise, and overlapping heartbeat characteristics. This study proposes a Metaheuristic-Optimized Graph Neuro-Fuzzy Temporal Transformer Capsule Network (MO-GNFTTCNet) for multiclass arrhythmia classification using ECG-derived Heart Rate Variability (HRV) features. The framework integrates graph-guided relational learning, temporal transformer encoding, capsule-based hierarchical representation, neuro-fuzzy inference, and Hybrid Whale–Firefly Optimization within a unified architecture. ECG signals are first pre-processed, followed by R-peak localization, RR-interval generation, and multi-domain HRV feature extraction. The extracted representations are progressively refined through graph, temporal, hierarchical, and uncertainty-aware learning stages. Evaluation is performed on the MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database using the AAMI-aligned N, S, V, and F heartbeat classes with subject-wise validation. The proposed framework achieves 98.42% accuracy, 98.45% precision, 98.42% recall, 98.43% F1-score, and 98.58% AUC. Subject-wise 10-fold cross-validation yields 98.44 ± 0.11% mean accuracy, while an accuracy of 92.34% is retained at 5 dB SNR. The results indicate stable classification, low misclassification, and robustness to ECG degradation under the evaluated conditions. The proposed outputs represent annotation-derived heartbeat classes and are not intended as patient-level clinical risk or prognostic estimates.

papers.title: The burden of depressive, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress symptoms among women internally displaced by the April 2023 war in Sudan: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: The ongoing conflict that has afflicted Sudan since April 2023 has resulted in a large number of internally displaced women who may have experienced several mental health disorders without being comprehensively reported. This study aimed to assess the proportions and severity of probable depressive, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) symptoms and identify factors associated with screening-positive outcomes among internally displaced women. A cross-sectional study was conducted between April and October 2025 among 651 displaced women. A random sampling method was applied to select participants within conveniently selected states, namely the White Nile, Kassala, River Nile, and South Darfur states in Sudan. A face-to-face interview was used to evaluate depression, anxiety, and PTSD. Associations between screening-positive outcomes for depressive, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress symptoms and sociodemographic and economic characteristics were examined using bivariate and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses. The proportion of participants screening-positive for probable PTSD, depression, and anxiety was high, at 58.2%, 53.8%, and 46.7%, respectively. Regarding symptom severity, 58.2% of participants reported severe or extremely severe PTSD symptoms, 33.9% for severe depressive symptoms, and 17.7% for severe anxiety symptoms. Compared with women living in camps, those residing in accommodation centers and rented houses had significantly lower adjusted odds of screening-positive for depression (AOR = 0.38, 95% CI: 0.22, 0.66; p = .001 and AOR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.15, 0.74; p = .007, respectively), anxiety (AOR = 0.45, 95% CI: 0.26, 0.78; p = .004 and AOR = 0.39, 95% CI: 0.18, 0.86; p = .020, respectively), and PTSD (AOR = 0.34, 95% CI: 0.20, 0.57; p < .001 and AOR = 0.29, 95% CI: 0.14, 0.61; p = .001, respectively). Women displaced from North Darfur had significantly higher adjusted odds of screening-positive for depression (AOR = 17.28, 95% CI: 7.26, 41.12; p < .001), anxiety (AOR = 10.97, 95% CI: 5.05, 23.81; p < .001), and PTSD (AOR = 8.00, 95% CI: 3.69, 17.33; p < .001) compared with women displaced from Khartoum. This study identified a substantial burden of depressive, anxiety, and post-traumatic stress symptoms among internally displaced women in Sudan, with high proportions of participants screening-positive for probable cases of these conditions. These findings highlight the importance of considering living conditions and displacement-related factors when designing and implementing context-specific mental health and psychosocial support interventions for internally displaced women in humanitarian emergencies.

papers.title: Microgrid day ahead day in day scheduling model considering controllable potential of electric vehicles
papers.abstract: With the growing penetration of distributed renewable energy and large-scale electric vehicle (EV) access, the randomness and volatility of microgrids on both source and load sides have become increasingly prominent. Traditional single-time-scale dispatching struggles to balance economic efficiency and operational stability. Based on V2G technology, EVs can provide bidirectional charging and discharging regulation, making them high-quality flexible resources for fine microgrid scheduling. However, the charging and discharging power of decentralized EVs is discretely distributed in time and space, and traditional monomer modeling suffers from high variable dimensions and difficulty in predicting scheduling potential. This paper proposes an EV-cluster modeling method based on Minkowski summation, in which decentralized EVs are equivalent to a generalized energy storage model. The scheduling potential of EVs is comprehensively evaluated from day-ahead and real-time perspectives, and a two-stage optimal scheduling model of the microgrid is constructed. First, an EV monomer model considering battery self-consumption loss is established, and EV clusters in different access periods are aggregated into a virtual energy storage model through Minkowski summation, greatly reducing variable dimensions. Second, a day-ahead scheduling potential evaluation process for EV charging stations is proposed, generating a day-ahead scheduling boundary using historical data and a prediction method. Then, an intra-day rolling calculation framework is designed to update the scheduling potential of the EV cluster in real time, and a two-stage scheduling model is constructed to minimize penalties for day-ahead and intra-day power deviations. A microgrid with four EV charging stations, a photovoltaic power station, and an energy storage power station is used for simulation. Results show that the proposed cluster modeling method effectively depicts the schedulability potential curve of different charging stations despite EV type differences. The overall trends of day-ahead and real-time schedulability potential curves are consistent, but non-negligible deviations exist. With the proposed two-stage scheduling model, the day-ahead and intra-day power deviation of the microgrid is controlled within 1 MW, and the power deviation between electricity purchase and sale is less than 0.5 MW in most periods, compared with more than 5 MW without the model. The proposed method effectively stabilizes declared power fluctuations, reduces unbalanced penalty costs, and improves the economy and security of microgrid operation. For the 2000-vehicle case, aggregation reduces the number of continuous decision variables from 576,000 to 1152, and that the two-stage rolling strategy reduces the root-mean-square day-ahead/real-time power deviation from 291.44 kW to 135.13 kW (53.63%) and the mean daily imbalance penalty from 21146.31 yuan to 11496.94 yuan (45.63%) over 29 comparable daily scenarios. The observed operational benefit is limited to power-balance feasibility, compliance with storage state-of-charge limits and reduced residual imbalance; voltage deviation, feeder loading and reserve adequacy were not evaluated.

papers.title: An adaptive federated edge–cloud framework for low-latency mobile healthcare systems
papers.abstract: Mobile healthcare systems increasingly depend on distributed edge–cloud infrastructures to handle continuous streams of diverse patient data in Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. However, effective data allocation and service provisioning remain challenging due to fluctuating workloads, limited edge resources, and latency-sensitive healthcare applications. This research presents an adaptive federated coordination-based edge–cloud approach aimed at optimizing data management, minimizing latency, and improving service efficiency and allocation efficiency under different workload conditions without requiring centralized aggregation of raw healthcare data. The proposed framework formulates data allocation and service scheduling as a constrained optimization problem that jointly considers storage capacity, processing latency, workload distribution, and data priority. A likelihood-based data organizing technique is integrated with a federated resource coordination mechanism, where edge nodes perform local allocation decisions and exchange optimization-level information rather than raw healthcare data or model parameters. This design prioritizes healthcare workloads according to the defined priority measure, reduces redundant processing, and promotes balanced resource utilization across distributed edge nodes. A comprehensive experimental assessment using a wearable sensor dataset demonstrates the performance of the proposed methodology. The results show that the framework reduces average system latency from 72 ms to 32 ms compared with the centralized cloud baseline, corresponding to an improvement of approximately 55.6%, while achieving a service efficiency of 0.86 and reducing backlog from 140 to 45 workload units. These improvements are associated with reduced unnecessary data transfers, adaptive workload distribution, and priority-aware allocation across edge resources. Although the federated coordination mechanism introduces lightweight communication overhead for metadata exchange, this overhead remains lower than the transmission of raw healthcare data to centralized processing layers. Furthermore, the framework exhibits stable delay behavior with controlled delay growth as workload volume increases within the evaluated workload range, indicating predictable scalability under the simulated high-load conditions. These simulation-based results suggest that the federated coordination and adaptive allocation mechanisms can support efficient management of distributed healthcare workloads while maintaining data locality at edge nodes.

papers.title: A two-level deep learning framework for brain tumor classification from multimodal MRI images using modified SegNet and hybrid pattern-shape features
