papers.abstract: Deep Learning (DL)-based automatic analysis can support accurate and efficient medical image interpretation, thereby providing valuable assistance to healthcare professionals. Brain tumor classification from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is challenging due to variations in tumor appearance, noise, and the complementary information contained in different MRI modalities. To address this challenge, a novel Two-Level CNN-BiLSTM-ILinkNet (2 L-CBILNet) framework is proposed for automated brain tumor classification. The framework consists of preprocessing, segmentation, feature extraction, and two-level classification. Multimodal MRI images are fused using Modified PCA-based Image Modality Fusion and processed using Wiener filtering. The filtered images are segmented using the GM-mSegNet model, followed by extraction of MBP, shape, and ILTP features. A CNN-BiLSTM model performs Level 1 normal/abnormal classification, while ILinkNet performs Level 2 tumor classification. Experimental results show that the proposed model achieves 0.961 accuracy, 0.963 sensitivity, 0.980 specificity, 0.973 precision, and 0.957 F-measure. The proposed GM-mSegNet also achieves a Dice coefficient of 0.929 and Jaccard coefficient of 0.910, demonstrating its effectiveness for brain tumor classification and segmentation.

papers.title: Safety, accuracy, empathy, and readability of four large language models answering esophageal cancer radiotherapy adverse-effect questions: a comparative study
papers.abstract: Patients receiving radiotherapy for esophageal cancer may consult large language model chatbots about treatment-related adverse effects, but the safety of their advice is uncertain. We submitted 42 researcher-developed, patient-oriented questions once each to ChatGPT, Gemini, DeepSeek, and Doubao through public web interfaces, obtaining 168 responses. Five blinded expert raters assessed potential harm, accuracy, and perceived empathic communication; information quality, visible source transparency, and formula-based readability were also evaluated. Twenty-one responses (12.5%) were classified as potentially unsafe; six could delay clinical assessment and ten involved potentially harmful self-management advice. Unsafe-response proportions ranged from 7.1% to 16.7% across models, with no statistically significant overall difference (Cochran’s Q = 1.981, P = 0.576). Median accuracy and expert-rated perceived empathic communication scores were 4 and 3 (on five-point scales) for every model. Between-model differences were statistically significant but small (accuracy: P = 0.001, Kendall’s W = 0.126; perceived empathic communication: P < 0.001, W = 0.149). Visible source-transparency indicators were limited, and formula-estimated readability differed across models. These single-query findings indicate that favorable accuracy ratings do not preclude potentially unsafe advice and cannot establish stable model rankings, patient comprehension, or clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Proximal policy optimization with adaptive fuzzy logic (PPO-AFL) for high-efficiency maximum power point tracking in three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic systems
papers.abstract: In this work, a new controller called Proximal Policy Optimization with Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (PPO-AFL) is introduced for Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) in a 4.98 kW three-phase grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system. All testing was done through MATLAB R2023b/Simulink. The PPO-AFL controller links a PPO reinforcement learning agent with Generalized Advantage Estimation (GAE) to a two-timescale Takagi-Sugeno-Kang (TSK) Adaptive Fuzzy Logic (AFL) unit. This setup adjusts the fuzzy membership function parameters in real time without needing any labelled training data. A combined reward signal simultaneously addresses maximum-power extraction, DC-link voltage regulation, grid-current harmonic distortion, and duty-cycle smoothness. The grid-side terms are evaluated against selected harmonic-distortion and power-factor criteria used as power-quality reference limits; full IEEE 1547–2018 compliance is not claimed. Under idealized MATLAB/Simulink simulation conditions, results indicate a steady-state tracking efficiency of 99.5%, a settling time of 52 ms, a power ripple of ± 3 W, a grid current THD of 0.8%, and a power factor of 0.998. These values are better than ten reference algorithms including P&O (92.1%), INC (93.6%), ANN-MPPT (97.3%), and DDPG-MPPT (97.9%) across all measured criteria. An ablation study with five system variants confirms that each component adds independently to the final performance. Statistical tests across 150 simulation runs per algorithm (1,650 observations across the eleven methods; one-way ANOVA, F(10, 1639) = 1124.7, p < 0.001) confirm the findings are significant. Hardware tests such as HIL, PIL, and DSP/FPGA prototype work are needed in future to verify these results in real conditions.

papers.title: A collaborative multi-model framework with large language model fusion for automated reservoir model quality assurance
papers.abstract: Reservoir models underpin field development decisions that involve substantial capital investment, yet their quality assurance prior to simulation remains a largely manual process. Experts inspect property histograms, production curves, and parameter files across three heterogeneous data modalities: spatial fields, well level time series, and tabular parameters. This workflow is time consuming, subjective, and structurally blind to defects that arise at the interfaces between modalities. Here we present a quality control framework that decomposes reservoir model inspection into four modality specific detection tasks, then fuses their outputs for integrated assessment. Four specialized algorithms each target a single data type: Isolation Forest identifies statistical outliers in well point residuals, a convolutional autoencoder flags anomalies in geological property planes, an LSTM autoencoder detects contextual anomalies in production time series, and XGBoost evaluates simulation parameter validity. Structured detection outputs are fused through a weighted scoring scheme into component scores, and a large language model guided by a domain knowledge base organizes the evidence and recommends a final quality decision in an evidence traced assessment report. All automated judgments are confirmed by a human expert. Evaluated on the 10 held out test sub-regions of the Baoqing-1 fault block model (partitioned from 50 sub-regions into 35 training, 5 validation, and 10 test) under a blind test protocol, the framework achieved a sub-region level final decision F1 score of 0.89 (9 of the 10 held out test sub-regions correctly decided, with no defective sub-region passing undetected), compared with 0.50 for the industrial rule based baseline and 0.67 for an end to end XGBoost classifier on the same 10 sub-regions. At the parameter judgment level, it achieved a defect detection F1 score of 0.90, reported as a secondary consistency metric. Quality control time was reduced from 144 hours to 28 hours per sub-region. These results constitute a proof of principle for LLM guided quality control of reservoir models: validation remains limited to 10 held out sub-regions of a single parent fault block model. Principled decomposition by data modality, combined with structured fusion and expert oversight, can turn fragmented manual inspection into a systematic, auditable workflow.

papers.title: A two-network audit shows when conformal prediction intervals for solar irradiance forecasts remain valid at newly commissioned stations
papers.abstract: A newly commissioned solar site needs trustworthy probabilistic forecasts immediately, yet conformal prediction’s coverage guarantee assumes local calibration data that a new site lacks. We audit this cold-start gap with leave-one-station-out experiments on two networks, 13 continental-US NOAA stations (donors 200–3700 km apart) and 28 PV-Live stations (donors 10–240 km apart), with four forecasters and four horizons (15 min to 6 h). Pooled-donor calibration with zero local data is near-nominal on average but not per station: at 6 h, only 54–69% of station-years stay within ± 2% points. Local calibration restores validity at horizons up to 1 h for three of four forecasters after a median 21–136 days of local data; a prospective self-certification rule reproduces this limit. At 3–6 h, most station-years never sustain coverage within ± 1% point through 182 days, a failure shared by dense donors and even a full local year, consistent with temporal drift. Delayed-feedback donor-seeded adaptive conformal inference holds every station’s marginal coverage near nominal by construction, at a Winkler-score cost of at most about 2% on identical evaluation steps for the learned forecasters, with occasional infinite intervals and a 30–60-day transient. We distill a deployment protocol for new solar sites.

papers.title: Unraveling the brain-imaging correlates of cerebral palsy: insights from Mendelian Randomization analysis of brain imaging-derived phenotypes
papers.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is the primary cause of motor disability in children, with a complex etiology involving genetic and environmental factors. Although neuroimaging has revealed brain abnormalities associated with CP, the causal relationships underlying these changes remain unclear. We conducted a two-sample Mendelian Randomization (MR) analysis of 419 brain imaging-derived phenotypes (IDPs) to examine their causal associations with CP risk, using genetic instruments from genome-wide association studies and multiple sensitivity analyses to assess robustness. Eight IDPs showed significant causal associations with CP risk. Increased volume of the left superior frontal gyrus, larger cortical surface area of the left precentral gyrus, and greater thickness of the right rostral anterior cingulate cortex were associated with higher CP risk, whereas higher fractional anisotropy in the left corticospinal tract was associated with lower risk. Altered diffusion metrics in the fornix, genu of the corpus callosum, and bilateral inferior longitudinal fasciculi were also associated with CP risk. These group-level genetic findings highlight brain IDPs as candidate markers that may inform understanding of CP and are hypothesis-generating; they are established at the population level and require validation before any predictive or clinical application.

papers.title: Determinants of participation in household food waste black soldier fly upcycling projects in Singapore
papers.abstract: Household food waste upcycling using black soldier flies (Hermetia illucens) has the potential to enhance urban food security and sustainability. Yet, the barriers to households’ participation in these nascent programs remain unstudied. We use the Theory of Planned Behaviour (TPB) and structural equation modelling to analyse interest in participation in a first-of-a-kind community insect food waste upcycling program (n = 600) in Singapore. Perceived behavioural control emerged as the strongest predictor of intention, followed by subjective norms. Moral norms significantly influenced all three core constructs, highlighting their centrality in residents’ intentions. Beliefs about environmental impact, social expectations (from family and government), actions from environmentalists and family members, time availability, and sanitary concerns also influence participation intentions. For those in charge of cooking at home, receiving practical guidance was key to participation, whereas, for non-cooks, support from household members played a more critical role. Three focus group discussions with 23 participants of an on-going community programme largely corroborated these findings, but also showed that participants with direct experience were less concerned about sanitary issues and were driven more by personal conviction than by social expectations. Our findings enhance the understanding of promoting insect upcycling food waste projects in Singapore, with implications for nascent initiatives globally.

papers.title: A Swin transformer-based real-time traffic sign recognition framework with multi-vehicle camera height validation and an integrated voice alert system
papers.abstract: Real-time traffic sign recognition (TSR) remains a key challenge in intelligent transportation systems (ITS), particularly for edge computing deployment under real-world conditions. Introducing SwinT-TSR, a new hierarchical Swin Transformer-based framework for detecting, classifying, and vocally announcing Indian traffic signs from two vehicle-mounted camera height configurations: Light motor vehicle (LMV) − 0.9 m and Heavy motor vehicle (HMV) − 1.6 m. In recent years, deep learning has become the prevailing standard for object recognition tasks, with transformer architectures increasingly outperforming convolutional models on large-scale vision benchmarks. The proposed framework is trained and validated on the Indian Road Traffic Sign Detection Dataset (IRTSD-DatasetV1), comprising 5,141 images across 37 sign classes from over 90 Indian cities, augmented with two purpose-built custom datasets totalling 6,560 images, yielding a combined 11,701 annotated images. SwinT-TSR combines shifted-window multi-head self-attention (SW-MSA) with a Residual Convolutional Attention Module (RCAM) neck, achieving enhanced multi-scale feature extraction without the quadratic cost of global self-attention. A monocular distance estimation module computes real-time sign-to-vehicle distance, relaying via a Text-to-Speech (TTS) voice pipeline on a Raspberry Pi 5. In head-to-head tests with you only look once (YOLO) v8n, YOLOv11n, and EfficientDet-Lite2, SwinT-TSR posts a 96.8% mean average precision (mAP@50) at 18.9 frames per second (FPS) on the same Pi 5, now paired with a Hailo-8 L neural processing unit (NPU). Applying these insights to practical considerations of the vehicle-height study, raising the camera from 0.9 m to 1.6 m results in a 2.7% drop in mAP and 43.1% drop in average bounding-box pixel area (from 2,784 px² to 1,584 px²; a 24.5% linear dimension decrease), which can guide optimal mounting positions for a mixed fleet of vehicles. The results demonstrate that transformer-based architectures outperform CNN-heavy detectors for real-time edge-deployed TSR applications, and the performance gains are feasible, as 96.8% detection accuracy at 18.9 FPS and sub-500 ms auditory alert latencies on low-cost edge hardware enable actionable hazard warnings to happen within critical human reaction time margins, making the proposed framework a feasible advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS) for complex traffic environments.

papers.title: Linking macroscopic and microscopic wood anatomy for species identification: a cross-scale benchmark and evaluation
papers.abstract: Timber trade controls such as CITES, the EU Deforestation Regulation and the US Lacey Act depend on knowing the species of traded wood, yet computational wood-identification benchmarks almost always evaluate within a single imaging modality. Whether macroscopic end-grain images and microscopic transverse sections of the same species can be brought into genuine species-level correspondence—and whether within-modality accuracy predicts this—has not been tested under controlled taxonomic overlap. We introduce XyloMaMi-Bench, a benchmark of 36,742 macroscopic end-grain images from 100 species, each label confirmed by concordant IAWA-guided anatomical examination and DART-TOFMS chemical fingerprinting, paired with a Central-African microscopic reference set of 1219 transverse sections from 77 species. The two collections share 33 species and 36 genera, which define three overlap-aware evaluation protocols. A macroscopic classifier exceeding 96% balanced accuracy yields below-chance (1.0%) cross-scale retrieval, whereas exact-species supervised contrastive alignment raises forward macro-to-micro rank-one retrieval to 80.2%; shuffled-label, hard-negative, and frozen-pretrained controls confirm that the effect requires genuine species correspondence rather than genus-level similarity, pair-count artefacts or general-purpose visual features. High within-modality accuracy therefore does not guarantee cross-scale correspondence. We release the benchmark splits, overlap-aware protocols, and evaluation code, and describe an on-device mobile implementation intended for first-line screening.

papers.title: Escalating marine heatwaves drive taxonomic and functional trait loss in the world’s warmest coral reefs
papers.abstract: The Persian/Arabian Gulf (‘the Gulf’) is an extreme, high-temperature ecosystem already experiencing thermal regimes projected for reefs elsewhere by 2100, making it a natural laboratory for anticipating future coral community trajectories under climate change. Extreme temperatures have driven well-documented declines in Gulf coral communities; however, their consequences for coral traits remain largely unexplored. Here, we applied a response-effect trait-based framework to 16 years of Gulf coral survey data to show that recurrent marine heatwaves and associated taxonomic losses drove an approximately 50% decline in functional richness, leaving coral communities increasingly reliant on fewer taxa. Trait composition shifted toward more disturbance-tolerant but less structurally complex growth forms, indicating functional simplification and homogenization. Our findings highlight that climate-driven declines in functional richness may reduce the capacity of coral communities to maintain key ecosystem processes under projected warming, underscoring the importance of conserving functional richness and the taxa that sustain it.

papers.title: Research on a spatiotemporal forecasting method for crop prices based on an improved CNN-LSTM hybrid model
papers.abstract: To address the problems that conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) lack constraints from economic physical laws in crop price forecasting and that their spatial modeling is limited by the regular-grid assumption, resulting in physically inconsistent predictions and inaccurate characterization of spatial transmission, this study proposes an improved hybrid CNN–LSTM model integrating physics-informed embedding and directed spatiotemporal graph convolution. First, a Physics-Informed CNN (PI-CNN) based on diffusion–reaction equation residual regularization is constructed, in which economic physical priors are embedded by enforcing feature representations to follow the laws of price-equilibrium diffusion and mean reversion. Second, regular spatial convolution is replaced with directed diffusion graph convolution, and out-degree and in-degree transition matrices are used to model forward transmission and reverse feedback along trade flows, respectively, thereby explicitly characterizing asymmetric price transmission in non-Euclidean directed trade networks. Finally, the above front-end is cascaded with a Long Short-Term Memory network (LSTM) to jointly learn local spatiotemporal patterns, directed spatial dependencies, and long-term temporal dynamics. Using multisource experimental data from 35 core market nodes in China during 2010–2024, including weekly prices, arrival volumes, meteorological variables, and holiday indicators, four-week-ahead forecasting experiments are conducted for corn, wheat, rice, and soybean. Ablation results show that the complete improved CNN-LSTM model reduces the average RMSE across the four crops to 185.6 yuan/t and MAPE to 5.11%, while increasing R2 to 0.865. Compared with the baseline CNN-LSTM model, RMSE is reduced by 25.01%, and the physical constraints and graph convolution exhibit a significant synergistic effect. Further comparisons with mainstream spatiotemporal forecasting models, including D2STGNN, STAEformer, and MegaCRN, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves clear advantages in both forecasting accuracy and generalization capability, while delivering substantial performance gains with only a small increase in the number of model parameters. The proposed method provides technical support for agricultural product price monitoring and early warning with high forecasting accuracy and lower PDE residuals, while its improved directional forecasting capability enhances the reliability of price-trend assessment.

papers.title: Integrated metabolomics and network pharmacology reveal candidate bioactive compounds of the endemic cliff plant Taihangia rupestris var. ciliata
papers.abstract: Taihangia rupestris var. ciliata (TRC) is an endangered cliff-dwelling plant native to the Taihang Mountains in China. Yet, its precise chemical composition remains undefined. Here, we employed multiple complementary approaches to analyze its metabolites and potential active compounds. Metabolomic observations revealed a high abundance of flavonoids in the leaves. Experimental antioxidant assays showed that both leaves and roots exhibited strong antioxidant activity, and correlation analysis provided a descriptive overview of flavonoid constituents that may be linked to these antioxidative properties. Computational predictions based on network pharmacology identified 8 compounds and 8 targets. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested that 3 core compounds (kaempferol, quercetin, and luteolin) and 2 targets (XDH and KDR) exhibited the most favorable docking scores, forming 4 compound-target pairs (Luteolin-XDH, Quercetin-KDR, Kaempferol-KDR, and Quercetin-XDH), and were therefore prioritized, with support from previous reports, as candidate core compounds and targets. These predictions hypothesize potential disease-relevant mechanisms against heart failure and hepatitis, but do not constitute experimental evidence of therapeutic efficacy. We tentatively propose that TRC leaves may represent the primary material for both tea consumption and medicinal development, pending further safety and sustainability assessments. Our findings provide insights into the exploration of potential active constituents in TRC, contributing to its biological prospecting, medicinal development, and species conservation.

papers.title: Apigenin-functionalized Fe 3 O 4 @SP nanocomposites modulate the expression of P53/miR-34a, miR-181a and their potential targets in AGS gastric cancer cells: in vitro analysis with docking insights
papers.abstract: Apigenin (4′,5,7-trihydroxy-flavone) is a naturally occurring dietary flavonoid with promising anticancer activity; however, its poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability substantially limit its therapeutic application. To address these challenges, we developed Apigenin- silyl propyl chloride functionalized iron oxide nanocomposites (Fe3O4@SP@Apigenin Nanocomposites) and evaluated their physicochemical characteristics and anticancer properties against AGS human gastric adenocarcinoma cells. Fe3O4 nanoparticles were synthesized by co-precipitation, coated with silica, and subsequently conjugated with apigenin. Comprehensive characterization using Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), vibrating-sample magnetometry (VSM), energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX), dynamic light scattering (DLS)/zeta potential, X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern, field-emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) confirmed the successful synthesis and functionalization of the nanocomposites. Biological evaluations, including the methyl thiazolyl tetrazolium (MTT) assay, Annexin V/propidium iodide (PI) staining, wound healing test, transwell assay, and quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (qRT-PCR), demonstrated that Fe₃O₄@SP@Apigenin NCs induced dose- and time-dependent cytotoxicity, with IC50 values decreasing from 78.21 to 38.66 µg/mL, between 24 and 72 h. Apoptosis induction and inhibition of cancer cell migration were confirmed in cells treated with Fe₃O₄@SP@Apigenin NCs at the 24 h IC50 concentration (78.21 µg/mL). Molecular analyses revealed significant upregulation of the tumor-suppressor miR-34a and downregulation of its potential targets in apoptotic pathways (P53, BAX, and CASP9 genes), as well as downregulation of oncogenic miR-181a and overexpression of its potential targets involved in cell migration and invasion (β-catenin, EGFR, MMP2, and MMP9 genes). Molecular docking simulations predicted favorable binding affinities of apigenin toward apoptosis- and metastasis-associated targets (p53, caspase-9, MMP-2, and MMP-9), offering supportive computational hypotheses regarding potential molecular interactions. Overall, Fe₃O₄@SP@Apigenin NCs represents a promising magnetic targeting platform for gastric cancer therapy and warrants further in vivo investigation.

papers.title: GeoDec-Net: a geometry decomposed oriented bounding boxes object detection network for remote sensing images
papers.abstract: Oriented Bounding Box (OBB) object detection is of significant application value in scenarios such as maritime monitoring, port management, and disaster assessment. However, many existing lightweight single-stage detection methods rely heavily on standard convolutions and isotropic pooling, which may lead to inaccurate localization and false detections of slender objects due to limited geometric adaptability. To address this issue, we propose a Geometry Decomposed OBB Object Detection Network for Remote Sensing Images (GeoDec-Net). Within this network, we design three modules: the Geometry-Decomposed Block (GDBlock), Geometry-Decomposed Pooling (GDPool), and Geometry-Decomposed Fusion (GDFusion). Specifically, GDBlock utilizes multi-branch depthwise convolutions to independently extract multi-dimensional geometric features, and achieves adaptive feature fusion through a spatial gating mechanism. GDPool combines isotropic and strip pooling, thereby mitigating the insufficient long-range modeling of objects. GDFusion utilizes coordinate attention and multi-directional residual branches at the high-resolution detection layer to enhance shallow details and suppress background interference. GeoDec-Net improves the localization of elongated objects in complex scenes by strengthening orientation aware representations and geometric modeling. Experimental results on the DOTA-v1.0 and HRSC2016 datasets demonstrate that GeoDec-Net achieves a competitive balance between detection accuracy and computational efficiency.

papers.title: Genetic diversity and population structure of Macrobrachium nipponense in the upper Huaihe River based on mitochondrial COI gene sequences
papers.abstract: The oriental river prawn (Macrobrachium nipponense) is an economically important freshwater crustacean widely distributed in China. Assessing its genetic diversity and population structure is essential for germplasm conservation and sustainable aquaculture. In this study, the mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase subunit I (COI) gene was sequenced to investigate the genetic diversity and population structure of M. nipponense populations in the upper Huaihe River basin. A total of 648 bp of COI sequences were obtained from 303 individuals. Nine wild populations from the upper Huaihe River basin (SGH, PH, GS, WY, SYH, BS, GL, NW, and ZHB) were defined as the target natural populations, while two additional populations were included as comparison objects: SJC, a wild population from the Yangtze River system, and XLS, a cultured population. For the target natural populations, 94 polymorphic sites and 35 haplotypes were identified, with overall haplotype diversity (Hd) of 0.809 and nucleotide diversity (Pi) of 0.00508, indicating moderate to high genetic diversity compared with COI-based studies of this species. Pairwise Fst values among the target natural populations ranged from − 0.019 to 0.504, revealing a wide spectrum of differentiation levels: most pairs showed moderate to high differentiation, while a few exhibited low and non-significant values. The haplotype network showed a star-like topology with three dominant haplotypes (Hap2, Hap7, and Hap8). Hap2 was mainly distributed in four populations (XLS, SJC, NW, and ZHB), whereas Hap7 and Hap8 were mainly distributed in seven populations (SGH, SYH, WY, BS, GL, GS, and PH). The NJ phylogenetic tree revealed no distinct geographic clustering. These findings provide a basis for identifying populations that deserve further assessment and monitoring for the conservation of M. nipponense germplasm resources in the Huaihe River basin.

papers.title: Conserved age-specific mortality patterns across pandemic-era disruption and recovery in patients with kidney failure receiving replacement therapy
papers.abstract: Patients with kidney failure experience markedly higher mortality than the general population. In the United States, mortality of these patients declined steadily throughout the 2010s but rose sharply with the onset of the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic. Here, we examined age-dependent mortality trends in the adult population of patients with kidney failure with replacement therapy (KFRT) based on data from the U.S. Renal Data System (USRDS), stratified by treatment modality (maintenance dialysis or kidney transplant) and transplant waitlisting status. Across all KFRT subpopulations, mortality followed a robust Gompertz law, with rates increasing exponentially with age, whereby mortality parameters strongly depended on the KFRT subpopulation. We further observed that as life expectancy increased, mortality curves steepened in a coordinated fashion, a pattern consistent with Strehler–Mildvan correlation, most clearly observed in the transplant population and, over parts of the observation period, in dialysis populations. Temporal analyses revealed abrupt shifts in mortality parameters coinciding with the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic. In 2020 and 2021, these parameters regressed along or parallel to their pre-2020 trajectories, with a partial reversion in 2022 and 2023, indicating that the entire mortality curve evolved along a constrained path, even under a large-scale public health disruption. These findings suggest conserved regularities in the joint dynamics of aging and temporal mortality trends in this highly vulnerable population, with implications for modeling mortality under future systemic shocks.

papers.title: Solar integrated biomass to dimethyl ether synthesis via auto thermal reforming and water electrolysis for efficient CO 2 utilization
papers.abstract: The shift toward low-carbon fuels increasingly depends on processes that can utilize biogenic resources, incorporate external CO2, and operate reliably with renewable electricity. This work introduces an integrated biomass-to-dimethyl ether (DME) pathway that links autothermal reforming of rice husk with a solid oxide electrolysis unit and a solar photovoltaic field. The aim is to quantify how solar-assisted, grid-buffered electrification of this route affects energy efficiency, plant-level CO2 utilization, and production cost relative to a grid-powered benchmark. An expanded multi-parameter decision space was constructed to capture interactions among ATR (auto-thermal reforming) conversion, operating temperature, solar irradiance, hydrogen generation, and catalyst behavior. The system was optimized using the recent R-DNEA (reference-point-based evolutionary algorithm) multi-objective algorithm to simultaneously raise overall energy efficiency, lower the net carbon balance (NCB), and reduce the levelized cost of DME (LC-DME). The solar-assisted configuration increased plant-level CO2 utilization from 0.651 to 0.989 kg/s, improved carbon efficiency from 85.47% to 86.48%, and shifted the gate-to-gate net carbon balance from − 0.320 to − 0.752 kg/s when electricity-related emissions are excluded; when grid-import emissions are included, net fixation is retained only for grid emission factors below 12.9 g CO2/kWh (grid-powered) and 41.3 g CO2/kWh (solar-assisted). The integrated design produced 4.52 kg/s of DME while strengthening thermal coupling between the ATR and electrolysis units through the beneficial use of electrolyser-derived oxygen. An annual electricity balance shows that a load-matched PV array (89.4 MWAC) with a short-duration battery buffer supplies 26.7% of the 679.3 GWh/yr electricity demand, while the grid supplies the remaining 73.3%. On this basis, the LC-DME is 385.1 USD/ton for the grid-powered configuration and 478.8 USD/ton for the solar-assisted configuration, and the solar-assisted route becomes cost-competitive only when the grid tariff exceeds about 99.6 USD/MWh, which equals the levelized cost of the PV-delivered electricity. Multi-objective optimization raised the overall energy efficiency to 86.12% at an NCB of − 0.713 kg/s, with a re-based LC-DME of about 465.7 USD/ton. These results show that coupling renewable electrolysis with controlled ATR chemistry achieves net CO2 fixation within the plant boundary, whereas the economic benefit of solar assistance depends mainly on the grid tariff and the PV capital cost. The framework also provides practical guidance for renewable-fuel plant design.

papers.title: ADNET adaptive dual stream network with hierarchical attention fusion for early stage Alzheimer’s disease detection from brain MRI
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder accounting for 60–80% of dementia cases worldwide, yet no curative treatment exists and early-stage detection remains a persistent clinical challenge. Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) offers a non-invasive means of capturing structural neurodegeneration, making automated MRI-based classification a high-priority research area. This study presents ADNET (Adaptive Dual-stream Network), a hybrid deep learning framework for multi-class AD staging from 2D brain MRI images. ADNET integrates a parallel dual-stream encoder combining EfficientNet-B3 for local convolutional feature extraction with a Swin Transformer for global self-attention, augmented by a Channel-Spatial Progressive Attention (CSPA) module with anatomical prior initialization targeting hippocampal and entorhinal cortex regions. A Hierarchical Attention Fusion (HAF) module enables multi-scale progressive feature integration, and an MRI-Specific Augmentation (MSA) pipeline incorporating seven physiologically grounded strategies addresses class imbalance and domain-specific data scarcity. The model was trained and evaluated on the publicly available Kaggle Alzheimer’s MRI Dataset (6,400 images; four classes) using stratified image-level 70/15/15% splits; because this public derivative dataset does not provide subject or session identifiers, subject-level separation could not be independently verified, and this is treated as a limitation of the study rather than a resolved methodological guarantee. ADNET achieved an overall classification accuracy of 99.41% (95% CI 99.02–99.79%), macro sensitivity of 99.18%, macro specificity of 99.72%, macro F1-score of 99.29%, and macro AUC-ROC of 0.9987 on this benchmark, numerically exceeding the accuracy figures reported in 8 previously published studies on the same or related Kaggle dataset whose citations we were able to independently verify (4 additional studies originally included in this comparison were removed after their source papers could not be located), although these comparisons use results as originally reported rather than baselines reproduced under an identical protocol. A subsequent independent reproduction of the complete described architecture and training recipe (Sect.  5.8) found that training budget mattered substantially: an initial attempt at 20 epochs achieved only 75.44% accuracy, but an extended run (up to 100 epochs, full-depth backbones since the exact backbone configuration could not be confirmed) reached 94.75% overall accuracy and 96.15% macro F1 across a complete, real 5-fold evaluation — still approximately 4.7 and 3.1 percentage points below the headline figures above, respectively, but far closer than the initial attempt suggested. Moderate Demented performance in this reproduction (100%, 64/64) closely matched the original claim. We report this gap prominently and have not fully resolved it; see Sect.  5.8 for the full training-budget progression and disclosed differences in configuration that may explain the remainder. ADNET attained an F1-score of 98.81% for the Very Mild Demented class; performance on the Moderate Demented class (F1 = 100%) is based on only 9–10 test images (depending on fold) and should be interpreted with corresponding caution (95% exact CI approximately 66–100%). Ablation experiments indicate the additive contribution of each architectural component on this dataset. Grad-CAM + + saliency maps showed attention patterns that the authors judged, through an internal, non-blinded qualitative review, to be broadly consistent with expected Alzheimer’s-related atrophy regions; this analysis has not yet been validated by independent clinical experts or registered to an anatomical atlas, and should be regarded as illustrative rather than confirmatory. With only 3.2 million parameters and an inference time of approximately 4 ms per image on the evaluated hardware, ADNET is computationally efficient. These results position ADNET as a promising research prototype for automated Alzheimer’s staging on this benchmark; we make no claim of clinical readiness, and any clinical or population-screening use would require prospective, multi-site, subject-level validation, which we identify as the principal direction for future work.

papers.title: Investigation of the effects of different in-office bleaching techniques on surface roughness and color changes of human dental enamel
papers.abstract: In-office tooth bleaching is widely used for esthetic treatment, yet commercial systems differ in formulation and application protocols, which may influence whitening response and enamel surface characteristics. This in vitro study compared three commercial in-office bleaching systems using 80 human enamel specimens allocated to four groups: untreated control, Opalescence Boost (40% hydrogen peroxide), Whiteness HP Blue (35% hydrogen peroxide), and Philips Zoom WhiteSpeed (6% hydrogen peroxide, light-activated) (n = 20). Surface roughness (Ra and Sa) and whiteness index for dentistry (WID) were assessed at baseline (T0), immediately after bleaching (T1; bleaching groups only), and after 30 days (T2). CIEDE2000 color differences (ΔE₀₀) were calculated for the T0–T1 and T0–T2 intervals. Representative specimens were additionally examined using SEM and descriptive EDX. Opalescence Boost produced the greatest immediate color change, whereas Opalescence Boost and Whiteness HP Blue showed greater 30-day color changes than Philips Zoom. No statistically significant changes were detected in Sa, whereas Ra showed a significant immediate increase in the Philips Zoom group; no significant changes in Ra were detected at the 30-day evaluation. SEM revealed localized micromorphological alterations, while descriptive EDX showed similar Ca and P distributions between unbleached and bleached regions of representative specimens. Overall, the tested commercial bleaching systems produced different whitening responses while a significant immediate increase in Ra was observed only in the Philips Zoom group; no significant changes in Sa or in surface roughness at the 30-day evaluation were detected, although localized micromorphological alterations were observed in representative SEM specimens.

papers.title: A bidirectional time-frequency domain CNN with attention mechanism for music genre classification
papers.abstract: Music genre classification is a fundamental task in Music Information Retrieval (MIR). However, conventional Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architectures often struggle to adequately capture the inherent temporal dynamics and spectral variations of audio signals. To address this limitation, this study proposes a bidirectional time-frequency CNN model employing supervised timbre and temporal modules to jointly model spectral and temporal features. Channel and spatial attention mechanisms are incorporated to dynamically recalibrate feature responses, thereby emphasizing discriminative time-frequency regions. Experiments were conducted on the publicly available GTZAN and FMA-small benchmark datasets. The proposed model achieved an average classification accuracy of 94.32% on the GTZAN dataset, achieving higher performance than ResNet, VGGNet, DenseNet, and recent state-of-the-art methods by at least 3.16%. Ablation studies further demonstrated that both the bidirectional time-frequency architecture and the attention modules made statistically significant contributions to the overall performance. These findings indicate that the proposed model provides an effective approach to music genre classification, with potential applications in MIR and offline music analysis. However, this study is limited to offline benchmark evaluation. Practical deployment, cross-dataset generalization, and robustness in noisy environments remain to be investigated in future work.

papers.title: Insights into kinetics, isotherms, and thermodynamic study on acid-activated cow dung waste for malachite green uptake
papers.abstract: Batch adsorption experiments were performed to examined the efficiency of acid-activated cow dung (ACD) for the sorption of malachite green (MG) dye from aqueous solution under varying experimental conditions. The structural elucidation of the prepared adsorbent was performed through Fourier Transform Infrared Spectroscopy (FT-IR), Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET), X-ray Diffraction (XRD), and Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), which confirmed the presence of abundant functional groups, porous surface morphology, amorphous carbonaceous material, and structural features favorable for adsorption. The impact of operational parameters including contact time, adsorbent dosage, pH, initial dye concentration, and temperature on MG uptake was evaluated. Optimum adsorption performance was attained at pH 9, adsorbent dosage of 0.25 g, contact time of 100 min, and temperature of 40 °C. The adsorption kinetics were best described by the pseudo-second-order kinetic model, while the equilibrium studies showed that the Langmuir isotherm model provided the best fit for the experimental data, with a maximum adsorption capacity of 38.15 mg/g and 33.12 mg/g for linear and none-linear methods respectively. The separation factor $$\:\left({R}_{L}<1\right)\:$$confirmed the favorability of the adsorption process. Thermodynamic assessment showed that the adsorption of MG onto ACD was spontaneous, feasible, and endothermic in nature. Study on regeneration further showed that the adsorbent retained substantial adsorption efficiency after repeated adsorption–desorption cycles, suggesting good stability and reusability. Thus, the study demonstrates that acid-activated cow dung is an efficient adsorbent for the remediation of dye-contaminated wastewater.

papers.title: Comparison of electroanatomic mapping-guided versus high-frequency stimulation-guided cardioneuroablation for vasovagal syncope: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: When conservative management yields unsatisfactory outcomes in patients with vasovagal syncope (VVS), cardioneuroablation (CNA) serves as a novel therapeutic approach with substantial efficacy in reducing syncopal recurrence. However, despite the availability of various feasible ablation modalities, the comparative efficacy among different strategies remains unclear. Accordingly, we performed a meta-analysis to compare the efficacy of electroanatomic mapping (EAM)-guided versus high-frequency stimulation (HFS)-guided CNA for VVS, with post-procedural syncopal recurrence as the primary endpoint and positive head-up tilt test (HUT) result as the secondary endpoint. We searched the PubMed, Cochrane, and Embase databases from their inception to 15 January 2026. Studies that included both EAM- and HFS-guided CNA were enrolled. Two authors independently evaluated the quality of the included studies using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) and the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ) tool. Meta-analysis was conducted with Stata 17 software, and a random-effects model was applied when pooling data with high heterogeneity. A total of 5 studies were included, involving 281 patients with VVS who underwent CNA (179 in the EAM group and 102 in the HFS group). Of these, 222 patients (156 in the EAM group and 66 in the HFS group) provided evaluable data for the primary outcome of syncope recurrence and were included in the pooled analysis. Results demonstrated that there was no statistically significant difference in syncopal recurrence rates between patients receiving EAM- and HFS-guided CNA (RR 0.76, 95% CI 0.09–6.74, I2 = 69.5%, p = 0.808). Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested a possible reduction in syncopal recurrence with EAM-guided CNA among the included European studies, all of which adopted biatrial ablation (RR = 0.06, 95% CI 0.01–0.49, p = 0.008). Furthermore, there was no statistically significant difference in HUT positive rates between the EAM and HFS groups (RR = 0.09, 95% CI 0.00–2.56, I2 = 81.2%, p = 0.158). While this meta‑analysis found no significant between‑group difference in syncope recurrence, exploratory subgroup analyses hinted at a potential benefit of EAM-guided CNA among the included European studies, all of which adopted biatrial ablation. Given the limited sample size, these findings should be interpreted with caution.

papers.title: Sex estimation from nasal complex morphometry on paranasal CT with reduced measurement sets and independent external validation
papers.abstract: Cranial sex estimation requires population-specific, independently validated methods. We evaluated nasal bone, piriform aperture (PA), and anterior nasal spine measurements on paranasal sinus CT for biological sex estimation in Turkish adults. Fourteen parameters were obtained in 351 adults (176 males). A ten-measurement elastic-net model and 16,383 measurement subsets were evaluated within nested cross-validation, and fixed models were applied to 110 adults imaged on a different scanner at a second center in the same city. PA perimeter was the strongest measurement (area under the ROC curve [AUC] 0.862). The ten-measurement model reached an AUC of 0.904 (95% CI 0.872–0.934) and a balanced accuracy of 85.2%, exceeding a PA perimeter-only model by 0.045 (95% CI 0.015–0.075). Nasal bone contour length, PA height, and PA perimeter were selected in 29 of 30 resamples (AUC 0.902). Externally, the ten- and three-measurement models reached AUCs of 0.875 (0.800–0.940) and 0.855 (0.773–0.927) and balanced accuracies of 82.8% and 80.1%, and under a 0.80/0.20 rule classified 64% and 56% of cases with 89% accuracy. Three measurements provide sex estimation validated across scanners within one population; transfer from clinical to postmortem CT remains to be tested, and probabilities should be reported with their decision rule, coverage, and calibration.

papers.title: Immunoinformatics applied to analyze Monkeypox virus isolates from Africa to design a broad-spectrum multi-epitope vaccine
papers.abstract: The global re-emergence of monkeypox virus (MPXV), particularly clade IIb and its variants, alongside its disproportionate burden in Africa, underscores the urgent need for next-generation vaccines targeting evolving viral clades. In this study, reverse vaccinology and immunoinformatics approaches were employed to design a multi-epitope vaccine, prioritizing African isolates from historically endemic regions. Whole-proteome analysis of 121 MPXV isolates with complete, high-coverage genomes identified 11 conserved and antigenic proteins. Cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL), helper T lymphocyte (HTL), and B-cell epitopes were selected based on conservation and immunological properties, exhibiting 100% sequence conservation across analyzed isolates. These epitopes were assembled into vaccine constructs using optimized linkers and adjuvants. Structural modeling and refinement supported predicted structural stability, while codon optimization and in silico cloning suggested potential for efficient expression in Escherichia coli. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations supported stable interactions between the lead construct (V1) and Toll-like receptors TLR2 and TLR4. Immune simulations predicted robust antibody production, coordinated humoral and cellular responses, and immune memory. Based on HLA allele frequencies, V1 achieved an estimated population coverage of 98.24%. Overall, V1 emerged as a promising in silico vaccine candidate against MPXV; however, experimental validation remains essential to establish its safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy.

papers.title: Solar-driven photocatalytic purification of textile wastewater using water hyacinth-derived cellulose nanocrystal/Ag@ZnO bioinorganic nanocomposites
papers.abstract: Improper disposal of dye-containing wastewater severely threatens aquatic ecosystems through intense water contamination. In this study, we synthesized high-surface-area cellulose nanocrystals from invasive water hyacinth (Pontederia crassipes) stems via acid hydrolysis and utilized the leaf biomass to prepare silver-doped zinc oxide (Ag@ZnO) nanoparticles through an eco-friendly green synthesis approach. These components were coupled in various ratios, CNC/Ag@ZnO (1:1), (1:0.5), and (0.5:1), to assemble ternary bio-nanocomposites. Extensive characterization revealed that the CNC/Ag@ZnO (1:0.5) configuration maximized interfacial contact, establishing a synergistic heterojunction that suppresses radiative electron-hole recombination and exploits surface oxygen vacancies for enhanced electron trapping. Consequently, this optimized composite achieved an exceptional 98.85% degradation of Methylene Blue under natural sunlight within 120 min, yielding an apparent first-order rate constant of 0.055 min⁻¹. When applied to real complex textile wastewater matrices, the composite overcame industrial solute interference to reach a 99.24% dye removal efficiency, while retaining 90.67% of its initial activity after 7 consecutive reuse cycles. Most importantly, biocompatibility assays using barley seeds demonstrated that the photocatalytically treated water completely decolorized the MB dye, promoting healthy plant development comparable to tap water controls and confirming its safety for agricultural irrigation. These findings highlight the CNC/Ag@ZnO (1:0.5) BNC as a highly sustainable, robust, and biocompatible photocatalyst platform capable of transforming hazardous industrial effluent into safe water for agricultural irrigation.

papers.title: Comparative genomic landscape of Rift Valley fever virus vaccine and circulating strains: identifying candidate vaccine-associated molecular signatures
papers.abstract: Rift Valley fever virus (RVFV) causes recurring zoonotic outbreaks across Africa, yet the three live-attenuated vaccines (Smithburn, MP-12, and Clone 13) lack the differentiating infected from vaccinated animals (DIVA) property and have incompletely characterized attenuation mechanisms. We performed an integrated genome-wide analysis of 245 RVFV sequences per genomic segment (240 non-vaccine circulating sequences and 5 vaccine or vaccine-related accessions) across all four coding regions, incorporating phylogenetic inference, reassortment screening, substitution spectrum analysis, site-specific selection pressure assessment, candidate vaccine-associated substitution identification, and in silico N-glycosylation prediction. Substitution rates ranged between 2.37⋅10− 4 to 3.71⋅10− 4 substitutions per site per year, with root dates predating the first documented 1931 outbreak. Thirty-one candidate reassortant sequences per segment were identified, confirming recurrent reassortment in RVFV. Frequency-based comparison of each vaccine accession against circulating sequences independently recovered the Clone 13 NSs deletion and all three positions previously shown by reverse genetics to contribute to MP-12 attenuation demonstrating concordance between population-level frequency analysis and experimental findings, and confirming that these positions are specific to the vaccine strain. Thirty-five Smithburn-specific candidate substitutions were identified, including three Gn substitutions within the primary neutralising antibody target. These findings provide a quantitatively bounded, cross-validated sequence resource to prioritise functional investigation of attenuation mechanisms and guide the development of molecular diagnostic tools, including candidate DIVA markers pending experimental validation.

papers.title: Valorization of Borassus flabellifer biomass into activated carbon for sustainable chlorpyrifos removal: response surface optimization and adsorption mechanism
papers.abstract: The organophosphate insecticide chlorpyrifos (CPS) has been frequently detected in water supplies, raising serious concerns about its effects on the ecological system and human well-being. The present study aims to synthesize phosphoric acid-treated Borassus flabellifer activated carbon (P-BFAC) for the remediation of CPS from a liquid medium. The developed activated carbon was analyzed using Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FE-SEM), Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR), thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), X-ray diffraction (XRD), particle size and zeta potential analysis, and Brunauer–Emmett–Teller (BET) methods. A hybrid response surface technique with CCD design (RSM-CCD) was established to model and enhance the CPS adsorption performance. In the study, key factors such as adsorbent dosage (0.05–0.6 g), initial pH (2–12), contact time (0–120 min), and initial concentration (2–30 mg/L) were taken. The RSM-CCD was very effective and fitted to a polynomial quadratic model with high regression parameters (R2 = 0.9991, adjusted R2 = 0.9982). The ideal parameter values for attaining 95.86% CPS removal were determined to be 0.328 g of P-BFAC, a pH of 6.35, an initial content of 5.81 mg/L, and a period of 65.5 min. The Langmuir isotherm model correlated well with the monolayer theory with a high coefficient of determination of 0.9936. The kinetics model was found to follow a pseudo-second order (R2 = 0.9901) suggesting a good fit of the model to the experimental data. The negative standard Gibbs free energy (ΔG°) revealed from thermodynamic studies is indicative of a spontaneous process. The positive value of entropy change (ΔS°) indicates the increase in disorder at adsorbent-solution interface and negative value of enthalpy change (ΔH°) indicates the exothermic nature of the process. The adsorption mechanism was studied and the regeneration tests showed good reusability for five cycles with a removal efficiency decrease from 96.12% to 90.13%. The activated carbon prepared from Borassus flabellifer showed high adsorption efficiency and regeneration ability, which revealed its potential as a sorbent for removal of CPS from simulated wastewater. This research provides the first investigation of CPS adsorption using this biomass-derived activated carbon.

papers.title: Maternal preconception calorie restriction reprograms coping strategies, socio-sexual behaviour, and endocrine function in adult rat offspring
papers.abstract: Maternal nutrition before conception is recognised as a determinant of offspring development; however, the behavioural and neuroendocrine consequences of preconception calorie restriction (CR) remain poorly understood. This study isolated the preconception window to examine how different CR patterns, stable (25% reduction; CR-25%), unpredictable deprivation (CR-A), and variable (25–75% fluctuation; CR-V), affect adult offspring outcomes. Male and female progeny from preconception CR female Wistar rats were assessed across domains sensitive to early-life programming, including anxiety- and depression-like behaviour, coping style, socio-sexual behaviour, and hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal (HPG) axis activity. Preconception CR produced sex- and diet-specific effects. Females exhibited transient reductions in exploratory behaviour and more active coping styles, particularly CR-25% and CR-V animals. In males, all CR regimens enhanced copulatory behaviour and reduced aggression toward females. Endocrine profiling revealed divergent HPG responses: CR-A males showed elevated basal faecal testosterone metabolites (fTM) but reduced basal serum testosterone, whereas CR-V males exhibited blunted androgenic reactivity post-social provocation. These findings demonstrate that maternal preconception CR can program male offspring toward a prosocial, sexually motivated phenotype and female offspring toward an enhanced coping style, underscoring this period as a sensitive window for shaping behavioural and endocrine trajectories.

papers.title: Beyond known resistance mutations: machine learning identified potential codons linked to HIV-1B integrase resistance
papers.abstract: Currently, integrase strand transfer inhibitors (INSTIs) are the backbone of antiretroviral therapy (ART). However, the potential for long-term resistance at uncharacterized codon positions still not well defined. Surveillance programs detect known drug resistance mutations (DRMs) but may not identify novel or parallel genetic pathways. Nevertheless, the development of machine learning-based predictive algorithms holds promise for optimizing the needs of people living with HIV. Herein, we develop a Random Forest machine learning model to predict HIVdb-derived INSTI resistance classifications from HIV-1 clade B sequences. A total of 3,833 HIV-1B sequences were extracted from the Los Alamos and Stanford databases and predefined major resistance positions were excluded to examine additional sequence features. Our model achieved 96% accuracy and an F1 score of 0.87 for resistant sequences and achieved higher accuracy and resistant-class F1-score than XGBoost and logistic regression, although XGBoost achieved a higher ROC AUC. The ROC curve demonstrated excellent discriminant power (AUC: 0.94). Ten non-canonical mutational codon positions (157, 160, 234, 97, 112, 101, 230, 74, 232, and 265) were identified as important features. Codon 157 emerged as as the strongest predictor of the HIVdb-derived classification. We demonstrate the potential of machine learning in highlighting integrase positions associated with HIVdb-derived INSTI resistance classifications. We showed that codon-level modelling can rank integrase positions that covary with these classifications, although further experimental studies are needed to determine whether they influence susceptibility. Our findings could contribute to the development of enhanced surveillance strategies rather than to clinical decision-making at this stage.

papers.title: Functional performance characteristics and associated physical and psychological factors among female sports and coaching students
papers.abstract: The rapid expansion of female participation in sport under Saudi Vision 2030 has increased enrollment in sports-related academic programs, exposing students to substantial physical and academic demands. However, the relationships between physical, functional, and psychological characteristics associated with functional screening indicators in female sports students remain poorly understood. This cross-sectional study investigated lower-limb strength, functional performance, dynamic balance, and academic self-efficacy among undergraduate Sports and Coaching students at Princess Nourah bint Abdulrahman University. Participants completed measures of self-reported musculoskeletal symptoms and academic self-efficacy and underwent isokinetic strength testing, the Y-Balance Test, and the Single-Leg Hop Test. Sixty-five female students participated, of whom 66.2% reported pain in at least one anatomical region. Isokinetic testing characterized dominant-limb concentric knee strength, with mean hamstring-to-quadriceps ratios of 46.1% at 60°/s and 39.3% at 180°/s. Functional screening showed that 52.3% of participants had a Single-Leg Hop Test LSI below 90%, while 30.8% had Y-Balance Test anterior reach asymmetry greater than 4 cm. Exploratory, unadjusted analyses indicated that academic self-efficacy was associated with selected dynamic balance measures and differed between the Single-Leg Hop Test LSI groups. These findings characterize musculoskeletal symptoms and functional performance characteristics among female Sports and Coaching students; however, the academic self-efficacy findings should be considered hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in future studies.

papers.title: A network-aware multi-level attention framework for intrusion detection in IoD networks
papers.abstract: In unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication networks, ensuring secure data transmission is challenging because of dynamic network topologies, high mobility, heterogeneous traffic patterns, and evolving cyberattacks. These characteristics limit the effectiveness of conventional intrusion detection systems in accurately identifying malicious activities. To address this issue, this paper proposes a deep learning framework, termed the GRU–Normalized Multi-Level Local Attention Transformer (GNMT), for intrusion detection in UAV communication environments. The key novelty of GNMT is its Normalized Multi-Level Local Attention (NMLA) mechanism, which performs localized self-attention using multiple attention heads with progressively increasing local windows, followed by normalization of the resulting representations to refine discriminative attack-related patterns. Unlike conventional GRU–Transformer and global-attention-based intrusion detection architectures, GNMT introduces NMLA as an intermediate feature-refinement stage between recurrent representation learning and global dependency modeling. Since the evaluated datasets do not provide a usable temporal entity, timestamp structure, each network-flow record is treated as an independent sample. The original tabular feature vector is internally projected into a sequence-compatible representation, enabling the GRU, NMLA, and Transformer components to process the learned feature representation without implying chronological or temporal ordering. Experimental evaluation was conducted on two UAV intrusion detection datasets, namely UAVIDS-2025 and the UAV Attack Dataset, using stratified training, validation, and held-out test partitions. UAVIDS-2025 contains five traffic classes and 1,22,171 cleaned flow records, on which GNMT achieved 99.57% accuracy. The UAV Attack Dataset contains three classes, namely Normal traffic, Jamming, and GPS Spoofing with 10,067 records, on which GNMT achieved 99.87% accuracy. SHAP-based explainability analysis was further employed to identify influential network-traffic features contributing to the model’s prediction decisions. The results demonstrate the effectiveness and interpretability of GNMT for flow-level intrusion detection across UAV communication datasets.

papers.title: First principles analysis of layer dependent structural, electronic, optical, thermodynamic and vibrational properties of monolayer and bilayer 2D SnTe phases
papers.abstract: The density functional theory (DFT) based first-principles calculations employing the generalized gradient approximation (GGA) with the Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) exchange correlation functional are used to investigate the structural, electronic, optical, thermodynamic, and vibrational properties of monolayer and bilayer phases (α, β, γ, hexa, π) of tin telluride (SnTe). All phases form low-dimensional 2D crystals with bilayer stacking introducing enhanced interlayer coupling that modulates lattice symmetry and stabilizes electronic states. Bond population and charge analyses reveal a mixed ionic-covalent character, with sp³ and sp³d hybridization governing Sn-Te interactions. The π-SnTe monolayer exhibits the strongest covalency, while bilayers uniformly show reduced bond populations and increased ionic contributions. Electronic band structures identify direct band gaps ranging from ~ 0.08 to 1.30 eV in monolayers and narrower or indirect gaps in bilayers. The hexa phase transitions to a metallic state upon bilayer formation, while only the γ-SnTe bilayer and π-SnTe monolayer maintain dynamical stability among the ten investigated configurations. Optical spectra exhibit weak infrared response but pronounced visible and ultraviolet absorption and conductivity, with bilayers generally showing enhanced optical responses and stronger plasmonic features compared with monolayers. Thermodynamic analysis shows that bilayers possess higher heat capacities (up to ≈ 190 Cal·K⁻¹ per cell) and Debye temperatures (≈ 1600 K), indicating enhanced thermal characteristics, while phonon dispersions reveal imaginary modes in most configurations, confirming their dynamical instability. These results provide a comprehensive comparative understanding of layer- and polymorph-dependent properties of SnTe and identify the dynamically stable γ-SnTe bilayer and π-SnTe monolayer as the most relevant configurations for further theoretical and experimental investigation.

papers.title: Factors accounting for the association between belonging to an Indigenous community and child chronic undernutrition in northern Bangladesh: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Indigenous children in Bangladesh experience a disproportionate burden of chronic undernutrition; but the underlying mechanisms contributing to this disparity remain insufficiently understood. This study examined the association between Indigenous identity and child chronic undernutrition and assessed the extent to which modifiable factors statistically account for it. In this cross-sectional study conducted in Godagari Upazila, Rajshahi district, nine Indigenous and nine non-Indigenous villages were randomly selected from a total of 398 villages. A total of 800 children aged 12–59 months (400 per group) were recruited using purposive quota sampling, as household sampling frame was unavailable. Chronic undernutrition was defined as a height-for-age z-score below − 2 standard deviations. Potential mediating factors included child feeding practices, micronutrient supplementation, childhood illness, healthcare-seeking behaviors, and indoor air pollution exposure. Statistical mediation for the binary outcome was assessed using the Baron and Kenny product-of-coefficients approach. Overall, chronic undernutrition affected 25.3% of children, with a substantially higher prevalence among Indigenous children than non-Indigenous children (34.0% vs. 16.7%). After adjustment for potential confounders, Indigenous children had higher odds of chronic undernutrition (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] = 1.81; 95% CI = 1.61, 2.51). Several modifiable factors statistically accounted for part of this association, including, inadequate dietary diversity (18.1%), lack of iodized salt use (8.2%), diarrheal illness (14.2%), incomplete vaccination (12.2%) and reliance on unclean cooking fuel (10.0%). These findings represent are local, cross-sectional associations and should not be interpretated as causal effects or population-representative estimates. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify pathways, and interventions addressing these modifiable factors should be evaluated for their potential to reduce inequalities in child nutrition among Indigenous communities in Bangladesh.

papers.title: Assessment of myocardial iron deficiency and response to iron therapy in heart failure using 3 T cardiac MRI T2 mapping
papers.abstract: While T2* cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) at 1.5 Tesla (T) is well established for assessing myocardial iron overload, T2* mapping at 3 T may be technically challenging due to artifacts. T2 mapping is less susceptible to these limitations, and a strong correlation between T2 and T2* values has been demonstrated in myocardial iron overload; however, the role of T2 mapping in myocardial iron deficiency (ID) remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate the association between myocardial T2 values measured using 3 T CMR and systemic iron status in patients with heart failure (HF) and to assess changes following iron therapy. This prospective study included 58 patients aged ≥ 18 years with HF who underwent CMR. The CMR protocol included multi-echo gradient-spin-echo (mGraSE) T2 mapping, T1 mapping, and late gadolinium enhancement. Serum iron indices were obtained on the day of CMR. Patients with LVEF < 50% and ID received ferric carboxymaltose, with follow-up clinical, laboratory, and CMR assessments. Patients with ID had significantly higher T2 than those without ID (56.8 ± 3.7 ms vs. 52.4 ± 3.5 ms, p < 0.001), with no heterogeneity across HF etiologies or LVEF categories (p-interaction > 0.05). T2 mapping demonstrated good discrimination for ID (AUC, 0.82); a cut-off of ≥ 53.5 ms yielded 85.7% sensitivity and 60.0% specificity. Among 12 patients treated with ferric carboxymaltose, T2 decreased significantly after treatment (57.3 ± 3.6 ms vs. 51.4 ± 3.9 ms, p < 0.001), accompanied by normalization of serum iron indices. In conclusion, in patients with HF, myocardial T2 at 3 T was associated with systemic iron status and decreased following iron repletion, suggesting its potential as a noninvasive marker of myocardial iron status and longitudinal changes following iron therapy.

papers.title: Human SEC23B -deficient hematopoietic stem cell model of CDAII recapitulates erythroid and cell-cycle defects
papers.abstract: Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type II (CDAII) is an inherited disorder affecting red blood cell development. It is caused by mutations in the SEC23B gene, which cause protein hypoglycosylation and morphological alterations in erythroid cells, such as the presence of bi/multinucleated erythroblasts in the patient’s bone marrow. Patients with CDAII suffer from anemia of varying degrees and jaundice, frequently associated with splenomegaly and/or hepatomegaly, and iron overload. A more comprehensive understanding of CDAII is hindered by the limited availability of human disease models that accurately recapitulate its pathophysiology. To address this limitation, we developed a human CDAII model by knocking-out the SEC23B gene in hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs) using gene editing. Edited cells exhibited impaired erythroid differentiation both in vitro and in vivo, characterized by a reduced number of mature erythroid cells and an increase in bi/multinucleated cells. Furthermore, transcriptome analysis revealed alterations in genes associated with erythroid differentiation and cell-cycle regulation, suggesting potential links between these processes in CDAII. This human cellular model successfully recapitulates key features of CDAII and provides a platform for studying disease mechanisms. It also offers a valuable tool for the identification and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies for CDAII.

papers.title: High symptom burden is associated with all-cause mortality in non-dialysis CKD patients: the REACH-J cohort study
papers.abstract: We hypothesized that the KDQOL-36 subscales are associated with all-cause mortality, dialysis initiation, and their composite endpoint in non-dialysis CKD (ND-CKD) patients. We analyzed data from 1,933 patients in the REACH-J Cohort Study (median age: 71 years, eGFR: 23.0 mL/min/1.73 m²). Patients with baseline subscale scores ≤ mean − 1 SD were classified into the ‘subscale-specific high-burden groups’. Outcomes were assessed over a median follow-up of 59.0 months. Multivariable Cox models were adjusted for demographics, eGFR, and comorbidities. During follow-up, 698 patients initiated dialysis and 246 died. While Kaplan–Meier and cumulative incidence analyses for mortality and dialysis initiation, respectively, indicated that a high burden across all subscales was associated with both outcomes, multivariable analysis showed that only the Symptoms subscale was significantly associated with all-cause mortality (HR: 1.90, 95% CI: 1.26–2.85) and the composite endpoint (HR: 1.32, 95% CI: 1.03–1.66). In exploratory item-level analyses, dry skin (HR: 1.50, 95% CI: 1.04–2.17), shortness of breath (HR: 1.60, 95% CI: 1.05–2.44), and nausea/upset stomach (HR: 1.78, 95% CI: 1.07–2.95) showed nominal associations with mortality, representing statistical trends after false discovery rate control (q = 0.095). No subscale was significantly associated with dialysis initiation in the primary fully adjusted cause-specific model. High physical symptom burden is a valuable prognostic indicator for mortality and composite outcomes in ND-CKD. Systematic symptom assessment may be considered for incorporation into routine care to contribute to clinical risk assessment and identify high-risk patients requiring comprehensive supportive care.

papers.title: Secondary flow and hydraulic irreversibility govern the optimal thermohydraulic performance of conical spiral heat exchangers
papers.abstract: The improvement of heat transfer in compact heat exchangers is often accompanied by increased flow resistance, which limits the effectiveness of passive enhancement methods. This study investigates the thermal and hydraulic behavior of a conical spiral heat exchanger equipped with twisted tape inserts and operating with hybrid nanofluids. Particular attention is given to the physical mechanisms governing the balance between secondary-flow enhancement and hydraulic irreversibility. A three-dimensional computational fluid dynamics model was developed using the finite-volume method to examine the combined effects of tube curvature, tape-induced swirl, and fluid thermophysical properties. The numerical results were compared with available experimental data to assess the reliability of the model. Increasing the Dean number strengthened secondary-flow mixing and improved convective heat transfer, but also increased pressure losses. Although the heat transfer coefficient and Nusselt number continued to increase with flow intensity, the most favorable thermohydraulic performance was obtained near a Dean number of 3025. At this operating condition, the reduction in thermal irreversibility was balanced by the increase in frictional losses. Among the investigated configurations, the ZnO–Al₂O₃/water hybrid nanofluid combined with twisted tape provided the highest thermohydraulic performance, with a reported improvement of approximately 37.8% compared with the reference configuration. The main contribution of this study is the identification of an operating regime in which further intensification of secondary flow becomes less beneficial because of the associated hydraulic losses. The findings indicate that maximum heat transfer does not necessarily correspond to optimum thermohydraulic performance and provide a physical basis for evaluating passive enhancement techniques in conical spiral heat exchangers.

papers.title: Gestational age-specific fetal biometry and maternal–fetal Doppler reference trajectories in pregnant Sprague–Dawley rats using a commercial color Doppler ultrasound system
papers.abstract: Commercial ultrasound offers a practical approach to longitudinal assessment of experimental pregnancy when measurements are interpreted against gestational-day-specific reference data. We examined fetal biometry, placental morphology and maternal and fetal Doppler indices daily from gestational day (GD) 7 to GD20 in Sprague–Dawley rats. Thirty dams completed follow-up, comprising 20 dams in the development cohort and 10 in a same-center secondary cohort, with four designated fetal–placental units per dam. Daily medians and empirical measurement ranges were summarized in the development cohort, with uncertainty in means and percentile limits estimated by dam-level bootstrap resampling. Interoperator reproducibility was assessed at GD17, and exploratory gestational-age equations were evaluated by repeated dam-grouped nested cross-validation. Fetal and placental dimensions increased with gestation, while maternal and fetal vascular indices showed distinct temporal patterns. Interoperator intraclass correlation coefficients ranged from 0.890 to 0.920. Cross-validated mean absolute errors for GD7–GD10, GD11–GD15 and GD14–GD20 were 0.545, 0.311 and 0.215 days, respectively. A dam-level spline analysis showed a nonlinear UA PI trajectory across GD11–GD20, with a fitted minimum near GD17; the GD15–GD19 interval was identified post hoc. These study-specific longitudinal measurements and empirical ranges provide a basis for experimental pregnancy assessment under comparable imaging conditions. The dating equations and vascular observations warrant evaluation in independent cohorts and pathological pregnancy models.

papers.title: Temporal molecular features of hepatic injury in mice infected with Echinococcus multilocularis revealed by DIA-based quantitative proteomics
papers.abstract: Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) causes progressive hepatic damage, yet the time-resolved molecular cascades linking metabolic perturbation, immune dysregulation and fibrogenesis remain unclear. This work aimed to delineate dynamic hepatic protein profiles during staged Echinococcus multilocularis(E.multilocularis) infection and identify molecular signatures of progressive liver injury. C57BL/6 mice were divided into sham-operated and E.multilocularis-infected groups, with liver specimens harvested at 1, 3 and 6 months post-infection (early, middle and late stages). Hepatic pathological lesions were assessed via haematoxylin and eosin(H&E) staining. Data-independent acquisition(DIA)-based quantitative proteomics was applied to screen temporally regulated differentially expressed proteins (DEPs). Integrated Gene Ontology(GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes(KEGG) enrichment, Mfuzz clustering, protein-protein interaction(PPI) network, transcription factor profiling and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) were performed to interpret pathway alterations. Temporal expression of core proteins Ahr, Thy1, Rtn4 and Prlr was validated by western blotting and immunofluorescence. Histopathology revealed mild hepatocellular oedema at the early stage, inflammatory cell-encapsulated metacestode vesicles at the middle stage, and extensive progressive hepatic fibrotic remodeling at the late stage. A total of 8537 proteins were identified, including 1140 DEPs, among which 75 proteins showed persistent differential expression across all stages. Early infection was dominated by cytochrome P450-mediated metabolic stress and mitochondrial dysfunction. The middle stage served as a critical transition phase suggesting involvement of Ahr/JAK-STAT signalling, which is associated with immune imbalance and potential onset of fibrogenesis. Sustained chronic inflammation and extracellular matrix remodelling are associated with substantial parenchymal injury in late AE. Thy1 expression rose continuously with disease progression, whereas mean expression levels of Ahr, Rtn4 and Prlr were highest at month 3, with no significant difference compared with month 6, indicating their potential as candidate stage-associated proteins for further biomarker validation.
