This study constructed a full-course time-series hepatic proteomic atlas of E.multilocularis infection and proposed a putative triphasic injury pattern: early mitochondrial metabolic stress, middle-stage Ahr/JAK-STAT-associated immune dysregulation, and late Thy1-associated hepatic fibrogenesis. These temporally resolved omics data support the monitoring of AE progression and the development of targeted therapeutic candidates.

papers.title: Anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic activity of marine sidestream-derived protein hydrolysates and chitosan
papers.abstract: The global fish processing industry generates large volumes of sidestreams that pose environmental and economic challenges. Marine sidestream-derived nutrients have attracted increasing interest due to their reported bioactivity and potential applications in functional foods. However, comparative assessments of materials derived from different fish species and processing technologies to allow selection of ones that are most bioactive to be used as dietary supplements remain limited. In this study, we evaluated the anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic effects of salmon and cod-derived protein hydrolysates as well as chitosan-derived extracts, using in vitro and in vivo models. Biological safety and cytotoxicity were assessed in Caco-2 intestinal epithelial cells and Raw264.7 macrophages. Anti-inflammatory effects were tested in RAW 264.7 macrophages, and the anti-adipogenic activity was evaluated in 3T3-L1 preadipocytes. The results highlighted a subset of extracts with anti-inflammatory and anti-obesity activity. To evaluate their potential bioactivity as nutritional supplements, the most potent extracts were evaluated in a mouse model of high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity and type 2 diabetes. The results demonstrated that marine-derived compounds can mitigate obesity-associated metabolic dysfunction through coordinated effects on adiposity, glucose homeostasis, and inflammatory status. Overall, these findings highlight the potential of marine protein hydrolysates as functional food components and emphasize the importance of processing technologies.

papers.title: Enhancing classification performance on medical datasets using multi-layer perceptron-based feature ranking
papers.abstract: Machine learning (ML) models aim to train on valuable data, where this data is passed through different preprocessing steps. The feature selection methods eliminate irrelevant features, simplify the model, and enhance its generalization. All these aspects effectively improve the model performance, thereby improving the accuracy. Accordingly, the feature selection methodologies are able to enrich the ML models, especially in the medical applications, where balancing performance and efficiency is very essential. Multi-layer perceptron (MLP) is the most common type of neural network that attempts to simulate biological neural networks’ functions. This paper proposes an MLP model as a feature selection strategy to determine the most relevant and significant features for medical datasets. More deeply, this MLP structure uses a bottleneck architecture with geometrically reduced hidden layers, which ensures progressive information compression and improves generalization to ensure a principled and interpretable architecture. The proposed MLP model determines the best subsets (k) of the features based on their accuracy to improve the classification performance. Thereafter, the required time for each (k) value is computed to specify the computational costs. Furthermore, other different classic feature selection methods are implemented, which are Chi-square (chi²), Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), Wrapper, Mutual Information (MI), and Variance thresholding methods. To evaluate the proposed MLP model, Breast Cancer Wisconsin (BCW), Cervical cancer, Parkinson’s, and Prostate cancer datasets are used. The current MLP model achieved an accuracy of 98.25%, 98.26%, 96.61%, and 96.77% for these datasets, respectively. According to these results, the MLP-based method not only delivered superior performance but also provided interpretable, weight-derived feature rankings through determining some features as highly weighted features, aligning with clinical relevance. This work illustrates that MLPs can serve as both high-performance classifiers and intrinsic feature selectors, presenting a powerful, interpretable, and competitive alternative method to traditional ones in medical diagnostic modeling, besides allowing for more informed clinical decisions.

papers.title: Neurofilament light dynamics in critically ill COVID-19 ARDS patients
papers.abstract: Neurological assessment in the intensive care unit (ICU) may benefit from blood-based neurobiomarkers. Neurofilament light (NfL) reflects neuroaxonal injury, but its dynamics in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) are poorly characterised, limiting interpretation of raised levels. In a single-centre cohort of 116 invasively ventilated severe COVID-19 ARDS patients (611 serial plasma NfL samples, median 5 per patient), we modelled the four-week trajectory using linear mixed models, testing whether peak NfL predicted one-year mortality before and after adjustment for age and creatinine, and whether NfL at extubation or discharge approximated peak NfL. Peak NfL was associated with mortality but lost significance after adjustment for age and creatinine, with modest discrimination (AUC 0.61 alone). NfL rose throughout admission, stabilising around day 16 (survivors) and day 21 (non-survivors) and reaching 5–8 standard deviations above age-specific reference values; levels at extubation and discharge approximated peak values in most patients. NfL was not clearly altered by stroke or dialysis in a case series. After accounting for age and renal function, NfL did not independently predict mortality. However it could be regarded as a marker of neuroaxonal injury dynamics; its stability at the accessible discharge timepoint supports prospective study for functional prognosis and guided rehabilitation.

papers.title: Insights into collapsibility and structural behaviors of unsaturated loess from a novel discrete element model
papers.abstract: The existing microscopic contact model based on capillary force can effectively simulate the consolidation and collapsibility behaviors of unsaturated loess under low saturation (≤ 30%), yet it fails to characterize the mechanical responses of loess under high saturation conditions and neglects inter-particle chemical bonding. Therefore, an improved microscopic contact model is proposed considering capillary force for full-range saturation conditions, and chemical bonding force by the secondary development and discrete element method (DEM). After the reliability and accuracy are verified through two-particle single-contact model tests, numerical collapse tests are carried out to explore the multi-factor influences of initial water content, relative compaction and chemical bonding strength on the collapsibility deformation of loess. The results demonstrate that the improved model expands the applicable saturation range and can accurately reproduce the wetting-induced collapsibility characteristics of structured loess. The increase of water content accelerates the attenuation of inter-particle capillary force and the softening of chemical bonding strength, which significantly enhances the collapsibility of loess. Higher relative compaction and stronger chemical bonding can effectively inhibit the collapse deformation of loess. Microscopic mechanism analysis reveals that loess collapse is essentially the structural stability loss caused by the weakening of inter-particle connection under hydro-mechanical-chemical coupling effects. These findings can provide a theoretical basis for macro-micro mechanism analysis of unsaturated loess and the prevention of loess collapsibility hazards in geotechnical engineering.

papers.title: A hybrid AI-blockchain architecture for intelligent zero-trust authentication for large-scale internet of things
papers.abstract: The IoT (Internet of Things) is expanding at a fast pace and one of the biggest security issues is device authentication. Centralized authentication systems have a single point of failure, are not tamper-proof, have no audit trail and unable to detect compromised devices after legitimate registration. In this paper, an authentication framework for IoT that integrates Ethereum’s smart contracts with an XGBoost behavioral classifier is proposed. It is managed through 3 smart contracts, each modular, such as Device Registry, Authentication and Audit that record all authentication events on-chain. Each request for authentication is also created with a challenge from the server, which is signed with the device’s secp256k1 private key, and is just for that request. So that the server can check whether the device has the private key for the registered key, it can test freshness and feature integrity before any inference is performed. The XGBoost model is trained using N-BaIoT traffic from nine physical IoT devices infected by the Mirai and BASHLITE botnets, with Gaussian feature perturbation (α = 1.6) only applied to the training split and 13% label flipping, and scaling, feature selection and hyperparameter selection all fitted on the training split only. The model has a test accuracy of 93.27% and an AUC-ROC of 0.9770 when tested on a clean held-out set. According to the authentication convention where accepting an attack sample is a false acceptance, the False Acceptance Rate (FAR) is 2.67% and the False Rejection Rate (FRR) is 20.27%. A semi-formal BAN logic analysis extracts device key binding, entity authentication and request freshness, server authentication and device-signed non-repudiation, depending on the explicit assumptions. Behavioral assessment is treated as a probabilistic risk signal outside the BAN logic. An adaptive trust scoring controlled ablation demonstrates that the number of requests that the attacker gets approved against a persistently compromised device drops to 0.11 per 1,000 requests, while occasionally hard-penalizing benign devices depends on the penalty setting. The differences in accuracy from the six baselines (Random Forest, SVM, Autoencoder, LightGBM, a multilayer perceptron and Isolation Forest) are statistically significant (Paired t-tests, P < 0.05) and 5-fold stratified cross validation resulted in an accuracy of 93.27% ± 0.20%. With a local Ganache network, an authentication cycle takes 210,408 gas (USD 8.42 at 20 Gwei and ETH = USD 2,000), end-to-end latency of 35.61 ms and 125.8 authentications per second with 20 concurrent devices. A set of 20 device identities (nine physical N-BaIoT devices and eleven synthetic variants that are leveraged just for load generation) are used in system-level experiments. The findings reveal (1) how the design can be implemented on permissioned blockchains (where the transaction fee is zero), and (2) the cost and usage compromises it must accept.

papers.title: Dynamic state transition model-based prognosis approach for degradation prediction of aerial bundled cables
papers.abstract: Aerial bundled cables (ABCs) consist of several cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE)-insulated phase conductors twisted together with a neutral conductor. Moisture that penetrates the insulation, together with electrical loading and thermal cycling, initiates insulation degradation, so timely maintenance requires methods that predict the future health state from the current one. In this work, the insulation degradation of in-service ABCs is monitored with infrared thermography, and a thermal degradation parameter (TDP, °C/A) is computed at every measurement instant. A particle filter (PF) is used to predict future TDP values. Conventional PF prognostic models keep the parameters of the state transition density fixed over the whole monitoring period; this work extends them by re-estimating the shape parameter of a Weibull transition density by maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) at every prediction instant. The method is evaluated on 90 weeks of TDP data from six segments of two in-service cable spans, over 30 independent runs, against fixed-parameter PF models, Gaussian process regression (GPR) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network. The adaptive model reduces the one-step RMSE by 42% relative to the exponential transition model and by 26% relative to the best fixed Weibull model (Diebold–Mariano p < 0.02), with RMSEs of 0.0206, 0.0320 and 0.0472 °C/A for one-, two- and three-week horizons. GPR and LSTM are more accurate one week ahead, whereas the adaptive PF has the lowest three-week error, although these differences are not statistically significant. The weekly TDP series analysed and the Python implementation are released with the paper.

papers.title: Parameter-space exploration of transitions between bounded and divergent regimes in a cubic–quintic oscillator
papers.abstract: This paper explores the nonlinear dynamics of a parameter-varied cubic-quintic dynamical system as a function of the governing parameters $$\alpha _1, \alpha _2, \alpha _3, \alpha _4$$ within the range $$[-2.0, 2.0]$$. A systematic computational scheme is proposed for the exploration of the parameter space, the identification of statistically distinguishable trajectories, the characterization of the vector field through its Jacobian at a prescribed reference state, and complementary nonlinear dynamics diagnostics. Analytical tools such as time-domain responses, phase portraits, power spectral density analysis, trajectory sampling, and bifurcation diagrams are used to characterize the nonlinear dynamics of the system, while Jacobian eigenvalues at the selected reference state characterize the local linear form of the vector field at that point. Since the system possesses a first integral, regular bounded non-equilibrium trajectories are periodic, and neither chaotic nor quasi-periodic dynamics can occur. The proposed methodology allows for the individual influence of each governing parameter on the system dynamics to be systematically isolated and quantified by applying consistent numerical and statistical classification criteria across the investigated parameter space. The framework characterizes the behavior of the system as a function of parameters by integrating statistical trajectory analysis, local linearized behavior, and representative nonlinear dynamical analyses. The results show that the governing parameters play an important role in the dynamical behavior of the system. In particular, the fraction of diverging trajectories increases from $$0\%$$ to $$50\%$$ as $$\alpha _2$$ is varied from $$-2$$ to 2; qualitative changes in the local linear structure occur only near the stability boundary $$\alpha _1=2.25\alpha _2$$. Statistical trajectory classification is used to identify regions of distinct observed dynamical behavior, while the eigenvalue analysis characterizes the corresponding Jacobian-based characterization at the prescribed reference state. The proposed framework offers a systematic, reproducible, and efficient approach for the characterization of nonlinear multi-dimensional parameter spaces and is easily extendable to the investigation of more complex nonlinear systems.

papers.title: Unveiling Alzheimer’s disease in subjective cognitive decline: a multimodal characterization integrating plasma biomarkers, cognition and empathy
papers.abstract: Subjective Cognitive Decline (SCD) is a heterogeneous condition that, when associated with Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology, may represent the earliest clinical expression of the disease. We investigated whether SCD associated with AD pathology is characterized by a multidimensional biological, cognitive, and socio-emotional profile. Ninety-seven SCD patients underwent CSF biomarkers and/or amyloid-PET and were classified as with (Core1 +) or without (Core1-) evidence of AD pathology according to the 2024 Alzheimer’s Association criteria. Demographic, neuropsychological, and emotional assessments were collected. Plasma p-tau217, p-tau181, NfL, and GFAP were quantified. Machine-learning (ML) models were used to predict AD pathology as an exploratory integrative approach. Core1 + patients were older and showed subtle, normal-range inefficiencies in memory and executive functions, together with informant-rated changes in Perspective Taking and Personal Distress. Plasma p-tau217 showed the strongest discrimination of Core1 status (AUC = 0.89). A two-cutoff strategy identified a gray zone in 24.67% of participants, with reflex p-tau181 correctly classifying 78.57% of cases. The multimodal ML model achieved an AUC of 0.83 (similar to plasma-only model AUC 0.81), with plasma biomarkers, executive and empathy-related features among top predictors. Plasma p-tau217 emerged as the strongest discriminator, while cognitive and socio-emotional features contributed to delineating the phenotype of SCD associated with AD.

papers.title: Effects of high dietary inclusion of black soldier fly larvae meal on the serum metabolome of healthy adult dogs
papers.abstract: The escalating global demand for animal protein has increased interest in sustainable alternatives for pet nutrition, with black soldier fly larvae meal (BSFL) emerging as a promising nutrient-rich ingredient. As unconventional ingredients are increasingly used in pet food, understanding their systemic metabolic effects is important. This study investigated the effects of including partially defatted BSFL meal at levels corresponding to 0%, 50%, and 100% replacement of poultry viscera meal on the serum metabolome of six healthy adult dogs (mean age 5.3 ± 1.03 years; mean body weight 23.0 ± 2.7 kg) over 22-day experimental periods, using a double Latin square design. Serum metabolomic analysis was performed using one-dimensional ¹H nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, followed by principal component analysis (PCA) and pathway analysis. A total of 40 serum metabolites were identified, and individual metabolite concentrations did not differ among dietary treatments (P > 0.05 for all metabolites). PCA also showed substantial overlap among treatments, with no clear separation between dietary groups. Pathway analysis identified glyoxylate and dicarboxylate metabolism; glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism; alanine, aspartate, and glutamate metabolism; and phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthesis as pathways meeting the statistical criteria applied in the analysis. However, these pathway-analysis results should be interpreted cautiously because none of the individual metabolite concentrations differed among dietary treatments. Overall, high dietary inclusion of partially defatted BSFL meal did not induce detectable alterations in the serum metabolomic profile of healthy adult dogs under the short-term conditions evaluated. These findings suggest short-term serum metabolomic stability following BSFL inclusion, although larger and longer-term studies are warranted to confirm these results and further evaluate its use as an alternative protein ingredient in dog nutrition.

Palladium modified carbon dots and their application in photocatalytic aerobic selective oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde
papers.abstract: Selective aerobic oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde is a highly desirable but challenging transformation because most reported catalysts suffer from limited toluene conversion and poor control over over-oxidation. Herein, palladium-modified carbon dots (Pd/CDs) are introduced as an efficient heterogeneous photocatalyst for this reaction. N-doped carbon dots were first synthesized from citric acid and ethylenediamine by a hydrothermal method and then functionalized with 1,10-phenanthroline-2,9-diamine to anchor Pd species. The resulting Pd/CDs catalyst (Pd loading: 4.28 wt%) was characterized by FT-IR, PXRD, XPS, EDS, WDX, SEM, TEM, DR-UV-vis, TGA, DSC, and ICP-OES. Under sunlight and aerobic conditions, the optimized system (50 mg catalyst, under sunlight and aerobic conditions without additional organic solvent, 3 h) achieved 93% toluene conversion and approximately 100% benzaldehyde selectivity. The catalyst also converted various substituted toluenes and xylenes into the corresponding aldehydes with high selectivity. Control experiments and scavenging studies revealed that the high surface area and electrical conductivity of carbon dots, combined with Pd active sites, promote efficient charge separation and generate reactive oxygen species and holes, which are responsible for the selective oxidation. The catalyst retained its activity and selectivity over ten consecutive runs, with only a slight decrease in the Pd content of the recovered solid. This work provides a sustainable route for solar-driven selective C–H oxidation and offers a basis for designing advanced photocatalysts for fine chemical synthesis.

papers.title: Neural signatures of cannabis use: associations with brain aging and cognitive function via functional connectivity
papers.abstract: Cognitive aging is a major concern in middle-aged and older adults, and functional brain networks implicated in aging partially overlap with those involving the endocannabinoid system. However, the relationships among cannabis use, brain aging, and cognition remain incompletely understood. Using large data from more than 23,000 UK Biobank participants, we examined associations among lifetime cannabis use, normative aging, cognitive performance, and whole-brain functional network connectivity (FNC). Adopting a connectome-wide, pattern-based framework, we quantified the spatial correspondence between cannabis-, age-, and cognition-related FNC effects. Lifetime cannabis use and normative aging were associated with systematically related but opposing FNC patterns, particularly involving subcortical–sensorimotor and subcortical–cerebellar networks. Lifetime cannabis use was also associated with differences in cognitive performance across multiple domains, and the corresponding FNC patterns showed positive spatial correspondence with cognition-related effects. Collectively, cannabis-related FNC patterns showed inverse spatial correspondence with age-related patterns and positive spatial correspondence with cognition-related patterns, providing a large-scale characterization of population-level associations among lifetime cannabis use, functional brain organization, and cognition in middle-to-late adulthood. These findings should be interpreted as population-level associations rather than evidence of causal or dose-dependent effects of cannabis use.

papers.title: Geometric and evolutionary deep learning prioritizes GPCR ligand interactions across the human metabolome
papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) are major drug targets, yet many orphan GPCRs lack well-characterized endogenous ligands, limiting the understanding of their physiological roles and therapeutic exploration. Here we show that G-LEAP, a deep learning framework integrating receptor sequence information with three-dimensional ligand structures, prioritizes receptor–ligand interactions. It performs well under random splits and when ligands or receptors are held out, and outperforms representative prior methods in paired comparisons. G-LEAP distinguishes active ligands from physicochemically matched decoys and rejects misleading docking hits in an independent test. Screening naturally occurring metabolites yields a catalog of more than 120 million predicted receptor–metabolite pairs, ranks known interactions highly, and identifies candidates for poorly characterized receptors. Structural modeling, molecular dynamics simulations, and tissue co-expression analyses support selected predictions. These results position G-LEAP as a scalable computational screening framework that generates testable GPCR–metabolite interaction hypotheses prior to pharmacological mode-of-action characterization, such as agonism versus antagonism.

papers.title: Identification of PUFA interaction site on ASIC3 suggests a complex regulatory mechanism
papers.abstract: Inflammatory mediators including polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) potentiate ASIC3 by altering channel gating, yet the molecular basis for their interactions remains poorly defined. Using all-atom Molecular Dynamics (MD) simulations and electrophysiology, we show that DHA accumulates around ASIC3 through interactions with a membrane-facing electropositive region along the outer leaflet of TM1. In the open state, a more buried binding site for the lipid is exposed that allows the carboxylate head group to bind a critical arginine along with nearby polar residues. Mutation of this site eliminates the DHA-mediated slowing of channel desensitization and also modestly reduces the effect PUFAs have on the proton sensitivity of channel activation. The same mutations do not prevent regulation by other lipid classes like N-acyl amino acids or lysophosphatidyl choline. Our results provide the first detailed description of a PUFA binding site on ASICs, offering new insights into lipid modulation and potential strategies for developing novel treatments for inflammatory pain.

papers.title: Integrating multilayered regulatory networks in grass rhizome development
papers.abstract: Rhizomes are specialized underground stems that enable vegetative propagation and perennial growth in many grasses. Despite extensive studies on their molecular mechanisms, current knowledge remains fragmented and an integrated framework for rhizome formation is still needed. Here, we synthesize recent advances in physiology, genetics, and multi-omics, using the wild rice Oryza longistaminata as a model system. We highlight the roles of plant hormones and conserved genetic modules that coordinate the balance between vegetative and sexual reproduction to construct a multi-layered, testable framework. These insights offer a foundation for developing resilient perennial crops to enhance sustainable agriculture.

papers.title: Comprehensive synthesis of K48/K63 ubiquitin pentamers by graph-empowered automation
papers.abstract: Linear, branched and heterotypic ubiquitin (Ub) chains regulate essential cellular processes, yet their structural and functional analysis remains limited by the difficulty of preparing defined, homogeneous samples. Here we establish a fully automated platform for the comprehensive synthesis of all 56 K48/K63-linked Ub tetramers and pentamers, by iterative cycles of K48- or K63-specific chemoenzymatic conjugations of chemically synthesized Ub monomers bearing a fast-cleaving lysine protecting group compatible with folded proteins. A graph-based digital encoding of Ub chain topologies enabled systematic enumeration and filtering of reaction pathways, guiding the selection of synthetic routes. This computational system generates reagent maps and executable code to direct iterative deprotection and conjugation cycles on a standard, laboratory liquid-handling robot. All 14 Ub tetramers and 42 Ub pentamers were obtained with high fidelity, as validated by SDS–PAGE and mass spectrometry. This work establishes a general framework for automated protein conjugate synthesis and provides access to the complete space of K48/K63 branched ubiquitin chains. The combinatorial space of ubiquitin chains hampers their preparation and study. Now, synthetic and computational tools have been developed for comprehensive access to all 56 K48/K63-linked ubiquitin tetramers and pentamers. This work uses advances in the chemical synthesis of selectively protected ubiquitin monomers, graph-based encoding of ubiquitin chains, and automated procedures.

papers.title: The power of O vacancies in electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Non-stoichiometric oxide materials are essential to chemistry, but controlling their synthesis towards a tuneable number of unpaired electrons trapped in the oxygen vacancies remains challenging. Now, a new synthetic strategy leveraging template chemicals renders these materials available for electron-driven electrocatalytic selectivity.

papers.title: Binuclear copper enzymes enable selective radical (pseudo)halogenation
papers.abstract: Synthetically valuable new-to-nature reactions in copper enzymes remain largely underexploited in chemical synthesis. Now, the combination of binuclear copper enzymes and a photoredox catalyst can efficiently perform enantioselective decarboxylative (pseudo)halogenation starting from redox-active esters.

papers.title: Integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance for high-resolution tracking of measles virus evolution and transmission
papers.abstract: Measles outbreaks have surged globally, challenging surveillance and control efforts. In South Africa, the 2024−2025 measles outbreak led to nearly 4,000 reported cases, triggering a nationwide vaccination campaign. However, tracking measles virus (MeV; species Morbillivirus hominis) transmission and evolution remains difficult at scale, particularly in settings with limited access to care, diagnostic testing and sequencing capacity. Wastewater can enable population-scale virus surveillance, but low MeV concentrations limit detection sensitivity and sequencing quality. Here we show that overcoming these technical challenges enables integrated wastewater and clinical genomic surveillance that expands the coverage and resolution of MeV monitoring. We developed a virus concentration and whole-genome sequencing (WGS) workflow and applied it to 4,502 wastewater samples collected across all nine provinces of South Africa during the 2024−2025 outbreak. Wastewater MeV genotype prevalence tracked clinical estimates, and phylogenetic analyses combining wastewater and clinical sequences revealed geographically structured transmission and previously undetected inter-provincial spread. WGS recovered transmission links not captured by the field standard approach, which targets a 450-nucleotide region of the nucleoprotein gene (N450), highlighting the importance of WGS to accurately characterize transmission dynamics. Our study provides a cost-effective and scalable genomic surveillance approach to support measles control and elimination. Whole-genome sequencing and phylogenetic analyses of wastewater and surveillance samples during the 2024−2025 measles outbreak in South Africa reveal previously undetected inter-provincial spread and transmission links, suggesting that wastewater-integrated whole-genome surveillance can improve measles monitoring and control efforts.

papers.title: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain–computer interfaces over a 20-year period
papers.abstract: The silicon microelectrode ‘Utah’ array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain–computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants. On average, arrays successfully recorded neural spiking waveforms on 35.6% of electrodes, with a modest 7 percentage point decline over the recording period (up to 7.3 years). Using a ‘decoding signal-to-noise ratio’ (dSNR) metric, we found that 11 of 14 arrays provided meaningful movement decoding throughout participation (median dSNR >1), with three achieving >70% accuracy compared with able-bodied mouse control. We also found that dSNR increased approximately logarithmically with the number of electrodes, providing a pathway for scaling performance. While longevity exceeded previous nonhuman primate studies, achieving peak performance consistently may require further improvements. Utah arrays recorded stable spiking activity for up to 7.3 years, with modest signal decline on average and sustained movement decoding in the majority of arrays analyzed, demonstrating the long-term feasibility of intracortical brain–computer interfaces.

papers.title: Antimicrobial living double-layer skin dressing for inflammation reduction and skin barrier restoration to alleviate Malassezia-induced skin damage
papers.abstract: Microecological imbalance associated with Malassezia overgrowth is closely related to the pathogenesis of diverse cutaneous disorders. However, conventional antifungal therapies face critical challenges, including pathogen resistance induction and inflammation exacerbation. To address these, developing safe and effective biological therapies is crucial for managing Malassezia-associated dermatitis. Here, a double-layer skin dressing is designed to efficiently inhibit Malassezia and mitigate Malassezia-induced skin inflammation in mice. The lower layer comprises Paenibacillus polymyxa JWYB12, which inhibits M. restricta, and the upper layer is a hydrogel composed of Pluronic F-127, polydopamine (PDA), anti-inflammatory exopolysaccharide EPS1, and oxygen-producing Spirulina (SP). Temperature elevation from 4 °C to 37 °C triggers rapid gelation and robust skin adhesion of the upper layer. SP-mediated oxygen production significantly upregulates energy metabolism genes, thereby enhancing JWYB12 proliferation, while EPS1 exerts a synergistic growth-promoting effect. Collectively, the upper layer markedly augments JWYB12 abundance and its inhibitory activity against M. restricta. In murine models, the dressing significantly reduces dermatitis scores and epidermal thickness, alleviates inflammation via cytokine downregulation, and restores skin barrier function by upregulating barrier proteins, thus effectively controlling M. restricta-induced inflammation. These properties make this double-layer skin dressing an effective clinical treatment for Malassezia-induced dermatitis, presenting a promising biological therapy strategy for pathogen-associated dermatoses.

papers.title: An in situ redox-converted molecule for all-perovskite tandem solar cells
papers.abstract: All-perovskite tandem solar cells (TSCs) are gaining prominence due to their ability to surpass the efficiency limit of single-junction perovskite solar cells (PSCs)1,2. However, the efficiency and stability of all-perovskite TSCs are limited by chemical instability at the hole transport layer/perovskite interface in the tin-lead (Sn-Pb) narrow-bandgap subcell, which introduces deep trap states from tin cations and promotes non-radiative recombination3-5. Here we incorporate a redox-converted molecule of p-aminobenzohydrazide (ABH) into poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) that neutralizes PSS acidity, heals Sn4+ defects, and generates a dipole passivation effect upon oxidation. During the preparation of Sn-Pb perovskites, ABH suppresses interfacial oxidation by reducing Sn4+ defects and converts to p-aminobenzaldehyde (ABD), which suppresses photogenerated hole-induced Sn2+ oxidation, aligning energy levels for efficient hole extraction. The in situ redox-converted molecule stabilizes the buried interface during both device fabrication and operation, reduces non-radiative recombination and enhances stability. The resulting narrow-bandgap Sn-Pb PSC achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.4% (certified 25.2%) with an open-circuit voltage of 0.92 V and a fill factor of 83.4%. Integrated into monolithic all-perovskite TSCs, the device delivers a PCE of 31.1% (certified 30.8%) together with enhanced thermal (ISOS-D-2I, 85 °C) and operational stability (ISOS-L-1I) under inert conditions.

papers.title: An enduring climatic burden from past peatland drainage
papers.abstract: Over millennia, peatlands have removed hundreds of gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (CO2) from the atmosphere but emitted a proportion back as methane (CH4), exerting a slow net cooling effect1. Artificial drainage of these ecosystems—a centuries-old practice2,3—causes decomposition and the re-release of CO2 but suppresses CH4 emissions4, with a net climatic effect that is not well quantified at the global scale5. Here we reconstructed the radiative forcing from worldwide peatland drainage over 1800–2020 by combining a new flux dataset, hydrologically driven models of CO2 and CH4 fluxes and a hindcast of drainage extent and intensity. We found that drainage has produced a net heating effect of +73 (48–99) mW m−2—equivalent to 2.7 (1.8–3.6)% of industrial-era radiative forcing—originating from 0.4–0.5% of global land area. The net heating results from the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions (+83 (52–110) mW m−2) over that of avoided CH4 emissions (−9 (−15–−2) mW m−2). Even without further expansion of drainage, maintaining currently drained areas could almost double the cumulative warming by 2100. Our reconstruction captures the opposing impacts of peatland drainage on global budgets of CO2 and CH4 and quantifies the strong legacy effects of historical drainage on present and possibly future climate. Reconstruction of radiative forcing resulting from worldwide peatland drainage over the past two centuries reveals a persistent net warming effect caused by the dominant forcing of drainage-induced CO2 emissions over that of avoided CH4 emissions.

papers.title: Single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map for coronary artery disease
papers.abstract: Although coronary artery disease (CAD) genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified hundreds of loci, most variants lie in non-coding regions, obscuring the causal gene programmes and cell types driving disease1,2. Here we performed single-nucleus multi-omic profiling of gene expression and chromatin accessibility in human coronary arteries from 44 people to construct a genome-wide single-cell variant-to-enhancer-to-gene map. We identified 11,269 chromatin accessibility quantitative trait loci (caQTLs) across principal vascular cell types, including CAD-associated caQTLs in smooth muscle cells (SMCs). Using dynamic single-cell caQTL modelling3, we show that variant effects on chromatin vary across SMC states. For example, rs658956 -mediated suppression of the FGGY-DT enhancer through disruption of an AP-1 motif is amplified as SMCs transition towards a fibromyocyte fate. We next performed genome-wide high-throughput chromosome conformation capture (Hi-C) in 15 human coronary arteries, showing that rs4887091 in the ADAMTS7 CAD locus has allele-dependent effects on CCCTC-binding factor occupancy and loop strength. Integrating Hi-C, Hi-C with chromatin immunoprecipitation and in vitro clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats interference (CRISPRi) nominated AMOTL2 as a distal SMC-specific CAD gene whose loss promotes proliferation and suppresses contractile identity. Finally, arrayed Perturb–seq of GWAS-nominated enhancers converged on extracellular matrix remodelling as a core SMC disease programme. Together, these findings provide a framework for mapping non-coding GWAS variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease. A multi-omic gene-expression and chromatin-accessibility map of human coronary artery disease provides a framework for mapping disease-associated genetic variants to cell types, chromatin states and gene programmes in human disease.

papers.title: Heterogeneity co-evolves with architecture to determine colon cancer outcome
papers.abstract: Intratumoural heterogeneity, originating from genetic, epigenetic and phenotypic diversity, is pervasive in cancer and a fundamental barrier to curative treatment1,2. How these heterogeneous cell states emerge and co-evolve within tumours remains poorly understood. Here we develop a deep-learning framework that quantifies colorectal cancer tissue architecture and nuclear morphology at subcellular resolution to predict patient outcome. Integrating this with spatial transcriptomics, multiplex immunofluorescence and patient-derived organoids, we identify a co-evolutionary relationship between tumour architecture and cancer cell states. We identify architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer that drive cell state diversification by promoting distinct cancer stem cell programmes. Specifically, tissue fragmentation generates compressive forces that activate YAP, suppressing classical stem cell programmes and inducing fetal/regenerative stem cell states that initially manifest as hybrid states with features of partial epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT). Subsequent tumour–stroma communication through TGFβ diversifies these into distinct stem cell and EMT states. Reciprocally, β-catenin activity tunes tumour cell responsiveness to architectural cues. Collectively, this work identifies a feedforward loop between cell states and tissue architecture that drives cancer heterogeneity and cell state diversification. Machine-learning-based analyses harness this co-dependency, independently of mutational status or cancer stage, to predict patient outcome. Architectural interfaces in colorectal cancer drive cell state diversification through mechanochemical reprogramming of stem cell identities.

papers.title: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut–brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop—a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut–brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states. In flies, sugar-sensing enteric neurons activate brain neurons that inhibit crop duct motor neurons, relaxing the foregut muscles to facilitate food transfer to the crop, which sustains ingestion and regulates food intake.

papers.title: Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing
papers.abstract: Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1–7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10–12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of $${\mathcal{O}}(1)$$ operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems. Quantum confocal microscopy enables deterministic preparation of high-photon-number Fock-like states with up to 500 photons, reducing photon-number variance by 21.5 dB and achieving record displacement-sensing precision 19.2 dB beyond the standard quantum limit.

papers.title: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST
papers.abstract: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST). Structural determination was enabled by zero-shot computational redesign of TnsA, which enhanced integration activity by nearly two orders of magnitude without compromising specificity. The structure of the holo integration complex reveals the conformational licensing events that govern activation of the integration machinery at the on-target site. Multiple components (Cascade–TniQ, TnsC and TnsA–TnsB) undergo conformational changes upon assembly into the holo integration complex, and the catalytically competent state is stabilized only within the full assembly. Comparison with existing CAST integration complex structures reveals conserved architectural features, suggesting a common molecular basis for RNA-guided transposition across CASTs. Our findings establish a general mechanistic framework for RNA-guided DNA integration and demonstrate that protein design is a powerful strategy for engineering highly active CAST systems. RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) is enhanced by redesigned TnsA and a holo complex whose coordinated conformational licensing reveals a conserved mechanistic framework for engineering highly active CASTs.

papers.title: Middle–Late Pleistocene Denisovans and unresolved Homo in southern China
papers.abstract: Molecular and morphological evidence increasingly supports the view that most East Asian Middle to Late Pleistocene archaic Homo belong to Denisovans1, yet the presence of other contemporaneous lineages has remained unclear. Here we report a set of newly discovered hominin fossils (4 isolated teeth; more than 100.8 thousand years ago and 104.5–42.6 thousand years ago, respectively) from 2 cave sites (Chuanshandong and Longchuandong) in Guangxi, southern China. Integrated morphological and palaeoproteomic analyses reveal substantial phenotypic and molecular diversity consistent with at least two distinct lineages. One lineage (Longchuandong) is assigned to a Denisovan-affinity population, owing to its extreme similarity to Altai Denisovans with respect to dental morphology and single amino acid polymorphisms that match those of Denisovans from Harbin, Penghu, Bianfu Cave and Altai. The other lineage, represented by the Chuanshandong hominin, is an unresolved archaic Homo, as it carries an ancestral variant (AMELY 179M) shared with Homo antecessor and great apes and another variant (AMBN 253G) that is diagnostic of East Asian Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus but lacks the Denisovan-associated AMBN 273V variant (it being highly probable that this is inherited from H. erectus). Dental morphology in this lineage exhibits a mosaic of plesiomorphic and derived traits but no clear Denisovan affinity. These findings indicate that diverse hominin populations may have inhabited subtropical China during the Middle and Late Pleistocene, including a Denisovan-affinity population and another unresolved archaic Homo. Dental morphology and proteomic analyses of fossils from southern China identify lineages with and without Denisovan affinity, indicating the diversity of hominin populations in this region in the Middle to Late Pleistocene.

papers.title: Sustainable cement production via a liquid-phase pathway
papers.abstract: Slowing climate change requires overcoming inertia in political, technological and geophysical systems1–3. Portland cement manufacturing is among the most challenging industrial processes to decarbonize, yet it remains indispensable for building the infrastructure underpinning the low-carbon transition4,5. Here, building beyond the two-century-old conventional cement process6, we report a route that creates sustainable cement, by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds. Our technique generates localized temperatures up to 2,400 °C, sufficient to liquefy the raw materials. These liquid-phase reactions promote elemental mixing and solidification, producing reactive clinker phases. Our in situ transmission electron microscopy captures the early-stage cement hydration process in real time, revealing that surface disorder accelerates clinker reactivity by facilitating the dynamic nucleation and growth of hydration clusters. Beyond typical limestone and clay feedstocks, we show that hydrated cement paste from waste concrete can also be processed into clinkers, meeting ordinary Portland cement specifications. By coupling circular resource use with ultrafast electrified processing, our approach enables sustainable, low-cost cement production at scale. Sustainable cement production can be achieved by accelerating its reaction kinetics through a microwave carbon-plasma method, reducing the standard processing time from hours to seconds.

papers.title: Context-dependent response of endothelial cells to PIK3CA mutation
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated mutations in PIK3CA underlie congenital overgrowth disorders that frequently involve the vasculature1,2. Among the affected tissues, the endothelium commonly exhibits aberrant expansion, leading to vascular malformations3. Notably, these lesions arise predominantly in veins and capillaries, whereas arteries are largely spared, for reasons that remain unclear. Here, using genetic lineage tracing, we show that endothelial expression of PIK3CAH1047R drives profound clonal expansion of capillary and venous endothelial cells, whereas mature arterial endothelial cells are refractory to pathological PI3K activation. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features, providing a mechanistic explanation for the paucity of arterial lesions after PIK3CA genetic perturbation. Mechanistically, these effects are mediated by two complementary downstream branches of PI3K signalling: increased proliferation, which drives vascular overgrowth, and upregulation of the venous-specifying transcription factor NR2F2 (also known as COUP-TFII), which suppresses arterial differentiation. Together, our findings reveal that pathogenic responses to PIK3CAH1047R are dictated by endothelial differentiation state and fate trajectory, and demonstrate that arterial endothelium is intrinsically resistant to oncogenic PI3K signalling. Arteries are therefore shielded from PIK3CA mutations, explaining the rarity of arterial malformations in PIK3CA-driven disease. Expression of PIK3CAH1047R in arterial precursors disrupts arterial differentiation and promotes the acquisition of venous features.

papers.title: Enzymatic living polymerization for polysaccharide synthesis
papers.abstract: Polysaccharides have myriad functions throughout biological processes, yet synthetic access to well-defined analogues remains a challenge1,2. Achieving high molecular weight, controlled stereochemistry and sequence precision simultaneously has been elusive using conventional chemical methods that rely on protecting-group manipulations. Here we propose enzymatic living polymerization, which enables the precision preparation of natural polysaccharides with molecular weights up to 660 kg mol−1 but polydispersity from low to less than 1.05. Such a living behaviour originates from the initiator weakly binding with the polymerase, realizing fast equilibrium of the active (bound) and dormant (unbound) species, as demonstrated by mechanistic and computational studies. Our approach is generalizable to diverse polysaccharide types, including sequence-controlled block copolymers, and provides a modular route to explore molecular-weight-dependent biological functions of natural polysaccharides. An enzymatic method for making high-molecular-weight polysaccharides in a way similar to synthetic polymerization techniques, rather than biosynthetically, is presented.

papers.title: Coherent parity oscillations in coupled minimal Kitaev chains
papers.abstract: Majorana zero modes provide a route to fault-tolerant qubits by encoding information non-locally in fermion parity. Their noise sensitivity is expected to decrease exponentially with separation between Majorana zero modes, a suppression known as topological protection1. Kitaev chains in quantum-dot–superconductor arrays can host Majorana zero modes at their ends1,2, even in two-site chains3. These minimal-chain modes, known as poor man’s Majoranas, retain characteristic Majorana properties, including near-zero energy and equal electron–hole character, but lack topological protection3–5. A key challenge is moving from identifying these modes in electrical transport to coherent qubit control. Here we demonstrate coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains3,6–8. Total fermion parity conservation separates the system into global even- and odd-parity manifolds. We observe coherent parity oscillations in both, with frequencies matching within 5% at the poor man’s Majorana sweet spot, consistent with largely isolated Majoranas6. The oscillation frequency, rotation axis and coherence depend systematically on inter-chain coupling and quantum-dot detunings, in agreement with our model for short chains. Our results establish coherent control of a qubit encoded in the fermion parity of Majorana zero modes, realized using minimal Kitaev chains. They lay the groundwork for universal qubit operations, comprehensive coherence characterization and probing protection in longer chains. Coherent time-resolved rotations between parity states encoded by four poor man’s Majoranas are demonstrated in two coupled minimal Kitaev chains, providing a foundation for topologically protected qubits in longer chains.

papers.title: Transcription from megabase-scale heterochromatin generates neural barcodes
papers.abstract: Heterochromatin typically represses genes1,2, yet some genes paradoxically require it for activation3–7. How can the same chromatin environment both silence and promote transcription? Here we address this question by interrogating the clustered protocadherin (Pcdh) locus, where subsets of genes are stochastically expressed while most remain silent8. In neurons, stochastic and combinatorial expression of Pcdh genes generates unique cell-surface barcodes required for self–non-self discrimination and neural circuit assembly8. By combining RNA labelling of Pcdh genes and neurodevelopmental cell types with single-molecule chromatin tracing and stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy, we find that a compact heterochromatin domain containing Pcdh genes forms as these genes become activated during development. Pcdh transcription occurs within the compact domain and reads through downstream genes, and distal enhancers must access the domain to engage target promoters. Genetic perturbations in mice suggest that opposing genome folding forces cooperate to establish Pcdh locus architecture and promote stochastic Pcdh expression. Specifically, while DNA loop extrusion allows enhancers to breach heterochromatin and find target promoters, heterochromatin-driven compartmentalization supports an expanded enhancer–promoter search space. These findings shed light on a process foundational to the development of vertebrate nervous systems and suggest a mechanism for how transcription can occur within seemingly silent chromatin environments. Interrogation of the clustered protocadherin locus shows an unexpected ability of genes to transcribe within a seemingly silent chromatin environment.

papers.title: Structural basis of RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CAST systems
papers.abstract: CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) achieve site-specific DNA integration by combining the RNA-guided targeting action of a nuclease-deficient CRISPR–Cas system with the assembly of a Tn7-like transpososome complex1,2. Understanding the detailed mechanisms of this elaborate process is paramount to engineering CAST systems into programmable genetic tools3–6. Type I-F Pseudoalteromonas CAST (PseCAST) shows the highest activity in mammalian cells so far7 and has been adapted extensively through directed evolution8. However, its continued rational engineering requires addressing critical gaps in our understanding of transpososome assembly and activation9. Here we perform structural analyses using cryogenic electron microscopy, validated by DNA transposition assays, to visualize the PseCAST system in a series of functional states that define the stepwise mechanism of RNA-guided DNA integration. The structures of the PseCAST targeting and transposase recruitment complexes revealed that conformational changes in the Cascade–TniQ module, induced by R-loop formation, are associated with target-DNA stabilization and TnsC heptamerization. This, in turn, results in the recruitment of the TnsAB transposase by conserved interactions with the carboxy-terminal tail of TnsB. Finally, the structure of the 1.2 MDa PseCAST transpososome holocomplex revealed allosteric coupling of TnsC–TnsB and TnsB–target-DNA interactions to the conformational remodelling of the TnsB catalytic site, activating donor-DNA integration. Together, these findings establish a unified mechanistic blueprint for RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CASTs and provide a structural framework to guide their engineering for genome-editing applications. Structural analyses reveal the mechanism underlying RNA-guided DNA integration by type I CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) and provide a framework for developing CASTs into site-specific genome-editing tools.

papers.title: An extremophile transgene improves drought resistance and yield in cereals
papers.abstract: Drought is a major environmental constraint limiting global crop production1,2. On average, crop productivity typically declines by 30–40% in moderate-drought years, whereas extreme droughts trigger far greater reductions3,4. As droughts become longer and more intense due to climate change, adverse effects on crop productivity are expected to escalate5. Breaking the trade-offs between stress resistance and yield is key to advancing crop genetic improvement as climate change sets in and the world population grows, but this is challenging for drought stress6. Here we show that heterologous expression of EpTFIIAγ, a gene encoding a transcription factor induced by osmotic stress in an extremophile lichen mycobiont, partially decouples trade-offs between stress resistance and grain production, enhancing plot yields of five wheat cultivars under water deficit by 19.4–32.8%, and per-plant yields of rice and maize by 19.7–42.4% in the greenhouse and multiple field environments. EpTFIIAγ physically interacts with endogenous transcriptional activators to synergistically enhance both stress-responsive and developmental transcriptional programs, simultaneously boosting photosynthetic capacity and water-use efficiency, while delaying senescence via multiple physiological and developmental enhancements, ultimately increasing grain yields. EpTFIIAγ uncouples antagonistic stress-response and biomass production pathways in multiple crops and delivers a straightforwards and broad-spectrum strategy for sustainably improving staple-crop yields regardless of water availability. The use of an extremophile fungus-derived gene decouples the trade-off of drought stress and reduced crop yield by boosting drought resilience and increasing yields in wheat, rice and maize.

papers.title: Disturbances and climate drive tree elevational shifts
papers.abstract: Climate change and disturbances are reshaping forest ecosystems worldwide1–4, yet their combined effects on species redistribution remain poorly understood. Here we analyse repeated measurements from 44,368 forest inventory plots spanning 1999–2025, with an average remeasurement interval of 10 years, to examine how climate and natural disturbances jointly influence the elevational redistribution of tree species across the western USA. We show that climate warming increased sapling abundance, whereas increasing drought frequency and recent natural disturbances (fire, insect outbreaks and disease) reduced tree abundance, particularly among adult trees. By contrast, legacy fire was associated with increased sapling abundance, with stronger positive responses in angiosperms than in gymnosperms. These influences were distributed unevenly across species’ elevational ranges: upper portions of species’ ranges generally experienced stronger warming, greater increases in drought frequency and more disturbance activity than lower portions, creating elevational asymmetries in stress and recovery. These elevational asymmetries were associated with more pronounced downslope shifts in basal area centres, probably reflecting disturbance effects on larger trees. By contrast, stem abundance centres showed more divergent shifts, consistent with sapling responses to both climate change and disturbance. Our findings reveal contrasting demographic responses to climate change and natural disturbances that shape the elevational redistribution of different species, with potential consequences for forest composition, resilience and long-term stability. Climate change and natural disturbances are key drivers of tree abundance dynamics: warming tends to shift tree abundance upslope whereas major disturbances, such as wildfires and insect outbreaks, tend to shift it downslope, creating opposing pressures on tree species’ elevational redistribution.

papers.title: Unconventional resistivity reduction in NbP semimetal nanoribbons
papers.abstract: Modern and future electronics harbour a key challenge: as conventional metal wires shrink to nanoscale dimensions, their resistivity increases sharply1 owing to surface and grain-boundary scattering. To circumvent this unwanted behaviour, here, we explore the fundamental limits of charge transport in topological semimetal niobium phosphide (NbP) nanoribbons down to approximately 6-nm widths, with industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication. The extracted NbP nanoribbon resistivity reaches 18 ± 4.1 μΩ cm at room temperature with an approximately 9-nm2 cross-sectional area, lower than that of conventional metals and semimetals with comparable size. The NbP nanoribbon resistivity decreases with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper. This trend suggests a growing relative contribution of surface and edge states as the nanoribbon cross-section is reduced, despite a certain amount of disorder, including edge roughness. Our findings advance the understanding of size-dependent transport and scaling in this class of semimetals, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects in future nanoelectronics. Niobium phosphide semimetal nanoribbons show decreasing resistivity with decreasing width, unlike the classical behaviour of metals such as copper, offering a platform for nanoscale wires and interconnects via industry-friendly top-down nanofabrication.

papers.title: De novo design of high-potency dual-target therapeutic peptides with ORIDTP
papers.abstract: Peptides capable of modulating two therapeutic targets offer opportunities for treating complex diseases1,2. However, the development of such peptides at both targets is challenging, limited primarily by low design success rates and weak bioactivity. Here we present ORIDTP, an artificial intelligence platform that integrates single-target knowledge transfer and dual-target reinforcement to enable the rational design of high-potency peptides. ORIDTP successfully designed dual-target co-agonists for the GLP-1R and glucagon receptor (GCGR, also known as GLR), six of which surpassed the strongest natural binders of each receptor in bioactivity. Notably, the lead peptide GA-Dual.R5.S3 induced substantial weight loss and glycaemic improvement in diet-induced obese mice, and exhibited pronounced antidiabetic effects in db/db mice, without inducing nausea or aversion. Furthermore, ORIDTP demonstrated generalizability through successful zero-shot design of dual-target co-inhibitors for structurally and mechanistically distinct immune checkpoints, PD-1 and CTLA-4. Out of 15 designed peptides, 8 blocked both checkpoint interactions and 3 further exhibited in vivo antitumour efficacy in human checkpoint knock-in tumour-bearing mice. The lead peptide IC-Dual.P3 achieved the strongest tumour growth suppression, reducing tumour volume by 94.2% relative to controls. Together, these findings establish ORIDTP as a powerful and generalizable platform for de novo dual-target peptide discovery. The artificial intelligence platform ORIDTP enabled de novo design of potent dual-target therapeutic peptides, generating candidate anti-obesity, antidiabetic and anticancer peptides with strong in vivo efficacy and broad cross-target generalizability.

papers.title: Engineering signalling centres to trigger human trunk morphogenesis in vitro
papers.abstract: Vertebrate trunk development is orchestrated by endogenous signalling centres that generate gradients of signals such as WNT and BMP to pattern cell fates and drive morphogenesis1–7. Whether these cues alone can reconstitute human trunk-like morphogenesis in vitro remains unknown. Here we present a synthetic embryology platform for high-throughput, spatiotemporal delivery of morphogen signals to epithelial cysts derived from human pluripotent stem cells. Transient WNT and BMP gradients are sufficient to drive the generation of axially elongating trunk-like structures that contain a central neural tube flanked by axial, paraxial, intermediate and lateral mesoderm. The geometry of the transient BMP signal exerts lasting control over mediolateral patterning and bilateral symmetry. Patterning and morphogenesis are sustained by neuromesodermal and lateral plate mesoderm progenitors induced by the initial cues, which act as endogenous signalling centres. Together, these findings define a minimal spatial code sufficient to reconstitute trunk-like morphogenesis in a human stem-cell-based model and establish a scalable platform for studying early human development and congenital disorders. A high-throughput synthetic embryology platform reveals how transient spatial cues establish two self-sustaining signalling centres that organize trunk-like morphogenesis, enabling the study of early human development and congenital disorders.

papers.title: Rare-variant genetic architecture of height in over 1.4 million individuals
papers.abstract: Highly heritable, polygenic and easily measured, adult height has long been the model trait in human genetics1,2. Although the landscape of height-associated common genetic variation has been studied extensively2, rare variation remains relatively unexplored1. Here, using rare protein-altering variants in a discovery set of 826,066 exomes, we identify 207 height-associated genes, 98% of which replicate in an additional 624,567 individuals. The rarest and most deleterious class of variation, singleton (frequency < 0.0001%) putative loss-of-function variants, implicated 17 genes with large effects on height ranging from −17cm (ACAN) to +11 cm (FBN1) per allele, 52× larger than the average effect of common height-associated variants and comparable to the 1% tails of a common variant polygenic score. Several genes (TET1, DTL and IGF2BP2) have effect sizes that are at least as large as established Mendelian height genes, yet lack documented stature or skeletal growth syndromes, particularly for genes associated with increased height. Our large-scale sequencing study elucidates the genetic architecture and allelic heterogeneity of rare variants in height, providing unique insights into their large effects—often similar to or larger than recognized Mendelian syndromes—and their impact on trait prediction, clinical evaluation, and discovery power to facilitate drug target prioritization. Analysis of exomes from over 1.4 million participants implicates 207 genes, including large effect coding variants and gene burden tests, and demonstrates the utility of large-scale sequencing for trait prediction and variant interpretation.

papers.title: Submillimetre hot-electron transport in manganese-doped quantum dot solids
papers.abstract: Colloidal quantum dot solids are promising for photoconversion and photochemistry, but their performance is fundamentally limited by rapid hot-carrier cooling, low carrier mobility and short transport ranges1. Here we demonstrate a spin-exchange-driven phototransport regime in manganese-doped quantum dot films that enables the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers. Ultrafast spin-exchange-mediated Auger upconversion promotes electrons into high-energy, delocalized states before phonon cooling2,3, establishing a transient high-mobility conduction channel. Crucially, spin-exchange interactions not only generate hot carriers but also enable their repeated re-excitation, thereby sustaining long-range drift. This mechanism yields room-temperature mobilities of about 150 cm2 V−1 s−1 and submillimetre drift lengths—far greater than those of conventional quantum dot solids and approaching values characteristic of crystalline semiconductors. Time-of-flight measurements confirm drift-dominated transport, with transit times scaling linearly with distance and inversely with electric field. These results establish a route to long-range energy transport in nanoscale materials and enable the use of hot carriers in photoconversion, photochemistry and transit-time-limited photodetection. A phototransport regime driven by spin exchange is demonstrated in manganese-doped quantum dot solids, enabling the generation, long-range transport and regeneration of hot carriers and yielding submillimetre drift lengths.

papers.title: From sketch to publication-ready flowchart: how AI tools can bridge the gap
papers.abstract: The use of generative AI is a practical way to translate hand-drawn scientific diagrams into digital formats without handing over total control, explains Ensar Aydemir.

papers.title: The world’s leading science cities are changing — here’s why
papers.abstract: Nature Index data reveal the cities that are gaining ground in research, as smart technologies transform how urban centres operate and compete for talent.

papers.title: Gut microbes can adapt to our ageing bodies
papers.abstract: A study of more than 10,000 individuals reveals specific mutations in gut bacteria that arise during human ageing, but few mutations associated with disease.

papers.title: China’s AI-powered smart-city model is going global
papers.abstract: China is using AI and big data to connect its cities and rural regions. Now, its smart-city technologies are attracting international interest.

papers.title: Pockets in compacted DNA tune gene activation
papers.abstract: The stochastic activation of specific genes is needed for the proper formation of neuronal circuits. Opposing forces act on inactive DNA to balance this process.

papers.title: Helsinki puts trust at the heart of its smart-city model
papers.abstract: Open urban data, recycled data-centre heat and a public AI register are helping the Finnish capital develop responsible urban technology.

papers.title: London’s people-first approach to smart-city development
papers.abstract: Digital twins and open-data platforms are part of London’s aim to innovate for citizens.

papers.title: Bogong moths can migrate using an internal geomagnetic compass
papers.abstract: Migratory moths distinguish poleward from equatorward by sensing the inclination of magnetic field lines.

papers.title: Can smart cities attract the talent they need to thrive?
papers.abstract: The challenges of high-tech cities in South Korea and China reveal what scientists really want.

papers.title: Dengue has exploded globally with shocking speed
papers.abstract: The number of recorded cases of the mosquito-borne disease worldwide rose by a factor of 34 over 34 years.

papers.title: The Mona Lisa Lottery
papers.abstract: Worth the wait.

papers.title: The world has a golden chance to improve HIV prevention: don’t squander it
papers.abstract: Generic versions of an effective HIV drug have been approved, and an HIV vaccine is on the horizon. Now is no time for funders to take their foot off the pedal.

papers.title: A guide to the Nature Index
papers.abstract: A description of the terminology and methodology used in this supplement, and a guide to the functionality that is available free online at natureindex.com.

papers.title: Succumbing to certainty is a failure in science
papers.abstract: Researchers can face pressure from policymakers and politicians to provide single, definitive answers to complex challenges. They should resist, says Andy Stirling.

papers.title: Rare gene variants can affect a person’s height by up to 17 centimetres
papers.abstract: An analysis of 1.4 million people uncovered rare gene variants that are helping to unpick the genetic architecture behind the heritability of height.

papers.title: Enzymatic reactions adapted to make ‘living’ chains of sugars
papers.abstract: By tuning the binding between enzymes that chain sugars together and the molecules that initiate the reaction, precise chain lengths have been made for biological studies.

papers.title: ‘If we can solve Riemann, what can’t we do?’: mathematicians shocked and excited by AI breakthroughs
papers.abstract: Awe, anxiety and opportunity: mathematics community shares mixed emotions following the solution of the field’s biggest unsolved problem.

papers.title: Just eight universities dominate Nobel and other top economics prizes
papers.abstract: Economics is the outlier — top prizes in science, engineering and other social sciences go to researchers at a greater variety of institutions.

papers.title: Augmenting reality with integrated photonics
papers.abstract: Augmented-reality (AR) glasses promise to transform how we interact with the world by seamlessly blending digital content with our physical surroundings. Yet making them viable for comfortable, all-day use remains deeply challenging, constrained by hard trade-offs of size, power and display performance. This calls for fundamentally new ways to generate and control light with high precision in an ultracompact form factor. Here we examine how integrated photonics can help bridge the technology gap in AR hardware. We review the basics of AR displays and recent advances in integrated photonics for new AR display components and architectures, then turn to key challenges and future directions, from component development to system innovation and scalable manufacturing, and highlight broader opportunities for synergy with fields such as quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing. Integrated photonics could overcome key size, power and performance trade-offs in augmented-reality glasses, enabling compact, efficient displays while opening opportunities across quantum computing, bioimaging and optical sensing.

papers.title: Clinical landscape of cardiometabolic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) has emerged as the predominant form of heart failure worldwide and is increasingly associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and systemic cardiometabolic dysfunction. This cardiometabolic HFpEF entity can be conceptualized as a mechanistically defined endotype marked by endothelial dysfunction, metabolic inflexibility and maladaptive inter-organ signalling involving the liver, kidney, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. The cardiometabolic endotype often corresponds to a clinically recognizable adiposity-related clinical phenotype. Despite the growing prevalence of cardiometabolic HFpEF, therapeutic progress has lagged. This is mostly because the classification structure used is based on a commonly over-interpreted biomarker—ejection fraction—although inadequate trial end points and a lack of mechanism-guided precision also have a role. Here we review the evolving epidemiology, mechanistic underpinnings and emerging therapeutic landscape of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We highlight limitations in current diagnostic criteria, the role of extracardiac drivers and the need for soft end points and systems-based modelling. Advances in '-omics', phenotyping and cross-disciplinary frameworks now offer a pathway towards mechanistically targeted interventions that could enable symptomatic control by modifying validated disease mechanisms that culminate in this syndrome. This Review covers the current state of research into heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) from a variety of perspectives, focusing on the clinical context.

papers.title: Observationally-constrained CMIP6 projections of a snow-free Northern Hemisphere
papers.abstract: This study presents a monthly emergent constraint based on observed warming that reduces CMIP6 inter-model variance and refines snow-free projections: Arctic summers become snow-free by 2040 s under SSP5-8.5, while snow disappearance is delayed by 7–34 years under SSP1-2.6 in vulnerable regions and months.

papers.title: Atomic-resolution insights into interactions of rifampicin and rifamycin derivatives with orphan CYP143 of M. tuberculosis
papers.abstract: The study reveals how the mutation associated with drug resistance facilitates the binding of rifampicin to the orphan enzyme of tubercular bacilli, thereby influencing protein-protein interactions. The findings explore pathogen adaptation mechanisms.

papers.title: Directional atomic-ordering gradients enable fatigue-resistant superelasticity in carbon tube aerogels
papers.abstract: The authors develop carbon tube aerogels with radial atomic-ordering gradients, enabling fatigue-resistant recovery under extreme compression and offering a strategy for designing durable lightweight porous materials.

papers.title: Carbon-neutral algal bloom management via algal organic matter repurposing
