papers.abstract: Algal organic matter (AOM) is repurposed as a crosslinker with metal coagulants, forming gel flocs that activate dissolved oxygen and generate microbubbles. This self-driven flotation effectively removes algae and AOM while reducing carbon footprint.

papers.title: Lithium coordination compound reduces nephrotoxicity and enhances therapeutic effects in Alzheimer’s disease female mice
papers.abstract: Here authors rationally design a lithium coordination compound BuLiPro. Compared with conventional lithium carbonate, BuLiPro improves brain lithium bioavailability, enhances GSK-3β inhibitory potency and reduces nephrotoxicity. In female AD mouse models, BuLiPro mitigates tau and amyloid-β pathologies and rescues cognitive deficits, showing potential for safer lithium-based therapeutics.

papers.title: Scalable 3D hybrid integrated photonic computing chiplets
papers.abstract: Integrated photonics promises fast, energy efficient information processing but remains difficult to scale. Here, authors develop HyPec, a hybrid photonic chiplet architecture combining 2D high-speed encoding with 3D photonic routing to enable scalable multi-chip computing.

papers.title: SMYD1 trimethylates myosin K129 to restrain cardiomyocyte hypercontractility
papers.abstract: How the muscle-specific enzyme SMYD1 regulates heart contraction and contributes to inherited heart disease has remained unclear. Here, the authors show that SMYD1 modifies the motor protein myosin to restrain heart-cell contraction, linking loss of this activity to hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

papers.title: Basal mantle motion causes Pacific hotspot drift
papers.abstract: This study shows that the average southward drift of Pacific hotspots since 80 Ma is linked to the migration of the underlying basal mantle structure, driven by large-scale lower-mantle flow associated with asymmetric subduction around the Pacific.

papers.title: Excited-state twisted intramolecular charge transfer enables reversible light control of rhodamine-graphene binding
papers.abstract: Rhodamine dyes are predicted to exhibit a twisted charge transfer that shapes their excited state. Here, the authors provide spectroscopic evidence for this and use it to control the dye’s binding to graphene using light.

papers.title: Quantitative prediction model of FB-113-driven self-assembly nanopesticides
papers.abstract: Nanopesticides offer new opportunities to improve pesticide efficacy, but predicting the formation of self-assembled nanopesticides remains challenging. Here, the authors report that the fluorescent brightener FB-113 drives the self-assembly of various pesticides into nanoparticles and that their self-assembly propensity can be quantitatively predicted from pesticide molecular structure.

papers.title: A neuroimmune dichotomy for T cell immunity in the mesenteric iymph node in mice
papers.abstract: The authors find that vagal and sympathetic neurons innervating the mesenteric lymph node sense distinct cytokines and release opposing signals—calcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP) and norepinephrine—to control the balance between regulatory and cytotoxic T cells during intestinal infection in mice.

papers.title: Restoring global forest canopy structure complexity for potential local warming mitigation
papers.abstract: Forest biophysical cooling is constrained by limited land for afforestation. This study suggest that increasing canopy structural complexity enhances forest biophysical cooling by 0.25 °C globally, offering a land-efficient forest management strategy.

papers.title: Directional codes for quantum LDPC error correction on square and hexagonal grid architectures
papers.abstract: Superconducting qubit platforms usually support only nearest-neighbour connectivity, complicating the implementation of efficient quantum low-density parity check codes. Here, the authors propose a family of qLDPC codes that replace long-range connections with local iSWAP-based circuits for stabiliser measurements, while outperforming the rotated toric code.

papers.title: Iron supplementation in iron-deficient Kenyan infants: a randomised controlled trial of vaccine immunogenicity
papers.abstract: In a trial of 288 Kenyan infants, daily iron supplements reduced iron-deficiency anaemia but did not improve antibody responses to routine vaccines. Diphtheria antibody levels were modestly lower with iron, while seroprotection rates were similar.

papers.title: CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis and inflammatory bone loss by sensing cholesterol and activating FES SYK STAT3
papers.abstract: Osteoclast overactivation causes inflammatory bone loss in periodontitis and arthritis. Here, the authors show that CD300LD drives osteoclastogenesis via a cholesterol-activated FES–SYK–STAT3 axis, and its deletion reduces bone loss and inflammation in mice.

papers.title: An explainable deep-learning framework for predicting multisystem outcomes in comorbidity-free MASLD
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects many organs, but long-term risks are hard to predict. Here, the authors show that in subset of MASLD patients indicated for biopsy, explainable AI uses liver biopsy images, clinical tests and yearly lifestyle data to predict multiple outcomes and plot changing risk over time.

papers.title: Tomato NLR R1L mediates SlSPL3 degradation to trigger a growth-to-defense switch against Phytophthora infestans
papers.abstract: Wang et al., characterize a tomato NLR protein R1L that specifically recognizes the Phytophthora infestans effector AVR1. The AVR1-R1L-SlSPL3-SlLTP3 module mediates a growth-immunity trade-off. In uninfected plants, SlSPL3 promotes growth and suppresses immunity via SlLTP3. Upon infection, R1L-mediated SlSPL3 degradation activates immunity and represses growth.

papers.title: Hepatokine AGP2 mediates physical exercise-induced bone augmentation through liver-bone signaling communication
papers.abstract: Exercise helps maintain strong bones, but the signals linking physical activity to bone growth have remained unclear. Here, the authors show that in mice exercise stimulates the liver to release AGP2, a hormone-like protein that promotes bone formation and protects against bone loss, revealing a potential treatment strategy for osteoporosis.

papers.title: A small RNA regulates iron homeostasis and host mucus colonization in Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron
papers.abstract: Here, the authors show how the beneficial gut bacterium Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron adapts to the intestinal mucous layer, identifying a small RNA regulator that balances capsule production, iron uptake, and host glycan utilization.

papers.title: A wearable reconfigurable surface electrode network for spatiotemporal control of hand motor output
papers.abstract: Selective non-invasive hand control remains challenging. Here, the authors present a wearable 32-electrode surface-stimulation system with programmable active–return routing, enabling current-path mapping and task-level control of wrist and hand actions.

papers.title: Preventing data leakage in neural decoding
papers.abstract: Neural decoding is widely used to understand how the brain represents the world, but data leakage can distort the results. Here the authors show that data leakage from preprocessing and cross-validation can both inflate and deflate decoding accuracy.

papers.title: An interaction module for mitochondrial ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants
papers.abstract: Mitochondrial ATP synthase is crucial for cellular energy production, but how it is assembled and maintained in plants is not fully uncovered. Here, the authors show that MTF5 and MTF5P form an interaction module essential for ATP synthase assembly and maintenance in seed plants.

papers.title: Achieving high-yield and pilot-scale synthesis of nano graphene oxide via photochemical defect engineering and oxidative cleavage
papers.abstract: This study presents a scalable photochemical and oxidative cleavage method converting micron-sized graphene oxide into stable, nanoscale flakes (20-60 nm). A pilot-scale reactor demonstrates its high-yield scaled-up viability.

papers.title: Giant nonlinear optical responses in the visible via lattice-controlled cascade amplification of photon avalanche
papers.abstract: This work extends and amplifies the nonlinear response of Tm³⁺ photon avalanche into the highly detectable visible region with optical nonlinearities exceeding 550, enabling sound 28-nm spatial resolution and multi-channel bioimaging application.

papers.title: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors show that seasonal live-attenuated influenza vaccination provides cross-protection against lethal infection with an antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 virus in ferrets, potentially through respiratory cellular immune responses.

papers.title: Low-pressure operation of all-solid-state batteries enabled by an organic electrode
papers.abstract: Low stack pressure is key for enabling practical solid-state batteries. Here, the authors demonstrate that low-modulus, low-hardness, creep-compliant, low-strain organic materials that readily deform in response to external pressures and microstructural changes enable stable cell operation at low stack pressures.

papers.title: Exploring enhanced self-esteem reactivity in response to social prediction errors in adolescence
papers.abstract: Adolescence is a period of heightened sensitivity to social experiences. Here, the authors show that unexpected social feedback shapes self-esteem most strongly in adolescence, both in the lab and in daily life.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into intracellular phase separation and maturation of FUS LC revealed by in-cell NMR
papers.abstract: Nishida and colleagues use in-cell NMR to capture time-dependent changes associated with the formation and maturation of FUS protein droplets, highlighting the influence of the cellular environment on these processes.

papers.title: Diabetes subtyping without HbA1c enhances identification of severe insulin-deficient diabetes
papers.abstract: Here, the authors propose a simplified diabetes subtyping approach that excludes HbA1c. The approach more accurately identifies severe insulin-deficient diabetes and improves prediction of beta-cell dysfunction and retinopathy in the tested cohorts.

papers.title: Chip-scale narrow-linewidth optical parametric oscillators
papers.abstract: Continuous-wave optical parametric oscillators can generate coherent light at wavelengths beyond semiconductor lasers, but narrow linewidth needs pure pump lasers. Here, authors couple a Kerr OPO to an ultralow-loss silicon nitride cavity, narrowing linewidth 15-fold to 10 Hz, enabling chip-scale, high-power, tunable, ultra-stable sources.

papers.title: Integration of Mott neurons and spintronic memories for event-driven spiking neural networks
papers.abstract: Spiking neural networks provide energy-efficient, event-driven computing, but separating volatile neuronal dynamics from non-volatile memory imposes costly signal transfer and conversion. Here we demonstrate a hybrid compute-and-store core that directly integrates thermally coupled vanadium dioxide Mott leaky integrate-and-fire neurons to spintronic memory. The neurons require no external resistive or capacitive elements for temporal integration and write their output spikes into either domain-wall racetracks or spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions without amplifiers or analogue-to-digital converters. In racetracks, spike number and amplitude are converted into domain-wall displacement, spatially preserving temporal histories and enabling up to six spikes per processing cycle. Distinct spike trains generated from encoded input patterns produce separable non-volatile states, demonstrating event-based processing and read-out. A network model parameterized by experimental leaky integrate-and-fire neuron dynamics achieves 96.3% accuracy on MNIST digit recognition. Functional coupling of a 500-nm leaky integrate-and-fire neuron to a 100-nm spin–orbit torque magnetic tunnel junction further establishes nanoscale compatibility. The demonstrated compute-and-store core consumes 51.9 nJ per spike-to-memory conversion, with sub-200-nm vanadium dioxide devices indicating operation near 200 pJ, offering a scalable route towards dense, low-power edge neuromorphic systems for real-time sensory processing. A hybrid compute-and-store core combining thermally coupled vanadium dioxide leaky integrate-and-fire neurons with domain-wall racetrack memory is presented. This architecture preserves temporal spike histories and achieves high recognition accuracy with low power consumption.

papers.title: Reversible ring formation enables force-responsive polymer networks
papers.abstract: Force-responsive interactions can enable materials that are compliant at low stress but stiffen under applied force, with applications ranging from impact-responsive materials to dynamic tissue scaffolds. However, engineering materials with tunable, force-dependent interactions remains challenging, and existing conceptual designs are limited. Here, we present a minimal synthetic framework for force-responsive dynamic polymer networks based on reversible ring-forming polymers. Using coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations, we show that materials with such a chemistry undergo fewer bond-breaking reactions as the stress increases and can even display a non-monotonic dependence of the strain rate on the applied stress, a macroscopic self-strengthening response directly linked to the underlying reaction kinetics. Our results highlight the potential of reversible ring formation as a general and versatile platform for designing mechanically adaptive materials with tunable durability and responsiveness.

papers.title: Reactivating retired wind turbines as distributed sources of physical inertia for resilient power systems
papers.abstract: The transition towards renewable energy systems introduces a dual challenge, with declining system inertia and the growing accumulation of end-of-life infrastructure. While inverter-based generation reduces the physical inertia required for frequency stability, large numbers of wind turbine generators are reaching retirement despite retaining substantial electromechanical capability. This creates a mismatch between emerging system needs and underutilised resources. We show that retired wind turbine generators can be reactivated as distributed sources of physical inertia, enabling electromechanical energy exchange with the grid through the controlled release and recovery of stored rotor kinetic energy. By linking frequency-responsive activation to rotor dynamics, these assets provide support during disturbances. System-level analysis indicates that reactivated generators improve frequency response across a range of operating conditions, increasing frequency nadir and reducing cumulative frequency deviation. Beyond the improvement in dynamic performance, this approach offers a pathway for the functional reuse of renewable infrastructure. By extending the operational role of existing assets, it connects system stability with circular resource utilisation. These results suggest that renewable technologies may evolve from single-purpose generation units into persistent system resources, offering a scalable route towards more resilient and sustainable low-carbon power systems. Yukai Huang and colleagues explore the potential of reusing retired wind turbine generators to provide physical inertia support in renewable-dominated power systems. The results suggest that reactivated generators may contribute to improved frequency response, offering an additional opportunity for the functional reuse of existing renewable energy infrastructure.

papers.title: The associations of screen time, sleep duration, and media usage rules on anxiety, depression, and aggression among South Korean infants
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the current status of screen time among infants and the associations of weekday and weekend screen times, sleep duration, and media use rules with anxiety, depression, and aggressive behavior among infants in South Korea. Data were drawn from the second wave of the Panel Study. A total of 1,005 infants were included. The data were analyzed using descriptive statistics and hierarchical multiple regression analysis. The results showed that most infants began watching videos between 11 and 15 months of age, watched videos every day, and spent 30 min or less per day screen times on both weekdays and weekends. Television was the most used device, and parents primarily used video viewing to occupy their children while working or resting. Weekday screen time and sleep duration were significant factors associated with anxiety and depression. Longer weekday screen time and poorer sleep quality were related to higher levels of emotional problems. Sleep duration was significantly associated with aggression. These findings underscore the importance of age-appropriate guidelines for healthy digital media use, the promotion of parent-child interaction, and the provision of caregiving support.

papers.title: Experimental investigation of carbamazepine removal from aqueous media using Al 2 O 3 /MWCNT nanocomposite for wastewater treatment through response surface methodology
papers.abstract: Carbamazepine (CBZ) is an anthropogenic persistent pollutant that is consistently present in treated effluent, as well as in water bodies that receive effluent from municipal treatment plants. As a result of its high resistant to degradation by these treatment processes, this study was performed to develop a hybrid sorbent consisting of alumina-coated multi-walled carbon nanotubes (Al2O3/MWCNTs). Characterization of the sorbent was performed using several techniques, and the results indicated that the Al2O3 (particle size of ~ 10–20 nm) was evenly coated on the surface of the MWCNT, producing a specific surface area of 136.82 m2/g with additional active sites available. Key operating variables affecting CBZ adsorption capacity as determined by coupled response surface methodology (RSM) using central composite design (CCD), were optimized through a systematic experimental approach, resulting in an RSM-predicted optimum value of 240.23 mg/g of CBZ adsorbed under mild alkaline conditions (pH 8.52 at 330 K), a sorbent dosage of 1.62 g/L, and an initial CBZ concentration of 400 mg/L. The Koble-Corrigan isotherm (qmax = 231.62 mg/g), which merges features of both the Langmuir and Freundlich models into an empirical hybrid framework, was the best fit for the experimental data, and analysis of the kinetic data indicated that the pseudo-second-order model best represented the CBZ adsorption kinetics, with evidence suggesting multi-step intraparticle diffusion mechanisms. The Al2O3/MWCNT composite was shown to greatly exceed the performance of all other known sorbents for CBZ and is therefore a viable alternative for tertiary treatment of wastewater contaminated with pharmaceuticals.

papers.title: Compositional ISS certification for aeroelastic flutter with input convex neural networks
papers.abstract: Suppression of supersonic airfoil flutter needs a controller that works over a wide airspeed range and a stability certificate that extends as subsystems are added. We combine input convex neural network (ICNN) controllers and ICNN Lyapunov functions with compositional input-to-state stability, in which the nonlinear small-gain theorem certifies the interconnection of plunge and pitch subsystems. Each network is built around a certified core, a pitch-feedback law and quadratic Lyapunov functions selected with linear matrix inequalities, with gains computed against the partner Lyapunov functions. With plunge measured at the center of gravity, this core certifies the Mach 5 closed loop with a small-gain spectral radius of at most 0.99 at every tested airspeed from 0.24 to 13 times the flutter speed, where hand-crafted quadratic candidates give 11 to $$2.1\times 10^4$$. The ICNN controller leaves this certificate unchanged and lowers the peak control for large disturbances by a factor of about five. The ICNN Lyapunov functions extend the numerically verified decrease to the whole large-perturbation domain. Against LQR, $$\mathscr {H}_\infty $$, and sliding mode control designed at the flutter speed, the design suppresses flutter from 0.3 to 1.2 times the flutter speed. A Mach 20 example and an actuator-augmented model complete the study.

papers.title: AI-based malicious traffic detection over protocols supporting RTSP streaming in smart city surveillance systems
papers.abstract: Smart city surveillance infrastructures increasingly rely on Internet-connected cameras and Internet of Things (IoT)-based video monitoring systems. They transmit real-time video streams through protocols such as the real-time streaming protocol (RTSP). These cameras are essential components of modern urban security systems, as they facilitate continuous monitoring and fast incident identification. However, a number of systems suffer from insufficient authentication techniques, default credentials, unencrypted communications, and poorly configured network settings. Security flaws that expose video streams to traffic analysis, eavesdropping, interception, and unauthorized access might compromise the integrity of surveillance activities and the privacy of individuals. In this paper, we propose an artificial intelligence (AI)-based malicious traffic detection scheme over protocols supporting RTSP streaming (in short, AIRSAD), which classifies network flows as normal or malicious and is intended to support smart city surveillance systems. To verify the security of the proposed AIRSAD, a security analysis is conducted. Then, the practical implementation of the proposed AIRSAD is provided and important performance parameters are estimated and compared with the existing schemes. During the performance comparisons with the existing schemes, it has been observed that the proposed AIRSAD achieves higher performance under the stated experimental conditions. This study has demonstrated the capacity of AI to strengthen the security of smart cities and improve cyber defense systems by efficiently identifying attempts to cyber attacks.

papers.title: Hierarchical self-organized crystallization in salt deposits induced by salt creeping
papers.abstract: Salt crystallization in nature forms remarkable macroscopic structures, sometimes reaching meters in size, such as desert roses in arid regions and salt pillars near saline lakes. Although visually striking, salt crystallization also presents significant challenges for the conservation of cultural heritage, material degradation, and soil management. By conducting controlled evaporation experiments on NaCl solutions and performing microscale analysis of efflorescent salt deposits, we reveal the mechanism behind the hierarchical, size-controlled precipitation of microcrystals within the precipitated salt. Our results reveal that these deposits consist of porous polycrystalline clusters that progressively increase in size as the salt solution spreads over previously precipitated microcrystals across multiple length scales. This mechanism creates smaller replicas nested within larger structures, forming fractal geometries with pronounced self-similarity. Additionally, we develop a hierarchical growth model showing that the ultimate height of our macroscopic salt deposit is primarily governed by the amount of the initial salt solution rather than the interplay of capillary and viscous forces of the salt solution flowing within the porous polycrystalline cluster during evaporation. Our results reveal how crystals self-organize at the microscale to build striking hierarchical structures at the macroscale, while also uncovering the microscale structure of desert rose as a natural salt deposit. These findings open avenues for bioinspired, self-organized materials that replicate mineral architectures found in nature for innovative scientific and engineering solutions.

papers.title: Determination of contamination of various insulators using K-means Clustering algorithm under various environmental conditions
papers.abstract: Environmental contamination of transmission-line insulators increases the leakage current and lowers the flashover voltage. Contamination arises from exposure to dust, moisture, rain, fog and other environmental agents, and contaminated insulators can cause flashover, grid outages and consequent economic losses. In this paper, a K-means clustering technique is proposed to assess the contamination level of various insulators under different environmental conditions. Artificial pollution tests were performed on insulators and their leakage current was recorded to evaluate insulator health. K-means clustering was applied to a dataset of 7000 insulator images, divided into training (5896), validation (364) and test (740) subsets, with the number of clusters fixed at K = 3 to match the low, medium and high contamination severity classes. Contamination was assessed through the electric potential, electric field strength, equivalent salt deposit density (ESDD), permittivity and leakage current, and the results were compared with conventional online monitoring reported in the literature. The effect of environmental conditions was analysed by applying salt and water contaminants to the insulators and evaluating the resulting contamination values. Because the study is based on artificially contaminated insulators, validation on naturally contaminated, field-aged insulators is identified as necessary future work.

papers.title: Optoelectronic and thermochemical properties of PLA, PLA/MgO and PLA/ZnO : DFT and TD-DFT study
papers.abstract: Polylactic acid (PLA) is a biodegradable polymer widely recognized for its numerous functional applications. In recent years, the incorporation of metal oxides in PLA has generated a lot of interest among researchers for several applications. In this study, PLA as well as the incorporation of metal oxides – MgO and ZnO with PLA are performed using Density Functional Theory (DFT) technique. The geometry, optoelectronic, and thermal characteristics of PLA/MgO and PLA/ZnO are investigated, and results are compared with pure PLA. The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO)- lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO) energy gap of PLA, PLA/MgO, and PLA/ZnO is found as 6.710, 6.666, and 6.153 eV respectively. HOMO-LUMO gap of the studied systems follows the order as: PLA > PLA/MgO > PLA/ZnO. Quantum-chemical descriptors- ionization potential, electron affinity, molecular hardness, softness, electronegativity, electrophilicity index and dipole moment of these complexes are analyzed. Natural bond orbital analysis, Time-dependent Density Functional Theory (TD-DFT) and thermochemical properties of PLA, PLA/MgO and PLA/ZnO are studied. Results show that integration of metal oxides- MgO and ZnO efficiently tailor’s PLA’s physicochemical properties, reinforcing its suitability for various applications.

papers.title: Machine learning-guided habitat optimization increases bacterial fitness to match genetic adaptation
papers.abstract: Bacterial fitness traditionally increases through genetic adaptation in fixed environments, while the contribution of environmental optimization is less well understood. Here, we used active machine learning to fine-tune growth media for Escherichia coli. Optimizing the habitat substantially increased growth, with gains comparable to those observed in selected experimentally evolved lineages. Two distinct machine learning models guided diverse ecological strategies, reflected in varied medium compositions and transcriptome reorganizations. Comparative analyses revealed that habitat reconstruction compensates for genetic constraints by modulating metabolic pathways, offering alternative adaptive routes. These findings demonstrate that machine learning-driven habitat optimization provides a practical experimental ecology approach to increase bacterial fitness, expanding adaptation concepts beyond genetics alone.

papers.title: Adult mice express salivary gland LPA4 and have elevated salivary lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) species levels in a periodontal disease model
papers.abstract: This study builds on our previous findings on the role of salivary lysophosphatidic acid (LPA) species in humans to investigate their presence, together with salivary gland LPA receptor (LPAR) expression in a model of periodontal disease (PD) using Porphyromonas gingivalis- infected C57BL/6J mice. Utilizing LC-MS/MS for LPA analysis alongside confocal LPAR imaging and second harmonic (SHG) imaging for collagen visualization, we compared mouse salivary LPA levels and gland LPAR expression to previously established human and mouse data. The findings reveal that while healthy mouse saliva maintains low homeostatic LPA levels, PD triggers a substantial increase, similar to the ~ 10-fold elevation we observed in PD patients. Furthermore, the study confirmed the presence of LPA1, LPA3, and LPA4 within submandibular gland (SMG) tissue. Notably, LPA3 was identified as the most widely distributed subtype, while providing the first evidence of LPA4 expression in adult mouse salivary glands. The presence of multiple LPARs suggests that LPA signaling is a critical factor in salivary gland biology. The documented existence of multiple LPARs within salivary glands indicates that they must be taken into consideration in future research concerning autoimmune conditions, and in pharmacological studies involving drugs that impact salivary gland biology and secretory function.

papers.title: Staged microbial transitions suggested by contrasting fungal and bacterial communities in Acacia mangium dieback
papers.abstract: Dieback disease in Acacia mangium plantations has long been attributed principally to infection by Ceratocystis species, yet its aetiology remains incompletely resolved in many tropical plantation systems. In this study, Illumina MiSeq amplicon sequencing of fungal ITS1 and bacterial 16S rRNA regions, complemented by culture-dependent fungal isolation, was used to characterise sapwood-associated microbial assemblages in symptomatic and asymptomatic trees from a Malaysian plantation. Fungal profiling revealed more than 50 taxa, including Ceratocystis fimbriata, Lasiodiplodia, Fusarium, and several wood-decay fungi, but no single taxon was consistently dominant across symptomatic samples. Notably, C. fimbriata was detected in both symptomatic and asymptomatic trees. Fungal community composition differed significantly between symptomatic and asymptomatic trees, although their distributions partially overlapped. One asymptomatic tree exhibited a fungal assemblage resembling those of several symptomatic trees, while its bacterial community remained closer to those of asymptomatic trees. Bacterial community composition also differed significantly between the two groups. Together, these findings suggest that fungal and bacterial community changes associated with A. mangium dieback may represent distinct stages of microbial reorganisation, providing a basis for a hypothetical model of staged microbial transitions.

papers.title: An enhanced cascade active disturbance rejection control strategy for step and ramp disturbances suppression in PMSMs
papers.abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motors (PMSMs) are widely adopted in high-performance motion control systems, yet their control performance is greatly limited by aperiodic disturbances including abrupt load torque variations and internal parameter deviations. Conventional linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) suffers from poor anti-disturbance ability and fails to eliminate steady-state errors under non-step disturbances. This paper proposes an enhanced cascade active disturbance rejection control (ECADRC) for PMSM speed regulation. A two-stage cascade extended state observer (ECESO) is constructed to realize coarse and refined estimation of total disturbances sequentially. Error differential correction is further introduced to accelerate disturbance estimation dynamics. Convergence and stability analyses are carried out, and frequency-domain results reveal that ECADRC attains a + 80dB/dec low-frequency disturbance rejection slope, superior to conventional ADRC. Comparative experiments validate that ECADRC achieves faster dynamic responses, smaller speed fluctuations and stronger robustness against parameter mismatches, effectively suppressing step and ramp disturbances with promising engineering applicability.

papers.title: Changes in fitness levels protect against the adverse responder phenotype in individuals living with type 2 diabetes
papers.abstract: The term exercise non-responder and adverse responder have been coined to describe the absence of benefits or deterioration with exercise training. However, little is known about the potential predictors associated with several responder phenotypes. The objective of this study was to investigate the associations between Type 2 diabetes (T2D) responder phenotypes and changes in body composition and fitness levels following a 9-month exercise intervention. T2D [glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) ≥ 6.5%] individuals (n = 188) were randomized to a control or an exercise training group for 9 months (NCT00458133). Changes in anthropometric measures (scale and tape measurement) and body composition (Dual-energy X-ray Absorptiometry) were assessed. Changes in fitness were evaluated using treadmill time duration (TTD) and the highest estimated metabolic equivalent tasks (METs). Participants randomized to exercise training were categorized based on the residual of the absolute change in HbA1c: (1) “adverse responders” (Δ HbA1c > 0.10%), (2) “non-responders” (Δ HbA1c ± 0.09%, and 3) “responders” (Δ HbA1c ≤ 0.10%). The proportion of adverse responders, non-responders, and responders was 38.8%, 16.5%, and 44.5%. Participants were more likely to be a responder compared to the control group if they improved weight, body mass index, waist circumference, percent body fat, and total fat mass (all p ≤ 0.05). Participants who increased their TTD or estimated METs were 1.93 (95%CI 1.43–2.58) and 4.50 (95%CI 1.22–9.25) times more likely to be exercise responders than the control group. Only participants who changed TTD [1.35 (95%CI 1.12–1.60)] or estimated METs [1.99 (95%CI 1.25–3.16)] were more likely to be a responder compared to an adverse responder. Even if exercise lead to improved HbA1c, some individuals did not improve beyond the coefficient of variation in the measure. Improvement in fitness may protects against the adverse responder’s phenotype in T2D individuals.

papers.title: AMS-Net: lightweight self-attention enhanced MobileNetV3 for fine-grained image classification on edge devices
papers.abstract: Fine-grained image classification on edge devices requires models that separate visually similar categories at a computational cost the device can sustain, yet lightweight backbones capture image-wide context only indirectly, through depth. We show that a reduced non-local module supplies this context at negligible cost. AMS-Net inserts three such modules (LSSAM) into an ImageNet-pretrained MobileNetV3-Small; pooled keys and values and a reduced channel width make each module 29–38$$\times $$ cheaper than standard spatial self-attention, and with one channel per attention group the module performs a learned image-wide aggregation with query-dependent sharpness. On the eight-class Flowers-WTT dataset, over three training runs, LSSAM raises test accuracy from 94.84 ± 0.28% to 97.63 ± 0.20% (McNemar $$p < 0.001$$ in every run) for 0.39% more parameters and 0.67% more FLOPs. It matches the unreduced self-attention block at 1/31 of its added FLOPs and outperforms CBAM, ECA, a convolutional block, and a global-context block at the same positions in every run. AMS-Net matches the accuracy of RepViT-M0.9 and EdgeNeXt-XXS with 14.1$$\times $$ and 3.4$$\times $$ fewer FLOPs and outperforms VGG-16 with 1/88 of its parameters. Gradual unfreezing reaches the best validation epoch 36% sooner at equal accuracy (97.71 ± 0.20%). AMS-Net runs at 80.9 FPS on a Jetson Nano with TensorRT and at 26.5 FPS on a Raspberry Pi 4B after static INT8 quantisation, and on Oxford-17 it improves on MobileNetV3-Small by 11 to 13 test images on each of the three official splits.

papers.title: Structural attribution of embodied carbon emissions using a regional input–output framework
papers.abstract: Understanding how carbon emissions are structurally generated within production systems remains a central challenge in environmental accounting. Existing input–output (IO) and multi-regional IO approaches, including structural path and production-layer decomposition methods, are effective for tracing embodied emissions across production networks, but they are often designed to identify where emissions occur or through which paths they are transferred. For many regional policy contexts, however, the immediate analytical need is to compare how a product’s embodied emission factor is composed by locally supplied inputs, externally supplied inputs, and direct emissions using commonly available regional IO data. This study proposes the regional embodied carbon share (RECS), a structural attribution framework that expresses a product’s emission factor as proportional input-level contributions within a unified IO accounting formulation. RECS complements conventional footprint and supply-chain decomposition approaches by focusing on how embodied emissions are structurally composed rather than reconstructing complete interregional production paths. The framework is applied to the lumber and wood products sector across five Japanese prefectures, where local forestry-resource use is often promoted as an emission-reduction strategy. Results show that similar overall emission factors can conceal substantially different contribution structures, particularly for forestry resources, electricity, intermediate wood products, and transport services. These findings demonstrate that embodied emissions depend on regional production structures rather than local sourcing alone, highlighting the value of structural emission attribution for regional comparison and mitigation policy design.

papers.title: Risk factors for red blood cell transfusion among very low birth weight infants with intact survival: a national cohort study
papers.abstract: Red blood cell (RBC) transfusion is common in neonatal intensive care units; however, its independent impact on long-term outcomes remains unclear because of confounding by indication. We identified clinical risk factors associated with RBC transfusion and evaluated its effects on long-term growth and neurodevelopment in a cohort of very low birth weight infants (VLBWIs) who achieved intact survival. We analyzed multicenter registry data from the Korean Neonatal Network collected between 2013 and 2023. Among 6,403 eligible infants without major severe neonatal morbidities, 2,750 (42.9%) received at least one RBC transfusion. Advancing gestational age and increasing birth weight were independently associated with significantly reduced transfusion requirements. Neonatal morbidities, including mild bronchopulmonary dysplasia (adjusted OR, 3.30; 95% CI 2.89–3.75; P < 0.001) alongside prolonged critical care indices, were independently associated with increased transfusion requirements. In this exploratory secondary analysis of infants with follow-up data, a multivariable regression revealed that RBC transfusion was not significantly associated with suboptimal height or head circumference catch-up after adjusting for baseline maturity and confounders. Although neonatal morbidities and critical care duration are strongly associated with transfusion requirements, RBC transfusion was not independently associated with long-term growth or neurodevelopment in VLBWIs with intact survival. Gestational age and birth weight remain the primary prognostic factors determining long-term outcomes.

papers.title: Dual-pipeline fake news detection via cross-attention fusion and meta-ensemble classification
papers.abstract: Digital media misinformation comes from two channels: tampered images and non-tampered text/posts. These are being dealt with in isolation of each other by existing detection systems thereby creating a gap. This paper proposes a dual-pipeline detection framework that combines an image forgery detector with a text-based fake news classifier. We put forth a dual-stream architecture in which EfficientNet-B0 and Vision Transformer (ViT-Small) are fused through Bidirectional Cross-Attention mechanism. This architecture has been trained on Error Level Analysis (ELA)-preprocessed images. Under a source-disjoint evaluation protocol on CASIA 2.0, in which no source image is shared between training and test data, the model achieves 91.82 ± 1.22% accuracy and a ROC-AUC of 0.973 over five training seeds, with significantly higher forgery recall than a re-implemented ELA-CNN baseline. A meta-classifier ensemble built from DeBERTa-v3 embeddings and Support Vector Machine and Logistic Regression classifiers is evaluated on three benchmarks for text-based detection. It achieves 99.86% accuracy on ISOT, 85.73% on GossipCop and 62.83% on the challenging LIAR benchmark, and on identical test splits it is never significantly worse than its individual components. An ablation study shows that the transformer stream provides most of the discriminative signal, while the CNN stream detects complementary forgeries missed by the transformer. A learned domain router directs each text input to the appropriate model with 98.9% accuracy.

papers.title: Determination of the 4-dimensional diffeomorphism function and establishment of the swallowtail catastrophe manifold for chip-branching in thread turning
papers.abstract: The catastrophe theory has the limitation of not providing a method for determining the 4-dimensional diffeomorphism function between actual state/control variables and theoretical state/control variables when establishing a catastrophe phenomenon model. This limitation prevents the establishment of a chip‑branching swallowtail catastrophe manifold equation that could eliminate many adverse effects caused by excessive cutting force under thread turning conditions. To solve above problems, a method is proposed to determine the diffeomorphism functions for control variables and state variables separately, and then composite them into a complete 4-dimensional diffeomorphism function between actual state/control variables and theoretical state/control variables. Utilizing this method, the precise equation for the swallowtail catastrophe manifold of chip-branching catastrophe in thread turning is successfully established. Verification experiments confirmed that the established equation accurately predicts both the unit main cutting force and the occurrence of chip‑branching. Using this equation, cutting layer parameters are designed to ensure that during thread turning, all or most feed times are in a chip‑branching state with minimum unit main cutting force, thereby achieving process energy savings.

papers.title: A Dirichlet-Multinomial model for uncertainty-aware lineup evaluation in basketball
papers.abstract: Offensive and defensive lineup ratings, defined as points scored or allowed per 100 possessions, are the primary publicly available metrics for evaluating basketball lineup performance. For the vast majority of lineups, which appear on the court for only a handful of possessions during a season, these raw ratings are highly unreliable as predictors of future performance. To address this limitation, we adopt a Bayesian shrinkage approach to estimate each lineup’s offensive and defensive scoring distribution. Specifically, we model possession outcomes as Multinomial draws from a lineup-specific probability vector, and place a Dirichlet prior on this vector informed by player-level ratings from the previous season. Exploiting the conjugacy of the Dirichlet-Multinomial model, the posterior is available in closed form. We additionally incorporate opponent strength adjustment via exponential tilting of the posterior, giving full credit to the quality of opponents faced without subjecting it to Bayesian shrinkage. Our out-of-sample evaluations show that the posterior predictive distribution outperforms several baselines that use only the observed lineup performance, with the largest gains observed for lineups with few possessions. Beyond point predictions, the proposed framework naturally quantifies uncertainty in lineup ability, enabling probabilistic comparisons between lineups that better reflect the inherent variability in basketball outcomes.

papers.title: Carbon fiber/GNP-reinforced SMPU composites: mechanical, thermal and shape memory properties
papers.abstract: Shape memory polyurethane (SMPU) possesses excellent shape memory characteristics; however, its relatively low mechanical strength and thermal stability limit its application in advanced engineering systems. In this study, carbon fiber (CF) mat-reinforced SMPU composites containing graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) were successfully fabricated using a solvent casting technique. The effect of GNP loading and post-fabrication annealing on the thermal, mechanical, thermomechanical and shape memory properties of the composites was systematically investigated. 75 °C for 2 h was identified as the optimum annealing condition among the conditions investigated. Differential scanning calorimetry (DSC) showed up to a 13% increase in the Tg of the composite. The S/CF/GNP-0.25 composite exhibited the highest tensile strength, showing a 45% improvement over the as-fabricated S/CF composite, which further increased to 105 MPa (139%) after optimum annealing. Furthermore, the developed hybrid composites exhibited efficient shape fixity and rapid shape recovery behavior. The results demonstrate that the combined effects of CF reinforcement, GNP loading, and post-fabrication annealing significantly enhance the structural, thermal, and shape memory performance of SMPU composites, making them promising candidates for smart structural and deployable engineering applications.

papers.title: Diet quality and its associated factors among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus attending public hospitals in East Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Evidence on diet quality and its determinants among adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) in Ethiopia remains limited. This study aimed to assess diet quality and its associated factors among adults with T2DM attending public hospitals in the East Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia. An institution-based cross-sectional study was conducted from March 9 to April 8, 2026. Data were collected using structured questionnaires and analysed using binary logistic regression. Overall, 38.1% (95% CI: 33.5–42.7) had good diet quality. Factors associated with good diet quality were monthly income of 10,000–20,000 ETB (AOR = 3.28; 95% CI: 1.57–6.83), monthly income > 20,000 ETB (AOR = 3.90; 95% CI: 2.09–7.29), no alcohol consumption (AOR = 8.53; 95% CI: 4.66–15.63), good nutrition knowledge (AOR = 2.65; 95% CI: 1.57–4.49), and being physically active (AOR = 7.56; 95% CI: 3.60-12.01). The findings highlight a significant proportion with poor diet quality, underscoring the importance of nutrition education, promoting physical activity, reducing alcohol consumption, and addressing socioeconomic barriers to improve diet quality.

papers.title: Risk-aware hybrid retrieval-augmented clinical section routing with CRUS uncertainty scoring and confidence-gated abstention
papers.abstract: Clinical section routing in medical dialogue systems requires accurate predictions and uncertainty estimates to support deferral of uncertain cases. We introduce a risk-aware hybrid retrieval framework combining BM25 sparse retrieval, dense retrieval using all-MiniLM-L6-v2 sentence embeddings, reciprocal rank fusion, and a coarse-to-fine cross-encoder reranking cascade. Candidate classes are shortlisted using label-string scoring, followed by reranking of character-truncated training dialogues. A bounded composite retrieval uncertainty score (CRUS) combines predictive entropy, retrieval-label entropy, and normalized reciprocal-rank-fusion score variance using fixed heuristic weights. The corrected MTS-dialog evaluation includes 1,288 retained dialogue records across 17 classes, partitioned into 773 training, 258 validation, and 257 test instances, with no group identifiers shared across splits. Training retrieval documents and validation/test queries contain normalized dialogue only. Gold section headers define routing targets; neither gold headers nor reference section text enter model inputs. Abstention policies are selected on validation data and frozen before test scoring. RiskAware-cascade achieved 70.43% pre-abstention accuracy (181/257). Its frozen CRUS gate accepted 117 cases (45.53% coverage), achieving 93.16% selective accuracy (109/117) and a 6.84% accepted-case misclassification rate (8/117), while deferring 140 cases. Counting abstentions as incorrect yielded 42.41% accuracy and 57.59% error. At matched 45.53% coverage using the same Cascade predictions, CRUS retained 109 correct predictions versus 106 for predictive entropy alone, a descriptive selective-accuracy difference of 2.56 percentage points. In a separate ranking-based baseline comparison retaining 117 cases per method, sigmoid-calibrated TF-IDF–Linear SVM achieved 99.15% selective accuracy (116/117), compared with 90.60% (106/117) for Cascade under that comparison’s ranking policy. These selections may retain different instances and are distinct from CRUS-based selection. The findings characterize an internal coverage misclassification trade-off rather than measured clinical harm reduction or superiority over supervised baselines. Independent external validation and evaluation of the deferred-case review workflow are required before drawing conclusions about clinical deployment.

papers.title: Measuring corporate ESG communication quality with an uncertainty-calibrated hierarchical mixture-of-experts framework
papers.abstract: Corporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosures vary considerably across document sources, reporting structures, firms, and reporting periods. Individual passages may relate to multiple ESG pillars and differ substantially in evidential quality, making isolated sentence classification and frequency-based firm measures inadequate. This study proposes ESG-HMoE, an uncertainty-calibrated hierarchical mixture-of-experts framework for measuring corporate ESG communication. The framework integrates target-sentence, local-context, section-level, document-level, source, and continuous-time representations. It further aligns disclosures with learnable environmental, social, and governance prototypes and dynamically combines a shared expert with pillar-specific experts. A rank-consistent ordinal module distinguishes symbolic, partially substantive, and evidence-rich disclosures. Here, disclosure substance denotes observable evidential characteristics of reported communication and does not verify the truthfulness, completeness, or real-world ESG performance represented by a claim. Calibrated pillar probabilities, ordinal substance estimates, and predictive uncertainty are aggregated into three firm-level measures: ESG communication coverage, conditional disclosure substance, and Quality-Adjusted ESG Communication Intensity (QACI). These measures characterize observable communication rather than a firm’s underlying ESG performance. The empirical analysis uses 13.846 million domain sentences, a newly constructed contextual multi-label corpus of 5,407 sentences, a public 2,000-sentence external benchmark, 900 ordinal substance annotations, and 2,568 annual reports. Under entity-grouped evaluation with test-entity documents excluded from domain-adaptive pretraining, ESG-HMoE achieves a macro-F1 of $$0.937\pm 0.005$$, a micro-F1 of $$0.948\pm 0.004$$, and a macro Expected Calibration Error of $$0.027\pm 0.004$$. The ordinal substance module achieves a Quadratic Weighted Kappa of $$0.816\pm 0.014$$. Under country-level holdout, macro-F1 decreases to $$0.881\pm 0.011$$, while calibration error rises to $$0.068\pm 0.009$$, indicating that geographical transfer remains challenging. A 2024–2025 external temporal audit yields a macro-F1 of $$0.899\pm 0.010$$ and an ECE of $$0.056\pm 0.008$$, further showing that performance and calibration should not be assumed invariant across reporting regimes. Firm-level analyses show that disclosure substance explains variation in external ESG ratings beyond communication coverage. QACI also correlates more strongly with blinded expert assessments than coverage alone. These associations are interpreted as convergent or external-criterion evidence rather than validation against an ESG-performance ground truth. These findings support a calibrated distinction between the extent of ESG communication and the substantive quality of that communication.

papers.title: Number processing is shaped by lexicalization
papers.abstract: Whether numerical cognition is shaped by language-specific representations or relies on language-independent place-value mechanisms remains debated. We tested 158 French- and German-speaking adults in a two-digit number comparison task to examine whether number words are activated during Arabic numeral processing and whether language modulates the parallel processing of decade and unit digits. A French-specific within-vigintade effect indicated number word activation in two-digit magnitude comparison. Number range also interacted with language: contrary to expectations, French participants responded faster to numbers above than below 60 despite the opacity of French vigesimal number words. Rather than indicating reliance on a single processing route, this pattern is consistent with weighted co-activation of language-independent numerical and language-specific verbal representations. Both groups showed a robust unit-decade compatibility effect, confirming parallel decade and unit processing. However, this effect was larger in French than German speakers, contrary to predictions based on German number word inversion. Several non-exclusive mechanisms - including adaptation to the stimulus distribution, accumulated linguistic experience, integrated lexical access, and verbal-zone organization - may have altered the relative weighting of co-activated representations. Thus, language shapes number processing, but its behavioral effects depend on experience and task context.

papers.title: Electrical property analysis of nickel ferrite nanoparticles synthesized via green chemistry
papers.abstract: Despite growing interest in green-synthesized ferrite nanoparticles, the combined influence of plant-extract phytochemistry on the structural, electrical, and magnetothermal performance of the resulting nanoparticles remains poorly understood. Here we test the hypothesis that extract polyphenol/flavonoid content systematically governs nanoparticle crystallite size, charge-transport mechanism, and magnetic heating efficiency. Nickel ferrite (NiFe₂O₄) nanoparticles were synthesized via green chemistry using aqueous extracts of raspberry leaves/stems (M2) and pomegranate peel (G2) as reducing and stabilizing agents. The G2 extract exhibited markedly higher phytochemical richness (TPC: 118 vs. 10.2 mg GAE/g; TFC: 15.5 vs. 3.0 mg QE/g; DPPH: 1284 vs. 94 µM TE/g). XRD confirmed a single-phase cubic spinel structure (space group Fd–3m; a = 8.38 Å) with crystallite sizes of 10.4 nm (M2) and 18.5 nm (G2). TEM revealed quasi-spherical, strongly agglomerated nanoparticles (3–30 nm). EIS measurements showed concentration-dependent conductivity (up to 0.04 S/m); M2 achieved values ~ 50% higher than G2 at 0.5 g/mL, attributed to smaller particle size and a thinner organic surface layer. Charge transport was thermally activated (Ea = 0.22 eV) via a small-polaron hopping mechanism, while dielectric spectra indicated dominant Maxwell–Wagner polarization. Magnetothermal measurements demonstrated effective heating (ΔT = 16.6 °C in 198 s; SAR up to 97.9 kW/kg), exceeding the therapeutic hyperthermia threshold. Extract composition is identified as a key determinant of the structural and functional properties of green-synthesized nickel ferrite nanoparticles.

papers.title: Adaptive multi-interval inversion for airborne TDEM data and its application in permafrost detection
papers.abstract: Airborne time-domain electromagnetic methods (TDEM) can determine the resistivity of subsurface media based on the responses of electromagnetic fields, thereby enabling the detection of subsurface structures. However, even similar types of subsurface media might exhibit varying resistivity values due to differences in composition, porosity, and water content. These resistivity values vary in a certain range, making it challenging to accurately determine the anomalous targets during inversion. Consequently, the inversion accuracy of target anomalies is reduced. To address this issue, this study develops a novel pseudo-two-dimensional smooth inversion algorithm for airborne TDEM data based on adaptive multi-interval transformations of model parameters. By constraining the inversion search process based on the resistivity distribution ranges of subsurface media, the proposed algorithm significantly reduces the search space and thereby enhances the inversion accuracy. The superiority of the proposed algorithm has been verified through the synthetic data of the high-resistance model. The impact of interval settings on inversion results was also discussed. The algorithm was applied to the inversion of permafrost data obtained from airborne TDEM surveys of the Jiangcang River basin on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau. The inversion results were validated using the existing borehole data. The airborne TDEM survey results reveal that the permafrost in the piedmont plain zone remains intact, while permafrost in the coal mining area tends to thaw and disappear. These results suggest human activities have disrupted the permafrost continuity in the survey area.

papers.title: Exploring AI literacy, perception, capability, and dependency among Iranian academic researchers: a modified UTAUT-2 model approach: a cross-sectional study
papers.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) tools are increasingly used in academic research. This cross-sectional study examined performance expectancy (PE), social influence/facilitating conditions (SI-FC), AI capability/literacy (AIC), AI dependency (AID), and behavioral intention (BI) among 563 Iranian academic researchers using a modified UTAUT-2 framework. The sample was randomly split into exploratory (n = 281) and confirmatory (n = 282) subsamples. In the exploratory subsample, a six-factor solution separated the five modeled constructs from current use behavior. A 19-item, five-factor measurement model estimated with WLSMV in the confirmatory subsample showed acceptable fit (robust CFI = 0.930, TLI = 0.916, RMSEA = 0.076; SRMR = 0.061); SI-FC had low reliability (omega = 0.59). PE was positively associated with BI (β = 0.488) and, contrary to the hypothesized negative direction, with AID (β = 0.476). SI-FC (β = 0.222) and AIC (β = 0.226) were positively associated with BI. AIC had a negative, borderline association with AID (β = −0.132, p = 0.053), and AID was not directly associated with BI after adjustment (β = −0.028, p = 0.679). Researchers who perceived AI as more useful reported both stronger intention to use it and greater reliance on it. These cross-sectional associations require replication.

papers.title: Truck-drone cooperative routing for post-disaster emergency medical supply distribution under road uncertainty
papers.abstract: This study proposes a truck-drone cooperative delivery system for post-disaster last-mile logistics, in which damaged roads delay the delivery of emergency medical supplies to rural areas. Five delivery modes span round-trip cooperative and truck-assisted dispatch operations, with demand points classified as truck-only, drone-only, or combined nodes. A Vehicle Routing Problem with Drones (VRPD) model minimizes delivery time and cost by incorporating stochastic road-blockage probabilities to enable dynamic node reclassification. A Demand-Priority-Aware Improved Genetic Algorithm (DPA-IGA) solves it. Benchmarks show DPA-IGA converges 17.55% faster than a standard GA and outperforms ACO. A Pakistan earthquake case study shows 36.72% shorter delivery time and 9.78% lower cost versus truck-only delivery.

papers.title: Physical activity dimensions and incident cardiovascular disease among Chinese middle-aged and older adults in a 5-year longitudinal study
papers.abstract: Physical activity (PA) plays an important role in the development and progression of various chronic diseases and may be associated with the risk of cardiovascular disease (CVD). However, the longitudinal associations of different physical activity factors, including frequency, duration, intensity, and total volume, with cardiovascular disease among middle-aged and older adults remain unclear, and the potential role of social isolation in this relationship has not been fully investigated. This study used data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) in 2015 and 2020, including 3,984 middle-aged and older Chinese adults without CVD at baseline in 2015. PA was assessed using a self-reported questionnaire. The dimensions of PA included intensity, frequency, daily duration, weekly volume, and total physical activity (TPA). Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between PA indicators and the risk of incident CVD during the 5-year follow-up. Restricted cubic spline and threshold effect analyses were used to evaluate the dose-response relationship between TPA and CVD risk, and the Karlson-Holm-Breen method was applied to assess the mediating role of social isolation. Subgroup analyses and interaction tests were further conducted to evaluate heterogeneity, and three sensitivity analyses, including machine learning–based propensity score inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW), were performed to assess the robustness of the findings. During the 5-year follow-up, the incidence of incident CVD was 16.6%. Compared with no activity individuals, participants engaging in vigorous-intensity physical activity (VPA) for ≥ 3 days per week had a lower risk of CVD; those engaging in moderate-intensity physical activity (MPA) for 1–2 days or ≥ 3 days per week also showed a lower CVD risk. Spending ≥ 30 min per day or accumulating ≥ 150 min per week on either VPA or MPA was associated with a lower risk of CVD. In contrast, no significant association was observed between light-intensity physical activity (LPA) and CVD risk. Higher TPA levels were associated with a lower risk of CVD, with the highest quartile showing a 48% lower risk of CVD (OR = 0.52, 95% CI: 0.45–0.58). A nonlinear dose-response relationship was observed between TPA and CVD risk, with an inflection point at 8982.0 MET-min/week. Mediation analysis showed that social isolation partially mediated the association between TPA and CVD risk, with a mediation proportion of 6.26%. Sensitivity analyses supported the robustness of the main findings.

papers.title: Thymoquinone-loaded casein nanoparticles attenuate methotrexate-induced hepatotoxicity by modulating oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis-related alterations in rats
papers.abstract: This study investigated the hepatoprotective effects and potential mechanisms of thymoquinone-loaded chitosan nanoparticles (TQ-Cas-NPs) against methotrexate (MTX)-induced liver injury using complementary in vivo and in vitro models. Sixty male Sprague–Dawley rats were randomly allocated into six groups: control, TQ, TQ-Cas-NPs, MTX, MTX + TQ, and MTX + TQ-Cas-NPs. MTX (5 mg/kg) was administered intraperitoneally as a single dose, whereas TQ and TQ-Cas-NPs (10 mg/kg TQ-equivalent) were administered intraperitoneally for seven days in TQ-only groups or five days following MTX exposure. Hepatic biochemical, molecular, mitochondrial, histopathological, immunohistochemical, and ultrastructural parameters were evaluated. Complementary primary rat hepatocyte experiments investigated cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, inflammation, and ferroptosis-associated alterations using ML385, BAY 11-7082, ferrostatin-1, and RSL3. MTX significantly impaired liver function, increased oxidative stress and inflammatory mediators, altered apoptosis-associated markers, and disrupted ferroptosis-related parameters, including GPX4, SLC7A11, ACSL4, TFR1, and iron. MTX also reduced ATP production and mitochondrial respiratory-chain complex activities and induced pronounced histopathological and ultrastructural damage. TQ-Cas-NPs significantly attenuated these alterations, generally demonstrating greater protective effects than free TQ. Consistently, TQ-Cas-NPs reduced MTX-induced LDH release, ROS, MDA, NF-κB, TNF-α, IL-6, iron, ACSL4, and 4-HNE while improving NRF2, HO-1, and catalase activity in primary hepatocytes. ML385 and RSL3 significantly attenuated these protective effects, whereas ferrostatin-1 reduced MTX-induced injury. BAY 11-7082 further reduced LDH release and TNF-α without significantly modifying most other evaluated endpoints. Blank chitosan nanoparticles showed no significant protective effects. Collectively, TQ-Cas-NPs attenuated MTX-induced hepatic injury through changes associated with NRF2/HO-1 antioxidant regulation, NF-κB-related inflammation, mitochondrial dysfunction, apoptosis-associated responses, and ferroptosis-related processes. These findings provide complementary pharmacological evidence supporting the involvement of antioxidant and ferroptosis-associated mechanisms, although further pharmacokinetic and genetic validation studies are warranted.

papers.title: Automated mealtime identification from continuous glucose monitoring to assess long-term postprandial glycemic exposure in non-diabetic adults
papers.abstract: Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) can quantify long-term glycemic exposure, but postprandial interpretation requires reliable temporal anchors for meal onset. We developed and evaluated a bidirectional long short-term memory model with conditional random field decoding (BiLSTM-CRF) to identify meal onsets directly from CGM traces and estimate 2 h postprandial glucose exposure. CGM datasets from 66 adults without diabetes who participated in three inpatient metabolic studies were used; meal onset times were recorded by research nurses. The model was trained using Abbott CGM data and evaluated in independent Abbott and Dexcom datasets. During development, the model achieved an accuracy of 0.93, precision of 0.89, recall of 0.84, and F1 score of 0.87 at a 15 min tolerance. In the independent Abbott dataset, precision, recall, and F1 score (mean ± SD) were 0.87 ± 0.11, 0.83 ± 0.11, and 0.85 ± 0.11 at a 15 min tolerance, and 0.95 ± 0.06, 0.91 ± 0.08, and 0.93 ± 0.07 at a 30 min tolerance. Model-predicted and recorded postprandial AUCs were highly correlated, and predicted AUCs showed similar associations with glycemic variability metrics. Automated meal-event identification may reduce reliance on manual food logging and enable scalable assessment of postprandial glycemic exposure.

papers.title: Phytochemical composition and antioxidant activity of dry pod Mareko Fana pepper ( Capsicum annuum L.) cultivated across agro-ecological districts in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia
papers.abstract: Capsicum annuum L. cv. Mareko Fana is a major commercial spice crop widely cultivated in West Gojjam, Northwest Ethiopia, where it is valued for its pungency, nutritional quality, and bioactive compounds. However, information on the phytochemical composition and antioxidant potential of its dried pods remains limited. This study presents the first systematic evaluation of dried Mareko Fana pepper produced in three major growing districts of West Gojjam: Bure Zuria, Jabitehnan, and Dembecha. Composite pod samples were extracted with 80% aqueous ethanol and analyzed for total phenolic content (TPC), total flavonoid content (TFC), ascorbic acid content (AAC), and antioxidant activity using the DPPH radical scavenging assay. Significant differences were observed among districts (p < 0.05). TPC ranged from 8.20 ± 0.45 to 12.97 ± 0.34 mg GAE/g, TFC from 2.56 ± 0.53 to 4.30 ± 0.50 mg QE/g, and AAC from 23.77 ± 0.22 to 34.22 ± 0.32 mg/ 100 g. Samples from Bure Zuria exhibited the highest phytochemical concentrations and strongest antioxidant activity (IC₅₀ = 21.84 µg/mL), whereas Dembecha samples showed the lowest activity (IC₅₀ = 72.35 µg/ mL). Strong negative correlations between IC₅₀ and TPC (r = − 0.996) and TFC (r = − 0.985) indicate that phenolic compounds are among the primary contributors to antioxidant activity. These findings identify Bure Zuria as a promising source of high-quality pepper for nutritional and industrial applications.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification, evolutionary characterisation and stress-responsive dynamics of SIZ1-type SUMO E3 ligase gene family in bread wheat ( Triticum aestivum L.)
papers.abstract: SUMOylation, a key post-translational modification in plants, modulates diverse stress responses through SUMO E3 ligases (SIZ1). The SIZ1 gene family remains uncharacterized in bread wheat (Triticum aestivum L.), despite its proven functional relevance in model systems. A genome-wide survey in bread wheat identified 14 TaSIZ1 genes distributed across homoeologous groups of 1, 3, 4, 5, and 7 in the Chinese Spring reference (IWGSC RefSeq v2.1). These intron-rich TaSIZ1 genes, containing 14–17 exons, encode nuclear-localized, hydrophilic SIZ proteins (pI: 4.89–6.60) that carry a conserved zf-MIZ1/SP-RING domain. The TaSIZ1 family expanded predominantly through whole-genome and dispersed duplications under purifying selection (Ka/Ks < 1). Synteny and orthology among wheat, barley, rice, maize, and sorghum SIZ1 genes further supported evolutionary conservation, with strong purifying selection (Ka/Ks: 0.09–0.53). Promoter analysis revealed abundant stress- and hormone-responsive cis-acting elements (ABRE, MBS, ARE, GT1), along with major transcription factor binding sites for members of the AP2/ERF, bZIP, MIKC_MADS, and MYB families. Expression profiling showed higher basal activity of TaSIZ1-1 A, TaSIZ1-1B, TaSIZ1-1D, TaSIZ1-3B, and TaSIZ1-3D across multiple tissues, with stress-dependent induction particularly under heat, combined drought–heat stress, powdery mildew infection, and leaf rust infection. Our study showed that TaSIZ1 genes are structurally conserved but functionally divergent across homoeologs and genotypes. This study provides the first comprehensive framework for understanding TaSIZ1 regulation in wheat and suggests candidate genes for multi-stress engineering and wheat breeding.

papers.title: Late-fusion radiomics with multi-sequence MRI distinguishes benign from malignant ovarian tumors: a two-center study
papers.abstract: Preoperative differentiation of benign from malignant ovarian tumors guides surgical planning, but single-sequence radiomics models leave complementary MRI information unused, and whether fusion should occur before or after modelling is unresolved. We studied 268 lesions from 231 patients at two centers; borderline tumors were grouped with malignant tumors, so “malignant” denotes the combined malignant/borderline endpoint (45 of 225 lesions in the training cohort and 9 of 43 in the external cohort). Center 1 (225 lesions) was the training cohort, analysed with patient-level five-fold GroupKFold cross-validation, and Center 2 (43 lesions) the external cohort, evaluated once. For four sequences (T1WI, T2WI fs, DWI, CE-T1WI), 1,197 PyRadiomics features per sequence were selected within each training fold, and the algorithm with the highest mean cross-validated AUC was carried forward. Early fusion concatenated and re-selected the features for logistic regression; late fusion averaged the four models with equal log-odds weights. Thresholds fixed on out-of-fold training predictions were applied unchanged externally. At those thresholds late fusion had the highest accuracy (0.884), specificity (0.912) and positive predictive value (0.700) and the lowest Brier score (0.143; 0.130 after Platt scaling) of the six models, classifying 3 of 34 benign lesions as malignant, against 16 for the best single sequence and 19 for T2WI fs, at the cost of one more missed malignant lesion (2 versus 1 of 9). Discrimination did not separate them: AUC 0.797 versus 0.820 for T1WI (P = 0.67), with no detectable pairwise difference. Late fusion had the highest net benefit at every threshold from 0.35 to 0.60. A consensus O-RADS reading reached an AUC of 0.920. Decision-level fusion gave a model with no better discrimination than the best single sequence but lower Brier scores and far fewer false positives. Its value is a calibrated probability that can be recomputed locally rather than a higher AUC, and it did not exceed O-RADS; with nine external events these comparisons are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Lived experiences of dietary restriction: a qualitative study of dietary adaptation among Chinese patients with chronic heart failure
papers.abstract: Chronic heart failure (CHF) is a growing global public health challenge. Nutritional imbalance and cardiac cachexia are closely associated with higher rates of hospital readmission and mortality. Appropriate dietary restriction is fundamental to improving clinical outcomes. Although current clinical guidelines provide evidence-based dietary recommendations, patients’ lived experiences and behavioural adaptation processes remain underexplored, particularly in non-Western sociocultural contexts. This study aimed to explore the experiences of dietary restriction among Chinese patients with CHF and to reconstruct the psychological and behavioural adaptation patterns they described. A descriptive qualitative study was conducted at a tertiary cardiovascular hospital in Zhengzhou, China. Fifteen inpatients with CHF were recruited via maximum-variation purposive sampling between September and November 2025 and each completed a single semi-structured interview. Data were analysed using directed content analysis guided by the Patient Health Engagement (PHE) model, combining deductive with inductive coding; data saturation was predefined and reached at the fifteenth interview. Ethical approval was granted, and written informed consent was obtained from all participants. Four core themes and 12 subthemes were identified, representing four interpretative patterns of engagement with dietary restriction reconstructed from participants’ retrospective accounts: Disregard and Stagnation, Shock and Awakening, Compliance and Dependence, and Integration and Autonomy. Participants’ accounts indicated non-linear movement between patterns rather than a fixed sequential progression, and revealed culturally specific tensions relating to family supervision and traditional Chinese food culture. Dietary adaptation in CHF appeared to be a complex, non-linear process rather than straightforward physiological deprivation. The findings offer a pattern-sensitive perspective that may help nurses tailor nutritional support to patients’ described engagement patterns; these patterns are interpretative categories reconstructed from retrospective accounts rather than validated stages or a clinical assessment tool, and longitudinal, multi-centre studies involving family caregivers are needed to validate and extend them.

papers.title: The molecular mechanism of HIF-1α mediated LATS1-YAP axis to exacerbate nerve injury after stroke
papers.abstract: AIS induces irreversible neuronal damage through persistent ischemia and hypoxia. Disulfidptosis has been implicated in synaptic function impairment, yet its regulatory mechanism in AIS cases still remains unclear. Our study investigates the molecular mechanism by which HIF-1α modulates LATS1-YAP axis to regulate disulfidptosis and neuronal injury. We constructed OGD cell models and MCAO mice models to simulate AIS conditions. Bioinformatics analysis, qPCR, WB, COIP, TEM and immunofluorescence were proceeded to elaborate pathway regulation in AIS progressions. LNPs encapsulating YAP siRNA were developed for targeted intervention, in order to explore its effect on neuro-protection post stroke. Our study confirmed that the expression of HIF-1α was obviously up-regulated in brain samples with ischemic and hypoxia by constructing cell/animal models. This factor could suppress LATS1 expression and thereby diminish LATS1-mediated YAP phosphorylation, thus leading to upregulation of YAP. Accordingly this axis induces disulfidptosis and apoptosis in neuronal cells by regulating their mitochondrial homeostasis. This pathological process could aggravate neurological injury in AIS cases by inhibiting synaptic function. Targeted intervention in YAP axis could alleviate nerve injury induced by ischemia/hypoxia and promote their function recovery. HIF-1α could regulate LATS1- DRP1 axis to induce mitochondrial dysfunction and disulfidptosis, thus aggravating neuronal injury after stroke. Targeted inhibition of YAP represents a promising therapeutic strategy for AIS treatment.

papers.title: Digital attack to deceive depth estimation models in autonomous vehicle systems using imperceptible adversarial perturbation
papers.abstract: This study introduces an innovative approach for crafting digital adversarial attacks against deep learning-based depth estimation models, including Monodepth2, MiDaS, and DepthAnythingV2. By leveraging Diffusion Models to generate initial perturbations with realistic textures of the targeted region, Grad-CAM maps to identify critical image areas, and optimization driven by multiple loss functions, digital adversarial perturbation were created to mislead models into predicting incorrect depths. The loss functions encompass perturbation smoothness, visual coherence with the environment (extracted from the feature maps of the VGG19 network), and depth prediction disruption. This method produces highly natural digital perturbations with high visual fidelity, making them challenging to detect. Evaluations on a road dataset demonstrated the approach’s effectiveness in disrupting depth predictions while maintaining a natural and seamless perturbation appearance. Results were analyzed using metrics such as Depth Estimation Error ($$\varepsilon _d$$), Affected Region ($$\mathcal {R}_a$$) and Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). This approach has significant implications for assessing the vulnerability of computer vision systems in real-world scenarios, such as autonomous vehicles.

papers.title: Preliminary ICP-OES assessment of trace elements in soil and water from selected coastal sites in Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh
