papers.abstract: This reconnaissance study examined selected trace elements in corresponding coastal soil and water samples from Cox’s Bazar, Bangladesh, using inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES). Five paired soil and water samples were collected during one dry-season survey and analyzed using ICP-OES. The analysis examined Cd, Pb, As, Cr, Cu, Fe, Mn, K, Ca, Mg, Zn, Co, and Se. Instrumental responses attributable to Cd were observed in the water samples; however, these responses occurred at or below the instrumental quantification limit and were therefore interpreted as screening-level evidence rather than definitive quantitative concentrations. Most other potentially toxic elements were below analytical detection limits. Quantitative soil contamination and ecological-risk conclusions were not retained because the concentration basis and applicable analytical limits could not be adequately reconciled. This study provides paired soil–water observations from five selected coastal locations and identifies analytical and sampling requirements for further investigation. Confirmatory monitoring requires improved Cd quantification, broader spatial coverage, and repeated seasonal sampling.

papers.title: NAFMR-Net: neuro-anatomical frequency memory reconstruction network for reliability-aware brain MRI super-resolution
papers.abstract: Brain Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) super-resolution is significant as it helps to create clearer images of the brain and makes the patient's journey of undergoing a MRI scan a little less uncomfortable and time consuming. Existing methods for enhancing image quality are mainly based on the acquisition of general high-frequency image information, but fail to accurately capture some of the important structures of specific brain regions and can create false structures that could mislead physicians. In order to address these issues, in this paper, the proposed NAFMR-Net (Neuro-Anatomical Frequency Memory Reconstruction Network) to accurately reconstruct brain MRI images with more useful information. The Neuro-Anatomical Frequency Memory Module is one of the major components of the new approach. This module will learn and store representative feature patterns in the frequency domain from the training MRI data to facilitate anatomically consistent reconstruction. This will enable the system to identify and employ the appropriate information to reconstruct images, providing more natural and realistic images. Also vital is the Reliability-Aware Module which helps to prevent the system from adding information not relevant to the situation and to minimize odd elements in the pictures. The method also features a Neuro-Frequency Consistency Loss that ensures consistency of the information of the new images with the original scans. The method is tested on real brain MRI data and is compared with other methods, and it is found that NAFMR-Net can improve the clarity of MRI images while preserving the important brain structure, and has advantages over the other methods. Across the four evaluated test datasets, NAFMR-Net achieved PSNR values of 38.54–39.82 dB, SSIM values of 0.981–0.988, RMSE values of 0.009–0.012, HFEN values of 0.097–0.114, EPI values of 0.958–0.972, NFCS values of 0.946–0.963, and HSR values of 95.8–97.5%. They are average test-partition performances of the whole experiment, conducted under the protocol listed above. The results show that the brain MR reconstruction performance with the investigated synthetic degradation setting is promising when using the reference data; however, further testing with realistic MRI degradation, prospectively collected LR data, radiologist assessment and subsequent diagnostic tasks is still needed before clinical use can be recommended.

papers.title: Interpretable federated multi-agent framework for energy-efficient resource management and predictive service optimization in industrial IoT networks
papers.abstract: Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) networks operating across distributed edge, fog, and cloud tiers face persistent challenges in energy-efficient resource management, accurate service demand prediction, and transparent allocation decision-making, as existing approaches address these challenges independently while lacking privacy preservation and interpretability. To overcome these limitations, an interpretable federated multi-agent system is proposed, in which heterogeneous operational data collected from distributed IIoT nodes undergoes structured preprocessing to produce high-quality feature representations. This is followed by Quantization-based Chained Privacy-Preserving Federated Learning (QC-PPFL) for collaborative model training without exposing raw industrial data. The Evolutionary Adversarial Autoencoder with Deep Spatial Pyramid Diffractive Neural Network (EAA-DSPDNN) is utilized for intelligent multi-agent resource monitoring and predictive service optimization across all tiers. Corrective Direction Particle Swarm Optimization (CDPSO) is then applied for constraint-aware allocation fine-tuning, while Trust-Aware Explainable Artificial Intelligence (TA-XAI) generates human-interpretable, trust-scored justifications for every allocation decision. Experimental evaluation against eight baseline methods demonstrates that the proposed system achieves a Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR) of 99.1%, throughput of 132.5 Mbps, latency of 92.3 ms, and a Quality of Service (QoS) score of 99.4, alongside task completion rate of 98.76%, resource utilization of 96.34%, prediction accuracy of 97.89%, and service reliability of 98.43%, consistently outperforming all compared methods. These results confirm that integrating privacy-preserving FL, multi-agent intelligence, constrained optimization, and decision transparency enables robust, energy-efficient, and trustworthy IIoT resource management across dynamic heterogeneous three-tier industrial deployments.

papers.title: Association of creatinine–cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rate with incident stroke in CHARLS and HRS
papers.abstract: Whether creatinine–cystatin C-based estimated glomerular filtration rate provides consistent information on incident stroke across populations remains uncertain. We analyzed 15,773 stroke-free adults from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS; n = 6,950) and the US Health and Retirement Study (HRS; n = 8,823), comparing the CKD-EPI (2021) creatinine–cystatin and EKFC creatinine–cystatin with eGFRcr. Associations were examined using Cox regression, restricted cubic splines, and Fine–Gray competing-risk models. During follow-up, 640 CHARLS and 219 h participants reported incident stroke. Per 1-mL/min/1.73 m² increase, adjusted hazard ratios for CKD-EPI (2021) creatinine–cystatin were 0.994 (95% CI, 0.988–0.999) in CHARLS and 0.987 (0.979–0.995) in HRS; corresponding estimates for EKFCcreatinine–cystatin were 0.990 (0.982–0.997) and 0.983 (0.973–0.994). These associations persisted after accounting for competing mortality. Mendelian randomization findings varied across kidney traits and stroke subtypes. In exploratory prediction analyses, the combined equations yielded numerically higher validation AUCs than creatinine-based eGFR (CHARLS, 0.695–0.698 versus 0.643; HRS, 0.679 versus 0.634), although discrimination was modest. Combined creatinine–cystatin C eGFR was consistently associated with incident stroke across cohorts, but its incremental predictive value remains uncertain.

papers.title: A p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy credibility multi-criteria group decision-making model for sustainable building material selection based on extended IRPA and MOWSCER
papers.abstract: Sustainable Building Material Selection (SBMS) is a complex Multi-Criteria Group Decision-Making (MCGDM) problem characterized by uncertain assessments of experts and causal relationships among criteria. However, existing decision methods for SBMS have some limitations, such as overlooking the credibility of experts’ judgments, ignoring the impacts of causal relationships among criteria on the importance of each criterion, and failing to capture the psychological behaviors and nonlinear perceptions of experts. To address these issues, this study develops an integrated MCGDM framework that combines p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy credibility sets (p, q-QOFCS), the Method of Weighting in the Structure of Cause and Effect Relationships (MOWSCER) and the Integrative Reference Point Approach (IRPA). First, the p, q-QOFCS is utilized to represent experts’ assessments by capturing membership, non-membership, and their respective credibility degrees. Second, MOWSCER is extended to the p, q-QOFCS environment to determine criteria weights, which accounts for causal relationships among criteria. Third, experts’ weights are derived via the p, q-quasirung orthopair fuzzy correlation coefficient (p, q-QOFCCC) combined with a similarity-based approach. Fourth, the IRPA is combined with p, q-QOFCS to rank the Sustainable Building Materials (SBMs), so as to consider experts’ self-defined reference points and nonlinear perceptions. Then, the proposed framework is applied to an illustrative case study of sustainable wall covering material selection for a university renovation project. The recycled plastic panels are the optimal choice, followed by magnesium oxide boards, recycled gypsum boards, cork panels, and bamboo fiber panels. Finally, sensitivity analysis reveals that the final ranking remains stable under variations in parameters p, q, credibility degrees, criteria weights, experts’ weights, and reference points. Meanwhile, comparative analysis against existing methods demonstrates the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed framework. The findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework as a reliable and practical decision-support tool for facility managers, construction companies, and policymakers to integrate uncertainty, credibility, and expert psychological behavior into sustainable material selection.

papers.title: Limitations of conventional Caco-2 permeability assays for macrocyclic peptides and the potential utility of pre-incubation
papers.abstract: Macrocyclic peptides (MCPs) have attracted considerable interest as therapeutic agents for intracellular targets. However, many MCPs occupy the beyond-rule-of-five (bRo5) chemical space and are characterized by low membrane permeability and high lipophilicity, making permeability assessment challenging. The influence of intracellular distribution on Caco-2 permeability measurements of low-permeability MCPs remains poorly understood. In this study, we compared conventional and pre-incubation Caco-2 permeability assays using a panel of eight macrocyclic peptides. Under conventional conditions, intracellular drug amounts increased during the measurement period, while basolateral transport rates changed over time. Following pre-incubation, intracellular amount ratios were lower, basolateral transport rate ratios were closer to unity, and basolateral transport profiles appeared more linear. Total recovery ranged from 7.5% to 103.6% under conventional conditions and from 77.7% to 111.2% following pre-incubation. Permeability values could be determined for all compounds following pre-incubation, whereas one low-permeability compound could not be quantified under conventional conditions. Positive correlations between Caco-2 permeability (Papp) and fraction absorbed in mice (Fa) were observed under both assay conditions, although permeability estimates differed between assay formats. The observed differences in intracellular amount ratios and basolateral transport rate ratios are consistent with previous concepts suggesting that intracellular distribution can influence transport profiles and permeability assessment. These findings suggest that pre-incubation may provide an additional option for evaluating low-permeability macrocyclic peptides that are difficult to characterize using conventional Caco-2 permeability assays.

papers.title: Compensatory online aggressive behavior is associated with psychological distress through emotional venting and negative affect duration, moderated by empathy
papers.abstract: Social media surrounding competitive sports events provides a highly emotional context in which aggressive expression may coexist with psychological distress. This cross-sectional study examined the association between compensatory online aggressive behavior (COAB) and psychological distress (PD), focusing on perceived emotional venting (PEV), negative affect duration (NAD), and empathy (EP). Data from 442 adult social media users were analyzed using structural equation modeling with 5,000 bias-corrected bootstrap resamples. COAB was positively associated with PD (B = 0.219, 95% BC CI [0.121, 0.314]). Significant indirect associations were observed through PEV (B = 0.086, 95% BC CI [0.047, 0.133]), NAD (B = 0.053, 95% BC CI [0.026, 0.090]), and the serial PEV → NAD pathway (B = 0.020, 95% BC CI [0.009, 0.036]). The COAB × EP interaction was negative (B = − 0.185, 95% BC CI [− 0.355, − 0.016]), indicating a weaker positive COAB–PD association at higher EP levels. These findings are consistent with an association-based framework in which perceived venting and persistent negative affect are relevant to the psychological correlates of COAB, while empathy may function as a potential buffering condition.

papers.title: Red-light-mediated transcriptional reprogramming associated with specialized metabolite accumulation in Eryngium foetidum L. in vitro culture
papers.abstract: Light quality is a crucial environmental modulator of specialized metabolism in medicinal plants; however, the molecular processes driving red light-induced enhancement of secondary metabolite accumulation in Eryngium foetidum L. remain mainly unknown. In this study, comparative de novo transcriptome sequencing was used to uncover the regulatory networks governing secondary- metabolite biosynthesis in plants exposed to red light. High-throughput sequencing resulted in a high-quality transcriptome with 104,040 transcripts, 92,253 unigenes, and 85,550 CDSs, of which 65,323 CDSs were successfully annotated to multiple databases. The differential gene expression analysis identified 3,279 highly regulated CDSs and 1,330 CDSs exclusively expressed in red-light-treated plants. KEGG Pathway enrichment and expression profiling indicated coordinated-regulation of phenylpropanoid, flavonoid, and terpenoid biosynthesis through the overexpression of important key enzymes, indicating widespread transcriptional reprogramming in response to red light. A total of 2,610 transcription factors (TFs) encoding CDSs belonging to 54 TF families were identified with bHLH, followed by MYB-related being the most abundant. The study provides the genome-wide de novo transcriptomic resource for E. foetidum and suggests that red light promotes specialized metabolism by coordinated-regulation of TFs and biosynthetic pathways, providing molecular targets for functional genomics, metabolic engineering, and cultivar improvements.

papers.title: A human-machine collaborative double-nested voting model, RC-voting, enables accurate monitoring of key rice growth traits across critical developmental stages
papers.abstract: Accurate and timely monitoring of rice growth is essential for precision cultivation, particularly in complex plateau environments where field conditions are heterogeneous. In this study, a human-machine collaborative double-nested model, RC-Voting (Random Search and Cross-Validation based Voting), was developed to monitor rice plant height (PH), leaf area, and SPAD values using multispectral image features. Field experiments were conducted in 2024 using the rice cultivar Dianheyou 615. Band statistical features, texture features, and vegetation indices were extracted, and Pearson correlation analysis was used to identify sensitive features. These analyses, together with the observed trait dynamics, determined the selected stage-restricted datasets for model construction: PH data from tillering and jointing, SPAD data from tillering through panicle elongation, and leaf area data from tillering through panicle elongation. Multiple linear regression (MLR), random forest regression (RFR), AdaBoost, and XGBoost were first established as base models. A Stacking ensemble was first employed to integrate the four aforementioned machine learning models for rice growth monitoring. Subsequently, a Voting strategy was applied to combine the Stacking model with the same four base learners, forming a nested monitoring framework. Finally, random search and cross-validation were utilized to optimize this nested Voting model, yielding the final rice growth monitoring model, RC-Voting. The RC-Voting model achieved the best overall performance, with R² values of 0.9387, 0.9281, and 0.9485 for PH, leaf area, and SPAD, respectively. These results indicate that integrating multispectral image features with nested ensemble learning can improve the monitoring of key rice growth traits and provide technical support for precision rice cultivation in plateau environments.

papers.title: miR-2355-5p restrains NSCLC tumorigenesis and metastasis through suppressing the HNF4G-SPTBN2 regulatory axis
papers.abstract: Malignant progression in NSCLC is influenced by regulatory pathways that connect miRNA loss with transcription factor activation and effector-gene expression. This study tested the hypothesis that miR-2355-5p suppresses NSCLC progression by targeting HNF4G and thereby reducing SPTBN2 transcription. TCGA-LUAD expression resources, survival tools, target-prediction platforms, and transcription factor motif analysis were combined with validation in 40 matched NSCLC tissue pairs. A549 and H1299 cells were subjected to miR-2355-5p gain- or loss-of-function, HNF4G silencing or re-expression, and SPTBN2 re-expression under HNF4G knockdown. Reporter assays, Ago2-RIP, ChIP-qPCR, proliferation, migration, and invasion assays, and in vivo modeling were then performed. miR-2355-5p was reduced in NSCLC samples, whereas HNF4G and SPTBN2 were increased and associated with worse survival. miR-2355-5p showed inverse relationships with HNF4G and SPTBN2, while HNF4G was positively related to SPTBN2. Increasing miR-2355-5p suppressed growth, motility, and invasion, whereas miR-2355-5p blockade enhanced these traits. Mechanistic experiments supported miR-2355-5p-mediated regulation of the HNF4G 3’UTR and demonstrated HNF4G occupancy at the SPTBN2 promoter. HNF4G re-expression partially reversed miR-2355-5p-mediated suppression, whereas SPTBN2 re-expression partially restored invasive capacity after HNF4G depletion. Mouse models showed reduced tumor growth, Ki-67/HNF4G/SPTBN2 staining, pulmonary bioluminescence, and pulmonary tumor nodules after miR-2355-5p restoration. miR-2355-5p inhibits NSCLC progression by suppressing HNF4G and thereby attenuating HNF4G-dependent SPTBN2 transcription.

papers.title: Medicinal plant use among 170,564 Iranianadults in the PERSIAN Cohort Study
papers.abstract: Medicinal plants, a cornerstone of numerous traditional healing systems, are widely used in Iran. However, national-level data on their current usage patterns remain scarce. This study aims to evaluate the prevalence and patterns of reported medicinal plant use in Iran and explore the factors influencing their usage. This cross-sectional study utilized baseline data from 170,564 participants of the prospective epidemiological research studies in Iran (PERSIAN), a nationwide survey of Iranian adults aged 35–70 across 18 cohort sites. Data collection included gathering biological samples, conducting physical examinations, and administering a structured questionnaire. Participants were asked whether they used medicinal plants (self-reported use). The variables analyzed encompassed sociodemographic factors and chronic conditions. Statistical analyses were performed using Stata software, employing descriptive statistics and robust Poisson regression. The crude prevalence of reported medicinal plant use was 75.0% (95% CI: 74.6% to 75.4%). Zataria multiflora, Borago officinalis, and Mentha piperita were the most commonly used plants. Reported medicinal plant use was more common among older adults (1.12, 95%CI: 1.11–1.14, P < 0.001), female gender (1.12, 95%CI: 1.10–1.13, P < 0.001), married individuals (1.04, 95%CI: 1.03–1.06, P < 0.001), rural residence (1.21, 95%CI: 1.20–1.23, P < 0.001), those with higher education (1.20, 95%CI: 1.18–1.22, P < 0.001), and high socioeconomic status (1.25, 95%CI: 1.23–1.27, P < 0.001). Usage was also notably high among individuals with chronic conditions, particularly fatty liver disease (82.0%). Additionally, significant variations were observed in utilization patterns across various ethnicities, with Fars participants exhibiting the highest rate at 87.4%. This study demonstrates a high prevalence and diverse patterns of reported medicinal plant use among adults participating in the PERSIAN Cohort. These findings highlight the importance of understanding factors associated with medicinal plant use and may inform future health policy and planning regarding the safe and evidence-based use of medicinal plants in healthcare settings.

papers.title: Genotype screening and machine learning-assisted yield prediction under varied irrigation in sorghum
papers.abstract: Sorghum is a major drought-tolerant cereal grown globally in many parts of the world in arid and semi-arid region. This study examined the effect of water deficit on key agronomic and physiological traits in ten forage genotypes under three irrigation levels (normal, mild, severe). Various method such as additive main effects and multiplicative interaction, genotype plus genotype × environment biplot, and best linear unbiased prediction were used to identify superior genotypes. Yield predictions were improvd by the use of linear regression (LR) and Random Forest (RF). The Genotype G1 had the highest fresh yield (FY) and dry yield (DY) at harvest 1 under normal irrigation (113.9 and 29.7 t ha−1, respectively), but the lowest DY under severe stress at harvest 2 (4.5 t ha−1). For FY, four genotypes had values above the overall mean with G1 being highest at 68.3 t ha−1, while top five genotypes for DY were G8, G9, G1, G3, and G6 (16.8–15.2 t ha−1). The prediction of LR and RF predicted FY and DY from genotype, water stress, and harvest. RF outperformed LR (FY: RF R² train 0.936, test 0.894 vs. LR 0.58, 0.596; DY: RF R² train 0.944, test 0.913 vs. LR 0.72, 0.647), supporting machine learning for drought-tolerance breeding, though multi-environment validation is needed.

papers.title: Pan-cancer analysis of CCDC69 prognostic and immunotherapy predictive value with functional validation in lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Coiled-coil domain-containing 69 (CCDC69) remains an understudied gene in oncology with poorly characterized pan-cancer expression patterns, prognostic relevance, and therapeutic implications. This study systematically investigated CCDC69’s multi-omics landscape across 33 malignancies using TCGA, GTEx, CPTAC, and HPA datasets, revealing significant downregulation at both mRNA and protein levels that correlated with advanced tumor stages. Survival analyses via Cox regression and Kaplan–Meier methods demonstrated that high CCDC69 expression predicted improved outcomes in multiple cancer types. Single-cell analysis using data from the TISCH database revealed CCDC69 expression across immune, stromal, and malignant cells. Pan-cancer immune and microenvironment analyses utilizing TIMER2.0, ssGSEA, ESTIMATE, and multiple deconvolution algorithms demonstrated that CCDC69 expression strongly correlated with cytotoxic CD8+ T cell infiltration, while GSEA linked high CCDC69 to immune activation. Clinically, high CCDC69 expression was associated with improved response to immune checkpoint blockade in immunotherapy cohorts. Experimental validation in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) using immunohistochemistry confirmed that CCDC69 downregulation was linked to poor prognosis. Additionally, immunofluorescence demonstrated CCDC69 protein co-localization with CD8+ T cells in tumor tissues, and CCDC69 overexpression in T cells enhanced their cytotoxicity against LUAD cells. Furthermore, functional assays in LUAD cell lines demonstrated that CCDC69 overexpression suppressed proliferation and cell cycle progression, whereas knockdown had the opposite effect. Mechanistically, CCDC69 bound to Aurora kinase B (AURKB) and modulated its expression, supporting CCDC69 as a tumor suppressor. Collectively, CCDC69 emerges as a pan-cancer biomarker with dual roles in immune modulation and tumor suppression, highlighting its potential for immunotherapy stratification and therapeutic targeting in precision oncology.

papers.title: Telomere length measurement in immunophenotypically defined human leukocyte subsets using multiparametric flow-FISH
papers.abstract: Telomere length (TL) is an important biomarker of the cell replicative history with applications in aging research, telomere biology disorders and hematological malignancies. Flow cytometry-fluorescence in situ hybridization (flow-FISH) is a reference method for TL measurement, but the simultaneous analysis of multiple leukocyte subsets remains technically challenging. Using a commercially available telomere probe flow-FISH kit, we developed a multiparametric flow-FISH assay to simultaneously measure relative TL (RTL) in several leukocyte subsets. Cross-linking with bis(sulfosuccinimidyl) suberate (BS3) before hybridization improved the retention of immunophenotypic marker staining during the procedure without detectable effect on the telomere signal, and imaging flow cytometry showed a predominantly nuclear probe signal in each subset. In controls, RTL measured by flow-FISH correlated with qPCR TL in sorted T cells (r = 0.595, q = 0.029) and declined with age in T cells (q = 0.008). In five patients with chronic myeloid leukemia and five with chronic lymphocytic leukemia, descriptive analyses suggested lower neutrophil and monocyte RTL in myeloid leukemia and heterogeneous RTL in CD16⁻ SSClow cells in lymphocytic leukemia. This proof-of-concept study supports the feasibility of cell type-specific TL measurement in a single assay and provides a basis for investigating telomere length in hematological disorders.

papers.title: Traceable acquisition and processing workflow for multispectral drone monitoring of orchards
papers.abstract: Reliable interpretation and reuse of UAV-derived orchard maps depend on clear documentation of image acquisition and processing. An evidence-aware reporting framework was developed for RGB and multispectral surveys using the DJI Mavic 3 Multispectral and applied retrospectively to records from three durian orchard blocks at two locations in Sarawak, Malaysia. The framework addresses flight geometry, illumination and radiometric records, RTK positioning and ground-control documentation, image processing, metadata retention and quality assurance. The assessment identified documented mission settings, processing-software roles and raster products, but did not establish a complete file-level link between source images, saved processing parameters and individual raster exports. Numerical scaling of analytical bands, independent positional accuracy and field-based agronomic validation also remained unverified. These findings highlight the distinction between documented acquisition and processing practices, computational reproducibility and independent measurement validation. The framework provides a structured basis for assessing UAV data provenance and identifying the records needed to support future reproducible orchard monitoring.

papers.title: Problematic smartphone use and smartphone-related psychological distress: self-discrepancy, emotional exhaustion, and online psychological safety
papers.abstract: Problematic smartphone use has become a major concern among university students. Yet, the psychological pathways associated with the relationship between problematic smartphone use and smartphone-related psychological distress remain insufficiently understood. This study integrates Self-Discrepancy Theory and Psychological Safety Theory. It examines Perceived Self-Discrepancy and digital emotional exhaustion as parallel indirect pathways, with perceived psychological safety online examined as a contextual moderator. The study used a time-lagged design with 648 university students from Saudi Arabia and structural equation modeling for data analysis. Results indicated that problematic smartphone use was positively correlated with Perceived Self-Discrepancy and digital emotional exhaustion, which in turn were positively correlated with smartphone-related psychological distress. Both pathways showed significant indirect associations. Further, the positive relationships between Perceived Self-Discrepancy and smartphone-related psychological distress, as well as digital emotional exhaustion and smartphone-related psychological distress, were found to be weaker at higher levels of perceived psychological safety. This study’s results provide evidence of complementary cognitive and affective processes and perceived psychological safety online as an important contextual condition. The paper brings together cognitive, emotional, and interpersonal elements in one place, thereby offering insights into digital well-being and recommendations for university support programs that address these various dimensions.

papers.title: Prevalence and factors associated with moderate acute malnutrition among children aged 0–2 years in India: insights from national family health survey-5
papers.abstract: Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) remains a persistent yet under-recognised public health challenge in India. If left untreated, MAM can progress to severe acute malnutrition (SAM), increasing the risk of morbidity and mortality among young children. This study aimed to assess the prevalence and factors associated with MAM among Indian children aged 0–2 years using data from the National Family Health Survey (NFHS-5) in India between 2019 and 2021. We defined MAM as a weight-for-length z-score (WLZ) between ≥-3 and ≤-2 standard deviations. We estimated weighted prevalence and performed multivariable logistic regression to identify factors associated with MAM, accounting for sampling weights, clustering, and strata. The study analysed data from 87,917 children. Overall, 22.5% of the children were wasted, of whom 13.0% had MAM. Significant regional variation was observed between the states, with the lowest prevalence in northern India. In the adjusted logistic regression analysis, children aged 12–24 months had lower odds of MAM than younger infants (aOR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.69–0.82), and normal birth weight (aOR: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.69–0.82) and macrosomia (aOR: 0.58; 95% CI: 0.44–0.75) were associated with lower odds of MAM compared with low birth weight. Higher odds of MAM were observed among children from the poorest wealth quintile (aOR: 1.36; 95% CI: 1.14–1.61), scheduled tribe households (aOR: 1.13; 95% CI: 1.01–1.26), those with recent diarrhoeal episodes (aOR: 1.19; 95% CI: 1.07–1.33), mothers with no formal education (aOR: 1.15; 95% CI: 1.02–1.31), and maternal underweight (aOR: 1.33; 95% CI: 1.23–1.44). Moderate acute malnutrition remains a substantial burden among young children in India, driven primarily by young infants, low birth weight, maternal undernutrition, and socioeconomic and tribal disadvantage. This highlights the importance of early infancy as a critical window for targeted intervention.

papers.title: Site-specific diel patterns and short-term predictability in fishway video annotations
papers.abstract: Fixed underwater cameras are increasingly used to monitor fish migration, but the resulting video archives are large, heterogeneous, and costly to annotate. Human annotations remain the most reliable ground truth for fish species, size, and behaviour, and their site-specific structure may provide useful reference information for the quality control of human and automated annotation outputs. Here, we investigate whether site-specific patterns in human annotations can provide a statistical basis for annotation quality control while assessing the short-term predictability of fish passage. We analyse data from three fishway monitoring sites in large freshwater rivers in Germany as availability-aware time series, considering only hours with available video observations. We first characterise size–behaviour and species–behaviour relationships together with diel (hour-of-day) activity patterns, and assess their consistency across sites with different species composition, abundance, and recording continuity. We then construct hourly count series and, using only past observations, fit Gaussian process models to forecast fish passage over the next 24 hours. Across all sites, fish passage showed a strong and consistent diel pattern, with activity concentrated between approximately 04:00 and 18:00, including peaks around 04:00–06:00 and 14:00–17:00, and was dominated by small cyprinids and upstream movements. Size and species primarily influenced the magnitude of activity, with comparatively little effect on its timing, and similar temporal structures were observed despite otherwise large site-to-site differences. Forecasts captured the broad diel structure but had limited ability to localise brief, spike-like passage events when recent observations were sparse. Predictive uncertainty was generally well calibrated, and forecast performance appeared more closely associated with recording continuity than with the total length of the training history. These results establish a transparent statistical baseline for hourly forecasting and identify interpretable, site-specific patterns that may provide useful reference information for the quality control of human and automated annotation outputs.

papers.title: ​Integrating DNA-based and morphological approaches improves biodiversity characterization of vulnerable marine ecosystems at Flemish Cap
papers.abstract: Recognized as biodiversity hotspots and by their high susceptibility to human activities, Vulnerable Marine Ecosystems (VMEs) are increasingly targeted for protection from fishing practices, particularly bottom trawling, which may impact benthic communities. Safeguarding these ecosystems requires non-destructive tools to describe and map seabed biodiversity at a faster pace than current imaged-based technologies. Environmental DNA (eDNA) is a promising approach, requiring only water sampling. However, its effectiveness relies on public DNA databases, which remain incomplete and error-prone, particularly for invertebrates in understudied habitats. One such area is the Flemish Cap, an isolated seamount with a long history of exploitation and home to several VMEs species indicators, yet still poorly documented. To address this gap, a 2022 survey collected and identified marine invertebrates through classical taxonomy and DNA barcoding (COI and 16 S), providing essential reference data to support non-invasive conservation strategies. Morphological analysis classified 434 specimens into 154 taxonomic categories, including 88 species-level taxa and 66 low-resolution categories. DNA barcoding revealed that although over 85.8% of sequences matched public database entries at 97% identity, only 32.9% yielded consistent assignments across markers and repositories. Integrative refinement improved taxonomic resolution in 140 specimens and increased the formal species-level inventory from 88 to 123 taxa, or to 133 taxa when open-nomenclature assignments were included. Persistent challenges remain for Porifera and Cnidaria, reflecting database gaps and amplification biases. Our results demonstrate that integrative taxonomy markedly improves assignment success and provides essential baseline data for deep-sea biodiversity assessments. By strengthening molecular reference resources for VME indicator taxa, this study directly supports the development of robust, non-invasive ecological indicators for long-term monitoring and conservation of vulnerable deep-sea habitats.

papers.title: Study on the progressive wear model of aerospace sliding splines after nitriding strengthening considering gradient hardness distribution
papers.abstract: Sliding splines serve as key components in aerospace transmission systems, undertaking both power transmission and axial motion. Under high-speed rotation and limited lubricant supply, tooth surface wear degrades transmission accuracy and affects service reliability. Therefore, accurately characterizing its wear evolution is essential for high-speed transmission systems. Nitrided splines exhibit a hardness gradient from the surface to the substrate. As wear proceeds, softer subsurface material is progressively exposed, which may accelerate wear. This change in contact surface hardness cannot be represented when a constant hardness is assumed. In this study, the measured hardness–depth distribution of nitrided spline teeth is incorporated into a progressive wear model, which is coupled with multi-degree-of-freedom dynamic equations established using the lumped parameter method. Depth-dependent friction and equivalent wear coefficients are identified from specimen tests. The accumulated wear is used to update the contact surface hardness, tribological parameters, and tooth flank clearance. Tooth wear is then calculated over 8400 reciprocating cycles at 3000 rpm. The predictions are compared with measurements from a sliding spline test conducted under intermittent drip-oil lubrication. When hardness is held constant, the predicted final wear depths of the internal and external splines are 0.1029 mm and 0.1187 mm, with relative errors of 26.50% and 40.65%, respectively. When the hardness, the equivalent wear coefficient, and the friction coefficient are all held constant, the predicted final wear depths of the internal and external splines are 0.0875 mm and 0.1010 mm, with relative errors of 37.52% and 49.54%, respectively. When the hardness gradient is considered, the corresponding predictions are 0.1500 mm and 0.1875 mm, and the errors are reduced to 7.14% and 6.25%. Improved agreement with the measured wear is thus obtained under the investigated conditions. These results demonstrate the importance of accounting for the progressive exposure of the hardness gradient and provide a basis for wear prediction and surface strengthening design of sliding spline components.

papers.title: A multi agent simulation of drone volunteer relay delivery for older adults with chronic diseases
papers.abstract: The continuous supply of prescription medications is critical for older adults with chronic diseases, yet last-mile logistics often fail in aging communities because of mobility barriers, building-access constraints, and workforce shortages. This study evaluates a Drone-Volunteer Relay Delivery (DVRD) configuration in which UAVs deliver to fixed community relay stations and local volunteers complete the final handover. We use a multi-agent simulation to quantify medication interruption risk under explicitly stated operational assumptions. The model represents older patients, UAVs, and community volunteers, and includes patient-specific interruption tolerance, nonlinear health penalties, stochastic volunteer availability, UAV energy consumption, weather disruption, and thermal exposure during handover. In the base scenario, the simulated Medication Interruption Rate (MIR) was 14.8% for a Direct-to-Home (DTH) UAV configuration and 3.2% for the DVRD configuration; the mean health penalty score decreased by 83.0%. These estimates describe the combined effect of fixed relay infrastructure and volunteer last-mile delivery, not the isolated effect of volunteer participation. Threshold analysis placed the volunteer-availability bottleneck at approximately 0.26 in the base ensemble, and severe wind conditions required payload reduction. The findings suggest that a socio-technical relay configuration may improve simulated medication access in dense aging communities, but the results are model-based and require external empirical validation before deployment.

papers.title: Structural analysis, electronic structure and optical properties of PFN–BST ceramic with photocatalytic and antimicrobial applications
papers.abstract: The article reports structural analysis, electronic structure, photocatalytic and antimicrobial properties of (Ba0.8Sr0.2)TiO3 modified Pb(Fe0.5Nb0.5)O3 oxide manufactured from a solid-state channel. Rietveld study showed a tetragonal structure as the major perovskite phase. Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy was performed to detect Ti–O and Nb–O vibrations. The phonon vibrations, structural compositions along with broadening of modes were examined from Raman spectroscopy. The surface microstructure and purity were examined using field emission scanning electron microscopy (FESEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS). Atomic force microscopy (AFM) was further employed to gain an insight into topographical and morphological characteristics. The chemical environment of the involved elements was studied by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The Ti K-edge (4966 eV), Fe K-edge (7112 eV) and Pb L3-edge (13035 eV) X-ray absorption near edge spectroscopy (XANES) and extended X-ray absorption fine structure spectroscopy (EXAFS) measurements were conducted to probe the local and electronic structure. UV-visible study showed a band gap of 2.56 eV suitable for optical applications. The influence of oxygen vacancies (OVs), distorted clusters and electronegativity on optical band gap was analysed. The photocatalytic experiment was performed for the degradation of a widely prevalent organic pollutant, methyl orange, under visible illumination, and the compound is expected to be useful in photocatalytic H2 production. A detailed antimicrobial study was carried out to test the efficacy of the material for potential antibacterial application. The antibacterial activity was tested by estimating the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values and zone of inhibition (ZOI) caused by the studied material along with a control antibiotic (Ampicillin) against a variety of bacterial strains.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of machine learning models for multi-class crop recommendation using soil and climate features
papers.abstract: Climate variability is a major constraint on agricultural production, with potential impacts on yields, soil degradation, and economic security. In order to solve this problem, the present study introduces a crop recommendation framework based on machine learning which considers the soil nutrients (N, P, K) and environmental factors (temp, humidity, rainfall, soil pH). The model is built using the publicly available Crop Recommendation dataset from Kaggle which has 2200 samples divided into 22 balanced classes of crops and no missing values. The data were preprocessed to ensure consistency, including Z-score-based outlier detection, standardization of features, and label encoding. The data set was divided into training (70%), validation (15%) and test (15%) sets and five-fold cross-validation was used to check the robustness of the model and its generalization. Random Forest (RF), XGBoost, LightGBM, Deep Neural Network (DNN) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) models were implemented and tuned with hyperparameter tuning using grid search. The accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, and macro F1-score were used to assess performance. Experimental results show that XGBoost and LightGBM models perform better than all the other models. The accuracy of XGBoost is 99.27% and that of LightGBM is nearly the same with 99.22%, which is also very stable in the cross-validation, thus the excellent generalization capability. Cross-validation scores (0.9909, 0.9955, 0.9955, 0.9955, 0.9932) further validate the robustness of ensemble-based approaches. Random Forest has an accuracy of 93% while DNN and MLP have an accuracy of around 98%, which are competitive but less stable than the ensemble methods from trees. The work shows that the optimized gradient boosting is better than deep learning when it comes to structured data from the agricultural domain.The study reveals that gradient boosting models like XGBoost and LightGBM outperformed deep learning models when applied to structured agricultural data sets.The study shows that structured agricultural data sets feature optimized gradient boosting models (XGBoost and LightGBM) that are consistently superior to deep learning models. What is new in this work is that it gives a comprehensive comparative analysis of various ensemble models and deep learning models and gives a strong evidence to choose one model for a crop recommendation system. Real-world noisy data and dynamic agricultural datasets like soil moisture, pest incidence, and temporal variability would be incorporated into the future to improve the applicability of the data.

papers.title: Mechanism of impact energy-enhanced breaking of deep hard rock under condition of rock strength weakening induced by horizontal in-situ stress releasing
papers.abstract: The high rock strength under high in situ stress lead to low rate of penetration in deep formation which restricts the utilization of the oil and gas resources, percussive drilling is the most efficiency method to improve the rock breaking energy. However, research shows that the dynamic rock strength increases under impact load in the condition of the high in situ stress, which is a significantly challenging to improve the rock breaking energy of hard rock in deep wells. Therefore, based on this idea, this paper aims to explore the mechanism of impact energy efficiency-enhanced breaking of hard rock under condition of rock strength weakening induced by horizontal in-situ stress releasing, solving the problem of rock strength improvement under impact load and high confining pressure. Firstly, the stress state during rock breaking is analyzed; secondly, the influence law of confining pressure stress releasing on induced rock strength; finally, impact rock breaking efficiency under condition of confining pressure releasing on the ratio of the shear stress to I1 is evaluated. The results show that the failure of rock is caused by the shear stress, and the shear stress level is determined by the ratio of the shear stress to I1 dominates rock breaking, and same rock breaking efficiency can be achieved under combination of high amplitude & low static load, which could achieve the rock breaking efficiency under relative low weight on bit, providing theoretical support for the research on rock breaking efficiency improving of hard rock in deep wells.

papers.title: Antibacterial, antifungal, antioxidant activities and phenolic composition of Arthrophytum Scoparium flowers
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal activities of flower extracts of Arthrophytum scoparium to provide scientific support for its traditional use. The total polyphenol and flavonoid contents of the extracts were determined, and their antioxidant activities were evaluated (DPPH, ABTS and FRAP). The chemical composition of the butanol extract was further investigated using ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (UHPLC-MS). Antimicrobial activity was assessed against Gram-positive (Staphylococcus aureus) and Gram-negative (Pseudomonas aeruginosa and Escherichia coli) bacterial strains and fungal microorganism (Candida albicans). The aqueous fraction residue (AQE) exhibited the highest total polyphenol content in both the acetone/water and methanol/water extracts, with values of 1633.721 and 1321.557 mg gallic acid equivalents (GAE)/100 g, respectively. The butanol extract (BE) showed the highest flavonoid content, reaching 167.904 and 136.204 mg quercetin equivalents (QE)/100 g in the acetone/water and methanol/water extracts, respectively. The AQE also demonstrated the strongest antioxidant activity in the DPPH, ABTS, and FRAP assays for both solvent systems. UHPLC-MS analysis of the butanol extract identified rutin, hesperidin, and quinic acid as the major compounds. Rutin was the most abundant, with concentrations of 12.678 and 7.004 mg/100 g in the methanol/water and acetone/water extracts, respectively, followed by hesperidin (6.947 and 4.270 mg/100 g) and quinic acid (4.616 and 4.175 mg/100 g). All extracts exhibited antibacterial and antifungal activities against the tested microorganisms, with inhibition zones ranging from 8 to 36 mm. Overall, the findings provide scientific evidence supporting the traditional use of Arthrophytum scoparium flowers for their antioxidant, antibacterial, and antifungal properties.

papers.title: Hearing loss among small-scale metal workers in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
papers.abstract: Small-scale metal industries may place workers at risk of hearing loss due to noise exposure levels that exceed 85dBA. This cross-sectional study assessed hearing loss among 178 male workers exposed to a mean noise level of 97.9 dBA and 72 male workers exposed to a mean noise level of 76.6 dBA. A structured questionnaire was used to obtain demographic and occupational information. Otoscopic examinations were conducted, followed by pure-tone audiometry performed inside a soundproof booth. Hearing loss was defined as a hearing threshold ≥ 25 dB 3000, 4000, or 6000 Hz in either ear. The prevalence of hearing loss was 90.4% in the high-noise exposure group and 41.7% in the low-noise exposure group. In regression analyses, work duration was significantly associated with hearing loss among workers exposed to high noise levels (OR = 1.51; 95%CI: 1.15–1.59), when adjustment for age, previous occupational noise exposure, leisure time noise, and lifestyle factors. The association was even stronger when the analysis was restricted to workers younger than 44 years (OR = 1.51; 95%CI: 1.20–1.90). These findings provide clear evidence of a strong relationship between occupational noise exposure and hearing loss. Preventive measures are urgently needed to reduce noise levels in metal industries and similar work environments.

papers.title: Early red cell distribution width to platelet ratio and clinical outcomes in sepsis associated acute kidney injury
papers.abstract: The red cell distribution width-to-platelet ratio (RPR) has been associated with adverse outcomes in critically ill patients, but its clinical relevance in sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (SA-AKI) remains uncertain. We evaluated the associations of early post-SA-AKI RPR with mortality and renal progression and explored its prognostic performance. This retrospective cohort study included adults with temporally defined SA-AKI from the MIMIC-IV database. The index RPR was calculated from paired red cell distribution width and platelet measurements obtained within 24 h after SA-AKI onset. The primary outcome was 30-day all-cause mortality; secondary outcomes were 90-day all-cause mortality, ICU mortality, and progression to KDIGO stage 3. Cox proportional hazards models were used for 30- and 90-day mortality, whereas ICU mortality and renal progression were analyzed using Fine–Gray competing-risk regression. Restricted cubic splines were used to assess nonlinearity. Exploratory analyses evaluated the stand-alone and incremental prognostic performance of RPR. Among 15,951 patients with SA-AKI, 3,923 died within 30 days, 4,854 within 90 days, and 2,388 died in the ICU. When modeled continuously on the log2 scale, each doubling of RPR was associated with higher 30-day mortality (adjusted HR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.15–1.22), 90-day mortality (HR, 1.18; 95% CI, 1.14–1.21), and ICU mortality (sHR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.14–1.25). Compared with the lowest quartile, the highest RPR quartile was associated with higher 30-day mortality (HR, 1.32; 95% CI, 1.21–1.44), 90-day mortality (HR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.20–1.40), and ICU mortality (sHR, 1.40; 95% CI, 1.25–1.56). Significant nonlinear associations were observed for all three mortality outcomes. In the 24-h renal landmark cohort, RPR was also associated with progression to KDIGO stage 3 (sHR per doubling, 1.17; 95% CI, 1.05–1.30; Q4 vs. Q1, 1.42; 95% CI, 1.07–1.89), without evidence of nonlinearity. RPR alone showed limited discrimination for both 30- and 90-day mortality (AUC, 0.567 for both), and addition of nonlinear RPR to the clinical model increased optimism-corrected AUC by only 0.008 at each time horizon. Early post-SA-AKI RPR was associated with short-term and 90-day mortality and with progression to KDIGO stage 3. Mortality associations were nonlinear, with the lowest risk observed at intermediate RPR levels and higher risk at the upper RPR range. However, RPR provided limited stand-alone discrimination.

papers.title: Implantation site influences tissue response to vaginal meshes in a material dependent manner
papers.abstract: Polypropylene (PP) meshes are associated with significant complications when implanted transvaginally for the treatment of stress urinary incontinence (SUI) and pelvic organ prolapse (POP). Efforts to circumvent this include developing more biocompatible synthetic materials and improving the pre-clinical development pathways. In this study, we compared the tissue response to novel vaginal meshes in a more traditional abdominal wall implantation and a more representative vaginal implantation model. Two novel electrospun poly-urethane (PU) and poly-lactic acid (PLA) materials were implanted in the vesico-vaginal space (VVs) and abdominal wall of female rabbits. Estradiol (E2)-loaded PU (PU-E2) was also implanted to compare it against unloaded PU mesh. A polypropylene (PP) mesh was used as a control. After three months, assessment of the implantation site revealed distinct reactions to the implants between the abdominal wall and vesicovaginal implantation sites. Extrusion and contraction of the meshes were only seen for PP and PLA in the vaginal implantation sites. Histologic examination revealed a mild inflammatory response to both PU and PP meshes in both implantation sites; while a strong inflammatory response was observed for PLA meshes. The capsule formation was similar between all groups and implantation sites, except for a thicker capsule for PP meshes implanted vaginally. Additionally, estradiol loaded PU meshes increased the cell infiltration and blood vessel formation compared to unloaded PU, particularly after vaginal implantation. The tissue response to mesh materials differed between abdominal and vaginal implantation in a material-dependent manner (significant for PLA and PU-E2 but not PP or PU). Implant-related complications were observed only following vaginal implantation. These findings suggest that the implantation site may influence the preclinical evaluation of biomaterials intended for vaginal application. Further studies are warranted to determine whether anatomically relevant implantation models provide additional predictive value for the preclinical assessment of vaginal biomaterials.

papers.title: AI-enabled semantic framework for evaluating institutional activity alignment with the sustainable development goals
papers.abstract: As the number of universities and research institutions adopting the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals continues to rise, there is an increasing demand for systematic methodologies to evaluate whether or not an institution’s activities are contributing positively to global sustainability priorities. However, there are most SDG reporting practices that follows qualitative narratives or manual mapping of activities to SDG targets, limiting scalability, consistency, and reproducibility. This study introduces SDG MetricX, an artificial intelligence–enabled framework designed to evaluate the semantic alignment between institutional activity outcomes and the SDG target system. The framework employs sentence-level semantic embeddings to represent activity descriptions and SDG target statements within a shared vector space, enabling quantitative similarity analysis between activities and the 169 SDG targets. To improve semantic coverage, SDG target descriptions were enriched with additional sustainability-related terminology prior to embedding generation. Similarity distributions reveal clear separation between weak and meaningful semantic associations, while threshold sensitivity analysis demonstrates a stable trade-off between mapping coverage and semantic strength. The resulting indicators quantify SDG engagement through target coverage, SDG coverage, mapping density, and goal-level semantic strength, providing a scalable and reproducible approach for automated SDG alignment assessment. Additionally, the framework incorporates a semantic recommendation mechanism that identifies closely related but unmapped SDG targets based on similarity continuity, enabling refinement of activity outcomes to enhance SDG alignment.

papers.title: Identification of circulating exosomal miRNA signatures and their potential association with tumor burden in feline mammary carcinoma
papers.abstract: Feline mammary carcinoma (FMC) is a highly aggressive malignancy characterized by rapid progression and poor prognosis, yet non-invasive tools for monitoring tumor dynamics remain limited. In this study, we employed an unbiased high-throughput small RNA sequencing approach to profile the miRNA landscape of FMC cells and their derived extracellular vesicles (EVs), identifying 10 candidate miRNAs—comprising fca-miR-21-5p, fca-miR-23a-3p, fca-miR-29a-3p, fca-miR-30a-5p, fca-miR-30d-5p, fca-miR-92a-3p, fca-miR-100-5p, fca-miR-146a-5p, fca-miR-222-3p, and fca-miR-1246. Quantitative evaluation using locked nucleic acid (LNA)-enhanced RT-qPCR and exogenous spike-in normalization revealed distinct compartmentalization patterns; notably, fca-miR-1246 showed higher abundance in the EV preparation than in the corresponding cellular preparation, suggesting a compartment-associated expression pattern that warrants further investigation. Longitudinal monitoring in FMC patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models further identified positive within-subject associations between circulating EV-associated miRNA levels, particularly fca-miR-21-5p and fca-miR-92a-3p, and tumor progression over an eight-week period, with repeated-measures correlation coefficients of up to 0.93 (p < 0.001). These findings indicate that selected circulating EV-associated miRNAs may track with changes in tumor burden over time. By bridging species-specific molecular profiling with in vivo longitudinal evaluation, this study provides a preclinical framework for further development of circulating EV-associated miRNAs as potential non-invasive monitoring tools for feline mammary carcinoma.

papers.title: Low overlap between bacterial and viral communities in meltwater and sediments of ice rise cryoconites
papers.abstract: Cryoconite microbial communities are regulated by viruses and a wide range of functional genes linked to cold adaptation, yet interactions between sediment- and water-associated communities remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the microbial, viral, and functional diversity of meltwater and sediments from cryoconites on the Ward Hunt Ice Rise of the Last Ice Area. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing was performed to assess microbial and viral biodiversity, while antibiotic resistance genes, virus-host matching and antiviral defense systems served as proxies for microbial interactions. Cryoconite holes host strongly compartmentalized microbial assemblages with contrasting diversity patterns. Bacteria, including filamentous Cyanobacteria and Actinomycetes, were more diverse in sediment, whereas eukaryotes such as dinophytes, green algae and rotifers were more diverse in meltwater. Viruses followed host patterns, with bacteriophages (Caudoviricetes) dominating sediment and giant viruses (Nucleocytoviricota) more prevalent in meltwater. Sediment communities also exhibited greater diversity of antibiotic resistance genes. These results demonstrate that meltwater and sediment aggregates from cryoconites support distinct biological communities and provide an initial baseline for future spatial and temporal comparisons.

papers.title: Distinct transcriptomic profile revealed adaptation change among tomato associated Salmonella Newport strains
papers.abstract: Salmonella enterica serovar Newport lineage III strains are frequently implicated in tomato-associated foodborne outbreaks. To investigate their adaptive mechanisms, comparative transcriptomic analyses were performed on S. Newport strains from multiple lineages, alongside Typhimurium and Enteritidis isolates, grown to mid-log phase in hand-expressed tomato cellular fluids (TCFs) from four tomato types at 37 C. RNA sequencing was conducted, and differential expressions were analyzed with DESeq2. Transcriptomic responses were modulated by tomato type alongside lineage- and strain-level differences across isolates. Specifically, among the examined S. Newport isolates, lineage III formed a distinct transcriptional cluster despite strain variation, characterized by increased regulation of genes linked to virulence, metabolism, motility, and stress adaptation, suggesting enhanced environmental fitness. High acidity and low moisture in TCF from grape tomatoes induced upregulation of asrA, asrB, and asrC, encoding the acid survival response activated under acidic, anaerobic conditions. In contrast, genes for copper homeostasis were upregulated in other tomato types relative to grape tomato. Compared with the Typhimurium and Enteritidis strains tested, Newport isolates exhibited broader metabolic and stress-adaptive induction, notably upregulating universal stress protein genes (uspC, uspE, uspF,and uspG). These findings reveal that serovar, lineage, and tomato type collectively shape Salmonella gene expression, reflecting finely balanced niche adaptation.

papers.title: Deep reinforcement learning guided multi-scale fusion for few-shot rotating machinery fault diagnosis under variable conditions
papers.abstract: Rotating machinery, as the core equipment of modern industrial systems, has a direct impact on the safe and stable production of major industrial equipment. In practical industrial environments, due to the complexity and variability of equipment operating conditions and the difficulty in obtaining fault samples, traditional intelligent diagnosis methods face the dual challenges of data distribution bias and sample scarcity. To address the issues of inconsistent data distribution under varying operating conditions and insufficient model generalization ability in small-sample scenarios, this study proposes a new intelligent diagnosis method that integrates deep reinforcement learning with multi-scale feature fusion. By constructing a multi-scale disturbance-resistant feature extraction network, robust feature representations that are insensitive to changes in operating conditions are extracted from raw vibration signals, effectively overcoming the shortcomings of traditional methods in terms of insufficient feature representation ability when operating conditions change. Combined with the deep reinforcement learning framework, this paper designs a diagnostic decision-making mechanism with domain adaptability, and guides the model to learn more stable fault discrimination strategies between different working conditions through reward feedback. The model is guided by a reward function to autonomously learn invariant feature representations of operating conditions, significantly enhancing its adaptability in scenarios with distribution bias. Finally, an end-to-end fault diagnosis model is formed, achieving the ability to quickly learn from limited samples and adapt to new operating conditions. Experimental results show that this method achieves leading performance in multiple cross-condition transfer tasks and small-sample settings. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness of each core module, feature distribution analysis reveals the intrinsic mechanism of model performance improvement, and engineering application cases further demonstrate the practical value of the method in real industrial scenarios, providing a new technical solution for intelligent operation and maintenance of rotating machinery.

papers.title: The Lactate-to-albumin ratio predicts short and long-term mortality in patients with traumatic brain injury: A retrospective cohort study from the MIMIC-IV database
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) exhibits significant prognostic heterogeneity, necessitating reliable early prognostic markers. The lactate-to-albumin ratio (LAR), a composite marker of tissue hypoxia and systemic inflammation, still needs to be validated as a prognostic indicator for TBI in a large-scale cohort. This study utilized the MIMIC-IV database (V3.1) to enroll adult patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) who were admitted to the ICU for the first time. The primary exposure variable was LAR within 24 h of admission. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality at 28 days, 90 days, and 365 days, as well as mortality during the ICU stay. Kaplan— Meier survival analysis compared survival differences across LAR quartiles. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models assessed the association between LAR and mortality risk, yielding hazard ratios (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis evaluated the dose–response relationship between LAR and mortality. Subgroup analyses by age, sex, surgery, sepsis, hypertension, and diabetes further examined this association. In the multivariable-adjusted model (Model 5), patients in the Q4 group exhibited significantly elevated mortality risks compared to the Q1 group: ICU mortality (HR = 2.20, 95% CI: 1.09–4.42, P = 0.027), 28-day mortality (HR = 1.83, 95% CI: 1.16–2.89, P = 0.009), 90-day mortality (HR = 1.71, 95% CI: 1.15–2.54, P = 0.008), and 365-day mortality (HR = 1.77, 95% CI: 1.24–2.53, P = 0.002). Restricted cubic spline analysis demonstrated a linear positive correlation between LAR and mortality risk (P for nonlinearity > 0.05). Subgroup analysis revealed effect modification of the association between LAR and prognosis in patients with sepsis (P for interaction < 0.001).LAR is an independent predictor of both short-term and long-term mortality in TBI patients. This readily obtainable metric facilitates early risk stratification.

papers.title: Box-Behnken design assisted optimization of a reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography method for the simultaneous estimation of bimatoprost and finasteride in co-loaded zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 metal-organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Combination of Bimatoprost (BIM) and finasteride (FIN) represents a promising therapeutic mechanism for the management of androgenetic alopecia (AGA), with BIM promoting hair follicle growth and FIN inhibiting dihydrotestosterone-mediated follicular miniaturization. Encapsulation of these drugs into Zeolitic Imidazolate Framework-8 (ZIF-8) metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offers advantages such as enhanced drug loading and targeted follicular delivery. However, to the best of our knowledge, no simultaneous analytical method has been reported for quantifying BIM and FIN in ZIF-8 MOF-based formulations, creating a significant gap for formulation development and analytical evaluation. Therefore, the present study focused on establishing a Reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for the accurate quantification of BIM and FIN in ZIF-8 MOFs. A risk-based Analytical Quality by Design (AQbD) approach was employed utilizing Design of Experiments (DoE) to ensure systematic method development. Potential critical method variables were determined using an Ishikawa fishbone diagram and subsequently prioritized through Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) using Risk Priority Number (RPN) ranking. Parameters with higher RPN values were considered critical and selected for optimization. A Box-Behnken response surface design was used to further optimize these variables, with the dependent responses comprising peak resolution (Rs), peak area, tailing factor (Tf), and number of theoretical plates (NTP) as the dependent responses. Chromatographic separation was optimized using a mobile phase consisting of 43% (v/v) ACN and 57% (v/v) acidified water containing 0.1% (v/v) triethylamine, with the pH adjusted to 3.0 using orthophosphoric acid, the column oven temperature was maintained at 25 °C, while the mobile phase flow rate was kept constant at 0.8 mL/min. The Limit of detection (LOD) and Limit of quantification (LOQ) were 31.32 ng/mL and 94.90 ng/mL respectively for BIM, and 10.00 ng/mL and 30.30 ng/mL respectively for FIN. System suitability, precision, accuracy, robustness, and specificity were in accordance with ICH guidelines, with no interference from the ZIF-8 MOF matrix. BIM and FIN remained stable under photolytic conditions but exhibited moderate degradation under mild acidic/alkaline conditions and marked degradation under strong acidic, alkaline, oxidative, and thermal stress. Entrapment efficiency of ZIF-8 co-loaded MOFs was 64 ± 3.2% for BIM and 41 ± 2.4% for FIN. The sustainability of the developed method was comprehensively evaluated using a multi-coloured analytical chemistry framework. For the simultaneous quantification of BIM and FIN in ZIF-8 MOF-based formulations, the developed RP-HPLC method proved to be sensitive, robust, and suitable for routine analysis.

papers.title: Towards new insights in the comparative biogeography of the Neotropical region with a focus on the Caribbean subregion
papers.abstract: The Caribbean subregion exhibits a highly diverse biodiversity and a very complex geological history. Interpreting this biogeographic pattern has been challenging for long, giving rise to hypotheses like GAARlandia and GrANoLA. This study employs comparative biogeography to investigate the biogeographic patterns and test these hypotheses within the Caribbean Islands biodiversity hotspot. We have compiled a dataset of phylogenies and distributions for 24 monophyletic groups, including 472 species, we applied three-item analysis (3ia) through the software LisBeth as well as maximum parsimony analysis with Paup 1.4 to elucidate biogeographic relationships. Our analyses support both GrANoLA and GAARlandia hypotheses, indicating a closer biogeographical relationship between the Northern Lesser Antilles and the Greater Antilles. The study highlights the need for more accurate distribution data and comprehensive dated phylogenies to strengthen this biogeographic pattern. This study provides a framework for understanding the evolutionary history and current biodiversity patterns in the Caribbean Islands, emphasizing the importance of historical factors in conservation planning.

papers.title: Static guided versus freehand techniques for fiber post removal: a comparative in vitro study
papers.abstract: To evaluate static guided digital technique and compare it with freehand techniques for fiber post removal, using Peeso reamers and ultrasonic diamond-coated instruments. Thirty-two extracted double-rooted maxillary premolars were endodontically treated ex vivo. Post space preparation and fiber post cementation were performed in the palatal canal following standardized protocols. The samples were randomly allocated into four groups based on the post removal method and instrument used (n = 8): peeso guided, ultrasonic guided, peeso freehand, and ultrasonic freehand. For the guided groups, virtual drill-and-guide planning was performed after superimposing CBCT and digital surface scans, and the guides were fabricated using three-dimensional printing. The drilling and total time taken to remove the fiber post were recorded. A postoperative CBCT was used to assess deviation between the planned and actual drill paths, remaining dentin thickness, and mishaps. Statistical analysis was performed using two-way factorial ANOVA with robust standard errors and Holm-corrected post-hoc tests (α = 0.05). Significant instrument type effects were found for coronal (p = 0.002 ), middle (p = 0.003 ), and total deviation (p = 0.027), with significant instrument $$\:\times\:$$ technique interactions at coronal (p = 0.043) and middle (p = 0.040) levels. The Peeso guided protocol exhibited the lowest total deviation ( $$\:0.325\pm\:0.148\;\text{mm}$$ ). Significant differences in RDT% were observed for main effects and interaction (p < 0.001). Peeso guided preserved the most dentin ( $$\:95.62\%\pm\:2.14\%$$ ), followed by Ultrasonic freehand ( $$\:91.39\%\pm\:2.85\%$$ ), Peeso freehand ( $$\:88.47\%\pm\:3.12\%$$ ), and Ultrasonic guided ( $$\:86.82\%\pm\:3.41\%$$ ). Drilling and total times differed significantly (p < 0.001), with Peeso guided requiring the shortest duration ( $$\:30.0\pm\:4.3\;\text{s}$$ ) and Ultrasonic guided requiring the longest ( $$\:685.4\pm\:37.7\;\text{s}$$ ). One root perforation occurred in the ultrasonic freehand group. Fiber post removal outcomes are multifactorial and primarily influenced by instrument-technique interaction. Therefore, optimal clinical performance of static guides relies on integrating appropriate instrument mechanics.

papers.title: Lenabasum attenuates cardiac injury in rats with sepsis induced by cecal ligation and puncture
papers.abstract: Sepsis-induced cardiac injury involves systemic inflammation, impaired antioxidant defense, and metabolic alterations. Lenabasum, a selective cannabinoid receptor type 2 agonist, has anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory potential, but evidence regarding its effects in the cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model remains limited. This study evaluated lenabasum’s effects on CLP-induced cardiac injury through biochemical measurements, cardiac antioxidant enzyme activities, targeted plasma metabolic profiling, and cardiac histopathology. A total of 30 rats were randomly allocated to five groups: Sham, CLP, CLP + lenabasum (1 mg/kg), CLP + lenabasum (5 mg/kg), and CLP + dexamethasone (1 mg/kg). Blood and cardiac tissue samples were collected 24 h after surgery. Serum creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB), troponin I, N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP), C-reactive protein (CRP), cardiac superoxide dismutase (SOD) and catalase activities, targeted plasma amino acid/acylcarnitine profiles, and cardiac histopathology, including blinded semi-quantitative scoring, were assessed. Compared with the Sham group, CLP-induced sepsis significantly increased serum markers of cardiac injury, cardiac stress, and acute-phase response, while decreasing cardiac antioxidant enzyme activities. Lenabasum at 1 and 5 mg/kg significantly attenuated these biochemical alterations, with a more pronounced protective pattern at 5 mg/kg. Targeted plasma metabolomic profiling showed distinct metabolic patterns among the Sham, CLP, and lenabasum-treated groups. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated CLP-associated cardiac injury, and blinded semi-quantitative scoring showed significantly lower inflammatory infiltration scores with lenabasum at 5 mg/kg compared with CLP. Lenabasum was associated with attenuation of CLP-induced cardiac injury, supported by complementary biochemical and cardiac tissue findings and accompanied by exploratory plasma metabolic differences. Together, these findings provide a preclinical basis for further mechanistic and translational investigation of lenabasum in sepsis-associated cardiac injury.

papers.title: Development of a Field Assay for the Identification of Sialidase-Producing Bacteria in the Tsetse Gut and Characterisation of a Paenibacillus sialidase
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota of Tsetse influences several aspects of the host physiology and vector competence. Trypanosome infection relies on trans-sialidases that catalyse the transfer of sialic acids from blood meal glycoconjugates to the parasite’s surface. In contrast, sialidases hydrolyse the glycosidic bond of terminal sialic acids, rendering them unusable for trans-sialidases; therefore, potential bacterial sialidases in the tsetse gut may disrupt the trypanosomal infection process in the fly. This study aimed to develop and optimize a field-compatible screening assay to detect sialidase activity within the tsetse gut, isolate potential sialidase-producing bacterial strains, and biochemically characterise the enzymatic properties of isolated recombinant bacterial sialidases. Tsetse collected from five African countries (Cameroon, Chad, Ethiopia, Ghana and Nigeria) were screened for sialidase activity to test and optimize the newly developed field-compatible assay presented in this study. The assay uses 4-methylumbelliferyl-N-acetylneuraminic acid as a synthetic fluorescent substrate and highly sialylated fetuin as sialic acid donor to detect sialidase activity based on a simple filter-spot approach with UV detection followed by qualitative and quantitative analysis in the laboratory on a single fly basis. Detectable sialidase activity was found only in 15% of fly samples collected during one application of the survey in Cameroon. Bacterial isolates representing several genera (Bacillus, Stenotrophomonas, Pseudomonas, Paenibacillus, Enterobacter) were obtained from fly samples of the same geographic location in a recurring survey and were screened for sialidase activity. Whole-genome sequencing identified a putative sialidase gene in a Paenibacillus species. The gene was cloned, transformed into E. coli, and the recombinant enzyme was purified and biochemically characterised. The purified recombinant sialidase exhibited an apparent molecular mass of approximately 110 kDa and showed dual pH optima at pH 5 and 7. Enzymatic activity was enhanced by Cu2+ ions. Kinetic characterisation using the synthetic substrate 4-methylumbelliferyl-N-acetylneuraminic acid revealed a vmax of 2.5 nmol/min/mg and a KM of 332.7 µM. The isolated enzyme should be further investigated for its potential to impair trypanosome infection and development in the tsetse gut.

papers.title: Optimized vision transformer with shifted patch and local attention for robust land cover mapping
papers.abstract: Land use and land cover (LULC) mapping is essential for monitoring ecological trends, resource management, and mitigating environmental risks. Although Vision Transformers (ViTs) provide powerful representation-learning capabilities, conventional ViTs generally require large-scale training data and substantial computational resources, making it challenging to achieve an effective balance among classification performance, model compactness, and computational efficiency when training from scratch on small- to medium-sized remote-sensing datasets. To address this technical gap, we propose a compact ViT-based framework integrating shifted patch tokenization (SPT) with local self-attention (LSA). SPT enriches visual tokens with neighboring spatial information, whereas LSA employs diagonal masking and learnable temperature scaling to refine inter-token attention and reduce excessive self-token dependency. In addition, a compact three-layer transformer encoder is employed to reduce model complexity and computational requirements.
