The proposed framework is evaluated on four benchmark land-cover datasets, namely AID, EuroSAT, WHU-RS19, and UCmerced land use dataset, using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score as evaluation metrics. The proposed model achieves classification accuracies of 96.8%, 97.5%, 96.7%, and 98.5% on AID, EuroSAT, WHU-RS19, and UCmerced land use dataset, respectively. On UCmerced land use dataset, the proposed model achieves 98.5% accuracy compared with 97.5% for MCPSF, corresponding to an improvement of 1.0 percentage point over the strongest comparison method reported in the current evaluation. Across the evaluated datasets and comparison methods, these results demonstrate that the proposed SPT-LSA framework provides a favorable balance between classification effectiveness and model efficiency for land-cover classification on small- to medium-sized datasets.

papers.title: The relationship between uric acid levels and fatigue: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Uric acid (UA) plays a dual biological role as both a neuroprotective antioxidant and a pro-inflammatory pro-oxidant. Its relationship with fatigue across various clinical populations remains fragmented and controversial. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to comprehensively synthesize clinical evidence regarding the association between serum uric acid (SUA) levels and fatigue. We searched PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, Cochrane, PsycInfo, CNKI, and SinoMed up to August 29th, 2026 for observational studies on SUA and fatigue. Two reviewers screened, extracted data, and assessed quality (NOS). Pooled correlation coefficients (r) and odds ratios (ORs) were estimated using random-effects models with REML and Hartung-Knapp adjustment. Eighteen studies (16 cross-sectional, 2 cohort; n = 3,225) were included. In Parkinson’s disease (3 studies, n = 248), SUA was consistently negatively associated with the NMSS sleep/fatigue domain (r = − 0.36, 95% CI: −0.47 to − 0.25; I² = 0%). In five cross-sectional studies on post-stroke fatigue, the pooled OR was 1.52 (95% CI: 0.34–6.80; I² = 92.1%) but did not reach statistical significance. The association between SUA and fatigue appears to be population-specific. In Parkinson’s disease, higher SUA levels were consistently associated with less severe sleep/fatigue symptoms, whereas the association in post-stroke fatigue remained heterogeneous and inconclusive.

papers.title: Harm from indoor air contaminants in an office building
papers.abstract: Indoor air quality in offices is usually interpreted through benchmark exceedance, although exceedance alone does not quantify health burden across a multi-contaminant mixture. This study applies benchmark comparison (HQ), regulated harm (RH), and disability-adjusted life-year (DALY)-based harm assessment to measured indoor air contaminants in a monitored public office building in Bolzano, Italy. In the primary benchmark assessment, propanal was the only contaminant with HQ > 1, while benchmark choice altered the ordering of contaminants below the exceedance threshold. When measured concentrations were translated into DALY-based harm, PM2.5, formaldehyde, and derived PM10–2.5 were identified as prospective contaminants of concern within the quantified set and together accounted for 99.3% of mean total harm among 15 contaminants with available harm inputs. Benchmark comparison, regulated harm, and DALY-based harm provided complementary interpretations of the monitored mixture. HQ quantified proximity to selected health-based benchmarks, RH the model-based harm implied at those benchmark concentrations, and DALY-based harm the model-based impact at the measured concentrations. Their joint use links benchmark screening with health-based prioritisation of site-specific office measurements.

papers.title: The perceived educational and psychological significance of memorial-space experiences among university students: a qualitative study in Province J, China
papers.abstract: This study explores university students’ perceptions of the educational and psychological significance of memorial-space experiences in Province J, China. Using a qualitative design, the study draws on semi-structured interviews with 30 university students to examine how they experience, interpret, and attribute meaning to their encounters with memorial spaces. The findings show that participants perceived memorial spaces as emotionally activating educational settings in which spatial atmosphere and historical narratives could evoke empathy, reflection, and affective engagement. Beyond emotional activation, participants described these spaces as sites of meaning-making and identity construction that helped some of them reconsider values such as responsibility, commitment, and collective belonging. Some participants further perceived emotional resonance and personally constructed meanings as psychological resources associated with resilience, self-reflection, and future-oriented self-positioning. However, these interpretations were conditional and varied across participants; some experiences were temporary, limited, neutral, or contradictory. Overall, the findings suggest that the perceived educational and psychological significance of memorial-space experiences depends on how students interpret particular spatial, narrative, and educational encounters rather than arising automatically from exposure to memorial spaces.

papers.title: A robust PID controller based on the coefficient diagram method for frequency regulation in renewable-dominated deregulated power systems
papers.abstract: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources (RESs) and the restructuring of electricity markets have introduced significant challenges to load frequency control (LFC) in deregulated power systems (DPSs). The intermittent nature of renewable generation, reduced system inertia, and market-based power transactions can result in larger frequency deviations, increased tie-line power oscillations, and degraded dynamic performance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a robust proportional-integral-derivative controller based on the coefficient diagram method (PID-CDM) for frequency regulation in a two-area DPS with high-RES penetration. In the proposed framework, the CDM stability indices and equivalent time constant are optimally determined using Coatis Optimization Algorithm (COA), and the resulting optimal parameters are subsequently employed to analytically derive the PID controller gains. Unlike conventional PID tuning approaches that rely solely on numerical optimization, the proposed method combines analytical controller synthesis with metaheuristic optimization, providing improved robustness and closed-loop dynamic characteristics. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is evaluated under various deregulated market scenarios, including poolco-based transactions, bilateral contracts, and contract violation conditions. The assessment further considers renewable generation fluctuations, system nonlinearities such as generation rate constraints (GRC) and governor dead band (GDB), as well as system parameter uncertainties. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PID-CDM controller significantly outperforms conventional PID controllers tuned using different algorithms. The proposed strategy achieves up to 85% reduction in frequency and tie-line power deviations, substantially decreases settling time, and improves overall system robustness under varying operating conditions. These results confirm the effectiveness of the proposed PID-CDM framework as a reliable solution for frequency regulation in renewable-dominated deregulated power systems.

papers.title: A new design for cooling photovoltaic systems using hexagonal fins with internal/external ribs filled with multiple phase change materials
papers.abstract: The thermal efficiency of the solar cells is highly dependent on the temperature at which the solar cells operate. The effectiveness of passive cooling using phase change materials (PCMs) is quite cost-effective; however, due to density differences, the molten PCM rises, causing a temperature gradient where the top section of the solar cell becomes hotter than the bottom section. In this work, the PV cell is integrated with a newly developed heat sink consisting of 6-hexagonal fins with internal/external ribs, each filled with two PCMs (RT-35 and RT-27). This system is compared with the conventional smooth case (PCM domain sited at the back of the PV cell), in which both systems contain an equal PCM volume. Hence, the geometrical sizes of the hexagonal fins were modified to match the PCM volume in the conventional system. The simulations were conducted for tilting angles of 30°, 60°, and 90° to analyze the PV cell temperature, electricity efficiency, and thermal management time with the new heat sink. Relative to the smooth configuration, the new configuration decreases PV cell temperature by 30.6%, 31.14%, and 33.2% for tilting angles of 90°, 60°, and 30°, respectively, during the thermal management time. During this stage, the proposed heat sink achieves an electrical efficiency of about 17.56%, compared to roughly 16.44% for the conventional smooth case (with a 6.81% improvement). The findings suggest that future PV-PCM system modeling should apply this proposed configuration for enhanced performance and further optimization.

papers.title: Classifying remote patient messages in primary care according to clinical relevance and physician expertise
papers.abstract: Following the surge in remote communication between patients and their primary care physicians (PCPs) during the COVID-19 pandemic, healthcare systems increasingly integrated this technology into routine primary care. This shift offers opportunities to improve patient access and physician efficiency, yet also introduces challenges related to workload management and the effective utilization of physician expertise. This study aimed to develop a framework for classifying remote communication between patients and PCPs, distinguish productive from unproductive messages, and estimate the prevalence of each type. Productive messages were defined as those that make effective use of PCP expertise and contribute to patient care. A qualitative two-stage design was employed. In Stage 1, 500 randomly sampled communication threads from a health service organization were used to develop classification criteria and thematic sub-categories, with input from three expert PCPs. In Stage 2, a new sample of 2,100 communication threads was independently classified by the same experts into productive or unproductive categories and thematic sub-categories. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using Fleiss’ Kappa, and frequency distributions were calculated. The experts developed five sub-categories of productive messages and seven sub-categories of unproductive messages. In the operational phase, only 702 of 2,100 threads (33.4%) were classified as productive, whereas 1,398 (66.6%) were unproductive. Productive messages most often concerned repeat prescriptions (13.0%) and medical advice (12.7%). Unproductive messages most often involved redundant prescription requests (22.0%) and issues requiring in-person visits (18.0%). Inter-rater reliability across categories was moderate (Kappa = 0.451–0.564). Most remote patient-PCP communications in the examined setting were classified as unproductive, suggesting potential inefficiencies that may contribute to greater physician workload and burnout risk. These findings support consideration of approaches such as structured patient input, automated routing to appropriate personnel, decision-support tools, and artificial intelligence applications, which may help reduce avoidable demands on PCPs and support more sustainable care delivery.

papers.title: Droop control meets resilience: quantifying DC microgrid performance under long missions and cascading shocks
papers.abstract: Sequential losses of generation, storage support, and grid connectivity can compromise load service in DC microgrids. This study examines a supervisory framework combining bounded primary droop control, priority-based partial load curtailment, and availability-constrained emergency support. Electric-vehicle (EV) charging and discharge are represented through connection and energy constraints; spatial mobility is outside the model. The assessment framework combines normalized voltage deviation, cumulative energy not served, and priority-weighted service continuity. A two-target PLECS RT BOX implementation is examined using one prescribed disturbance sequence on a 168 h mission-profile coordinate. The reported stress-case minimum is 297.22 V, corresponding to a 15.08% undervoltage relative to the 350 V reference. The critical-load served fraction briefly decreases to 0.8 and returns to unity after emergency support becomes available; the combined diesel-generator/EV power peaks at approximately 1.95 kW. These observations support a qualitative interpretation of disturbance absorption, operational adaptation, and service restoration. Under stress operation, the results yield 9.08009 kWh of nominal requested-service curtailment over the mission horizon, a final served-energy ratio of 0.96710 and a priority-weighted service index of 0.98404. Under the stated assessment weights, the horizon-mean composite score is 0.78221 in the stress case and 0.79141 in normal operation. These dispatch-based mission-profile quantities complement the voltage response.

papers.title: A process evaluation of the Missing ​L​ink care transition intervention for people with stroke and TIA
papers.abstract: The transition from hospital to home is a vulnerable situation for patients with stroke or transient ischemic attack. Therefore, the multi-component Missing Link intervention was developed and evaluated and was shown to have a positive effect on the perceived quality of care transitions. This process evaluation aims to evaluate the implementation of the Missing Link intervention. Data were collected from September 2022 to January 2024. Data included the Normalization MeAsure Development Questionnaire; interviews with staff and managers; and field notes from observations of interactions between patients and staff, and research meetings. Results showed that the training was well received, and the intervention was appreciated, however, its continuous use in clinical practice was challenging due to staff rotation, time pressure, and lack of adaptation to the clinical context. All aspects of the multi-component intervention did not appear to have been implemented or applied equally. In conclusion, the staff appreciated and valued the intervention, but the implementation was insufficiently adapted to fit staff work procedures and challenged by high staff workload. Future studies should explore how to support clinicians’ participation and well-being in clinical trials.

papers.title: An ultrawide-field TEM/CLEM imaging strategy to investigate the gastric squamous–columnar junction
papers.abstract: The gastric squamous–columnar junction (SCJ) is a clinically important region. It represents a boundary where squamous and columnar epithelia meet, forming a complex architecture implicated in epithelial transformation and tumorigenesis. Despite accumulating evidence that this region harbors cells of origin for disease, its ultrastructural organization remains poorly defined due to the limited field of view of conventional electron microscopy. Here, we established an ultrawide-field TEM imaging protocol that enables seamless visualization of the SCJ across multiple spatial scales: from entire SCJ tissue architecture, to spatial organization of cells, individual cell morphology, and subcellular ultrastructural details. Using this approach, we revealed distinctive architectural features, including widened intercellular spaces between columnar cells of the SCJ gland and the presence of cells with intermediate morphology at the gland’s base which exhibit squamous-like structures but in a less rigid arrangement. We further integrated this approach with correlative light and electron microscopy and performed biomarker-guided ultrastructural imaging of DCLK1+ and CD44+ cell populations, extending beyond prior studies of their localization and functional significance. These methods provide a framework for molecularly informed ultrastructural analysis of the gastric SCJ and support future studies aimed at understanding how its unique architecture influences physiological and pathological processes.

papers.title: Effects of calf neuromuscular electrostimulation on hemodynamics and systemic fibrinolytic activity: a randomized clinical pilot study
papers.abstract: Muscular physical exercise is a stimulus to circulatory development. But it is not always possible. In this context, there was the development of intermittent pneumatic compression therapy and, more recently, neuromuscular electrical stimulation. A clinical, interventional, prospective, single-center, randomized, single-blind study was carried out to evaluate the effect of neuromuscular electrical stimulation on lower limb hemodynamics and systemic fibrinolytic activity in 10 healthy subjects. The study protocol was approved by the Research Ethics Committee of the Botucatu Medical School, UNESP (CAAE: 30680120.0.0000.5411). The flow volume variation was significant, in the joint analysis of the limbs, at the popliteal vein. The diameter of the vessels proved to be the most sensitive to neuromuscular electrical stimulation in the joint analysis of the limbs. Flow velocities varied statistically significantly only in the femoral vessels. In the popliteal vessels, there was a variation in flow increment, but it was not statistically significant. There was no statistically significant change in the plasminogen activator inhibitor. For plasminogen activator, there was numerical variation, with continuous increment, but this did not represent a statistically significant change (p > 0.05). There was no adverse event and all subjects had the lowest tolerance score (no feeling of discomfort). NMES significantly improved popliteal and femoral hemodynamics. Although numerical increases in plasminogen activator were observed, they did not reach statistical significance (p > 0.05). The protocol proved to be safe and well-tolerated. Trial registration: Brazilian Registry of Clinical Trials (ReBEC) RBR-6gs4bdh. UTN U1111-1301-5055. Registered on January 29, 2024. URL: https://ensaiosclinicos.gov.br/rg/RBR-6gs4bdh.

papers.title: Lactic acid bacteria promote antitumor immunity in bladder cancer associated with tumor microenvironment modulation and interferon-JAK/STAT pathway upregulation
papers.abstract: Bladder cancer remains a major clinical challenge, with BCG therapy offering limited efficacy and substantial toxicity. Emerging evidence highlights the influence of the tumor microenvironment and microbiome on tumor progression and therapeutic response. Fermented foods such as Kimchi contain probiotic bacteria with immunomodulatory potential. Here, we investigate two Kimchi-derived Weissella cibaria strains, WiKim0164 and WiKim0166, as microbiota-based therapeutics for bladder cancer. Using human and mouse bladder cancer cell lines and a syngeneic MB49 mouse model, we evaluated antitumor effects through cytotoxicity assays, flow cytometry, histology, bulk RNA-seq, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics. Both strains induced cytotoxicity in bladder cancer cells via endoplasmic reticulum stress-driven apoptosis and immunogenic cell death. In vivo, treatment suppressed tumor growth and promoted strong immune activation. Early responses included increased infiltration of natural killer cells and effector memory CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells. At later stages, the TME exhibited reduced immunosuppression, with decreased PD-1 and LAG-3 expression on CD8⁺ T cells and lower frequencies of regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells. Mechanistically, treatment with WiKim0164 and WiKim0166 was associated with interferon-JAK/STAT signaling, which correlated with cytotoxic CD8⁺ T-cell activation and stronger T-cell receptor signaling. Both strains also promoted dendritic cell maturation in tumor-draining lymph nodes, supporting improved antigen presentation and adaptive immune priming. These findings demonstrate that Weissella cibaria WiKim0164 and WiKim0166 elicit potent antitumor immunity in bladder cancer by inducing immunogenic cell death, strengthening effector T-cell responses, and alleviating TME immunosuppression. These strains represent promising microbiota-based immunotherapies with potential to complement current bladder cancer treatments.

papers.title: Fourier-inspired automatic Cobb angles measurement for adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
papers.abstract: Cobb angle measurement from anteroposterior (AP) radiographs is the clinical standard for assessing adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS). However, manual assessment is time-consuming and often inconsistent. Clinicians must subjectively select end vertebrae and place measurement lines, which introduces substantial inter- and intra-observer variability. To address these limitations, we introduce an automated pipeline that estimates the three Cobb angles corresponding to the annotated spinal curves in the dataset, leveraging a compact, Fourier-inspired representation of spinal curvature that jointly learns whole-spine segmentation and curvature prediction in the frequency domain. Specifically, we extract a centerline from the predicted spine mask, compute its low-frequency spectrum, and train a projection head to regress the concatenated real and imaginary Fourier coefficients. This spectral representation serves as a structured intermediate target that bridges the gap between high-dimensional radiographs and low-dimensional Cobb angle outputs. Finally, a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP) regresses the Cobb angles from the predicted spectrum. We evaluate our approach on two publicly available benchmarks, AASCE and Spinal-AI2024, achieving competitive accuracy with symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of $$11.36\%$$ and $$14.57\%$$ , respectively. These results demonstrate that frequency-domain supervision improves robustness compared with direct spatial regression. Our approach also enables fast, reproducible, and automated Cobb angle assessment for routine clinical workflows and resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Evaluation of flexural strength and stiffness of face-welded double-tee beam-to-SHS column joints
papers.abstract: This study addresses the design and modelling of face-welded beam-to-Square Hollow Section (SHS) column joints within the Component Method framework. Particular attention is given to the SHS-to-plate component, which represents the beam flange-to-column attachment and strongly influences the overall joint stiffness and resistance. Current design provisions provide a semi-empirical formulation for the resistance of this component, while no stiffness expressions are available. To address these limitations, finite element models of SHS-to-plate connections and beam-to-column sub-assemblies are validated against experimental data and subsequently used in parametric studies comprising 41 SHS-to-plate components and 33 SHS-to-IPE beam-to-column joints. A closed-form expression based on yield-field theory is applied for the resistance of the SHS-to-plate component, providing accuracy comparable to the current Eurocode formulation while retaining a fully theoretical basis. For stiffness, an existing theoretical mechanical model is adapted to SHS-to-plate connections and validated against the numerical results. The resulting resistance and stiffness formulations are then combined with the column shear component within a Component Method model to predict the flexural response of SHS-to-IPE joints. Comparison with the numerical results shows average deviations of 4–5% and coefficients of variation of 8–11% for stiffness and plastic resistance, supporting the accuracy of the proposed mechanically based framework.

papers.title: Machine learning-based optimization of compact wideband terahertz MIMO antenna for next-generation communication systems
papers.abstract: A wideband terahertz (THz) MIMO antenna is proposed in this article where graphene is utilized as radiating element due to its surface conductivity, mechanical strength and high carrier mobility. These properties result in compact size and wider bandwidth of antenna which makes it suitable choice for future wireless communication systems. The suggested antenna is made to meet the demanding requirements of the upcoming 6G network. The proposed compact antenna is 160 μm × 160 μm in size and resonating from 2.10 THz to 3.45 THz with wide bandwidth of 1.35 THz with radiation efficiency greater than 90% over entire operating band. The performance analysis shows isolation better than -17 dB across the operating band without having any decoupling mechanism between radiating elements and 6.76 dB of peak gain. MIMO diversity performance is validated by computing the results of Envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) < 0.002, diversity gain (DG) of ≈10 dB, total active reflection coefficient (TARC) of less than -10 dB, channel capacity loss (CCL) < 0.4 bits/sec/Hz, and mean effective gain (MEG) of approximately − 3 dB. These results demonstrate excellent diversity performance and validate the suitability of the proposed antenna for high-performance MIMO communication. The suggested small MIMO antenna is a suitable option for future 6G communication that requires low latency, and high capacity data transfer because of its wide bandwidth, adequate gain, and strong isolation. Regression techniques driven by machine learning (ML) are employed for reflection coefficient performance prediction to increase design accuracy and efficiency. This achieves great stability with simulation results and minimizes the necessity for numerous revisions. Optimizing the parameters using machine learning techniques gives excellent results with R2 = 0.9779. This implies that high-performing terahertz antennas can be made using graphene. This antenna’s wide operation, innovative performance optimization, and sophisticated material use make it a great choice for integration into the upcoming generation of terahertz-enabled products.

papers.title: Multi-criteria microzonation based roadmap for seismic risk and economic loss assessment in Al-Seeb, Oman
papers.abstract: This study presents a comprehensive and integrated framework for seismic vulnerability and risk assessment of residential areas in Al-Seeb, Muscat, Sultanate of Oman. It represents the first detailed microzonation-based assessment for the region, combining seismic, geotechnical, structural, environmental, and socioeconomic parameters within a GIS-based multi-criteria approach using the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP). A diverse building inventory, including reinforced concrete, masonry, dual systems, and non-engineered structures, was evaluated to capture variations in structural performance. The region was classified into five seismic risk zones, supported by spatial risk indices and zone-specific damage matrices. To improve the reliability of damage estimation, uncertainty in structural vulnerability and damage progression was incorporated through probabilistic vulnerability modelling, while nonlinear simulations were used to derive updated damage ratios and average damage indices. Three probabilistic models were assessed, with the updated Gaussian distribution model demonstrating the highest consistency. The framework further integrates economic risk through Average Annual Loss (AAL), Loss Exceedance Curves (LEC), and Probable Maximum Loss (PML), enabling asset-level risk evaluation. The results reveal strong spatial variability in seismic risk, influenced by site conditions, construction quality, and urban density. Rusayl Industrial Estate emerges as a critical hotspot, while Al-Hail North, Old Al-Khoud, and Al-Mawaleh North exhibit elevated vulnerability due to dense development and aging infrastructure. In contrast, Al-Maabilah shows relatively better performance. Masonry and non-engineered buildings are identified as the most vulnerable typologies. The proposed framework supports risk-informed planning and offers a scalable model for rapidly urbanizing regions, aligning with Oman Vision 2040 and UN-SDG 11 to enhance urban seismic resilience.

papers.title: Hybrid machine learning-driven disease detection framework for internet of healthcare things with energy-efficient routing
papers.abstract: The Internet of Healthcare Things (IoHT) enables continuous health monitoring using body-worn biosensors, but energy constraints and limited clinical datasets remain significant challenges. This study proposes a dual-objective framework, the Hybrid Golden Eagle and Genetic Optimization Algorithm (HGEGA), to jointly optimize energy-efficient routing and disease detection. HGEGA selects cluster heads and routing paths by combining Golden Eagle global exploration with Genetic Algorithm-based local exploitation, while minimizing energy consumption and latency and maximizing throughput and packet delivery ratio. It also optimizes the hyperparameters of a heterogeneous ensemble comprising Random Forest, HistGradientBoosting, SVC, XGBoost, and LightGBM for disease classification. Simulation results show that HGEGA achieved a routing cost of 0.0174 and outperformed BWO, CO, RPO, ESO, and RPESA in energy consumption, delay, residual energy, throughput, and packet delivery ratio for 50–150-node networks. On the Diabetes, Heart Disease, and Lung Cancer datasets, the proposed ensemble achieved accuracies of 98.01%, 98.83%, and 96.52%, with MCC values of 0.9559, 0.9769, and 0.9346, respectively. The results demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively integrates energy-efficient routing with accurate disease detection for IoHT applications.

papers.title: Biomass-derived carbonized agrowaste biosorbents for efficient removal of phenolic compounds and herbicides from industrial effluents
papers.abstract: Biomass-derived carbonized agrowaste biosorbents (CAN-RH and CAN-CC) were prepared by hydrothermal carbonization, phosphoric acid activation, and controlled pyrolysis and systematically evaluated for the removal of phenol, 2,4-dichlorophenol (2,4-DCP), atrazine, and glyphosate. CAN-RH exhibited a hierarchical porous structure with a BET surface area of 1245 m2 g−1 and total pore volume of 0.682 cm3 g−1, compared with 1089 m2 g−1 and 0.594 cm3 g−1 for CAN-CC. The experimental equilibrium adsorption capacities of CAN-RH were 142.8, 176.3, 128.4, and 95.3 mg g−1 for phenol, 2,4-DCP, atrazine, and glyphosate, respectively, with 2,4-DCP exhibiting the highest (qmax) of 312.7 mg g−1. The Langmuir model provided the strongest fit to the equilibrium data, while the pseudo-second-order (PSO) model offered the best empirical description of the adsorption kinetics. Surface characterization using FTIR, CHNS analysis, EDS, Boehm titration, and pH-drift analysis supported the contributions of accessible surface functional groups, electrostatic interactions, hydrogen bonding, π–π interactions, and pore filling to the adsorption process. CAN-RH maintained substantial removal efficiency in the presence of inorganic salts and humic acid, whereas competitive adsorption in the quaternary system reduced adsorption capacities by 17.0–28.6%. The pH-stability study showed the lowest phosphorus release and mass loss under near-neutral conditions, with greater leaching under strongly acidic and alkaline conditions. After five regeneration cycles, CAN-RH retained 87.1% of its initial adsorption capacity, although its BET surface area decreased from 1245 to 742 m2 g−1. Batch treatment of real pharmaceutical and pesticide wastewaters at an adsorbent dose of 2 g L−1 for 3 h achieved 92.4–96.1% removal of the major target pollutants. These findings demonstrate the potential of agrowaste-derived carbon materials for multi-pollutant wastewater treatment while highlighting the importance of regeneration-induced textural changes, competitive effects, and pH-dependent stability in assessing their practical applicability.

papers.title: AFsample3 generates and selects multiple conformational states with AlphaFold3
papers.abstract: Accurately capturing the conformational diversity of proteins is essential for understanding their mechanisms and regulation. Current structure prediction methods, including those derived from AlphaFold, are largely limited to a single dominant conformation, and improved sampling has extended this to predicting two states. Here we present AFsample3, an enhanced sampling framework built on AlphaFold3 that improves both the generation and the selection of diverse protein conformations. Across a benchmark of 238 non-redundant proteins with multiple experimentally determined states, AFsample3 models the alternative conformation better than AlphaFold3 for 24% of targets and worse for only 3%, and increases the number of proteins whose alternative conformation is recovered at near-experimental accuracy from 57 to 96, a gain of 68% (p < 0.0001). The predicted ensembles are also markedly more diverse (p  < 0.0001), allowing intermediate and additional states to be modeled. These results demonstrate that, without retraining the underlying network, the improved sampling in AFsample3 can capture multiple native-like conformations, representing a significant advance in modeling protein conformational landscapes. This study presents AFsample3, a method that randomly masks the multiple sequence alignment during AlphaFold3 inference and then ranks the generated models to select distinct conformations. AFsample3 recovers alternative conformations for more proteins than AlphaFold3 and yields markedly more diverse ensembles, without retraining the network.

papers.title: Disrupted balance of gray–white matter interactions across psychiatric disorders
papers.abstract: Transdiagnostic neuroimaging has revealed convergent functional alterations in brain gray matter (GM) but has overlooked functional signals in white matter (WM). Although GM–WM interactions are essential for integrated brain function, it remains unclear whether these interactions exhibit shared alterations across psychiatric disorders. Here, we investigate the balance between redundant and synergistic information processing in GM–WM interactions using multi-site resting-state functional MRI data from 1,620 patients with one of five psychiatric disorders and 1,691 healthy controls. The dominant cross-disorder component explains 33.65% of the variance across disorder-specific case–control effects and follows a macroscale sensorimotor–association axis, differentiating the somatomotor network from frontoparietal and default-mode networks. Transcriptomic analyses link this cross-disorder pattern to astrocyte-related genes and synaptic pathways. Multiscale biological and functional features jointly explain 37.51% of its spatial variation, with cognitive associations and aerobic glycolysis contributing significantly. These findings identify a shared information-theoretic alteration in GM–WM interactions across psychiatric disorders and provide insight into their common neurobiological mechanisms.

papers.title: Phosphorylation of the C-terminus of PI4KA inhibits lipid kinase activity
papers.abstract: Phosphatidylinositol 4-kinase α (PI4KA) is a lipid kinase that generates phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P) from phosphatidylinositol (PI) at the plasma membrane (PM). PI4P generated by PI4KA is essential for both plasma membrane identity and for PIP2 and PIP3 signalling driven by the PLC and PI3K family of enzymes. While the structure of PI4KA is known, the regulatory mechanisms that control its activity are undefined. Here, we discovered PI4KA can be inhibited through phosphorylation of Y2090 in the kinase domain, which can be phosphorylated by multiple tyrosine kinases. Y2090 phosphorylation causes local conformational changes in the kα12 C-terminal helix. PI4KA activity is predominantly controlled through membrane recruitment by EFR3, with Y2090 phosphorylation inhibiting EFR3 bound PI4KA. Phosphorylation of the kα12 C-terminal helix is found in PI3Ks and PI4Ks, suggesting an evolutionarily conserved regulatory mechanism for diverse phosphoinositide kinases. Overall, our work reveals molecular insight into inhibitory post-translational regulation of PI4KA.

papers.title: Altered nuclear and synaptic distribution of HTT-associated ANP32E and PP2A-C in ataxic mutant mice and Huntington’s disease
papers.abstract: The acidic nuclear leucine-rich repeat phosphoprotein ANP32E removes H2A.Z.1 from chromatin and participates in protein phosphatase 2 A (PP2A)-associated synaptic signalling. This study investigated how Huntingtin (HTT) contributes to routing the acidic nuclear protein member E of 32 kDa (ANP32E) between nuclear and synaptic states. In silico modelling indicated proximity between ANP32E and HTT, either through the histones H2A.Z.1/H2B or PP2A-C. Using aptamer-based FRET in neuron-differentiated SH-SY5Y cells, we detected ANP32E–HTT proximity, influenced by retinoic acid differentiation and phosphatase modulation. Synaptosomal pull-down assays during cerebellar synaptogenesis revealed ANP32E, HTT, PP2A-C, and associated proteins like myosin Va. In cerebellar mutant models, staggerer and weaver showed genotype-specific changes in ANP32E–HTT–PP2A-C organisation. Imaging of human HD4 striatum samples revealed altered distribution of these proteins, supporting a model in which HTT regulates ANP32E routing between chromatin-associated and synaptic-associated states.

papers.title: High-resolution single-cell O-PTIR spectroscopy with supervised machine learning distinguishes erythrocyte maturation states and Plasmodium falciparum infection
papers.abstract: Interpreting high-dimensional single-cell spectroscopy data remains challenging, often obscuring subtle biological heterogeneity. Here, we combine high-resolution Optical Photothermal Infrared (O-PTIR) spectroscopy with supervised machine learning (ML) for quantitative, interpretable classification of closely related erythrocyte states. We evaluate this workflow in two settings: human erythrocyte maturation (reticulocytes vs. normocytes) and Plasmodium falciparum infection. While principal component analysis summarized major spectral variance, it did not consistently resolve these closely related classes. By contrast, supervised models, particularly k-nearest neighbours (k-NN), Naïve Bayes and Stochastic Gradient Descent achieved >85% accuracy for discriminating infected from healthy red blood cells and >70% for separating reticulocytes from normocytes. Discriminative wavenumbers identified by the best-performing models were grouped into broader spectral windows, revealing biochemical differences in protein-, phosphate/nucleic-acid-, and lipid-associated bands. Notably, infected reticulocytes exhibited larger infection-associated shifts in nucleic-acid/phosphate and lipid regions than infected normocytes, consistent with stronger biochemical remodeling in immature host cells. Extending our previous infrared spectroscopy study, this work applies O-PTIR to a four-group single-cell design with supervised, interpretable classification. Our results provide a validation framework for single-cell vibrational phenotyping in erythrocyte maturation and malaria infection. Interpreting high-dimensional single-cell spectroscopy data remains challenging, often obscuring subtle biological heterogeneity. Here, the authors combine high-resolution optical photothermal infrared spectroscopy with supervised machine learning for quantitative, interpretable classification of closely related erythrocyte states.

papers.title: Copper derived from deep-sea hydrothermal vent minerals facilitates hydrogen cyanide formation from glycine in alkaline aqueous environment
papers.abstract: In prevailing origin of life scenarios, hydrogen cyanide (HCN) is a key molecule for forming life’s essential building blocks, as demonstrated by HCN-centric prebiotic chemistry. However, whether HCN can be in-situ generated near deep-sea hydrothermal vents (HVs) has remained unexplored. Here, we show that a Cu-rich natural HV mineral reacts with glycine to generate HCN under alkaline, anaerobic conditions. Using 13C-isotopic labelled glycine, in-situ generation of HCN from glycine is confirmed, reaching concentration of 451.42 nM at 25 °C in 24 hours. HCN yield increases threefold at 10 °C. Copper leaching, and HCN generation from a glycine-CuCl2 mixture, or from synthetic Cu(Gly)2 in an anaerobic alkaline solution, indicate that copper(II) functions as an oxidant in this process. Because glycine can be generated through multiple pathways, our findings integrate cyanide chemistry into alkaline Cu-bearing HV environments, expanding the chemical diversity accessible within alkaline vent environments and potentially analogous systems beyond Earth.

papers.title: Childhood involvement with child protection services in Japan and adult health outcomes
papers.abstract: Prior research from Western contexts has linked childhood out-of-home care to adverse health conditions later in life, but evidence from Japan remains limited. This study investigated associations between childhood involvement with child protection services (CPS, Jidō Sōdanjo), and subsequent interventions, in relation to adult health and well-being in Japan. We analyzed data from the Japan COVID-19 and Society Internet Survey (JACSIS), a nationwide internet survey of randomly selected participants from an internet panel. Participants who were asked about CPS involvement during childhood were included (n = 15,426). All data were assessed in 2024. We conducted Targeted Maximum Likelihood Estimation to compare adults with and without CPS involvement. Subgroup analyses assessed outcomes by intervention type among those screened by CPS (n = 1491). Nearly 10% of participants report CPS screening in childhood. CPS screening is associated with a higher risk of several health conditions, including heart disease, stroke, and mental illness, while no significant differences are observed for behavior or sociodemographic characteristics. Among participants screened by CPS, individuals removed from their homes show significantly worse outcomes, including increased physical and mental health conditions. CPS screening alone is associated with poorer adult physical health outcomes, but not with adult behavioral or sociodemographic outcomes. Among participants who report CPS involvement, those placed in shelters or out-of-home care have a higher risk of adverse adult health outcomes than those not removed from their homes. Given the cross-sectional and retrospective design, these findings should not be interpreted causally. Rather, they underscore the need for research into the factors that contribute to these differences. Child maltreatment affects children worldwide, and understanding its long-term impact is essential for improving support systems. In Japan, child protection services (CPS) provide family interventions or relocate children to temporary shelters or care facilities. We surveyed over 15,000 Japanese adults about their childhood CPS experiences and current health and well-being. Adults with any CPS involvement had a higher risk of cardiovascular disease and mental illness. Those who were relocated from their homes showed even greater health risks compared to those who remained with their families. These findings suggest that children in out-of-home care may need enhanced support. Following Japan's 2024 child welfare reforms, systematic monitoring and improved care quality will be essential for addressing these disparities. Okuzono et al. surveyed over 15,000 Japanese adults about their childhood child protection services experiences and current health and well-being. Adults with any involvement showed higher risks of cardiovascular disease and mental illness, with those relocated from home showing even greater health risks than those who remained with their families.

papers.title: Predictive uncertainty representations in clinical AI shape physicians’ advice uptake, accuracy, and trust
papers.abstract: Machine-learning-based clinical decision support is entering routine care, but its value depends on whether clinicians can judge when to follow its advice and when to override it. Evidence suggests this judgment is often poorly calibrated in both directions. Whether displaying a model’s predictive uncertainty helps physicians integrate advice more selectively is unclear. In a preregistered, randomized vignette experiment, 227 physicians produced 1,802 sepsis risk assessments. Physicians gave an initial risk estimate, saw advice from a machine-learning system, and revised their estimate. They were randomized to see a risk score alone, or the score together with one of two visual representations of predictive uncertainty: icon arrays with uncertainty bands, or quantile dotplots. Outcomes were advice uptake, accuracy of the revised risk estimate, and trust. Here we show that both uncertainty representations increase advice uptake relative to the risk score alone, by 23% and 21%, and that the gap between correct and incorrect advice is descriptively about twice as large. Uptake of incorrect advice is not reliably reduced. Both formats improve the accuracy of revised risk estimates, with the larger effect for quantile dotplots, but only icon arrays increase trust. Physicians describe uncertainty as actionable only where they can tell why it is elevated. Displaying predictive uncertainty changes how physicians integrate machine-learning advice, but the representation format determines whether the benefit appears mainly as accuracy or trust. The effect is partial: uncertainty representations support recognizing reliable advice more than rejecting unreliable advice. AI systems can estimate how likely a patient is to develop a serious condition such as sepsis, but they are not always right, so doctors must judge when to follow them. We asked whether showing doctors how uncertain the system is about its own estimate helps that judgment. 227 doctors assessed eight patient cases, first alone and then after seeing the estimate; some also saw a picture of how uncertain it was. Doctors moved closer to the system when it was right and became more accurate, but not better at rejecting it when it was wrong. Showing uncertainty is therefore useful, but on its own it does not help doctors catch the cases where the system gets it wrong.

papers.title: Towards causal prediction models to guide personalised clinical decisions
papers.abstract: Clinical risk prediction models are widely championed as a way to deliver a precision medicine approach by guiding personalised care. However, in this perspective, we argue that current clinical risk prediction models are unable to guide personalised clinical decisions. This is because they are static models of association, rather than correctly specified counterfactual prediction models based on modifiable causes. They do not tell us whether changing a predictor variable will alter the outcome for an individual. Instead, the interventions recommended based on current risk prediction models are unrelated to the model itself and only shown to work on average across the population. To facilitate personalised care, clinical prediction models should be based on causation rather than association, model the conditional average treatment effect and predict counterfactuals, while also accounting for time-varying confounding. Then prediction models will be closer to meeting the precision medicine ideal. Leighton et al., argue that current clinical risk prediction models rely on associations, so they cannot show whether changing an individual’s predictors alters their outcome. The authors propose causal, counterfactual models that account for treatment effects and time-varying confounding to better guide personalised care.

papers.title: Molar-mass- and sequence-defined vinyl macromolecules via iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of α-substituted acrylates
papers.abstract: Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers enables mass production of widely used polymers, but typically affords products that are poorly defined in molecular size and monomer sequence. Despite advances in precision polymerization, chain growth remains probabilistic, precluding molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules. Here we report photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates, which enables quantitative addition of single building blocks without oligomerization. The α-acyl radical generated upon acrylate addition is irreversibly deactivated by rapid electron transfer within the photocatalytic cycle. A C(sp3)-centred radical is regenerated only after conversion of the terminal ester into a carboxylic acid and subsequent photoredox decarboxylation. Iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition yields vinyl macromolecules comprising residues identical to the repeat units of conventional vinyl polymers, without inseparable oligomeric impurities. Aperiodic vinyl-residue sequences can be assembled rapidly in continuous-flow reactors, offering a route towards fully automated synthesis of synthetic macromolecules and exploration of their sequence-dependent functions. Free-radical polymerization of simple vinyl monomers typically provides limited control over molecular size and monomer sequence. Now iterative photoredox decarboxylative addition of bulky α-substituted acrylates has been shown to enable quantitative incorporation of single monomers without oligomerization, supporting rapid continuous-flow synthesis of aperiodic molar-mass- and sequence-defined macromolecules.

papers.title: Coherent manipulation of interacting electron qubits on solid neon
papers.abstract: Electrons trapped on solid neon surfaces can serve as low-noise charge qubits with full electrical control and a compact device footprint. However, quantum information processing requires the implementation of two-qubit gates, which has been difficult to achieve in this system. Here we report the coherent manipulation of multiple interacting electron-on-solid-neon charge qubits. Using electrons that are naturally confined in close proximity on the neon surface, we demonstrate strong qubit–qubit coupling and implement the cross-resonance and bSWAP types of two-qubit operations using global microwave drives. Our results indicate that engineering electron confinement on solid neon may enhance control over the qubit–qubit interactions and yield a compact and scalable quantum computing architecture. Electrons on the surface of solid neon have been established as high-quality individual qubits. Now two-qubit gates have been demonstrated using the strong coupling between electrons confined in close proximity to each other.

papers.title: Supersolid crystals of dipolar excitons in a lattice
papers.abstract: In condensed-matter physics, long-range correlations introduce quantum states of matter that challenge intuition. For example, supersolids combine density order that manifests as symmetry-breaking spatial arrangement, and frictionless superfluid flow. However, supersolids have proven to exist only under very stringent conditions, with evidence limited to a few spontaneously fragmented superfluids observed in the weakly interacting regime. Here we demonstrate a framework to realize crystalline supersolids in the strong-interaction regime, by confining dipolar bosons in a lattice with long-range hopping. We show that dipolar excitons realize this lattice model. At fractional lattice fillings of one-quarter, one-third and one-half, we observe mesoscopic quantum crystals across around 100 sites that spontaneously break the lattice translational symmetry. At the same time, coherent long-range hopping induces off-diagonal long-range order such that the exciton solids are superfluids. Our numerical methods quantitatively confirm that supersolidity builds up in the ground state of the lattice Hamiltonian. Supersolids have previously been observed in weakly interacting scenarios. Now several supersolid phases are demonstrated in a strongly correlated system of dipolar excitons confined to a lattice with long-range hopping.

papers.title: Laser-induced streaking of megaelectronvolt electrons in a liquid medium
papers.abstract: Electron–laser interactions in liquids constitute fundamental processes underpinning a broad range of ultrafast spectroscopic and diffraction techniques, including time-resolved photoelectron spectroscopy, attosecond spectroscopy and ultrafast electron diffraction. Despite their central role, the interaction between free electrons and optical fields in a liquid environment remains largely unexplored. Here we present a comprehensive study of laser-induced streaking (LIS) of megaelectronvolt electrons in liquids using a state-of-the-art liquid-phase ultrafast electron diffraction setup. We identify a streaking mechanism distinct from the gas phase: instead of plasma lensing, liquid-phase LIS arises from a direct electron–light interaction mediated by the liquid’s dielectric response, regardless of whether the laser intensity is above or below the ionization threshold. This conclusion is supported by the dependencies of the streaking on laser incident angle, laser field strength and liquid thickness, as well as by the resulting distortion of scattering patterns. Furthermore, we demonstrate that LIS can be, under current experimental conditions, completely suppressed at near-collinear electron–laser incidence, even above the ionization threshold. Our findings elucidate a previously unknown interaction mechanism and provide critical guidance for preventing scattering pattern corruption in future liquid-phase ultrafast electron diffraction experiments. The liquid LIS phenomenon also has the potential to serve as a built-in timing tool for liquid-phase ultrafast electron diffraction experiments. Researchers demonstrate the laser-induced streaking of megaelectronvolt electrons in liquids. The effect originates from a dielectric-mediated electron–light interaction rather than plasma lensing. Experimental conditions under which the streaking can be suppressed are identified.

papers.title: Health impacts of urban water network upgrades from the PAASIM matched cohort trial in Beira, Mozambique
papers.abstract: We conducted a matched-control study to assess the impact of substantial improvements to the urban water system in Beira, Mozambique, on child health and enteric infections. The intervention reduced overall infection with individual pathogens by 10% and co-infection by 13%, especially among children with more than two pathogens. However, we found no impact of the intervention on infection with bacteria or protozoa as classes of pathogens, nor on diarrhoea, child growth or child mortality outcomes. We found no association between direct household water connections—independent of intervention status—on any outcomes. Our evidence points to potential impacts of the intervention on enteric pathogen infections, but estimates were imprecise. The impact of the intervention may have been limited by the lack of provision of continuous, reliable water supply and lack of safe water storage, leading to household contamination and infection from non-water-supply routes of exposure. Urban water infrastructure investments aim to reduce exposure to enteric pathogens and improve child health. Assessment of the effects of neighbourhood-level water infrastructure improvements in Beira, Mozambique, suggests that such improvements are associated with lower individual pathogen and co-infection prevalence, although they did not reduce diarrhoea, improve growth or affect child mortality.

papers.title: Feasibility is not the only measure of value in water research
papers.abstract: It is reasonable to ask how water research might matter in practice. It is less reasonable to expect every early-stage study to answer that question fully.

papers.title: Ultrafast cellulose nanocrystal production from diverse lignocellulosic biomass
papers.abstract: The production of cellulose nanocrystals conventionally relies on hazardous chemicals and energy-intensive purification, limiting their sustainable and scalable manufacture. Here we propose a hydrolytic quasi-solvent strategy that enables the rapid extraction of CNCs from microcrystalline cellulose within 15 min, and lignin-containing cellulose nanocrystals directly from untreated biomass within 1 h, with near-closed-loop solvent recycling. Composed entirely of the ionic liquids 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium hydrogen sulfate and 1-butyl-3-methylimidazolium chloride, the quasi-solvent leverages synergistic ionic interactions to enhance cellulose accessibility, surface functionalization and crystallite dispersion. Meanwhile, the imidazolium cations facilitate lignin removal from raw biomass through localized π–π interactions. Life cycle assessment shows that the recyclable process substantially reduces environmental impacts relative to conventional sulfuric acid hydrolysis and 2,2,6,6-tetramethylpiperidine-1-oxyl-mediated oxidation, while lowering estimated production costs by 55% and 33%, respectively. By integrating rapid nanocellulose extraction, direct biomass processing and solvent circularity, the present strategy provides a scalable and economically viable route towards resource-efficient lignocellulosic biorefineries. Producing cellulose nanocrystals conventionally involves hazardous chemicals, complex purification and high energy consumption. A recyclable hydrolytic quasi-solvent strategy now enables rapid production of cellulose nanocrystals from cellulose and untreated biomass with lower environmental impacts and costs.

papers.title: Superspreading droplets for scalable and green perovskite photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Transitioning perovskite solar cells from laboratory demonstrations to commercial production requires minimizing raw material waste while maximizing manufacturing throughput. Although drop-coating is a continuous, potentially waste-free manufacturing route, its sensitivity to substrate surfaces has limited its wider adoption. Here we describe an ink formulation containing driving solvents that amplify outward surface-tension gradients, forcing droplets to rapidly spread over a wide range of materials, including highly hydrophobic surfaces. This superspreading mechanism enables near-complete utilization of the precursor chemicals, while accelerating film-deposition rates by more than 30-fold. Fully drop-coated perovskite solar cells achieved a power conversion efficiency of 26.36% (certified 26.11%). The formulation also preserves the underlying crystallization pathway during scale-up, allowing direct translation to industrially relevant coating techniques. A large-area minimodule fabricated by blade-coating achieved an efficiency of 22.81% over a 54.8 cm2 aperture. By decoupling droplet spreading from substrate surface chemistry, this strategy provides a broadly applicable route to high-throughput, material-efficient perovskite film manufacturing and advances the scalable production of high-efficiency photovoltaics. Scaling up the manufacturing of perovskite solar cells requires rapid, zero-waste film deposition. The authors design a universal ink that accelerates production 30-fold, achieving high efficiencies.

papers.title: STEP Young trial shows semaglutide benefits in children
papers.abstract: In a phase 3 study, children with obesity lost significantly more weight with semaglutide than with placebo, with more than one third achieving a body mass index below the threshold for obesity.

papers.title: Author Correction: On-premise medical AI agents for reliable clinical decision-making
Later-born generations have better memory and lose it more slowly
papers.abstract: Dementia risk at any age has been falling for decades. An analysis of ~219,000 people followed for up to 30 years shows that newer generations start old age with a larger cognitive capacity that declines more slowly than that of previous generations, and this combined advantage is large enough to account for the fall in dementia incidence.

papers.title: Functional cardiac maturation and the loss of regenerative capacity in warm-blooded hearts
papers.abstract: Heart regeneration capacity differs between ectotherm and endotherm species. Many endotherms lose this ability shortly after birth while most ectotherms retain regenerative capacity throughout life. Here, we dissect critical differences in the endothermic heart, highlighting stronger cardiovascular function and a higher metabolic rate as key acquisitions. The gain of these properties during early neonatal development in mammals coincides with the gain of full thermogenic potential, cardiac maturation and loss of cardiac cell cycle activity. We discuss these maturation aspects in light of cardiac regeneration, how they influence proposed proliferation barriers and current knowledge gaps. These insights are complemented by supporting evidence in mouse genetic studies, case reports of humans with genetic mutations and drug treatments, where decreased contractile function can extend the postnatal proliferative window. Collectively, we highlight a compelling overarching paradigm that increased contractile function and metabolic demand are associated with the evolutionary loss of cardiac regenerative capacity. Devilée et al. explore reasons to explain the loss of cardiac regenerative capacity in endotherms, and highlight how postnatal increases in thermogenic capacity require increased cardiac performance and metabolic demand, driving cardiomyocyte maturation, epigenetic programming and cell cycle exit, linking evolutionary adaptations to diminished heart regeneration.

papers.title: A systematic review and meta analysis of extended reality interventions for chronic respiratory conditions
papers.abstract: Extended reality (XR) is increasingly used in rehabilitation but its effectiveness in chronic respiratory conditions remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies comparing XR-based interventions with usual care or alternatives. Searches were performed from inception to March 2025 and risk of bias was assessed by two independent reviewers. Fifteen experimental studies were included. XR-based interventions significantly improved 6-min walk distance (mean difference [MD] = 29.90 meters), forced vital capacity (MD = 0.37 liters), reduced dyspnea (standardized mean difference [SMD] = −0.61), anxiety (SMD = −2.08), and depression (SMD = −1.10), and improved quality of life (SMD = −1.87). No significant effects were observed for forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted or fatigue. Subgroup analyses showed stronger effects in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and with comprehensive XR programs. Exercise-based XR improved quality of life only, while activities of daily living simulations improved forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted, and nature-based interventions showed no significant benefit. Heterogeneity was substantial, but sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of primary outcomes. XR-based rehabilitation may improve exercise capacity, symptoms, and quality of life, but larger multicenter trials are required to confirm long-term effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: Multimodal AI for bacterial vs viral upper respiratory tract infection multicentre development and internal validation
papers.abstract: Distinguishing Group A streptococcus (GAS) pharyngitis from viral upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) is critical for appropriate antibiotic use but remains difficult on symptoms alone. We developed and internally validated a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model fusing pharyngeal images (Swin Transformer) with clinical metadata via gradient boosting decision trees, using 6666 visits and 119,988 images from 44 facilities collected March 2023–August 2025. For discriminating GAS from non-GAS (influenza A/B, COVID-19), the fusion model achieved area under the curve (AUC) 0.917 (95% confidence interval 0.907–0.926), outperforming image-only (0.902), metadata-only (0.871) and proxy Centor/McIsaac scores. At a pre-specified high-specificity threshold (≥0.90) sensitivity was 0.761; simulations indicated antibiotic-prescription reductions of 23–56% across GAS prevalences of 5–20%. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed.

papers.title: Sequential framework for predicting postoperative recurrence and antiseizure-medication withdrawal risk in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy
papers.abstract: Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (mTLE) is a common drug-resistant epilepsy. Temporal lobe resection is the most effective treatment, but postoperative recurrence and antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal remain major clinical challenges. Existing prediction tools are limited by endpoint specificity, restricted external validation, and lack of integration into sequential postoperative management pathways. We developed a sequential modelling strategy in mTLE, spanning recurrence prediction to ASM withdrawal risk stratification. In phase 1, postoperative recurrence models were developed and validated using 52 preoperative multimodal features in 1278 patients across cohorts 1–4 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.926–0.932 (internal) and 0.830–0.931 (three external sets), with a three-tier (low/intermediate/high) risk stratification. In phase 2, ASM withdrawal recurrence models were developed and validated in 679 seizure-free, phase 1 low/intermediate-risk patients eligible for withdrawal across cohorts 5–8 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.897–0.902 (internal) and 0.789–0.933 (three external sets), with risk stratification for individualized withdrawal estimation. Models showed good calibration, net clinical benefit, and SHAP-based interpretability. A research-based risk-estimation web tool was developed to support potential clinical translation. This promising modelling strategy integrates population-level risk stratification with individualized prediction, providing preliminary postoperative guidance: high-recurrence-risk patients may not be ideal for early ASM withdrawal despite seizure freedom, while low-risk patients may be considered for earlier withdrawal evaluation. Given the primarily retrospective design and relatively small phase 2 prospective cohort, further prospective external validation and clinical-impact studies are required before routine implementation.

papers.title: Potential of multimedia-supported informed consent in clinical practice: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Providing targeted, quality-assured patient information is essential for informed and autonomous decision-making but remains resource-intensive when delivered face-to-face. Multimedia-supported informed consent may enhance patient understanding and satisfaction while reducing physician time by complementing, rather than replacing, direct interaction. Our PRISMA-based systematic review, aiming to enable clinicians to implement and evaluate such a supplement, identified 907 articles of which 110 reports from OECD countries were included, including 62 randomized controlled trials. Among studies assessing the outcomes of interest, 71% reported improved patient understanding with multimedia tools compared to standard consent, 41% reported increased patient satisfaction (none reported decreases), and 91% found reduced or unchanged patient anxiety. In synthesis, to the extent possible despite substantial heterogeneity, findings suggest benefits and potential efficiency gains, and we were able to derive recommendations. However, considerable methodological variability and limitations affecting internal validity highlight the need for high-quality head-to-head comparative studies to draw more robust conclusions.

papers.title: Engineering vision: the comparative role of 3D printing and 3D bioprinting in corneal regeneration
papers.abstract: Corneal blindness remains a major global cause of vision loss, and the limited availability of donor tissue has intensified efforts to engineer functional corneal substitutes with appropriate optical, mechanical, and biological performance. Advances in additive manufacturing have positioned 3D printing and 3D bioprinting as promising platforms for fabricating anatomically informed constructs that may recapitulate key aspects of the cornea’s hierarchical architecture. This review provides a mechanistic comparison of these technologies with respect to material systems and (bio)ink formulation, processing strategies, scaffold architecture, cell incorporation, and biological integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the trade-off between high-fidelity 3D-printed scaffolds that can be seeded after fabrication and cell-laden bioprinted constructs that better capture early cell–matrix interactions, but remain constrained by bioink rheology, resolution, mechanical integrity, and shape retention. The review further examines emerging strategies, including decellularized extracellular matrix (ECM) bioinks, functionally graded hydrogels, and hybrid electrospun–printed constructs, for improving bioactivity, structural mimicry, collagen alignment, optical transmittance, and stromal-like ECM deposition. Persistent challenges include nanoscale and membrane-like architectural replication, long-term phenotype stability, reproducible manufacturing, surgical handling, storage, and regulatory classification of combination products. By integrating material science, fabrication physics, cellular responses, and translational considerations, this review delineates the complementary roles of 3D printing and 3D bioprinting and identifies the key design criteria required to advance printed corneal constructs toward clinically translatable regeneration.

papers.abstract: Predicting where species live is key to protecting biodiversity. The authors present EcoVAE, a generative model that rapidly and accurately predicts global species distributions, reveals species associations, and identifies sampling gaps.

papers.abstract: Identifying proteins in medium- to low-resolution cryo-electron tomography density maps remains challenging. Here the authors develop DomainSeeker, which combines AlphaFold2 models with experimental data to identify protein domains from density maps.

papers.title: CD33-CD45 interaction in Alzheimer’s disease susceptibility
papers.abstract: CD33 and CD45 are both genetically linked to Alzheimer’s risk. Here the authors show the two proteins physically interact, and this interaction is increased in Alzheimer’s disease.

papers.title: Subsets of regulatory T cells are CD1a-reactive and dysfunctional in psoriasis
papers.abstract: T regulatory cells (Treg) cells may be involved with the regulation of immune responses in psoriasis. Here, using psoriasis samples from humans, the authors characterize the function of CD1a-responsive Treg cells in psoriasis and show that these cells secrete IL-10 in response to lysophosphatidylcholine and are found in close proximity to CD1a + antigen-presenting cells and are potentially dysfunctional in psoriasis.

papers.title: A spectral-spatial interweaver for hyperdimensional photonic computing
papers.abstract: Photonic computing promises faster, more energy-efficient AI, but hardware scaling remains challenging. Here, the authors present HyperON, a TFLN-based hyperdimensional photonic computing network combining a spectral-spatial interweaver with wavelength-parallel modulators.

papers.title: Distinct mechanisms of CNV formation at the human 15q13.3 locus
papers.abstract: Recurrent copy-number variants at chromosome 15q13.3 cause neurodevelopmental disorders. Using long-read genome assemblies the authors show that these events arise via recombination promoted by inversions that vary in frequency across populations.

papers.title: Catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation for precise synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes
papers.abstract: The synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes typically requires metal catalysts, which show poor polymerisation control and require post-synthesis purification. Here, the authors report a metal catalyst-free thermal dehydropolycondensation strategy for the synthesis of silicon-incorporated polythiophenes with well defined structures, narrow dispersities and high charge carrier mobilities.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived phenylacetylglutamine exacerbates aortic aneurysm and dissection via activating macrophage integrin β1 in male mice
papers.abstract: Here the authors report a link between the gut microbial metabolite PAGln and aortic aneurysm and dissection in patients and show that it worsens disease in mice by promoting inflammation in the aortic wall.

papers.title: Host control of rhizobial proliferation in soybean nodules
papers.abstract: Legumes must tightly regulate rhizobial proliferation to optimize symbiotic benefits and avoid pathogenicity. Here the authors show a role for cell wall derived demethylesterified pectin in constrains rhizobial growth in soybean nodules

papers.title: Dissecting the root-fungal interface in 3D reveals spatially distinct signalling landscapes
papers.abstract: Plant-fungal interactions in the rhizosphere influence plant health. Here the authors describe an optically transparent granular microgel matrix that mimics the mechanical properties of natural microenvironments to dissect fungal development and pathogenesis.

papers.title: Bacteria-induced TLR2 signaling unleashes multiple mechanisms to reduce Treg immunosuppression and enhance cancer immunity
papers.abstract: Toll-like receptor (TLR) signaling is known to support T cell priming, but how different TLRs regulate intratumoral effector T cell function is unknown. The authors here demonstrate that TLR2 signaling in dendritic cells upon Listeria infection enhances cancer immunity by disrupting regulatory T cells and promoting tumor antigen presentation by DCs to CD8 T cells.

papers.title: Diminished subsurface oxygen maximum linked to rapid decline of the North Pacific Central Mode Water
papers.abstract: North Pacific Central Mode Water (CMW) shows a rapid decline from early 2020s, decreasing the subsurface oxygen maximum documented by Station ALOHA. Remarkably, the 2023–2024 El Niño failed to restore CMW due to atmospheric teleconnection.

papers.title: A macrocyclic peptide inhibitor of the antibiotic transporter NorA
papers.abstract: In this work, peptide efflux pump inhibitors were developed for Staphylococcus aureus NorA to serve as antibiotic adjuvants by leveraging chemical synthesis and design, structure-based insights, and screening approaches to probe NorA pocket engagement.

papers.title: A meta-analysis of genome-wide DNA methylation in endometriosis
papers.abstract: Epigenetics are increasingly thought to have a role in endometriosis. Here, the authors meta-analyse DNA methylation data to show the methylation differences between healthy endometrial tissue and ectopic endometrial lesions.

papers.title: Promoted phase transition in perovskite heterojunctions via in-situ regulated 2D intermediates enables stable solar cells
papers.abstract: Efficient perovskite solar cells require graded layered junctions, yet spacer-driven ion exchange offers poor control. Yue et al. added a preformed layered perovskite to direct vertical phase growth at the buried interface, improving efficiency, stability, and module scalability.

papers.title: Programmable synaptic and stochastic regimes in a monolayer hBN atomristor
papers.abstract: 2D materials show rich dynamic behaviors, but most devices support only one operating regime. Jeon et al. report that a monolayer hBN memristor enables electrically programmable switching between synaptic and stochastic behaviors, providing distinct operating regimes within a single atomically thin device.

papers.title: Iso-Seq enables discovery of novel isoform variants in human retina at single-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Iso-Seq enabled isoform discovery of human retina at single cell levels. This study revealed novel isoforms, splice junctions and alternative promoters across major retinal cell types, providing insights into the retinal transcriptomic landscape.

papers.title: Unidirectional rolling of single-crystal graphene into nanoscrolls
papers.abstract: Rolled-up nanoscrolls based on 2D materials exhibit interesting emerging properties, but their scalable synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report the fabrication of aligned graphene nanoscrolls with tunable thickness via deterministic rolling of wafer-scale single-crystal graphene films during post-growth cooling, showing enhanced photoresponse and high carrier mobility.

papers.title: 3D-MINSTED nanoscopy and protein tracking in densely labelled living cells
papers.abstract: 3D-MINSTED enables single fluorophore 3D tracking with precision down to <1 nm. Despite dense labelling and background, it resolves sub-10 nm DNA-origami spacing and 16 nm kinesin-1 steps in fixed and living cells at high labelling density.

papers.title: Single-molecule landscape of DNA replication pausing
papers.abstract: Rare DNA replication pauses can destabilise genomes but are hard to detect. Here, the authors use single-molecule nanopore sequencing to map pauses across a eukaryotic genome. They find widespread pauses enriched near transcribed genes and with a leading-strand bias over the promoter of an epigenetically regulated gene.

papers.title: Autosomal dosage compensation in aneuploidy and cancer involves transcriptional burst regulation
papers.abstract: Aneuploidy alters chromosome copy number and is often associated with impaired cellular function. Here, the authors show that cells compensate for autosomal chromosome gains and losses through genome‑wide transcriptional and protein‑level buffering mechanisms, helping to maintain gene dosage balance in normal and cancer cells.

papers.title: Bidirectional control of a metabolic transition by the GID ubiquitin ligase
