papers.title: Highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing for monogenic and polygenic diseases from spent medium
papers.abstract: Traditional preimplantation genetic testing for in vitro fertilization (IVF) requires invasive trophectoderm biopsy, which may harm the embryo. Non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing (niPGT) utilizing cell-free DNA from spent embryo culture medium (SCM) has been attempted, but trace DNA content, maternal cell contamination and high allele drop-out rates are barriers. Here we report an niPGT methodology achieving high diagnostic accuracy among reportable samples across diverse embryo and disease contexts. Reengineered linear whole-genome amplification (scm-LIANTI) with an extremely low error rate is followed by application of a Bayesian algorithm designed to determine which parental haplotypes are inherited at disease-causing sites. Among 191 SCM samples from 29 families affected by rare monogenic disorders, our method amplified all samples and enabled diagnosis of 220 out of 277 pathogenic alleles. All diagnoses (220/220) were concordant with invasive biopsy control. For select embryos, personalized genome-wide genotyping enabled exploratory polygenic risk assessment for type 2 diabetes. Our methodology requires no modification to IVF workflows and represents a key technological advance towards scalable, accurate and safe niPGT for both monogenic and polygenic diseases. A reengineered linear whole-genome amplification approach combined with Bayesian linkage analysis enables highly accurate non-invasive preimplantation genetic testing of embryos from families with rare monogenic disorders.

ISOMPRA enables the disambiguation of transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of genetic variants
papers.abstract: Some classic massively parallel reporter assays to study transcriptional regulatory effects of DNA sequence elements cannot readily distinguish these from post-transcriptional regulatory effects of the same element on RNA. Therefore, we developed an approach enabling assessment of DNA/RNA regulatory elements in parallel: Inferred Stability Optimized Massively Parallel Reporter Assay (ISOMPRA). ISOMPRA quantifies pre-spliced RNA to more directly assess transcription rate, and spliced RNA, corrected for transcription rate, to identify RNA stability-altering 3′-UTR elements. We benchmark ISOMPRA with both predicted enhancers and 3′-UTR elements, including regions containing autism patient mutations. We identify numerous functional enhancers and UTRs and discover a subset with high-impact mutations. We further show that failing to consider both potential transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects results in numerous possible false positives and false negatives. Finally, we adapt ISOMPRA for cell-type-specific in vivo use, enabling analyses of variants in specific cell types in the brain and measurement of regulatory impacts of in vivo traits, such as sex. ISOMPRA is a new method for assessing transcriptional and post-transcriptional effects of regulatory elements in a massively parallel reporter assay. This method can be used in vivo or in vitro to understand variants associated with disease.

papers.title: Author Correction: GHT-SELEX demonstrates unexpectedly high intrinsic sequence specificity and complex DNA binding of many human transcription factors
Modular mRNA-encoded helper proteins enhance DNA delivery
papers.abstract: DNA delivery is limited by inefficient nuclear translocation and restrictive intracellular environments. Here we present mRNA-enhanced DNA delivery (MEND), a system that codelivers mRNA-encoded helper proteins to actively prime cells for enhanced DNA processing. We demonstrate three classes of MEND proteins: DNA translocators, host modulators and immune dampeners. MEND’s modular framework boosts transgene expression across various delivery vehicles and DNA formats in vitro and in vivo with LNP delivery. DNA delivery is improved with codelivered helper proteins.

papers.title: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose-based dissolving microneedle platform enabling efficient transdermal delivery of a poorly water-soluble drug
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop an optimal microneedle based on hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) matrix for the effective transdermal delivery of dexibuprofen (DXI). After evaluating the mechanical strength and drug solubility of various biocompatible polymers, HPMC was selected as the optimal microneedle matrix. HPMC not only provided sufficient mechanical strength for the microneedle but also enhanced the solubility of DXI. Various microneedle formulations with different DXI-to-HPMC weight ratios were developed and comprehensively evaluated in terms of physicochemical and mechanical properties, skin insertability, solubility, in vitro drug release, ex vivo skin permeability, in vivo pharmacokinetics, and post-insertion skin safety. Among them, the optimal HPMC-based microneedle with a DXI:HPMC weight ratio of 1:1.25 (w/w) was selected. The selected formulation demonstrated excellent mechanical strength and insertability. The HPMC-based microneedle system enhanced drug solubility, release rate, and skin permeability, achieving a 13-fold increase in relative bioavailability compared with the needleless film. Histological evaluation based on H&E staining showed that the skin structure recovered within 3 days, with no obvious histological signs of irritation or inflammation. These findings suggest that HPMC-based microneedles may serve as a useful transdermal delivery platform for improving the solubility and relative bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs such as DXI.

papers.title: Experimental investigation of factors affecting the strength performance of geopolymer-stabilized clay soil
papers.abstract: Implementing construction projects in areas with swelling clay soils has always been challenging for civil engineers. Swelling clays undergo significant volumetric changes due to variations in water content. This situation causes significant damage to structures built on the land in question. For this reason, the engineering properties of the soil must be improved before construction. Cement is one of the most commonly used materials in soil stabilization. However, cement production is a process that consumes natural resources and energy, involving the release of large amounts of carbon dioxide (CO2) into the atmosphere. In this study, the effects of fly ash content (12, 16, 20%), NaOH molarity (8, 10, 12, 14), curing time (7, 28, 56 days), and temperature (25, 50, and 80 °C) on the strength of clay-fly ash geopolymer mixtures were investigated. Unconfined compressive tests were performed on samples compacted to the maximum dry density using an alkali activator at the optimum water content. As a result, high strength values were obtained in the prepared geopolymer samples. The unconfined compressive strength (UCS) of the geopolymer samples increased as the fly ash content, molarity, and curing time increased. Furthermore, the highest strength values were obtained in samples cured at 80 °C.

papers.title: Explainable validation of pseudo-label via spatial consensus for semi-supervised semantic segmentation of remote sensing images with sparse ground-truth and representational bias
papers.abstract: Addressing the challenges of sparse annotations, representational bias, and unreliable pseudo-label propagation in aerial image segmentation, a semi-supervised learning framework is proposed. It strategically integrates representational bias handling and pseudo-label refinement through an explainable validation via spatial consensus. An implicit student-teacher setup is employed wherein the base segmentation model acts as the student and the teacher role is fulfilled implicitly through auxiliary bias correction and XAI-based validation modules, without requiring a separate mirrored network. The base segmentation model generates initial predictions on unlabeled data. A binary classifier identifies instances likely containing under-represented classes, which are subsequently refined using a specialised segmentation model trained on under-represented class samples. To ensure reliability, class-specific Grad-CAMs are generated via a VGG16 encoder fine-tuned with image-level labels and compared with predicted masks through an IoU-based external alignment score. Simultaneously, internal Grad-CAMs extracted from the decoder output channels of the base segmentation model are compared with the external Grad-CAMs to derive a spatial consensus score across architecturally independent models. Together, these two diagnostic signals are combined to find the most confident pseudo-labels with weights based on the consensus score to guide a pixel wise focal loss. Rather than treating all these pseudo labels equally, this mechanism continuously adjusts how much each label contributes during retraining. It assigns more weight to those that pass semantic verification and gives less preference the ones that don’t. This approach has been evaluated on the DLRSD and DeepGlobe benchmarks where it consistently outperformed existing methods. The gains were pronounced even when labeled data was scarce with improvements in mIoU, F1 score and per-class robustness.

papers.title: Automatic generation of interface limit equations for power systems using rule-augmented instruction-tuned large language models
papers.abstract: Dispatch centers must frequently maintain and verify interface limit information as the operating patterns of new power systems become more complex. Such information often exists as unstructured text, including procedural clauses, experiential descriptions, and table annotations, and manual interpretation and formula compilation are inefficient and prone to omissions. This paper formulates the conversion of interface limit text into formulas as a grammar-constrained generation problem and proposes a neuro-symbolic framework whose released outputs are verified against an explicit output grammar. First, the mapping between interface limit information and standardized formulas is analyzed, an expert rule repository and a corpus are constructed, and a domain-adapted BERT-CNN model extracts entities and logical relationships. Second, LoRA instruction fine-tuning is combined with retrieval-augmented generation, so that formula candidates are grounded in repository rules. Third, an abstract-syntax-tree validator checks syntactic validity, type consistency, unit dimensional consistency, and condition coverage on every candidate, and each released formula is therefore closed under the output grammar. Experiments on a document-level partitioned corpus of 2547 segments from a provincial grid show that the proposed method achieves 96.83% entity recognition F1 and 92.50% execution accuracy, outperforming traditional deep learning models and general-purpose large language models. The corpus is derived from a single provincial grid, and the quantitative results are scoped accordingly. The system serves as a decision-support tool under expert review and helps power companies reduce omissions in interface limit maintenance.

papers.title: Research on image classification recognition model based on multi-attention mechanism and deep learning
papers.abstract: The accurate image classification is among the basic requirements for the implementation of artificial intelligence in various fields. Designing image classification techniques based on multi-attention mechanisms and deep learning is still a big challenge. This work presents the Enhanced Multi-Attention Network (EMAN), a new image classification network architecture that aggregates complementary attention in a holistic fashion. EMAN takes advantage of the merits of different types of attention, namely Dilated Large Kernel Attention (DLKA), Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM), Efficient Channel Attention (ECA), and Global Context Block (GCBlock), to effectively attend to both local details and global context across images. Extensive experiments conducted on the CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny-ImageNet-200, and Birds-400 datasets show that the proposed method achieves strong performance compared with existing techniques while maintaining acceptable computational cost. Feature extraction studies confirm the unique role of each attention mechanism in the overall system performance and highlight the importance of using them in combination. In the visual analysis, each attention mechanism pays attention to different specific regions of the input image, so that the understanding of the image content is more complete, the performance is better than single-attention methods. The results show that the proposed model achieves high classification accuracy and maintains a balanced performance in terms of precision, recall and F1-score across datasets of different complexity levels.

papers.title: Multi-signal open-set intrusion detection and incremental learning for smart grid cybersecurity
papers.abstract: Smart grids depend on communication networks. This exposes them to attacks that were never seen during training. Most learning-based intrusion detection systems (IDSs) assume a closed set of attack classes and cannot adapt without full retraining. We present OSI-AE-CNN-GRU, a framework that couples autoencoder latent features and a CNN–GRU classifier with a seven-signal open-set score and prototype-guided incremental learning. Unknown traffic is ranked for analyst review and, once verified, folded into the model. On CICIDS2017, holding out Bot, PortScan, FTP-Patator and SSH-Patator in turn, the framework reaches open-set AUROC of 0.875, 0.885, 0.813 and 0.910 (mean 0.871), with area-under-precision–recall lifts of 3.7–6.2 times over chance. We also report a new diagnostic finding. Minimum distance to the nearest class prototype is anti-correlated with novelty in this latent space (validation AUROC 0.06 in all four rounds). Correcting its sign raises mean AUROC from 0.810 to 0.871. We show which novelty signals can be calibrated from a proxy class and which cannot. Single-stage adaptation reaches new-class F1 of 0.967–0.991 with forgetting of 0.070–0.090; after four sequential additions the model retains 92% of the joint-retraining bound. Ranking quality degrades gracefully under Gaussian noise and inference costs 0.09–0.11 ms per flow. At realistic prevalence (0.06–0.27%) the absolute recall at deployable alert budgets is low, which we quantify and state as the main limitation.

papers.title: Effects of a gender-mixed avatar with male and female body halves on gender identity
papers.abstract: Virtual reality can induce ownership of a virtual body unlike the user’s own, enabling exploration of gender identity. Opposite-gender avatars make gender identity more fluid but do not yield a dual masculine and feminine identity. We examined whether a gender-mixed avatar (male right half, female left half) elicits body ownership and promotes acquisition of both gender identities. Twenty participants used gender-mixed, same-gender, and opposite-gender avatars under synchronous and asynchronous movement. We measured ownership and agency by questionnaire, explicit gender roles with the Bem Sex Role Inventory (BSRI), and implicit gender identity with a single-category Implicit Association Test (IAT). Synchronous movement increased ownership and agency, but ownership of the gender-mixed avatar was lower than for the same-gender avatar and below the midpoint. BSRI scores did not change. IAT responses were faster after the opposite-gender than after the gender-mixed avatar, independently of synchrony. The gender-mixed avatar was not experienced as a body of both genders, since its effects did not exceed those of the opposite-gender avatar. As these effects were independent of synchrony, they likely reflect higher-order cognitive processes rather than the ownership illusion. Because the avatar also combined two individuals into an implausible body, conclusions are specific to this implementation.

papers.title: Persistence and selective modal excitation of topological interface state in one-dimensional periodic-on-average photonic crystal heterostructure
papers.abstract: Topological interface states exhibit robustness against certain defects and local disorder as long as the bulk band gap remains open and the perturbations preserve the underlying symmetry. Here, we systematically examine the impact of global structural disorder on topological interface states in a one-dimensional periodic-on-average topological photonic crystal heterostructure and identify the disorder level up to which these states persist. Two distinct photonic crystals are designed to possess overlapping band gaps and distinct topological invariants, characterized by the Zak phases of their bulk bands. The concatenation of these crystals gives rise to three interface states at different band gaps. Structural disorder induces spectral fluctuations in the topological interface states, which increase with increasing disorder. Statistical analysis reveals that the probability of disorder-deformed interface state occurrence decreases, the mean spectral position remains stable, and the quality factor decreases exponentially with increasing disorder amplitude. The spatial confinement of disorder-deformed topological interface states is quantified using the inverse participation ratio, which reveals an exponential decay of the quality factor with the effective localization length of the interface state. Sub-threshold modal gain analysis in the topological heterostructure is carried out by introducing non-saturable optical gain in the constituent layers. For a relatively weaker disorder, the topological interface state reaches the threshold at a relatively low gain owing to its high quality factor. Increasing disorder raises the modal gain threshold and leads to the emergence of competing disorder-localized modes. By matching the spatial gain profile of the photonic heterostructure with the field profile of the disorder-deformed interface states, the interface states are selectively excited, enabling disorder-resilient topological lasers.

papers.title: Benchmarking lightweight YOLO detectors for plastic and beverage-carton packaging on an operational sorting line
papers.abstract: Plastic packaging is widely discarded rather than recycled, and recovering it depends on efficient sorting of mixed waste. Automated sorting lines increasingly use computer vision to identify recyclable items on moving conveyors, but many reported results come from curated imagery with less clutter than real waste streams. We benchmarked twelve compact YOLO detectors and a medium-capacity YOLO11m reference under a common fine-tuning protocol, using 5,261 annotated frames from two continuous video recordings of an operational sorting conveyor and covering polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high-density polyethylene (HDPE), mixed plastic, and beverage cartons. Because consecutive frames can show the same objects, frames were grouped into temporal blocks, and a temporal buffer excluded test frames within 20 frames of training or validation data; five models underwent block-grouped five-fold cross-validation. On the buffered test set, YOLOv8s led the compact models with a mean average precision (mAP@0.5:0.95) of 0.470, compared with 0.482 for YOLO11m. Across cross-validation folds, YOLO26s and YOLOv9s had the smallest mean accuracy gaps from YOLO11m. No comparison with the reference was significant after multiplicity adjustment; equivalence was not established. In the class-specific analysis of YOLOv9s, HDPE showed the largest per-frame recall decline, falling by 0.369 between the least and most cluttered quartiles. Increasing input resolution from 512 to 1280 pixels raised mAP by 0.089–0.103, with no clear evidence that capacity or resolution preferentially mitigated clutter-related degradation. Box-level copy-paste augmentation produced small average gains, positive in ten of twelve paired seed comparisons. Although operational suitability requires system-level validation, YOLO26s retained 93% of the reference’s test-set mAP at approximately one-third of its single-thread CPU pipeline latency, suggesting that compact detectors merit consideration for sorting lines with limited computing resources.

papers.title: Detecting multimodal sarcasm through temporal emotion drift modelling
papers.abstract: The ambiguity between the literal and the intended sense of the communication has made the Sarcasm detection a challenge in the natural language processing and sentiment analysis. The traditional text-based methods are usually unable to recognize the intent of sarcasm as it is rarely expressed exclusively in words and is defined by the presence of minor indicators within the prosody, facial expressions, and conversation. This constraint decreases the strength of sarcasm detection systems in real world scenarios like conversational agent, social media monitoring and human-computer interaction. In order to fill this gap we have suggested a Temporal Emotion Drift Model (TEDM) that combines textual, acoustic, and visual input and explicitly models temporal emotion drift, which is the gradual transformation of emotion cues across dialogue turns. As opposed to the fixed feature fusion methods, TEDM is sensitive to the dynamic variation of the emotional tracks and as such, the model is designed to capture temporal inconsistencies associated with sarcastic reversals. Our model uses a lightweight transformer-based fusion network to fit the multimodal embeddings (text, audio, and video) and then, temporal attention is used to follow the pattern of affective drift. The proposed model was evaluated on the MUStARD and MUStARD + + multimodal sarcasm detection benchmarks, demonstrating competitive sarcasm detection performance across both datasets. The ablation results showed that removing the emotion-drift component reduced the F1-score by 6.45% points on MUStARD, indicating its contribution under the evaluated experimental setting. The results indicate that modelling temporal changes in multimodal affective representations provides useful cues for sarcasm detection. The measured edge-device performance further demonstrates the feasibility of low-latency inference under the evaluated deployment configuration.

papers.title: Electroactive and antibacterial bioadhesive based on bio-ionic liquids for tissue repair
papers.abstract: Recently, improvement of the bioelectrical microenvironment of injured skin has emerged as a promising strategy to accelerate tissue regeneration, since endogenous electrical cues play a crucial role in regulating cell behavior and the wound healing process. However, achieving an optimal balance among electrical conductivity, robust tissue adhesion, mechanical stability, antibacterial activity, and cytocompatibility within a single, biocompatible, filler-free hydrogel platform remains challenging. Here, we design a hydrogel composed of gelatin, tannic acid (TA), and various concentrations of a choline–acrylate bio-ionic liquid (BIL), termed the BIL-TA-Gelatin (BTG) hydrogel, to create an electrically responsive platform for skin repair. The BTG hydrogels exhibit swelling ratios of 258–291%, together with BIL-dependent ionic conductivity (0.18–2.00 mS/cm), compressive modulus (1.90–3.00 MPa), and compressive strength (0.55–1.55 MPa). In vitro assays also demonstrate excellent fibroblast attachment and proliferation, along with significant antibacterial activity. Moreover, the hydrogels show robust tissue adhesion (270–341 kPa). In summary, by integrating efficient ionic conductivity with robust mechanical, adhesive, and biological properties, the developed BTG hydrogel provides a multifunctional electroactive matrix capable of supporting electrically responsive skin regeneration and represents a promising multifunctional platform for wound dressing applications warranting further in vivo evaluation.

papers.title: Disrupted developmental trajectory of ultrasonic vocalizations in a rat model of fragile X syndrome
papers.abstract: Communication deficits are a defining feature of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and among the earliest detectable markers of atypical neurodevelopment. Yet how specific genetic ASD risk factors shape the developmental trajectory of vocal communication remains poorly understood. Fragile X syndrome (FXS) is one of the most common inherited causes of ASD, resulting from the transcriptional silencing of the FMR1 gene, and a majority of FXS individuals exhibit impaired language development and atypical vocal communication. Rodent ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) produced during maternal isolation provide a tractable model for studying the developmental trajectory of early vocal communication in FXS. Here, we characterized isolation-induced USVs in male Fmr1 knockout (KO) and littermate wildtype (WT) rats from postnatal days 3–21 to determine whether Fmr1 mutation disrupts the acoustic structure, temporal organization, or sequential syntax of USVs across postnatal development. We found that Fmr1 KO rat pups exhibited reduced call number during the peak developmental window for isolation-induced calling (p6–p10), while acoustic structure and temporal organization were largely preserved. Network analysis of call transitions revealed that WT pups exhibited a progressive increase in syntactic complexity from p3–p10. However, this developmental trajectory was significantly altered and delayed in Fmr1 KO pups. Together, these findings demonstrate that Fmr1 mutation not only disrupts vocal production but also syntactic flexibility in rats, highlighting USV syntax as a sensitive marker of atypical communicative development in FXS rodent models.

papers.title: T-ResUNet: a spatiotemporal residual U-Net for decade-scale landuse and landcover change trend segmentation
papers.abstract: Accurate Landuse Landcover (LULC) change detection is critical for urban sprawl monitoring, environmental impact assessment, agriculture, and water resource management. Despite advances in LULC mapping, existing methods inadequately capture decade-scale land-cover dynamics across heterogeneous regions. This work addresses this gap through a temporal deep learning framework that enables accurate and scalable LULC change trend analysis. Building on these contributions, the present research extends the scope to long-term, multi-temporal LULC change detection across two diversified geographic regions of Jaipur (Rajasthan-India) and Paris (France) for the year 2015–2025. This study proposes T-ResUNet (Temporal ResNet-U-Net) hybrid model, an enhanced deep neural network architecture that integrates the strengths of ConvLSTM, U-Net with a ResNet encoder for LULC change trend segmentation. T-ResUNet is different from typical ResNet-U-Net architectures that mainly focus on spatial feature extraction and segmentation and ConvLSTM-based architectures that mainly focus on temporal dependency modeling by integrating both capabilities into a common encoder-temporal modeling-decoder architecture. The open-source Sentinel-2 sensor is used to acquire high resolution satellite imagery with multi-spectral and multi-temporal data. The LULC monitoring and trend analysis are done in the context of urbanization for the nine classes (water, trees, grass, flooded vegetation, crops, shrub & scrub, built-up (urban), bare ground, and snow & ice classes). The proposed T-ResUNet achieves 92.7% classification and segmentation accuracy, with better IoU and F1-scores for long-term LULC change detection, compared to SOTA models. The best performance was achieved with the built-up class (F1-score 0.91 for Jaipur and 0.94 for Paris and IoU 0.84 for Jaipur and 0.89 for Paris. The results demonstrate the potential of T-ResUNet for transferable long-term LULC change analysis across geographically and environmentally distinct urban regions, with diverse climatic and ecological conditions to determine the model generalizability.

papers.title: Chronic insomnia: efficacy of very low dose mirtazapine and gabapentin
papers.abstract: Chronic insomnia is a highly prevalent sleep disorder. The management of insomnia is frequently challenging, and combined behavioral non-pharmacological interventions and medications are often used in clinical practice. The long-term safety concerns and efficacy issues associated with FDA-approved insomnia medications often lead providers to treat insomnia with medications approved for other indications, including anxiety and depression. This report describes 41 patients with chronic insomnia treated with very low dose mirtazapine with and without the combination of low dose gabapentin during a mean follow-up period of 11 months, and reveals adequate clinical response and effectiveness, with minimal intolerance. Several patients were weaned off medications with a higher level of dependence (e.g. benzodiazepines). Therefore, low doses of safe medications may provide a better strategy to treat chronic insomnia and are deserving of further studies to explore these findings.

papers.title: Diminished spatial dynamics and maladaptive spatial complexity link resting brain network disruption to cognition in schizophrenia
papers.abstract: Resting-state fMRI studies typically emphasize temporal connectivity fluctuations, overlooking intrinsic spatial dynamics of brain networks. We introduce “dynamic spatial network complexity and connectivity" (dSNCC), combining dynamic independent component analysis with volume and fractal dimension (FrD) to quantify network expansion, contraction, structural complexity changes, and interactions. Analyzing 508 subjects (315 controls, 193 patients), schizophrenia was associated with higher mean FrD across networks, indicating disorganized spatial boundaries. Volume-residualized analyses confirmed this boundary complexity alteration persists independently of volume changes. Crucially, patients exhibited reduced “dynamic flexibility" - a widespread loss of temporal variability in volume and FrD from network core to periphery. Higher complexity and reduced flexibility (maladaptive complexity) were associated with cognitive impairment in processing speed and visual/verbal learning. Patients also showed aberrant fractal dimension coupling between networks, indicating overly synchronized complexity changes. dSNCC provides a scale-free biological signature demonstrating spatial disorganization and dynamic spatial rigidity underlie cognitive deficits in schizophrenia.

papers.title: Organization, development, and plasticity of the serotonergic dorsal raphe nucleus projectome
papers.abstract: The dorsal raphe nucleus (DRN) is the main source of serotonin in the central nervous system. Serotonergic DRN neurons modulate a wide range of physiological functions and brain states via their widespread projections. Yet the organizational logic, developmental dynamics, and experience-dependent plasticity of these projections remain poorly understood. By reconstructing the whole brain projections of 81 serotonergic DRN neurons across developmental stages in the larval zebrafish, we find that these neurons exhibit diverse projection patterns, ranging from broadly distributed to spatially confined. We identify two previously uncharacterized, projection-defined subpopulations within the larval DRN, which selectively target either the telencephalon or the spinal cord. This organization is consistent with the existence of anatomically distinct serotonergic pathways that may differentially influence forebrain and sensorimotor circuits. Longitudinal analysis revealed that the gross architecture of serotonin neurons remained stable during larval development, although region-specific remodeling occurred in all neurons. Importantly, stress exposure during the first week of development, but not thereafter, altered the density of projections to telencephalic regions, suggesting a critical window of increased plasticity during early life. Collectively, our findings clarify the developmental trajectory, maturation, and stress-induced plasticity of the serotonergic circuitry, providing important insights for deciphering the pathophysiology of stress-related mental disorders.

papers.title: Single-cell and genomic landscapes reveal the tumor microenvironment of adolescent minimally invasive lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: The rising detection of adolescent pulmonary nodules highlights a clinical gap, as applying adult guidelines risks overtreatment. Here, we integrate whole-exome sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-cell transcriptomics to profile the tumor ecosystem of adolescent minimally invasive lung adenocarcinoma. Adolescent tumors show a distinct mutational landscape with lower tumor mutational burden. In the microenvironment, ITGA2+ malignant cells exhibit higher stemness, while CCDC138+ macrophages show transcriptional signatures of reduced antigen presentation, suggesting susceptibility to early tumor initiation. Despite these features, adolescent tumors often follow an indolent course. Type 1 terminally differentiated effector memory CD8 T cells that re-express CD45RA (CD8_EMRA1) exhibit elevated Granzyme A expression and transcriptional signatures of enhanced cytotoxicity, correlating with favorable clinical outcomes. Age-dependent analysis identifies 22.1 years as a critical point when CD8_EMRA1 abundance declines. Radiomics- and pathomics-based models enable evaluation of CD8_EMRA1 enrichment, supporting risk stratification and personalized management. These findings provide a multi-omics resource and conceptual framework to inform age-adapted clinical strategies.

papers.title: Nasopharyngeal colonisation by Streptococcus pneumoniae enhances host anti-viral responses to respiratory virus infection
papers.abstract: Viral-bacterial interactions during co-infection are often synergistic and can increase disease severity. Emerging evidence indicates that some bacteria can antagonise viral infection, although the host responses driving this process remain unclear. Using infant mice co-infected with the nasopharyngeal inhabitant and pathogen Streptococcus pneumoniae and pneumonia virus of mice (PVM) to model antagonistic interactions, we found that prior bacterial colonisation enhances and prolongs anti-viral immune responses during co-infection, compared with viral infection alone. Transcriptomic, immunological, and histological analyses showed that pneumococcal colonisation prior to PVM infection enhanced and prolonged interferon signalling, increased anti-viral cytokine and chemokine protein levels. Notably, over 50% of differentially expressed host genes during co-infection were not differentially expressed in either infection alone. Our work shows that bacterial colonisation can modulate host immunity, shaping how the immune system responds to incoming viral infections, which has potential for future therapeutic applications.

papers.title: MHC-E presentation of lentivirus antigens can induce differential NKG2C NK cell responses
papers.abstract: Natural killer (NK) cells represent a critical component of host defense against viral infections. NK cell activation requires integration of activating and inhibitory receptors to lyse infected or aberrant cells, and these integrated signals are primary determinants of the global NK cell response. In HIV/SIV infections, presentation of viral antigens by major histocompatibility complex E (MHC-E) on infected cells has been linked to differential NK cell responses: viral escape mediated by CD94/NKG2A recognition, or viral restriction mediated by CD94/NKG2C adaptive and antigen-specific recognition. However, significant gaps persist in our knowledge of the viral peptide repertoire and MHC-E binding. We first performed in silico genome-wide analyses of multiple SIVs and HIVs and found high conservation of peptides predicted to bind MHC-E. NK cell activity toward K562 MHC-E+ cells presenting lentivirus peptides was highly correlated to the MHC-E variant and internalization rate, as well as affinity for specific NKG2C alleles. Additionally, our data showed significant associations between cytotoxic NK cell activity, peptide affinity, and key peptide residue interactions in the MHC-E binding pocket as shown by predicted 3D structures. Overall this study presents peptide repertoires likely associated with MHC-E presentation in HIV/SIV infection, and variations in NK cell responsiveness to these lentivirus antigens, that may inform translational applications for HIV vaccine development, infectious and chronic disease modeling, and immunotherapies exploiting HLA-E-viral peptide-targeting strategies.

papers.title: Multiplexed double-transmon coupler scheme in a scalable superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Precise control of superconducting qubits is essential for advancing quantum simulation and error correction. Transmon qubit systems employing the single-transmon coupler scheme have demonstrated high-fidelity gate operations by dynamically tuning the effective coupling between qubits. However, this scheme increases control-line count, posing a bottleneck for chip routing and scalability. To address this challenge, we propose a control-line multiplexing scheme based on a double-transmon coupler architecture, which enables shared coupler control lines to substantially reduce wiring complexity. We experimentally verify that this multiplexed configuration efficiently suppresses static ZZ coupling while maintaining accurate two-qubit gate control. We further demonstrate the feasibility of the architecture through two gate implementations: a fast coupler Z-control-based controlled-Z gate and a parametric iSWAP gate. To validate the practical applicability of this approach, we prepare Bell and three-qubit GHZ states with fidelities exceeding 99% and 96%, respectively. This architecture offers a route to reducing wiring overhead in two-dimensional qubit arrays, enhancing the scalability of superconducting quantum processors.

papers.title: Accurate recognition of fractional orbital angular momentum of light in complex scenarios using physics-informed deep learning
papers.abstract: Light carrying fractional orbital angular momentum (FOAM) has received increasing attention in many fields due to its rich orbital angular momentum information. However, the recognition of FOAM beams in complex scenarios is challenging. Here we report physics-informed untrained neural networks (UNN) and polar mapping for accurate recognition of FOAM beams in complex scenarios. The physics-informed UNN is designed to retrieve high-quality FOAM patterns from a series of single-pixel light intensities collected through time-varying scattering media, and the retrieved FOAM patterns are further mapped in a polar coordinate. Characteristics of the mapping curves are substituted into a recognition algorithm to identify FOAM modes. Optical experiments illustrate that our method can implement accurate recognition of FOAM beams in complex scenarios. It is found in experiments that even with a mode separation distance of 0.05 in FOAM, the FOAM mode recognition can still be implemented. This work opens up an avenue for a further exploration of FOAM beams in complex scenarios. Light carrying fractional orbital angular momentum (FOAM) has received increasing attention in many fields, but it is challenging to recognize FOAM beams in harsh environments. Here, physics-informed untrained neural networks and polar mappings are developed to implement accurate recognition of FOAM beams with a mode separation distance of 0.05 in complex scenarios.

papers.title: High-dimensional polarization encoding with random higher-order Poincaré-sphere beams for robust optical communication
papers.abstract: Structured optical fields provide a powerful platform for high-dimensional information encoding by exploiting multiple optical degrees of freedom, yet robust image transmission under complex environmental perturbations remains a fundamental challenge. Here, we report a robust image-encoding framework based on random higher-order Poincaré-sphere (HOPS) beams, where information is encoded into the high-dimensional states of polarization (SOP) supported by partially coherent vectorial fields. Owing to the statistical robustness of the underlying coherence–polarization structure, the proposed scheme enables stable information delivery under severe occlusion and scattering conditions without adaptive-optics compensation. A convolutional neural network is employed solely as an efficient read-out tool for discriminating the rich SOP states, without altering their underlying physical dimensionality. Polarization-resolved detection provides an additional level of physical-layer protection against intensity-only interception. These results establish random HOPS beams as a robust information carrier for high-dimensional polarization encoding and perturbation-resistant optical communication in complex environments. Optical communication can be disrupted when light carrying encoded information is blocked or scattered during transmission. The authors demonstrate that random higher-order Poincaré-sphere beams can encode information in multiple polarization states, enabling robust image transmission even under strong occlusion and scattering.

papers.title: Construction of benzochalcogenaboroles via single-atom editing of boracycles
papers.abstract: Benzoxaborole is arguably the most important boron-based pharmacophore. Since Torssell’s 1957 synthesis, hundreds of benzoxaborole derivatives have emerged, including US Food and Drug Administration-approved tavaborole and crisaborole. However, while peripheral modifications are well studied, synthetic challenges leave isoelectronic core modification less explored, despite its potential to enhance potency and reveal unexplored functions. Here we report a challenging ring expansion of benzoboretenes with elemental chalcogens, where benzoboretenes act as a ‘diradical reservoir’. This synthetic protocol provides a versatile and modular platform for accessing three previously inaccessible classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeletons, in which the oxygen atom of the benzoxaborole core is formally replaced with Se, S or SO2. Preliminary biological evaluation reveals that this ‘O-to-S’ modification confers potent ferroptosis-inhibitory activity. Furthermore, its excellent functional group compatibility enables structure–activity optimization, leading to a 20-fold increase in cellular potency. This research not only expands the chemical space of boron-containing pharmacophores via single-atom ring expansion but also exemplifies how skeletal editing can unlock biological activities. Skeletal editing can be harnessed to unlock biological activity. Here the reversible interconversion of benzoboretene and a boron–carbon diradical—termed a diradical reservoir process—enables modular access to three classes of benzochalcogenaborole skeleton, a selection of which are tested for ferroptosis-inhibitory activity.

papers.title: Author Correction: Molecular-docking electrolytes enable high-voltage lithium battery chemistries
Rich quantum phase diagram revealed in semimetallic rhombohedral graphene
papers.abstract: Previous studies of rhombohedral graphene have focused on a single topological and flat conduction or valence band isolated by strong electric fields. Rhombohedral hexalayer graphene is now found to host various quantum phenomena in the correlated semimetallic regime, featuring symmetry breaking, electric-field-driven band inversion, dual-carrier superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism.

papers.title: Publisher Correction: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
Challenges in AI based tumor board case summarization and recommendations
papers.abstract: Tumor boards, recurring meetings at hospital institutions, assemble cancer specialists (e.g., medical oncology and pathology) to discuss patient care. In this work, we formally define tumor board case summarization, options generation, and meeting outcome prediction as AI tasks. We study datasets from four medical institutions and evaluate state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) from the DeepSeek, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen families using expert human assessment. Medical oncologists created ~9.6k reference texts and 16k human judgments across tasks. Clinicians rated LLM-generated case summaries 3.57–4.59 out of 5.0 across institutions, but recommendation generation remained more challenging, with average scores of 2.0–3.6. Clinical alignment analyses showed modest correlations of ~0.2 for case summarization subtasks and higher correlations of ~0.6 for recommendation generation using LLM-as-Judge metrics. Our proposed TBFact metrics were competitive with LLM-as-Judge approaches in longer prose free-text settings, suggesting a promising direction toward explainable evaluation. This study, to our knowledge the largest expert-grading study of tumor board tasks with both granular and direct assessments, found that criterion-level scores and overall judgments are related nonlinearly. Experts also frequently assigned high ratings to responses that differed substantially from their reference texts, challenging assumptions underlying reference-based automatic evaluation metrics.

papers.title: AI-assisted chest CT scan analysis of body composition at ICU admission and 6-month mortality
papers.abstract: Abnormal body composition at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with worse survival, but it is rarely measured in practice because manual CT analysis is labor-intensive. We conducted a secondary analysis of a single-center prospective cohort of 509 patients who underwent chest CT within 24 h of ICU admission, of whom 475 were included in the final analysis. Open-source AI segmentation was used to quantify body composition, and the resulting features were related to 6-month survival. Risk scores derived from body composition were significantly associated with 6-month survival (p < 0.001, log-rank test). In five-fold cross-validation, the AUC for discriminating survivors from non-survivors was 0.73; when feature selection was accounted for, the AUC was 0.68 by nested cross-validation and 0.69 by bootstrap optimism correction. The study shows that the automated AI-based analysis of admission chest CT yields body composition scores significantly associated with 6-month mortality after ICU admission.

papers.title: Multimodal AI-enabled repurposing and prioritization of ferroptosis-targeting drug combinations in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) lacks scalable and mechanism-informed computational strategies for prioritizing repurposable drug combinations. Here, we developed FeNetDP, a multimodal AI-guided framework that integrates transcriptomic, proteomic, single-cell, spatial, and clinical survival data to enable biologically grounded drug repurposing and combination prioritization in PDAC. FeNetDP combines gene-level network proximity analysis with a biologically constrained neural ranking model to identify candidate compounds and drug pairs linked to a disease-relevant ferroptosis suppressor program. Using this framework, we defined an eight-gene ferroptosis suppressor module enriched in ductal cells and associated with poor prognosis, and prioritized candidate repurposable compounds and combinations targeting this network state. Prospective experimental validation identified panobinostat plus sorafenib as a synergistic combination that suppresses tumor growth and promotes ferroptosis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, the combination impaired ferroptosis resistance through coordinated disruption of glutathione-dependent antioxidant defense and AIFM2 (FSP1)-associated glutathione-independent protection. Together, these findings establish FeNetDP as a multimodal and experimentally grounded framework for computational repurposing and mechanism-informed therapeutic prioritization in cancer.

papers.title: Generative fundus angiography from misaligned handheld images for non-invasive screening of infantile retinal diseases
papers.abstract: Infantile retinal diseases are a leading cause of childhood blindness, and vascular findings that guide screening and management are often poorly visible in color fundus photography (CFP). Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) provides angiographic visualization of retinal vascular abnormalities, but its invasive nature and reliance on fluorescein dye limit routine use in vulnerable infants. Generative synthesis may provide non-invasive angiographic approximations. However, infant imaging often relies on manually operated handheld contact fundus cameras, with variations in probe angle, contact pressure, and field of view between separate CFP and FFA acquisitions contributing to weak spatial correspondence between modalities. In this paper, we present InfantAngio, a diffusion-based framework that reformulates CFP-to-FFA synthesis as a deterministic latent transport trajectory. Developed and evaluated using 83,950 registration-derived image-pair records from 259 infants, InfantAngio showed favorable performance across quantitative image-quality benchmarks, while ophthalmologists distinguished real from synthesized FFA images with near-chance accuracy of 49.8% in blinded assessment. Adding synthesized FFA to CFP improved both downstream classifier performance and overall diagnostic accuracy in a retrospective ophthalmologist reader study. These results support synthesized FFA as a potentially useful non-invasive adjunct for screening high-risk infants, with the possibility of reducing reliance on dye-based procedures in real-world clinical scenarios.

papers.title: Divergent legal consequences of cyberattacks on healthcare organizations worldwide
papers.abstract: Healthcare cyberattacks and related data-security failures have divergent publicly observable legal consequences. A purposive corpus of 133 records from 24 countries maps civil litigation, regulatory enforcement, and selected incidents without located civil compensation claims. Litigation records concentrate in the United States. Uneven source coverage and nonpublic remedies limit comparison and preclude causal inference. Consistent reporting could improve understanding of accountability and patient redress.
