papers.title: Hexa-substituted benzene synthesis with non-classical carbocations
papers.abstract: Benzene rings are the most frequently encountered ring system in small-molecule drugs1. However, benzenes with six substituents are notably absent from small molecule libraries, owing to challenges associated with their synthesis and the limited availability of commercially available aromatic building blocks2. Therefore, new chemical processes that enable their synthesis with predictable regiochemical control and broad substituent diversity could enable medicinal chemists to explore this uncharted aromatic chemical space in hit-to-lead and lead optimization campaigns. Herein, we describe a highly modular and programmable platform for accessing hexa-substituted benzene rings from aromatic cyclopropenium cations and (trialkylsilyl)allenes, with precise control over all six benzene positions encoded in the starting materials. The exceptional regioselectivity observed originates from the selective evolution of an unusual non-classical carbocation featuring four-centre four-electron bonding as revealed by density functional theory calculations. Our benzannulation enables the selective installation of synthetic handles that were exploited for the synthesis of previously inaccessible penta- and hexa-substituted analogues of the anticancer drug sonidegib and the antihypertensive drug telmisartan, as well as the polyaromatic hydrocarbon triphenylene. Notably, the use of enantiopure allenes unlocks a new route to enantioenriched multi-substituted biaryls through our benzannulation occurring with “memory of chirality”.

papers.title: Continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis
papers.abstract: Current state-of-the-art peptide synthesis faces a significant global challenge in efficiency and sustainability.1 With demand for peptide therapeutics growing rapidly,2,3 our ability to provide these important medicines is under increasing pressure.4 Chemical synthesis typically proceeds C-to-N and requires protecting groups, whereas ribosomal synthesis proceeds N-to-C from unprotected amino acids (AAs). To improve efficiency and sustainability, we developed a continuous N-to-C Peptide Synthesis (NCPS) using N-/C-unprotected AAs or fragments without intermediate isolations, achieving ≥95% average yield per coupling and ≤1.0% epimerization. The method enabled seven consecutive couplings. Starting from N-/C-unprotected AAs, peptide assembly requires fewer isolations than those needed to prepare the corresponding Fmoc-AA building blocks before conventional synthesis can begin. This method accepts all 20 canonical AAs and a wide range of non-canonical AAs important for drug-like profiles.5 Longer peptides can be readily assembled through continuous fragment coupling while maintaining chiral integrity. This approach reduces isolations by ~10-fold and waste generation by up to ~100-fold. We further developed a flow synthesizer that enhances speed and productivity while mitigating batch manufacturing risks. The method enabled the synthesis of a tirzepatide heptapeptide fragment, degarelix, a 14-mer engineered macrocyclic peptide, and semaglutide. Overall, continuous NCPS has the potential to transform peptide manufacturing.

papers.title: Architecture of the poxvirus early-transcription machinery and portal complex
papers.abstract: Poxviruses enclose a complete viral transcription machinery alongside their dsDNA genome within the viral core, a transcription-competent compartment delimited by a permeable multi-layered protein shell. Upon infection of a cell and core release, this machinery almost immediately starts synthesizing early mRNAs, which are extruded across the core wall into the cytoplasm for translation. While in vitro structures of the isolated viral DNA-dependent RNA polymerase (vRNAP) have been described1–3, its native in virio architecture, spatial organization, and physical coupling to the genome remain unknown. Using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging on purified Vaccinia virus cores, we reveal that packaged vRNAP exists not as monomer, but as massive 1.8 MDa resting-state dimer bridged by fully ordered vaccinia virus early transcription factor (VETF). We also identify a subpopulation of these dimers bound to the essential kinase VPK2 and the core protein L4, which directly tether the transcribing engines to the packaged genome near the inner core wall. Furthermore, we determine a sub-nanometer structure of the putative poxvirus mRNA extrusion portal complex, revealing a rigid assembly integrated into the core wall comprising an E8 hexameric crown, an E6 hexameric central hub, and a basal L3 dodecameric channel suited for nucleic acid export. Together, these structures provide a comprehensive architectural blueprint of important components of the poxvirus core and open new structural and functional avenues for investigating poxvirus genome packaging, transcription activation, and mRNA extrusion.

papers.title: Mariana Trench holds deepest-ever evidence of volcanic explosion
papers.abstract: Robotic vehicle spots telltale rocks in Challenger Deep.

papers.title: COP31 went up in flames over fossil fuels — it sends an important message
papers.abstract: Nature reporter James Dinneen reflects on the first international climate summit to collapse since 2009.

papers.title: ORE1 stabilizes PIF4 protein through a UBP12/UBP13-dependent regulatory module in thermomorphogenesis
papers.abstract: Plants adapt their growth to warmth, but how aging signals tune protein stability remains unclear. Here, the authors show that the senescence factor ORE1 acts as a scaffold to stabilize the heat regulator PIF4 via UBP12/UBP13-mediated deubiquitination, driving warmth induced growth.

papers.title: Non Hermitian synthetic phase shifter with topologically protected phase control via tunable losses
papers.abstract: Programmable photonic circuits typically rely on refractive-index modulation for active control, limiting scalability. Here, authors develop and validate a synthetic phase-shifter framework using optical loss modulation to achieve full-cycle phase control protected by topological quantities.

papers.title: Biomass-based platform for pesticide management balancing field efficacy with postharvest residue via dynamic adhesion switch
papers.abstract: Pesticide formulations must balance two competing requirements—robust adhesion during cultivation and efficient removal in postharvest. Here, the authors developed a thermoresponsive biomass-based dynamic adhesion switch and constructed a Pickering emulsion system loaded with the UV-sensitive pesticide emamectin benzoate.

papers.title: Mesophase-induced vitrification in coordination polymers via aliphatic chain dynamics
papers.abstract: Coordination-polymer glasses offer structural functionality and processability but are hindered by poor thermal stability and high melting points. Here, the authors report mesophase-induced vitrification in magnesium-based frameworks, enabling glass formation without melting while preserving network integrity and mechanical stiffness.

papers.title: Intramolecular electrophilic aminations of indoles enable divergent bond migrations to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines
papers.abstract: C–C migration rearrangements of spiro[indole-3,3′-pyrrolidines] are well established, but their isomeric spiro[indole-3,2′ pyrrolidine] counterparts remain unexplored. Here, the authors report a versatile strategy enabling selective C–C or C–N migration to access piperidinoindolines and δ-carbolines, with promising antitumour activity.

papers.title: Quasi-degenerate cation occupation enables oxygen-vacancy defect healing in nonlinear optical crystals
papers.abstract: A quasi-degenerate cation occupation strategy offers a pathway to overcome substitution-induced defects in functional crystals. Its validation in La 3 TiGa 5 O 14 demonstrates effective oxygen-vacancy healing and improved nonlinear optical performance.

papers.title: CARM1-mediated methylation controls interactions of ALIX with key partners important for cytokinesis
papers.abstract: ALIX methylation by CARM1 controls CD2AP levels at the midbody and is important for cytokinesis. Their findings reveal a role for protein arginine methylation in the last step of cell division.

papers.title: Nationwide high-resolution assessment reveals the underestimated carbon sink of Chinese parks
papers.abstract: Based on net primary productivity, the 8,137 parks across mainland China sequestered 52.7 Mt C in 2020. Within the 5,425 urban parks, large ones (>100 hectares) contributed over 90%, while 10-50 hectares ones drove the shift from carbon sources to sinks.

papers.title: Photocatalytic control of diamond color center charge states via laser-induced surface oxidation
papers.abstract: Controlling the charge states of diamond defects is important for quantum technologies. Here, the authors use light-driven surface oxidation to locally and continuously tune silicon-vacancy charge states in diamond nanopillars.

papers.title: Immunoglobulin A promotes stable colonization of Bifidobacterium to protect against allergic inflammation under fiber deprivation
papers.abstract: Here, the authors show that Bifidobacterium induces IgA that enhances its mucosal persistence under fiber-deprived conditions, with its metabolites suppressing allergic inflammation, revealing a self-reinforcing host–microbial mutualism.

papers.title: Eco-evolutionary dynamics of active virus-host interactions in a freshwater lake revealed through metaHi-C
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors detect phage-bacteria associations using metaHiC, revealing diverse community-level infection dynamics in freshwater including cellular level co-infection, broad host range and kill-the-winner; and link them to underlying evolutionary processes.

papers.title: LitMOF: An LLM Multi-Agent for Literature-Validated Metal-Organic Frameworks Database Correction and Expansion
papers.abstract: Errors in metal-organic framework databases mislead screening. The authors present an LLM multi-agent system that reads the source database and publications to repair them, yielding 189,567 valid structures

papers.title: Harnessing plant cells as oral drug delivery capsules for synergistic therapy of ulcerative colitis
papers.abstract: Plant cells have been explored as carriers for drug delivery through genetic engineering. Here, the authors report a plant cell-based oral colon-targeted delivery system that links drug-loaded, maleimide-modified liposomes to carrot cells through maleimide-thiol click chemistry.

papers.title: Longitudinal changes in mis-splicing in a cohort of female twins are widespread and highlight mechanisms of ageing
papers.abstract: This study identifies a striking increase in alternative splicing errors in ageing female twins over a six-eight-year timespan, providing insights into the molecular mechanisms of both healthy ageing and age-related diseases.

papers.title: A multimodal ultrasound foundation model for diagnosis of unexplained lymphadenopathy
papers.abstract: Unexplained lymphadenopathy (ULA) has the potential to delay cancer diagnosis due to its complex nature, and the current ultrasound artificial intelligence models that rely on single-modality static images can be limited in their clinical applicability. Here, the authors show that the ultrasound multimodal foundation model LSF-NET could improve diagnosis of ULA.

papers.title: 3D-printed Eutectic high-entropy alloys with dynamic protection for tribological damage resistance
papers.abstract: Alloys with high tribological damage resistance are critical for advanced engineering. The authors propose a nanoarchitecture-driven dynamic protection concept to achieve this, demonstrating the concept in 3D-printed eutectic high-entropy alloys.

papers.title: A leptin receptor–LRP1 complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry into the mouse brain
papers.abstract: Leptin resistance in obesity may reflect impaired transport of leptin into the brain. Here, the authors show that an LRP1–LepR complex in the choroid plexus and tanycytes mediates leptin entry and is disrupted in obesity.

papers.title: Fluorination‑driven σ‑bonding design enables practical aqueous zinc-vanadium‑oxide batteries
papers.abstract: Amorphous vanadium oxides can store zinc rapidly but often suffer from structural instability in water. Here, authors use fluorine coordination to stabilize the local vanadium environment while preserving fast ion transport, enabling durable aqueous zinc batteries.

papers.title: ALK R1275Q expands Schwann cell precursor-like cells during sympathoadrenal commitment, creating a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation
papers.abstract: Neuroblastoma develops from the sympathoadrenal lineage of the neural crest, with activating ALK mutations being frequent oncogenic events. Here, the authors develop a patient-derived iPSC model of sympathoadrenal development and find that the ALK activating mutation, R1275Q, drives expansion of Schwann cell precursor-like cells in early sympathoadrenal development establishing a permissive state for neuroblastoma initiation.

papers.title: Marine volatile organic compounds air-sea exchange dynamics across a summer-to-autumn ecosystem transition
papers.abstract: Continuous measurements of air-sea exchange at a Baltic Sea island reveal how phytoplankton and physical processes together shape the release and uptake of diverse volatile organic compounds as summer turns to autumn.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal brain dynamics of limb ownership perception
papers.abstract: Using magnetoencephalography, the authors generate a time-resolved whole-brain map of neural activity underlying the experience that a hand is one’s own, revealing how distributed cortical and cerebellar networks are sequentially engaged.

papers.title: A scalable pipeline for patient-matched pediatric solid tumor models and cell lines
papers.abstract: An open-access collection of orthotopic patient-derived xenografts (O-PDXs) of pediatric solid tumours has previously been reported, representing an invaluable resource for preclinical research. Here, the authors expand this resource by generating 3D organoids, 2D primary cultures, and cell lines from these O-PDXs and demonstrate that these models preserve key molecular and cellular features of the original tumours.

papers.title: Ultralow-volume shallow microwell-based collection and processing for scalable spatial proteome mapping of tissues
papers.abstract: Spatial proteome mapping is essential for understanding tissue heterogeneity and microenvironment. Here, authors report USMCP-MS, a robust, scalable, unbiased spatial proteomics method for proteome mapping of tissues at high spatial resolutions as well as high-throughput single voxel proteomics.

papers.title: Biophysical brain twins map the phenotype–expotype architecture of ageing and dementia
papers.abstract: Biophysical whole-brain models may reveal causal links between neural dynamics and biological–environmental variation, yet no framework has explained how these factors become embedded in mechanistic dynamics. Here we develop individualized biophysical digital twins mechanistically linked to phenotypes and expotypes (that is, combinations of exposomal influences) leveraging resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging data (n = 6,986, 16 countries) of healthy controls and participants with mild cognitive impairment, Alzheimer’s disease and frontotemporal dementia. Personalized twins improved goodness-of-fit over group-level models. They reproduced structure–function coupling between regional excitability and brain volume, captured age, sex and neurodegeneration, and encoded 68 expotypes. Associations remained robust after controlling for demographics, data quality, model fit and scanner/site, with the strongest effects for social and physical (pollution) exposomes. We release an open resource (empirical data, code, >3 million simulations) for future research. These findings ground phenotypic–exposomic variation in individualized biophysical twins, enabling in silico testing of mechanisms and potential model-informed interventions. The generation of individual biophysical digital twins at massive scale from resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging enables individualized insights into regional signatures and excitatory/inhibitory balance, with features that can be linked to key phenotypes and expotypes.

papers.title: Advances in molecular imaging of the tumour microenvironment
papers.abstract: The tumour microenvironment (TME) is a multidimensional dynamic and complex system of cells and non-cellular components that not only drives tumour progression but also substantially influences response to therapy. Understanding TME biology for basic research and identifying biomarkers in the TME to stratify patients for therapy is crucial for optimizing therapeutic outcomes. Current standards for investigating TME dynamics, if even considered beyond preclinical work, rely predominantly on samples for tissue staining and sequencing and require invasive procedures to obtain tissue via surgery or biopsies. This leads to limited assessment of spatial heterogeneity and minimal temporal information as this depends on the timing of tissue sampling, which results in undefined clinical utility. Molecular imaging provides promising solutions by enabling non-invasive, real-time multidimensional spatiotemporal probing of the TME that can complement current ex vivo practices. This Review highlights the relevance of molecular imaging agents and methods that can effectively capture spatiotemporal TME characteristics in situ, offering critical insights into tumour behaviour and treatment response. We provide an overview of current preclinical imaging strategies and their applications in identifying cellular and non-cellular components of the TME, along with monitoring progression-associated processes and treatment response. We showcase new developments and avenues being explored in preclinical imaging, as well as offer perspectives into existing and emerging clinical imaging of the TME to enhance patient care and highlight opportunities for improvement. Overall, integrating TME imaging into clinical practice holds the potential to bridge critical gaps in spatiotemporal resolution, ultimately enabling more precise diagnosis, patient stratification and personalized therapeutic interventions. This Review discusses molecular imaging probes and modalities for studying the complexity and dynamics of the tumour microenvironment in preclinical research and further highlights emerging clinical applications in diagnostics and intervention.

papers.title: Depth-robust super-resolution nanofabrication for 3D mesoscopic photonic structures
papers.abstract: Mesoscopic optical systems underpin photonic interconnects, on-chip metrology, quantum computing and miniature microscopy, but monolithic integration of these components is currently limited by fabrication methodologies that only offer limited depth control. At depth, the super-resolution performance of stimulated-emission-depletion direct laser writing is hindered by absorption, scattering and aberrations arising from refractive index mismatch that distort the depletion focus. Here we show that maintaining axial alignment between the excitation and depletion fields overcomes this limitation. We implement this principle through an axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion direct laser writing strategy that keeps the depletion zone aligned with the Gaussian excitation focus. Axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion produces isolated lines 56.2 nm wide and resolves gratings with a 150-nm period and a 110-nm linewidth at a 160 μm depth with a numerical aperture of 1.27, while maintaining a 167.3-nm linewidth at 1,400 μm, using a numerical aperture of 1.1. We use axially tuneable Bessel beam stimulated emission depletion to fabricate axially extended mesoscopic optical systems, including 4f systems, vortex phase plates, miniaturized objectives and microlens arrays. An axially tuneable Bessel-beam STED approach maintains excitation–depletion alignment, enabling high-resolution fabrication of three-dimensional mesoscopic optical structures.

papers.title: Tracking individual birds by their song
papers.abstract: An automated approach to analyzing soundscape recordings distinguishes differences in song structure between individual birds of the same species. This represents a new, non-invasive tool for monitoring birds across the landscape.

papers.title: A unified framework for scalable differential testing for spatial omics
papers.abstract: A key challenge in spatial omics is identifying features whose values vary depending on both cell type and the surrounding cellular niche. Existing methods designed for spatial transcriptomic data do not generalize well to modalities beyond count-based data and do not scale efficiently to current data volumes. Here we introduce spotGLM, a mixture-aware generalized linear modeling framework for cell-type-specific differential testing across spatial modalities, and SPARROW, a power-preserving data distillation strategy for scalable inference. SpotGLM accommodates diverse data types including count-based gene expression, binomial isoform proportions and continuous chromatin accessibility scores within a unified statistical framework. We demonstrate the framework across spatial omics applications. On Visium HD data of colorectal cancer and mouse kidney, we recover cell-type-specific niche effects with serial-slice cross-platform validation. On long-read spatial RNA-seq data, we resolve cell-type-specific isoform switching in the mouse olfactory bulb. On spatial ATAC-seq data from mouse brain, we recover cell-type-specific spatial variation in regulatory motif accessibility. A scalable framework enables cell-type-resolved analysis of spatial omics data.

papers.title: Mapping safety zones as lithium-ion batteries degrade to improve safety
papers.abstract: Battery safety is crucial for reliable system operation, yet current safety assessments remain largely based on fixed thresholds that do not evolve with battery degradation, leading to suboptimal operational decisions. Here we show that safety performance evolves as batteries degrade, requiring safety management to adapt throughout battery life. We introduce a physics-based framework that characterizes safety performance through evolving safety zones and boundaries linked to the initiation and severity of thermal runaway. Using a comprehensive model that integrates multiple degradation and failure mechanisms, we demonstrate how the safety landscape of a commercial 21700 cell shifts under different degradation conditions, potentially resulting in false negatives under existing management strategies. We further show that degradation pathways strongly affect safety characteristics, causing different safety outcomes despite similar capacity fade and exposing the limitations of capacity-based health assessments. Finally, we map possible degradation-to-failure pathways and highlight diagnostics and modeling needs for lifelong safety management. This study demonstrates that conventional battery safety management using fixed thresholds and capacity-based metrics can misjudge risk. Similar capacity fade can hide divergent safety states, motivating adaptive, usage-aware safety approaches across battery lifetime.

papers.title: Genetic control of active matter
Dynamic microcomputed tomography data quality enhancement using InSituRes
papers.abstract: X-ray micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) provides non-destructive three-dimensional (3D) imaging of porous materials. In situ experiments including mechanical loading or reactive transport require dynamic, four-dimensional (4D) imaging with volumes repeatedly acquired during experiments. To achieve high temporal resolutions, projections, exposure times, and/or fields of view are reduced which can increase noise, blur, and artifacts in the reconstructions. To address these challenges post-experiment, this study introduces InSituRes, a physics-informed, image quality enhancement framework for dynamic X-ray micro-CT reconstructed data. InSituRes maps paired fast-acquisition volumes to higher-quality long-acquisition reconstructions of the same specimen. The model integrates 3D convolutional feature extraction with slice-wise transformer attention to capture local and broader in-plane context. A learnable, forward degradation model approximates rapid acquisition effects, including spatial blur, intensity scaling, and signal-dependent noise. Unseen datasets show improved reconstruction fidelity and enhanced preservation of fine microstructural features relative to conventional interpolation and learning-based approaches. InSituRes enhances quantitative interpretation of 4D X-ray micro-CT scans of evolving materials. This study introduces InSituRes, a physics-informed, image quality enhancement framework for dynamic X-ray micro-computed tomography reconstructed data. The model maps paired fast-acquisition volumes to higher-quality long-acquisition reconstructions of the same specimen.

papers.title: Real-time x-ray imaging of combustion reaction inside an operating engine
papers.abstract: Direct, operando characterization of combustion reaction inside an operating engine has long remained experimentally inaccessible. Conventional optical diagnostics becomes increasingly challenging under the high-pressure, mechanically vibrating, and optically opaque conditions inherent in reciprocating engines. Here, we report operando, time- and space-resolved measurements of combustion in a 3.5 cc reciprocating methanol engine equipped with a glow plug under realistic engine operation, using high-energy synchrotron x-ray Compton scattering. By decomposing the measured Compton profiles into molecular components, we determine that combustion proceeds via a nearly complete single-step reaction. After ignition, a sharp temperature rise occurs, reaching approximately 1300 K within  ~ 0.6 ms near the glow plug; ignition delay is about 0.33 ms. Although the combustion chamber is semicircle in shape with 6 mm diameter, we reveal pronounced spatial inhomogeneity in temperature, with differences approaching 450 K, providing direct insight into the microscopic structure of the combustion event. These results demonstrate x-ray Compton scattering as a powerful platform for quantitative, operando combustion diagnostics applicable to next-generation fuels.

papers.title: LPAG Vgat neurons promote REM sleep and ameliorate chronic stress-induced sleep deficits in mice
papers.abstract: Disruption of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep is a hallmark feature of stress-related psychiatric disorders, yet the underlying cell-type-specific neural mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we reveal that neurons in the lateral periaqueductal gray (LPAG) display heterogeneous, state-dependent firing patterns across the sleep-wake cycle. Using in vivo optrode recordings, optogenetics, and chemogenetics, we demonstrate that LPAG GABAergic neurons promote REM sleep initiation and maintenance, whereas excitatory glutamatergic neurons drive arousal from both non-rapid eye movement (NREM) and REM sleep. In addition, we identify a local microcircuit in which GABAergic neurons form reciprocal inhibitory connections with one another and send inhibitory projections to glutamatergic neurons. Notably, chemogenetic activation of LPAG GABAergic neurons simultaneously ameliorates REM sleep deficits and anxiety-like behaviors in a chronic restraint stress (CRS) mouse model. Collectively, our findings establish the LPAG as a critical bidirectional regulator of sleep-wake states and suggest that LPAG GABAergic neurons may represent a promising direction for future therapeutic investigation in stress-related sleep and emotional disorders.

papers.title: Spatial logic of transcriptional activation by a methylation-binding synthetic effector on circular DNA
papers.abstract: Understanding how the spatial arrangement of transcriptional activators influences gene expression is important for gene regulation studies and synthetic biology. Here, we use a fusion protein consisting of the DNA-binding domain from the bacterial restriction enzyme DpnI (DPN) and the VP64 transcriptional activation domain to systematically investigate positional effects on transcription from episomal plasmid DNA. DPN specifically binds 6-methyladenosine within GATC motifs introduced during bacterial plasmid propagation. By engineering plasmids with different numbers and spatial arrangements of methylated GATC sites, we show that transcriptional activation increases with proximal GATC content and depends more strongly on binding site distribution than on the total number of GATC sites. These findings establish a modular experimental platform for investigating how the spatial arrangement of activator-binding sites influences transcriptional output from episomal DNA and illustrate how bacterial DNA methylation can be leveraged to study positional effects on synthetic transcriptional activation.

papers.title: Strain-resolved HiFi assemblies reveal seep microbiome adaptive divergence and interactions with viruses
papers.abstract: While seep-associated microbes have been broadly characterized, their strain-level genomic divergence, adaptive evolution, and virus–host interactions remain largely obscured. Here we employ HiFi sequencing to investigate microbial diversity in Haima cold-seep sediments. We recover 214 complete and 79 high-quality single-contig microbial genomes. This dataset comprises 191 species, 46 of which exhibit strain-level diversity. Anaerobic methane-oxidizing archaea (ANMEs) that act as the primary marine methane sink are specifically investigated, and the ANME-1b lineage shows substantial intra-species genetic and functional diversity. Evolutionary analyses indicate that ANME-1b is under purifying selection and harbors an open pangenome potentially mediated by mobile genetic elements. We identify 18,594 viral operational taxonomic units, including nine putatively novel viral families associated with ANMEs. Extensive gene exchange between these viruses and ANME hosts may contribute to genetic divergence among ANME populations. These results provide a critical strain-level genome dataset, which facilitates illuminating their genomic and functional divergence and the driving forces that govern them.

papers.title: Neural representation of tactile and visual words in the ventral occipitotemporal cortex
papers.abstract: While reading is typically grounded in visual experience, growing evidence suggests that the ventral occipitotemporal cortex (vOTC)—canonically associated with visual word recognition—may encode word representations in a modality-independent manner. Here, we investigated how this region supports word representations across visual and tactile modalities and adapts to modality-specific demands. Using functional MRI, we examined sighted adults as they explored 3D-printed words by touch and viewed matched visual stimuli. Both modalities activated the vOTC, and cross-modal decoding revealed shared word-form information, with classification performance following an inverted U-shaped spatial profile along the left vOTC. Tactile primes did not elicit reliable repetition suppression for visual words, whereas congruent tactile-visual pairs evoked enhanced thalamic activity. Functional connectivity further showed stronger vOTC coupling with sensorimotor regions during tactile word recognition and with language-related regions during visual reading. Together, these findings identify the vOTC as a convergence region supporting shared word-form representations across modalities while flexibly adapting its network interactions to modality-specific demands.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into gating dynamics of the ionotropic glutamate delta receptor GluD1
papers.abstract: Ionotropic glutamate delta receptor 1 (GluD1) regulates excitatory and inhibitory synapses and is genetically linked to neuropsychiatric disorders, yet the structural coupling between ligand recognition and its transmembrane channel remains incompletely understood. Here, we determine cryo-electron microscopy structures of mouse GluD1 in apo, D-serine-bound, constitutively leaky mutant, and amino-terminal domain (ATD)-truncated states. D-serine closes the ligand-binding domain (LBD) clamshells, disrupts LBD dimers, and reorganizes the LBD and ATD layers while the channel gate remains closed, defining a desensitized-like conformation. The A654C substitution separates adjacent M3 helices and is associated with long-range rearrangements across the receptor, suggesting a structural basis for its previously reported leak phenotype. ATD deletion preserves the resting LBD-transmembrane domain architecture and ligand-induced LBD rearrangements. In the ATD-truncated receptor, γ-aminobutyric acid stabilizes asymmetric LBD conformations associated with transmembrane variability. Together, these structures delineate interdomain conformational coupling in GluD1, potentially opening new avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting neuropsychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Enhanced viral facilitated microbial host adaptability in deep-sea seamount sediments
papers.abstract: Marine viruses regulate microbial communities and biogeochemical cycles via intimate host interactions. However, viral ecology in extreme deep-sea seamount sediments remains largely underexplored, particularly virus-host metabolic and immune dynamics. Using integrated metagenomic and metatranscriptomic analyses of South China Sea seamount sediments, we recovered 85 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) and 1,592 viral operational taxonomic units (vOTUs), establishing 610 predicted virus-host linkages dominated by Pseudomonadota and Planctomycetota. Notably, 33% of vOTUs (527) encoded genes associated with stress response, DNA repair, and a subset classified as putative auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs), with potential viral contributions to host-associated processes under extreme conditions. Transcription signals of these virus-encoded genes suggest their potential roles in enhancing host resilience. Hosts encoded diverse defenses, including an uncharacterized subtype II-C Cas9 homolog (Tgu_Cas9) in Planctomycetota, with a candidate spacer-protospacer match to a viral contig adjacent to a CGG PAM. These findings highlight the important roles of viruses in shaping microbial diversity and adaptation in deep-sea seamounts, with broad implications for marine viral ecology, biogeochemical cycles, and biotechnological applications.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of USP7 and MAGEL2 complex assembly
papers.abstract: The WASH complex regulates endosomal trafficking and is linked to several neurodevelopmental diseases, including Prader-Willi syndrome, Schaaf-Yang syndrome, and Hao-Fountain syndrome. Its function is tightly controlled by ubiquitination and maintained by the multi-subunit MUST complex, which contains both a ubiquitin ligase (MAGEL2/TRIM27) and a deubiquitinase (USP7). However, the mechanism underlying the assembly of the MUST complex remains poorly understood. In this study, we investigate the assembly of USP7 and MAGEL2 components of the MUST complex using NMR spectroscopy, isothermal titration calorimetry, X-ray crystallography, and cellular assays. We show that the USP7/MAGEL2 interaction is bipartite and multivalent. Two distinct domains of USP7, TRAF and UBL1-2, recognize two unstructured but evolutionarily conserved regions of MAGEL2, one of which contains multiple TRAF-binding sites. Furthermore, we determined the high-resolution crystal structure of the TRAF/MAGEL2 complex and identified Hao-Fountain syndrome-linked mutations in USP7 that disrupt USP7/MAGEL2 complex formation in cells. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the pathogenic basis of Hao-Fountain syndrome and related Schaaf-Yang and Prader-Willi syndromes.

papers.title: Quantifying noise-induced tipping via first-passage resetting thermodynamics
papers.abstract: Noise-induced tipping (N-tipping) occurs across climate, ecological, and engineering systems as abrupt transitions triggered by stochastic fluctuations under unchanged deterministic stability. While Although its statistical characteristics statistics and triggering conditions have been are widely examined, the underlying studied, cross-basin probability transport and associated dissipation remain difficult to resolve under realistic observational constraints. Here, we formulate early warning of N-tipping as an inference problem of irreversible probability transport, arguing that the relevant mechanism is the evolution of irreversible emphasizing probability currents rather than a degradation of degraded local deterministic stability. We introduce first-passage First-passage resetting to close closes rare excursions into repeatable transport cycles, inducing a nonequilibrium steady state with measurable currents and enabling state. We define a resetting entropy production rate (R-EPR) that quantifies the entropy production associated with to quantify reset-induced directed cross-basin transport. Across stochastic models, R-EPR increases monotonically with tipping risk and remains robust under white and temporally correlated noise; in noise. In a stochastic Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation model with the mean freshwater forcing fixed at an SSP5-8.5-derived year-2090 level, enhanced weather-scale variability yields appreciable near-term switching risk. These results provide establish a practical thermodynamic framework for quantifying and comparing linking irreversible probability transport to noise-induced tipping risk.

papers.title: Mechanisms and gene therapy of GJB2 related deafness
papers.abstract: GJB2 (Connexin26, Cx26) mutations account for over half of nonsyndromic hearing loss, ranging from profound congenital deafness to mild, progressive late-onset hearing loss. More than 100 pathogenic GJB2 loci have been identified, affecting protein synthesis, membrane trafficking, hemichannel and gap junctional channel assembly, channel gating, and permeability. However, in most cases, it lacks clear genotype–phenotype correlations, and definitive links between specific channel or cellular defects and hearing outcomes. In mouse models, despite the absence of connexin expressions in sensory hair cells, Cx26 deficiency causes hair cell and spiral ganglion neuron degeneration, cochlear developmental abnormalities, endocochlear potential (EP) reduction, and active cochlear mechanics impairment. Profound congenital deafness primarily results from disrupted cochlear development, whereas mild, progressive late-onset hearing loss is mainly attributable to defects in active cochlear mechanics. Although pathological evidence from human cochlea remains limited, available data suggest similar mechanisms operating in humans. Currently, preclinical gene therapy studies demonstrate that restoration of Cx26 expression in the cochlea is feasible; however, robust and clinically meaningful hearing recovery has not yet been achieved. Priorities of future work include deepening the mechanistic understanding of GJB2 pathogenesis, developing mutation-specific knock-in animal models, improving efficacity and cell-type specificity of gene delivery vectors, identifying modifiers of hearing loss outcomes, and elucidating intrinsic pathways that promote compensatory connexin expression in the cochlea following Cx26 deficiency.

papers.title: An artificial photoenzyme constrains substrates for selective antarafacial electrocyclizations
papers.abstract: Electrocyclizations are a fundamental class of pericyclic transformations that can proceed through thermal or photochemical pathways. Although thermal electrocyclizations have been implicated in numerous biosynthetic pathways, there are few examples of enzyme-mediated processes, and the structural requirements for efficient catalysis are poorly understood. Here we develop an artificial photoenzyme for 6π-electrocyclizations (PhotoElectroCyclase PEC1.3) by introducing ten mutations into a recently reported [2 + 2]-cyclase. PEC1.3 processes diverse acrylanilide substrates with exceptional yields, regiocontrol and stereocontrol. A 1.3-Å crystal structure shows the substrate ideally positioned for energy transfer from a genetically programmed benzophenone triplet sensitizer. Interestingly, hydrogen-bonding interactions that were critical to [2 + 2] cyclase activity were abandoned during evolution of PEC1.3. Instead, the enzyme employs a network of hydrophobic interactions to constrain the substrate into a reactive geometry for selective antarafacial electrocyclization, allowing PEC1.3 to retain activity at cryogenic temperatures where appreciable molecular motions are frozen out. This example of controlled reaction outcomes without polar substrate–enzyme contacts points towards selective conversions of substrates lacking functional handles. Enzymatic electrocyclizations are scarce, with little known about the structural requirements for efficient catalysis. Now, an artificial photoenzyme has been engineered for highly selective 6π-electrocyclizations of acrylanilide substrates. The evolved enzyme pre-organizes the substrate through an extended network of hydrophobic interactions into a highly favourable geometry for enantioselective antarafacial electrocyclization.

papers.title: Richer data improve predictions of T cell receptor binding to specific antigens
papers.abstract: We introduce Hi-TPH, a large-scale hierarchical dataset with more complete molecular sequences for predicting T cell receptor–antigen binding. Protein language models trained on Hi-TPH outperform existing tools on an external experimental benchmark and reveal how molecular components jointly contribute to binding prediction performance.

papers.title: Contouring mitigates voiding at the lithium/ceramic electrolyte interface on discharging solid-state batteries
papers.abstract: Interfacial void formation during discharge limits the practical performance of lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here we show that introducing an egg-box topography at the Li/Li6PS5Cl interface increases the discharge current at which voiding commences tenfold, from 0.2 to 2 mA cm−2 at 2 MPa and 30 °C. The contoured interface also sustains pulsed currents up to 3 mA cm−2 at 30 °C and 8 mA cm−2 at 60 °C without cell failure. Under these conditions, it does not completely eliminate void formation but suppresses void growth and associated voltage polarization. Consequently, it sustains discharge profiles derived from the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure, representing realistic electric vehicle driving demands, whereas non-contoured interfaces fail rapidly. A full cell with a thin contoured solid electrolyte retains this advantage over its non-contoured counterpart. Contouring the Li/solid electrolyte interface is therefore an effective strategy for enabling practically relevant discharge rates in solid-state batteries. Discharge-induced voids are a major barrier to practical lithium metal solid-state batteries. Here the authors show that an egg-box-contoured lithium–electrolyte interface increases the voiding threshold by an order of magnitude and enables realistic electric vehicle discharge profiles without polarization.

papers.title: Author Correction: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
Ex vivo and in vivo CAR engineering
papers.abstract: The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapies in the treatment of B cell malignancies has spurred exploration of CAR therapies for a myriad of indications, including solid tumours, autoimmune diseases, infection, organ transplantation, fibrosis and tissue repair. By engineering a patient’s own immune cells to target antigens, CAR therapies offer a fine-tuned, personalized method of immune modulation as a potential alternative to broad cancer therapies or immunosuppressive treatments. However, the success of CAR therapies is limited by risks of patient relapse, treatment-associated toxicities, weak activity in solid tumours and burdensome individualized manufacturing. Advances in synthetic biology, genome editing, biomaterials and gene delivery are expanding the opportunities for therapeutic engineering, including direct generation of CAR immune cells in vivo. Multiplex engineering can advance CAR therapies by combining validated interventions to address these limitations without sacrificing manufacturability. In this Review, we analyse engineering strategies for ex vivo and in vivo CAR immune cell therapy. By examining clinical successes and failures, we define design constraints throughout the engineering process, including cell source, genome engineering, receptor and circuit design, delivery and manufacturing. As CAR therapy has become increasingly diverse and complex, an integrated framework of these engineering approaches will be informative for understanding their complementary strengths and limitations for basic, translational and clinical research and development of this powerful therapeutic modality. The landscape of CAR therapy is rapidly evolving. This Review examines how genetic and cellular engineering shape ex vivo and in vivo CAR therapies, spanning cell source, genome editing, receptor and circuit design, delivery, manufacturing, and safety. It also proposes a framework for aligning engineering strategies with disease-specific therapeutic needs.

papers.title: Designing solar panels for realistic end-of-life scenarios
papers.abstract: The rapid growth of photovoltaics is generating vast waste streams, a portion of which flows to regions where recycling is unregulated. Solar panel design criteria do not account for these end-of-life realities, creating global asymmetry in environmental burdens. This Comment proposes research directions beyond material substitution to address these design gaps.

papers.title: Proteins derived from MRL/MpJ tendon provisional extracellular matrix and secretome promote pro-regenerative tenocyte behavior
papers.abstract: Tendinopathies are prevalent musculoskeletal conditions that have no effective therapies to attenuate scar formation. In contrast to other adult mammals, the tendons of Murphy Roths Large (MRL/MpJ) mice possess a superior healing capacity following acute and overuse injuries. Here, we hypothesized that the application of biological cues derived from the local MRL/MpJ tendon environment would direct otherwise scar-mediated tenocytes towards a pro-regenerative MRL/MpJ-like phenotype. We identified soluble factors enriched in the secretome of MRL/MpJ tenocytes using bioreactor systems and quantitative proteomics. We then demonstrated that the combined administration of structural and soluble constituents isolated from decellularized MRL/MpJ tendon provisional ECM (dECM) and the secretome stimulate scar-mediated rodent tenocytes towards enhanced mechanosensitivity, proliferation, intercellular communication, and ECM deposition associated with MRL/MpJ cell behavior. Our findings highlight key biological mechanisms that drive MRL/MpJ tenocyte activity and their interspecies utility to be harnessed for therapeutic strategies that promote pro-regenerative healing outcomes.

papers.title: Bio3D graft engineered from human mesenchymal stromal cells/extracellular complexes facilitates periodontal tissue regeneration
papers.abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease leading to irreversible loss of tooth-supporting tissues, remains a major unmet clinical challenge. Among emerging regenerative strategies, cellular constructs composed of mesenchymal stromal cells and their self-produced extracellular matrix may represent one possible cell-based approach for treating severe periodontitis. Here, we developed a human Bio3D graft fabricated from clumps of mesenchymal stromal cells and their self-produced ECM (C-MSCs) using a Bio3D printer. When transplanted into a critical-size periodontal defect in immunodeficient rats, the Bio3D graft achieved safe and reproducible regeneration of cementum, periodontal ligament, and alveolar bone without ectopic or excessive bone formation. Transcriptomic and histological analyses revealed enhanced YAP/TAZ signaling in the Bio3D graft compared with C-MSCs, and functional inhibition of YAP/TAZ abolished periodontal reconstruction, demonstrating its essential role. These findings establish a foundation for next-generation, scaffold-free cell therapies capable of reconstructing complex periodontal structures.

papers.title: Health-state instability and progression in longitudinal clinical records reveal heterogeneous ageing trajectories
papers.abstract: Longitudinal clinical records capture health changes, but most models reduce them to endpoint risks or single-time biological-age estimates. We developed VitaFlux, a representation-learning framework that uses next-visit forecasting to encode clinical encounters as latent health states. Applied to 178,970 individuals with 4,439,390 aligned visits from the Zhejiang Population Health Cohort, VitaFlux learned a reproducible representation organized by age-associated, disease-burden and multisystem physiological variation. Forecast instability measured predicted health-state change at the next visit and was associated with observed one- and three-year mortality. Continuous trajectory measures captured heterogeneous progression, while current and forecast states improved the prediction of multiple clinical outcomes compared with a comprehensive clinical baseline. After cohort-specific adaptation, future-state forecasting outperformed a no-change persistence baseline in two independent aging cohorts. VitaFlux provides a unified framework for representing health-state position, forecasting near-term dynamics and quantifying longer-term progression from longitudinal clinical records.

papers.title: Multimodal CT-pathology imaging deep learning model for risk stratification in resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma is a highly heterogeneous disease, highlighting the need for more accurate prognosis prediction. We developed a multimodal deep learning model combining preoperative computed tomography (CT) and postoperative whole slide image (WSI) to predict the disease-free survival (DFS) of resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma. Based on a cohort of 1078 patients from multiple centers, our dual-information instance neural network achieved superior performance over unimodal approaches. The risk stratification defined by the model effectively distinguished DFS in both validation cohorts and served as an independent predictor, suggesting the complementary value of the model beyond clinicopathological factors. An exploratory scoring system integrating the model-derived risk stratification with key clinicopathological factors was developed, identifying patients with significantly different prognostic outcomes. Further analyses suggested that patients with high-risk stage IB disease or high scores might derive DFS benefit from adjuvant chemotherapy, warranting prospective validation. Beyond its predictive capacity, the model also provided morphological insights, identifying prognostically significant structures such as tertiary lymphoid structures and stroma barriers, while RNA-sequencing analysis revealed distinct oncogenic pathway activation and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments in high-risk patients. By leveraging routinely acquired clinical images, this multimodal approach offers a practical tool for improving prognostic stratification, with potential implications for informing patient selection for adjuvant chemotherapy in resected stage I lung adenocarcinoma.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence model for pancreatic cancer risk prediction in patients with pancreatic cystic lesions
papers.abstract: Pancreatic cystic lesions (PCLs) are prevalent and potential precursors of pancreatic cancer. Cancer risk assessment is a crucial step in PCL management, but the complexity and limited accuracy of existing approaches contribute to suboptimal patient care. We developed and validated an artificial intelligence (AI) model that uses radiology reports and clinical data to predict the future risk of pancreatic cancer in patients with PCLs. The model was developed and tested in a 13-year retrospective cohort comprising 23,398 abdominal CT/MRI examination reports from 8707 patients with PCLs across a multisite healthcare system. Of these, 430 (1.8%) corresponded to patients who later developed pancreatic cancer, defined as adenocarcinoma, invasive mucinous neoplasm, or high-grade dysplasia. Among the models evaluated, XGBoost achieved the highest performance, with AUCs of 0.960, 0.945, and 0.944 for predicting pancreatic cancer incidence at 1, 3, and 5 years after imaging, respectively. The model outperformed guideline-based risk stratification, with AUC improvements of 0.161 to 0.235 (P < 0.001). For examinations conducted within a year before cancer diagnosis, radiologists identified potential cancer in 51.5% of cases, while the AI model flagged 82.3%. These findings support the potential of AI to complement existing approaches for individualized pancreatic cancer risk stratification in patients with PCLs.

papers.title: Electrically induced glass transition of polyelectrolyte complexes enables kinetic ionic diodes
papers.abstract: The glass transition induces changes in material properties, transforming a rigid glass into a soft rubber. Here the authors demonstrate an electrically induced glass transition in a polyelectrolyte complex, sandwiched between two oppositely charged ionoelastomers and applying time-temperature-salt superposition principle.

papers.title: The genetic and proteomic determinants of pediatric stature development and their link to adult height and type 2 diabetes
papers.abstract: Childhood growth reflects complex genetic and biological processes, but their developmental timing is not fully understood. Here, the authors identify stage‑specific genetic and proteomic influences on growth from infancy through childhood, and reveal links between early growth patterns and later type 2 diabetes risk.

papers.title: A quantitative deep-learning-based framework reveals a continuum of chromatin sensitivities across transcription factors
papers.abstract: The authors develop a deep-learning-based framework revealing that TF binding sensitivity to chromatin is a continuum rather than a binary feature, and that binding patterns can be explained by a mixture of hierarchical and cooperative mechanisms.

papers.title: Benzoxaboroles target CPSF3 for degradation through a SUMO-dependent pathway in trypanosomes
papers.abstract: Benzoxaborole drugs, such as acoziborole, target CPSF3 and mRNA processing in multiple parasites. Here the authors find that these drugs rapidly and specifically target trypanosome CPSF3 for degradation, in a SUMO- and proteasome-dependent manner.

papers.title: Foliar and floral frost damage reshape reproductive phenology with limited carry-over effects
papers.abstract: Late spring frost can damage plant tissues and disrupt reproduction. The authors show that frost damage to leaves shortens the fruit development period, whereas damage to flowers prolongs it, with limited carry-over effects into the following year.

papers.title: Chronically stable, frequency-selective auditory brainstem stimulation via ultra-flexible penetrating electrode arrays
papers.abstract: Surface auditory brainstem implants have poor spatial resolution and limited tonotopic access. Here, the authors develop a high-density, ultra-flexible penetrating array for frequency-selective cochlear nucleus stimulation and use-dependent plasticity in downstream auditory circuits.

papers.title: Desmin filaments extend along actin filaments within the mouse skeletal muscle sarcomere
papers.abstract: Here, the authors use super-resolution microscopy to show that desmin filaments extend beyond Z-lines and align with actin inside mouse skeletal muscle sarcomeres, where they help support force generation when sarcomeres are stretched.

papers.title: Denitrogenative glycosylations of glycosyl sulfonohydrazides
papers.abstract: Despite notable progress, the development of novel and efficient glycosyl radical precursors that are readily accessible, synthetically versatile, and compatible with stereoselective coupling platforms remains an ongoing challenge. Here the authors report a nickel-catalysed stereoselective denitrogenative glycosylation of redox-neutral glycosyl sulfonohydrazides via anomeric C–N bond homolysis.

papers.title: Super-resolution microscopy reveals distinct epigenetic states regulated by estrogen receptor activity
papers.abstract: Here the authors show that super-resolution imaging reveals a spatial dimension to H3K27ac chromatin organization in ERα-responsive and endocrine-resistant breast cancer, linking elongated enhancer architectures with MED1 recruitment and enhanced transcription.

papers.title: Heparan sulfate sulfatases are essential for the patterning of human stem cell-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons
papers.abstract: This study identifies the extracellular matrix modifying enzymes SULF1 and SULF2 as essential for human stem cells to acquire a midbrain dopaminergic neuron identity, the cell type selectively lost in Parkinson’s disease.

papers.title: Episodic memory consolidation by reactivation of human concept neurons during sleep reflects contents, not sequence of events
papers.abstract: Recording from epilepsy patients during learning, recall, and sleep, the authors show that semantically tuned concept cells in the medial temporal lobe encode the content, but not the sequential order of remembered events

papers.title: CLEC2D orchestrates immune evasion and intrinsic oncogenic signals to fuel triple-negative breast cancer
papers.abstract: The lack of effective therapeutic targets and the resistance to chemotherapy are major problems in treating triple negative breast cancer (TNBC). CLEC2D mainly functions as an immune checkpoint molecule for NK cells through binding the inhibitory receptor CD161 in NK cells. Here, we found that TNBC with higher CLEC2D was associated with poor prognosis. CLEC2D expression in TNBC cells inhibited T cell cytotoxicity and growth. Furthermore, the anti-CD161 blocking antibody enhanced T cell efficacy against TNBC tumor with CLEC2D overexpression. Importantly, we also uncovered that CLEC2D expression autonomously enhanced the growth, survival, migration/invasion, and metastasis of TNBC. Mechanistic studies revealed CLEC2D via its extracellular domain interacted with Integrin β4, activating the FAK-COL8A1 signaling axis to drive the malignant phenotypes of TNBC cells. Our findings demonstrate that CLEC2D promotes TNBC progression both autonomously and non-autonomously. CLEC2D and its regulated pathways are promising therapeutic targets for the development of TNBC treatments.

papers.title: Topology of brain-wide co-fluctuations distinguishes task states and shows associations with personality and behavioral symptoms
papers.abstract: Functional connectivity in network neuroscience is traditionally characterized using time-averaged correlations between brain regions. While these summaries capture stable large-scale organization, they do not fully reflect the temporal structure of moment-to-moment co-fluctuations. We investigate how the order of co-fluctuation used to represent brain dynamics shapes the organization recovered from neural data. We compare three representations of fMRI dynamics: regional activation (node time series), pairwise co-fluctuations (edge time series), and higher-order triplet co-fluctuations (triangle time series) within a common topological framework using Mapper from topological data analysis. Across task and resting-state, Mapper representations derived from pairwise co-fluctuations more distinctly segregate task conditions than activation-based or higher-order representations. This organization reflects structured coordination patterns beyond activation polarity and is driven by high-amplitude co-fluctuation events. Beyond task states, modularity quality computed across all Mapper representations is highest for edge time series and is modestly associated with stable individual differences: higher modularity is associated with higher conscientiousness and lower internalizing and externalizing symptom dimensions. Together, these findings suggest that behaviorally relevant information is reflected in the topology of moment-to-moment brain co-fluctuations. Topological analysis of co-fluctuation-level dynamics provides a complementary and interpretable framework for linking large-scale neural coordination to cognition, personality, and mental health.

papers.title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors
papers.abstract: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.
