papers.abstract: The authors develop DBCata, a generative model trained without energy or force labels to produce near-equilibrium adsorption structures, enabling faster screening of candidate catalysts.

papers.title: Greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change vary by ecosystem and conversion pathway
papers.abstract: This study shows that greenhouse gas responses to coastal wetland land use change depend on the original ecosystem and conversion pathway, highlighting the climate value of conserving vegetated wetlands and targeting restoration.

papers.title: Mapping temperature using transmission Kikuchi diffraction
papers.abstract: Measuring nanoscale temperatures is hard: contact probes perturb samples and optical methods lack resolution. Here, authors develop Kikuchi diffraction thermometry, a non-contact electron microscopy method that maps nanoscale temperatures via tiny heat-induced lattice changes.

papers.title: Entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity enables near-decoupled polarization–strain behavior for high-density energy storage
papers.abstract: Strong polarization–strain coupling limits the energy density and reliability of lead-free dielectric capacitors. Here, the authors show that entropy-engineered polar heterogeneity weakens this coupling, enabling ultrahigh energy storage with minimal electrostrain.

papers.title: Shape conforming Janus hydrogel for preventing anastomotic leaks
papers.abstract: Anastomotic leaks remain a major complication of gastrointestinal surgery, yet existing sealants often fail to provide durable coverage of irregular tissue surfaces. Here, the authors develop a Janus powder-derived dressing composed of an adhesive porous layer mechanically interlocked with a non-adhesive backing. The material conforms to anastomotic tissues, resists unwanted post-surgical adhesions, and provides sustained sealing, offering a promising strategy for leak prevention and repair.

papers.title: A global atlas of digital dermatology to map innovation and disparities
papers.abstract: The authors map 1.1 million dermatology images to assess the diversity of data used to train AI and find major gaps in darker skin tones and children, highlighting the importance of representation for future data collection.

papers.title: [c2]Daisy-chain molecular turing machines with switchable fluorescence outputs
papers.abstract: Synthetic small-molecule machines capable of bidirectionally reading and writing information on molecular tapes with visual output remain elusive due to the challenge in amplifying molecular-scale motions into macroscopic signals. Here, the authors report two [c2]daisy-chain molecular Turing machines that convert mechanical motions into fluorescence signals.

papers.title: Deep ultraviolet gallium-oxide avalanche photodiodes reaching an impulse-response-derived gain-bandwidth record of 152 GHz
papers.abstract: Solar-blind gallium oxide photodetectors enable secure deep-ultraviolet communication but face a trade-off between speed and gain. Dong et al. engineered a multilayer avalanche device achieving nanosecond response, high gain, and a record gain-bandwidth product.

papers.title: Landscape fire sourced PM2.5, cause-specific paediatric hospitalisations, and the role of tree cover
papers.abstract: Greater tree cover is associated with lower risks and burdens of landscape fire smoke-related hospitalisations in children and adolescents across seven countries and territories, suggesting potential benefits of expanding tree cover.

papers.title: Plankton ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven weakening of the ocean biological pump
papers.abstract: Using one Earth system model with increasingly complex plankton food webs, the study finds that greater ecological complexity amplifies climate-driven declines in ocean carbon export, suggesting simple models may underestimate future weakening.

papers.title: Localized strain-engineered 1D electron guides in 2D MoS 2 devices with synaptic memory and high-mobility transistor functionalities
papers.abstract: Local strain engineering can tune the electronic and transport properties of 2D semiconductors. Here, the authors report the realization of multifunctional strained 2D MoS 2 devices on patterned HfO 2 substrates, showing synaptic memory or high-mobility transistors functionalities depending on the carrier transport direction.

papers.title: G3BP1-induced retrograde transport blockade triggers HSC activation and liver fibrosis via COPI alternative splicing
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is driven by hepatic stellate cell activation, but its molecular drivers remain unclear. Here, the authors show that G3BP1 promotes COPI alternative splicing via SRPK1–hnRNPM, impairing Golgi-to-ER transport and causing ER stress that activates these cells and drives fibrosis.

papers.title: A highly distorted benzenium cation
papers.abstract: In contrast to the well-explored peripheral functionalization of benzene, its skeletal alteration remains underdeveloped. Here, the authors report a highly distorted benzenium cation, 2,3-dihydroxy−1,4,6-triamino-5-nitrobenzenium.

papers.title: Early-life skin molecular signatures are predictive of atopic dermatitis risk in an Asian preconception birth cohort
papers.abstract: Here, via a multi-omics analysis of the infant skin microbiome and host immune markers, the authors identify preclinical molecular signatures in the first week of life that predict the onset of atopic dermatitis by 18 months, offering an early window for preventive care.

papers.title: Structural basis for constitutive activation of oncogenic gp130 mutants found in human inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas
papers.abstract: Inflammatory hepatocellular adenomas are benign liver tumors primarily driven by constitutively active gp130 mutants. The authors employ cryo-EM and mutagenesis to reveal the structural mechanism of ligand-independent activation of these mutants.

papers.title: Influenza A virus orchestrates ciliated cell fate and injury during the mucociliary damage repair cycle
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors show how influenza A virus reshapes ciliated cell fate and function throughout the airway damage repair cycle, uncovering viral and host mechanisms that drive persistent mucociliary dysfunction.

papers.title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids
papers.abstract: Tabernanthe iboga produces the medically important alkaloids voacangine and ibogaine, but key steps in their biosynthesis, as well as the biosynthetic route to the structurally distinct alkaloid ibophyllidine, have remained unresolved. Using genome sequencing, bulk and single-cell transcriptomics, and biochemical reconstitution, the authors identify the missing enzymes required for coronaridine and voacangine biosynthesis, elucidate the complete pathway to ibophyllidine, and achieve heterologous production of voacangine in Nicotiana benthamiana .

papers.title: Visible light drives bright extreme-ultraviolet high harmonics
papers.abstract: High-harmonic generation (HHG) brings bright extreme ultraviolet (XUV) light to the laboratory, but achieving high photon flux at short wavelengths remains a challenge. Here, the authors demonstrate visible-light-driven HHG with exceptionally high flux at 13.5 nm, enabled by plasma-core-induced self-guiding and efficient phase-matching conditions.

papers.title: Dynamic price-incentivized spatiotemporal coordination of grid-friendly data centers and distribution systems
papers.abstract: Data centers constitute not only rapidly growing high-density loads but also potential flexible resources for distribution networks, enabled by suitable price signals and coordination mechanisms. However, under practical demand response rules with response thresholds and penalties for invalid responses, translating computational flexibility into valid and verifiable grid-side responses remains challenging. Here, we propose a bilevel framework that coordinates distribution network operations through dynamic electricity prices and schedules spatiotemporal workloads across multiple data centers. The framework explicitly incorporates the practical demand response mechanism implemented in Guangdong, China, and is solved by a lexicographic damped alternating algorithm with engineering stability. Simulations on a modified IEEE 32-bus system and a 60-bus practical system show that the proposed method decreases the cost of data centers, increases the accommodation of renewable energy, and improves valid response delivery. These results indicate that under threshold-based settlement, participation in the demand response is not necessarily beneficial unless flexibility can be delivered in a valid and verifiable form.

papers.title: Vocal divergence accompanies auditory and neural changes in urban Eurasian tree sparrows
papers.abstract: Urbanization elevates chronic anthropogenic noise that can mask acoustic communication, yet changes in vocal signals, auditory reception, and neural processing are rarely examined together. Here, we compared urban and rural populations of Eurasian tree sparrows (Passer montanus) in Shijiazhuang, China, integrating vocal acoustics, auditory brainstem responses (ABRs), external and inner-ear morphology, adult neurogenesis, and proteomic profiles of the caudomedial nidopallium (NCM). Urban and rural birds differed markedly in syllable composition, with only a subset of syllable types shared between habitats. Shared syllable types also showed syllable-specific acoustic differences between habitats, including higher peak frequencies and intensities in several urban syllable types. In parallel, urban birds exhibited selective reductions in ABR amplitudes, smaller ear apertures, and altered cochlear hair cell organization. At the neural level, urban birds showed evidence of reduced adult neurogenesis in both the lateral ventricle and NCM, alongside proteomic changes associated with stress responses, synaptic organization, and neuronal development. Together, these co-occurring patterns suggest that potential vocal compensation may be accompanied by sensory and neural constraints, although their consequences for signal perception and communication success remain untested. These findings highlight the importance of examining signal production, auditory reception, and neural processing together when evaluating responses to urban environments.

papers.title: Structural and functional characterization of hemagglutinin E190D and Q226H minor variants in human H5N1 A/British Columbia/PHL-2032/2024
papers.abstract: H5N1 HA variants (E190D, Q226H) identified in a human-derived isolate disrupt glycan binding without enabling human receptor switching, suggesting reduced fitness for transmission but highlighting the need for continued surveillance of key receptor-binding mutations.

papers.title: Mapping cellular senescence, cellular plasticity, and alveolar niche heterogeneity in human lung development
papers.abstract: Integrated single-nucleus and spatial analyses identify non-canonical, gene-protein-level senescence programs shaping pediatric lung development and bronchopulmonary dysplasia, highlighting spatially restricted remodeling pathways.

papers.title: CDK4-dependent phosphorylation of USP35 promotes the growth of ER+ breast cancer through the mTOR-SOX2 axis
papers.abstract: The majority of estrogen receptor-positive (ER + ) breast cancers are treated with endocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 or mTOR inhibitors, but resistance persists. Deubiquitinase USP35 overexpression promotes tumor growth, yet its regulation by post-translational modifications remains unknown. We showed that CDK4 phosphorylated USP35 at Ser982, which was critical for ER+ breast cancer cell growth in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, USP35 interacted with TSC2, Ser982 contributed to USP35-mediated reduction of TSC2 protein and its association with TSC1, thereby activating mTOR signaling. Elevated signaling upregulated SOX2, driving oncogenic effects. Importantly, the CDK4/6 or mTOR inhibitor effectively suppressed the growth of USP35-high ER+ breast cancer cells and tumors. Furthermore, the phospho-USP35 Ser982 was positively correlated with the phospho-4E-BP1 level in ER+ breast cancer tissues. Our findings uncover that CDK4/USP35/mTOR/SOX2 signaling axis promotes ER+ breast cancer progression. ER+ breast cancer with high phospho-USP35 S982 level might benefit from CDK4/6 or mTOR inhibitor-based therapies.

papers.title: DNA methylation profiling of immune cells identified large-scaled methylation changes associated with ITP in CVID
papers.abstract: Common Variable Immunodeficiency (CVID) is the most frequent primary antibody deficiency in adults. It is characterized by recurrent infections and immune dysregulation, including autoimmune conditions such as immune thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP). While genetic defects explain up to 30% of cases, most patients lack a clear monogenic cause, suggesting that epigenetic changes may contribute to disease development. Here, we present what is, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive genome-wide methylation profiling of B cells and CD4 + T cells from CVID patients with ITP but no known genetic defect. Using the Illumina EPIC 850 K array, we identify distinct methylation signatures in these patients compared to CVID patients with infection-only phenotypes and healthy controls. Our results reveal global hypomethylation, large-scale differentially methylated regions, and abnormalities in coding and non-coding genomic areas. Some changes affect immune regulation genes, potentially implicating epigenetic mechanisms in the development of autoimmunity. These findings suggest a link between extensive epigenetic alterations and CVID and ITP. Our work provides a foundation for understanding autoimmune mechanisms in CVID and reveals epigenetic markers that could represent potential diagnostic tools or therapeutic targets.

papers.title: A differences-in-differences study of staff experience in the English NHS after investment in digital technologies
papers.abstract: England’s National Health Service invests in digital technologies to improve productivity, but their effects on staff experience are uncertain. We assess whether funding through the 2021–22 Digital Productivity Programme is associated with changes in staff morale and engagement. We combine programme funding records with organisation-level National Health Service Staff Survey data for 103 Acute and Acute and Community Trusts from 2018 to 2023. A two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences design compares 26 funded and 77 unfunded trusts before funding (2018–2021) and after funding (2022–2023). Event-study models assess pre-treatment trends, and entropy balancing addresses measured baseline differences. Here we show that overall programme funding has no association with most outcomes and is marginally associated with a less favourable thinking-about-leaving score ( − 0.06, 95% confidence interval −0.14 to 0.01; p = 0.09). Automation and artificial intelligence funding shows no detectable associations. Real-time location system funding is associated with less favourable stressors, engagement, motivation and involvement scores. Virtual reality results are not reported because pre-treatment trends are inconsistent. The associations between digital investment and staff experience differ by technology type. These findings support technology-specific evaluation and staff-focused implementation, while residual unobserved selection and the short follow-up period limit causal interpretation. England’s National Health Service is investing in digital tools to improve care and productivity. We assessed whether staff experience changed after 26 hospital trusts received funding for automation, real-time location systems or virtual reality. We compared scores of staff experience in their workplace in funded and unfunded trusts from 2018 to 2023, accounting for differences between trusts and national changes. Overall funding was not linked to changes in most scores. Funding for automation showed no detectable association, while funding for real-time location systems was linked to less favourable scores for stressors, engagement, motivation and involvement. Future digital programmes should evaluate staff experience alongside intended productivity benefits. This study compares staff experience in their workplace before and after digital-technology investment across 103 English NHS trusts using a difference-in-differences design. Real-time location system funding is associated with less favourable stressors, engagement, motivation and involvement scores, while automation and artificial intelligence funding shows no detectable association.

papers.title: ECG foundation models for cardiovascular screening in a cohort of young competitive athletes
papers.abstract: AI-powered cardiac screening could evolve sports medicine by boosting accuracy, efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, with automated ECG interpretation based on foundation models becoming key for large-scale athlete screening. Before deployment, it is crucial to verify whether these clinically developed models are applicable to this population. We evaluated whether ECG foundation models trained on general clinical populations can diagnose athlete-specific ECG findings. We fine-tuned three models (ECG-FM, HuBERT-ECG, ECGFounder) on PhysioNet/CinC 2021, 87,662 samples, and tested them on 43 expert-annotated ECGs from highly trained/national-level athletes. Performance was strong on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (AUROC 0.97, AUPRC 0.57, Sensitivity 0.89) but dropped on athletes’ data, confirming domain shift. ECGFounder performed best (AUROC 0.84, AUPRC 0.72, Sensitivity 0.57) and detected the most frequent findings, Sinus Bradycardia (AUROC 0.87) and Sinus Arrhythmia (AUROC 0.95), well. Per-label estimates for rare classes must be interpreted cautiously, given the small cohort. This work contributes to developing athlete-focused AI frameworks for reliable ECG-based screening.
