papers.title: Chemical upcycling of mixed polyolefins via rapid C–H nitration
papers.abstract: Post-polymerization modification provides a route to upcycle polyolefin waste, but most current systems have long reaction times and are substrate specific. Here, the authors report the rapid C-H nitration of various polyolefins with high selectivity and functionalisation degrees, forming functionalised polyolefins with enhanced tensile and adhesive properties.

papers.title: Optical observation of ultrafast carrier separation in InGaN photocatalyst nanostructures
papers.abstract: The authors show that ultrafast carrier separation causes the rapid photoluminescence decay in nanostructured InGaN photocatalysts from time resolved photoluminescence and differential reflectance spectroscopy supported by numerical modelling.

papers.title: SMC5/6 safeguards chromatin compartments and TAD boundaries for genome stability
papers.abstract: The SMC5/6 complex protects genome stability, but how it shapes 3D genome folding is unclear. Here, the authors show that SMC5/6 loss in human cells alters chromatin compartments and activates inflammatory and cancer-related genes, changes that are uncoupled from DNA damage.

papers.title: Linking human sources to antibiotic resistance genes in global surface waters
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors used measurement data combined with modeling and machine learning to estimate global human generation of five individual ARGs and intI1 , discharge, and surface-water abundance, highlighting hotspots of per-capita generation and total abundance.

papers.title: Double-membrane-spanning RNA export pores are a conserved feature in nidovirus replication organelles
papers.abstract: This study shows that arteriviruses, like coronaviruses, form pore complexes that span their double-membrane replication organelles, pointing to a conserved nidovirus strategy that links the synthesis, export and packaging of viral RNA.

papers.title: Laser ablation rapid evaporative ionisation mass spectrometry imaging with few-micrometer sampling pixels
papers.abstract: In mass spectrometry imaging, smaller pixel sizes usually come at the cost of reduced signal and more complex sample preparation. Here, authors develop a gentle infrared laser ablation approach that maps metabolites and lipids at few-micron pixel sizes in fresh-frozen and clinical tissue in open air.

papers.title: Wnk1 drives CD4+ T cell lineage fate determination and bone marrow homing in a mouse model of retinal autoimmune disease
papers.abstract: CD4 T cells are central to the pathogenesis of uveitis and related inflammatory responses by promoting myeloid cell infiltration. Here, by leveraging scRNA-seq and a mouse model of experimental autoimmune uveitis, the authors identify the kinase Wnk1 as a key regulator of CD4 T cell differentiation, migration and metabolic reprogramming and as a coordinator of T cell-bone marrow crosstalk that contributes to myeloid-biased hematopoiesis.

papers.title: High-κ bismuth molybdate single-crystalline dielectric for high-temperature two-dimensional transistors
papers.abstract: High temperature stability is an important requirement for future electronic circuits based on 2D semiconductors. Here, the authors report the synthesis of high-κ (54.2) Bi 2 MoO 6 single-crystalline nanosheets and their application as gate dielectric for 2D MoS 2 transistors, showing good thermal stability of the devices up to 500 K.

papers.title: Opposite migrations of Pacific and Atlantic tropical cyclones during the Medieval Warm Period
papers.abstract: During the Medieval Warm Period, natural warming drove tropical cyclones poleward in the western North Pacific but equatorward in the North Atlantic. In the modern warm period, both basins shift poleward, likely due to anthropogenic warming.

papers.title: VHSeek: biology foundation model-based virus representations revealing virus host associations
papers.abstract: The authors present VHSeek, a tool that uses DNA and protein sequence representations to predict viral hosts and prioritize candidate virus-host associations across large viral collections.

papers.title: var2csa transcription implicates variant surface antigen switching in cerebral malaria pathogenesis
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors report case-control studies in Mali and Malawi showing that cerebral malaria is associated with increased transcription of var2csa and EPCR-ICAM1 dual binding PfEMP1s, rather than EPCR-binding variants alone suggesting that var gene regulation may be a driver of severe disease.

papers.title: Orbital spectroscopy links dust source composition to atmospheric acidity and nitrate
papers.abstract: Orbital observations constrain estimates of how spatial variations in dust mineralogy influence atmospheric chemistry and climate: calcite alters aerosol acidity and nitrate formation, whereas iron oxides have stronger radiative effects.

papers.title: Environmental toxicant-induced epigenetic and transcriptional reprogramming of transposable elements
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors, characterize how transposable elements respond to early-life toxicant exposures in adult mouse liver through epigenetic and transcriptional changes.

papers.title: Glycoverse: a multi-functional R framework for glycomics and glycoproteomics data analysis
papers.abstract: Glyco-omics analysis is challenging because glycans have complex structures and analysis tools are fragmented. Here, the authors introduce glycoverse, an R toolkit that unifies glycan parsing, visualization, motif analysis and derived-trait analysis, and demonstrate its use in glycomics and glycoproteomics.

papers.title: Pathway-dependent chiral toroid self-assembly and topological transformations based on large π-conjugated dipeptides
papers.abstract: Rational introduction of large π-conjugated moieties to peptides is crucial for their assembly, luminescence, chiral expression, and functional applications. Here the authors functionalize a series of dipeptides with large conjugated benzoperylene imide segments demonstrating programmable chiroptical and self-assembly behaviors.

papers.title: Intravenous phage therapy for difficult-to-treat infections: a systematic review and meta-analysis of individual patient data
papers.abstract: This systematic review synthesises evidence on clinical, microbiological and safety outcomes of intravenous phage therapy, together with pharmacokinetic and immune neutralisation data, suggesting therapeutic potential but raising questions about limitations of the intravenous route.

papers.title: A genome-wide imaging screen reveals epigenetic and mechanistic partitioning of lamina-associated chromatin
papers.abstract: Here the authors present a genome-wide imaging-based screen which identifies over 100 regulators of LAD positioning, revealing hnRNPK as a key organizer of nuclear architecture. The study uncovers that multiple mechanisms underlie the peripheral positioning of epigenetically distinct LAD subclasses and a genetic framework governing 3D genome organization and transcriptional regulation.

papers.title: Viscoelasticity of synthetic antigen presenting cells reprograms T cell metabolism for TCR-T cell manufacturing and therapy
papers.abstract: Li and colleagues have previously reported the generation of viscoelastic synthetic antibody-presenting cells for CAR-T therapy. Here the authors report that fast-relaxing synthetic viscoelastic activating cells presenting antigen promote the expansion of antigen-specific T cells toward a favourable metabolic state with enhanced anti-tumor efficacy in TCR-T cell therapy.

papers.title: Efficient n–i–p all-perovskite tandem solar cells enabled by interconnection layer engineering
papers.abstract: Jeong et al. overcome an interconnecting-layer bottleneck in n–i–p all-perovskite tandem solar cells, improving charge balance and achieving efficiencies of 25.3% in double-junction devices and 28% in four-terminal triple-junction devices.

papers.title: Soybean Pb encodes a WD40 protein regulating pubescence tip morphology and seed size during domestication
papers.abstract: The genetic basis of pubescence tip morphology remains poorly understood. Here, the authors identify a WD40 protein-encoding gene underlying trichome shape at the Pb locus and reveal potential links between trichome morphology, herbivory resistance, and seed size.

papers.title: A renewable autologous biomaterial for reprogramming cellular metabolism
papers.abstract: Autologous blood-derived products are attractive materials for tissue repair. Here, the authors use gas-shearing microfluidics combined with ionic and fibrin-based enzymatic crosslinking to generate autologous serum microspheres, that improve joint lubrication and support cartilage repair in an osteoarthritis models.

papers.title: Combinatorial mutagenesis of N-terminal sequences reveals expanded stability determinants of the Escherichia coli N-degron pathway
papers.abstract: Understanding how a protein’s sequence impacts its stability is critical to modern protein science and engineering. Here, the authors screened over 2 million N-terminal motifs to understand what sequences lead to protein degradation via the N-degron pathway in the model microbe Escherichia coli .

papers.title: Controlling intertwined electronic orders in FeSe with exfoliation
papers.abstract: The authors perform angle-dependent Andreev reflection spectroscopy on pristine crystal edges of the unconventional superconductor FeSe. They show substantial weakening of nematic order in thin flakes and further observe that the spectra evolve from zero-energy bound states to coherence peaks as the junction’s orientation is rotated.

papers.title: A protein repeat interruption rule governs Nebulin stability and explains in-frame NEB mutations
papers.abstract: Nemaline myopathy is a congenital muscle disorder often caused by mutations in NEB, but how many in-frame deletions disrupt Nebulin function is unclear. Here, the authors show that partial super-repeat deletions destabilize Nebulin and cause severe disease phenotypes, whereas complete super-repeat deletions preserve protein function and muscle development.

papers.title: Wafer-scale thin-film PZT photonic integrated circuits enabling multi-terabit optical transmission
papers.abstract: Researchers establish an 8-inch thin-film PZT photonic integration platform through scalable, low-loss fabrication and demonstrate an integrated 3.2-Tbps wavelength-division multiplexing transmitter for high-speed optical communication.

papers.title: Twist-engineered arbitrary polarization detection for intelligent polarimetric sensing
papers.abstract: Twist-photonics can tailor light-matter interactions but is difficult to integrate into active devices. Here, the authors show a twist-stacked plasmonic metasurface-black phosphorus platform for arbitrary polarization detection, full-Stokes sensing, and polarization-programmable in-sensor computing.

papers.title: Highly elastic ceramic fibers with a high tensile fracture strain
papers.abstract: Researchers report elastic SiO 2 ceramic fibers with 13.59% tensile strain and 1.23 GPa fracture strength, created by a nanoporous, low-crosslinked Si–O network. These fibers enable super-elastic, highly-insulating aerogels for extreme thermal protection.

papers.title: Fully stretchable moisture-electric generators with peak milliamp-scale output via conformationally adaptive ionic hydrogels for wearables
papers.abstract: Moisture-electric generators (MEG) typically have limited moisture-responsive signal generation, producing only microampere-level currents. Here, the authors develop fully stretchable MEGs using conformationally adaptive ionic hydrogels that achieve peak milliamp-scale output and stable performance under 200% strain.

papers.title: Nanofriction strengthened mechanically adaptive electrolytes for safe lithium metal batteries
papers.abstract: Mechanical damage can trigger short circuits and thermal runaway in high-energy lithium metal batteries. Here, authors develop a mechanically responsive electrolyte that thickens under impact, reduces peak force, prevents short circuits and suppresses thermal runaway.

papers.title: A spectral framework for revealing the hidden low-dimensional structure in stochastic reaction networks
papers.abstract: Stochastic reaction networks underline many noise-driven biological processes, but their high dimensionality makes it difficult to characterize transient dynamics and infer system properties from data. Here, the authors develop a stochastic Koopman operator-based spectral framework to identify dominant low-dimensional dynamical modes from simulated trajectories, enabling efficient analysis of moments, sensitivities, and cross-spectral densities, and demonstrate its utility for analyzing synthetic gene circuits, comparing intracellular controllers, and inferring initial-state distributions from time-resolved single-cell data.

papers.title: Wafer-scale transferable hexagonal boron nitride membranes via interfacial engineering for multilevel storage
papers.abstract: Hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) has shown promising results for the realization of memristive devices, but its large-scale thickness-controlled synthesis remains challenging. Here, the authors report an interfacial modulation strategy via controlled sapphire substrate nitridation to grow wafer-scale h-BN membranes and fabricate high-performance memristor arrays.

papers.title: Hyperelastic microfibers as bioinspired proprioceptive artificial muscles
papers.abstract: Designing actuators for artificial muscles is promising for soft robotics, though it is challenging to integrate feedback without compromising performance. Here the authors design thermally drawn hyperelastic fibers that integrate optical sensing and hydraulic actuation for artificial muscles

papers.title: σ-complex stabilization shapes enzymatic C -glycosylation and restricts the scope of natural C -glycosides
papers.abstract: Enzymes offer a sustainable route to C -glycosides, valuable compounds containing hydrolytically stable C-C bonds, but few are known to display C -glycosylation activity and their mechanism remains unclear. Here, the authors investigate a C -glycosyltransferase from maize, Zm UGT708A6, reveal two flexible gates that control substrate access and reactive conformations, and suggest that substrate hydroxylation patterns, protonation states, and σ-complex energetics restrict the scope of C -glycosides.

papers.title: A framework-driven pathway to dehydration embrittlement in gypsum fault gouge
papers.abstract: Using X-ray imaging, the researchers capture in real time how dehydration reorganises gypsum fault material, turning widespread grain flow into localised brittle failure even as water escapes – a pathway to fault instability.

papers.title: Cholesterol dysregulation contributes to hematopoietic failure in parn -mutant zebrafish with implications for dyskeratosis congenita
papers.abstract: Researchers show that abnormal cholesterol metabolism and Erk signalling disrupt blood formation in a zebrafish model of dyskeratosis congenita, identifying potential therapeutic targets for restoring healthy hematopoiesis in this patient population.

papers.title: Large language models' complicit responses to illicit instructions across socio-legal contexts
papers.abstract: Here, the authors investigate LLMs’ susceptibility to complicit facilitation across diverse socio-legal contexts, revealing widespread provision of unlawful guidance, variation across illicit scenarios and intents, demographic disparities, and limitations in existing safety benchmarks and alignment datasets.

papers.title: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases drive cancer risk through subtype-specific and shared proteomic mediators
papers.abstract: Endocrine, nutritional and metabolic diseases (ENMs) may influence cancer development, but their effects across cancer trajectories remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that ENM subtypes are linked to cancer risk through shared and subtype-specific proteomic mediators.

papers.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations
papers.abstract: Bischoff and colleagues present velotest, a statistical method for assessing RNA velocity visualisations, revealing substantial differences in how faithfully different methods, datasets and regions within a dataset represent underlying cellular dynamics.

papers.title: Genome-wide association study identifies a functional myostatin variant increasing lean mass in humans
papers.abstract: This large genome-wide meta-analysis identifies 63 genetic loci associated with lean mass, including a rare MSTN variant linked to greater muscle mass and strength, and provides insight into the long-term potential effects of myostatin inhibition.

papers.title: Expert operating skills learning-based intelligent shared control method for a CT-guided percutaneous biopsy robot
papers.abstract: CT-guided lung biopsy requires precise needle placement while limiting radiation exposure and tissue injury. Here, the authors show that a robot using learned expert skills and shared control improves insertion stability, force regulation and targeting accuracy in phantom and animal tests.

papers.title: ER-associated biogenesis of PINK1 preprotein for neuronal mitophagy
papers.abstract: Neuronal mitochondria associate with Pink1 mRNA regulated by AMPK signalling. Here, the authors show, that the PINK1 protein switches between co- and post-translation import associated with ER chaperones depending on the localization of the mRNA.

papers.title: Benefits and harms of antihypertensive treatment a modelling study in 5.5 million electronic health records
papers.abstract: A cardiovascular risk model was developed and externally validated in patients eligible for antihypertensive treatment. Findings suggest that antihypertensive treatment was more likely to prevent major cardiovascular events than cause serious falls.

papers.title: Local niche-derived immunosuppressive CXCR2 + cells impair antiviral immunity
papers.abstract: The mechanisms underlying individual differences in the severity of viral infection remain to be explored. The authors here show in mice that differential brain accumulation of immunosuppressive CXCR2 + cells contributes to divergent disease outcomes and identify the skull bone marrow as a local source of these cells.

papers.title: Disaccharide production in marine cold seeps links dissolved organic carbon to anaerobic oxidation of methane
papers.abstract: Anaerobic methanotrophic microbial communities in marine cold seeps produce disaccharides, thereby establishing a molecular link between methanotrophy and the pool of dissolved organic carbon.

papers.title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces
papers.abstract: High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur–sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur–carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm−2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15–25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg−1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li–In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage. All-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries are a next-generation high-energy-density solution for energy storage. Here catholyte/cathode interfaces are found to be as important as transport tortuosity in thick sulfur cathodes, and an areal capacity of 10 mAh cm−2 is demonstrated at a stack pressure of 15 MPa and sulfur loading of 6.1 mg cm−2.

papers.title: The person behind the scientist
papers.abstract: Matteo Seita and Mengying Liu discuss their reflections as organizers of The Past Metallurgists Society lecture series, where scientists meet to share stories of distinguished metallurgists from the past.

papers.title: Nanostructures strengthen titanium alloys
papers.abstract: Machine learning guides the design of an additively manufactured titanium alloy containing superfine features at the 10 nm scale through controlled martensitic transformation, which achieves an ultimate tensile strength of more than 1.7 GPa and 7.5% uniform elongation.

papers.title: Four-dimensional X-ray nano-holotomography reveals multiscale chemomechanics in composite graphite–silicon battery electrodes
papers.abstract: Linking electrode microstructure to electrochemical performance is essential for optimizing Li-ion batteries. However, this requires mechanistic four-dimensional observations at the ultimate spatiotemporal scales, which remain elusive. Here we demonstrate the use of interrupted-operando synchrotron X-ray nano-holotomography combined with digital volume correlation to track chemomechanical dynamics at both particle (local) and electrode (averaged) scales. Quantitative scale-bridging image analysis is applied to composite graphite–silicon electrodes during their electrochemical formation cycle. Our findings reveal that local ionic diffusion properties, graphite particle morphology and position in the electrode, distance to silicon clusters, surface contact with the liquid electrolyte solution, and mechanical deformations all directly affect local electrochemical activity and irreversibility, although these parameters are not equally important. In particular, we identify fast ionic diffusion channels that play a key role and counterbalance intrinsic depth-dependent reaction heterogeneities arising from ionic and electronic diffusion limitations. The various structural factors that determine the electrochemical performance of composite graphite–silicon electrodes in Li-ion batteries beyond ensemble properties are classified using a scale of influence, providing a practical framework for the optimization of materials and electrode manufacturing. Particle-resolved 4D nano-tomography identifies fast ionic transport pathways as key regulators of electrochemical activity and reversibility in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

papers.title: Antireflective bilayer metasurfaces with complete wavefront control
papers.abstract: Antireflection coatings are widely used in optical systems to increase transmission and suppress unwanted reflections by matching the optical impedance across a uniform interface. Applying the same idea to metasurfaces is fundamentally more challenging because their wavefront control relies on arrays of geometrically distinct meta-atoms, presenting as a spatially varying optical impedance. Here we show that vertical integration can overcome this limitation by allowing bilayer meta-atoms to act simultaneously as phase shifters and impedance-matching stacks. By treating meta-atoms as multilayer thin films, we derive a design rule that links the effective refractive indices of two independently patterned layers and identifies antireflective bilayer libraries with full 0–2π transmission phase coverage. We demonstrate the approach with a free-standing TiO2/TiO2 metalens operating at 1,310 nm, which suppresses reflection below that of bare glass while maintaining diffraction-limited focusing. These results establish bilayer metasurfaces as a platform for jointly engineering optical impedance and wavefront response at the meta-atom level. A bilayer meta-atom structure engineers the antireflective capabilities of the metasurface, without affecting its full 0–2π transmission phase coverage.

papers.title: Tracking local chemomechanics in graphite–silicon composite electrodes
papers.abstract: Operando 4D imaging reveals how local ionic pathways govern activity in graphite–silicon battery electrodes.

papers.title: CMOS surprises
papers.abstract: Unexpected effects are still being discovered in complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) circuits, and the results could have implications for the advance of quantum computing.

papers.title: Enabling lab autonomy with reward functions and executable workflows
papers.abstract: Autonomous scientists enabled by large language models and agentic reasoning have become a compelling narrative for accelerating research. Here we pose that labaoratory autonomy is not primarily a text problem, as experiments have to be run in the world of instrument-addressable actions and constraints, and planned based on costs, latencies and rewards. We argue for a bottom-up foundation for self-driving laboratories that complements language-first planning by introducing frameworks that translate hypotheses into decisions executable on real tools. We propose three operational principles. First, self-driving laboratories should adopt an information-efficiency objective that maximizes decision-relevant information per unit experimental cost. This requires combining comprehensive data acquisition with minimal, decisive experimental design. Second, hypotheses should be compiled into experimental footprints defined by accessible actions, constraints, observables and decision rules. Third, reward design should be treated as a central bottleneck in closed-loop experimentation, especially when high-dimensional measurements must be mapped to utility or extended to sequential decision-making. We frame self-driving laboratories as long-horizon, out-of-distribution discovery systems where accelerating the full experiment–model–decision loop and emphasizing physical and chemical knowledge discovery over short-term correlations is necessary to translate lab-scale optimization into durable technological and manufacturing impact. Kalinin et al. argue that for self-driving laboratories to achieve autonomy in the physical world, large language model hypothesis generation needs to be complemented by bottom-up optimization translating hypotheses into executable workflows.

papers.title: Computational methods for cell–cell communication via single cells
papers.abstract: Cell–cell communication (CCC) analysis has become a cornerstone in dissecting single-cell and spatial omics data, having an indispensable role in high-throughput screening and comprehensive characterization of tissue communication landscapes. Computational models and analytical objectives have emerged continuously in recent years, propelling CCC methodology development and leading to unprecedented biological discoveries. Methodological varieties and differences in their characteristics underscore the urgent need for a coherent framework bridging between CCC biology and computational advances. Here, we systematically curate 161 published CCC methods, classifying them hierarchically into two primary categories and nine subcategories based on their functions and model features and highlighting the power of CCC methods using oncology examples. Four directions for future CCC methodology development are presented, emphasizing AI–biology integration. This Review aims to delineate the CCC algorithm–demand landscape, thereby fostering comprehensive, in-depth and reliable elucidation of CCC and facilitating broad applications in biology and disease studies. This Review examines the diversity of algorithmic methods for cell–cell communication.

papers.title: A two-platform blueprint for modeling human brain development
papers.abstract: No single experimental system spans human neural-plate induction through late-stage circuit maturation. Brain organoids have transformed human developmental neuroscience, yet a decade of progress has clarified their intrinsic limitations: they cannot fully recapitulate neural induction driven by embryo-scale developmental signals, nor achieve the degree of circuit maturation that requires an in vivo physiological context. Stem cell-based embryo models are positioned to provide mechanistic access to peri-gastrulation and early neurulation, whereas interspecies chimeras provide the physiological milieu to study myelination, pruning and circuit-level function. Here we propose a two-platform roadmap that integrates stem cell-based embryo models to decode developmental logic with interspecies chimeras to study functional maturation. We outline reproducibility and reporting standards, including rigorous benchmarks for neural-tube formation and closure, and present a milestone-based oversight framework anchored to verifiable developmental landmarks. Together, these complementary platforms enable causal interrogation of human neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disease while remaining responsive to ethical and technical constraints. This Perspective discusses modeling approaches for human brain development as well as experimental and biological barriers and ethical considerations.

papers.title: Through the lens of fog
papers.abstract: Hyomin Lee explores why a surface that repels large water droplets can still become covered with fog, and how scaling arguments suggest an unexpected solution.

papers.title: Indentation-induced polar domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave semiconductor EuTe<sub>4</sub>
papers.abstract: Controlling polar domains in conducting materials by external fields could unlock polarisation-based electronic functionalities, yet remains experimentally challenging. While mechanical actuation driven by local strain, stress, or strain gradients has been proposed as an external-voltage-free route, its experimental demonstration in relatively conducting polar materials remains limited. Here we demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the charge-density-wave (CDW) semiconductor EuTe4 at room temperature, whose resistivity is on the order of 10 mΩcm. Polarised-light microscopy and second-harmonic-generation measurements reveal CDW-induced in-plane polarisation domains with an approximately 90° domain configuration. Local indentation with a ~ 1 µm-apex-radius needle reconfigures these domains, producing write/erase-like changes in wedge-shaped regions. These results establish local mechanical-field domain engineering in a relatively conducting CDW semiconductor, with possible contributions from both ferroelastic-like and flexoelectric mechanisms. Controlling polar domains in conducting materials via external fields is key to advancing polarisation-based electronics, yet remains experimentally elusive. Here, the authors demonstrate mechanically induced polar-domain reconfiguration in the CDW semiconductor EuTe₄, using local indentation to achieve write/erase-like changes, highlighting a novel approach for domain engineering in conducting materials.

papers.title: Collaborative mining enables efficient multi-scale feature compression for machine vision
papers.abstract: Machine-oriented multi-scale feature compression aims to remove task-insensitive redundancy while preserving task-critical semantic and structural information. Existing methods primarily focus on reducing cross-scale redundancy, while intra-scale redundancy within individual feature maps remains insufficiently explored. To address this limitation, we propose a Collaborative Mining Network (CMNet), a unified redundancy-aware framework that progressively suppresses both intra-scale and cross-scale redundancies. CMNet first employs an intra-scale redundancy-aware module to suppress redundant responses within each feature map while preserving task-relevant information. It then uses a context-guided adaptive fusion module to dynamically model spatial and channel correlations across scales, thereby reducing cross-scale redundancy. Experiments on multiple downstream machine vision tasks demonstrate that CMNet achieves superior rate-accuracy performance over existing multi-scale feature compression methods, enabling more efficient transmission of task-relevant multi-scale features. Renyi Chen and colleagues develop CMNet, a collaborative mining framework that progressively suppresses intra-scale and cross-scale redundancy in multi-scale features for machine vision. CMNet achieves superior rate-accuracy performance across multiple downstream tasks, enabling more efficient transmission of task-relevant features.

papers.title: A phosphorylation-gated C-tail YxxΦ motif drives β-arrestin–independent parathyroid hormone receptor-1 internalization through AP2
papers.abstract: G protein–coupled receptor (GPCR) signaling is tightly regulated by intracellular trafficking, which shapes the timing, location, and magnitude of downstream responses. Although GPCR internalization is classically mediated by β-arrestins, evidence for alternative, β-arrestin–independent mechanisms has emerged. Here, we define β-arrestin–dependent as well as phosphorylation-gated, β-arrestin–independent pathways for internalization of the parathyroid hormone receptor-1 (PTH1R), a prototypical class B1 GPCR. Both pathways depend on adaptor protein 2 (AP2). In the absence of β-arrestins, PTH1R internalization requires a phosphorylated C-terminal tail, as disruption of GRK activity or mutation of C-tail phosphorylation clusters impairs this β-arrestin–independent pathway. We further identify a conserved tyrosine-based YxxΦ motif within the PTH1R C-tail that mediates phosphorylation-dependent AP2 recruitment. Mutation of this motif markedly impairs AP2 recruitment and delays receptor internalization. Notably, disruption of either the β-arrestin-dependent or independent pathway increases the dependence of receptor internalization on the other, revealing a compensatory relationship between the two mechanisms. Together, these findings support an internalization paradigm for PTH1R in which C-tail phosphorylation drives PTH1R endocytosis through either a canonical β-arrestin-mediated pathway or an alternative β-arrestin–independent, AP2-mediated pathway.

papers.title: Mechanical strength is a conserved SMC complex feature
papers.abstract: Cohesin and condensin are members of the Structural Maintenance of Chromosomes (SMC) complex family, ring-shaped protein architects of higher-order eukaryotic chromatin structure. Cohesin rings encircle two replicated DNAs to counteract mitotic spindle forces during cell divisions. In the case of fission yeast cohesin, one ring withstands forces of ~20 pN before it breaks at its ‘hinge’ interface. Here, we investigate whether the strength of the ring is conserved amongst cohesins from different species, and between different members of the SMC family. We find that DNA-DNA interactions generated by fission yeast condensin withstand the same forces as fission yeast cohesin. Thus, their physical strength is a conserved feature amongst SMC complexes. Human cohesin in turn can withstand significantly greater forces than its fission yeast counterpart. Our results emphasise the importance of considering mechanical forces when studying the role of SMC complexes in chromosome organisation.

papers.title: Anxiety phenotypes accompany reduced Htr2a expression in prelimbic parvalbumin neurons following chronic heat exposure
papers.abstract: Extreme heat is an increasingly important environmental stressor, but the neural alterations associated with sustained heat exposure remain poorly understood. Here we show that chronic heat exposure (36 °C, 4 h/day for 60 consecutive days) is associated with anxiety-like behaviors and altered local field potential and single-unit activity in the prelimbic cortex of male C57BL/6 mice. Optogenetic activation of parvalbumin-preferentially targeted prelimbic neurons ameliorates several behavioral alterations. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling indicates reduced Htr2a expression. Fluorescence in situ hybridization shows lower Htr2a signal intensity in parvalbumin-positive neurons, whereas quantitative immunofluorescence shows reduced serotonin 2A receptor immunoreactivity within these neuronal regions. Fiber photometry reveals altered local serotonin-related sensor responses and calcium responses in parvalbumin-preferentially targeted neurons. Htr2a overexpression in these targeted neurons shifts several behavioral and electrophysiological measures toward control levels. Together, these findings associate chronic heat exposure with altered prelimbic circuit activity, reduced Htr2a messenger RNA expression, and reduced serotonin 2A receptor immunoreactivity in parvalbumin-positive neurons, supporting a functional contribution of serotonin 2A receptor signaling to heat-associated anxiety-like behaviors.

papers.title: Parallel ZNF598 and GIGYF2 pathways mediate conserved collision dependent mRNA decay with divergent endonucleolytic features
papers.abstract: Quality control of aberrant mRNAs is essential for maintaining cellular homeostasis, and ribosome collisions caused by translational stalling trigger surveillance pathways that eliminate faulty transcripts. In yeast, two major collision-responsive pathways, the Hel2-Cue2 pathway and the Syh1–Xrn1 pathway, act in parallel to degrade aberrant mRNAs. However, whether analogous mechanisms operate in mammals has remained unclear. Here we show that ZNF598 and GIGYF2 function in parallel to promote degradation of collision-inducing mRNAs in mammalian cells, with GIGYF2 making a stronger contribution. In contrast, N4BP2, the proposed mammalian counterpart of the yeast endonuclease Cue2, is dispensable for this decay. In yeast, we further reveal that distinct cleavage modes of Cue2 contribute differently to mRNA decay. Together, these findings uncover both conserved and divergent features of collision-dependent mRNA surveillance across species.

papers.title: Declining juvenile survival of Adélie penguins in Antarctica
papers.abstract: Juvenile Adélie penguin survival declined by 32% over a 14-year period in Adélie Land, Antarctica. This decline was associated with reductions in sea ice after fledging, and mirrored trends already observed at other locations. Lower rates of juvenile survival may provide early warnings of climate-driven population change across Antarctica.

papers.title: Serotype-dependent fusion loop and pr antibody profiles in primary dengue virus infections
papers.abstract: Dengue viruses (DENV1-4) are a leading cause of arboviral disease worldwide. The envelope (E) and premembrane (prM) proteins are major antibody targets; within E, the conserved fusion loop (FL) is an immunodominant cross-reactive epitope. Antibodies to pr and FL have been linked to antibody-dependent enhancement, yet their contribution to the cross-reactive response in polyclonal serum remains undefined. Here using recombinant antigens and a multiplexed serological assay with sera from the Nicaraguan Pediatric Dengue Cohort Study, we show that anti-pr responses are serotype-dependent in magnitude yet broadly cross-reactive among DENV1–4, with very limited ZIKV recognition. All primary DENV infections generated FL-reactive antibodies, but the E-FL fraction varied by infecting serotype and detection antigen, revealing asymmetric serotype-dependent shaping of cross-reactive responses. Interestingly, the greater the magnitude of cross-reactive E binding, the lower the proportion of FL-sensitive binding. These findings show that primary infection imprints serotype-specific patterns on cross-reactive antibody landscapes to dengue and Zika viruses that may influence subsequent infection outcomes.

papers.title: Ascorbate availability shapes inflammatory and metabolic trajectories during endotoxemia
papers.abstract: Ascorbate is widely regarded as an antioxidant modulator of inflammation, yet its role in determining systemic inflammatory fate remains unclear. Here we show that reduced physiological ascorbate availability reshapes lethal trajectories during endotoxemia. Using Akr1a-deficient mice, which have limited endogenous ascorbate biosynthesis, together with ex vivo–differentiated macrophages, we found that ascorbate availability during differentiation programs inflammatory responses. Akr1a-deficient mice exhibited markedly reduced survival and segregated into two distinct patterns: an early cytokine-driven collapse and a delayed metabolic failure characterized by mitochondrial dysfunction and progressive organ injury. Multi-omics analyses revealed disrupted tricarboxylic acid cycle activity, impaired anaplerosis, and polyamine accumulation, particularly spermine. In macrophages, spermine suppressed nitric oxide production, whereas enhanced spermine oxidation was associated with acrolein-modified proteins in tissues and plasma. Ascorbate supplementation improved cytokine balance, metabolic resilience, and survival. These findings identify dysregulated polyamine oxidation as a candidate pathway associated with inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction, while impaired AKR1A-mediated aldehyde detoxification may also contribute to the observed aldehyde stress.

papers.title: Physiologically realistic gamma activity produced in silico by weakening the PING attractor state
papers.abstract: Computational explanations for gamma oscillations in brain activity are traditionally oversimplified from the biological reality. Here, the authors show that more realistic gamma activity can be produced in computational models by incorporating the brain’s complexity rather than idealizing it away.

papers.title: Sympathetic beta adrenergic signaling supports macrophage recruitment through the tibia muscle vascular axis during regeneration
papers.abstract: Macrophage recruitment is essential for skeletal muscle regeneration, yet the cellular sources that replenish macrophages in regenerating muscle remain incompletely understood. Here we show, in a mouse cardiotoxin-induced tibialis anterior muscle injury model, that adjacent tibial bone marrow contributes myeloid cells to regenerating muscle in association with a vascular route at the tibia-muscle interface. Congenic parabiosis showed that most leukocytes entering injured muscle were host-derived despite shared blood circulation. Local fluorescent labeling of tibial bone marrow cells, together with three-dimensional vascular imaging and fluorescent dextran perfusion, supported movement of tibial bone marrow-derived myeloid cells toward regenerating muscle through a vascular network. Single-cell transcriptomic and in vivo analyses identified early endothelial changes involving endothelial nitric oxide synthase and beta 2 adrenergic receptor. Beta-adrenergic blockade or sympathetic denervation reduced vascular dilation, macrophage recruitment, and muscle regeneration, supporting a role for sympathetic adrenergic signaling in this vascular response during muscle repair.

papers.title: Structural basis of the lobster carapace blue colour mediated by an HPR protein
papers.abstract: The chemical basis underlying the dark blue colour of live H. americanus, known as the American lobster, is  studied in evolutionary biology and in polyene physical chemistry. Carapace colouration is generated by the antioxidant astaxanthin bound within the carotenoprotein crustacyanin complexes. Here, we present the ex vivo structure of the most abundant α-crustacyanin and β-crustacyanin forms, determined respectively by cryo-electron microscopy and X-ray crystallography to a resolution of 2.75 Å. Our structural analysis reveals α-crustacyanin as an elongated arrangement of β-crustacyanin heterodimers tethered by a heptatricopeptide repeat (HPR) protein. In vitro complex formation between the β-crustacyanin unit and synthetic heptatricopeptides identifies the HPR protein, in concert with crustacyanins, as a contributor in tuning carapace colour. Overall, these results explain how nature adjusts the colour from one end of the visible spectrum to the other by exploiting the bathochromic shift of astaxanthin from its unbound red form (λmax = 478 nm) firstly to the β-crustacyanin vivid blue bound form (λmax = 591 nm), and then to the α-crustacyanin bound dark blue form (λmax = 631 nm).

papers.title: Age-associated structural decline is linked to arterial flow territories in the brain
papers.abstract: The effect of biological aging on brain structure is widespread and apparent. However, little is understood regarding which regions exhibit similarities in vulnerability, and what biological processes drive regional patterns of senescence-associated atrophy. Here, we investigate whether associations between age and brain structure exhibit distinct patterns of regional vulnerability, and if so, whether they are related to patterns of cerebral physiology which also show age-related decline. Using both data-driven and hypothesis-driven approaches, we identify recurring patterns of accelerated and delayed decline across the lifespan. Notably, the results mapped using unsupervised clustering methods mirror the organization of major arterial flow territories, supporting the idea that vascular architecture may contribute to the spatial organization of brain aging. These results provide support for future research to further link patterns of structural deterioration to physiological processes that may be useful for identifying ‘at risk’ individuals and developing novel therapeutics for neurodegenerative disorders.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals AR7 ameliorates rotenone-induced Parkinson’s disease via gut-serum-brain axis modulation
papers.abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a multifactorial neurodegenerative disorder associated with metabolic disturbances and gut microbiota dysbiosis. However, the underlying molecular networks and therapeutic implications remain unclear. This study investigated rotenone-induced PD and the therapeutic potential of AR7 using an integrated multi-omics approach. Colon tissue, serum, and intestinal contents were analyzed by transcriptomics, metabolomics, and metagenomics, respectively. Transcriptomics showed upregulation of mitochondrial and oxidative stress-related genes (Sod, Cox5, Cox6, Vdac1, Sdhc) and downregulation of Slc18a1, indicating impaired oxidative phosphorylation and dopamine transport. Metabolomics revealed decreased trigonelline and isopentenyl pyrophosphate and increased hydroquinone and methylpicolinate, reflecting disrupted energy metabolism and oxidative stress. Metagenomic analysis revealed enrichment of Lactobacillus acidophilus and depletion of Akkermansia muciniphila. AR7 treatment altered microbial community composition, increasing the abundance of Streptomyces viridochromogenes, Prevotella salivae, and Paenibacillus algorifonticola. Integrated multi-omics analysis identified mitochondrial dysfunction and oxidative stress as key processes associated with rotenone-induced PD, while oxidative phosphorylation and glutathione metabolism emerged as major pathways altered by AR7 treatment. AR7 treatment was also associated with improved metabolic homeostasis and changes in gut microbial composition. These findings provide insights into the potential involvement of the gut–serum–brain axis in rotenone-induced PD and support further investigation of AR7 as a potential therapeutic candidate.

papers.title: Dynamic visualization of cell adhesion molecule interactions using reversible split-HaloTag labeling in living cells
papers.abstract: Critical for diverse cellular functions, cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) interact to transduce information from the external environment to drive coordinated intracellular responses. However, direct visualization of CAM interactions in living cells and organisms remains a major challenge. Recent developments in split-HaloTag technology present a promising strategy for chemical labeling of protein–protein interactions. Here, we apply this method to dynamically monitor CAM interactions in living HEK293T cells using split-HaloTag-CAM fusion proteins. With high specificity, we visualized trans-cellular interactions between known adhesion pairs natively found in neuronal and immunological synapses. To expand the system’s versatility, we adapted a modified split-HaloTag component (cpHaloΔN272H) that enables reversible dye exchange and facilitates rapid time-lapse imaging of CAM interactions. Leveraging fluorogenic HaloTag dyes, split-HaloTag-CAMs measured the real-time disassembly and reassembly of Ca2+-dependent CAM junctions in live cells. These tools enabled imaging long-term changes in surface contacts mediated by CAM binding, thus providing a robust platform for dissecting the spatiotemporal dynamics of CAM interactions in cellular and organismal contexts.

papers.title: Low-field proton relaxation and rapid resonant thermalization in hyperpolarized glasses
papers.abstract: Spin hyperpolarization enables new applications in areas spanning from nuclear magnetic resonance to quantum sensing. These applications often require a sample transfer from the point of hyperpolarization to the point of use. During this transfer, the sample is typically exposed to fields below 0.1 T. Here, we investigate low-field proton relaxation in nitroxide-doped frozen glasses. These glasses are widely used in dynamic nuclear polarization (DNP), where polarization is transferred from free electron spins to nuclear spins. Using fast-field-cycling (FFC) experiments, we identify two relaxation pathways. Above ~0.25 T, we establish a heuristic description of radical-induced relaxation, which is modeled using a radical-mediated triple-spin-flip mechanism. Below ~0.25 T we report an unexpected process that we call rapid resonant thermalization (RRT). RRT occurs on a millisecond timescale and is observed when radicals are present, but importantly also in the absence of radicals when deuterium is present. Our findings will guide the development of improved transfer protocols and sample formulations for preserving hyperpolarization.

papers.title: Self-organized fractal architectures driven by motility-dependent chemotactic feedback
papers.abstract: Complex organization in living systems often emerges through self-organization driven by local interactions. During processes such as vasculogenesis and epithelial remodeling, cells both generate and respond to self-produced chemical cues to coordinate collective behavior. Here, we introduce a minimal agent-based model in which agents deposit a chemical only while moving and subsequently bias their motion up local chemical gradients through a saturating chemotactic response. Systematic variation of the deposition and decay rates reveals a phase diagram spanning homogeneous states, sparse and dense networks, compact clusters, and a re-entrant homogeneous state. Fractal dimensions, cluster-size distributions, tagged-particle mean-squared displacements, and post-quench coarsening dynamics quantify the structure and evolution of these morphologies. A coarse-grained continuum theory captures the onset of pattern formation and the re-entrant transition through linear stability analysis. Our results identify a simple and testable design principle that stabilizes fractal-like network architectures in biological and synthetic active systems.

papers.title: Discovery of a phenylalanine hydroxylase stabilizer that lowers blood phenylalanine in Pah<sup>R408W/R408W</sup> phenylketonuria mice
papers.abstract: Phenylketonuria (PKU) is an inherited metabolic disease that is caused by loss-of-function mutations in the liver enzyme phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH), which metabolizes blood phenylalanine (Phe) to tyrosine (Tyr). The result is the systemic accumulation of Phe in the body that can lead to neurotoxic effects if left untreated. Numerous mutations in PAH lead to the destabilization and misfolding of the enzyme that result in PKU. A cellular phenotypic assay was developed to identify compounds that could stabilize PAH and increase the conversion rate of Phe to Tyr. Screening hits were then used to design an exemplar compound which was scaled up and crystallized with purified enzyme to determine the PAH binding site, and also orally dosed to mice engineered with the most common mutation that causes PKU in humans, R408W. Here, we report the discovery of a small-molecule chaperone that promotes stabilization of PAH R408W both in vitro and in vivo. Moreover, this molecule restores the endogenous metabolic pathway, thus normalizing the elevated blood Phe concentrations of the PAH R408W homozygous mice. These studies demonstrate in a preclinical mouse model that use of a drug-like small-molecule pharmacological chaperone can be a viable approach for the treatment of severe PKU. Phenylketonuria is an inherited metabolic disease and many of those who have it are unable to reduce their symptoms or eat a normal diet with conventional treatments. Since the disease is known to be caused by an inadequate amount of a liver enzyme, a laboratory test was devised to find chemical compounds that could increase the amount of the enzyme. One promising compound identified was tested in mice engineered to have phenylketonuria. The compound was shown to increase the amount of enzyme in mouse liver, thereby increasing its metabolic rate. Together, the results suggest that chemical compounds can be designed as medicines to restore normal metabolic function for those with phenylketonuria. Okamura et al. identifies compounds that stabilize mutant phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) and develop an optimized small-molecule chaperone, characterizing it structurally and evaluating it in a PKU mouse model. The chaperone stabilizes PAH R408W and restores phenylalanine metabolism, normalizing blood phenylalanine concentrations in mice and supporting its potential as a treatment for severe PKU.

papers.title: Ketamine promotes strategic and efficient approach-avoidance conflict resolution
papers.abstract: Adaptive behavior requires flexibly balancing approach and avoidance in risky or threatening environments, a flexibility disrupted in depression and other disorders marked by excessive avoidance. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam broadly dampen neural excitability and synaptic plasticity, whereas ketamine may enhance both. We therefore asked whether ketamine promotes more strategic and efficient motivational behavior. In this completed randomized crossover study, 34 healthy participants with no lifetime neurological or psychiatric disorders and no regular medication use were assessed at the University Medical Center Freiburg (DRKS00025471). Participants completed three visits separated by seven days: a control visit without medication, followed by intranasal ketamine (50 mg) and oral lorazepam (1 mg) in randomized, counterbalanced order. Threat probability and loss magnitude were varied independently in a dynamic approach–avoidance conflict task conducted after ketamine’s acute dissociative phase. Reported behavioral outcomes were net token gain, approach behavior, and approach and withdrawal latencies. Behavioral assessors were blinded to condition; participants and physicians were not. Mixed-effects models were used. All 34 randomized participants completed each condition and were analyzed. Ketamine yielded 57% higher token gains than control (β = 0.09, 95% confidence interval 0.05 to 0.13; p < 0.001) and 33% higher gains than lorazepam (β = 0.05, 0.01 to 0.09; p = 0.009). Behavior following ketamine was more strongly guided by outcome value than threat probability and showed faster approach and withdrawal responses. Lorazepam produced a less selective increase in approach behavior. No unexpected adverse events occurred. In healthy participants, ketamine was associated with more efficient and value-sensitive approach–avoidance behavior than control and lorazepam. Many everyday decisions involve weighing a possible gain against a possible harm. In depression, this balance shifts toward avoidance, and people withdraw from rewarding opportunities. Ketamine is a fast-acting antidepressant, but how it restores motivation is unclear. We asked 34 healthy volunteers to play a computer game in which they collected coins while avoiding a virtual attacker, once without medication, once after ketamine and once after lorazepam, a widely used calming medicine. After ketamine, volunteers earned far more coins. They acted more quickly and judged each situation better, taking chances when little could be lost and holding back when much could. Lorazepam did not produce this selective pattern. Ketamine may therefore work in depression by restoring flexible, goal-directed engagement with the environment.

papers.title: Globally antiaromatic anthracene–porphyrin nanobelts
papers.abstract: Conjugated molecular belts show unusual electronic and magnetic properties owing to their radially oriented p orbitals. Now, anthracene-bridged porphyrin nanobelts have been synthesized through a nickel(0)-mediated coupling strategy followed by Scholl oxidation. These hybrid nanobelts show global antiaromaticity, with Hückel circuits of 72, 96 or 120 π electrons.

papers.title: Isolable crystalline oxoboranes
papers.abstract: Oxoboranes, compounds featuring a central dicoordinate boron atom engaged in a B–O triple bond, have long been regarded as highly reactive and are typically observed only as transient species. Although attempts to synthesize them date back to the 1960s, their isolation in the condensed phase has proved challenging. Now, two independent studies describe the isolation of neutral and cationic oxoboranes derived from related diboracumulenes.

papers.title: Quantum analogue-to-digital converter for phase estimation
papers.abstract: Traditional quantum metrology assesses precision using the figures of merit of continuous-valued parameter estimation. Recently, quantum digital estimation was introduced: it evaluates the performance information-theoretically by quantifying the number of significant bits of the parameter, redefining key benchmarks like the Heisenberg bound. Here we report the first experimental realization of a quantum analogue-to-digital converter for quantum metrology, which takes a continuous parameter as the input and outputs a bit string, using an advanced photonic platform comprising a fully reconfigurable integrated circuit and a quantum dot source of highly indistinguishable photons. We implement a protocol for digital phase estimation that is capable of surpassing classical strategies in terms of mutual information between the output bit string and the unknown parameter, through the simultaneous use of different entangled state resources. We tackle experimental imperfections by using machine learning techniques for noise deconvolution and estimation process refinement. Our protocol is experimentally benchmarked against classical strategies via the number of recoverable bits of the unknown parameter. Our results open new perspectives for future implementation of quantum digital estimation strategies. A proof of concept of a quantum analogue-to-digital converter is implemented on an integrated photonic platform, tailored for digital quantum phase estimation in metrology. This converter yields a higher number of useful bits compared with the classical interferometric estimation.

papers.title: Zinc carries hydrogen beyond pipelines
papers.abstract: A machine-learning-identified lactate ligand doubles the solubility of Zn(II) in alkaline solutions, enabling metallic zinc to function as a transportable energy vector that releases hydrogen on demand without an external circuit.

papers.title: Beyond selectivity in ion separations
papers.abstract: Selectivity is the dominant metric for ion-selective separations, yet it often fails to predict process performance by itself. A new framework allows for a more reliable comparison between processes based on multiple separation outcomes.

papers.title: System of agentic AI for the discovery of metal–organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Generative models and machine learning promise accelerated material discovery in metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) for CO2 capture and water harvesting, but face substantial challenges in navigating vast chemical spaces while ensuring synthesizability. Here we present MOFGen, a system of agentic artificial intelligence (AI) comprising interconnected agents: a large language model that proposes MOF compositions, a diffusion model that generates crystal structures, quantum mechanical agents that optimize and filter candidates, and synthetic-feasibility agents guided by expert rules and machine learning. Trained on a broad set of experimentally reported MOFs and computational databases, MOFGen generated hundreds of thousands of MOF structures and synthesizable organic linkers. The uniqueness of our approach lies in its ability to generate large MOF structures with atomic precision, beyond the scale of conventional generative models limited to tens of atoms. This approach was validated through high-throughput experiments and the successful synthesis of four ‘AI-dreamt’ MOFs. An agentic AI system, MOFGen, is developed to accelerate the discovery of synthesizable metal–organic frameworks.

papers.title: Predicting degradation of polymeric materials in complex chemical environments via molecular modeling
papers.abstract: So far, developing a comprehensive theory of polymer degradation has been difficult owing to the vast range of time and length scales that characterize breakdown. Physical modeling of a polymer’s response to external stimuli is poised to clarify the connection between chemical interactions and the evolution of properties throughout and beyond their operational lifetime. In this Perspective, we explore how physical models, enhanced by big data and artificial intelligence, have and will accelerate our understanding of the degradation of complex soft materials. This Perspective explores how physical models, in collaboration with big data and artificial intelligence, can accelerate our understanding of the degradation of soft materials.

papers.title: Environmental and material implications of global climate mitigation pathways
papers.abstract: Reaching the goals of the Paris Agreement requires a rapid transformation of global energy systems. Yet, energy supply and use exert multiple pressures on ecosystems, human health and natural resources, raising questions about the broader environmental consequences of alternative decarbonization pathways and the resources they require. Here we analyse 24 climate mitigation pathways from three integrated assessment models using a life-cycle perspective. This enables a system-wide comparison of environmental impacts and resource requirements of global final energy provision from 2020 to 2100. We find that deep decarbonization delivers substantial cobenefits for human health and ecosystem quality, but does not systematically reduce pressures on land, water or mineral resource extraction. For metals central to electrification, climate change mitigation ambition primarily reshapes the timing of extraction rather than cumulative volumes. Pathways achieving similar climate targets can impose markedly different environmental and resource pressures, shaping the feasibility and desirability of alternative transitions. Deep decarbonization benefits health and ecosystems but does not necessarily reduce land, water or mineral pressures. Here the researchers show that different pathways can shift when metals are extracted without changing total demand.

papers.title: Improving compatibility in mixed-matrix membranes
papers.abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes promise to combine the processability of polymers with the transport advantages of porous fillers, yet poor compatibility between the two limits their performance. New research shows that tailoring interfaces between polymers and covalent organic frameworks enables high filler loadings, producing improved membranes for carbon capture.

papers.title: O6-type layered oxides for sustainable high-energy battery cathodes
papers.abstract: Developing sustainable lithium-ion battery cathode materials with high energy density and structural stability is critical for the global clean energy transition. Oxygen-redox chemistry in lithium-rich layered oxides offers additional capacity, but irreversible structural changes cause progressive voltage decay. Here we report a family of lithium-rich layered cathodes, Lix(Li0.15Ni0.20Mn0.65)O2, with a unique O6-type stacking sequence formed by atomic-scale intergrowth of O3- and O1-type subunit cells, and reveal how this architecture regulates oxygen-redox activity and structural reversibility. Combining first-principles calculations with structural and spectroscopic analyses, we show that this intergrown architecture suppresses destructive structural evolution responsible for oxygen-redox degradation, including transition-metal migration and irreversible oxygen dimerization. By preserving the local oxygen coordination environment during cycling, the O6 framework stabilizes oxygen-redox activity and mitigates the associated voltage decay. Consequently, the O6-type cathode exhibits negligible voltage decay and superior energy density retention. Our findings establish atomic-scale stacking as a key design parameter for controlling structural dynamics and oxygen-redox reversibility, providing a general strategy for developing durable, high-energy-density cathodes for next-generation green batteries. Cobalt-free cathodes are vital for green energy but suffer from structural instability. Here the authors report a unique O6-type framework that stabilizes oxygen redox for exceptional cycling durability.

papers.title: Plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots for crop disease management
papers.abstract: Fungal plant pathogens, such as Fusarium graminearum, can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security worldwide. Fungicides play a key role in conventional plant disease management, but their overuse has led to severe environmental pollution, harm to non-target species and the emergence of resistant pathogens. To tackle these issues, sustainable alternatives are urgently needed. Here we used nanotechnology to synthesize amphiphilic carbon dots (CDs) derived from turmeric plant. Under natural-light illumination conditions, the CDs target the biomembrane system of F. graminearum via generating reactive oxygen species in situ to inactivate fungal spores and reduce pathogenicity in vitro and in planta. The CDs adhere to and enter the spores by endocytosis, localizing to membranous organelles and causing oxidative damage that disrupts cellular homeostasis. A 3-year field trial demonstrated that the CDs can efficiently control wheat Fusarium head blight with little effect on wheat growth, microorganisms and non-target organisms (earthworm, honeybee and silkworm). Overall, this research introduces an eco-friendly antifungal strategy, thus offering a sustainable solution to global challenges in food security and ecosystem health. Plant fungal pathogens in crops can lead to substantial economic losses and pose a severe threat to food security. To tackle wheat Fusarium head blight, a devastating disease infecting wheat crops, an effective antifungal strategy using plant-derived photocatalytic carbon dots has been developed.

Fermentable dietary fiber controls blood pressure by lowering large intestinal pH and activating the proton-sensing receptor GPR65
papers.abstract: High blood pressure (BP) is the most common cause of death globally due to increased risk of cardiovascular disease. Fermentable dietary fibers regulate BP through gut microbial production of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), acidic metabolites. How SCFAs regulate BP remains unclear. Here we show that, in a phenome-wide association study, the proton-sensing G protein-coupled receptor GPR65 gene is associated with human hypertension and cardiorenal phenotypes. Fermentable dietary fibers, delivered as a type 2 resistant starch (RS2), regulated luminal and interstitial tissue pH in the large intestine through gut microbial SCFA production in mice. High RS2 intake reduced pH, increased cAMP production via GPR65 signaling and CREB phosphorylation, and restricted the release of pro-hypertensive inflammatory cytokines by CD8+ T cells. Gpr65−/− mice spontaneously developed hypertension, cardiac and renal hypertrophy, and fibrosis. The benefits of a high-RS2 diet, which prevented these effects, were reduced in Gpr65−/− mice. Adoptive transfers revealed that GPR65 deficiency in CD8+ T cells explained this phenotype. Xie et al. show that dietary fibers can reduce intestinal pH and activate pH-sensitive signaling pathways in CD8+ T cells, limiting the production of pro-hypertensive inflammatory cytokines.

papers.title: Shape-informed cardiac mechanics surrogates in data-scarce regimes via geometric encoding and generative augmentation
papers.abstract: High-fidelity computational models of cardiac mechanics provide mechanistic insight into the heart function but are computationally prohibitive for routine clinical use. Surrogate models can accelerate simulations, but generalization across diverse anatomies is challenging, particularly in data-scarce settings. We propose a two-step framework that decouples geometric representation from learning the physics response, to enable shape-informed surrogate modeling under data-scarce conditions. First, a shape model learns a compact latent representation of left ventricular geometries. The learned latent space effectively encodes anatomies and enables synthetic geometries generation for data augmentation. Second, a neural field-based surrogate model, conditioned on this geometric encoding, is trained to predict ventricular displacement under external loading. The proposed architecture performs positional encoding by using universal ventricular coordinates, which improves generalization across diverse anatomies. Geometric variability is encoded using two alternative strategies, which are systematically compared: a PCA-based approach suitable for working with point cloud representations of geometries, and a DeepSDF-based implicit neural representation learned directly from point clouds. Overall, our results, obtained on idealized and patient-specific datasets, show that the proposed approaches allow for accurate predictions and generalization to unseen geometries, and robustness to noisy or sparsely sampled inputs.

papers.title: Tele-Cranio: a CT-free AI solution for remote diagnosis and planning of craniomaxillofacial deformities
papers.abstract: Computed tomography (CT) is central to craniomaxillofacial (CMF) deformity care, yet dependence on in-hospital imaging constrains remote preoperative assessment and outcome visualization, and repeated imaging can increase radiation and access burdens, particularly for children. We developed Tele-Cranio, a telemedicine-oriented artificial intelligence framework that uses mobile-acquired 2D facial photographs to reconstruct 3D facial morphology, estimate corresponding skeletal morphology and support postoperative facial simulation conditioned on surgeon-defined skeletal plans. Tele-Cranio was developed using 539 paired multimodal samples comprising 2D facial photographs, 3D facial scans and CT-derived skeletal models from individuals aged 3–60 years, including 334 patients with CMF deformities across malocclusion, cleft lip with/without palate, hemifacial microsomia and rare anomalies. Its core model, the Bidirectional Craniomaxillofacial Model-Deformity, learns a shared anatomical representation linking facial soft tissue and skeletal structures across normal and pathological morphology. For remote assessment, Tele-Cranio converts facial photographs into 3D facial surfaces and then infers 3D patient-specific skeletal geometry. For simulation, it generates individualized 3D postoperative facial previews after clinicians complete skeletal planning using standard clinical tools. Validated across heterogeneous CMF subgroups, Tele-Cranio provides an interpretable CT-free layer for remote triage, pre-CT consultation, radiation-free follow-up and surgeon–patient communication, while complementing rather than replacing CT-based definitive diagnosis and operative planning.

papers.title: Virtual atrial fibrillation dynamics reflect clinical outcomes after catheter ablation
papers.abstract: Chamber-wide assessment of restitution dynamics is not feasible in vivo during atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. We reconstructed left-atrial digital twins from high-density (HD) bipolar electroanatomical maps in 323 patients, computed node-level restitution steepness (maximal restitution slope [Smax]; >0.4 million nodes), and induced virtual AF with standardized ramp pacing to classify sustainability (sustained ≥16 s vs non-sustained <16 s), excluding 32 cases with extensive low-voltage substrate and depressed mean Smax. We found that clustering of HD restitution profiles identifies four restitution patterns that stratify clinical atrial arrhythmia recurrence, with the Overall-Low pattern (aHR, 0.37) and the Average-Homogeneous pattern (aHR, 0.59) each showing lower risk than the Overall-High pattern. Furthermore, non-sustained virtual AF independently predicted lower recurrence (aHR: 0.27). Adding restitution pattern and sustainability to clinical covariates improved discrimination (ΔHarrell’s C-index: 0.050), and the combined digital-twin model remained incremental after adjustment for low-voltage area burden, supporting digital-twin outputs as complementary functional descriptors for risk stratification after pulmonary vein isolation.

papers.title: Epidemiology-informed graph neural networks for predicting and interpreting transmissible hospital-acquired infections
papers.abstract: Transmissible hospital-acquired infections (HAIs) arise from complex, time-varying interactions among patients, healthcare workers, and clinical environments. Although data-driven approaches like graph neural networks (GNNs) effectively model these contacts, they often function as black boxes that overlook established epidemiological principles, limiting interpretability and clinical trust. Inspired by physics-informed neural networks, we propose an epidemiology-informed GNN (EIGNN) framework for patient-level state transitions prediction in dynamic hospital settings, integrating mechanistic epidemiological models into GNNs in a principled manner. Patient-level risk factors learned from dynamic contact networks are jointly leveraged to infer latent epidemiological states, predict state transitions across multiple horizons, and estimate key epidemiological parameters, including transmission and recovery rates. We evaluate the approach on a real-world hospital-onset COVID-19 cohort and two public datasets simulating viral and bacterial HAIs. Across multiple architectures and horizons, EIGNNs achieves AUC-ROC up to 98.46% while providing interpretable, mechanistically consistent insights, offering a transparent tool for infection prevention and control.

papers.title: Cloud vs. on-premise large language models for urgent patient-portal message screening: a comparative evaluation
papers.abstract: Patient portal messaging carries a substantial share of outpatient communication, and rising message volume has slowed clinical response to urgent concerns embedded in routine traffic. Whether large language models (LLMs) can triage these messages, and whether locally hosted open-weight models can match cloud-hosted ones, remains unclear. We evaluated six LLMs (GPT-4o, GPT-5, GPT-5 Mini, Llama 4 Scout, GPT-OSS 20B, Gemma 3 27B) against a physician reference standard in three cohorts: 500 primary care messages enriched for urgent cases, 503 epilepsy clinic messages from the same health system, and 300 patient-authored messages from public platforms outside it. Under Majority adjudication in primary care, GPT-5 missed no urgent message, and four of six models, including one deployable on-premises, reached sensitivity 0.97 or higher and negative predictive value 0.98 or higher. Rank ordering held across cohorts. Both cloud-hosted and on-premise LLMs can rule out urgent messages with high sensitivity, though specificity remained limited.
