papers.title: Calcium catalysed nucleophilic fluorination
papers.abstract: New catalytic manifolds that challenge existing boundaries for synthesis and sustainable manufacturing are notoriously difficult to implement1, particularly for catalytic paradigms based on metals which lack access to the fundamental processes that underpin many established d-block mechanistic pathways (e.g. oxidative addition and reductive elimination). The widespread exploitation of systems based on main-group elements therefore requires alternative elementary steps to effect turnover. Herein, we demonstrate a new catalytic platform for nucleophilic fluorination, which exploits a complex based on calcium (the fifth most Earth-abundant element) as the fluoride delivery vehicle. The key intermediate is a calcium-fluoride complex featuring a terminal Ca–F interaction, a unique structural geometry enabled by a highly sterically encumbered dianionic ligand-scaffold. This intermediate links reactants and products through F– capture and release steps, and thereby unlocks catalytic F– shuttling. Late Ca–F bond breaking in the rate-determining fluoride-delivery transition-state means that electronic and steric tuning of F– by calcium is chemically significant; proof-of-concept results show a hitherto unprecedented level of selectivity for substitution over elimination brought about by Ca-modulation. In a broader context, this work demonstrates how control over catalyst speciation and reagent binding affinity are key factors for the future development of sustainable non-transition metal paradigms in catalysis.

papers.title: Disturbance increases soil microbiome functional redundancy but decreases capacity for insurance via winnowed environmental responsiveness
papers.abstract: More redundancy doesn’t always mean more resilience. Here, the authors use seven-year-long metagenomics data from soils above Centralia’s coal seam fire to show that heat disturbance increases microbial functional redundancy but narrows environmental responsiveness, potentially lowering insurance against future stress.

papers.title: Bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes as saturated bioisosteres of meta -benzene
papers.abstract: The authors synthesize bicyclo[2.1.1]hexanes and provide support for their ability to mimic meta-substituted benzenes in biological contexts.

papers.title: Early face-experience deprivation leads to long-lasting deficits in macaque cortical face processing
papers.abstract: The emergence of category selectivity is not fully understood. Sharma and Livingstone show that when face experience is delayed in macaques, higher-order visual cortex remains plastic beyond early development, but the resulting neural representations do not develop typically.

papers.title: Automated data to model transformation for constraint programming with AI
papers.abstract: The authors introduce CPAM-LLM, a framework that converts unstructured optimization problems into executable constraint models using LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, data augmentation, and dynamic constraints.

papers.title: In vivo programming of dual-targeted CAR-T cells facilitates vascular disruption and T-cell infiltration in solid tumors
papers.abstract: Li and colleagues introduce an mRNA lipid nanoparticle platform for the selective transfection of endogenous T cells within the spleen; by dual-targeted CAR T cell in vivo programming, the authors show that VEGFR2 CAR-T cells disrupt the tumor vasculature, favoring the infiltration and activity of tumor-directed CAR-T cells.

papers.title: Modulating FCC/HCP phase boundaries in inverse Co@BO x catalysts via crystal-phase-ratio variation for propane oxidative dehydrogenation
papers.abstract: Oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) offers a promising route to propylene, but developing catalysts that operate efficiently at low temperatures while maintaining high activity and selectivity remains a formidable challenge. Here, the authors report a Co@BO x inverse catalyst in which phase boundaries within the subsurface cobalt promoter enable efficient low-temperature ODHP.

papers.title: Interfacial mechanisms of gas-bubble friction
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. report the interfacial mechanisms governing bubble friction on solids, demonstrating how surface structure, chemistry, and gas identity regulate bubble mobility. These insights advance friction tunable interfaces in bubble transport.

papers.title: Designing 3D oxygen–diffusion scaffolds for high-performance metal fuels
papers.abstract: This work develops a Ce-assisted strategy to build 3D oxygen-diffusion scaffolds in Al fuels, overcoming Al 2 O 3 diffusion barriers and achieving complete oxidation and enhanced combustion.

papers.title: Atomically ordered few-layer molybdenum boride MBenes for enhanced electromagnetic response
papers.abstract: The authors develop a theory-guided molten-salt route that selectively removes aluminum to produce atomically ordered, few-layer MoB MBenes with few Mo vacancies. The preserved Mo−B framework enhances polarization and electromagnetic response.

papers.title: Asymmetric coordination triggers dual-site synergy in gold nanoclusters for efficient aerobic oxidation
papers.abstract: The construction of atomically precise heterogeneous catalysts that integrate multiple distinct active sites into a synergistic architecture is highly attractive but challenging. Here, we report an Au 39 nanocluster with heteroatoms introduced to modulate the local coordination environment and construct asymmetric coordination units on the surface.

papers.title: Hybrid-parity sliding multiferroics
papers.abstract: Sliding multiferroicity allows electrical control of magnetism. Here, the authors uncover a sliding multiferroicity in unconventional magnet with hybrid-parity spin splitting, enabling ferroelectric switching of even and odd parity spin splittings, both of which are manifested in spin currents.

papers.title: Bordetella pertussis adapts to human nasal mucosa through biofilm-associated virulence reprogramming and host-defense attenuation
papers.abstract: Here, authors show how Bordetella pertussis forms protective biofilms on human nasal epithelium, rewires host-pathogen gene expression, reduces the production of vaccine-antigens and virulence factors.

papers.title: Greenland ice sheet retreat intensifies the African monsoon through a polar-tropical atmospheric teleconnection
papers.abstract: This study reveals stronger North African summer monsoon rainfall under sustained mid-Pliocene warming than under comparable transient future warming, linked to Greenland Ice Sheet retreat and a polar–tropical atmospheric teleconnection.

papers.title: Facial photographs reveal mortality risk beyond triage and clinical risk scores
papers.abstract: Using 27,660 smartphone facial photos, researchers showed that the facial appearance from emergency admission predicts mortality and high-risk patients better than triage, early warning scores, vitals, or lab tests.

papers.title: A dual-anchoring mechanism for hemimethylated CG-guided histone ubiquitylation
papers.abstract: VIM proteins regulate maintenance of plant CG methylation. Here the authors show how the interaction of VIM1 with hemimethylated linker DNA and the acidic patch of a nucleosome governs its histone ubiquitylation activity for maintenance of DNA methylation.

papers.title: Protecting-group-lean platform for synthesizing diverse phenylethanoid glycosides uncovers antifibrotic leads
papers.abstract: Phenylethanoid glycosides constitute one of the most structurally diverse classes of natural glycosides, yet systematic investigation is constrained by limited access to preparative quantities. Here, the authors report a protecting group-lean platform that delivers a 29-member library of phenylethanoid glycosides.

papers.title: Structure-guided design of a dual-antigen mRNA vaccine conferring broad protection against Henipaviruses
papers.abstract: The authors develop a structure-guided mRNA vaccine combining two Nipah virus proteins. All vaccinated hamsters survive challenge with Nipah-Malaysia, Nipah-Bangladesh or Hendra virus, with reduced viral burden.

papers.title: Vertically aligned dual-channel metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes for gas separation
papers.abstract: Vertically aligned metal-organic framework nanosheet membranes create dual transport pathways that reduce diffusion tortuosity and enable efficient hydrogen separation, providing an alternative architecture for molecular sieve membranes.

papers.title: The evolutionary plateau of efflux-mediated drug resistance in mycobacteria
papers.abstract: Multidrug efflux pumps are major drivers of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria. Here, Sharma et al. use experimental evolution in mycobacteria and show that, after prolonged selection, drug resistance achieved through efflux pump overexpression reaches a stable level, apparently due to exhaustion of cellular energy.

papers.title: Interstitial proton buffering enables decoupled transfer dynamics for acidic wastewater decontamination
papers.abstract: Strong acidity stifles high-valent metal-oxo chemistry in water purification. Here, the authors show that interstitial boron in cobalt-manganese phosphide buffers protons and decouples proton-electron transfer, sustaining oxidation below pH 2.

papers.title: Mitigating brittleness in ceramics via transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity
papers.abstract: A nanotwinned tantalum nitride ceramic combines transformation- and twinning-induced plasticity, enabling up to 60% compressive strain while retaining high hardness (~43 GPa). This offers a route to developing strong, damage-tolerant ceramics.

papers.title: Chiral SERS and photochemistry via collective hotspot asymmetry in metasurface-templated gold networks with disordered nanoscale porosity
papers.abstract: Enantioselective SERS and photochemistry suffer from inherently weak interactions between chiral molecules and light. Here, the authors demonstrate that superchiral fields generated by shuriken-templated nanoporous plasmonic metasurfaces enable attomole-scale chiral sensing and enantiospecific photochemistry under linearly polarized light.

papers.title: Atom-level pinning effect reinforced electrooxidative coupling of anilines into azos
papers.abstract: Electrooxidative coupling of anilines is a sustainable way to produce azo compounds, yet its efficiency is limited by sequential N–H dehydrogenation and N–N coupling. Here, the authors report an atom-level pinning strategy to manipulate H removability and Ni–O– Ni distance, favoring azo synthesis.

papers.title: Estimating malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa under intervention disruption using satellite-derived representations
papers.abstract: Satellite-derived deep-learning-based environmental representations and Bayesian modelling suggest that malaria burden in sub-Saharan Africa could reach 422 million annual cases under a low-intervention baseline.

papers.title: Harnessing regioselective aryl migration of pyridone-based aryl-λ 3 -iodonium salts to access iodine-substituted aryloxypyridines
papers.abstract: 2- and 4-Aryloxypyridines are common pharmaceutical motifs, yet efficient routes to diversely substituted pyridine scaffolds remain limited. Here, the authors report a transition metal-free ‘hook-and-slide’ strategy that enables selective aryl migration to oxygen, providing scalable access to versatile aryloxypyridines.

papers.title: Droplet-Assisted Growth of Re-Entrant Micro-Mushroom Surfaces with Switchable Superhydrophobicity and Adhesive Resistance
papers.abstract: Chen et al. develop durable mushroom-shaped silicone coatings with unique re-entrant structures that combine tunable water wetting, strong resistance to sticky materials, and versatile protective capabilities.

papers.title: Macrophage-exacerbated viral lung injury and mechanical overdistension-driven bacterial superinfection replicated in a human lung chip
papers.abstract: Lung-on-a-chip methods can be used to characterize the function of various cells and biophysical cues within the lung microenvironment. Here, the authors use a lung-on-a-chip method to show that macrophages exacerbate viral lung injury and mechanical overdistention further promotes lung inflammation and bacterial superinfection, implicating SIRT1 as a candidate therapeutic target.

papers.title: A metal ion-assisted workflow for practical and scalable enrichment of small extracellular vesicles from biofluids
papers.abstract: Efficient isolation of small extracellular vesicles is key for clinical applications. Here, the authors develop IonNet, a metal ion-assisted workflow that enables practical and scalable enrichment of functional small extracellular vesicles from biofluids via conventional centrifugation.

papers.title: Numerosity is directly sensed and dynamically transformed in the human brain
papers.abstract: Brain recordings show that humans sense how many objects are in a scene almost instantly and directly, not by combining cues like size or spacing, with this number sense sharpening over the following milliseconds.

papers.title: Symmetry-breaking antibody binding reveals extensive capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus
papers.abstract: This manuscript by Apostol and Anish et al. describes how the pandemic human norovirus capsid undergoes various conformational modalities to accommodate binding of neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibodies to hidden epitopes.

papers.title: Large electrocaloric effects in unannealed multilayer capacitors of partially ordered lead scandium tantalate
papers.abstract: Heat pumps can exploit bespoke ceramic capacitors that get hot and cold when a voltage is applied and removed. The paper shows that the best such capacitors work well even without an economically expensive and environmentally damaging heat treatment.

papers.title: Coherence toroidal vortices and statistic-veiled correlation topologies
papers.abstract: The authors experimentally observe toroidal vortices in partially coherent stochastic optical wavefields, unveiling statistically veiled correlation topologies that remain robust against strong atmospheric turbulence.

papers.title: Parental leave benefits and fathers’ postpartum mental health in Sweden
papers.abstract: Fathers receiving basic-level parental leave benefits were more likely to use any mental healthcare, be prescribed antidepressants or anxiolytics or use specialist outpatient care than those receiving higher-level earnings-related parental benefits.

papers.title: Rapid and selective metal-free O 2 reduction to H 2 O 2 using a molecular Cp N3 electrocatalyst
papers.abstract: Hydrogen peroxide is an important commodity chemical whose conventional production is energy-intensive and dependent on precious metals. Here, the authors report a metal-free electrocatalyst that produces H₂O₂ from O₂ under ambient conditions with >99% Faradaic efficiency, revealing an unusual radical-rebound mechanism.

papers.title: Quantum sensing-enabled deuterium NMR spectroscopy with nanoscale sensitivity at low magnetic fields
papers.abstract: Nuclear magnetic resonance provides unique insights into molecular structure and dynamics but typically requires large sample volumes and high magnetic fields. Here, diamond quantum sensors enable nanoscale deuterium NMR at low magnetic fields with greatly enhanced spin sensitivity, revealing molecular dynamics and phase transitions through characteristic quadrupolar spectra.

papers.title: Impacts of medications for obesity on global health and the environment
papers.abstract: This study examines how medications for obesity could affect global food demand, health and land use. It finds that reduced calorie intake could lower mortality and reduce agricultural land, with larger effects when combined with healthier diets.

papers.title: Trypanosomes Maintain Propulsion in Confined Environments by Modulating Rotational Motility from Swimming to Network-Threading Propulsion
papers.abstract: We show how a parasite can manage to maintain its remarkable swimming capabilities while it infests diverse tissue spaces in vertebrate bodies. We show in 3D how the flagellated cell body flexibly adjusts in response to divers confinement conditions.

papers.title: Lanthanide-dependent methanotroph thrives on radioactive promethium
papers.abstract: In this study, the authors show that the methane-consuming bacterium Methylacidiphilum fumariolicum SolV grows with radioactive promethium as its sole lanthanide source and removes 98% of it from the medium while its key enzyme remains active with the element.

papers.title: Evolutionary plasticity of bacterial surface layer protein exoskeletons
papers.abstract: Prokaryotic surface-layer (S-layer) exoskeletons are built out of proteins that display high sequence diversity and heterogeneous multidomain organisation. Here, the authors show that extensive sequence divergence, modular evolution, and lateral gene transfer drive lineage-specific S-layer diversification across bacteria.

papers.title: The retention of nanoparticles in solid tumours
papers.abstract: Interactions between nanoparticles and tumour components after entering and before exiting govern retention of the nanoparticles. A computational framework is reported to predict nanoparticle residence time and, hence, to guide treatment.

papers.title: Nanoparticle transport and retention in tumours
papers.abstract: Mathematical modelling and systematic studies in mouse tumour models uncover pathophysiological features and nanoparticle design criteria that promote tumour retention, providing cues and clues for improving the efficacy of cancer nanotherapy.

papers.title: 4D ultrasound cerebral angiography reveals the hemodynamics of the circle of Willis in primates
papers.abstract: Four-dimensional ultrasound cerebral angiography (4D UCA) allows imaging of hemodynamic activity in the macaque through the intact skull, as demonstrated by imaging the circle of Willis.

papers.title: Characterizing the solution space of migration histories of metastatic cancers with MACH2
papers.abstract: MACH2 reconstructs all parsimonious migration histories of metastatic cancers.

papers.title: Scalable electron tomography for connectomics
papers.abstract: Electron tomography enables connectomics and volume electron microscopy by imaging thick tissue sections at a few tilt angles and reconstructing the volumes computationally.

papers.title: Space-map: 3D single-cell atlas reconstruction from serial sections
papers.abstract: Space-map is a highly robust computational method that enables reconstruction of three-dimensional tissue from two-dimensional serial-section data.

papers.title: Space-map is a tool that integrates tissue slices into detailed 3D cell maps
papers.abstract: We developed a tool that reconstructs three-dimensional tissue maps from serial sections profiled for RNA or proteins. By aligning information from across multiple sections, Space-map reduced cumulative distortion and preserved intestinal microanatomy, while handling millions of cell measurements more efficiently than other methods tested.

papers.title: Programmable functional RNA design with a virtual scientist
papers.abstract: Programmable functional RNA design is central to synthetic biology and therapeutics, yet both human expertise and existing computational methods struggle to directly program the three-dimensional structures that govern function. Here we introduce RhoAgent, an agentic system that designs RNA candidates and iteratively refines them using experimental feedback. RhoAgent uses RDiff, a diffusion-based generative tool conditioned on base interactions and functional motifs. First, we validate RhoAgent by generating diverse and active ribozymes with only 40–70% sequence similarity to their wild-type counterparts. Second, we enhance the cleavage efficiency of the structurally uncharacterized hovlinc ribozyme by up to sixfold relative to the human-expert-truncated construct. Furthermore, RhoAgent generates a fluorogenic aptamer scaffold that improves fluorescence by 230% relative to the wild-type aptamer. Finally, we design three-dimensional scaffolds that spatially position two distinct functional cores, creating aptamer-based Förster resonance energy transfer systems. This design overcomes a key barrier in compositional RNA design by preserving the binding activities of both components. RhoAgent designs functional RNA molecules by constraining secondary structure, base interactions and functional motifs.

papers.title: Transport without a tether
Unusual melting behavior of nitrogen at extreme pressures from large-scale machine-learned potential simulations
papers.abstract: The phase diagram of nitrogen under extreme conditions is crucial for elucidating pressure-induced polymerization and designing novel high-energy-density materials, yet its melting behavior remains controversial. Resolving this debate has been challenging, because simulating a reliable melting curve requires equilibration of both solid and liquid phases over large system sizes that exceed what standard first-principles simulations can afford computationally. In this work, we develop a machine-learned potential trained to SCAN meta-GGA accuracy to perform large-scale molecular dynamics simulations lasting several nanoseconds. Our simulations qualitatively reproduce the experimentally reported phase diagram of nitrogen and predict an unusual melting curve with a cg-N/molecular-liquid/polymeric-liquid triple point that marks the onset of a plateau. These behaviors arise from the solid polymerizing before the liquid under compression, a process we term asynchronous polymerization. Furthermore, the melting-curve plateau coincides with the onset of optical reflection in dynamic laser-heating experiments. By clarifying the microscopic origin of the unusual melting behavior, this work provides a theoretical benchmark for nitrogen under high pressure.

papers.title: Super-resolution tactile sensing through geometric encoding in liquid-metal microchannels
papers.abstract: High-resolution tactile perception is important for dexterous manipulation and immersive human-machine interaction. Conventional tactile skins typically achieve fine spatial resolution by increasing sensor density, with corresponding costs in wiring, readout, and structural complexity. Here we present a thin liquid-metal electronic skin that achieves super-resolution touch localisation and normal-force sensing from only four resistive channels by encoding contact information directly into microchannel geometry. A kernel-based fast simulator predicts topology-dependent resistance responses without repeated full-field finite-element simulations, enabling noise-aware optimisation of channel geometry for spatial distinguishability. The selected interlocked topology balances spatial sensitivity and fingerprint separability, while a hierarchical mixture-of-experts (HMoE) decoder jointly estimates position and force. Across three independently fabricated devices, the sensor achieved a mean localisation RMSE of 0.230 mm, demonstrating reproducible sub-millimetre localisation. A representative device reaches 0.228 mm localisation RMSE and a force RMSE of 0.043 N, corresponding to a super-resolution factor of 58.3. Force-modulated handwriting and a wearable pressure-tiered keyboard further demonstrate continuous and discrete human-machine interaction, with the keyboard achieving 95.38% joint key-and-mode classification accuracy. These results establish simulation-guided geometric encoding as a route to high-resolution tactile sensing with sparse readout and a thin, compliant form factor.

papers.title: Plasmonic nano-candle platform for phase-resolved optical tracking of Pd hydrogenation with structure-sensitive readout
papers.abstract: Hydrogen detection requires platforms that are not only highly sensitive but also capable of tracking inherent gas–matter dynamics. This study reports a Λ-shaped Pd/Au nano-candle array that leverages reverse-tapered nano-slits to amplify light–matter interactions and provide dual-mode spectral readouts through extremely strong light localization and enhancement. Resonance shifts were interpreted as being dominated by dielectric variations during Pd→PdH transformation, whereas transmittance changes were used as a structure-sensitive readout to infer model-assisted effective gap evolution under ambient conditions. Comparison between the optical measurements and finite-difference time-domain simulations enabled a model-assisted interpretation of phase-dependent optical responses and effective gap evolution during Pd hydrogenation. The optimized sensing platforms with Pd/Au achieved rapid response (<5 s) and a low detection limit of 0.05% H2 with high reversibility, outperforming the corresponding Pd-only design. Beyond hydrogen monitoring, this dual-mode nanophotonic strategy offers a broadly applicable framework for analyzing coupled optical and structural responses in functional materials, enabling new opportunities in catalytic sensing, reconfigurable meta-surfaces, and adaptive photonic devices.

papers.title: Fangchinoline activates cGAS/STING-interferon signaling by binding cGAS and promotes anti-tumor/viral immunity
papers.abstract: The cyclic GMP-AMP synthase (cGAS)-mediated type I interferon (IFN-I) signaling axis plays an essential role in antiviral defense, inflammation, autoimmunity, and cancer. Targeting cGAS represents a promising therapeutic strategy with broad clinical implications. However, currently available small-molecule cGAS agonists remain limited. Here, we identify Fangchinoline (Fan), a natural bibenzyl isoquinoline alkaloid, as a potent cGAS activator. Mechanistically, Fan directly binds and activates cGAS, promoting intracellular cyclic GMP-AMP synthesis and subsequent activation of the STING/TBK1/IRF3 signaling cascade, independent of Toll-like receptor or RIG-I/MDA5 pathways. This activation elicits broad-spectrum antiviral responses via upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes. Importantly, Fan-driven IFN-I signaling remodels the tumor immune microenvironment, enriching cytotoxic CD8+ T lymphocytes and macrophages, thereby exerting potent antitumor effects across multiple murine cancer models and synergizing with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy. Collectively, our results suggest that Fan is a cGAS activator with dual therapeutic efficacy, offering theoretical basis for the treatment of cancer and infectious diseases.

papers.title: Shared and distinct neural pathways of aversive and appetitive pain-related learning
papers.abstract: Aversive and appetitive learning are central to adaptive behaviour, and pain and avoidance are powerful examples of such forces shaping human behaviour. Alterations in learning are thought to contribute to the development and maintenance of chronic pain, yet their neural underpinnings remain unclear. In this registered within-subject fMRI study (German Clinical Trials Register, DRKS-ID: DRKS00027448), we examined both aversive and appetitive pain learning during acquisition and extinction in 68 healthy individuals. Ratings confirm successful learning, with exploratory analyses suggesting stronger aversive acquisition and incomplete extinction. Both conditions engage the visual cortex during acquisition, with increased connectivity to the right operculum. Aversive acquisition further elicits stronger mediodorsal thalamus activity and heightened connectivity with the locus coeruleus, alongside sustained parahippocampal activation during extinction. Incomplete aversive extinction is linked to ongoing visual cortex activity during pain anticipation. Findings suggest shared neural substrates, but stronger aversive recruitment of rapid encoding and persistent memory systems.

papers.title: Insulin-independent glucose uptake into mouse skeletal muscle by a sodium/glucose linked transporter
papers.abstract: A glucose uptake process in skeletal muscle imports glucose together with Na+ using the Na-gradient generated by Na,KATPase-α2. The underlying transporter shares properties with the Slc family of sodium linked nutrient transporters.

papers.title: NSUN4 promotes the growth and metastasis of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma by modulating mitochondrial translation and respiratory-chain function
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is an aggressive liver cancer with limited treatment options. NSUN4 supports mitochondrial protein synthesis, but its role in this cancer remains unclear. We investigated its clinical relevance and biological function. We analyzed public gene-expression datasets, 43 tumor specimens, 37 non-tumorous bile duct specimens, and survival data from 34 patients. NSUN4 depletion and rescue experiments were performed in two cancer cell lines. Tumor growth and lung colonization were assessed in male BALB/c nude mice (eight per group). Statistical analyses included analysis of variance, nonparametric tests, log-rank tests, and Cox regression. Here we show that NSUN4 expression is elevated in tumors and associated with unfavorable clinical features and shorter survival. NSUN4 depletion suppresses cell proliferation, migration, invasion, tumor growth, and lung colonization. It also reduces mitochondrial ribonucleic acid methylation, impairs mitochondrial protein synthesis and energy production, and increases susceptibility to cisplatin-induced cell death. Wild-type NSUN4 restores selected respiratory-chain protein levels, cell proliferation, and migration more effectively than a catalytic-site mutant. NSUN4 supports mitochondrial protein synthesis and energy metabolism in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. These findings support further investigation of NSUN4 as a potential prognostic marker and therapeutic target. Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma is a cancer that develops in the bile ducts inside the liver. Treatment options are limited, so new treatment targets are needed. We studied NSUN4, a protein that helps mitochondria, the energy-producing parts of cells, make proteins. We examined patient tissue samples and tested cancer cells in the laboratory and in mice. Higher NSUN4 levels were associated with poorer survival. Reducing NSUN4 slowed cancer-cell growth, reduced lung tumor formation in mice, and disrupted energy production. These findings suggest that cancer cells may depend on NSUN4 to maintain their energy supply. Further research is needed to determine whether targeting NSUN4 could provide a safe and effective treatment for people with this cancer. The authors identify the mitochondrial RNA methyltransferase, NSUN4 as a potential therapeutic target in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, with evidence that NSUN4 expression is elevated and is associated with poor patient prognosis. Mechanistically, NSUN4 is shown to bind and methylated mitochondrial rRNA, to preserve mitochondrial structure and respiratory function.

papers.title: Metabolic and gut microbiome responses to personalized nutrition during metformin therapy in prediabetes and early‑stage type 2 diabetes: a randomized clinical trial
papers.abstract: People with type 2 diabetes can have too much sugar in their blood stream, which can lead to health problems. Metformin is a common medication for people with type 2 diabetes, but it does not always improve blood sugar levels. This study tests whether diet guidance, based on an individual’s data, could reduce blood sugar spikes after meals more than following a standard healthy diet. In this study, people starting metformin followed either a personalized diet or a standard low fat, high-fiber diet for six months. Both groups showed similar improvements in blood sugar, body weight, and health markers. The personalized diet reduced short-term blood sugar fluctuations slightly more, but the difference was small.

papers.title: Designing functional proteins from natural language
An alternative path for artificial intelligence in Africa
papers.abstract: African governments face a perceived choice between investing in costly national data centers and dependence on foreign technology providers. Both options rest on assumptions that the evidence no longer supports. We argue for a third path, distributed sovereignty: cooperative infrastructure designed for African conditions.

papers.title: Generative molecular design needs oracle grounding
papers.abstract: Generative molecular design is guided by oracles, computational proxies of experimental goals that models can exploit. We argue that oracle grounding, in which experiments diagnose and correct oracle failures, will allow generative models to discover not only new molecules but also new chemistry.

papers.title: Formal proof search enables reliable AI-driven mathematical discovery
Exploring the distributional implications of targeted residential electrification in California
papers.abstract: Residential electrification can reduce emissions but its household economics remain uncertain in regions with high electricity prices. Here we report a household-level analysis of 21,609 gas-heated homes in California, evaluating costs, emissions and equity under alternative end-use, tariff and rollout scenarios. Across modelled scenarios, only 15% of households achieve positive net present values. Cost-effectiveness is substantially higher for homes with existing air conditioning: 53–72% break even when electrifying space heating, compared with fewer than 10% of homes without it. Lower-volumetric tariffs improve bill savings under full electrification for many households, although outcomes vary by assistance-programme enrolment. Modelled income-targeted rebates substantially improve outcomes for low- and moderate-income households. Targeting areas with older gas infrastructure yields emissions reductions comparable to higher-income-first adoption but a larger aggregate private net present value shortfall. Lower installation costs, targeted incentives and tariff reform are therefore central to equitable, widespread residential electrification across high-cost electricity regions. Using data from 21,609 homes in California, this study finds that electrification economics vary widely, with homes that have air conditioning better positioned to benefit. Targeted incentives and rate reform could support equitable adoption.

papers.title: Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR + T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy
papers.abstract: Multimodal profiling of patients with biopsy-confirmed immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis following ciltacabtagene autoleucel shows that CAR T cell infiltrates are concentrated in the duodenum and have a more cytotoxic and clonal phenotype with loss of resident T cells, suggesting that this is a lymphoproliferative disorder with neoplastic characteristics.

papers.title: Multicenter characterization of enterocolitis associated with BCMA-directed CAR T cell therapy
papers.abstract: In a large multicenter case series, only 32% of patients who developed immune effector cell-associated enterocolitis following treatment with BCMA-directed CAR T cells had achieved disease resolution at last follow-up, with some deaths directly attributable to complications of this disorder.

papers.title: Nanocellulose strengthens bamboo from within
papers.abstract: An article in Advanced Materials reports bamboo veneers reinforced with cellulose nanocrystals that are strong, flexible and can be made at scale.

papers.title: Harvesting thermal energy from sunlight with wood
papers.abstract: An article in Advanced Functional Materials reports a wood–metal–organic framework thermoelectric that converts both heat and evaporation-driven water flow into electricity, inspired by the transport functions of natural trees.

papers.title: Physician AI disclosure, condition severity, and public trust in digital medicine
papers.abstract: Public trust is central to the implementation of artificial intelligence (AI) in digital medicine, yet little is known about how patients respond to different forms of physician AI disclosure across clinical risk contexts. In a 5 × 2 factorial experiment in mainland China, 1574 adults were randomly assigned to physician profiles varying by AI use type and condition severity. Administrative AI was rated more favorably than diagnostic and therapeutic AI across physician perception and care-seeking intention outcomes. High-severity conditions amplified negative responses to therapeutic AI, whereas explicit non-AI disclosure was associated with greater appointment willingness under high severity. Exploratory mediation analyses suggested that competence, trust, and empathy accounted for different disclosure-related response patterns. Main effects were directionally consistent in a supplementary offline community sample from Macao (n = 128). These findings suggest that AI disclosure in digital medicine should distinguish administrative from clinical uses and be calibrated to clinical severity, while highlighting the need for preregistered replication using behavioral outcomes.

papers.title: Multicenter evaluation of radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for colorectal cancer diagnosis and survival prediction
papers.abstract: Reliable preoperative classification and outcome prediction could improve management of locally advanced colorectal cancer. We retrospectively studied 879 participants from two centers, including 741 patients with locally advanced colorectal cancer and 138 with benign colorectal lesions. Clinical, radiomics, deep learning, and early fusion models were trained at center A (n = 615) and independently tested at center B (n = 264) using pretreatment contrast-enhanced computed tomography and clinical data. The clinical-radiomics nomogram achieved a test AUC of 0.957 for benign-malignant classification. For 3-year and 5-year overall survival, radiomics achieved test AUCs of 0.874 and 0.898, while fusion achieved 0.870 and 0.899, respectively. These findings identify CT radiomics as a promising digital biomarker for colorectal cancer stratification and show that early deep learning fusion offers limited incremental value over an optimized radiomics baseline.

papers.title: Imaging-based biological age gap and risk of mortality and incident diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence-derived imaging ageing clocks enable estimation of biological ageing from medical images. Yet meta-analytic quantification of the associations between imaging age gaps and both mortality and incident age-related diseases across multiple organs remains lacking. This study synthesised 40 eligible reports, of which 21 contributed to the meta-analysis. Meta-analyses showed that each 5-year increase in imaging age gap was associated with a higher hazard of all-cause mortality (HR 1.31, 95% CI 1.19–1.44), although heterogeneity was substantial (I² = 96.3%), with organ type and sample size contributing to heterogeneity. For cancer-specific mortality, the pooled HR was 1.06 (95% CI 0.96–1.18). Higher imaging age gaps were associated with incident dementia, stroke, heart failure, diabetes and hypertension, but not Parkinson’s disease. Imaging age gaps may support non-invasive risk stratification and long-term health management, but clinical translation requires standardisation, diverse external validation, interpretability, and evidence of clinical utility and equity.

papers.title: Band-Edge-Extended Heterointerfaces for Perovskite Solar Cells and Tandems
papers.abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have emerged as a promising photovoltaic technology, with efficiencies rapidly approaching those of established crystalline-silicon solar cells. Further efficiency gains, however, are increasingly limited by charge extraction and recombination at the interface between the perovskite absorber and the electron-transport layer. Interfacial modifiers are widely used to suppress these losses, yet many conventional ammonium-based modifiers are weakly electronically coupled to the perovskite surface and can introduce barriers to electron extraction 1-5. Here we realize electronically coupled heterointerfaces by introducing a family of heteroatom-containing, fully conjugated formamidinium interfacial modulators, establishing band-edge-extending conjugated heterointerfaces that overcome the bottleneck of inefficient interfacial electron transfer. The resulting band-edge-extended heterointerface establishes delocalized electron connectivity at the perovskite/electron transporting layer (ETL) interface and suppresses interfacial non-radiative recombination. We report a certified power-conversion efficiency (PCE) of 27.96% and a stabilized power output (SPO) of 27.84% for inverted PSCs. The corresponding devices retained over 95% of their initial efficiency after 2000 h continuous maximum-power-point tracking under 1-sun irradiation (ISOS-L). Extending this strategy to monolithic perovskite–silicon tandems enables a certified SPO of 34.71%, establishing band-edge extension as a broadly applicable approach to overcoming the conventional trade-off between interfacial passivation and charge extraction.

papers.title: Widespread deciduousness reveals diverse Amazonian phenological strategies
papers.abstract: A basin-wide assessment of Amazonian deciduousness using high-resolution satellite observations shows a diverse range of phenological strategies across the Amazon rainforest, contrary to the prevailing view of Amazonian phenology.

papers.title: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs
papers.abstract: A transition from continuous to periodic pulsed superradiant emission in coupled spin–resonator systems is demonstrated, revealing connections to time crystals and enabling synchronized microwave and optical frequency combs.

papers.title: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions
papers.abstract: Analogue simulation of massive relativistic quantum fields in 2 + 1 dimensions (two spatial dimensions and time) is realized using two coherently coupled spin components in a two-dimensional atomic Bose–Einstein condensate.

papers.title: A glucose-powered artificial neuroimmune axis for metabolic control
papers.abstract: NeuroAxis restores glucose tolerance, improves insulin sensitivity and normalizes glycaemic control, with therapeutic effects persisting after treatment cessation in rat models of type 1 and type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Conservation of the tumour microenvironment across organs and species
papers.abstract: A pan-cancer single-cell analysis of the tumour microenvironment across 42 cancer types and across 2 species is described.

papers.title: Quantum position verification with remote untrusted devices
papers.abstract: A loophole-free Bell-test quantum protocol demonstrates secure, device-independent position verification, achieving up to 4.53-fold smaller localization volumes than classical methods and enabling tamper-resistant location-based authentication.

papers.title: Quantum resistance paradox of low-dimensional superfluids
papers.abstract: A defect-free unitary Fermi gas is used in a digitally programmable transport geometry to isolate geometric effects on superfluid dissipation and discover a paradox.

papers.title: Fully integrated perovskite active polaritonic circuits
papers.abstract: A fully integrated perovskite polaritonic circuit that brings the functionalities of fully integrated on-chip polaritonic systems simultaneously delivering room-temperature waveguide lasing, controllable optical routing and amplification together in a single-step-grown platform is shown.

papers.title: TransA-MERFISH reveals divergent post-retinal direction-selective circuits
papers.abstract: TransA-MERFISH combines anterograde trans -neuronal tracing and spatial transcriptomics and reveals distinct retinal on–off direction-selective ganglion cell-dependent and independent motion-selective pathways in superior colliculus, establishing a sensitive cell-type-resolved framework for wiring-diagram reconstruction in early visual processing.

papers.title: Flat-band-induced integer doping and phase transition in monolayer graphene
papers.abstract: An architecture comprising monolayer graphene doubly aligned to bulk and monolayer hBN on either side shows a gate-tunable global structural phase transition between two stacking configurations, accompanied by flat-band-induced integer doping.

papers.title: Rainforest adaptation in late Homo erectus from southern China
papers.abstract: Eight Homo erectus teeth from two caves in southern China reveal that the species persisted in closed rainforest ecosystems between 324 and 184 ka, challenging assumptions about their ecological preferences and behavioural limitations.

papers.title: Bogong moths navigate with a light-dependent geomagnetic inclination compass
papers.abstract: During their biannual migration, nocturnal Bogong moths ( Agrotis infusa ) rely on both a stellar and a geomagnetic compass for navigation, enabling them to maintain their migratory direction even if one of these cues is missing.

papers.title: An inspiral of a star inside a common envelope with its giant companion
papers.abstract: Observations of AT 2025abao provide direct evidence of common-envelope inspiral, revealing frictional energy dissipation and constraining how orbital energy drives stellar-envelope ejection during binary evolution.

papers.title: Global patterns and drivers of bee richness and endemism on islands
papers.abstract: Gobal analysis of bee species across 305 islands reveals that islands account for 20% of global bee diversity, with more than 4,100 species and high levels of endemism, and shows that richness is shaped by island size, isolation and evolutionary diversification.

papers.title: Host–microbe interactions in engineered immunocompetent human gut tissues
papers.abstract: Engineered barrier models of the small intestine and colon that include immune cells and a microbial compartment enable characterizations of the human epithelial response to Salmonella Typhimurium at the single-cell level.

papers.title: Injury-induced signalling coordinates immunity and cannibalism in locusts
papers.abstract: Studies in migratory locusts identify a dual role of volatile guaiacol emission, enhancing survival of individual insects following minor injury but attracting cannibalistic attack once an injury severity threshold has been exceeded.

papers.title: Structural and regulatory evolution across the genus Hordeum
papers.abstract: Chromosome-scale pangenomics across diploid Hordeum species reveals extensive structural variation, hybridization, introgression, horizontal gene transfer and regulatory evolution, revealing adaptive trait diversification and providing genomic resources for barley improvement.

papers.title: Evidence for late Middle Pleistocene Homo erectus in mainland East Asia
papers.abstract: Late Middle Pleistocene hominin teeth from the Naxian and Baxian caves of southern China, dated to around 324–184 thousand years ago, fill a gap in the geographical and chronological distribution of Homo erectus in East Asia.

papers.title: Closest relatives of poxviruses prevail in human and animal guts worldwide
papers.abstract: A diversified group of DNA viruses with large linear genomes is discovered, egoviruses, that comprise a putative viral order most closely related to animal-infecting poxviruses, and prevail in the animal digestive system.

papers.title: Evidence for p -wave magnetism in electronic band structure of metallic EuSi
papers.abstract: A combination of symmetry analysis, first-principles calculations, neutron scattering and photoemission spectroscopy shows p -wave magnetism in the near-Fermi-level electronic structure of stoichiometric metallic EuSi.

papers.title: Designing dislocation-driven polar vortex networks in twisted perovskites
papers.abstract: Experimental and theoretical investigation of twisted freestanding SrTiO 3 layers using various analytic methods from 4DSTEM to DFT reveal a long-range ordered screw dislocation pattern as well as topological polar vortex arrays in the interface plane.

papers.title: Transient contacts between filaments impart its elasticity to branched actin
papers.abstract: Stiffness of branched actin networks emerges from the formation of contacts between filaments, with growth under load resulting in stiffer networks.

papers.title: Tropical land-use intensification restructures biodiversity
papers.abstract: Tropical land-use intensification drives substantial biodiversity loss and reorganizes community composition, with aboveground assemblages showing an increase in nestedness in monocultures compared with forests, underscoring the need for landscape-scale, multi-taxon conservation that integrates agricultural and natural habitats.

papers.title: Ferroptosis in cancer cells triggers PGE 2 production for tumour immune escape
papers.abstract: Ferroptotic cancer cells activate a molecular program that causes increased levels of PGE 2 , which in turn impairs type 1 conventional dendritic cell function, compromising antitumour CD8 + T cell immunity.

papers.title: Hypothalamic volume and cell-type changes in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease
papers.abstract: HypoAD, an atlas of the human hypothalamus in ageing and Alzheimer’s disease that combines high-resolution magnetic resonance imaging from 458 individuals with single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 614,403 nuclei, reveals that metabolism- and circadian-regulating subregions, and their inhibitory neurons and microglia, are particularly vulnerable.

papers.title: Encoding atomic-layer thickness via spin-dependent optical differentiation
papers.abstract: The determination of atomic-layer thickness is essential for both fundamental studies and device applications based on 2D materials. Here, the authors report an optical differentiation approach exploiting the spin Hall effect of light that enables a single-shot readout of the film thickness without spectrometers, scanning probes, or computational post-processing.

papers.title: A master gene for Drosophila male courtship prevents the behavior in females via a truncated protein
papers.abstract: The fruitless gene has long been thought to function only in male flies to control male courtship. Peng et al. identify a transiently expressed, truncated Fruitless protein in females that suppresses male-typical courtship behaviour.

papers.title: Lysine- R 2HGylation-C5 identified as a post-translational modification in R 2HG-elevated cancers
papers.abstract: R-2-hydroxyglutarate is a cancer-linked metabolite whose mechanisms are incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify and structurally characterize lysineR2HGylation as a protein modification and develop probes that reveal GSTP1 as a functional target in leukemia cells.

papers.title: Selective mTOR inhibition via FLCN drives TFE3-dependent VLDL-TG secretion and protects from MAFLD/MASH
papers.abstract: The study identified a pathway that coordinates VLDL assembly and secretion regulated by non-canonical mTOR signaling. Targeting the pathway efficiently suppresses liver steatosis.

papers.title: Real estate wealth inequality and exposure to natural disasters with evidence from France
papers.abstract: Most studies on climate disaster exposure exclude nonresidents, missing about half of housing in floodplains. Including them in France reveals major differences, with implications for subsidized insurance and housing overvaluation.

papers.title: Low-temperature operation of Ag—C based anodeless all-solid-state pouch cells
papers.abstract: Initially anode-free all-solid-state batteries with Ag-C interlayers promise high energy density but degrade in the cold. Here, authors identify suppressed Li-Ag alloying as the failure mechanism and introduce an activation protocol enabling durable cold cycling of pouch cells without material redesign.

papers.title: A revised genome annotation of the model cyanobacterium Synechocystis based on start and stop codon-enriched ribosome profiling and proteogenomics
papers.abstract: Information on protein-coding segments in a genome is frequently incomplete and genes encoding very short proteins are often overlooked. Here, the authors present a riboproteogenomic approach. The results support the existence of many additional protein-coding sequences in a model cyanobacterium.

papers.title: Supervised deep learning for efficient cryo-EM image alignment in drug discovery with cryoPARES
papers.abstract: Cryo-electron microscopy studies often generate multiple datasets of closely related samples. Here, the authors present cryoPARES, a supervised deep-learning framework that reuses prior alignments to rapidly determine particle poses.

papers.title: LRRK2-mediated phosphorylation of exocytic RABs disrupts neurotrophin/neuropeptide secretion
papers.abstract: This study reveals that distinct RAB proteins control neuropeptide release in different neuron types and identifies LRRK2-mediated inhibition of RAB recruitment as a mechanism that may contribute to Parkinson’s disease-related neurodegeneration.

papers.title: Impact of Comorbid Depression and Anxiety on the Mortality among Adults with Cardiometabolic Diseases
papers.abstract: Cardiometabolic diseases often coexist with depression or anxiety, but their prognostic implications remain unclear. Here, the authors show that depression/anxiety after cardiometabolic disease onset is associated with higher mortality, with variation by socioeconomic status.

papers.title: VapC40 diverts autophagic flux from xenophagy to mitophagy via ammonia-dependent metabolic toxicity
papers.abstract: In this work, the authors show that a bacterial virulence factor from Mycobacterium bovis rewires nitrogen metabolism in infected immune cells, producing ammonia that damages lysosomes and mitochondria and allows the bacteria to avoid destruction.

papers.title: Boosting Sensitivity of High-Dimensional Solid-State NMR of Proteins by Optimizing Coherence Transfers
papers.abstract: The authors show that for complex state-of-the art solid-state NMR experiments on proteins, custom-designed pulses can strongly facilitate data acquisition, with important implications in the study of larger proteins.

papers.title: Ikaros transcription factors prevent the activation of an endothelial cell program in bone marrow hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells
papers.abstract: Taroni, Bianchi et al demonstrate that the Ikaros and Helios transcription factors restrict the plasticity of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells by preventing the activation of an endothelial cell program.

papers.title: Superionicity and premelting of iron-rich (Fe,Mg)O at Earth’s core-mantle boundary
papers.abstract: Zhang et al. find that oxygen moves rapidly through iron-rich oxides near melting, lowering viscosity and enhancing element transport at Earth’s core-mantle boundary, with implications for ultralow-velocity zones.

papers.title: An ingestible, bio-inspired self-powered electrocapsule for in situ ethanol clearance mitigates systemic and neurobehavioral toxicity
papers.abstract: Alcohol intoxication remains a leading cause of death and accidents. Here, the authors develop a self-powered electrocapsule that enables local intestinal ethanol conversion, reducing systemic ethanol exposure and associated toxicity in rats.

papers.title: Distinct DNA-binding modes of Sp8 and Sp6 shape a hierarchical regulatory network in limb ectoderm
papers.abstract: Limb patterning relies on coordinated signaling and transcription factors. Here, the authors define the Sp8/Sp6 network in limb ectoderm controllingproximo-distal and dorso-ventral axes, showing Sp8 as dominant node and partnership with Dlx factors.

papers.title: A spatiotemporal scaffold in the human subiculum supports episodic memory and its enhancement through navigation training
papers.abstract: Episodic memories are bound to their spatiotemporal context. High-resolution fMRI revealed that the subiculum, the hippocampus’s main output region, is central to spatiotemporal memory recall and functionally enhanced by navigation training.

papers.title: Bioenergetic responses to β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes depend on actomyosin driven forces
papers.abstract: β-adrenergic stimulation in beige adipocytes is coupled with rapid Myh9-mediated actomyosin contraction and cell stiffening. These mechanical changes activate FAK, supporting the expression of thermogenic and oxidative genes and contributing to mitochondrial activity and thermogenic function.

papers.title: Dual-functional-unit modulation enables superior energy storage in high-entropy relaxor ferroelectrics
papers.abstract: Dielectric ceramic capacitors are limited by the polarization–breakdown trade-off. Here, the authors show that high-entropy design overcomes this conflict via local structure regulation and microstructural optimization, achieving 16.19 J cm −3 density and 91.3%.

papers.title: Quantum-accurate vibrational and conformational dynamics from small molecules to proteins with machine-learned force fields
papers.abstract: Machine-learned force fields reproduce quantum-mechanical vibrational spectra from small molecules to proteins, matching experimental infrared measurements at a cost that makes finite-temperature biomolecular simulation practical.

papers.title: 4D printing of multi-state pH-responsive microstructures
papers.abstract: Deep eutectic systems (DESs) are emerging versatile functional materials for 3D printing. Here, the authors demonstrate the fabrication of multi-state pH-responsive microactuators based on polymerizable DESs using multiphoton 3D laser printing.

papers.title: Chromosomally unstable cancer cells exhibit heightened dependence on the mitotic SKA complex
papers.abstract: Targeting chromosome segregation in chromosomally unstable cancer cells holds promise for anti-cancer therapy. Here, Schoot Uiterkamp et al. identify the mitotic SKA complex as a potential target to combat chromosomally aberrant cancer.

papers.title: GTP hydrolysis by Ras proceeds without a stabilized nucleophilic water molecule
papers.abstract: Ras proteins switch off by hydrolyzing GTP, but the structural pathway remains unclear. Here, authors use time-resolved crystallography to show that Ras can convert from state 1 directly to GDP without adopting state 2.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven regulation of the four-electron LiOH pathway in lithium–oxygen batteries with prolonged cycling
papers.abstract: Lithium–oxygen batteries are limited by slow oxygen reactions and unstable discharge products. Here, authors use machine learning to identify a Ni–Co dual-atom catalyst that promotes a four-electron LiOH pathway, enabling high capacity and over 2,000 stable cycles.

papers.title: Bicontinuous Fibre Formation via Co-precipitate Attenuated Solvent Transfer Induced Assembly
papers.abstract: Continuous formation of bicontinuous fibres is known, but can be impacted by pore coarsening, leading towards fibre core collapse. Here, the authors report a method in which amphiphilic species precipitate in situ and are retained in the polymer rich phase, delaying domain growth and preserving bicontinuity.

papers.title: Designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine for enhanced solid tumour penetration and therapy
papers.abstract: While nanomedicines hold great promise for solid tumour therapy, their penetration and access to tumour cells is limited by large glycosylated proteins called mucins that are enriched in the tumour microenvironment. Here we show that mucins induce the disassembly of self-assembled mPEG–polyester micellar nanoparticles into smaller unimers. Leveraging this finding, we designed a mucin-responsive, paclitaxel-conjugated nanomedicine (mrPNM) whose unimers are capable of escaping the mucin-binding barrier. Following intravenous injection, this designer mucin-responsive nanomedicine exhibited markedly deeper penetration than the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and albumin, resulting in 3.9- and 1.5-fold increases in tumour cell delivery, respectively, in a pancreatic mouse tumour model. The mrPNMs also achieved superior tumour growth inhibition compared to both the mucin-nonresponsive nanomedicine and Abraxane, the FDA-approved nanoparticle albumin-bound paclitaxel, in three solid tumour models. The mucin-responsive nanomedicine platform could provide a general strategy for improving the treatment of solid tumours. Tumour-associated mucins induce the disassembly of a designer PEGylated paclitaxel-conjugated nanomedicine into small unimers that escape the mucin-binding barrier, enhancing tumour penetration and therapeutic efficacy in mouse models of solid tumours.

papers.title: Designed broken symmetries facilitate configurational complexity in nematic vortex crystals
papers.abstract: Hierarchical defects in nematic liquid crystals act as meta-atoms for the development of soft-matter-based topological memory and neuromorphic computation.

papers.title: Pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles for systemic immune modulation in diabetes therapy
papers.abstract: Embryonic development is characterized by remarkable immune tolerance, yet whether this property extends to pluripotent stem cell-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) has remained unclear. Here we show that EVs from pluripotent stem cells (PSCs), including embryonic stem cells and induced pluripotent stem cells, outperform mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs in suppressing proinflammatory cytokine secretion, reducing T cell activation and inducing regulatory T cells. PSC EVs display distinct molecular signatures, containing unique proteins and microRNAs absent from mesenchymal stem cell-derived EVs, including the pluripotency-associated proteins ROR1 and CD133 and members of the miR-302 family. Dynamic suspension culture of PSC aggregates enhances the EV yield, providing a scalable and reproducible source. Delivered via a biomaterial scaffold, two local injections of induced PSC EVs significantly improved diabetes-free survival in an antigen-specific type 1 diabetes model, increasing regulatory T cell populations in draining lymph nodes, as well as inducing systemic immune modulation and preserving β-cell mass. These findings establish PSC EVs as a scalable immunomodulatory platform for autoimmune disease and for immune tolerance in cell therapy. Pluripotent stem cells secrete extracellular vesicles that induce immune tolerance and, when produced at scale in suspension culture and delivered from an injectable hydrogel, protect insulin-producing cells in a mouse model of type 1 diabetes.

papers.title: An extracellular contractile injection system for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells
papers.abstract: Protein delivery into plant cells remains a major barrier in plant biotechnology. The Photorhabdus virulence cassette (PVC) is an extracellular contractile injection system, a phage tail-like bacterial nanomachine that naturally delivers proteins into insect host cells. Here we retargeted PVCs to plants by engineering their tail fibres to recognize the plant cell surface receptor FLAGELLIN SENSITIVE 2 (FLS2). We designed and characterized a library of FLS2-targeting PVCs and evaluated their ability to deliver native and non-native cargoes, including a fluorescent protein, Cre recombinase and R2 retroelement genome editor. Engineered PVCs delivered Cre into wild-type Arabidopsis thaliana and Nicotiana benthamiana protoplasts and leaf cells with efficiencies up to 16%. Delivery was FLS2 dependent and scaled with receptor abundance, reaching 75% of leaf cells in FLS2-overexpressing Arabidopsis. We further demonstrated the PVC-mediated delivery of R2 protein, resulting in the targeted insertion of a reporter gene into the plant genome and the expression of the integrated gene. This work establishes PVCs as a platform for receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, laying the foundation for targeted and precise plant genetic engineering. A modular extracellular contractile injection system, repurposed from a bacterial nanomachine, enables receptor-mediated protein delivery into plant cells, establishing a versatile platform for precision genome engineering and biotechnology applications.

papers.title: A pluripotent source of immune tolerance
papers.abstract: Pluripotent stem cells produce extracellular vesicles with unique molecular signatures and potent immunomodulatory activity.

A zero-shot spillover denoiser for highly multiplexed images
papers.abstract: SpillOT is a zero-shot denoising and spillover correction tool for multiplexed imaging data.

papers.title: The effect of inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste on the catalytic cracking of polyolefins
papers.abstract: Impurities in post-consumer plastic waste (PCPW) are a major barrier for the conversion of polyolefin waste into useful chemicals. While detrimental effects of common impurities in crude oil, such as sulfur, nitrogen and metals, have been studied extensively, their PCPW counterparts have not. Here we study the effects of various inorganic impurities during catalytic cracking of polyolefins using ultrastable zeolite Y. The most critical inorganics are typical zeolite poisons. Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu led to noticeable zeolite deactivation at 0.14 wt% loading on pristine polymer. Inert metal oxides, such as SiO2 and TiO2, cause deactivation only at high loadings (~1 wt%) by blocking access to the zeolite surface, whereas S and Cl contamination did not lead to deactivation. Ultrastable zeolite Y retains considerable activity for the cracking of PCPW even after processing 60 times its weight in PCPW. Metal and metal oxide impurities largely remain on the zeolite material, highlighting the potential of catalytic cracking yielding cleaner pyrolysis oil than thermal pyrolysis. Polyolefin upcycling is challenged by inorganic impurities in post-consumer plastic waste. Here the authors show that common metal contaminants, particularly zeolite poisons such as Na, K, Ca, Mg and Cu, drive catalyst deactivation during cracking, while sulfur and chlorine are more benign. The catalyst remains active over extended operation and has the potential to yield cleaner pyrolysis oils than thermal pyrolysis.

papers.title: Dendrites trigger the alarm
Associations of two insect-specific bunyaviruses with development and RRSV vector competence of the brown planthopper
papers.abstract: Despite the discovery of numerous novel Insect-specific viruses (ISVs) in agricultural pest insects, their fundamental biology remains largely unexplored beyond sequence data. Here, we discovered two insect-specific bunyaviruses in the brown planthopper, a major rice pest and plant virus vector. The two viruses are widespread, persist throughout development, and are efficiently passed through generations via egg transmission. Importantly, NLBV1/NLBV3 co-infection was associated with prolonged nymphal development and reduced transmission of a damaging rice virus under microinjection-based experimental conditions. We further show that these viruses can replicate in related planthopper species occupying similar rice-field habitats. Our findings suggest that ISVs warrant further investigation as potential modulators of insect biology and plant virus transmission.

papers.title: Optical coherence tomography and radiomics for structural, vascular and motion analysis of chorioallantoic membrane xenografts
papers.abstract: The in ovo model is an alternative in vivo system for studying tumor biology. However, non-invasive, label-free, rapid visualization of tumor growth, morphology, motion and vascularization at micrometer resolution remains challenging. Here, we investigated the potential of optical coherence tomography (OCT) and OCT angiography (OCT-A) to fill the gap as imaging tools for tumor development monitoring. Using a self-built OCT system (at 1304 nm), combined with automated radiomics analysis, we investigated patient-derived xenografts grown on the chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) and the CAM itself. OCT, OCT-A, motion-mode OCT, and Doppler OCT were acquired without immobilization, yielding high-contrast images ( ~ 4 mm penetration) at micrometer resolution. This enabled differentiation of chick extra-embryonic membranes, assessment of CAM layers and thickness, vessel architecture, diameters, flow, as well as embryonic motion. Biological features of CAM xenografts were consistent with literature, and xenograft development was tracked over time and correlated with endpoint histology. Automated radiomics analysis extracted quantitative features of xenograft progression that support qualitative findings. OCT, its functional extensions, and radiomics thus provide a high-performance imaging platform for investigating tumor biology in CAM xenograft models.

papers.title: Bomb-radiocarbon validated otoliths reveal 130-year lifespans and declining recruitment for blue sucker Cycleptus elongatus of the Upper Missouri River, Montana, USA
papers.abstract: Validated age-based life history traits are crucial towards understanding the biological complexity of the natural world. The blue sucker Cycleptus elongatus is a migratory freshwater fish of the family Catostomidae native to North America. For decades, there has been conservation concern for the species across much of its range, including populations with skewed size distributions indicative of recruitment bottlenecks. Nonetheless, no validated age-based life history information exists for the species, which is a major knowledge gap. Using thin-sectioned otoliths validated by bomb radiocarbon dating we found that individual blue sucker often live more than 100 years, exhibit sexually-size dimorphic growth, increased fecundity with size, and spot-pigmentation with age. Across 42 individuals from the Upper Missouri River, Montana, we observed a maximum lifespan of 131 years, which is 70 years older than previously reported. Furthermore, 64–76% of individuals were from hatch years that pre-date the completion of Fort Peck Dam (1940), Canyon Ferry Dam (1954), and Tiber Dam (1956), which suggests recruitment failure is more likely in the post-dam era. Our findings redefine our understanding of blue sucker, parallel recent population demographic discoveries for buffalofishes (Ictiobus spp.), and further identify the diversity of the centenarian catostomid guild.
