papers.abstract: The shandite compounds garnered great interest due to exhibiting complex magnetic interactions and Weyl fermions. While previous results have shown magnetic transport phenomena driven by topological features, there is little understanding of magnetic interactions and their effect on Weyl features. Here, we employ first-principles calculations to investigate such compounds, including Co3Sn2S2, Co3Sn2SeS, and Co3Sn2Se2. The Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction (DMI) is found to be negligible even when inversion symmetry is broken, while the exchange interaction and magnetocrystalline anisotropy are present. However, we identify that a decisive role is played by spin-chiral interaction (SCI) arising from the kagome lattice topology in stabilizing magnetic textures. Furthermore, we demonstrate that short-wavelength magnetic textures drive phase transitions of the Weyl nodes, leading to band flattening and gap opening. This newly identified SCI, together with the associated electronically driven phase transitions, provides a promising route for manipulating transport properties in spintronic devices.

papers.title: Patient-derived organoids reveal strain-specific efficacy of engineered bacteria in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: ED Summary: O’Connor et al. use a patient-derived organoid co-culture platform to evaluate engineered bacterial therapies for colorectal cancer and capture strain- and patient-specific responses. Both bacteria preferentially colonise tumours, but attenuated Salmonella shows stronger colonisation and biological effects than E. coli Nissle.

papers.title: Unveiling the sulfammox paradox through cryptic oxygen permeation driving ammonia oxidation over presumed sulfate reduction
papers.abstract: The sulfate-reducing ammonia oxidation (sulfammox) process describes a novel anaerobic nitrogen cycle in which sulfate serves as the direct electron acceptor. Integrating bioreactor studies, kinetic assays and multi-omics, this study demonstrates that ammonia oxidation proceeds independently of sulfate supply (ΔN/ΔS up to 12.4 versus theoretical 2:1). Mechanistically, cryptic oxygen permeation through silicone tubing creates micro‑oxic niches that enrich Nitrosomonas and Candidatus Brocadia, establishing a canonical partial nitritation–anammox cascade. Quantitative flux calculations suggest that this oxygen permeation could sustain the observed nitrification. Meta‑omics reveals that functional genes for ammonia oxidation and sulfate reduction were neither genomically co‑localized nor co‑expressed. Thus, the observed activity is driven by oxygen permeation‑induced nitrification–anammox, not by direct coupling to sulfate reduction, which redefines the coupling mechanism and proposes passive membrane aeration as an alternative route for sustainable, low‑carbon wastewater treatment. This study shows that ammonia oxidation in the proposed sulfammox process occurs independently of sulfate reduction and is instead associated with an oxygen-permeation-driven nitrification–anammox cascade under micro-oxic conditions.

papers.title: Minimizing data requirements for chemical and material property prediction via cluster-based training set selection
papers.abstract: Machine learning is increasingly used to predict chemical and material properties, and when data are scarce, data acquisition is often necessary to support these efforts. Despite the practical advantages of minimizing acquisition costs, it remains unclear which data acquisition strategies are the most efficient across diverse property prediction tasks or what principled basis underlies their relative performance. Here we survey 100 space-filling and active learning algorithms across 60 property prediction tasks, finding that cluster-based training set selection consistently outperforms active learning when choosing from a predefined candidate library, a result that runs counter to prevailing practice and is robust to the dimensionality of material representations, the choice of fixed or learned representations, and training set size. A theoretical framework grounded in Gaussian process variance establishes cluster-based selection as the principled optimum in the low-data limit, providing a unified basis for understanding training set quality across contexts. Overall, this work establishes cluster-based training set selection as a broadly effective and principled strategy for data-efficient, machine-learning-enabled materials design. A survey of 100 algorithms across 60 chemical and materials property prediction tasks finds that cluster-based selection of training data outperforms active learning, and a theoretical framework establishes why this occurs in the low-data limit.

papers.title: Targeted technology coadoption for reconciling energy savings and equity gains in the residential energy transition
papers.abstract: The transition to net-zero residential energy relies on the rapid integration of photovoltaics (PV), electric vehicles and heat pumps, yet their systemic interactions remain under-examined. Using machine learning across 17,900 households, we show that targeting energy use and cost reduction leads to technology allocation to traditional early adopters—wealthy, single-family homeowners, reinforcing spatial clustering. Conversely, aiming at minimizing population-wide energy burden produces a socio-demographic realignment, directing technologies to underserved households and yielding a more spatially dispersed distribution. PV deployment to these households leads to strong equity gains relative to electric vehicles or heat pumps. Promoting co-adoption further reduce energy burden. These results underscore the need for targeted, bundled support that extends beyond homeowner-centric models to deliver PV access and integrated technology portfolios to low-income renter and multi-family sectors. Targeting burden reduction realigns technology distribution towards disadvantaged households. The study shows that solar co-adoption for these households can deliver equity gains, highlighting the need for bundled, multifamily and renter-accessible policies.

papers.title: Wood-derived membranes for water purification
papers.abstract: An article in Advanced Materials reports a Janus membrane based on wood and polydimethylsiloxane that enables rapid, highly selective recovery of aromatic compounds from saline wastewaters through a soft-gated transport mechanism.

papers.title: Thermal-shock catalysts
papers.abstract: Thermal-shock catalysts (TSCs), synthesized under non-equilibrium conditions through rapid heating to high temperatures followed by ultrafast cooling, represent a transformative class of materials that overcome key limitations of traditional catalyst fabrication. Unlike near-equilibrium routes with slow cooling, which favour phase separation and thermodynamically stable structures, thermal-shock synthesis kinetically traps metastable, finely dispersed and often single-phase structures. Here, we present an integrated review of TSCs, highlighting thermal shock as a versatile non-equilibrium strategy for synthesizing single-atom, bimetallic, multi-elemental and other complex high-performance catalysts. By precisely tailoring temperature profiles to regulate thermodynamic and kinetic processes and controlling the chemical environment, thermal shock tunes particle size, strain, defects, phase, structure, entropy and composition, thereby governing active-site properties and catalyst stability. We further propose a closed-loop, artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted platform that integrates rational design, high-throughput thermal-shock synthesis, automated testing and data-driven predictive modelling to accelerate the autonomous discovery and smart manufacturing of next-generation TSCs. Thermal-shock catalysts, synthesized under non-equilibrium conditions through rapid heating to high temperatures followed by ultrafast cooling, represent a transformative class of materials. This Review discusses the use of thermal shock as a versatile non-equilibrium strategy for synthesizing single-atom, bimetallic, multi-elemental and other complex high-performance catalysts.

papers.title: Network meta-analysis of digital interventions for fibromyalgia
papers.abstract: This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluated digital interventions for function, pain, and depression in adults with fibromyalgia. PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched up to 1 February 2026. Risk of bias and evidence certainty were assessed using RoB 2.0 and Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA). Twenty-three randomized controlled trials involving 1540 participants were included. Random-effects network meta-analysis showed that digital psychological-behavioral interventions (DPI) and tele-rehabilitation guidance (TRG) significantly reduced pain versus waitlist (WL) or treatment-as-usual (TAU) controls (DPI: SMD: −1.25, 95% CI: −2.01 to −0.48, moderate certainty of evidence; TRG: SMD: −1.15, 95% CI: −1.86 to −0.43, low certainty of evidence). No significant overall effects were observed for fibromyalgia impact or depression. Exploratory subgroup analyses suggested different patterns across age and intervention-duration strata, but effect modification was not formally tested. Heterogeneity and imprecision limit interpretation. Larger standardized trials are needed to clarify treatment modifiers and inform personalized care.

papers.title: Bridging vision-language reasoning and learned control for legged navigation in the wild
papers.abstract: Science Robotics, Volume 11, Issue 120, November 2026.

papers.title: Controlled flight of an insect-scale flapping-wing robot via integrated onboard sensing and computation
papers.abstract: Science Robotics, Volume 11, Issue 120, November 2026.

papers.title: Printing powerful soft robots on a desktop
papers.abstract: Science Robotics, Volume 11, Issue 120, November 2026.

papers.title: In-chip volumetric printing of perfusable and stretchable collagen-I scaffolds for mammary tissue models
papers.abstract: Engineered epithelial models require three-dimensional extracellular matrix environments that support organized cell growth and allow independent access to luminal and basal compartments. However, many organ-on-chip (OoC) fabrication strategies rely on planar geometries, non-native materials, or multi-step assembly workflows that limit architectural complexity and experimental control. Here, we report a direct in-chip volumetric printing (VP) strategy for fabricating stretchable and perfusable collagen-I scaffolds inside custom OoC devices. A vitamin C-regulated ruthenium/sodium persulfate photocrosslinking system enabled high-fidelity printing of collagen-I into open-lumen architectures with ductal- and alveolar-inspired features. By generating scaffolds directly within the final culture device, this workflow eliminates post-print transfer and integrates defined collagen architectures with compartmentalized fluidic access and a mechanically actuable chip format. To support chip-based culture, printed collagen constructs were stabilized after fabrication using 1-Ethyl-3-(3-dimethylaminopropyl)carbodiimide/N-hydroxysuccinimide (EDC/NHS) (EDC/NHS) chemistry, which limited thermally induced collagen densification, improved shape retention, and maintained scaffold anchorage during perfusion. The chip design provided separate access to the printed lumen and surrounding basal compartment, which enabled compartment-specific fluid handling while preserving scaffold integrity during inflation, stretching, and perfusion of the printed construct. On the collagen-I scaffolds, human milk-derived mammary epithelial cells formed epithelial layers with tight junctions and lactation associated markers. The platform further supported perfusion culture, in situ staining, and whole-chip volumetric imaging. Together, this work establishes direct in-chip collagen-I VP as a biofabrication strategy for creating perfusable epithelial tissue chips with native matrix architecture and compartment-specific fluidic access.

papers.title: Hybrid chitosan–BSA bioinks for DLP biofabrication and DLP-assisted molding of 3D hydrogel constructs with embedded branched structures
papers.abstract: Digital light processing (DLP) bioprinting enables rapid fabrication of high-resolution three-dimensional constructs, but its broader application remains limited by the availability of bioinks that combine structural stability with biological functionality. Here, we present a hybrid chitosan methacrylate–bovine serum albumin methacrylate (ChiMA–BSA-MA) bioink that integrates the structural support of methacrylated chitosan with the biologically favorable properties of methacrylated bovine serum albumin for DLP biofabrication. The hybrid formulations exhibited shear-thinning behavior, rapid photocrosslinking under 405 nm light exposure, and composition-dependent rheological and mechanical properties suitable for vat photopolymerization. Selected formulations enabled fabrication of free-standing constructs exceeding 10 mm in height while maintaining preserved microscale features. Representative complex geometries and embedded branched structures were successfully fabricated using direct DLP printing together with a complementary DLP-assisted molding strategy. Unlike many existing approaches that rely on extrusion-based bioprinting, support-bath printing, sacrificial templates, coaxial nozzles, or other multistep fabrication procedures, the proposed workflow combines direct DLP printing with a simple secondary molding step using a conventional DLP printer. Biological evaluation demonstrated sustained metabolic activity and cell viability over 14 days. Under chondrogenic differentiation conditions, RT-qPCR showed increased expression of SOX9, COL2A1, ACAN, ELN, COL10A1, and MMP13, indicating induction of chondrogenic and hypertrophy-associated marker expression. Overall, the ChiMA–BSA-MA hybrid bioink provides a versatile platform for DLP biofabrication of tissue models with embedded branched structures, expanding the range of photocurable bioinks available for advanced in vitro tissue engineering applications.

papers.title: Nuclear quadrupole resonance spectroscopy as an operando tool for mechanochemistry
papers.abstract: Mechanochemistry is an attractive green synthetic approach, but it still lacks mechanistic insight. Here the authors report the use of Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance spectroscopy as an operando technique to monitor mechanochemical reactions.

papers.title: EpiPack: A computational framework for reference mapping and out-of-reference detection for single-cell ATAC-seq data with heterogeneous peak features
papers.abstract: EpiPack maps single-cell chromatin accessibility data across heterogeneous datasets and identifies cell types and states absent from reference atlases, enabling analysis of disease-associated cellular changes.

papers.title: Deep strong light-matter coupling in 3D Kane fermions without Dicke criticality
papers.abstract: In the deep-strong light-matter coupling regime, the interaction strength exceeds the frequencies of uncoupled light and matter excitations. Here, the authors access the deep-strong-coupling regime in mercury cadmium telluride and report a single-mode coupling ratio of 1.6 above room temperature.

papers.title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
papers.abstract: RSM01 showed broad neutralizing activity against circulating LMIC RSV strains. Authors found a high barrier to resistance, supporting RSM01 as an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

papers.title: Dearomatization and cycloaddition of furans and indoles enable divergent syntheses of spirooxindole alkaloids
papers.abstract: Dearomatization offers powerful routes to molecular complexity, yet strategies that couple distinct dearomatization products remain underdeveloped. Here, the authors report an oxidative strategy linking indole and furan dearomatization to rapidly access diverse tetracyclic spirooxindoles, including natural products.

papers.title: Upcycling of polyolefin and polyester mixtures via a single-atom alloy
papers.abstract: Mixed plastic waste is difficult to recycle because different polymers require separate processing. This study develops a catalyst that converts mixed plastics directly into fuel-range hydrocarbons with high liquid yield.

papers.title: Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
papers.abstract: The authors study the electronic structure of cuprate superconductor Bi 2 Sr 2 Ca 2 Cu 3 O 10+ δ with three CuO 2 planes in the unit cell. They find that proximity coupling of the underdoped inner CuO 2 plane to the overdoped outer CuO 2 planes simultaneously strengthens pairing and quasiparticle coherence.

papers.title: Whole-brain modeling of dynamic causal circuits in human cognition using amortized variational inference
papers.abstract: Here, the authors develop a computational framework which maps dynamic whole-brain causal interactions from fMRI data. Validated through simulations, optogenetic-fMRI and multi-scale analyses, it reveals task-dependent network coordination during working memory.

papers.title: Mpox virus replication and drug resistance in the central nervous system of a man with advanced human immunodeficiency virus at autopsy
papers.abstract: This study provides insight into MPXV co-infection with HIV. Authors quantified MPXV DNA in 76 autopsy tissues, including visceral organs and brain. Authors recovered infectious MPXV from CNS tissues, and performed tissue sequencing, revealing widespread tecovirimat resistance-associated isolates.

papers.title: In vivo dynamics of ovulation and oocyte entrance into the oviduct in mice
papers.abstract: Here they use intravital volumetric imaging to study mouse ovulation dynamics, revealing how follicle opening, oocyte release, and pulsatile oviductal fluid flows coordinate transport of the ovulated oocyte into the oviduct.

papers.title: STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis links innate immune activation to tau pathology
papers.abstract: How innate immune activation and cholesterol metabolism converge to drive tauopathy is unclear. Here, the authors identify a STING–IFN–CH25H lipid axis that amplifies microglial inflammation, tau propagation and neurotoxicity.

papers.title: Transforming spinel LiMn 2 O 4 into a Na-layered cathode
papers.abstract: Spinel LiMn 2 O 4 has potential to be transformed into a layered Na-storage material, but the mechanism remains unclear. Here, authors investigate the ion migration mechanism during the transformation and evaluate the Na storage performance of the resulting material, including application in pouch and cylindrical cells.

papers.title: Hydroxyl-mediated oxygen anchoring steers CO electroreduction toward ethanol
papers.abstract: Converting carbon monoxide into ethanol is hindered by oxygen removing pathways. Here, the authors report a strontium-modified copper catalyst designed to organize surface hydroxyl groups, promoting oxygen retention and ethanol formation at industrially relevant current densities.

papers.title: Gut microbiota GABA regulation by intestinal pH osmolality and microbial consumption
papers.abstract: Here, the authors show that low pH and high osmolality promote microbial GABA production, yet physiological acidity fails to raise GABA in colon models due to microbial consumption. In mice lacking GABA-consuming bacteria, acidification increased GABA, highlighting a pH, osmolality regulated production–consumption balance.

papers.title: Morphogenesis of the muscular ventricular septum is driven by retinoic acid signalling to myocardium
papers.abstract: Here they characterize a mouse mutant with a deep cleft between the right and left ventricles of the heart, revealing that muscular ventricular septal morphogenesis is driven by retinoic acid signaling directly to myocardium.

papers.title: Full-circle polychromatic photoluminescence in Mn-doped zero-dimensional metal halide under high-pressure
papers.abstract: Mn 2+ -doped zero-dimensional halides combine blue host emission with green-to-red Mn 2+ emission. High pressure and low temperature tune excitons, carrier dynamics and energy transfer, enabling multicolor emission across the visible gamut.

papers.title: Atomic-level coordination-engineered quantum dots orchestrate mitochondrial energy rescue for diabetic bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Here the authors identify deleterious mitochondrial transfer in osteoimmunological processes as a key driver of impaired diabetic bone healing and engineer quantum dots to boost energy-regulation and restore functional mitochondrial transfer.

papers.title: Exciton binding regulation in oxygen-independent tumor photooxidation enables synchronous photoluminescence for cancer theranostics
papers.abstract: Overcoming the accuracy-efficiency trade-off in light-driven cancer therapy is challenging for developing theranostic systems. Here, the authors report a fullerene-loaded heptazine‒perylene nanopolymer that facilitates cancer theranostics through the oxygen-independent oxidation of intracellular biomolecules, and through spatiotemporal fluorescence imaging with resistance to photobleaching.

papers.title: Lipid droplets amplify inflammasome-driven cytokine secretion in infection and inflammation
papers.abstract: Lipid droplets in infected macrophages act as innate immunity hubs, bridging ISGylation and inflammasome pathways to boost IL-1β production during tuberculosis.

papers.title: A map of multi-omics quantitative trait loci in a Chinese population reveals regulatory variations and disease links
papers.abstract: The authors establish a multi-omics quantitative trait locus (QTL) atlas in a Chinese population by characterizing protein and metabolite QTLs and integrating DNA methylation QTLs, revealing shared genetic regulation across molecular layers and links to human diseases.

papers.title: Single-cell mass accumulation reveals copiotrophic bacterial growth rates in native seawater
papers.abstract: Marine bacteria are central to Earth’s carbon cycle, yet in situ growth rates remain poorly understood. Despite their low abundance, Vibrionaceae consistently grow rapidly, suggesting a disproportionate role in marine carbon turnover.

papers.title: Constructing radiative dipolar excitons via frontier-state hybridization in 2D perovskites
papers.abstract: Dipolar excitons offer long-range interactions but typically suffer from weak optical activity. Yan et al. engineer frontier-state hybridization in a two-dimensional perovskite to realize optically active dipolar excitons with long-range repulsive interactions.

papers.title: Stepwise transitions unlock three spin states and diverse SHG in a polar Fe(III) spin-crossover complex
papers.abstract: Multifunctional spin-crossover materials hold promise in the fields of information storage and nonlinear optics but achieving stepwise phase transition and efficient switching of second harmonic generation signals during spin transitions remains a critical challenge. Here, the authors report an air-stable polar spin-crossover complex.

papers.title: Focused ultrasound neuromodulation of mediodorsal thalamus disrupts decision flexibility during reward learning
papers.abstract: This study shows that focused ultrasound thalamotomy reduced decision flexibility by increasing reliance on learned reward values, revealing a causal role for the thalamus in flexible human decision-making.

papers.title: Ligand-Mediated Long-Range Interactions Enable Selective Activation of H 2 O 2 for Efficient Water Decontamination
papers.abstract: Biomimetic second coordination sphere engineering (BSCSE) steers H 2 O 2 activation toward superoxide generation, enabling efficient and durable contaminant removal in complex water matrices.

papers.title: Expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water during Northern Hemisphere Glaciation
papers.abstract: As the climate transitioned from the warm Pliocene to the cooler Pleistocene (~3 Ma), the Atlantic Ocean deep circulation changed, with a permanent expansion of North Atlantic Deep Water, according to new neodymium isotope records.

papers.title: Forced displacement is associated with health service delivery disruption beyond the effects of armed conflict
papers.abstract: Analyzing 193 countries over 24 years, researchers find that sudden mass displacement is linked to childhood vaccination coverage falling 3–6 percentage points for up to three years, independently of armed conflict or natural disasters.

papers.title: Identification of translation events that drive nonsense-mediated mRNA decay reveals functional roles for alternative RNA isoforms
papers.abstract: Nonsense-mediated mRNA decay (NMD) controls transcript levels and is implicated in human disease. Here, the authors use 40S ribosome profiling to identify premature termination events that trigger NMD and reveal a role in degradation of alternative transcript isoforms involved in gene regulation.

papers.title: Population-level characterisation of the human gut phageome and its association with microbial metabolites
papers.abstract: Here, the authors perform a population-scale profiling of the human gut phageome, and show extensive associations between phages, bacterial communities and microbial metabolites, highlighting phages as an integral component of the gut ecosystem.

papers.title: Mapping redox networks in cardiomyocytes reveals non-overlapping response pathways for cytosolic versus mitochondrial H₂O₂ signaling
papers.abstract: The site of hydrogen peroxide production in heart muscle cells controls how the signal spreads, which proteins are oxidized, and whether redox signaling remains adaptive or disrupts sarcomeres and contraction.

papers.title: Partially functional hypomorphic missense variants in BRCA2 are reduced penetrance pathogenic variants
papers.abstract: Germline BRCA2 reduced penetrance pathogenic missense variants partially reduce BRCA2 DNA repair activity, confer breast cancer lifetime risks of 25%, rarely cause homologous recombination deficiency in tumors and need modified clinical management.

papers.title: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET
papers.abstract: Slow sample preparation remains a bottleneck for cryo-electron tomography in tissues. Here the authors explore high-current plasma-FIB milling to accelerate sample preparation, providing a non-damaging pipeline demonstrated in yeast and mouse heart.

papers.title: Posterior alpha/beta oscillations reflect oculomotor dynamics underlying subsequent memory effects
papers.abstract: Alpha/beta power reductions during learning have been linked to subsequent memory. Across four experiments, the authors show that alpha/beta dynamics were consistently modulated by eye movements, and manipulating eye movements dissociated alpha/beta power reductions from subsequent memory.

papers.title: Author Correction: The global patent landscape of bispecific antibodies: technological innovations and therapeutic applications
Jumping from scaling to scale-up
papers.abstract: Jonathan Boreyko discusses how to utilize scaling analysis to progress from fundamental discovery toward practical applications with a close look at capillary-inertial jumping droplets.

papers.title: Dynamic reorganization of prefrontal population codes supports learning
papers.abstract: The adaptive reorganization of population codes in the medial prefrontal cortex subserves adaptive behavior; however, the circuit mechanisms that enable this task-dependent flexibility are less defined. Here we show, using in vivo single-unit recordings and graph neural network modeling during baseline and fear extinction learning, that dynamic node- and edge-level features predict behavioral outcome. Successful learning in controls is accompanied by time-dependent increases in firing rates, flexible spike-timing, and strengthened functional connectivity. To probe this network flexibility, we utilized an induced early-life seizure model as a controlled developmental perturbation. Seizure-induced dysfunction is characterized by reduced neuronal firing, rigid spike-timing, and weakened functional connectivity, all predicting impaired extinction learning. We next tested whether adrenocorticotropic hormone, a clinically relevant neuroprotective peptide, could preserve these disrupted network dynamics. The hormone prevents these deficits, preserving network flexibility and enabling successful fear learning. These findings highlight flexible medial prefrontal cortex population coding as a correlate of learning and suggest that adaptive prefrontal reorganization contributes to learning and can be protected through early intervention.

papers.title: SP6 scaffolds DNA-PKcs and recruits PP2A to license DNA damage repair in human multipotent trophoblasts
papers.abstract: SP6 functions as a scaffold for DNA-PK complex assembly and promotes PP2A-mediated dephosphorylation of DNA-PKcs to enable NHEJ DNA repair in human multipotent trophoblast stem cells.

papers.title: Macrophage Slfn4 attenuates colonic inflammation and tumorigenesis through Rac1-dependent phagocytosis and oxidative burst
papers.abstract: Phagocytosis and oxidative burst, induced through Rac GTPases and Toll-like receptors (TLRs), are central innate immune responses involved in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colorectal cancer (CRC). However, their regulation in macrophages and involvement in colonic inflammation remain poorly characterized. We investigated Schlafen4 (Slfn4) using global and macrophage-specific Slfn4-deficient mice subjected to dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis and colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC). Gut microbiota alterations were assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), and co-housing. Macrophage phagocytosis, ROS production, bacterial clearance, F-actin organization, and Rac1 activation were examined to define the underlying mechanism. We demonstrate that the upregulation of Slfn4 in macrophages upon TLR stimulation or bacterial infection is crucial for maintaining intestinal immune homeostasis. Global and macrophage-specific Slfn4 depletion exacerbated DSS-induced colitis and CAC, accompanied by gut microbiota dysbiosis. FMT and co-housing further supported the contribution of altered microbiota to aggravated colitis. Mechanistically, Slfn4 interacted with and activated Rac1 to remodel F-actin organization, thereby enhancing phagocytosis, ROS production, and bacterial clearance. Consequently, Slfn4-deficient macrophages exhibited impaired phagocytic and bactericidal activities, associated with disrupted barrier integrity and intestinal homeostasis. Notably, the Rac1 inhibitor NSC23766 counteracted the effects of Slfn4 deficiency. Slfn4 is an inducible regulator of macrophage innate immunity that promotes Rac1-dependent phagocytosis, ROS production, and bacterial clearance, thereby maintaining gut microbiota and intestinal homeostasis. Slfn4 protects against colitis and CAC and may represent a potential therapeutic target for IBD. Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) causes chronic inflammation in the intestine and is closely associated with changes in gut bacteria. Macrophages are immune cells that protect the intestine by engulfing and killing harmful bacteria, but how this process is controlled remains unclear. In this study, we found that a protein called Schlafen4 (Slfn4) helps macrophages eliminate bacteria and maintain intestinal health. Mice lacking Slfn4 developed more severe intestinal inflammation and colitis-associated colorectal cancer, together with greater disruption of their gut bacteria. We found that Slfn4 activates Rac1, which helps macrophages engulf bacteria and produce reactive oxygen species needed for bacterial killing. Without Slfn4, these antibacterial functions were impaired, allowing intestinal microbial imbalance to worsen. Our findings reveal a previously unrecognized role for Slfn4 in linking macrophage antibacterial defense with gut microbiota homeostasis and suggest that this pathway may provide new opportunities for understanding and treating IBD.

papers.title: Synthesis and reactivity of a dimetallocarbene
papers.abstract: Atomic carbon is the most fundamental C1 building block. Bonding to transition metal atoms generally results in tetravalent carbido species, represented by allenic (M=C=M′) and propargylic (M–C≡M′) dinuclear forms. By contrast, dimetallocarbenes (M–C–M′), in which a divalent carbon atom is bound to two metal substituents through predominantly σ-type M–C bonds, have remained elusive. Here we report the in situ spectroscopic, crystallographic and computational characterization of a PdII–C–AuI complex featuring this bonding motif. The singlet ground state of the complex is attributed to residual donor–acceptor interactions between the carbon centre and the metal substituents. However, the small singlet–triplet gap (∆ES–T = −6.8 kcal mol−1) gives rise to diverse, ambiphilic reactivity, including carbene-centred insertion into strong C(sp3)–H bonds, radical H transfer and addition of CO, CO2 and phenyl disulfide. This {PdII–C–AuI} dimetallocarbene expands the fundamental chemical bonding space of organometallic chemistry. While tetravalent carbido species are well established, dimetallocarbenes featuring a divalent carbon atom bound to two metals have remained elusive. Now a singlet PdII–C–AuI dimetallocarbene is reported. The small singlet–triplet gap enables diverse and ambiphilic reactivity towards C(sp3)–H bonds, radical H transfer, CO, CO2 and phenyl disulfide.

papers.title: A scalable three-unit continuous operation platform for efficient porphyrin production
papers.abstract: Porphyrins possess broad applications in medicine, agriculture, materials and food. However, their industrial production is hindered by inefficient biosynthetic routes and limited derivative diversity. Here we establish a scalable three-unit operation platform that deconstructs the porphyrin synthetic process into three streamlined units, enabling scalable production of porphyrin compounds that were previously challenging to obtain. We first achieve high-yield production of 5-aminolevulinic acid in minimal medium using glucose as the sole carbon source by globally rewiring the metabolic pathways in Escherichia coli in the first fermentation unit. Such design allows seamless integration with the subsequent biocatalysis unit, where we establish a tailored thermophilic multienzyme system in E. coli that enables the orthogonal whole-cell catalysis of 5-aminolevulinic acid to porphyrin intermediates uroporphyrin I, uroporphyrin III or coproporphyrin III at 60 °C. These high-purity intermediates are then transferred to the third derivatization unit, which expands porphyrin diversity by chemical derivatization. Using this platform, we have synthesized 13 porphyrins and evaluated their promising applications in pigmentation, anticancer and plant-growth promotion applications. Porphyrins have broad applications in medicine, agriculture, materials and food; however, their bioproduction is restricted by inefficient and limited biosynthetic processes. Now a scalable three-unit integrated platform—comprising microbial fermentation, thermostable whole-cell catalysis and chemical derivatization—is reported for producing porphyrin intermediates and derivatives that are inaccessible via conventional routes.

papers.title: Biology meets chemistry for improved porphyrin synthesis
papers.abstract: The combination of fermentation, biocatalysis and chemical derivatization enables porphyrin synthesis.

papers.title: Time for water to take centre stage
papers.abstract: Transforming the water agenda requires a shift to more inclusive governance, greater community empowerment and a stronger focus on foresight, alongside the recognition of water’s central role in addressing society’s greatest challenges.

papers.title: Water innovation-sharing must become a tool for peace-building
papers.abstract: Water innovations such as desalination, wastewater reuse and rainwater harvesting can do more than strengthen water security. International cooperation is needed to ensure that these technologies promote equitable benefit-sharing, mobilize investment and reduce tensions in regions where climate stress and water scarcity threaten stability.

papers.title: Anode-free zinc batteries enabled by structurally robust solid–electrolyte interphase
papers.abstract: Zinc metal batteries are sustainable, but deep cycling triggers a catastrophic structural collapse of the solid–electrolyte interphase. By retaining trace reserved zinc during stripping, this work prevents solid–electrolyte interphase degradation, enabling a 99.96% Coulombic efficiency and stable anode-free pouch cells.

papers.title: Resilience as a governing principle in water governance
papers.abstract: Water governance often treats resilience as an end state, achieved mainly through technocratic decision-making and standard engineering tools. Drawing on five international cases, we argue that resilience should instead guide governance design and operation through adaptability, coordination, learning and accountability.

papers.title: Accounting for the mining industry’s global water footprint
papers.abstract: Millions of people share rivers, aquifers and coastlines with mining operations, but years of regulation and voluntary schemes have left these communities with limited knowledge of what water is withdrawn, discharged or contaminated. De-risking the sector requires mandatory transparency, which should be made a condition of the capital now flowing into critical mineral supply chains.

papers.title: Monitoring water attacks
papers.abstract: Attacks on critical water infrastructure have become normalized in modern military conflict. To counter this, argues Hussam Hussein, water scientists must build and maintain real-time monitoring and documentation infrastructure in active conflict zones.

papers.title: Water as our common denominator in the fragmented world
papers.abstract: In the era of growing political polarization, water can be a force for cooperation towards a global agenda of unity, security, prosperity and sustainability, argues Kaveh Madani.

papers.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
papers.abstract: A study of longitudinal cohorts from Europe and the United States over 30 years showed that later-born generations benefit from higher cognitive capacity and memory stability, which may explain the trend of declining dementia incidence rates.

papers.title: Author Correction: Comprehensive m6A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure
The need for electrolyte innovation in next-generation batteries
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, battery electrolytes have evolved from a mere ion-conducting media into active regulators of the electrode reaction, interfacial chemistry and cycling stability. Innovations spanning advanced liquid, solid-state and emerging electrolyte systems are opening new pathways towards safer, higher-energy and application-specific batteries.

papers.title: Structure-based design of a decorin mimetic targeting TGF-β1
papers.abstract: Decorin mitigates fibrosis by docking onto transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1), but its dense glycosylation and disulfide-rich caps hinder scalable manufacturing. Here we present miniDec, a 15-kDa decorin mimetic built from leucine-rich repeats 4–6 with newly designed, cysteine-free terminal caps. The aglycosylated construct folds efficiently in E. coli, yields >25 mg L⁻¹ after a two-step purification, and binds TGF-β1 with low-nanomolar affinity. miniDec blocks TGF-β-driven transdifferentiation of human corneal fibroblasts and, when applied topically, reduces corneal opacity, restores corneal surface regularity and accelerates epithelial wound closure in a mouse alkali-burn model, with efficacy comparable to that of full-length decorin at the fixed topical doses tested. The protein is non-cytotoxic to corneal epithelium and stromal cells. This new scaffold overcomes the production hurdles of the native proteoglycan while retaining its anti-fibrotic activity, establishing that decorin’s glycosaminoglycan chain, N-glycans and disulfide-bonded caps are dispensable for anti-fibrotic function in the cornea, and providing a manufacturable route to decorin-based therapy for corneal fibrosis.

papers.title: Tracking human HSCs and MPPs in mice reveals distinct clonal dynamics and responses to pre-transplant conditioning
papers.abstract: Blood and immune cell regeneration is sustained by hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs), which form the therapeutic basis of bone marrow transplantation. While the functional hierarchy of mouse HSPC subsets is well characterized, the distinct roles of human HSPC populations remain less well defined, particularly at clonal resolution and in the context of transplantation conditioning. Here, we performed quantitative clonal tracking of purified human HSCs (hHSCs) and human MPPs (hMPPs) in NSGW41 mice across primary and secondary transplantation under no conditioning, and busulfan or irradiation conditioning. We found that hHSC clones generated more blood cells, initiated lymphoid production earlier, and exhibited more robust multilineage differentiation than hMPP clones. hHSC clones were also less sensitive to conditioning, maintaining stable lineage biases. Notably, busulfan and irradiation differentially affected the magnitude, lineage bias, and timing of hematopoietic reconstitution without altering engraftment. During secondary transplantation, hHSCs and hMPPs contributed comparably to hematopoietic reconstitution but with substantially reduced output and increased clonal diversity. Extramedullary hematopoiesis was observed in all secondary recipients. These findings advance our understanding of human hematopoiesis and provide a framework for optimizing experimental models, improving transplantation conditioning strategies, and informing the preclinical evaluation of HSC-based cell and gene therapies.

papers.title: FIRE-EVIDENCE: enabling LLM-driven, machine-readable evidence synthesis for women’s health
papers.abstract: Clinical evidence is abundant in the published literature yet remains fragmented and underutilized, particularly in women’s health and menopause, where timely, personalized decision-making is critical. Conventional evidence synthesis relies on resource-intensive manual review, limiting scalability and delaying translation into practice, while automated approaches often produce outputs that are not directly computable or integrable into decision-support workflows. We present FIRE-EVIDENCE, a large language model framework that transforms full-text clinical studies into structured, Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)-aligned computable evidence. The pipeline was optimized on seven development documents and evaluated on two datasets: a primary dataset of 26 expert-annotated randomized controlled trials and a secondary dataset of 18 studies derived from five systematic reviews. Across expert-annotated trials, FIRE-EVIDENCE achieved 94.35% completeness, 94.61% correctness, 97.36% source faithfulness, and an F1 score of 94.43%. FHIR-compliance testing in a 10-output native FHIR-R5 subset showed that all validated outputs passed base HL7 FHIR validation without errors. FIRE-EVIDENCE demonstrates a feasible pathway for standard-based, machine-readable evidence synthesis.

papers.title: Deep learning retinal vascular biomarker predicts preeclampsia in a multicenter prospective cohort
papers.abstract: Preeclampsia (PE) causes maternal and perinatal morbidity and mortality, yet noninvasive screening remains limited. We developed Retina-PE, a multimodal deep learning model integrating retinal photographs, maternal clinical factors, and mean arterial pressure to predict subsequent PE. Prospectively collected multicenter data from 8616 pregnant individuals were used for retrospective model development and evaluation. Development-dataset image-level areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) were 0.853 and 0.708 for PE occurrence at 24–28 and 28–32 weeks, 0.871 and 0.791 for 1- and 4-week preterm PE, and 0.979 and 0.862 for 1- and 4-week early-onset PE. Corresponding external-validation-dataset AUCs were 0.728 and 0.815, 0.801 and 0.801, and 0.776 and 0.766. Incremental performance was task-specific. Patient-level analyses showed similar patterns but included few events in some tasks. These findings support prospective evaluation of retinal imaging for maternal risk stratification.

papers.title: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic health age using wearables and blood biomarkers
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic (CKM) syndrome represents a growing public health crisis, yet its subclinical heterogeneity remains underexplored. Early detection of physiological deviation is critical for preventing irreversible organ damage. Here, we characterize the prevalence and interplay of CKM impairment in a US cohort (WEAR-ME study, N = 819 participants) by integrating continuous wearable data with clinical biomarkers. We assessed cardiovascular, kidney via clinical biomarkers, namely Chol/HDL, eGFR, as well as metabolic health risk through Homeostatic Model Assessment of Insulin Resistance (HOMA-IR). We show that while metabolic and cardiovascular disruptions are significantly associated (r = 0.26, p < 0.001), early-stage kidney impairment manifests independently. Utilizing a normalized deviance score, we identified significant health impairments in 29.0% of the cohort. Cardiovascular deviation was the most prevalent singular phenotype (13.3%), followed by metabolic (9.1%) and renal (6.25%) deviations, with dual metabolic-cardiovascular impairment occurring in only 2.2% of participants. These findings suggest that high system-specific deviance may serve as an indicator for accelerated physiological aging within the respective organ system. Furthermore, step count, active zone minutes, and resting heart rate were identified as the key wearable predictors of cardiovascular and metabolic decline. Leveraging wearables metrics and blood biomarkers, we developed a CKM Health Age model that tracks physiological health, aligning with established clinical standards (Metabolic syndrome severity and modified AHA Life’s Essential 8) and user-reported overall health. These findings underscore the necessity of a multi-system subtyping approach, demonstrating that wearable-derived phenotypes and routine blood biomarkers can facilitate the early, targeted interventions required to manage the complex landscape of CKM syndrome.

papers.title: Routine laboratory trajectories predict organ-level complications in cancer
papers.abstract: Routine laboratory panels drawn during cancer treatment constitute longitudinal physiological recordings of organ function, yet their temporal structure is discarded by single-timepoint prognostic tools. A transformer trained on 2,777,595 laboratory measurements from 3905 patients with multiple myeloma or ovarian cancer predicted which of 162 treatment-associated complications would be newly recorded within two years, spanning eight clinical categories, achieving 1.5- to 6.1-fold enrichment above prevalence. Across individual endpoints it exceeded non-sequential baselines, including engineered-trajectory models, by +0.024 to +0.070 in mean AUROC. Predictions generalised across both cancers, divergence concentrating in disease-specific complications, and biomarker masking recovered signatures consistent with established pathophysiology. External validation on MIMIC-IV and MMRF CoMMpass showed transferability, strongest for renal and metabolic endpoints, attenuated for infection endpoints. On CoMMpass it added prognostic value to ISS staging. Routine oncological laboratory data carry complication-specific physiological signal months before a complication is recorded, and require no testing beyond standard oncological care.

papers.title: Regulation of hepatic stellates cell activation by biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels with uniform and heterogeneous matrix stiffness
papers.abstract: Current research on liver fibrosis predominantly relies on culture matrices with uniform stiffness, largely overlooking the pathophysiological relevance of stiffness heterogeneity—the spatially uneven stiffness distribution characteristic of fibrotic liver tissue. To address this, we engineered biomimetic fibrotic hydrogels using decellularized liver matrix from fibrotic tissues and methacrylated hyaluronic acid. These hydrogels replicated the distinct stiffness profiles of normal, early-stage fibrotic, and late-stage fibrotic liver. Using a custom honeycomb-shaped mold, we integrated them into a unified platform featuring both uniform and heterogeneous mechanical regions. By co-culturing hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) on this platform, we investigated how matrix stiffness regulates HSCs proliferation, migration, and activation. Results demonstrated that on uniformly stiff substrates, particularly those mimicking late-stage fibrosis, extracellular matrix components and high stiffness promoted HSCs activation, upregulated the Piezo1-YAP signaling axis. In contrast, although the low-stiffness region of the mechanically heterogeneous platform exhibited increased HSC proliferation and activation, the proliferation and activation levels in the medium- and high-stiffness regions were significantly reduced. The expression patterns of the Piezo1-YAP signaling pathway further corroborated this phenomenon. These findings suggest that mechanical heterogeneity may exert a negative regulatory effect on HSC activation. This study provides new insights into the mechanobiological mechanisms underlying hepatic fibrosis and reveals potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Architecture of a portal complex embedded in the poxvirus core
papers.abstract: Gene transcription within the viral core is a distinctive feature of poxvirus replication. Following entry into the cytoplasm, the poxvirus core dissociates from the lateral bodies and undergoes expansion, functioning as a compartment for early transcription1. However, how molecules are exchanged between the viral core and the host cytoplasm remains poorly understood. Here, using cryo-electron tomography and sub-tomogram averaging, we determine the structures of the portal complex and its central pore on the vaccinia virus core at 6.7 Å and 4.4 Å resolution, respectively. Guided by structural predictions and experimental density, we identify three viral proteins, E8, E6 and L3, as the principal components of the pore and construct a structural model of their organization. The pore contains a narrow, positively charged constriction formed by conserved lysine residues in L3, substitutions of which impair viral gene expression and propagation. The dimensions and electrostatic properties of the channel are consistent with a potential role in molecular exchange across the core wall. Together, our findings establish a structural framework for understanding the organization and potential function of the poxvirus portal complex.

papers.title: Brønsted/Lewis acid-catalyzed divergent cascade cyclization of alkoxyallene for the total synthesis of eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids
papers.abstract: Eburnane and aspidofractinine alkaloids are biogenetically related yet structurally distinct polycyclic monoterpenoids, whose syntheses have traditionally proceeded separately. Here, the authors report a divergent cascade from a common alkoxyallene precursor, enabling access to both scaffolds through acid controlled tandem pathways and total syntheses of representative alkaloids.

papers.title: Knowledge-guided machine learning deciphers spatiotemporal dynamics in chemical reactor systems
papers.abstract: A physics-informed neural network embeds coking and heat transfer knowledge via an output integration layer and region-weighted loss to predict reactor spatiotemporal fields; it matches conventional simulation results, improves peak wall temperature accuracy, and runs about five orders of magnitude faster than conventional simulations.

papers.title: Improving molecular property prediction with score-based diffusion models
papers.abstract: This work introduces a diffusion-based approach for small molecule prediction across a range of structure-activity and ADME tasks. It demonstrates strong predictive calibration and support for ensemble-driven uncertainty ranking.

papers.title: Leveraging sequence purification for accurate prediction of multiple conformational states with AlphaFold2
papers.abstract: Proteins often adopt distinct conformations to carry out their functions. Here, the authors introduce AF-ClaSeq, a method that improves multistate structure prediction by clarifying evolutionary signals.

papers.title: Encapsulating an iron complex within a heme and anthraquinone codecorated capsule for multiphoton C( sp 3 )−H bond oxygenation
papers.abstract: The allosteric effect in proteins controls biological function omnipotently, but simulating both the regulatory functions and catalytic processes of analogues is challenging. Here, the authors report the allosteric catalysis of a non-heme Fe(III)-complex encapsulated in the cavity of an anthraquinone and heme co-decorated coordination capsule.

papers.abstract: Conventional thin-film epidermal electronics can accumulate residual stress on complex surfaces. Liang et al. directly fabricate conductive nanofibres on skin, forming a breathable nanomesh that conforms to arbitrary shapes for reliable sensing.

papers.title: A precommissural nucleus-cingulate circuit coordinates a stress-induced agitation-like state
papers.abstract: Agitation links motor restlessness with negative affect, but its circuit basis is unclear. Here, the authors show that a stress-sensitive Prc-CCK-to-Cg2 pathway coordinates motor restlessness with aversive behavior in mice.

papers.title: Identification and deployment of a wild soybean FD allele for high-density planting and increased yield
papers.abstract: Loci that confer short internodes while increasing yield remain scarce in soybean. Here, the authors report wild soybean-derived basic leucine zipper transcription factor FDc1 that exerts a negative regulator effect on internode length, which enhances dense planting and grain yield.

papers.title: A redox-coupled ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 axis controls hepatic lipid catabolism
papers.abstract: Peng et al . demonstrate a critical role for the ROMO1–LONP1–SIRT3 signaling axis in protecting against hepatic steatosis and liver injury. By preventing LONP1 sulfenylation and the resultant SIRT3 degradation, ROMO1 promotes hepatic lipid catabolism.

papers.title: Highly conductive halide Na-ion conductor enabled by cost-effective aliovalent carbonate polyanion substitution for all-solid-state sodium batteries
papers.abstract: Zr-based halide solid electrolytes are promising for their lower cost but suffer from limited ionic conductivity. Here, authors introduce carbonate polyanion using cost-competitive soda ash to enhance structural disorder and Na + transport, achieving 1.02 mS cm −1 ionic conductivity and stable all-solid-state battery cycling for 850 cycles.

papers.title: Phenotypic discovery of GABA A receptor-mediated general anesthetics with analgesic activity
papers.abstract: In this study, high-throughput screening in zebrafish led to the discovery of nidradine, a new general anesthetic that acts on GABA A receptors and, unlike most general anesthetics, also relieves pain at non-sedating doses.

papers.title: Co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM causes replication stress associated with DNA damage and cohesion loss
papers.abstract: The mechanistic basis for chromosomal instability characteristic of RECQ helicase disorders remain difficult to understand due to their molecular genetic complexity. Here, the authors demonstrated that co-deficiency of RECQL1 and BLM helicases causes pronounced replication stress, DNA damage, and chromatid cohesion loss.

papers.title: Burst-like intracellular antibody infusion via membrane-permeabilizing peptide microcondensates

papers.title: MyoGen: unified biophysical modeling of human neuromotor activity and resulting signals
papers.abstract: Editorial summary: Simulating human motor control usually means treating spinal circuits, muscle mechanics, and EMG separately. Here the authors present MyoGen, an open-source framework that couples these elements and generates decomposable surface and intramuscular EMG.

papers.title: A near-quantum-limited diamond maser amplifier operating at millikelvin temperatures
papers.abstract: Amplifying faint microwave signals at millikelvin temperatures has so far relied entirely on superconducting devices. Here, authors demonstrate a diamond maser amplifier that works without superconductivity, reaching over 30 dB of gain and near-quantum-limited noise.

papers.title: Self-powered bubble motor microswarms for ultrasensitive detection, monitoring and prediction in cancer liquid biopsies
papers.abstract: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) have shown great potential for disease detection from liquid biopsies. However, the lack of optimized isolation and detection methods limited their clinical application. Here we engineer a bioinspired, reconfigurable, self-powered bubble motor (Butor) microswarm to streamline intelligent isolation and ultrasensitive profiling of circulating EVs for cancer liquid biopsies. Butor microswarm shows jellyfish-like, self-propelled lifting locomotion along lumen-like vertical or inclined tubular path in parallel, allowing rapid isolation (10 min, near 90%) of EV subtypes via three-dimensional directional scanning capture even in high-viscosity biofluids. Furthermore, the buoyancy-activated Butors achieve ultrasensitive EV profiling near a single-particle level, enable early diagnosis of non-small cell lung cancer with an accuracy of up to 94% (95% sensitivity) in a pilot cohort and improve the outcome in cancer staging (I–IV) discrimination, response monitoring of surgical treatment and efficacy prediction of immunotherapy in patients with non-small cell lung cancer. Our self-powered motor represents an intelligent, fast, inexpensive, sensitive and multiplexed liquid biopsy tool for accurate cancer diagnostics and treatment monitoring in clinical settings. A self-powered bubble motor inspired by microswarm motion enables ultrasensitive extracellular vesicles profiling, monitoring of surgical treatment response, staging discrimination, prediction of immunotherapy and early diagnosis in patients with non-small cell lung cancer.

papers.title: Two-dimensional material membranes with precisely tunable interlayer spacing from nanometre to submillimetre
papers.abstract: A deprotonation–ion coordination strategy is developed for microstructural engineering of layered material membranes, enabling the precise and reversible modulation of interlayer spacing over five orders of magnitude.

papers.title: Controlling the flow of information in optical metrology
papers.abstract: By treating Fisher information as a conserved wave quantity, nanophotonic systems can be designed to control information generation and flow, opening a route to improve optical measurement and sensing precision.

papers.title: Mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology for high-performance integrated circuits
papers.abstract: Low-dimensional semiconductors, such as one-dimensional carbon nanotubes and two-dimensional transition metal dichalcogenides, could be used to build scaled, energy-efficient electronic devices. However, although these materials can exhibit excellent unipolar device performance, complementary integration with balanced performance and low power consumption remains a challenge. Here we report a mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology that combines two-dimensional single-crystal molybdenum disulfide n-type transistors and one-dimensional aligned carbon nanotube p-type transistors. We integrate enhancement-mode top-gate transistors with symmetric threshold voltages using a hard mask technology and pre-deposition annealing process. We use the approach to create complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor inverters that exhibit rail-to-rail operation with a peak static power of less than 1 pW and a single-stage delay of 19 ps. We also fabricate 180-nm-node area-equivalent static random-access memory that offers robust read–write operations with a noise margin of 22% and 40% operating voltage. The uniformity of the transistors and inverters also allows us to create basic logic gates and a 4-bit full adder. With the help of a hard mask technology and pre-deposition annealing process, two-dimensional single-crystal molybdenum disulfide n-type transistors and one-dimensional aligned carbon nanotube p-type transistors can be integrated to create a mixed-dimensional complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor technology.

papers.title: Interpretable distance-resolved graph learning for cancer gene priority screening
papers.abstract: Systematic screening for cancer genes (CGs) is still a central goal in precision oncology, yet integrating sparse and spatially dispersed oncogenic signals to identify testable candidates remains challenging. Here we present CGMap, an interpretable graph-learning framework that uses a width-oriented parallel architecture to prioritize potential CGs from biomolecular networks and trace mechanistic cues. By constructing distance-resolved channels, CGMap localizes spatially dispersed CG signals across multiple topological scales while avoiding representation homogenization. A global diffusion module quantifies gene cooperativity along pathway contexts and yields traceable virtual interactions that map predictions to potential regulatory hypotheses, providing intrinsic interpretability for model decisions. Across multiple biomolecular networks in a pan-cancer setting, CGMap analysed 12,022 genes, consistently outperformed existing methods while remaining computationally efficient and prioritized 70 reliable candidates, including those previously unannotated in established databases. Importantly, the prioritized candidates were associated with the suppression of tumour-related phenotypes, including reduced cell proliferation, migration and invasion, along with a shift of epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-related features toward a non-mesenchymal state, as supported by parallel loss-of-function assays across cancer and non-malignant cell lines. Wang et al. propose CGMap, a distance-resolved graph-learning framework that maps dispersed oncogenic signals into structured priorities, narrowing the cancer gene candidate space and establishing an interpretable path from hypotheses to practical validation.
