papers.abstract: Superb-seq integrates CRISPR–Cas9, T7 in situ transcription and scRNA-seq to capture genome edits and gene expression in single cells.

papers.title: A CD7-targeted AAV variant enables efficient T and NK cell engineering in vivo
papers.abstract: Adeno-associated virus (AAV) vectors have been applied for precise genome engineering in human T cells but poor tropism restricts their efficiency and translational potential. Here, through directed evolution of the AAV6 capsid in primary human T cells, we identified a family of variants containing an APR motif at residues 455–457. The lead candidate, AAV.APR31, enabled robust transduction of primary T and NK cells at nearly 100–1,000-fold lower doses than AAV6 and outperformed the human T cell-tropic capsid AAV-hT7. CRISPR screening identified CD7 as a lineage-specific entry enhancer alongside the canonical AAVR pathway and structural analysis suggested that the APR motif facilitates CD7 engagement. Unlike existing delivery systems confined to one engineering mode, AAV.APR31 enabled transient transgene delivery, site-specific knock-in and transposon integration in human T and NK cells, generating CAR-T cells functionally equivalent to lentiviral vector-manufactured products. Systemic administration of AAV.APR31-generated CAR-T cells in vivo resulted in potent tumor control in hematologic and solid tumor mouse models. Adeno-associated virus vectors targeted to CD7 enable T and NK cell engineering in vivo.

papers.title: Thermally programmable metamaterials via bimaterial beam architectures
papers.abstract: Thermoresponsive metamaterials offer a powerful route to adaptive mechanical systems, but broad and reversible thermal programming of force-displacement behavior and multistability has remained elusive. Here, we introduce a general design paradigm for thermally programmable multistable metastructures based on bimaterial beam cells that harness coefficients of thermal expansion (CTE) mismatch to reconfigure mechanical states. The unit cells are engineered to undergo thermally triggered transitions between monostable and bistable regimes, enabling direct control of local stability and snap-through behavior. Hierarchical assembly of these cells with designed thickness gradients translates this cell-level tunability into system-level programmability, yielding metastructures with temperature-controlled mechanical responses, deformation sequences, and energy landscapes. A predictive theoretical framework captures the thermomechanical response across operating conditions and agrees with experiments. We demonstrate precise thermal tuning of multistability and energy absorption, and further showcase programmed mechanical information encoding and temperature-dependent decryption as representative functionalities. This strategy expands the design space of programmable metamaterials and establishes a scalable platform for adaptive soft robotics, shape-morphing architectures, flexible electronics, and reconfigurable impact-mitigation systems. Thermoresponsive metamaterials are key to design adaptive mechanical systems, yet achieving broad, reversible thermal programming of force-displacement behavior remains challenging. Here, the authors present a design paradigm using bimaterial beam cells with coefficients of thermal expansion mismatch, enabling temperature-controlled multistability and energy absorption, advancing applications in soft robotics, shape-morphing architectures, and flexible electronics.

papers.title: Thermal-regulating smart windows for a sustainable future
papers.abstract: Thermal-regulating smart windows are emerging as key technologies for improving building energy efficiency while preserving daylight access and visibility. Conventional windows allow excessive solar heat gain, heat loss, condensation, and frost, which increase energy demand. This review examines thermal-regulating smart windows from an integrated perspective, focusing on the coordinated combination of heating, cooling, and dynamic optical modulation under changing seasonal conditions. Active approaches, including Joule heating, dielectric heating, and thermoelectric cooling, provide controllable surface heating or cooling. Conversely, passive strategies, including low-emissivity coating, solar-thermal conversion, radiative cooling, and evaporative cooling, regulate heat exchange without continuous energy input. Chromic technologies, including electrochromic, mechanochromic, thermochromic, and photochromic systems, enable adaptive control of solar and thermal radiation. By comparing these mechanisms based on their complementary seasonal roles, spectral selectivity, energy requirements, and integration potential, this review differentiates multifunctional thermal management from single-function smart-window concepts. Applications in buildings, vehicles, greenhouses, and wearable or flexible devices are also discussed. Finally, we identify key perspectives for next-generation windows, including multifunctional integration, independent spectral control, climate-responsive operation, scalable manufacturing, long-term durability, life-cycle sustainability, and real-building validation. These advances could enable adaptive glazing platforms that simultaneously manage heat, light, comfort, and energy under dynamic environmental and seasonal conditions. This Review differentiates multifunctional thermal management from single-function smart-window concepts. Applications in buildings, vehicles, greenhouses, and wearable or flexible devices are discussed.

papers.title: Life-cycle assessment and exergy analysis of enzymatic polyethylene terephthalate recycling
papers.abstract: Plastic recycling and upcycling are effective strategies for mitigating plastic pollution. Rapid advances in protein engineering have enabled the optimization of natural polyethylene terephthalate (PET) hydrolases, thereby accelerating the industrialization of enzymatic PET recycling. In this study, process modeling, life-cycle assessment, and exergy analysis were conducted for an enzymatic PET recycling process based on China’s energy structure. Compared with virgin petrochemical production, the enzymatic recycling process reduced global warming potential (GWP) by 17%. Abiotic resource depletion intensity was reduced by only 2% owing to the inclusion of the resource value of waste PET itself. Sensitivity analysis identified the key factors influencing the sustainability of enzymatic PET recycling, and subsequent process optimization achieved a 36% reduction in GWP and a 17% reduction in resource depletion intensity. These findings identify the major process flows and critical operating parameters contributing to resource depletion and environmental impacts, thereby providing valuable guidance for improving the sustainability of enzymatic PET recycling technologies. Zheng-Jie Qian and colleagues model the enzymatic PET recycling process through life-cycle assessment and exergy analysis, identifying the key factors influencing its sustainability. The optimized process reduces global warming potential and resource depletion intensity by 31% and 17%, respectively, compared to the petrochemical route.

papers.title: Nanochannel-stabilized Donnan–water-state coupling enables stable solar evaporation of hypersaline brines
papers.abstract: Solar-driven interfacial evaporators provide a promising pathway for sustainable desalination and resource recovery from hypersaline brines, yet their performance is often limited by inefficient interfacial energy utilization and salt crystallization fouling. Although interfacial water-state regulation and charged-interface-mediated salt management have been explored separately, their coupled physicochemical interactions remain insufficiently understood. Multiscale channels were fabricated by in situ Schiff-base polymerization of electrospun membranes to increase the fraction of intermediate water and immobilize sulfonate groups for Donnan-effect-mediated ion regulation. This coupled structure–charge design promotes vapor generation while alleviating interfacial salt accumulation at the evaporation surface. The resulting evaporator achieves stable evaporation rates exceeding 1.30 kg m−2 h−1 in 15 wt% brines over nine consecutive 12 h cycles under 1 sun irradiation, reaching 2.04 kg m−2 h−1 under reduced pressure. This work provides a mechanistic bridge between nanoconfinement, water-state regulation and Donnan-effect-mediated ion redistribution, providing a design principle for durable solar desalination and brine concentration under hypersaline conditions.

papers.title: Multi-timescale neural adaptation disturbances in major depression
papers.abstract: Major depression is usually characterized in terms of momentary abnormalities, such as negative bias or emotional blunting, derived largely from paradigms that measure only the initial response to a stimulus. Yet depressive experience in daily life is repetitive and cumulative. Here we show that neural adaptation to repeated negative stimuli is altered in major depression and provides information beyond initial reactivity. Using a repeated negative-stimulus paradigm, we quantify adaptation at micro and macro timescales from electroencephalographic recordings in 28 patients with major depression and 34 healthy controls, measuring event-related potentials, frontal theta activity, and large-scale traveling-wave propagation. Relative to controls, patients with major depression show reduced micro-scale attenuation of the frontal late positive potential and theta activity, alongside macro-scale increases in the late positive potential and decreases in theta power. Within-participant decoding shows weaker First-versus-Second neural differentiation in major depression and lower recoverable repetition-state information. Thus, repeated exposure reveals neural dynamics beyond initial reactivity, particularly reduced rapid recalibration in major depression.

papers.title: Priming parallel fiber signals drive plasticity in the in vivo cerebellum
papers.abstract: The cerebellar role in motor adaptation rests – according to the foundational theories of Marr and Albus – on the detection of (near)coincident activity between parallel fiber (PF) and climbing fiber (CF) inputs onto Purkinje cells. Supported by numerous in vitro studies, these theories predict synaptic adaptation based on temporal precision detected in time windows of ≤ 150 ms. These predictions have not been tested in intact animals. Using two-photon imaging from cerebellar Crus I in intact, awake mice, and dendritic calcium signals as a measure of PF response strength, we show here that coincident stimulation of PF and CF inputs does not readily initiate plasticity. Rather, long-term depression (LTD) is reliably evoked by prolonged constant or ramping PF activity that precedes a CF burst by 400 ms. In Crus I, a lobule involved in sensory-prediction tasks, prolonged PF activity may present expected sensory contexts and prime synapses for plasticity supervised by CF signals.

papers.title: InferPloidy enables CNV guided tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery from single cell RNA sequencing
papers.abstract: Identifying malignant cells in single-cell gene expression data is essential for understanding tumor heterogeneity, but existing computational methods can be slow and perform inconsistently across datasets. Here, we present InferPloidy, a framework that combines graph-based cell grouping with iterative probabilistic modeling to distinguish cells with normal and altered chromosome copy numbers using profiles generated by InferCNV. Across breast, lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancer datasets, the evaluated workflow reduces computation time by up to two orders of magnitude compared with existing tools and improves agreement with published cell annotations. This classification supports the identification of established therapeutic targets and candidate cell surface markers associated with tumor subtypes. The low proportion of unclassified cells helps preserve information for downstream analyses of gene expression differences and tumor population characteristics. These findings support InferPloidy as an efficient framework for tumor cell stratification and biomarker discovery within the evaluated workflow. Its performance with inputs from other copy number inference methods requires further validation.

papers.title: Transferring active inference to newly encountered prism-shifted environments
papers.abstract: Rapid adaptability to sudden changes in environmental contingencies is a hallmark of biological intelligence. However, how animals flexibly adapt to novel environments remains largely unclear. To investigate the brain’s generalizability, this work focuses on prism adaptation, a classical visuomotor phenomenon reflecting rapid recalibration of perception–action coupling. Modeling is conducted based on canonical neural networks that instantiate active inference at the circuit level. Namely, we develop canonical neural networks equipped with multiple policy matrices in parallel, enabling the reuse of previously acquired sensorimotor knowledge. We demonstrate that the proposed model recapitulates key features of prism adaptation in an arm-reaching task, including rapid error reduction and after-effects following prism removal. Networks employing policies pretrained for different target positions adapt substantially faster than naive networks that relearn policies from scratch. These results suggest a biologically plausible mechanism by which neural circuits flexibly reuse prior knowledge to support rapid adaptation.

papers.title: Separating energy and entropy contributions in two-dimensional melting
papers.abstract: How two-dimensional materials melt shapes the stability of advanced coatings and nanoscale devices, yet the fundamental rules governing this transition remain unresolved. While the existence of an intermediate hexatic phase is established, it is unclear whether melting proceeds via an abrupt first-order shift or a continuous transformation. Here we show that the melting pathway is governed by a universal competition between energy and entropy encoded in the curvature of the free energy. At relatively high temperatures, energy consistently imparts convex curvature, whereas entropy imparts non-convex curvature; a first-order transition occurs when the non-convex entropic contribution dominates. This balance distinguishes systems with low-temperature coexistence, where energy acquires non-convexity as entropy turns convex, sustaining abrupt melting to very low temperatures. Vibrational entropy drives the non-convex total entropic curvature, while configurational entropy switches character in tandem with defect proliferation. Our work establishes thermodynamic curvature as a predictive principle, offering a robust framework for interpreting and engineering phase behavior in two-dimensional systems. Two-dimensional melting underpins the stability of advanced nanomaterials, yet the rules governing whether it occurs abruptly or smoothly remain contested. By linking the curvature of the free energy to the interplay of energy and entropy, this work reveals a universal predictor: non-convex entropy drives abrupt transitions, while a shift in this balance explains why some systems retain first-order melting even at low temperatures.

papers.title: The health and economic impact of COVID-19 vaccine misinformation in Canada
papers.abstract: Ozawa et al. simulated the impact of misinformation in Canada on individuals delaying and refusing vaccination during the COVID-19 pandemic. They found that misinformation resulted in up to 4.7 million fewer people getting vaccinated, 273,000 more illnesses, 18,400 more hospitalizations, 3,210 more deaths and this cost $21 billion Canadian dollars in 2021.

papers.title: A bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an aromatic cyclopentadienide ring
papers.abstract: Five-membered rings are ubiquitous in non-planar π systems, but are typically neutral, non-aromatic or anti-aromatic. Now a bowl-shaped nanocarbon incorporating an anionic, aromatic cyclopentadienide ring has been prepared and found to exhibit unusual structural and electronic properties, enabling site-selective reactivity on its π surface for both covalent functionalization and metal coordination.

papers.title: Extension of coherence time beyond breakeven point using only drives and dissipation
papers.abstract: Quantum error correction aims to mitigate the loss of quantum information to the environment and is a central requirement for scalable quantum computing. Existing implementations are mainly based on measurement-based feedback, but constraints on read-out fidelity, hardware latency and system complexity can limit performance and scalability. Autonomous quantum error correction offers a complementary route based on engineered drives and dissipation, without repeated measurements or classical feedback. Here we implement an autonomous quantum error correction protocol, derived from quantum channel simulation, that repeatedly restores a photon-loss-corrupted logical qubit by transferring error information to ancilla qubits and resetting them. Unlike earlier demonstrations based on manifold stabilization through code-specific Hamiltonian and dissipation engineering, our approach is, in principle, applicable to arbitrary recovery maps. Using a binomial code encoded in a long-lived bosonic mode, we extend the logical qubit coherence time to 1.04 times that of the best physical qubit in the system. This result shows that drives and dissipation can extend the coherence time of an error-corrected bosonic logical qubit beyond the breakeven point. An autonomous quantum error correction protocol based on engineered drives and dissipation extends the coherence time of a bosonic logical qubit beyond that of the best physical qubit in the same system.

papers.title: Extending qubit lifetime beyond break-even and enhancing quantum sensing by autonomous quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Extending the lifetime of a logical quantum bit (qubit) beyond that of the best physical qubit available within the same system—the break-even point—is a prerequisite for building practical quantum computers. Previous demonstrations have crossed this threshold using active quantum error correction (QEC), which measures an error syndrome and then applies an adaptive correction. Reaching the break-even point with autonomous QEC, which removes the need for resource-intensive measurement and feedback, remains challenging. Here we demonstrate beyond-break-even autonomous error correction in a circuit quantum electrodynamics system. We encode a photonic logical qubit in a superconducting microwave cavity and protect it against photon loss using engineered dissipation. The protected logical qubit achieves a lifetime of about 2.0 ms, 18% longer than that of the best physical qubit available in the system. We then use the protocol to measure a small frequency shift, obtaining a metrological gain of 6.3 dB relative to the most robust Fock-state superposition. These results show that autonomous QEC not only represents a necessary step towards fault-tolerant quantum computation but also offers advantages for robust quantum sensing. A measurement-free quantum error-correction protocol is shown to extend the lifetime of a bosonic logical qubit beyond the best physical qubit in the same system. This also offers prospects for enhanced quantum sensing.

papers.title: 150 years proving fundamental science is worth the wait
papers.abstract: Founded in 1876, the Indian Association for the Cultivation of Science created an early space for Indians to pursue science. Its achievements offer valuable lessons for strengthening today’s research landscape in India.

papers.title: Cognitive grounding improves LLM simulation of collective human behavior
papers.abstract: The study shows that guiding AI agents with descriptions of how people make decisions in a supply-chain game helps agents reproduce collective human behavior.

papers.title: Assessing the carbon emissions and energy consumption of US hyperscale data centres
papers.abstract: The growing number of hyperscale data centres raises concerns about their environmental impacts. This study presents a facility-resolved attributional framework to assess the carbon footprint of hyperscale data centres in the USA using plant-level electricity-generation and emissions data.

papers.title: Unlocking sustainable thermoelectric generation with zinc antimonide
papers.abstract: Thermoelectric technologies must balance conversion efficiency with resource sustainability. Here the authors demonstrate that eco-friendly zinc antimonide (ZnSb) is a viable materials choice, delivering ~8% efficiency alongside exceptional cost-effectiveness.

papers.title: An open agentic AI co-scientist for clinical and biomedical discovery
papers.abstract: Biomedical research is constrained by the time and domain expertise required to analyze increasingly large and complex datasets. Here we present OpenScientist, an open-source agentic AI co-scientist designed to address this gap by investigating scientist-defined queries and generating verifiable, data-grounded analyses. OpenScientist was evaluated by domain experts across five biomedical case studies, completing analyses in minutes that otherwise would take months of human time and expertise. It accurately quantified Alzheimer’s blood biomarker performance, generated a plasma proteomic survival model that predicted survival in a hidden-evaluation cohort, proposed a reproducible mechanism linking tau pathology to altered lysosomal acidification, generated multiple myeloma hypotheses validated in an external cohort with attenuated signal in randomized controls, and demonstrated concordance with an independent human analysis in a blinded, prespecified proteomic comparison. These results support the use of OpenScientist to assist biomedical data analysis in concert with human experts. To support research involving sensitive clinical datasets, OpenScientist can operate in a fully air-gapped environment using open-source models for inference. OpenScientist demonstrates that open, auditable, agentic AI can support real-world clinical research by researching the literature, generating hypotheses, executing analyses, and generating insights from complex datasets.

papers.title: Interplay of duration and intensity
Sex differences in activity thresholds
Dual chain-of-thought AI‑PDCA framework for clinical history taking and documentation
papers.abstract: Clinical history-taking and documentation are foundational competencies in undergraduate medical training, yet scalable and individualized training tools remain limited. Large language model (LLM)-based systems provide automated practice opportunities but often lack structured medical reasoning, closed-loop instructional design, and integration into formal curricula. As part of a curriculum reform initiative, we constructed a clinical case repository, developed an artificial intelligence (AI)-integrated faculty Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) training framework supported by dual chain-of-thought (CoT)-driven LLMs, and evaluated the reliability of AI-based scoring against faculty assessment. We then conducted a retrospective observational analysis of routinely collected educational performance data from 135 undergraduate medical students enrolled in one of three existing instructional configurations: traditional instruction, AI-assisted training, or AI + PDCA training. Educational outcomes were assessed using standardized Objective Structured Clinical Examination (OSCE) assessments. The AI + PDCA configuration was associated with the highest OSCE performance in both history-taking and clinical documentation. Among the two AI-supported configurations, longitudinal mixed-effects modeling showed steeper learning trajectories in the AI + PDCA configuration than in the AI-assisted configuration. These findings suggest that integrating AI-derived learning analytics with faculty-guided instructional intervention may support a closed-loop educational model associated with favorable competency acquisition while maintaining human oversight. This framework offers a scalable approach for implementing trustworthy, competency-based AI-enhanced medical education in routine academic practice.

papers.title: STBI: dataset of over 12000 brain CT scans for machine learning in traumatic brain injury
papers.abstract: Publicly available traumatic brain injury (TBI) imaging datasets remain limited by the absence of longitudinal imaging, standardized annotations, and linked clinical outcomes. We developed and validated the Shiraz-TBI (STBI) dataset, a large-scale multimodal resource comprising 3602 patients, 12,155 serial non-contrast brain CT examinations, and 376,195 DICOM images, with all studies additionally available in NIfTI format. Radiologists generated structured annotations for intracranial hemorrhage subtypes, mass effect, midline shift, skull fractures, Marshall CT scores, and other imaging features, while temporal variables and time-to-surgery outcomes were derived. Internal validation by neurosurgeons demonstrated near-perfect inter-rater agreement (κ > 0.85 for most variables). A multimodal subset of 1259 patients includes demographic, clinical, laboratory, treatment, and functional outcome data. By integrating patient-level longitudinal chronologically ordered serial neuroimaging with standardized annotations, temporal information, and prognostic outcomes, STBI provides a publicly available, machine learning-ready resource for imaging analysis, disease progression modeling, prognostic prediction, and clinical decision support in TBI.

papers.title: Interpretable AI links routine clinical gout phenotypes to multi-omic signatures and divergent health trajectories
papers.abstract: Integrative frameworks that connect scalable clinical phenotypes with molecular mechanisms are needed to resolve disease heterogeneity. We developed and externally evaluated an interpretable gout clinical-subset framework using routine data from 21,235 participants across UK Biobank (UKB; n = 10,599), the multicentre Chinese GoutRe registry (n = 8617), and MIMIC-IV (n = 2019). Unsupervised learning on six prespecified routine laboratory variables identified three subsets: C1, a low-burden state with preserved reserve; C2, a urate-metabolic inflammatory state with the greatest recurrence liability and a greater cardiometabolic and hepatic comorbidity burden; and C3, a state characterized by systemic vulnerability and higher mortality. In UKB, death-competing recurrence analysis showed a higher recurrence incidence for C2 versus C1 (subdistribution hazard ratio [sHR] 1.896, 95% CI 1.710–2.101), whereas C3 did not differ from C1 (sHR 0.994, 95% CI 0.887–1.112). A six-variable CRT model reconstructed the locked subset labels using nested 10-fold out-of-fold evaluation in UKB and external application without retraining in GoutRe and MIMIC-IV. One-versus-rest AUCs were 0.965/0.945/0.980 in UKB, 0.906/0.914/0.953 in GoutRe, and 0.912/0.898/0.962 in MIMIC-IV for C1/C2/C3, respectively. Genetic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses supported distinct urate-inflammatory and systemic-vulnerability axes, although the C3 senescence-related genetic signal was nominal and requires replication. Routine laboratory data can identify gout clinical subsets with distinct molecular profiles and patterns of recurrence and mortality; whether these subsets can guide clinical management requires prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Machine learning-based Taylor cone analysis for electrospinning process-window identification and cell-laden nanofiber scaffold fabrication
papers.abstract: Electrospinning is a powerful biofabrication technique for constructing fibrous scaffolds that mimic extracellular matrix architectures. However, the process is highly nonlinear and involves strongly coupled parameters, making fiber architecture and biological performance difficult to control empirically and limits reproducibility. Most ML studies still focus on static correlations between processing parameters and outcomes rather than on dynamic modeling of electrospinning evolution and regulation, thereby hindering real-time, precise process control. Here, we establish a data-driven framework that links process parameters, Taylor cone geometry, and nanofiber/cell outcomes through high-speed imaging and ML. A custom image-processing pipeline is developed to automatically extract cone angle, height, and width from in situ images with improved accuracy via a rotating-ray–based geometric algorithm. Using datasets collected from three representative polymer systems PVDF, PVB, and PEO, RF models outperform SVM and MDL, achieving moderate-to-good prediction of Taylor cone descriptors (R2 ≈ 0.57-0.83) across varied voltages, flow rates, and needle–collector distances. We further extend this framework to PEO-based cell electrospinning. By correlating predicted cone geometries with experimentally measured viability of 293 T cells and umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells, we identify a Taylor cone ‘safe window’ that simultaneously stabilizes jet formation and preserves cell survival (>95%). Guided by this window, a bilayer cell-laden scaffold comprising a PVB support layer and a PEO–cell layer is fabricated with improved process robustness. This enables stable delivery of high-density, highly viable cells and facilitates the fabrication of three-dimensional cell-laden nanofiber scaffolds. Overall, this ML-guided Taylor cone analysis strategy provides a quantitative framework for process-window identification in polymer and cell electrospinning, and may support future integration with real-time monitoring, online inference, and closed-loop control in intelligent biofabrication.

papers.title: In vitro human arteriole microphysiological system with physiological scale and functional vasoactivity enabled by a dual material fabrication strategy
papers.abstract: Arterioles are the principal regulators of vascular tone, yet their small size and deep tissue location hinder direct investigation of their roles in microvascular disease. To address this, we developed a human microphysiological arteriole distinguished from previous models by simultaneously integrating an arteriole-scale caliber (∼200 μm), continuous perfusion culture, and active vasoactivity. The vessel autonomously forms and matures under flow through a spatially regulated coating strategy that eliminates post-seeding manipulation. The engineered vessels exhibit vasoactivity in response to both biochemical and metabolic cues. In particular, the metabolic response is a physiological form of vasoactivity rarely reproduced in previous in vitro systems. Leveraging the ease of sample harvesting, proteomic profiling and mechanical testing indicated that flow-induced maturation promotes a contractile phenotype consistent with arteriogenesis-like remodeling. This accessible platform provides a versatile tool for studying arteriolar physiology and microvascular remodeling.

papers.title: Microfiber-reinforced GelMA hydrogels with tunable Poisson’s ratio enhance chondrogenesis under dynamic loading
papers.abstract: Hydrogels are widely used in cartilage tissue engineering but fail to replicate key mechanical features of native cartilage, particularly its near-zero Poisson’s ratio, which governs lateral deformation under load. Here, we demonstrate that matching deformation behavior in addition to compressive stiffness may contribute to the enhanced chondrogenic response under physiological mechanical stimulation. Human articular chondrocytes were encapsulated in GelMA hydrogels reinforced with melt electrowritten scaffolds engineered to independently tune the effective compressive modulus and Poisson’s ratio. Reinforcement increased the compressive modulus from 33 kPa (neat GelMA) to 245–345 kPa, while reducing the Poisson’s ratio from 0.42 to 0.12 in hybrid designs, approaching native cartilage values. Under dynamic loading, constructs matching both properties showed significantly higher expression of the chondrogenic markers SOX9 and ACAN compared to both neat GelMA and lattice-reinforced constructs, which exhibited a physiologically relevant compressive modulus but a higher Poisson’s ratio, along with increased COL2A1 expression compared to the latter specifically. Histological analysis confirmed enhanced and more homogeneous extracellular matrix deposition, with up to 76% GAG and 36% collagen type II coverage. These findings suggest that lateral deformation behavior, alongside compressive stiffness, contributes to directing chondrocyte matrix synthesis under mechanical stimulation, establishing Poisson’s ratio as an important and previously underexplored design parameter in cartilage tissue engineering, and providing a framework for engineering mechanically instructive biomaterials for load-bearing tissues.

papers.title: A fibrochondrogenic polymer fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold with graded architecture, mechanics and composition for meniscus repair
papers.abstract: Developing biomaterials for meniscal repair that reproduce native tissue biomechanics while providing pro-regenerative bioinstructive cues remains challenging. To address this need, we developed a zonal biomimetic fibre-reinforced collagen-based scaffold designed to recreate key microstructural and mechanical features of the meniscus and support fibrochondrogenesis in vitro. A multilayer scaffold was fabricated with a circumferential electrospun (ES) fibre core composed of polycaprolactone (PCL), polylactic acid (PLA), or a hybrid PCL/polyvinyl alcohol (PVA)/PLA reinforcement, together with radially oriented melt-electrowritten (MEW) PCL intermediate zones and multidirectional MEW PCL superficial zones, followed by integration with a collagen I-chondroitin-6-sulphate matrix. Fibre-reinforced scaffolds combining MEW PCL with the hybrid ES PCL-PVA-PLA reinforcement framework demonstrated the best-balanced biomechanical performance, achieving mechanical properties within the range reported for native meniscus under comparable test conditions, including tensile, compressive and complex moduli of 140.62 ± 26.31 MPa, 723.21 ± 147.09 kPa and 25.91 ± 1.21 kPa, respectively. Moreover, human bone marrow-derived mesenchymal stem cells cultured on this scaffold exhibited enhanced sulphated glycosaminoglycan production, balanced type I and type II collagen expression, and fibrocartilage-like extracellular matrix deposition with the reinforced architecture supporting deeper and more uniform matrix formation. Together, these findings support zonal fibre reinforcement as a design strategy to integrate mechanical fidelity with scaffold-dependent modulation of hMSC fibrochondrogenesis in vitro, identifying the hybrid PCL-PVA-PLA-reinforced scaffold as a best-balanced configuration for meniscal repair.

papers.title: Phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover enables rate-matched nitrate-sulfate paired electrolysis for ammonium persulfate synthesis
papers.abstract: Electrochemical conversion of nitrate-rich wastewater to valuable ammonium salts is promising. We report a phosphorus-mediated reverse hydrogen spillover mechanism that synchronizes nitrate-reduction and sulfate-oxidation kinetics, enabling direct electrosynthesis of ammonium persulfate.

papers.abstract: Characterizing the energy spectrum of semiconductor quantum dots is essential for spin qubit operation but remains challenging across broad parameter ranges. Here, the authors use molecular spectroscopy to map one and two electron energy levels in a silicon double quantum dot as functions of detuning, tunnel coupling, and magnetic field.

papers.title: Cytotoxic drugs and bispecific T cell engagers synergize to rewire host immunity and elicit polyclonal antitumor T cell responses

Here, the authors show that cytotoxic therapies reprogram the tumor microenvironment and augment the antitumor immunity induced by TAA×CD28 bispecifics.

papers.title: Exercise-induced 3-oxoLCA promotes antitumor immunity with CD8⁺ T-cell involvement in colorectal cancer
papers.abstract: Exercise is associated with reduced colorectal cancer risk, but the circulating factors linking exercise to antitumor immunity remain unclear. Here we show that plasma collected within one hour after exercise suppresses colorectal tumor growth in mice. Metabolic profiling identifies 3-oxolithocholic acid, a bile acid metabolite that increases after acute exercise in mice and humans. Oral administration of this metabolite suppresses tumor growth and is associated with increased tumor infiltration by CD8+T cells, which can kill cancer cells, and altered immune-response markers. Exploratory single-cell analysis reveals differences in gene activity related to immune function and metabolism in these cells. Depletion of CD8+T cells attenuates, but does not eliminate, tumor suppression. These findings identify an exercise-responsive metabolite that promotes antitumor immunity in a mouse model of colorectal cancer and support a contribution from CD8+T cells, while leaving additional mechanisms unresolved.

papers.title: Maternal polystyrene nanoplastics exposure compromises ovarian reserve by disrupting oocyte adhesion and granulosa cell homeostasis
papers.abstract: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs), as an emerging environmental contaminant, have attracted growing concern owing to their widespread distribution and bioaccumulation capacity. This study investigated the effects of maternal PS-NPs exposure on primordial follicle (PF) assembly in offspring, a process critical for lifelong ovarian reserve establishment. Using a mouse model combined with single-cell RNA sequencing, we characterized the impact of PS-NPs on oocytes and granulosa cells during early folliculogenesis. We demonstrate that PS-NPs undergo intergenerational transfer, crossing the placental barrier to accumulate preferentially in the ovarian cortex of offspring. PS-NPs exposure significantly impaired cyst breakdown and PF assembly, resulting in a marked reduction in ovarian reserve. Mechanistically, PS-NPs enhanced intercellular adhesion within germline cysts by activating the JNK/WNT-β-catenin signaling, causing cyst dissociation defects. Also, PS-NPs suppressed the FAK/PI3K signaling, inhibiting granulosa cell proliferation and inducing apoptosis, ultimately impeding PF formation. This work provides a scientific basis for understanding nanoplastic-associated ovarian disorders, including premature ovarian insufficiency.

papers.title: Mechanisms of β ↔ γ transformations in tin induce asymmetric kinetics
papers.abstract: Solid-solid phase transformation mechanisms need to be understood to establish suitable kinetic laws. Here, the β-Sn  ↔ γ-Sn phase transformations are investigated at different strain rates at 300 K. On one side, single crystals have been statically compressed and characterized using in situ x-ray diffraction. Multiple transformation cycles were performed in diamond anvil cells to measure their conditions and the associated microstructures. (101)β∣∣(110)γ and $${[10\bar{1}]}_{\beta }| | {[1\bar{1}1]}_{\gamma }$$ orientation relationships (OR) between β-Sn and γ-Sn are observed in most cases, for both direct and reverse transformations. An atomic martensitic transformation mechanism, associated with self-accommodation, is proposed to account for these OR and variant selection. However, γ-Sn  → β-Sn reversion also presents features that are consistent with recrystallization in β-Sn or a massive transformation. On the other side, time-resolved (22 μ s scale) dynamic diamond anvil cell experiments have been carried out. They show that while β-Sn  → γ-Sn transformation is fast (Pβ→γ=10.9  ± 0.2, insensitive to strain rate), reversion pressure Pγ→β varies with strain rate, from 9.4 ± 0.8 GPa to 6.35 ± 0.7 GPa. Moreover, timescales of β-Sn formation and subsequent recrystallization/growth in this phase can be distinguished. A different kinetic description needs to be used for direct and reverse transitions. Solid-solid phase transformation mechanisms need to be understood to establish suitable kinetic laws. Here, the beta-phase Sn  ↔ gamma-phase Sn phase transformation is investigated at different strain rates at 300 K.

papers.title: Global weight deep equilibrium attention for numerical simulations on unstructured meshes
papers.abstract: Graph-based neural networks have emerged as efficient and versatile surrogates for mesh-based numerical simulations. However, achieving high predictive accuracy remains challenging due to over-smoothing, under-reaching during message passing, and disregard for mesh connectivity. To address this, we propose Global Weight Deep Equilibrium Attention (GDEA). GDEA constructs a sparse global weight matrix from mesh connectivity via the direct stiffness method, introducing an inductive bias toward diagonal dominance. We apply the resulting matrix iteratively until convergence, allowing information to propagate globally without adding extra message-passing layers. We formulate the iterative process as a Deep Equilibrium Model (DEQ) to reduce memory consumption, and we use Anderson acceleration to speed convergence. Extensive experiments across multiple numerical simulation datasets, including the newly introduced Deformed ABC dataset with diverse geometries, materials, and boundary conditions, demonstrate that GDEA outperforms other methods on Deformed ABC while remaining competitive on established benchmarks. An accurate surrogate model that can handle diverse design configurations can facilitate efficient early-stage design exploration. Junghun Lee and Conrad Tucker present Global Weight Deep Equilibrium Attention, which builds a global weight matrix from mesh connectivity and propagates information via equilibrium iterations, reducing over-smoothing and under-reaching. Their model outperforms existing surrogates on Deformed ABC, a new diverse dataset, and stays competitive on established benchmarks.

papers.title: Low-frequency phase in early visual cortex gates prefrontal influence on perception
papers.abstract: Perceptual experience depends on interactions between sensory inputs and top-down predictions, yet how intrinsic cortical rhythms shape this interaction remains unclear. Here, we use rare human intracranial recordings from the prefrontal and early visual cortices during bistable motion perception, including two patients with simultaneous coverage of both regions, to investigate how oscillatory phase shapes perceptual outcomes. We show that prestimulus low-frequency phase in early visual cortex and prestimulus theta phase in prefrontal cortex are each associated with subsequent perceptual reports. Crucially, directed connectivity and cross-frequency coupling analyses, conducted in the two patients with simultaneous prefrontal and early visual cortex coverage, show that prefrontal theta phase modulates visual high-frequency activity preferentially at specific phases of early visual low-frequency activity, consistent with a probabilistic, phase-dependent gating of top-down influence. A computational model implementing low-frequency-phase–dependent gating successfully reproduces these empirical dynamics, suggesting a unifying mechanism by which cortical state constrains top-down modulation. Together, these findings provide preliminary human intracranial evidence that ongoing low-frequency phase in early visual cortex is associated with the efficacy of top-down influence from prefrontal cortex, and thereby with perceptual interpretation under ambiguity.

papers.title: ADAMTS7 impairs endothelial angiogenic function via suppressing POSTN-mediated VEGFR2 activation in pre-eclampsia
papers.abstract: Angiogenic imbalance drives endothelial dysfunction in pre-eclampsia (PE). Here, the authors show the metalloprotease ADAMTS7 is elevated in the circulation of PE patients and impairs endothelial angiogenic function, suggesting the ADAMTS7/POSTN/VEGFR2 axis as a therapeutic target for PE.

papers.title: Artificial skyglow at night disrupts chronobiology and physiology in Crassostrea gigas
papers.abstract: Artificial skyglow at night (ASAN) is widespread in coastal environments, with consequences beginning to be highlighted but still understudied. Long-term ASAN field studies are needed to better understand the real challenge that nocturnal light poses to coastal organisms. To fill this gap, we investigated during one year in Arcachon Bay (France), ASAN’s impact on the oysters’ biological rhythms and major physiological parameters: behavior, growth, and gametogenesis. Results show that ASAN affects oysters’ behavioral valve activity rhythms, whether they are directly driven by light cycles (daily, lunar, and annual) or not (tidal and semi-lunar), suggesting a disruption of the oyster’s internal clock functioning. Our study also reveals that ASAN affects oyster physiology at the annual scale by inducing a phase advance in body weight and shell length growth, and gametogenetic cycle. These chronobiological and physiological effects of ASAN could lead to a disruption of the oyster’s fitness.

papers.title: Circulating HSPCs enhance their self-renewal by augmenting the endocytosis and lysosomal acidity via MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis
papers.abstract: Human circulating hematopoietic stem/progenitor cells (cHSPCs) in steady-state blood are a rare, underutilized resource limited by poor ex vivo expansion and unclear regulation. Using an immune-cell screening platform, we found that monocytes most effectively promote cHSPC expansion while preserving long-term hematopoietic reconstitution in serial transplantation. Mechanistically, cHSPCs engage the MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A axis to enhance endocytosis and lysosomal acidification, which upregulates CD34+CXCR4+ cells, reduces ROS, stabilizes HIF-1α, and maintains glycolytic activity and stemness. Monocyte co-culture or pathway agonizts (MIF, EN6) also expanded HSPCs from cord blood, bone marrow, and poor-graft-function patient samples. Thus, cHSPC self-renewal is driven by an MIF-(CXCR4_CD74)-ATP6V1A-dependent mechanism modulating endocytosis, lysosomal function, and metabolism. This offers a universal expansion strategy for diverse clinical sources, including steady-state peripheral blood, cord blood, and functionally compromised hematopoietic cells.

papers.title: In planta -specific transcriptional regulatory circuit regulates expression of MoHTR1 , a nuclear effector gene of Magnaporthe oryzae
papers.abstract: During host-pathogen interactions, fungal pathogens secrete effectors into host cells to manipulate the host immune system and facilitate infection. Although many effector genes are highly expressed during infection stages, there is limited information on the mechanisms regulating their in planta expression. Here, we characterize the promoter of MoHTR1, a nuclear effector gene of the rice blast pathogen, to elucidate its in planta-specific expression. Using promoter deletion and mutation analyses, we identified a core cis-element (TATTTCGT) within the MoHTR1 promoter, designated the in planta inducible (IPI) element, which is crucial for in planta-specific expression. The IPI element is responsible for the expression of not only MoHTR1, but also Slp1, a known effector gene. Furthermore, the IPI element enables the in planta expression of MobZIP14, a gene specifically expressed during vegetative growth. The IPI element plays a critical role in fungal virulence by enabling MoHTR1 expression. Bioinformatic and DNA-protein interaction analyses revealed that RGS1, a transcription factor containing a winged-helix binding domain, acts as a transcriptional regulator of MoHTR1 by directly binding to the IPI element. Our findings provide insights into the regulatory mechanisms driving the in planta-specific expression of fungal effector genes.

papers.title: Amyloid pathology compresses dynamic range and degrades spatial coding in an Alzheimer’s mouse model
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) disrupts neural circuits vital for memory and cognition. Using two-photon calcium imaging in behaving 5xFAD mice, we examined how amyloid pathology alters hippocampal CA1 activity and spatial coding. We found elevated baseline activity but reduced locomotion-driven firing, leading to a diminished neuronal dynamic range. To our knowledge, this is the first direct experimental evidence for reduced dynamic range in an AD model. These abnormalities were strongest near amyloid plaques and became more widespread with age. We also observed altered network synchrony, degraded spatial coding, and increased neuronal response variability. Furthermore, place fields emerged more slowly in both familiar and novel environments, indicating impaired recall and learning. By showing a link between local plaque pathology and impaired flexible modulation of CA1 activity and progressive deficits in spatial memory coding, our study offers new insights into the circuit basis of cognitive decline in AD.

papers.title: Critical dynamics govern the evolution of political regimes
papers.abstract: Political regimes lack a stable endpoint: they shift between more and less democratic configurations over time, as illustrated by historical democratic waves and recent backsliding. We analyse the historical trajectories of countries within a two-dimensional regime space derived from the principal components of the Varieties of Democracy dataset. We observe dynamics consistent with weak non-ergodicity, unfolding in an effective landscape of sparse and shifting basins of stability. Step sizes and sojourn times follow heavy-tailed distributions near the critical regime where mean values diverge, pointing to intermittent and heterogeneous regime change. A continuous time random walk model reproduces the average dynamics and trajectory-to-trajectory variability of the last three decades. The temporal evolution of the ergodicity breaking parameter recovers waves of democratisation and periods of heightened global political divergence, demonstrating the framework’s diagnostic potential. These results suggest that political regime evolution follows universal stochastic principles while remaining punctuated by unique historical pathways.

papers.title: Author Correction: Shear-induced Fickian yet non-Gaussian diffusion in athermal jammed matter
Trait absorption association with ketamine’s benefits and drug-context interactions in treatment-resistant depression: exploratory results from the MUSIK randomized clinical trial
papers.abstract: Garel et al. explore the influence of the personality trait absorption in the MUSIK trial which administered 181 doses of ketamine, with either music or mindfulness, for treatment-resistant depression. Higher absorption is associated with larger antidepressant effects, reduced suicidality, and more mystical experiences, especially with music-based support.

papers.title: Learning uncertainty fields for joint brain stroke diagnosis and intrinsic lesion localization in CT and MRI
papers.abstract: Early stroke changes can be difficult to detect and localize on neuroimaging, particularly when lesion boundaries are indistinct. We developed the Dynamic Fuzzy Encoder Network (DFE-Net), which uses learnable fuzzy membership fields to represent spatial uncertainty and jointly classify stroke and localize lesions. We evaluated the model on a multicentre computed tomography (CT) cohort comprising 6650 patients and 8873 images and a separate magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) cohort comprising 67 patients and 615 images. Training and testing were performed separately within each modality. DFE-Net achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.974 and an F1 score of 0.897 on CT, and corresponding values of 0.978 and 0.879 on MRI. In the CT cohort, lesion localization against expert annotations yielded a Dice score of 0.70. MRI localization was assessed using gradient-derived pseudo-targets because expert lesion masks were unavailable. Expected calibration error was ~0.022 in both cohorts, and the model contained 0.20 million parameters. These results support joint diagnosis and spatial localization with a compact model, while prospective validation and expert-annotated MRI evaluation remain necessary.

papers.title: Learning health system frameworks and the integration of artificial intelligence and data science in United States health care: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Learning Health Systems (LHSs) use routinely collected data to generate evidence that informs practice through continuous learning cycles. Artificial intelligence (AI) and data science may strengthen this model, but how LHS frameworks and AI applications relate remains unclear. We mapped LHS frameworks and their components and examined how AI and data science are integrated. Searches identified U.S.-based, English-language studies published January 2007–August 2025; two reviewers independently screened and extracted data, resolving disagreements by consensus. We included 54 framework studies (24 [44%] conceptual adaptations; 30 [56%] real-world implementations) and 30 AI/data science studies. Five components recurred across the frameworks: data infrastructure and interoperability, governance and stakeholder engagement, learning and improvement cycles, evidence generation and translation, and equity and ethics. Relative to framework studies, AI studies less often addressed governance and stakeholder engagement (17% vs 35%) or equity (13% vs 22%), emphasizing computational over organizational functions. Most AI studies (27/30) focused on the data-to-knowledge phase; only three extended to knowledge-to-practice, and none described practice-to-data feedback with post-deployment outcomes informing model updating. AI applications capture only part of the LHS vision, concentrating on knowledge generation with less attention to the organizational and feedback mechanisms needed to translate insights into practice and sustain learning.

papers.title: Measurement fidelity and external validation of automated breast DCE-MRI segmentation
papers.abstract: Automated breast dynamic contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging (DCE-MRI) segmentation could facilitate quantitative tumor measurement, but geometric overlap alone does not establish the fidelity of mask-derived measurements. We developed an enhancement-aware three-dimensional MedNeXt framework with gated skip fusion and boundary supervision and evaluated it in a retrospective multi-cohort design spanning locked internal testing, source-held-out assessment, retrospective external validation, and radiologist review. Measurement fidelity was the primary endpoint. Across 521 paired internal-test and DUKE cases, median errors were 9.7% for tumor volume, 1.8 mm for 3D maximum surface diameter, and 10.2% for operational enhancement-defined volume, with corresponding ICCs of 0.97, 0.80, and 0.97. Median Dice was 0.831 internally and 0.823 in the DUKE source-held-out stratum, and was 0.812 and 0.806 in the BC-MRI-SEG and public BreastDCEDL_AMBL retrospective external-validation cohorts, respectively, using the frozen checkpoint without external-label tuning. No major correction was required for 78 of 80 masks in the blinded two-reader review. In 276 paired response-analysis cases, AUROC was 0.732 with automatic geometry and 0.757 with expert geometry (difference, −0.025; 95% CI, −0.095 to 0.045); discrimination non-inferiority was not demonstrated. These findings support automated segmentation as a starting point for radiologist-supervised retrospective quantitative research within the evaluated cohorts, while distinguishing measurement fidelity from downstream predictive equivalence.

papers.title: The patient in the conversation
papers.abstract: The translational promise of biomedical technologies often becomes clearer when viewed from the perspective of the intended patient.

papers.title: A unified and practical taxonomy for false discovery rate control in omics research
papers.abstract: False discovery rate (FDR) control is central to omics research, yet the diverse procedures used rely on different assumptions. This Comment proposes a 2 × 2 matrix that helps sequencing-based and mass-spectrometry-based omics researchers choose the appropriate family of FDR procedures, or alternative methods that may be more rigorous, depending on data and study design.

papers.title: Immersive and wearable bi-directional thermal rendering for physical and virtual interaction in augmented reality
papers.abstract: Augmented reality blends virtual content with the physical world, creating a challenge for thermal feedback: users must feel virtual temperature cues without losing dexterity or access to real-world thermal information. Here we show that a palm-mounted warm/cool thermal feedback prototype can address this challenge through three design considerations: indirect feedback that leaves the fingertips unobstructed, active thermal passthrough that senses and reproduces the temperature of contacted physical surfaces, and spatially and temporally varying thermal stimulation. Human-subject experiments show that indirect feedback preserves immersion and comfort despite reduced realism when visual contact occurs at the fingertips; thermal passthrough supports discrimination between real and rendered temperatures; and moving thermal patterns increase immersion and realism compared with static stimulation. These findings suggest that our design considerations are viable design strategies for AR thermal haptics, while also clarifying tradeoffs for applications that require precise realism versus broader immersive thermal experience.

papers.title: Multiplexed node-pore sensing for high-throughput, label-free single-cell detection
papers.abstract: We present a multiplexed four-channel Node-Pore Sensing (NPS) platform in which each channel is encoded with a unique Manchester-coded sequence selected by combinatorial optimization for minimum aperiodic cross-correlation. A structural classifier based on the node-pore structure of each Gold code sequence achieves 99.3% single-channel identification accuracy on 1480 labeled experimental transit events, without template alignment or velocity correction. A linear support vector machine successfully distinguishes single-channel events from multi-channel coincidences, enabling label-free, high-throughput single-cell detection across all four channels. This multiplexed architecture provides a route to measuring cell mechanical properties, such as stiffness and recovery time, across parallel channels, extending NPS mechanophenotyping of primary human mammary epithelial cells toward the throughput needed for clinical study.

papers.title: Hippocampal somatostatin neurons gate context generalization during fear memory updating
papers.abstract: Freezing is used as a readout of fear memory in rodents, but it remains unclear how distinct freezing features reflect discrimination and generalization of threatening and neutral contexts. Using pose-tracking and unsupervised analysis in male and female mice undergoing contextual fear conditioning, we show that fear in neutral a context is expressed through fragmented freezing that resist experience-dependent updating, in contrast with more sustained, uninterrupted, and adaptable freezing in a threatening context. Neuronal recordings revealed that recalling neutral context fear is associated with increased activity of dentate gyrus somatostatin inhibitory neurons (SST INs). Chemogenetic suppression of SST INs during fear memory updating selectively facilitated neutral context freezing adaptation while activation prevented generalization of contextual information by restricting long-term fear reduction in contexts that differed from the updating context. These findings identify DG SST INs as context-specific modulators of fear memory updating and suggest that freezing dynamics serve as a behavioral signature of generalization.

papers.title: Pesticide-exposed bees fail to thermoregulate leading to cold colonies with consequences for offspring development
papers.abstract: For many organisms, effective thermoregulation is needed to cope with changing environmental temperatures. But if exposure to pesticides in the environment were to impair this homoeostatic process, reproduction and population viability could be at risk. Focusing on an important insect pollinator, we conducted three complementary experiments exposing bumblebees to a pesticide under different temperature challenges and measuring the impacts on thermoregulatory ability and brood development. First, we reveal that pesticide-exposed individuals (food spiked with a neonicotinoid insecticide) cannot maintain a stable thorax temperature, especially at lower temperatures. Second, that reductions in body temperature are accompanied by behavioural changes with pesticide-exposed colonies failing to maintain the brood temperatures that control bees achieved. Third, that such collective impairment of brood thermoregulation (not the pesticide toxicity to offspring per se) leads to delayed pupal development and reduced adult population growth. Our study provides a plausible mechanistic pathway for why terrestrial insects requiring brood thermoregulation may be vulnerable to decline. With frequent extreme weather events forecasted, our findings have concerning implications for how populations will adequately persist and grow under current pesticide-use regimes with ramifications for pollination services.

papers.title: E2F7 and E2F8 attenuate diabetic kidney disease by suppressing E2F1-induced tubular senescence
papers.abstract: Resveratrol reduces kidney fibrosis and cellular senescence in diabetic kidney disease by suppressing E2F1 through induction of E2F7/8 repressors. Targeting this E2F1-E2F7/8 regulatory axis may offer a promising strategy to slow DKD progression.

papers.title: End-to-end mapping of membrane transport from chemical structure to microorganisms
papers.abstract: Membrane transport is a fundamental biological process with profound implications for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology. While computational approaches have largely adopted a protein-centric perspective to annotate transportomes, inferring transport function directly from the intrinsic properties of substrates remains a major challenge. Addressing transport at the compound level enables the systematic evaluation of whether molecules undergo active transport and by which mechanisms, independent of prior transporter annotation. Here, we introduce ChemProFlow, a comprehensive computational framework that redefines transport analysis from a substrate-centric perspective. By integrating geometric deep learning with orthology-based genomic mapping, ChemProFlow predicts molecular transportability, assigns transport mechanisms according to the Transporter Classification Database, and identifies the microorganisms encoding the corresponding transport systems. We show that this integrated pipeline enables scalable, end-to-end mapping of substrate-transporter-organism relationships, with broad applications in pharmacology for anticipating drug transport, in biotechnology for guiding strain engineering, and in microbiology for dissecting substrate utilization across diverse taxa. By capturing the chemical determinants of transportability, ChemProFlow generalizes to previously unseen substrates and provides a high-throughput framework for systematic exploration of molecular transport across diverse biological contexts. Membrane transport is crucial for pharmacology, biotechnology, and microbiology, yet predicting transport function from substrate properties remains challenging. Here, the authors introduce ChemProFlow, a substrate-centric computational framework that integrates geometric deep learning and genomic mapping to predict molecular transportability.

papers.title: Boundary-controlled imbibition reveals liquid-structure coupling in soft jammed systems
papers.abstract: Transport in soft jammed materials is often described as liquid flow through a fixed structure, yet foam imbibition frequently deviates from classical Lucas–Washburn scaling. Here, we investigate liquid imbibition in foams while directly visualizing both liquid penetration and foam motion under controlled boundary conditions. When foam motion is allowed, liquid uptake is accompanied by collective translation of the unimbibed foam, while the penetration relative to the foam matrix follows approximately xrel ∝ t1/2. When foam motion is suppressed, compression accumulates ahead of the imbibition front and the apparent propagation becomes slower than t1/2. We interpret these behaviors using an effective osmotic driving pressure reduced by a counterpressure generated by foam compression. When the matrix can move, this compression does not accumulate substantially; under a closed boundary, it progressively increases and suppresses further imbibition. These results demonstrate that foam imbibition is governed by coupling between capillary transport and the mechanical response of the foam matrix.

papers.title: Rosette formations as symmetry breaking events
papers.abstract: Multicellular rosettes are ubiquitous structures in biological systems, observed in contexts ranging from morphogenesis to wound healing and cancer progression. Although some molecular insights have been gained to explain the presence of these assemblies of cells around a common center, the tunable global features that favor/hinder their formation are still largely undefined. Here, we use a Voronoi dynamical model in combination with fluorescence microscopy experiments on neural cell populations derived from induced pluripotent stem cells to investigate the ingredients driving the emergence of rosettes. We find that (i) breaking the local spatial symmetry of the system by introducing local curvature-inducing defects allows for the emergence of rosette-like structures, (ii) whose probability of formation depends on the characteristics of the cellular layer. A trade-off between tissue fluidity and single-cell deformability controls the assembly of transient rosettes, which are stabilized in the presence of cell self-alignment interactions. This work provides a physical framework for interpreting the organization of the rosette in developing tissues.

papers.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia in patients with AML undergoing chemotherapy
papers.abstract: Infections are among the main complications in patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing intensive chemotherapy, increasing morbidity and mortality. However, no established tools exist to detect early signs of infection. Here, we develop and validate a machine learning model to predict the daily risk of febrile neutropenia (FN). We conducted a retrospective observational study using registry data from two university hospital districts in Finland. We included adult patients with newly diagnosed AML undergoing intensive chemotherapy (n = 271, 48-hour FN outcomes=540), excluding acute promyelocytic leukemia. The model used a 48-hour prediction window and 1.2 M clinical data points to generate daily FN risk estimates. We built the model using the Extreme Gradient Boosting algorithm, explained variable importance with Shapley Additive Explanations, and evaluated and validated performance using measures of discrimination, calibration, and clinical utility. We show how seven variables predict daily FN risk: white blood cell count, temperature, time since cycle start, C-reactive protein trend, absolute neutrophil count, treatment phase, and prior antibiotic treatment. We achieve an AUROC of 0.91 (95% CI, 0.89–0.93) and a calibration slope of 0.95 (95% CI, 0.73–1.16) in the development cohort’s test set (n = 55, 48-hour FN outcomes=109) and validate performance in the external cohort (n = 136, 48-hour FN outcomes=124, AUROC 0.79 (95% CI, 0.75–0.82), calibration slope 0.65 (95% CI, 0.51–0.79)). While prospective validation is warranted, this study suggests that routinely collected clinical data may be useful for daily prediction of FN and that further development of such screening tools could potentially support personalized infection prevention. Infections can be a life-threatening complication of chemotherapy in patients with acute myeloid leukemia. Here, we developed a screening tool to help physicians detect these infections early. Using registry data from two Finnish university hospital districts, we trained an AI model to predict early infection onset over the next 48 hours. The model required seven variables, including routine laboratory tests, temperature measurements, time since each chemotherapy cycle started, and information on the treatment phase and antibiotic use. Such a screening tool could potentially support more personalized supportive care. However, the results must be confirmed prospectively before clinical adoption.

papers.title: Analyses of plasma protein levels in relation to body composition in the UK Biobank
papers.abstract: Orešković et al. use UK Biobank proteomic and body composition data, applying machine learning, cis Mendelian randomisation, and colocalisation to prioritise targets for lowering fat mass without lowering fat-free mass. MR analyses yield 21 proteins related to fat mass, five of which also colocalised with the trait; seven proteins had no, and one had an opposite-direction association with fat-free mass.

papers.title: Contextualizing biological heterogeneity in brain structural normativity assessments across the aging continuum with the nearest neighbor normativity framework
papers.abstract: Leenings et al. methodologically reformulate neuroimaging standards to explicitly account for natural inter-individual variability of brain physiology. Applied to brain structural decline, the result is a diversity-aware biomarker which improves the detection of disease signals in both statistical and machine learning analyses.

papers.title: Just publish it
High-harmonic generation during ultrafast melting of a Mott insulating state
papers.abstract: High-harmonic generation in solids exposed to an intense laser field can provide information on carrier dynamics and band structures in weakly correlated systems. In strongly correlated systems, a laser field can induce a transition between the various electronic phases formed by the entanglement of charge, spin and orbital degrees of freedom via carrier generation. The high-harmonic generation accompanying this process can carry information on the non-equilibrium electronic-state dynamics along the oscillating field, an aspect that remains unresolved. Here we show that an intense mid-infrared pulse induces melting of a Mott insulating state in a one-dimensional cuprate, Sr2CuO3, the evolution of which leaves a trace in the high-harmonic spectra. Carriers are efficiently generated when the electric field amplitude exceeds 6 MV cm−1, and each harmonic frequency decreases from odd multiples of the mid-infrared frequency. Dynamical mean-field theory suggests that these redshifts originate from a series of electronic-structure reconstructions in each electric field cycle during the melting of the Mott insulating state, which modifies the radiation phase from carrier recombination cycle by cycle. This phenomenon is negligible in rigid-band systems. This study suggests that high-harmonic spectroscopy could obtain information on the cycle-by-cycle dynamics of non-equilibrium transitions in correlated materials. High-harmonic spectroscopy under an intense mid-infrared field reveals redshifts of high-harmonic peaks during the ultrafast melting of a Mott insulating state, while dynamical mean-field theory links them to cycle-by-cycle electronic-state changes.

papers.title: Synthetic interfaces in perovskite photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Synthetic interfaces, created in situ through physical and chemical processes that facilitate structural interlocking, chemical bridging and surface restructuring, offer a scalable pathway to commercially viable perovskite photovoltaics.

papers.title: Antenatal inflammation drives postpartum cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
papers.abstract: Bert et al. show that inflammatory alterations associated with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy are linked to persistent postpartum cardiac dysfunction. Combining clinical and mechanistic studies, they identify reduced progesterone as a key driver and suggest antenatal progesterone supplementation as a potential strategy to mitigate long-term maternal cardiovascular risk.

papers.title: Multiparametric assessment of TNNI3 variant phenotypes in human iPSC-cardiomyocytes correlates with disease severity in patients
papers.abstract: Staudt et al. introduce a high-throughput human induced pluripotent stem cell-cardiomyocyte platform that links TNNI3 genetic variants to contractile and calcium-handling phenotypes. The approach identifies pathogenic variants, provides evidence of pathogenicity for variants of uncertain significance and correlates functional defects with disease onset.

papers.title: Mechanisms of cardiac dysfunction in hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
papers.abstract: Our study combines human clinical and mouse preclinical data to investigate the induction and persistence of cardiac dysfunction during and after pregnancy complicated by hypertensive disorders. We hypothesize that antenatal maternal inflammation drives cardiac dysfunction during pregnancy and contributes to long-term cardiovascular risk among women affected by these high-risk conditions.

papers.title: ZEUS has spoken: lessons for IL-6 inhibition and the road ahead
papers.abstract: Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling has been implicated in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), yet neutralizing IL-6 with ziltivekimab did not cut cardiovascular events in patients with ASCVD and chronic kidney disease in the ZEUS clinical trial. I explore possible explanations and implications for immune-targeting strategies in ASCVD.

papers.title: Enhanced skin tone and blood estimation through AI-enabled upscaling of discrete reflectance spectra
papers.abstract: Objective quantification of epidermal melanin content and dermal blood volume is crucial for equitable applications in dermatology and in the evaluation and engineering of  optical devices, such as pulse oximeters, where variable amounts of melanin may introduce inaccuracies. Here, we demonstrate a method leveraging diffuse reflectance spectroscopy and a machine-learning framework using fully connected neural networks (FCNNs) to non-invasively estimate melanin and blood indices from sparse data through spectral upscaling. We validated the algorithm on custom phantoms, porcine skin, and in vivo human participants. In phantoms with variable blood and melanin (0–20%), the model achieved high accuracy (R2 > 0.90) to absolute concentrations. In porcine skin, estimated melanin strongly correlated with histology-derived density scores (Pearson r = 0.95). Across six regions of the human hand, the FCNN accurately estimated pigmentation from sparse wavelengths, even during hand-raise challenges that induce confounding blood volume changes. After upscaling, sparse-wavelength estimates strongly correlated with a model using over 450 wavelengths (Pearson r = 0.96), reducing data requirements ~ 150-fold without compromising accuracy. These findings highlight the importance of high-spectral information for disentangling melanin and blood contributions in reflectance spectra and the capacity of machine-learning to restore predictive performance from sparse inputs. These findings demonstrate that artificial-intelligence -driven spectral upscaling can enhance objective skin tone quantification in wearable optical devices.

papers.title: Multicenter benchmarking of large language models for bladder cancer management recommendations from mpMRI reports
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can interpret radiology reports, but their ability to generate guideline-concordant recommendations from bladder cancer multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) reports remains uncertain. Following TRIPOD-LLM, we retrospectively evaluated nine API-accessed LLMs using 590 mpMRI reports from three hospitals under two input conditions: original Chinese reports and clinician-translated, quality-controlled English reports. Two physicians independently rated each model-generated recommendation on a 1–5 ordinal scale. We analyzed 21,240 ratings using patient-level random-intercept cumulative link mixed models, with paired Wilcoxon tests as secondary exploratory analyses. The association between input condition and physician rating differed across LLMs (likelihood-ratio chi-square = 683.05, df = 8, P < 0.001). Compared with original Chinese input, clinician-translated English input was associated with higher ratings for chatgpt-o3-pro (OR 2.79, 95% CI 2.29–3.41), deepseek-v4-flash (OR 1.46, 95% CI 1.19–1.81), claude-opus-4-7 (OR 3.07, 95% CI 2.47–3.82), and gpt-5.5 (OR 1.88, 95% CI 1.53–2.32), but with lower ratings for claude-sonnet-4-5 (OR 0.29, 95% CI 0.23–0.36; all Holm-adjusted P < 0.001). Four LLMs showed no clear input-condition difference. Center-specific contrasts also depended on input condition and were materially unchanged after adjustment for age, sex, pathological T stage, tumor grade, tumor number, and maximum lesion diameter. Inter-rater agreement was substantial (quadratic weighted kappa range, 0.621–0.743). Readability did not track physician-rated recommendation quality. These findings argue against clinician-translated English as a universal optimization strategy and support model-specific validation of input conditions before clinical deployment. LLM-generated recommendations from mpMRI reports are best positioned as clinician-supervised, imaging-based decision support rather than standalone treatment advice.

papers.title: Challenges for human oversight in detecting system malfunctions in AI-assisted medical diagnostics
papers.abstract: Increasingly, physicians must oversee AI systems to detect system malfunctions. We studied 48 physicians in a randomized controlled study using an increasingly malfunctioning AI for cardiac auscultation. Diagnostic performance declined alongside AI reliability, even when physicians were cognitively forced to make an initial classification, and when human performance exceeded AI reliability. Physicians’ confidence declined faster than their trust in AI. Results call for specification of oversight goals and processes ensuring patient safety.
