papers.title: Granular hydrogel bioink for macroporous pancreatic spheroid scaffolds
papers.abstract: Cells positioned more than several hundred microns away from a vascular network experience insufficient oxygen and nutrient supply due to diffusion limitations, leading to compromised viability and impaired function. This challenge is especially relevant in large, engineered 3D constructs which exceed the diffusion limitation of 100–200 µm, resulting in necrotic cores. Granular hydrogels have emerged as a promising approach for tissue engineering due to their inherent porosity. Their interconnected pores can facilitate mass transport of oxygen and nutrients, and therefore support cellular function. In this work, we developed a facile method to prepare bioprintable granular hydrogel bioink containing microparticles with tunable diameters, that can form porous scaffolds with different pore sizes and porosities. The bioink remained shelf-stable for at least 60 d when stored at 4 °C, as determined by the melt temperature. The macroporous granular hydrogel scaffold has inherent void spaces between the hydrogel microparticles, in which spheroids can be embedded. Pancreatic spheroids incorporated into the scaffold showed improved viability compared to free spheroids, indicating the granular microenvironment supports spheroid survival. Furthermore, functional studies of embedded pancreatic spheroids with glucose-stimulated insulin secretion demonstrated preserved insulin secretion functionality. Our approach thus serves as a tunable platform for supporting the culture of functional spheroids and organoids, that has potential regenerative medicine applications in restoration of physiological functions when implanted.

papers.title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
papers.abstract: Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

papers.title: High-pressure phase transitions, electrical conductivity and recoverability of uranium polyhydrides
papers.abstract: The uranium-hydrogen system has the potential to host numerous polyhydride compounds with diverse properties, but there are conflicting experimental data on their synthesis and stability. Here, the authors use laser-heated diamond anvil cell experiments and synchrotron X-ray diffraction to map the uranium-hydrogen high-pressure phase diagram, revealing new phases and their properties, with implications for understanding hydrogen-rich materials.

papers.title: Membrane-coupled conformational switching of VISTA regulates CC′ loop accessibility and immune checkpoint signaling
papers.abstract: V-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T-cell activation (VISTA) is an immune checkpoint that suppresses T-cell responses and has emerged as a promising target for cancer immunotherapy. Here we show, using atomistic molecular dynamics simulations of both truncated glycan-free and full-length glycosylated membrane-bound human VISTA, that the extracellular and transmembrane domains remain structurally stable, while the unusually long CC′ loop is stabilized by extensive hydrogen-bonding interactions. Principal component analysis and conformational clustering reveal a recurrent rotational motion of the extracellular domain relative to the membrane, producing two conformational states: an “Up” state with a solvent-exposed CC′ loop and a “Down” state in which the loop transiently associates with the membrane. These transitions are coupled to proline-mediated bending of the transmembrane helix. We propose that this membrane-coupled Up/Down switching regulates CC′ loop accessibility, providing a structural mechanism that may influence VISTA-mediated immune checkpoint signaling.

papers.title: Isofalcarintriol ameliorates gestational diabetes mellitus-induced β-cell dysfunction by targeting MIF to enhance mitophagy
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance and pancreatic β-cell dysfunction are closely associated with impaired mitophagy, forming a core pathological mechanism in gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM). This study investigates the role of isofalcarintriol (IFT), a carrot-derived polyacetylene, in regulating mitochondrial function in GDM-related β-cells. Here, we use a high-fat diet-induced C57BL/6 J pregnant mouse model and high-glucose/palmitic acid (HG/PA)-treated MIN6 β-cells; IFT ameliorates hyperglycemia and insulin resistance, promotes β-cell maturation and proliferation, induces mitophagy, and enhances β-cell antioxidant capacity. Mechanistically, IFT promotes the dissociation of macrophage migration inhibitory factor (MIF) from ubiquitin-specific protease 7 (USP7) through its C224 residue, and induces MIF ubiquitination through F50/L59 residues, thereby driving the phosphatase and tensin homolog (PTEN)-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin-mediated mitophagy and pancreatic injury recovery. A mitophagy inhibitor eliminates the beneficial effects of IFT, while PINK1 knockdown reverses the mitophagy-promoting effect induced by MIF knockdown. This study reveals IFT as a potent antioxidant protecting β-cells against GDM-induced injury through MIF, highlighting its potential value in GDM treatment.

papers.title: A covariance-aware variational generative model preserving gene correlation structure in single-cell transcriptomic data
papers.abstract: Measuring gene activity in individual cells reveals the diversity within tumors but is costly, technically noisy, and often captures too few rare cells. Computer-generated cells could fill these gaps. Here we show, across two independent groups of pancreatic cancer patients, that a deep generative model produces realistic synthetic cells. Explicitly modeling correlations within the model’s compressed description of each cell does not improve preservation of gene-gene relationships over a simpler matched model, which appears to capture this structure implicitly. Nevertheless, the model’s sampling strategy yields cells that faithfully reproduce gene activity patterns, cell-type markers, and cellular organization and compare favorably with established methods. The model trains 100 to 1,000 times faster than a diffusion-based alternative. Synthetic cells blend with real data and support standard analyses, including reconstruction of a precancerous transition. These findings support using synthetic cells to enrich rare populations, benchmark methods, and simulate transitional states in tumors.

papers.title: Salvage of host-derived geranylgeraniol limits fosmidomycin efficacy in murine Plasmodium berghei malaria
papers.abstract: Despite promising preclinical activity, fosmidomycin has shown limited clinical efficacy against malaria. It inhibits the methylerythritol 4-phosphate (MEP) pathway, which supplies precursors for farnesyl and geranylgeranyl pyrophosphate (FPP, GGPP) synthesis and protein prenylation. In vitro, fosmidomycin toxicity is transiently rescued by exogenous prenols such as geranylgeraniol (GGOH) via a Plasmodium prenol kinase (PolK)-dependent salvage pathway, suggesting that host-derived isoprenoid salvage limits drug efficacy. Here we show that PolK-deficient Plasmodium berghei (ΔPbPolK) parasites remain viable but cannot use exogenous prenols, rendering murine infections more responsive to fosmidomycin. In P. falciparum, PolK loss caused metabolic remodeling, including altered glycolysis and increased isoprenoid biosynthesis. Accordingly, pharmacological inhibition of PolK by geraniol blocked GGOH utilization and potentiated fosmidomycin in vitro and in vivo. These findings identify prenol salvage as a mechanism by which malaria parasites exploit host-derived prenols, link it to glycolytic and isoprenoid regulation, and reveal it as a constraint on fosmidomycin efficacy, with implications for antiparasitic strategies targeting isoprenoid-dependent pathways.

papers.title: Multi-omics analyses reveal dynamic interactions between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry ripening
papers.abstract: Fruit ripening is a complex developmental process involving coordinated changes in gene expression, metabolism, and epigenetic regulation. How DNA methylation dynamics influence gene transcription and metabolite accumulation during black raspberry (Rubus occidentalis) fruit ripening remains poorly understood. Here, we performed developmental-series transcriptome, methylome, and metabolome analysis; the results from this analysis reveal extensive epigenetic reprogramming during black raspberry fruit ripening. Fruit tissues exhibit globally higher DNA methylation than leaves, particularly in CHG and CHH contexts. Local methylation in all cytosine contexts progressively decreases in promoter regions during ripening, whereas CHG and CHH methylation increase in transposon-rich regions. Two primary methylation transitions—promoter hypomethylation and CHH hypermethylation—govern transcriptional shifts in genes involved in ripening processes. Methyl-binding transcription factors with activation potential likely promote CHH hypermethylation-linked transcriptional activation. Multi-omics integration reveals that coordinated anthocyanin accumulation parallels expression of biosynthetic and regulatory genes within coherent networks. Elevated non-CG methylation in heterochromatin coincides with increased transcription of histone variants mediating chromatin compaction, suggesting chromatin remodelers fine-tune accessibility for methyltransferases. Our study highlights both genome-wide and locus-specific epigenetic reprogramming and demonstrates a coordinated interplay between DNA methylation and transcriptional regulation during black raspberry fruit ripening.

Crystallinity control of spin torque efficiency in CuNi alloys
papers.abstract: Light metals are gaining increasing attention in spintronics due to their advantageous properties over traditional heavy metals. This work investigates the origin of large spin torque efficiency (ξSOT) in CuNi alloys using spin-torque ferromagnetic resonance in FeNi/CuNi bilayers. Polycrystalline CuNi shows a ξSOT comparable to heavy metal Pt. By controlling crystallinity, we observe a significant modulation of ξSOT, as epitaxial CuNi (001) and (111) films exhibit similar but markedly lower values than their polycrystalline counterparts. This suggests that the charge-spin conversion in CuNi is strongly influenced by crystallinity and primarily dominated by extrinsic scattering. Temperature-dependent studies further support a dominant contribution from extrinsic scattering in both paramagnetic and ferromagnetic phases, with minimal contribution from spin fluctuations across the Curie temperature. Our findings deepen the understanding of charge-spin interconversion in light metals and highlight their potential for spintronic applications.

papers.title: Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance
papers.abstract: The evolution of quantum states can be described by quantum channels. The task of estimating an unknown quantum channel, known as process tomography, is a central problem in quantum information theory. A long-standing open question is how many uses of an unknown channel are required to learn it to a precision quantified by the standard metric for distinguishing quantum processes, known as the diamond distance. Here we address this by establishing the query complexity of channel tomography with optimal dependence on the dimensions of the input and output spaces and the channel’s Kraus rank at any fixed constant accuracy in diamond distance. We design an algorithm that establishes an upper bound and prove a matching lower bound for learning a channel to the given accuracy. Our algorithm follows the strategy of performing optimal tomography on the Choi-state representation of the process, and we show that channel tomography can be reduced to the well-studied problem of pure-state tomography. As channels subsume states, unitaries and measurements as special cases, our protocol provides a unified framework for tomography of these tasks. Quantum channels can be used to describe the evolution of quantum states, including both unitary evolution and measurement. Now the optimal number of uses needed to learn an unknown channel to any fixed accuracy has been found.

papers.title: Climate risk management must move from hazards to impacts
papers.abstract: The next frontier in climate risk management is not just better hazard detection, but better impact prediction. A five-layer framework could help transform physical observations into forecasts of real-world consequences and more effective responses.

papers.title: Robust hydrogel ion channels for osmotic energy harvesting and environmental sensing
papers.abstract: Salinity gradient blue energy offers a promising alternative to fossil fuels. Here the authors develop ultrarough, self-healing hydrogel ionic conductors that achieve an excellent power density while maintaining over 91% of their performance after damage and enable autonomous environmental sensing.

papers.title: Effect of two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens on the gut microbiome in a randomized phase 3 trial
papers.abstract: In a prespecified companion study (BMT CTN 1801) of the randomized phase 3 BMT CTN 1703 trial comparing two common GVHD prophylaxis regimens, microbiome diversity at engraftment did not associate with non-relapse mortality, but secondary analyses found baseline microbiome diversity was associated with clinical outcomes.

papers.title: DeepTNR: predicting tumor drug sensitivity from spatial transcriptomics with deep graph contrastive and transfer learning
papers.abstract: Heterogeneity within the tumor microenvironment remains a major obstacle to precision oncology. Although existing drug-sensitivity models can capture transcriptional heterogeneity, they generally do not account for the spatial organization of predicted drug responses. Here, we developed DeepTNR, a spatially resolved framework that integrates tumor-stroma interface features, spatial autocorrelation, and distance-dependent associations between local cellular composition and predicted drug sensitivity. Across nine tumor types, with colorectal cancer (CRC) as a representative example, DeepTNR identified irinotecan as the most sensitive drug and revealed significant spatial autocorrelation in its predicted response patterns. Spatial proximity effect analysis further showed that local enrichment of immune and proliferative programs positively was associated with increased irinotecan sensitivity. Together, these findings demonstrate the potential of DeepTNR to resolve intratumoral therapeutic heterogeneity and identify niche-specific vulnerabilities.

papers.title: Efficient catalyst-controlled C–H arylation of arenes
papers.abstract: Direct arylation of C–H bonds in arenes offers a streamlined alternative to widely used cross-coupling reactions.1 However, native substrates lack the preinstalled functional handles that ordinarily provide both reactivity and control over the site of reaction. Consequently, despite long-standing interest in directly engaging C–H bonds as reactive sites,2–4 the design of general catalysts that deliver high yields across diverse substrate classes while controlling site selectivity remains a challenge.5–12 Here we show that a microenvironment around a prototypical palladium dicarboxylate catalytic site can provide high selectivity for direct arylation of sterically exposed C–H sites, while high efficiency is achieved using an advanced palladium(II) precatalyst and tailored diaryliodonium reagents for selective aryl transfer. The applicability of this system spans from electron-rich to electron-deficient arenes, while electron-neutral benzene, which is often a challenge for C–H arylation, undergoes successive sterically controlled arylations, delivering functionalized polyaryl compounds. In addition to removing the necessity for pre-functionalized substrates, the mild conditions enable direct late-stage C–H arylation and the installation of aryl groups equipped with functionalities that are typically either reactive in traditional cross-coupling catalysis, such as triflates, iodides, and boronate esters, or sensitive to the basic conditions, such as N-hydroxysuccinimide esters. The results emphasize the distinct synthetic value of palladium-catalyzed direct C–H arylation reactions and showcase a catalyst platform that facilitates high yields and control over site-selectivity.

papers.title: Human replisomes direct a dedicated leading-strand primase for fork restart
papers.abstract: Structural and biochemical studies show that the CMG helicase directly recruits PRIMPOL for leading-strand repriming, enabling replication fork restart and limiting post-replicative DNA gaps.

papers.title: Bureaucratic incentives shaped effectiveness of the one-child policy in China
papers.abstract: Stronger bureaucratic incentives under China’s one vote veto policy intensified enforcement of the one-child policy, accounting for nearly half of China’s fertility decline during the 1990s.

papers.title: Validation of clinical and preclinical obesity across global cohorts
papers.abstract: A large-scale data analysis assesses the Lancet Commission’s proposed diagnostic framework for obesity, finding that this framework, in which BMI is combined with other criteria, such as waist circumference and organ function, is more useful than classifications based on BMI alone.

papers.title: UNC13A splice correction rescues synaptic dysfunction induced by TDP-43 loss
papers.abstract: TDP-43 loss induces a predegenerative state in which neurons remain structurally intact and suffer a substantial breakdown in synaptic communication; a therapeutic strategy is found that corrects UNC13A cryptic splicing by using splice-switching antisense oligonucleotides.

papers.title: NRF2 is a mechanosensitive checkpoint for NLRP3 inflammasome activation
papers.abstract: The stiffness of the extracellular matrix is identified as a pivotal factor that influences activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome in vitro and in vivo.

papers.title: Non-halogen aqueous electrolytes for four-electron iodine conversion
papers.abstract: An electrolyte framework that harnesses anionic chemistry to coordinate the interfacial microenvironment and molecular interactions enables reversible four-electron iodine conversion in halogen-free aqueous electrolytes, and is validated in metal–iodine batteries.

papers.title: Bistable regulation of adipocyte heterogeneity governs thermogenesis
papers.abstract: IL-1β from neutrophils and macrophages stabilizes nearby brown adipocytes in a low-UCP1 state; cold temperature reduces IL-1β via sympathetic nerves, leading to transition to a high-UCP1 state and increased thermogenesis, while higher temperatures have the opposite effect.

papers.title: Epigenetic heterogeneity in breast tumours informs diagnosis and prognosis
papers.abstract: Single-cell epigenetic analyses reveal a conserved epigenetic signature across patients that may help identify those at increased risk for disease relapse in breast cancer.

papers.title: A plant RNA-binding protein senses 2′,3′-cNMP produced by insect effectors
papers.abstract: The rice RNA-binding protein NIB1 detects 2′,3′-cyclic nucleotide products from insect saliva RNase, forming nuclear condensates that recruit EDS1 to activate defence, revealing a conserved messenger-based immune pathway in plants.

papers.title: Flexible rubber blades for tidal turbines
papers.abstract: Flexible tidal turbine blades with passive trailing-edge deformation match the energy yield of active pitch-controlled blades while reducing fatigue-inducing load fluctuations by up to one-third, lowering maintenance complexity.

papers.title: Hadean mantle depletion and 3.95-Gyr subduction implied by North China rocks
papers.abstract: Analysis of a 3.95-Gyr-old trondhjemitic gneiss from eastern Hebei, China, reveals a composition suggesting a low-temperature altered basaltic source, that originated from a mantle depleted in the Hadean, was most likely transported to mantle depths through a transient subduction event and partially melted to produce the trondhjemite.

papers.title: Human land use drives microplastic abundance in terrestrial wildlife
papers.abstract: Microplastic burdens in Brazilian tapirs and anteaters rise with human-modified land use and proximity to development, however animals in remote habitats also carry microplastics, showing that landscape change and individual space use jointly shape wildlife exposure.

papers.title: Transient nuclear softening for zygotic gene activation in mice
papers.abstract: A distinct physical nuclear state acquired by embryos at the beginning of life supports the initiation of the zygotic transcription program.

papers.title: Suppression of epithelial proliferation and tumorigenesis by IgA
papers.abstract: Experiments in mouse models show that immunoglobulin A in the gut lumen has a role in regulating the turnover of colon epithelial cells and reduces the susceptibility of mice to colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Evolutionary dynamics in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia
papers.abstract: The somatic evolutionary histories of haematopoietic cells in the years preceding acute myeloid leukaemia diagnosis show that the clonal dynamics of blood comply with a set of simple evolutionary rules.

papers.title: Scale-rich network-based metamaterials
papers.abstract: A network-science-based framework that embeds network heterogeneity into mechanical metamaterials is used to produce scale-rich metamaterials that exhibit properties inaccessible to traditional single-scale systems.

papers.title: The molecular basis of replication fork restart via repriming by PRIMPOL
papers.abstract: PRIMPOL is recruited to stalled forks through an interaction with the replicative helicase CDC45–MCM2–7–GINS, facilitating primer handover from PRIMPOL to the high-fidelity polymerase ε, minimizing mutagenic DNA synthesis.

papers.title: Domain-alteration chimeras rewire oncogenic complexes in prostate cancer
papers.abstract: A novel therapeutic modality enforces non-native androgen receptor (AR)–p300/CBP interactions to collapse AR transcriptional programs, producing super-inhibitory, lineage-selective suppression of metastatic prostate cancer and establishing domain-alteration chimeras as a broadly applicable therapeutic strategy leveraging induced proximity.

papers.title: Glycosylation and importins liquefy the FG barrier in live nuclear pores
papers.abstract: Nuclear pore proteins maintain a fluid, spatially organized barrier through coordinated molecular interactions, explaining how cells achieve selective transport and reconciling competing models of pore structure.

papers.title: Severe drought and warming increase the extinction risk of cacti
papers.abstract: Severe drought and warming will substantially increase the loss of suitable climatic area for cactus species.

papers.title: Low-power 2D CFETs using single-crystal high- κ dielectrics
papers.abstract: A transferable single-crystal anatase titanium dioxide dielectric enables high-quality interfaces with two-dimensional semiconductors, yielding near-ideal switching, low hysteresis and ultra-low-power complementary transistors and inverters.

papers.title: Independent interferometric observable confirms black hole shadow in M87*
papers.abstract: An imaging algorithm using closure-invariant formalism and diffusion-based reconstruction applied to supermassive black hole very long baseline radio interferometry datasets enables independent recovery of the ring-like shadow and mass that is free from the usual calibration and imaging assumptions.

papers.title: Mitochondrial protein import defects enhance tumour immunogenicity

papers.title: Metasurface waveguides for all-day augmented reality glasses
papers.abstract: An all-day-wearable augmented reality glasses prototype using a dual-layer metasurface-based waveguide and three matched grating patterns achieves a 30° field of view in an 8 × 8-mm 2 two-dimensional eyebox while maintaining high luminance efficiency.

papers.title: Author Correction: A HO-1 gene knockout using a NanoCRISPR scaffold suppresses metastasis in mouse models
A high-polarity molecular-anchor design for stable high-mobility perovskite transistors
papers.abstract: Perovskite transistors have recently achieved field-effect mobilities comparable with commercial polycrystalline silicon devices, but their practical applications remain limited because of poor operational stability and current–voltage hysteresis caused by ion migration. Unlike in optoelectronic devices, transistors have high gate electric fields that exert strong Coulombic forces on mobile ions, making robust ion-anchoring interactions essential for suppressing field-induced ionic motion. Here we report a data-driven additive design strategy that uses molecular polarity to strengthen binding to mobile ions. We perform the high-throughput screening of fluorinated ammonium-based molecules with dual hydrogen-bonding capability across a compound chemical space comprising >108 molecules and identify 14 candidates that combine high molecular polarity with suitable size. Three of these additives allow us to fabricate transistors with field-effect mobilities exceeding 25 cm2 V−1 s−1, with 4-(trifluoromethyl)-phenethylammonium performing the best, having a mobility of 41.3 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stability over 9,000 on/off switching cycles. Molecular polarity can be used to guide the rational and targeted design of additives that suppress ion migration in metal halide perovskite transistors, leading to mobilities of over 40 cm2 V−1 s−1 and stabilities of over 9,000 on/off cycles.

papers.title: Making van der Waals heterostructures through substitution
Designing additives for perovskite transistors using molecular polarity as a guide
papers.abstract: Molecular polarity can be used as a predictive descriptor to screen potential additives for halide perovskite lattices, allowing robust and high-performance tin-based perovskite transistors to be created.

papers.title: Tensegrity continuum robots enable task-adaptive morphologies for cooperative behaviours
papers.abstract: Robots that can change their morphologies and behaviours for different tasks and environments hold great promise for adaptable, multifunctional systems. Modular reconfigurable robots can achieve such functionalities by docking and rearranging individual units, but most rely on rigid modules that lack structural compliance, resulting in limited capabilities. Continuum robots offer compliance through flexible backbones, yet they cannot self-reconfigure into task-adaptive multi-robot configurations. Here we introduce a modular reconfigurable robot that unifies the advantages of both architectures by combining a tensegrity-based compliant body with claw-based connection mechanisms. Each robot can manipulate and locomote independently, and multiple robots can self-reconfigure into different morphologies (for example, chains, loops, branches) for cooperative manipulation and locomotion. We demonstrate the robots’ capability across diverse tasks and environments, including coordinated object manipulation and transport, multimodal locomotion, and loco-manipulation in real-world scenarios. These results lay a foundation for adaptable and multifunctional robotic collectives, with broad potential applications in manufacturing, space exploration and search-and-rescue operations. Saikot et al. present flexible modular robots that combine locomotion and manipulation in a single unit, then physically connect and collaborate in task-adaptive forms to carry objects, cross gaps and navigate challenging terrain.

papers.title: Orientational locking in a turnstile metal–organic framework for cyclohexene/cyclohexane separation
papers.abstract: This study presents a metal–organic framework that enables the stepwise ternary separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane via two temperature-tuned fixed-bed columns operated at room temperature and higher temperatures, exploiting thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientational locking for selective discrimination.

papers.title: Turnstile metal–organic framework for the efficient separation of cyclic C<sub>6</sub> hydrocarbons
papers.abstract: The industrial separation of cyclic C6 hydrocarbons is crucial but challenging. Now, a metal–organic framework is developed that features –CF3 pairs at the pore apertures. Through a synergy of thermally controlled pore gating and interaction-induced molecular orientation locking, this ‘turnstile’ metal–organic framework enables the stepwise separation of benzene, cyclohexene and cyclohexane.

papers.title: “Rivet” cations enhance mechanical stability of Ni-rich layered cathode materials for Li-ion batteries
papers.abstract: Mg²⁺ and Ni²⁺ ions at Li sites enhance Ni-rich NMC stability by acting as structural rivets that suppress layer gliding and cracking. Here, the authors show that Mg²⁺ and Ni²⁺ at Li sites synergistically enhance the mechanical strength and toughness of single-crystal NMC811.

papers.title: Oral absorption, bioavailability, and uptake routes of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid derived 17(S)-HDHA, 15(S)-HEPE, RvD1 and RvE1 in healthy rats
papers.abstract: Lipid mediators derived from omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), are critical mediators of inflammation. In contrast to EPA and DHA, the bioavailability of their lipid mediator derivatives remains unstudied. Oral, intravenous (IV), and intraduodenal administration of stable isotope labeled n-3 PUFA, and lipid mediators was used to establish their bioavailability, half-lives, and absorption routes in rats. Blood and lymph were analyzed by liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry. Orally administered 17(S)-HDHA-d5, 15(S)-HEPE-d5, and RvD1-d5 were rapidly absorbed into the unesterified plasma pool, reaching peak concentrations within 15 min to 1 h, with a bioavailability of 3–6%. IV administration revealed rapid plasma clearance of n-3 PUFA and administered lipid mediators (half-life ~30 s). Lymph cannulation reduced plasma appearance of 17(S)-HDHA-d5 and 15(S)-HEPE-d5 but not RvD1-d5, indicating structure-dependent changes in absorption via lymphatic or portal routes. These findings demonstrate n-3 PUFA-derived lipid mediators are absorbed following oral intake, providing a foundation for oral delivery.

papers.title: Lysine 69 deacetylation of NFIC drives autophagy-induced epithelial–mesenchymal transition and chemoresistance in glioblastoma
papers.abstract: Autophagy-induced the deacetylation of NFIC at Lysine 69 site accelerates tumorigenesis by activating FOXK1/HERC3 axis, revealing an acetylation-dependent mechanism that can be targeted by peptide Pe-k69 to overcome TMZ resistance in glioblastoma.

papers.title: Self-paced silent speech brain-computer interface for device control

papers.title: Aging remodels the suprachiasmatic nucleus and weakens ultradian rhythms and activity–temperature coupling
papers.abstract: Aging alters daily physiology, but how these changes relate to remodeling of the suprachiasmatic nucleus (SCN) remains incompletely understood. Here, we examined time-resolved SCN transcriptomic profiles alongside longitudinal recordings of core body temperature and locomotor activity, using separate cohorts for the molecular and physiological analyses. Aging was associated with extensive SCN transcriptomic remodeling, including enrichment of innate immune, interferon-related, complement-associated, and glial programs, while selected canonical clock genes retained detectable rhythmic expression. The composition and temporal profiles of broader rhythmic transcriptional programs also differed between young and aged SCN samples. Aged mice retained detectable circadian rhythms but showed reduced 2–6 h ultradian wavelet power in locomotor activity and body temperature, lower activity–temperature correlations, and altered optimal integration windows and time-of-day-dependent relationships. Histological analyses revealed glial remodeling and reduced neuronal marker-positive cell density in the aged SCN. These findings identify parallel age-associated changes in SCN molecular and cellular organization and in physiological rhythmic power and activity–temperature associations.

papers.title: Dysfunction of hepatic lipid metabolism in mice haploinsufficient for the histone methyltransferase Kmt2c
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction is influenced by various factors including environmental effects and genetic variants, and recent evidence reveals close associations between metabolic dysfunction and neurodevelopmental or neuropsychiatric disorders. However, the mechanistic link between them remains unclear. To clarify these relationships, we utilized mice with haploinsufficiency in the autism spectrum disorder-related gene lysine methyltransferase 2c (Kmt2c) (Kmt2c+/fs mice), in which we previously confirmed significantly less body weight. We characterized body composition, small intestinal transcriptome, fecal metagenome, plasma metabolome, and hepatic mitochondrial morphology and biochemical activity in male Kmt2c+/fs mice and wild-type controls. Hepatic transcriptomic changes and lipid accumulation were also assessed. Group comparisons were performed using two-sided Mann-Whitney U-tests, two-way repeated measures ANOVA, and enrichment analyses with appropriate multiple-testing correction. Here we show that Kmt2c+/fs mice have decreased body mass index and body fat mass. The small intestine and fecal metagenome show minimal alterations, while plasma metabolomic analysis reveals an increase of metabolites related to glucose and amino acid metabolism. Hepatic mitochondria display altered morphology and biochemical activity. The liver of Kmt2c+/fs mice exhibits decreased lipid accumulation and the downregulation of genes related to lipid metabolism, particularly fatty acid synthesis. These findings indicate that KMT2C deficiency triggers functional defects in lipid metabolism in the liver, accompanied by upregulation of glucose and amino acid metabolism and consequently less body weight. The mechanism of metabolic dysfunction observed in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders largely remains unclear. Lysine methyltransferase 2c (Kmt2c) is one of autism spectrum disorder (ASD)-related genes, and Kmt2c mutant mice exhibit ASD-like phenotypes and less body weight. We precisely analyzed metabolic profiles of Kmt2c+/fs mice, and discovered lower body mass index and decreased fat mass. While these phenotypes were unlikely to be explained by changes in the intestine or gut bacteria, we found changes in morphology and biochemical activity of hepatic mitochondria. The liver of Kmt2c+/fs mice showed decreased lipid accumulation and downregulation of lipid metabolism-related genes. These results provide insight into the onset mechanism of metabolic dysfunction in neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders, especially associated with epigenetic regulations.

papers.title: Conformationally driven negative chemotaxis in synthetic vesicles
papers.abstract: Achieving negative chemotaxis without catalytic designs remains challenging in artificial systems. Now it has been shown that intrinsic membrane conformational dynamics generate interfacial tension gradients, driving polymersomes away from a lactic-acid source without requiring external energy input.

papers.title: Catalytic enantioselective dual C–H cross-coupling enabled by a radical-buffering strategy
papers.abstract: Enantioselective cross-coupling of two inert C–H bonds represents the pivotal advance long sought in asymmetric synthesis, enabling much more efficient and direct construction of essential chiral molecular scaffolds, including those for therapeutics and agrochemicals. Here, taking advantage of the highly regioselective electrophilic reactivity of arenes, we report an enantioselective formal cross-coupling between aryl C–H and benzylic C–H bonds through a photoredox/copper relay catalysis, enabling efficient access to a diverse array of chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds with excellent enantioselectivity. Mechanistic investigations underscore the critical role of the copper catalyst as a radical buffer. Operating at a higher loading than the chiral ligand, it buffers the transient aryl radical, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing its side reactions, enabling highly efficient asymmetric dual-radical cross-coupling. This protocol exhibits a broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance, highlighting its practical utility in the streamlined synthesis of bioactive molecules. Photoredox and copper relay catalysis enables enantioselective formal cross-coupling between aryl C–H and benzylic C–H bonds, providing access to a range of chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds. Mechanistic analysis reveals the copper catalyst acts as a buffer for the transient aryl radical intermediate, prolonging its lifetime and suppressing potential side reactions.

papers.title: Aryl radical buffering facilitates asymmetric dual C–H cross-coupling
papers.abstract: A method for the enantioselective cross-coupling of arene and benzylic C–H bonds through photoredox–copper relay catalysis is demonstrated, providing efficient access to diverse chiral 1,1-diaryl compounds with high enantioselectivity. The copper catalyst buffers aryl radicals to prolong their lifetime and suppress side reactions, increasing the efficiency of the method.

papers.title: A non-methylphosphonate process for immediate oxic methane production in stratified freshwaters

papers.title: Integrating science and transboundary water law when renegotiating The Indus Waters Treaty
papers.abstract: The ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan, heightened by the April 2025 terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, has led to an unprecedented abeyance of India’s participation in the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT). Although this treaty has often been described as an example of hydrological cooperation despite regional conflict, it has systemic problems from the perspective of long-term environmental, political and social sustainability. We identify several factors that justify renegotiating and revising the IWT, leveraging multilateral and domestic policy frameworks to formulate a more effective and comprehensive agreement. This includes metrics set forth on transboundary water cooperation under the Sustainable Development Goals (Indicator 6.5.2) as well as a range of international legal guidelines for drafting ecologically viable treaties. We explore the role that nascent regional organizations could play in reducing tensions over the Indus Basin and facilitating new discussions. Ultimately, a reset in the IWT could catalyse broader confidence-building and a lasting peace in a region where two nuclear rivals share a 3,200-km-long contiguous border. The ongoing conflict between India and Pakistan, exacerbated by the April 2025 terrorist attack in Kashmir, has led to India’s unprecedented suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty. A renegotiation of the treaty should leverage international and domestic frameworks to enhance environmental, political and social sustainability, potentially fostering regional peace.

papers.title: An organic semiconductor-based photocatalyst sheet for overall solar-driven water splitting
papers.abstract: Splitting water into hydrogen and oxygen using sunlight offers a route to renewable fuel, but translating this reaction into systems suitable for industrial implementation remains difficult. Photocatalyst sheets can overcome key limitations of common direct water-splitting approaches (photoelectrochemical devices and photocatalyst dispersions), but existing photocatalyst sheets rely on inorganic semiconductor nanoparticles and processing techniques that can be difficult to scale. Here we show that solution-processed organic semiconductors can form water-splitting photocatalyst sheets by simply tailoring the charge extraction layer beneath the light-absorbing film. A single organic semiconductor active layer (deposited as a bulk heterojunction blend) drives either hydrogen or oxygen evolution depending on its underlying molecular contact, yielding photocathode and photoanode half-cells with well-matched photocurrents. Combining both reactions on one substrate using a microdomain-patterned molecular underlayer affords a photocatalyst sheet that achieves unassisted water splitting under simulated sunlight for over 2 h and generates hydrogen at a stabilized rate of 1.3 µmol h−1 cm−2, which corresponds to a solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 0.1%. Solar water splitting offers a route to renewable hydrogen, but developing photocatalyst sheets from scalable, solution-processable materials remains a challenge. Here the authors use underlayer engineering to build an organic semiconductor photocatalyst sheet that enables unassisted overall water splitting under simulated sunlight.

Cost-effective climate change mitigation through land sector contributions
papers.abstract: Land-based mitigation can substantially lower the cost of climate action and ease energy sector decarbonization. Ionic-liquid-assisted room-temperature dry etching of metal–organic frameworks
papers.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks are promising nanoporous materials, but their sensitivity to electron and ion beams limits fine patterning. Here, the authors developed a room-temperature dry-etching method for metal–organic frameworks by infiltrating them with ionic liquids, improving beam resistance and enabling sub-100 nm patterning while elucidating possible damage mechanisms.

papers.title: AI-guided human-in-the-loop inverse design of high performance engineering structures
papers.abstract: Dat Quoc Ha and colleagues develop an AI co-pilot framework integrating machine learning into human-in-the-loop topology optimization to predict user-preferred structural regions for interactive modification. This approach eliminates iterative selection bottlenecks, boosting linear buckling load by 39% or enhancing manufacturability with minimal added computational time.

papers.title: Advances in engineered 3D cardiac tissue for functional biosensing, disease modeling, and regenerative medicine
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) engineered cardiac tissues are miniaturized in vitro cardiac models to recapitulate essential aspects of native heart physiology for applications in drug testing, disease modeling and regenerative therapy. Building on advances in microfabrication, biomaterials, bioelectronics and stem cell biology, these systems reproduce myocardial architecture, mechanical dynamics, electrical conductivity, and disease-specific phenotypes. Existing reviews treat biofabrication, biomaterials, functional biosensing, disease modeling, and cardiac regenerative therapy as separate topics, while few have framed these components within a unified micro- and nanoengineering framework that links tissue architecture, functional biosensing, and application-driven performance. This review addresses this gap by highlighting recent advances in biofabrication strategies for precise control over tissue architecture and cellular microenvironments and discusses the incorporation of microelectronic, optical, and mechanical biosensors for real-time, multiparametric monitoring of tissue contractility and electrophysiological activity. We further summarize representative applications in disease modeling such as cardiomyopathies, ischemic injury, and drug-induced cardiotoxicity, as well as the development of bioengineered cardiac constructs and patches as transplantable grafts to restore myocardial function. Finally, key challenges and future directions toward predictive, scalable, and translational cardiac microphysiological systems are discussed.

papers.title: Trade-offs among selection regimes shape trait evolution and resilience in three-guild networks
papers.abstract: Eco-evolutionary feedbacks can alter species traits and reshape ecological networks, influencing network resilience to disturbance. Here we combine ecological dynamics, trait evolution and interaction rewiring in a three-guild adaptive network to test how biotic (antagonistic and mutualistic) and abiotic (environmental) selection pressures interact to shape community structure and stability. We focus on how different selection regimes affect trait directionality, functional diversity, temporal variability and network resilience. We find that weak trait directionality, high functional turnover and variability, and strong resilience are tightly linked. The greatest trait variability and resilience arise when antagonistic and environmental selection pressures are symmetrical. In species-rich communities, fluctuating selection emerges naturally, while dominance of antagonistic pressure consistently dampens trait directionality. Coupled ecological and evolutionary processes favour trait matching and generate both nested and modular network structures. Compared with bipartite antagonistic networks, network architecture plays a weaker role in shaping trait coevolution in three-guild systems. Together, these results show how trade-offs among antagonistic, mutualistic and environmental selection pressures govern trait evolution and resilience in complex ecological networks.

papers.title: Altered developmental profile of the head-direction signal in a rat model of fragile X syndrome
papers.abstract: Fragile X Syndrome is a common inherited, monogenic cause of intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, but the altered neural mechanisms underlying it remain unclear. Here, we investigate the development of the head-direction system in a rat model of Fragile X Syndrome (Fmr1-/y rats) through electrophysiological recordings in the postsubiculum during exploration and sleep. Surprisingly, juvenile Fmr1-/y rats exhibited enhanced head-direction tuning and increased stability of the head-direction signal in relation to the external environment. Sharper intrinsic head-direction tuning persisted in rapid eye movement sleep.  In contrast, adult Fmr1-/y rats exhibited normal intrinsic head-direction tuning but its stability in relation to the external world was impaired. These findings suggest a transient improvement of head-direction coding in juvenile Fmr1-/y rats, followed by a degradation of tuning stability in adulthood, mirroring the developmental regression often observed in neurodevelopmental conditions including Fragile X Syndrome. Overall, our work reveals systems-level dysfunctions in a rat model of Fragile X Syndrome and their developmental trajectories.

papers.title: Exceptional preservation reveals the deep-time reproductive ecology and trophic breadth of Early Cretaceous viviparid gastropods
papers.abstract: Direct empirical evidence regarding the reproductive biology and trophic strategies of ancient freshwater invertebrates remains scarce due to the typical loss of internal anatomical and dietary records. Here, we report an exceptionally preserved assemblage of the freshwater snail ‘Viviparus’ sp. from the Lower Cretaceous (c. 120 Ma) Kitadani Formation, central Japan. High-resolution X-ray micro-computed tomography and microfossil extraction reveal key ecological adaptations: obligate ovoviviparity with up to 16 embryonic shells showing an axial developmental size gradient within the maternal body whorl, female-biased sexual size dimorphism, and continuous indeterminate growth. Analyses of gastrointestinal residues and taphonomic associations further indicate trophic flexibility (epilithic microalgal grazing, suspension feeding, and detritivory) alongside opportunistic microhabitat use within articulated unionid bivalves. This high-fidelity preservation—retaining delicate embryonic shells, intact protoconchs, and organic residues—is linked to a distinctive taphonomic window, wherein alkaline ash from palaeo-wildfires is inferred to have buffered ambient freshwater acidity, mitigating post-mortem carbonate dissolution. Our findings demonstrate that modern-type viviparid reproductive and feeding adaptations were already established by the Early Cretaceous, illustrating how wildfire-mediated geochemical buffering can preserve rare biological records in Mesozoic limnic ecosystems.

papers.title: Chain-length-selective cooperative assembly underlies β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1
papers.abstract: Lectin receptors recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here we report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin. Native mass spectrometry revealed that laminarin exists as heterogeneous chains spanning a degree of polymerization (DP) of 22–44, while Dectin-1 is strictly monomeric in solution. Isotopic mass tagging with uniformly ¹³C-labeled Dectin-1 established a preferred 3:3 receptor-to-laminarin stoichiometry (~80–85 kDa). Flow-induced dispersion analysis demonstrated cooperative binding with an apparent dissociation constant of 46 μM and a Hill coefficient of ~3, accompanied by a large increase in hydrodynamic radius. Analysis of the bound ligand fraction revealed selective enrichment of chains with DP 25–36, defining a preferred chain-length window. High-speed atomic force microscopy showed that individual Dectin-1 molecules undergo cooperative clustering on both laminarin and the longer β-glucan scleroglucan, while chemical crosslinking provided independent evidence for ligand-induced receptor association. Together, these findings demonstrate that β-glucan recognition by Dectin-1 is governed by chain-length selectivity and cooperative receptor assembly, consistent with a molecular ruler mechanism in which lectin receptors extract specific biological information from heterogeneous glycan populations. Lectin receptors on mammalian cell surfaces recognize specific glycan features within heterogeneous glycan populations to initiate immune signaling, yet how defined signals are extracted from structurally diverse ligand mixtures remains poorly understood. Here the authors report the molecular basis by which the innate immune receptor Dectin-1 recognizes the soluble β-glucan laminarin.

papers.title: Physics-inspired Potts machines of coupled oscillators for low-energy sampling and combinatorial optimization
papers.abstract: Many optimization and sampling problems involve variables with more than two states, beyond the binary Ising model. For the standard q-state Potts model, we introduce an oscillator-based dynamical system that favors low-energy states and can be implemented with coupled oscillators.

papers.title: Direct observation of phase-space dynamics during energetic-particle-driven MHD bursts
papers.abstract: The authors study the phase-space (velocity and real-space) dynamics of bulk ions during an energetic-particle-driven MHD burst in LHD. They find a rapid increase in ion energy parallel to the magnetic field within 0.1 ms of the MHD burst onset, rising by 30% at the MHD burst location and contributing to the rise in core-ion energy.

papers.title: Comparing malaria transmission blocking efficacy of Primaquine and Tafenoquine with in vivo pre-clinical models
papers.abstract: Duffey, Zakutansky, et al compare the transmission-blocking activity and drug exposure of primaquine and tafenoquine in two preclinical malaria models. They find that primaquine shows stronger early activity, while tafenoquine maintains activity for longer, supporting further investigation as a transmission-blocking intervention.

papers.title: Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics model for predicting radiotherapy response in thyroid eye disease
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy is a pivotal treatment for active, moderate-to-severe thyroid eye disease (TED), but responses vary. Conventional indicators such as the clinical activity score (CAS) are subjective and have limited response predictive value. We constructed a multi-sequence predictive model integrating clinical data, conventional imaging, and radiomic features of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict radiotherapy response in TED patients. 85 TED subjects treated with standardized radiotherapy (20 Gy) were retrospectively enrolled. Pre-treatment orbital MRI, including fat-suppressed T1-weighted contrast-enhanced (T1CE) and T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), was analyzed. Radiomic features from extraocular muscles (EOMs) were extracted and selected to develop single-sequence and multi-sequence models as well as integrated models incorporating clinical data, imaging metrics, and radiomic features using nine machine learning algorithms. Models were evaluated using DeLong’s test, calibration curves, Brier scores, decision curve analysis, and SHAP analysis. Among 85 patients, 46 were responders and 39 were non-responders. Baseline CAS was the only clinical variable significantly different between groups. Clinical models showed limited predictive performance (AUC = 0.700), whereas radiomic models achieved higher discrimination, with AUCs of 0.850, 0.875, and 0.933 for T1CE, T2WI, and multi-sequence radiomics, respectively. The integrated model combining radiomic features and imaging metrics achieved the highest AUC (0.942) and significantly outperformed the clinical model (P = 0.040), with favorable reliability and clinical utility in calibration and decision curve. Multi-sequence MRI-based radiomics integrated with conventional imaging metrics provides an objective approach for predicting radiotherapy response in TED. The combined model demonstrated superior discrimination, favorable calibration, and clinical utility compared with clinical prediction approaches, supporting individualized risk stratification after prospective validatio/n. Thyroid eye disease is an autoimmune orbital disorder that causes orbital inflammation and visual impairment. Orbital radiotherapy is widely used to treat active disease, but treatment responses vary substantially across patients, leaving many individuals exposed to unnecessary radiation without clinical benefits. Currently, no reliable preoperative tools can accurately predict radiotherapy outcomes. Here, we developed a simple and non-invasive predictive model based on multi-sequence MRI radiomics. By integrating multi-sequence radiomic features, orbital conventional imaging metrics and clinical indicators, our optimized model accurately distinguishes radiotherapy responders from non-responders before treatment. This quantitative tool helps guide individualized decision-making, reduce ineffective radiotherapy, and advance personalized management for thyroid eye disease.

papers.title: Passive and continuous assessment of subjective sleep quality using smartwatches
papers.abstract: Hausner et al. develop a machine learning framework combining commercial smartwatch data with individual characteristics to assess subjective sleep quality. The model achieves high performance in distinguishing extreme levels of self-reported sleep quality, opening the possibility of passive and continuous assessment of subjective sleep quality.

Widespread North American pollution and health impacts from early twentieth century copper production
papers.abstract: Mining and industrial emissions can be substantially reduced by technological interventions. The historical case of copper production in Anaconda, Montana shows the widespread health burdens that can result when lax regulation delays such interventions.

papers.title: Agricultural data source choice as a dominant control on nitrogen surplus uncertainty
papers.abstract: Environmental impacts from nitrogen surplus in agricultural regions make it critical to understand the nature and drivers of excess nitrogen. Bhaduri and colleagues show that data source uncertainty must be accounted for to avoid misalignments in management and mitigation decisions.

papers.title: Blood-based RNA biomarker for the early detection of ovarian cancer
papers.abstract: Tested in a cohort of 506 individuals, the RNA-based biomarker of microenvironment fitness Tu-stroma shows high performance in discriminating early-stage ovarian cancer from benign lesions, outperforming CA125.

papers.title: Bioprinting, ten years on: from shape to function
papers.abstract: Bioprinting has moved from building organ-like shapes that keep cells alive to constructs judged by function. However, function only emerges when computational design, printing hardware and instructive bioinks are coupled in one process. Making this coupling routine and reproducible is essential for translating printed tissues into credible therapies and models.

papers.title: TrkA<sup>+</sup> sensory nerves coordinate regeneration through NGF-associated regulation of mitochondrial homeostasis
papers.abstract: Sensory nerves are emerging as critical regulators of musculoskeletal repair through neurotrophic signaling, vascular interactions, and direct communication with bone-resident cells. While their requirement for regeneration is well established, the specific contributions of distinct sensory nerve subtypes and their underlying mechanisms remain poorly defined. Mammalian digit tip regeneration provides a unique model to study this process, as it recapitulates complete tissue replacement, including bone, nail organ, and marrow. Previous studies using denervation or altered mechanical loading demonstrate that neural input controls regeneration but do not resolve subtype-specific functions. Here, we identify TrkA/NGF signaling as a dominant sensory nerve-associated pathway during digit regeneration using spatial transcriptomics and functional interrogation in TrkAF592A mice. Selective inhibition of TrkA signaling reduced regeneration, decreasing proliferation while accelerating osteogenic differentiation during the patent blastema phase, resulting in a shortened regenerate. Mechanistically, TrkA/NGF disruption induced a compensatory increase in NGF expression within the blastema, associated with increased mitochondrial fusion and fatty acid oxidation (FAO). This NGF-associated shift in mitochondrial dynamics promoted osteogenic differentiation, linking neurotrophin signaling to cellular metabolism and fate decisions. Together, these findings establish a central role for TrkA+ sensory nerves in coordinating regenerative timing and patterning and identify NGF-mediated regulation of mitochondrial homeostasis as a potential therapeutic target for enhancing bone repair.

papers.title: Synthetic data to lower barriers towards equitable artificial intelligence in rapid diagnostic test interpretation
papers.abstract: Rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs) support affordable disease diagnosis. Machine learning (ML) can improve RDT interpretation but often relies on large, proprietary, and costly real-world image libraries. We present SynSight – a ML-enabled RDT segmentation and classification pipeline trained on synthetic data. Validated on HIV (98% sensitivity, 99% specificity) and COVID-19 RDTs (up to 99% accuracy), SynSight enables rapid ML training without real-world training images, keeping pace with new RDT development.

papers.title: Multimodal cell foundation models require synergistic integration beyond alignment
papers.abstract: Integrating measurements across modalities and scales into unified quantitative frameworks of cellular function is a central goal in computational biology. Although powerful unimodal foundation models exist, the scarcity of large-scale paired data limits joint multimodal training. This constraint favours compositional foundation models, which fuse frozen unimodal experts through a learned interface. However, it remains unclear when such fusion provides task-relevant information beyond the strongest unimodal representation rather than merely aggregating redundant signal. Here we introduce Synergistic Information Score, a metric grounded in partial information decomposition that quantifies information gain arising only from cross-modal interactions. Extending theory from self-supervised learning, we show that standard alignment-based objectives with frozen encoders collapse to detect linear redundancies, which constrains their ability to capture nonlinear synergistic states. This distinction is especially important for tasks that connect tissue morphology with gene expression. Benchmarking ten fusion methods on spatial transcriptomics datasets, we demonstrate that tasks dominated by linear redundancies are well served by unimodal baselines, whereas complex niche definitions benefit from synergy-aware integration. Finally, we perform a scaling analysis and show that fine-tuning a dominant unimodal expert is the most sample-efficient strategy for standard tasks. Together, these results suggest that progress in multimodal modelling of cellular state requires shifting from alignment-based objectives to synergy-driven integration that exploits complementary cross-modal signal. Richter et al. show that simply aligning different types of biological data does not fully integrate them, revealing when data repeat the same information and, conversely, when they provide complementary insights.

papers.abstract: Stereochemistry greatly influences polymer structure and assembly, yet its use in controlling polymer network topology remains underexplored. Now, homochiral self-sorting is used to suppress primary-loop formation in end-linked polymer networks, offering a strategy for controlling network topology.

papers.title: Bound states in the continuum through quantum interference in ultracold atomic collisions
papers.abstract: Resonances in ultracold collisions couple to scattering states, causing interactions and loss. Now it is shown that the interference of Feshbach resonances creates a bound state in the continuum that decouples from elastic and inelastic scattering.

papers.title: Active-flow-driven DNA remodelling generates millimetre-scale mechanical oscillations
papers.abstract: Active matter can exhibit turbulent or coherent flows. Now it is shown that active flows can entangle DNA polymers, leading to a non-equilibrium transition from disordered turbulence to periodic motion.

papers.title: Mitsunobu reactions using iminophosphorane reagents
papers.abstract: The Mitsunobu reaction is one of the most celebrated reactions in organic synthesis, enabling stereospecific C–O, C–N and C–S bond formation from abundant alcohol feedstocks. However, its widespread use is constrained by the need for explosive reagents, laborious product purification and a pronucleophile pKa window that precludes C–C bond formation. Here we disclose iminophosphoranes as a class of reagents for the Mitsunobu reaction that readily overcome these limitations. The key iminophosphorane reagent is rapidly and quantitively formed in situ from commercially available 1-azido-4-methoxybenzene and a trialkylphosphine, allowing the construction of C–O, C–N, C–S and, notably, C–C bonds from primary and secondary alcohol substrates with vastly simplified product purification. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the direct use of a solution of preformed iminophosphorane eliminates end-user azide handling altogether. The utility of the reaction was demonstrated through reaction scale-up and late-stage functionalization of pharmaceutically relevant compounds. An in situ-generated iminophosphorane enables C–O, C–N, C–S and C–C bond formation from primary and secondary alcohols. The process overcomes the pronucleophile pKa limitation associated with traditional Mitsunobu reactions while simplifying purification and avoiding the requirement for explosive azodicarboxylate reagents.

papers.title: Data centres asymmetrically exacerbate energy burdens through wholesale price increases and regressive grid cost shifting
papers.abstract: As data centres increase pressure on power systems, the costs of accommodating their growth are becoming a concern. Here the researchers show that data centres raise wholesale prices and shift transmission costs onto households, with the largest burden increases in rural and low-income communities.

papers.title: Craft and engineering

papers.title: Open-source hardware for biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Open-source biomanufacturing hardware, such as liquid handlers and bioprinters, can approach commercial performance at substantially lower cost, but many designs remain poorly documented, inconsistently validated and difficult to maintain. To address these challenges, we developed the DIY Biofabrication Atlas, a public resource based on curated paper records and publication metadata, with standardized reporting of cost, components and performance.

Nature Reviews Materials speaks with Liangbing Hu, professor at Yale University and founder of InventWood, about the development of Superwood, the diversification of wood-based technologies and the path towards commercialization.
