papers.title: Biomass-derived bamboo photonic crystals for narrowband lasing
papers.abstract: Narrowband multicolor lasing is crucial for advancing bioimaging, biosensing, and optoelectronic displays, yet current photonic crystal substrates face challenges in biocompatibility and energy efficiency. Here, the authors achieve narrowband multicolor lasing by coupling quantum dot emission with bamboo-derived photonic crystals, enhancing biocompatibility and biodegradability while simplifying fabrication, thus expanding applications in biomedicine and sustainable optoelectronics.

papers.title: Vacuum Evaporation Enabled Economical and Eco-Friendly Composite Copper Current Collectors
papers.abstract: The composite copper current collector holds enormous potential for boosting the energy density and safety of lithium-ion batteries, yet manufacturing throughput and substrate cost remain key barriers to its widespread adoption. Here, we demonstrate a hybrid manufacturing technique combining designed vacuum evaporation and electroplating that achieves sub-second (0.38 s) metallization of economical polyethene terephthalate, dramatically improving throughput. The as-fabricated composite copper current collector demonstrates favourable attributes, including electrochemical stability and significant weight savings. For the composite copper current collector-graphite electrode, it would achieve an over 11% increase in whole electrode specific capacity, even compared to the 4.5 μm pure copper foil at 6.5 mAh cm−2. This performance translates to the potential for extending electric vehicle range and saving 19.44 ~ 22.28 GWh in the production of lithium-ion batteries in 2025. Beyond performance, this work includes a life-cycle assessment, unveiling a reduced carbon footprint and substantial global copper conservation enabled by composite copper current collector, while also elucidating its intrinsic safety mechanism. These findings offer a potential pathway for fabricating sustainable and high-safety lithium-ion batteries.

papers.title: Allosteric network rewiring governs enzyme functional duality via a distal switch
papers.abstract: How specialist enzymes reconcile the fundamental trade-off between catalytic fidelity and functional promiscuity within a conserved active site is a central paradox in enzymology. Using a representative Type II meso-DAPDH enzyme from Symbiobacterium thermophilum (StDAPDH) as our model system, we identify the distal residue M176 as a switch whose substitutions decouple the enzyme’s amination and deamination activities. We find that substitutions at this site are associated with substrate-dependent reorganization of the enzyme’s intra-subunit contact-correlation network. These network changes are accompanied by distinct substrate-dissociation free-energy profiles and catalytic outcomes, including activity retention, inhibition, and functional decoupling. Combined simulations and mutational analyses support the functional importance of specific residues associated with functional decoupling, while distinguishing recurring network-level features from putative residue-level routes. Together, these results provide an ensemble-based view of functional duality in Type II meso-DAPDH and suggest that distal network modulation may aid the engineering of substrate-dependent enzyme activities.

papers.title: The sympathoadrenal contribution to inferior vena cava formation
papers.abstract: Although vascular development is fundamental during embryogenesis, the developmental basis and tissue interactions underlying anatomical variation in major veins are not fully understood. The renal segment of the inferior vena cava exhibits significant anatomical variations that often affect the safety of retroperitoneal surgery. Using mouse embryos, we show that the renal segment of the inferior vena cava is not primarily dependent on the subcardinal vein as classically proposed, but instead forms from a vascular plexus closely associated with the developing para-aortic ridge. Genetic models further indicate that sympathoadrenal development in the para-aortic ridge contributes to the proper organization and remodeling of this vascular network. This revised developmental framework highlights a sympathoadrenal–vascular coupling as a developmental basis for inferior vena cava formation and thereby challenges classical subcardinal vein-dependent models.

papers.title: Corticosteroid treatment dysregulates perirhinal circadian rhythms and synaptic function in rats
papers.abstract: Chronic synthetic glucocorticoid treatment disrupts perirhinal cortex circadian rhythms, synaptic plasticity, and the proteome, shedding light on molecular mechanisms underlying cognitive side-effects of widespread clinical therapies.

papers.title: Principles of coarse-scale functional organization in occipitotemporal cortex
papers.abstract: Occipitotemporal cortex (OTC) is known to support visual object processing, yet identifying general principles underlying its coarse-scale functional organization remains challenging. Previously proposed organizational dimensions, such as animacy or real-world size, may not generalize to more diverse, naturalistic stimuli and strong intercorrelations of object properties complicate determining which dimensions, if any, dominate OTC organization. We addressed these challenges through detailed analyses of the cortical topography underlying 15 object properties, using fMRI responses to thousands of natural images, focusing on animacy and size given their established prominence. Our results confirm many characteristics of the purported animacy-size organization, but reveal distinctions that challenge dominant notions of this organization, highlighting the importance of generalizing to large-scale naturalistic data. Beyond animacy and size, many properties could alternatively serve as organizational dimensions, yet none emerges as clearly dominant throughout OTC. Together, our findings reveal a more refined animacy-size organization than previously assumed and highlight challenges of assigning individual principles to account for OTC organization.

papers.title: Machine-learning-guided discovery of selective CK2 inhibitors with reduced CDK off-target activity
papers.abstract: A key challenge in drug development is identification of druggable targets, the modulation of which attenuates disease progression, while avoiding inhibition of proteins that lead to dose-limiting toxicities. Here, we investigate a drug target, casein kinase 2 (CK2) - a serine/threonine kinase implicated in multiple cancers - for which existing inhibitors have so far failed in clinical trials. Using molecular and pharmacoepidemiology approaches, we show that small molecules targeting cyclin-dependent kinase (CDK) family members CDK1/2/7/9, including the existing CK2 inhibitors, have a higher risk to induce adverse effects or failing in clinical trials. We then establish a machine learning (ML)-assisted discovery pipeline to redesign more specific and allosteric lead compounds against CK2, with more selective on-target binding and favourable off-target profile. Importantly, we show that such selective design is possible when standard molecular docking, CDK-liability filtering and ML algorithms are combined with an error prediction model. Taken together, we report a simple yet efficient ML-powered drug discovery pipeline and novel submicromolar inhibitors targeting the clinically relevant CK2 kinase with no clinically approved antagonists currently available. Our prediction pipeline was able to achieve a 90% hit-rate, significantly reducing the need for subsequent wet-lab validation.

papers.title: Integrating noncanonical amino acids and synthetic cofactors for the development of artificial metalloenzymes
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes harness the sophisticated synergy between canonical amino acids and metal cofactors to catalyze life-sustaining reactions. However, the limited chemical diversity of the twenty standard amino acids often restricts non-natural transformations. To overcome these constraints, artificial metalloenzymes (ArMs) integrate synthetic cofactors into protein scaffolds to enable unnatural catalytic functions. This review highlights how noncanonical amino acids (ncAAs) bridge the gap between natural enzyme architecture and synthetic chemistry. We examine genetic code expansion and codon optimization technologies as robust strategies for the site-specific incorporation of ncAAs. By introducing unique chemical moieties—such as chelating groups, photo-responsive elements, and bio-orthogonal handles—ncAAs enable precise mechanistic probing of active sites and the rational design of biomimetic centers. Furthermore, we discuss the strategic use of ncAAs in anchoring metal ions and large-sized synthetic cofactors via bio-orthogonal reactions, allowing for the creation of hybrid catalysts that maintain structural integrity while exhibiting novel reactivity. Ultimately, the combinatorial design of ncAAs and synthetic cofactors provides a transformative toolkit for protein engineering. Integrating these structural elements transcends natural limitations, laying a foundation for ArMs with enhanced catalytic efficiency, expanded substrate scope and programmable activity for industrial and therapeutic applications.

papers.title: Wrist photoplethysmography encodes dietary information
papers.abstract: Whether wearable photoplethysmography (PPG) encodes dietary information remains unknown. We trained a language model on 1.1M meals to align PPG with meal descriptions. Near-meal PPG carries a meal-specific signal beyond individual traits; predictability decreases farther from meals. This transfers to dietary tasks: PPG increases AUC by 11% for a caloric-intake proxy and satiety across held-out and independent cohorts. Wearable PPG may augment text-based logging, compensating for brief descriptions.

papers.title: MambaSleepCVD for prediction of long term cardiovascular outcomes from polysomnography
papers.abstract: Long-term cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk prediction remains a major global clinical priority. This study investigates how much prognostic information full-night polysomnography (PSG) carries after explicitly controlling demographic confounding, and whether combining specialized unimodal representations with continuous fusion mechanisms can effectively leverage it. We adopt a modular framework based on Coupled Mamba for simultaneous cross-modal and temporal fusion, capturing long-range dependencies and dynamic interactions between physiological modalities throughout sleep. With this capability, we assess whether specialized supervised representations from task-specific unimodal encoders offer prognostic value comparable to task-agnostic multimodal self-supervised pre-training. Validated on the Sleep Heart Health Study (SHHS) dataset, our approach achieves performance comparable to or better than current state-of-the-art architectures in the fully supervised, data-abundant regime, although the cardiac channel alone accounts for most of the discriminative signal. More importantly, we show that in the reference dataset chronological age strongly drives survival ranking; when provided as an explicit input, it can create a shortcut that obscures the contribution of PSG-derived physiology. Ultimately, our findings suggest that supervised unimodal experts integrated through a fusion engine provide a flexible pathway for prognostic risk ranking from sleep recordings, while reliable CVD screening will require independent external cohorts and explicit confounder control.

papers.title: An All‐Natural Multifunctional Hydrogel Incorporating Carrier‐Free Self‐Assembled Microparticles for the Treatment of S. aureus‐Infected Wounds
papers.abstract: Advanced Healthcare Materials, EarlyView.

papers.title: In Vivo CRISPR Base Editing of ANGPTL3 for Durable Lipid Lowering
papers.abstract: Circulating concentrations of low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and triglyceride-rich lipoproteins are leading risk factors for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease1. Despite several approved lipid-lowering medications, most patients fail to achieve target lipid levels under the chronic care treatment model2,3. Here, we describe a potential single-course treatment in which an infusion of guide RNA and mRNA encoding a CRISPR adenine base editor—encapsulated within a GalNAc–lipid nanoparticle—leads to durable, liver-selective inactivation of angiopoietin-like 3 (ANGPTL3), a known driver of increased LDL-C and triglyceride concentrations. Analyses in human liver cells in vitro confirmed that the base editor introduces a DNA base-pair change at the target ANGPTL3 locus with no detectable off-target editing at any of approximately 3000 candidate sites or treatment-related structural variants. Targeted ANGPTL3 inactivation in nonhuman primates was well-tolerated and led to a > 90% mean reduction in circulating ANGPTL3 protein, with durability confirmed out to 3 years following a single dose. In mouse and nonhuman primate models of hyperlipidemia, gene inactivation was associated with reductions of approximately 40 to 50% in LDL-C and 50 to 70% in triglycerides. These results provided the scientific foundation for initiation of an ongoing first-in-human clinical trial in patients with refractory hyperlipidemia syndromes.

papers.title: In situ CAR engineering and nanoparticle-mediated TREM2 degradation for macrophage reprogramming in malignant ascites
papers.abstract: Targeted lipid nanoparticles reprogram TREM2 + -tumour-associated macrophages in ascitic fluid into chimeric antigen receptor macrophage cells, providing an in situ cell engineering strategy that alters the tumour microenvironment and promotes tumour cell elimination in rodent models.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal intensity-cycling microscopy unveils many-body interactions and correlated transport in van der Waals semiconductors
papers.abstract: Intensity-cycling spatiotemporal microscopy separates single-particle and multi-particle transport, enabling imaging of charge mobility, exciton interactions, and correlated many-body states in van der Waals semiconductors, including Mott transitions.

papers.title: Towards ecologically meaningful foundation models
papers.abstract: Ecology aims to explain and predict how organisms interact with each other and their environments across space and time. Yet both ecological data and theory are fragmented, leading to models that generalize poorly beyond specific systems or scales. Empirical evidence spans diverse modalities, resolutions and contexts, while theory is distributed across partially overlapping frameworks that are rarely integrated within a single predictive model. We argue that ecological foundation models (ecoFMs), trained on large, multi-modal ecological datasets and informed by ecological theory, offer a route towards unifying data and theory within a common framework. Beyond their scientific value for ecology, ecoFMs present a challenging and consequential testbed for machine learning, demanding advances in multi-modal representation learning, theory-guided modelling and uncertainty-aware inference. By learning shared representations of organisms, environments and interactions, ecoFMs could improve generalization, link pattern to process and enable synthesis across ecological subdisciplines. We outline a roadmap for developing ecoFMs, including requirements for data infrastructure, model architectures, evaluation strategies and governance, and assess where current machine learning and ecological approaches fall short. If developed responsibly and collaboratively with ecological practitioners and other actors, ecoFMs could enable new modes of analysis and strengthen ecological forecasting, while simultaneously driving advances in machine learning for multi-modal integration, theory-guided learning and generalization in complex, data-limited systems. Ecology struggles to make broad predictions, as ecological data and theories are scattered across many different sources, scales and approaches. Gardiner et al. propose to create ecological foundation models, which combine large, multi-modal ecological datasets with ecological theory, as a way to create more generalizable and predictive models.

papers.title: Cas12a-based combinatorial knockout screens define the genetic architecture of the DNA damage response
papers.abstract: A genetic interaction map of the DNA damage response (DDR) identifies functional relationships among DDR genes and pathways.

papers.title: IDR acquisition from human ortholog reprograms Snf11 to form HDAC-compartmentalizing condensates and drives yeast flocculation
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) regulates protein function by organizing proteins into dynamic condensates, yet how divergence in LLPS among orthologs gives rise to species-specific functional outputs remains poorly understood. Here, we show that intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) act as transferable modules whose sequence composition encodes phase separation capacity and functional outputs. Incorporating the QPGY domain from human SS18 into its yeast ortholog Snf11 yields a chimeric protein (Snf11-QPGY) that forms dynamic intracellular condensates. These condensates activate the adhesion genes FLO1 and FLO11, triggering calcium-dependent flocculation absent in wild-type cells. Mechanistically, Snf11-QPGY sequesters histone deacetylase subunit Rpd3 within condensates, reducing its occupancy at FLO promoters and promoting histone acetylation and transcriptional activation. Substituting QPGY with a heterologous LLPS-competent IDR restores condensate formation but does not recapitulate QPGY-driven transcriptional-phenotypic outputs. These findings reveal how evolutionary diversification of IDR sequences drives functional divergence among orthologs and offer a framework for engineering IDR-dependent regulatory modules.

papers.title: DECTIN1 + myeloid-derived suppressor cells mediate therapeutic effect of MSCs in haplo-HSCT for severe aplastic anemia
papers.abstract: Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a life-threatening bone marrow failure disorder marked by pancytopenia and marrow hypoplasia. As a promising therapeutic option, haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (haplo-HSCT) is still limited by graft rejection and delayed immune reconstitution, which can be effectively mitigated by mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) coinfusion. Here, we demonstrated that haplo-HSCT significantly restored the proportion and immunosuppressive capacity of bone marrow myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs) in SAA patients, and DECTIN1+MDSCs emerged as central immunoregulators. MSC coinfusion further enhanced this effect. Mechanistically, MSC-derived exosomal ANXA2 upregulated DECTIN1 expression in MDSCs, which in turn activated STAT3 signaling to increase TNFAIP3 expression, thereby suppressing inflammatory T-cell responses. These changes were also reflected in peripheral blood. Human bone marrow organoid experiments confirmed that MSC coinfusion promoted DECTIN1+MDSC expansion and accelerated bone marrow microenvironment recovery. Our findings revealed a previously unrecognized MSC-mediated mechanism and highlighted DECTIN1+MDSCs as key immunoregulatory mediators and potential therapeutic targets in SAA.

papers.title: Lunar and Martian regolith simulants compromise airway barrier function and trigger inflammation
papers.abstract: Little is known on the health risks for the astronauts exposed to space-derived materials such as regolith, the mixture of dust and rock particles covering the surfaces of Moon and Mars. We combine an in vitro model of exposure of human airway epithelial and peripheral blood mononuclear cells to regolith, with an in vivo murine exposure model, to assess the effects of Martian and Lunar regolith simulants. Exposure to both Moon or Mars regolith causes cellular cytotoxicity and induced strong proinflammatory responses in vitro. In mice, intranasal regolith exposure impairs epithelial barrier integrity in the airways, increases pro-fibrotic gene expression, immune cell recruitment, and elevates amounts of inflammatory proteins in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid. Lunar regolith simulant LMS-1 shows particularly strong barrier-damaging and inflammatory effects in differentiated bronchial epithelial cells and in the in vivo mouse model. These findings highlight regolith as an airway irritant driving inflammation and barrier dysfunction, underscoring the need for dust mitigation strategies to protect astronaut health during long-term space missions on Moon or Mars.

papers.title: The subcommissural organ secretes SCO-spondin, associated with stress response and mood
papers.abstract: The subcommissural organ (SCO) is an evolutionarily conserved structure in the brains of vertebrates, but its function remains largely unknown. The protein SCO-spondin, exclusively produced by the SCO, may hold the key to understanding its function. Here, by whole exome sequencing of a family with schizoaffective disorder, we identified a protein-truncating variant (PTV) mutation in the SCO-spondin gene (SSPOP) segregating with this disease. To explore the potential role of this gene in this mood disorder, we generated a mouse model carrying this mutation in the SCO-spondin gene (Sspo). We conducted behavioral tests and multi-omics studies on male mice. The mouse model exhibited abnormal mood-related behaviors, including heightened anxiety, reduced stress-induced depression-like behaviors, and increased prepulse inhibition. Multi-transcriptomics, encompassing whole-brain, spatial, and single-cell transcriptomics, revealed dysregulated genes in the SCO and CSF-contacting brain regions. These genes are linked to stress response and human mood disorders, involving molecular pathways and cell-cell communications related to the CSF-barrier cells. This comprehensive study elucidates the role of SCO in stress response and mood regulation through a novel regulatory axis: the SCO-CSF-barrier axis.

papers.title: Transcriptomic biomarkers reveal jasmonic and salicylic acid states under field herbivory in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.abstract: Plants coordinate defence against pathogens and herbivores through the crosstalk between salicylic acid (SA) and jasmonic acid (JA) signalling pathways. However, little is known about how plants integrate the phytohormone concentration profiles to shape defence states in complex field environments. Here we show that systematically varying combinatorial SA and JA concentrations in Arabidopsis thaliana reveals 43 distinct combination-specific transcriptional signatures beyond SA–JA antagonism. Leveraging these data, we develop and validate machine-learning-based transcriptomic biomarkers that independently measure the SA and JA response states from gene-expression data. Applying these biomarkers to field-grown A. thaliana shows that SA/JA response states are associated with the abundance and co-occurrence patterns of herbivores on individual plants. Our study provides a strategy for decoding hormonal responses to biotic environments from field transcriptomes, bridging the gap between molecular signalling and ecological dynamics.

papers.title: Interpretable side reaction detection via atom representations derived from multi-tier reaction perspectives
papers.abstract: Recent deep learning-based methods have advanced chemical retrosynthesis. However, they neglect side reactions, strong competitors to desired synthesis reactions that reduce the yield of anticipated product molecules. To identify side-reaction sites, we introduce an atom representation learning framework, SideReact, which explores synthesis reactions from a top-down chemical perspective (i.e., from reaction to motif, to property, and to quantum w.r.t. atoms). Its multi-tier atom encoder (MtAE) extracts top-down observations as atom representations, including reaction paradigms, motif reactivities and co-reactivities, atomic identities and bonding circumstances, and atoms' electron-attracting abilities. Moreover, its hierarchical cross-attention module (HCA) captures the chemical hierarchy among encoding tiers in a bottom-up way. Especially, HCA enables an interpretable path through the hierarchy to reveal how to find reaction sites among atoms in reactants. The comparison with ten state-of-the-art methods demonstrates the superiority of SideReact in both side reactions and desired reactions. Furthermore, a real case study, including ten synthetic examples in textbooks, a complex synthetic reaction of Atorvastatin with side-reaction sites, and a synthetic reaction for a drug-like molecule, substantiates the effectiveness of SideReact. More importantly, analyses demonstrate how its MtAE works and how its HCA unveils the interpretable inference of side-reaction sites, highlighting its potential in retrosynthesis planning.

papers.title: Conformational inhibitors of the HIV-1 Rev response element identified through a FRET-based screening approach
papers.abstract: The complex formed between the HIV-1 protein Rev and the Rev Response Element (RRE) in the genomic RNA of the virus represents an attractive target for antiretroviral therapy. To date, however, there are no RRE-Rev inhibitors in clinical use. In this study we have applied a fluorescence resonance energy transfer (FRET) assay based on placing Cy3- and Cy5-labeled oligomeric probes at distal domain locations within the RRE to identify small-molecule compounds capable of perturbing the spatial organization of RRE domains and disrupting the association of Rev monomers. After screening a library of bioactive compounds and approved drugs, we identified two molecules, myricetin and raloxifene, that recognize the RRE and inhibit the RRE-Rev interaction in vitro and in cellulo. Both compounds exhibited antiretroviral activity with favorable selectivity indexes, and further analyses involving RRE mutants suggested that myricetin modulated the conformation of the RRE through binding to a four-helix intersection. Collectively, these findings provide proof of concept for targeting the RRE-Rev complex and identify myricetin and raloxifene as promising starting points for the development of novel anti-HIV agents.

papers.title: Rapid peptide mapping of monoclonal antibodies with direct infusion mass spectrometry
papers.abstract: Peptide mapping is a critical tool for characterizing biotherapeutic proteins and is essential for the development of monoclonal antibody drugs. Here we describe a new direct infusion technology that streamlines peptide mapping data collection and analysis, accelerating the method by up to 100-fold. This method, which we term RaPiD-mAb-MS, combines high-throughput plate-based sample preparation with direct infusion mass spectrometry analysis. RaPiD-mAb-MS allows analysis of 96 samples within ~ 1.5 to 2 hours, routinely achieves >95% sequence coverage, and has been successfully applied to 28 unique antibodies and over 2000 samples. Here we demonstrate that RaPiD-mAb-MS detects and quantifies oxidation, deamidation, isomerization, glycosylation, and sequence variants with results comparable to conventional LC-MS based methods in a fraction of the time. Further, by eliminating chromatography, data analysis is greatly streamlined and simplified. By allowing for the collection of ~ 1000 peptide maps per day, RaPiD-mAb-MS is positioned to accelerate all phases of antibody-based drug discovery & development and sets the stage for collection of massive datasets that would allow artificial intelligent prediction of optimal antibody variants and formulations.

papers.title: Harvesting magic resource in curved spacetime
papers.abstract: The quantum vacuum is not really empty; it is a reservoir of operationally accessible non-classical resources. Understanding how to extract these resources, especially in curved spacetime, to fuel information processing is one of the core objectives in quantum technologies and lies at the heart of relativistic quantum information (RQI). We investigate the harvesting of non-stabilizerness by a qutrit Unruh-DeWitt detector interacting with a scalar field in anti-de Sitter spacetime, which is intractable by using traditional numerical integral method. To this end, we develop an analytic series method to deal with divergence of the coherence, which has remained largely overlooked in RQI and even in quantum field theory. We show that stronger spacetime curvature and higher dimensionality significantly suppress the amount of extractable magic resource from the vacuum. Our series method can have broad application in quantum theories and field theories.

papers.title: Trajectory and genetic correlation mapping of cross-disease risks following incident type 2 inflammatory diseases
papers.abstract: Type 2 inflammatory diseases (T2IDs) such as atopic dermatitis (AD), asthma, food allergy, eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE), chronic sinusitis (CS), and others, are immune-mediated conditions that frequently co-occur across organ systems and contribute to substantial disease burden. While the atopic march has long served as a conceptual model for T2ID progression, it remains unclear whether this linear sequence captures the broader comorbidity structure of T2IDs. We systematically analyzed comorbidity patterns across nine T2IDs using two complementary methods: Large-scale real-world data (RWD) from over 129 million electronic health records, genome-wide and local genetic correlation, including three novel (asthma, chronic sinusitis, allergic rhinitis) metanalyses of genome-wide association studies. Retrospective matched cohort analyses reveal a highly interconnected disease network in which CS emerged as a central node, increasing the risk of multiple other T2IDs across diverse patient populations. AD, food allergy, and vasomotor and allergic rhinitis also show strong cross-disease effects. Subgroup analyses uncover notable age-, sex-, and race-specific disparities. Genetic correlation analyses support shared heritability among many disease pairs, complemented by the temporal ordering of associations present in the RWD. Local genetic correlation position asthma as the central node of the shared polygenic architecture, converging on canonical type 2 inflammatory loci. Together, our results highlight that T2ID progression extends beyond the atopic march and is shaped by a complex and heterogeneous network of interactions. This work provides a data-driven framework to guide risk stratification, inform early preventive strategies, and prioritize upstream disease targets within the type 2 inflammatory spectrum. Some long-lasting diseases, for example such as eczema, asthma, food allergy and ongoing sinus inflammation, are driven by the same kind of overactive immune response. People who develop one often go on to develop others, but the order in which they appear is not well understood. We studied health records from more than 129 million people to see which conditions tended to follow which. We also compared the genetic make-up behind each condition. We found that these diseases form a connected network rather than a fixed sequence. Ongoing sinus inflammation often appeared first and was followed by several others. Risks also differed by age, sex and ethnic background. Knowing which condition may come next could help doctors identify people at risk earlier.

papers.title: Coherence enhancement through equilibration to near-zero optical temperatures
papers.abstract: Phase-space conservation bars coherence enhancement in passive linear optics, a limit often bypassed by gain or feedback. Here conservative nonlinearity reshapes phase space, thermodynamically driving incoherent light towards a coherent equilibrium.

papers.title: All-optical thin-film lithium niobate memristor
papers.abstract: Photonic memristors are essential components for neuromorphic optical computing, but their integration with optical waveguide platforms currently relies on complex fabrication procedures with high manufacturing costs. Here we show that thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a widely adopted photonic platform, can be transformed into an all-optically controlled memristive material, enabling the direct fabrication of photonic memristors on TFLN without the need for heterogeneous integration. Through a complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible oxygen-ion implantation process, spatially separated oxygen-doped and defect-rich layers are formed in TFLN, enabling all-optically controlled refractive index modulation. The resulting oxygen-implanted devices exhibit 3-bit multilevel non-volatile memory, ultralow switching energy of hundreds of femtojoules per bit, submicrosecond optical response and long data retention over extended operation. Wafer-scale production of TFLN and complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor-compatible ion implantation thus provide a homogeneous, scalable and programmable material platform for integrated photonic circuits and systems, with the potential for future large-scale photonic neural networks. Oxygen-ion implantation allows the direct fabrication of photonic memristors in thin-film lithium niobate. The resulting devices combine 3-bit non-volatile optical memory, submicrosecond responses and femtojoule-level switching energies.

papers.title: Synthesis of molecular 8 5 and 5 1 knots from azaindolyl bithiophene ligands
papers.abstract: A low-symmetry eight-crossing knot was assembled from a binuclear rhodium unit and a semi-rigid ligand featuring a conformationally flexible bithiophene spacer and π -stacking azaindole donors. Size-directed assembly of the same system also afforded a five-crossing knot.

papers.title: Ab initio simulation of excited-state potential energy surfaces with transferable deep quantum Monte Carlo
papers.abstract: Transferable deep-learning quantum Monte Carlo for molecular excited states is introduced. Sharing parameters, an ansatz represents the wavefunction across molecular geometries and states, reducing the cost of modeling potential energy surfaces.

papers.title: Photocatalytic nitrogen reduction to high-concentration ammonia via interfacial evaporation
papers.abstract: Synthesis of valuable ammonia through photocatalytic reduction of nitrogen is a promising sustainable route, but its efficiency remains limited. This work shows that coupling the reaction with solar-driven interfacial evaporation can substantially improve ammonia yield, concentration and purity.

papers.title: A gait foundation model for prediction of multisystem health phenotypes from 3D skeletal motion
papers.abstract: A gait foundation model, developed using three-dimensional skeletal motion data from 3,328 adults, predicts a wide array of clinical characteristics and diagnoses, including cardiometabolic, mental health and frailty phenotypes.

papers.title: Evaluation of PainWaive: a consumer-grade EEG headset for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain
papers.abstract: Affordable electroencephalography (EEG) headsets could widen access to EEG-based treatment and assessment, but require rigorous validation. We evaluated PainWaive, a custom-developed 2-channel central scalp EEG headset designed for remote EEG monitoring and neurofeedback research in chronic pain. Eighty participants completed two resting-state EEGs using PainWaive and a research-grade system (LiveAmp). Alpha, beta and theta power, and peak alpha frequency (PAF), were derived from homologous central channels. PainWaive demonstrated good-to-excellent test-retest reliability for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.72–0.93), with beta and theta ranging from moderate-good (ICCs = 0.42–0.76). Across 160 home-based neurofeedback sessions in two chronic pain samples, reliability was good-to-excellent across metrics (ICCs = 0.72–0.88). Spectral-shape correlations between PainWaive and LiveAmp were excellent (r > 0.91). Cross-device agreement was moderate-to-good for alpha power and PAF (ICCs = 0.53–0.74), but weaker for beta and theta (ICCs = 0.16–0.51). Sensitivity analyses showed alpha power and PAF were robust across choices, whereas beta and theta agreement varied by pipeline. Overall, PainWaive demonstrated reliable measurement of central scalp EEG metrics, supporting repeated within-device monitoring. Cross-device findings showed correspondence with research-grade EEG for some measures but should not be interpreted as establishing direct numerical interchangeability between systems. These findings provide a technical foundation for future remote EEG and neurofeedback studies in chronic pain.

papers.title: Opportunistically Detecting Signs of Hypertension on a Consumer Smartwatch
papers.abstract: Hypertension is a silent killer, with over half of affected adults unaware of their condition1,2. This lack of awareness is a major concern, as early intervention is critical for preventing major adverse cardiovascular events3,4. Here we show that applying artificial intelligence (AI) to multimodal waveforms (photoplethysmography and accelerometry) recorded using a widely available consumer smartwatch (AI-PPG-ACC-HTN), without any cuff calibration, can detect hypertension with accuracy levels comparable to traditional cuffed blood pressure (BP) devices in the existing clinical framework. We validated AI-PPG-ACC-HTN in a prospective, multicenter study of 196 diverse participants free from known cardiovascular disease and antihypertensive medication against gold-standard 24-hour ambulatory BP monitoring. Over seven days of real-world monitoring, AI-PPG-ACC-HTN detected hypertension with a sensitivity of 65.8% (95% CI, 54.0%-76.3%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%), and positive predictive value (PPV) of 80.6% (95% CI, 68.6%-89.6%). In comparison, initial office BP screening achieved a sensitivity of 55.3% (95% CI, 43.4%-66.7%), specificity of 90.0% (95% CI, 83.2%-94.7%) and PPV of 77.8% (95% CI, 64.4%-88.0%). These results highlight an opportunity for consumer smartwatches to facilitate population-level opportunistic hypertension screening by prompting at-risk individuals toward clinical assessment and confirmatory diagnosis using established cuff-based methodologies, offering an accessible tool to address this major public health challenge.

papers.title: Hydrogen Derivatives Enable Cost-Effective Carbon Neutrality in China
papers.abstract: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change recommended 1.5°C carbon reduction target, requiring powerful enforcement from major economies. China, the largest CO2 emitter, is facing severe difficulties for both variable renewable accommodation and decarbonization of hard-to-abate sectors. Hydrogen, as a critical green energy carrier bridging renewable to end-users, faces significant obstacles in real-world deployment such as costly transportation, storage and fuel-cell adoption. Affordable and coordinated hydrogen deployment plan to accelerate the carbon-neutral transition remains ambiguous. Here, we present cost-effective carbon-neutral transition pathways for entire energy economy of China emphasizing the significant role of hydrogen and derivatives as green energy carriers, considering high-resolution renewable deployments, hourly power system operations in 29 provincial regions, over 46,000 rail/road/marine/pipeline transfer routing of hydrogen derivatives, process-level fuel adoption strategies in all end-use sectors. Results show that incorporating hydrogen and derivatives can reduce the overall transition cost by $ 10.7 trillion compared with renewable and electrification pathways, achieving negative carbon abatement costs ($-6.15/ton), eliminating external oil import expenses, equivalent to over 50% of China trade surplus (2023 level)1, significantly boosting employment and economic growth. Hydrogen derivative based transition pathway offers a vital direction for affordable and secure decarbonization for China and beyond under volatile international energy markets.

papers.abstract: Deep learning outcomes are hard to predict and reproduce. Ly and Gong propose fractal basin geometry as a mechanism: starting points leading to different outcomes interweave at arbitrarily fine scales, so greater precision yields little improvement.

papers.abstract: DIRAC is a geometric deep learning model that enables both vertical and horizontal integration and annotation of spatial multi-omic data.

papers.title: Interplay of superconductivity and ferromagnetism in ferromagnetic-semiconductor-based Josephson junctions
papers.abstract: The interplay between superconductivity and ferromagnetism offers a pathway to unconventional Josephson effects and novel superconducting device applications, yet suitable materials are scarce. Here, the authors utilize epitaxial Al/InAs/(Ga,Fe)Sb heterostructures to achieve atomically precise interfaces, revealing proximity-induced superconductivity and unconventional Fraunhofer patterns consistent with induced ferromagnetism and edge-channel superconducting transport.

papers.title: A handheld tool for Young’s modulus characterization of soft materials: towards point-of-care tissue assessment
papers.abstract: Palpation is a rapid and widely used physical examination technique for assessing tissue characteristics and guiding decisions about further imaging procedures. However, its effectiveness depends heavily on clinician experience, making standardized interpretation difficult. This paper presents SensoPal, a portable palpation-based system for quantitative non-invasive tissue stiffness assessment through measurement of the temporal and spatial Young’s modulus of soft materials. SensoPal integrates a handheld device with a miniature load cell and magnetometer, alongside a low-cost camera for position tracking, enabling the generation of spatial stiffness maps. User studies demonstrated Young’s modulus measurement accuracy of approximately  ~ 87% (±4%) and repeatability of approximately  ~ 86% (±4%). In localization tasks with flat silicone phantoms containing rigid nodules, stiffness maps identified deep-seated nodules undetectable through touch alone. Experiments on curved biofidelic phantoms with soft nodules demonstrated the system’s ability to capture spatial stiffness variations under realistic low-contrast conditions. SensoPal also distinguished compliant nodules embedded beyond depths of 8 mm, where manual detection became increasingly difficult. These findings establish SensoPal as a reliable, low-cost platform for quantitative tissue characterization in point-of-care diagnostics, telemedicine, and patient self-assessment.

papers.title: Insect-inspired hexapod robot with magnetically coupled compliant and modular drive system
papers.abstract: Legged robots are increasingly inspired by insects’ ability to combine rigidity and compliance for agile, damage-tolerant locomotion in cluttered terrain. Herein, we introduce INSECTRON, a centimeter-scale hexapod robot that employs magnetic transmission to achieve robust mobility with minimal mechanical complexity. Each leg connects to the drivetrain via neodymium magnets, forming a self-aligning micro-clutch that transmits torque under normal load and safely slips under overload, while additional magnetic couplings between drive modules accommodate load imbalances and perturbations. Hall effect sensors provide proprioception for a phase-domain controller maintaining persistent anti-phase coordination. The magnetic transmission architecture introduces intrinsic mechanical adaptability, functionally analogous to biological preflex mechanisms, enabling rapid responses to external perturbations without additional control complexity. Experiments demonstrated stable locomotion across multiple slopes and substrates. Maneuverability was achieved through differential turning and spin-in-place. A minimum Cost of Transport (CoT) of 30 was achieved during locomotion experiments. Under vertical perturbations, INSECTRON autonomously recovered in over 90% of trials, highlighting strong passive impact tolerance. The architecture eliminates the need for precision alignment and mechanical fasteners, enabling tool-free leg replacement and rapid mechanical reconfiguration. This work establishes a scalable route toward modular, resilient, and field-deployable miniature legged robots for confined and uncertain environments.

papers.title: Staphylococcus aureus coagulases increase survival of Pseudomonas aeruginosa during coinfection
papers.abstract: Polymicrobial infections involving Staphylococcus aureus are often more severe than single-species infections. S. aureus typically initiates the infection, creating conditions that allow secondary pathogens like Pseudomonas aeruginosa to establish. In this study, we investigate how coagulase production and the resulting clots contribute to the persistence of polymicrobial infections and influence interactions between these pathogens. Our results reveal a systemic metabolic shift in both bacteria when cocultured. We also find that P. aeruginosa can benefit from the coagulases produced by S. aureus. P. aeruginosa displays enhanced survival in an in vitro clinical model and ex vivo samples of human blood where coagulases are available. Using a murine model of infection, we demonstrate that coagulases also contribute towards the hematogenous spread and persistence of P. aeruginosa in organ tissues. Taken together, we elucidate why S. aureus and P. aeruginosa coinfections are recalcitrant and result in worse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Brain-writing-BERT for generalizable handwriting brain-computer interface
papers.abstract: Handwriting Brain-Computer Interfaces (BCIs) offer a direct brain-to-text pathway, holding significant promise for neural rehabilitation. However, existing research has primarily focused on alphabetic languages. Unlike the sequential nature of alphabetic handwriting, logographic characters like Chinese incorporate complex spatial structures that embed semantic information, presenting a greater challenge for neural decoding. To address this, we propose Brain-Writing-BERT, a novel BCI framework that learns the structural semantic priors from logographic characters to facilitate decoding. We evaluate our system with a clinical participant in Chinese character decoding tasks. All clinical and experimental procedures were registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ref.ChiCTR2100050705, date of registration: 03/09/2021, registry name: Research on Brain-Computer Interfaces for Individuals with High Cervical Spinal Paraplegia). The proposed BCI achieves an online accuracy of 94.45% for a 295-character vocabulary, with an average speed of 8.55 ± 2.77 characters per minute. This study advances high-performance handwriting BCIs for logographic systems, broadening communication possibilities for diverse languages.

papers.title: Acquired resistance to vorinostat in cutaneous T cell lymphoma involves augmented ERK phosphorylation
papers.abstract: Vorinostat is the first approved histone deacetylase inhibitor used in many countries for treating advanced cutaneous T cell lymphoma (CTCL). However, prolonged application of this drug leads to the development of resistance, presenting a significant challenge to therapy. To better understand the mechanisms through which CTCL cells gain resistance, we established a vorinostat-resistant clone of the human CTCL line HuT78 (HuT78VR). HuT78VR cells exhibited enhanced drug efflux ability with increased expression of the drug efflux pumps ABCB1 and ABCG2. Employing an integrated transcriptomics and proteomics approach, we identified molecular signatures of vorinostat resistance. Specifically, HuT78VR cells presented increased expression of metastasis-related genes (LAIR2, VIM, MMP-9, IFNG, FASLG, CCND1, and CDKN1A) with increased cellular invasiveness and defective apoptosis. Further scrutiny of differentially expressed genes and proteins revealed the involvement of mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling. In line with this, HuT78VR cells gained cross-resistance to inhibitors of histone deacetylase and topoisomerase but remained sensitive to inhibitors of MAPK/ERK. Ulixertinib, an ERK inhibitor, re-sensitized HuT78VR cells to vorinostat in vitro as well as in cell-derived xenografts in mice. These findings expand the understanding of vorinostat resistance in CTCL and suggest that ERK inhibition is an effective therapeutic approach to overcome vorinostat resistance.

papers.title: Structures of methanogenic schizorhodopsins reveal divergent strategies for proton transport and thermal adaptation
papers.abstract: Schizorhodopsins (SzRs) are a newly identified rhodopsin family with unusual thermostability and inward proton-pumping activity, occupying an intermediate position between microbial rhodopsins and heliorhodopsins (HeRs) in sequence-based phylogeny. Cryo-EM structures and functional studies of SzRs from Methanoculleus taiwanensis ( Mt SzR) and Methanoculleus sp. ( M sSzR) reveal distinct structural determinants of the extreme thermostability and inward proton transport mechanisms.

papers.title: Drought reduces Ascochyta rabiei infection in chickpea through proline/P5C/mitochondrial-ROS mediated fungal suppression
papers.abstract: Co-occurring abiotic and biotic stresses can have negative or positive interactions with plants. Previously, our field study showed reduced incidence of Ascochyta blight in chickpea under drought conditions. Here, we investigated chickpea’s molecular responses to Ascochyta rabiei under drought, pathogen and combined stress using transcriptomics, gene expression, and amino acid profiling, identifying proline dehydrogenase (CaProDH2) as a key regulator of resistance under combined stress. MiRNA-induced silencing (MIGS) of CaProDH2 reduced the expression of pathogen stress-responsive genes and lowered mitochondrial P5C and superoxide levels under combined stress. In contrast, CaProDH2 overexpression restricted fungal colonization and reduced in-planta fungal load. Co-transcriptome analysis of wild-type plants under combined stress showed suppression of fungal growth- and virulence-associated genes. Here we show that CaProDH2 mediates the catabolism of drought-induced proline, thereby triggering a defense response involving mitochondrial ROS, which likely induces cell death in A. rabiei. Our findings highlight how co-occurring stresses can interact positively, linking drought-induced metabolic changes to fungal resistance through the proline/P5C pathway.

papers.title: A microfluidic mother machine for high-throughput single-cell analysis of human leukemia T cells
papers.abstract: We present a mother machine-like microfluidic device tailored for high-throughput, long-term tracking of non-adherent T-cell proliferation via live-cell microscopy. Our platform consists of an array of microchannels whose geometry was optimized through computational fluid dynamics simulations, facilitating single-cell capture and ensuring a continuous nutrient supply, enabling cell proliferation over multiple generations under controlled growth conditions. We demonstrate the device efficacy by characterizing the growth dynamics of human leukemia T-cells. Specifically, our findings reveal that these cells undergo slightly asymmetric volume division, employing a sizer-like strategy to compensate for stochastic fluctuations in cell size.

papers.title: P53-assisted METTL14-mediated m⁶A modification of SLC7A11 drives ferroptosis and inflammation in polycystic ovary syndrome
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is characterized by chronic inflammation and follicular arrest, yet the molecular drivers linking these pathologies to granulosa cell (GC) death remain elusive. Here, we identify a ferroptosis-inflammation cascade as a critical determinant of ovarian dysfunction in PCOS. We demonstrate that the N⁶-methyladenosine (m⁶A) methyltransferase METTL14 is aberrantly upregulated in human PCOS GCs, correlating with oxidative damage. Mechanistically, we uncover a non-canonical paradigm where upregulated P53 functions as an essential RNA-binding cofactor, recruiting METTL14 to the SLC7A11 transcript. Validated by AlphaFold3 modeling, this METTL14-p53 complex catalyzes SLC7A11 m⁶A hypermethylation and mRNA destabilization. The resulting SLC7A11 deficiency dismantles antioxidant defenses, driving ferroptosis and amplifying local inflammation. Crucially, in a DHEA-induced PCOS rat model, genetic ablation of Tp53 severed this pathogenic axis, restoring redox balance, suppressing inflammation, and reversing the polycystic phenotype. Collectively, our findings reveal a pivotal epigenetic mechanism linking m⁶A reprogramming, iron-dependent cell death, and inflammation, highlighting the METTL14-p53-SLC7A11 axis as a therapeutic target in PCOS.

papers.title: Overview of models for predicting risk of developing ovarian cancer: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Ardasheva et al. provide an overview of models developed to predict the risk of developing ovarian cancer which may be used to identify individuals at a high risk.

papers.title: DExT for direct ex vivo drug testing
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular basis of drug treatments is important for drug screening and drug efficiency testing to identify suitable interventions. However, heterogeneity among individual patients contributes to variation in responses to different treatments, making it difficult to predict treatment outcomes based on the disease or drug type alone. Therefore, developing effective approaches for evaluating drug responses in individual patients is important. Functional analyses using patient-derived cell lines, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), or organoids are conventionally used for such purposes; however, these models can be time-consuming and difficult to establish. We applied Drug Ex vivo Test (DExT) to tumor tissues from two clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) PDX models. Tissues were exposed ex vivo to the dual mTOR complex inhibitor TAK-228 for up to 120 minutes, and treatment-associated phosphorylation changes were measured by quantitative mass spectrometry-based phosphoproteomic analysis relative to time-matched untreated controls. Here we show that DExT captures acute drug-induced phosphorylation changes in ccRCC tumor tissues. TAK-228 reduces phosphorylation of EIF4EBP1-S65, consistent with inhibition of mTOR signaling. These findings demonstrate the initial feasibility of DExT for measuring drug-induced molecular responses directly in tumor-derived tissue material and provide a foundation for further evaluation with additional therapeutic agents and clinical specimens. People with the same type of cancer can respond differently to the same treatment. Current drug-response tests often require growing tumor cells or creating tumor models, which take time and may not always succeed. We developed Drug Ex vivo Test (DExT), which applies a drug directly to tumor tissue for a short period and then measures molecular changes caused by the treatment. We tested DExT using tumor tissues from two clear cell kidney cancer models and a drug that blocks a cancer-related signaling pathway. We detected changes consistent with the expected drug effect. These findings support further development of DExT through larger studies using patient tumor samples and a wider range of drugs.

papers.title: A minimal 13-Transcript signature for HIV-TB coinfection in African children
papers.abstract: Diagnosing tuberculosis (TB) in children living with HIV remains challenging due to difficulty in obtaining adequate samples, the paucibacillary nature of the disease, and symptom overlap with other infections. We previously identified hundreds of differentially expressed transcripts (DETs) in Ugandan and Southern African children living with HIV, yet their number limits clinical utility. Machine learning approaches can derive a compact, translatable diagnostic signature. We analyzed whole blood RNA-seq data from children living with HIV in Uganda (discovery, n = 59) and Southern Africa (Botswana, Eswatini; cross-regional test cohort, n = 38). An independent adult HIV-TB cohort from India (n = 25) provided an external test cohort. DETs were identified using DESeq2 and recursive feature elimination (RFE) with 10-fold cross-validation, and Random Forest was employed to derive a minimal signature. Performance was evaluated by AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. We derived a 13-transcript minimal signature from 566 DETs with a cross-validated AUC of 0.865 in the Ugandan cohort. In the Southern African cross-regional pediatric test cohort, AUC is 0.943 (95% CI 0.858–0.992), with all 16 NoTB cases correctly classified (specificity 1.000, Wilson 95% CI: 0.806–1.000). Performance in Indian adults is modest, with AUC of 0.773 (95% CI 0.564–0.929). Across cohorts, the signature outperforms neutrophil proportions alone. Nine transcripts converge on neutrophil degranulation. This 13-transcript signature, identified via machine learning, discriminates HIV-TB coinfection from HIV mono-infection in African children, with promising performance in a small Southern African cross-regional test cohort. The signature showed high specificity in African cohorts, though larger sample sizes are needed to establish its clinical utility as a rule-in test. Diagnosing tuberculosis (TB) in children with HIV is difficult because they often cannot provide the samples needed for standard tests, and their symptoms can look like other infections. In this study, we looked for an easier way to detect TB using a blood test. We had previously described how molecules called RNA transcripts differ between children with HIV and TB and those with HIV only. In this current study, we used advanced computer analysis to find the smallest number of RNA transcripts that can be used to distinguish children with HIV who have TB from those who do not. The signature correctly identified all children without TB in the Southern African test group, although this group was small. Nine of the 13 transcripts were linked to immune cells called neutrophils. These results suggest the signature may eventually help confirm TB in children with HIV, but validation in larger, diverse cohorts is essential before clinical use can be considered.

papers.title: Aptamers enable a distinct mode of conformational DNA recognition
papers.abstract: Aptamers have generally been understood as nucleic acids that recognize a specific ligand. Now it has been shown that secondary aptamers can recognize the ligand-bound conformation of a primary aptamer, enabling recognition of molecules that lack multiple binding sites for sandwich assays. This mechanism can be integrated into lateral flow assays for targets, including serotonin.

papers.title: A binuclear copper enzyme platform for enantioconvergent radical (pseudo)halogenation
papers.abstract: Binuclear metalloenzymes remain underexplored for new-to-nature biocatalytic reactions. Now binuclear copper enzymes, particularly a Bacillus megaterium tyrosinase, are used as a catalytic platform for stereoselective radical azidation, bromination, chlorination and isothiocyanation reactions, expanding metalloenzyme catalysis beyond mononuclear systems.

papers.title: Scalable physical deep learning using optical dynamics with state-skipping training and single-map architecture
papers.abstract: This study presents a scalable, efficient framework for unconventional computing with physical neural networks. It replaces dense connections with uncoupled one-dimensional dynamics, simplifies training, improves performance and reduces resource use.

papers.title: Digital readiness for cardiovascular care in high-burden US communities with cardiology workforce constraints
papers.abstract: As presented at 2026 AHA Scientific Sessions: Analysis of U.S. Census and other national health data identifies communities with high cardiovascular care needs and assess health system readiness for digital care deployment.

papers.title: Opposing microbiome-mediated axes link modifiable lifestyles to health and chronic diseases
papers.abstract: Fecal shotgun metagenomics from 6,803 adults in the Japanese 4D cohort and microbiome-based prediction scores validated across 13 independent and geographically diverse cohorts revealed two opposing microbiome-mediated axes linking lifestyle to health and 15 diseases.

papers.title: Comprehensive m 6 A landscape from direct RNA sequencing reveals SYNPO2L RNA isoform regulation mechanisms in heart failure
papers.abstract: Xu et al. use nanopore direct RNA sequencing to map heart failure-associated m 6 A RNA modifications at transcriptome-wide and single-site resolution. Their findings reveal conserved m 6 A remodeling patterns and isoform-specific regulation of SYNPO2L, highlighting complex epitranscriptomic mechanisms that influence cardiac gene expression and contribute to heart failure progression.

papers.title: Polar crystals as catalytic platforms for solar energy conversion
papers.abstract: Polar crystals possess non-centrosymmetric structures that generate spontaneous polarization and a built-in electric field, enabling efficient charge separation. This Review discusses their use as catalysts for converting solar energy into chemical energy, covering the advantages of polar single crystals, multilevel polarization engineering, key challenges and future directions.

papers.title: Exposure to legitimate and illegal online medicine vendors via search engines in 30 European countries
papers.abstract: Online medicine sales have not only improved access but also expose consumers to illegal online medicine vendors (IOMVs) selling substandard/falsified products. This study provides the first pan-European assessment of exposure to legitimate online pharmacies (LOPs) and IOMVs in search engine results (SERs). We scraped the top-50 Google results in 30 European countries for six tracer active pharmaceutical ingredients across three categories: controlled substances, prescription-only medicines (POMs), and over-the-counter products (OTCs). Links were categorised as LOPs or IOMVs based on official registries. From 9000 SERs, 3839 linked to medicine-selling websites (63.7% LOPs, 36.3% IOMVs). LOPs outnumbered and outranked IOMVs, though IOMV:LOP ratios reached 2.37 (Norway) and 2.18 (Cyprus). Search engine redirection affected 56.6% of IOMV links. IOMV prevalence increased with regulatory control: 1.4% (paracetamol), 5.5% (ibuprofen), 10.2% (omeprazole), 55.1% (amoxicillin), 76.2% (alprazolam) and 77.5% (clonazepam). IOMV links were less likely to be highest-ranked and less common in the top-10 SERs in countries permitting online OTC and POM sales, than in those prohibiting them. Despite LOP dominance, Europeans face substantial exposure to IOMV links, higher for controlled substances and in countries prohibiting online sales. Harmonised regulatory action, supported by search engine providers, is needed for safer online medication access.

papers.title: Collaborative generalist-specialist AI for safe worklist deprioritization of non-contrast brain computed tomography
papers.abstract: Safe deprioritization of non-contrast brain computed tomography (NCCT) demands high sensitivity and negative predictive value (NPV) across common and uncommon findings requiring clinical attention. Here, we present a collaborative safety net integrating BrainCT-CLIP, a generalist foundation model via contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP), with commercial detectors. Every examination remained in the reporting workflow, deprioritized only when no model returned a positive result. In a retrospective multicenter external validation of consecutive emergency and trauma cohorts (n = 2001), standalone commercial detectors left 31 of 324 remarkable examinations deprioritized, including 16 target-disease false negatives and 15 outside their indications. In contrast, the collaborative system recovered every remarkable examination at a threshold prespecified in the development cohort, achieving 100% sensitivity and NPV while deprioritizing 18% of examinations (368/2001; 95% CI, 17–20). These findings support generalist-specialist AI for safe worklist deprioritization under radiologist oversight, with high sensitivity for intracranial findings requiring clinical attention.

papers.title: AI-driven multi-horizon risk stratification for heart failure hospitalization in UA with HFpEF: a Chinese multi-center cohort study
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) complicated by unstable angina (UA) represents a major challenge in chronic disease management with high risk of recurrent heart failure hospitalization (HFH), and despite the availability of multicenter real-world data, AI-driven tools for multi-horizon risk assessment remain limited. This multicenter retrospective cohort enrolled 4367 patients with UA and HFpEF, and an ensemble feature selection pipeline integrating LASSO, SVM-RFE and Boruta identified robust predictors, followed by training of twelve machine learning algorithms to estimate HFH risk at 12-, 24- and 36-month horizons with external validation. The optimal time-specific models (ET, GBDT and LightGBM) achieved strong discrimination in the training cohort with AUCs of 0.818, 0.834 and 0.863, and maintained performance in external validation with AUCs of 0.839, 0.836 and 0.851, respectively, while SHAP analysis highlighted diabetes mellitus, TyG-BMI and NT-proBNP as the most influential predictors. We developed and externally validated a multi-time-point machine learning framework for HFH risk stratification in UA and HFpEF, which showed acceptable calibration and potential clinical utility on decision-curve analysis. Further prospective and real-world validation across diverse populations and healthcare systems is needed to confirm clinical effectiveness and support translation into routine practice.

papers.title: External validation of an image-only ultrasound model for delivery-date prediction in four Chilean public hospitals
papers.abstract: Pregnancy dating fails the women who need it most: those who reach care without a first-trimester scan. We externally validated a commercial image-only ultrasound deep-learning model for delivery-date prediction, applied unmodified to 64,235 frames from 3788 examinations of 2550 pregnancies (34% migrant) at four Chilean public hospitals. Mean absolute error was 6.9 days versus 11.6 for the conventional due date, yet most of this gain reflected a shorter local gestation and fell below one day against recentred comparators. Fixed-term comparators assign every pregnancy the same gestational age at birth and therefore cannot rank who will deliver early, at any level of point accuracy: accuracy metrics are blind to the ranking on which management turns whenever the outcome distribution is concentrated, as in term-dominated cohorts. In a prespecified landmark analysis the model’s separate image-only risk score discriminated preterm birth with an area under the curve of 0.86, against 0.52 for gestational age alone; outside the landmark restriction it exceeded a clinical baseline of coded diagnoses plus same-examination biometry by 0.09, although it was miscalibrated. Error and calibration were also assessed by maternal nationality. These classification analyses are exploratory, and no woman was managed with the model; they identify what a prospective study should test.

papers.title: Carbon radical generation by irreversible metal-to-ligand charge transfer
papers.abstract: Metal-to-ligand charge transfer (MLCT) is a fundamental photoinduced process that underpins a broad range of energy- or electron-transfer events1,2. In the absence of productive substrate engagement, the MLCT excited state typically relaxes to the ground state via photophysical deactivation, reflecting its largely reversible character3,4. Here we report a class of isolable copper–heteroaryl sulfone complexes that, upon visible light irradiation, undergo an irreversible MLCT-driven fragmentation through C–S bond cleavage within the coordinated sulfone ligand, generating carbon-centered radicals. Spectroscopic and computational studies support the formation of MLCT-derived excited states and a low-barrier pathway for C–S bond cleavage. This reactivity is largely independent of the reduction potentials of the corresponding free sulfones, enabling the generation of fluoroalkyl and non-fluorinated tertiary, secondary, and primary (even methyl) alkyl radicals. We demonstrate the utility of this platform in copper-catalyzed C–H fluoroalkylation of arenes and terminal alkynes. Leveraging these MLCT-generated trifluoromethyl radicals to initiate halogen-atom transfer (XAT) from perfluorocyclobutyl iodide (I-FCB), we also achieve radical perfluorocyclobutylation–iodination of alkenes, addressing a longstanding challenge in the incorporation of perfluorocyclobutyl motifs.

papers.title: Observation of prethermal dynamical phase transitions and resonant melting

papers.title: Ecological and social cues orchestrate concerted courtship in Drosophila
papers.abstract: In Drosophila erecta , food odours initiate male sexual arousal, which is subsequently reinforced by the visual motion of other courting flies, creating a multisensory mechanism that synchronizes courtship in groups when conditions are favourable for reproduction.

papers.title: Multimodal X-ray imaging reveals hierarchical fibre mechanics
papers.abstract: The X-ray visualization platform TomoSAXS, demonstrated here on intervertebral spinal discs, can visualize nanoscale to macroscale mechanics in intact biological organs and fibrous materials.

papers.title: Towards observing interstitial hydrogen in solution in metal lattices
papers.abstract: Using deuterium as a proxy for hydrogen, atom probe tomography provides experimental evidence for interstitial hydrogen in solid solution across different FCC phases, consistent with theoretical predictions of hydrogen affinity, revealing hydrogen partitioning in structural alloys.

papers.title: Decoding the regulatory programs governing glioblastoma plasticity
papers.abstract: Multi-omic analyses of cells from patients with glioblastoma (GB) provide insight into the role of non-genetic cellular plasticity in disease progression, showing that state stability in GB cells is controlled by a network of interacting activators and repressors.

papers.title: Comprehensive mapping of essential-gene interactions in M. tuberculosis
papers.abstract: A high-throughput CRISPR-interference platform allows the mapping of interactions between essential genes in Mycobacterium tuberculosis , revealing many previously unknown genetic interactions and providing insight into gene function and drug–target relationships that could enable the development of new therapies for tuberculosis.

papers.title: Conjugation-regulated self-assembled molecules for tandem solar cells
papers.abstract: Rationally engineered molecular spatial conjugation is used for the formation of highly ordered, conformal self-assembled molecules, enabling the fabrication of high-performance perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells.

papers.title: Hard X-ray attosecond metrology
papers.abstract: Metrology techniques are developed to characterize and control attosecond hard X-ray pulses, directly measuring a 170-attosecond duration and enabling ultrafast studies of electronic dynamics in quantum systems.

papers.title: Cancer-selective gene circuits via intrinsic ribosomal frameshifting
papers.abstract: Codon-pair-dependent ribosomal frameshifting is a feature of translational dysregulation in cancer cells.

papers.abstract: Genome-wide data from 4,587 ancient individuals are analysed, focusing on Bronze and Iron Age Europe, to test the extent to which alternative archaeological and linguistic models for the origin and spread of Celtic fit reconstructed demographic histories.

papers.abstract: Longitudinal tracking of endothelial cells shows they can adapt to loss of VEGFR2 and form new functional vessels, challenging conventional views of the essential role of VEGF receptors in angiogenesis and providing insight into resistance to anti-VEGF therapies.

papers.title: The neural basis of flavour–nutrient learning
papers.abstract: A dopamine pathway to the basolateral amygdala is necessary for associating nutrients with flavours.

papers.title: Nectin-4 mediates rubella virus entry in airway and placental cells

papers.title: Aggression experience and observation drive shared behavioural and neural changes
papers.abstract: Aggression experience and observation recruit a brain-wide network of excitatory, inhibitory and valence signals, and changes to this activation pattern predict a shared adaptive behaviour-control policy in a new aggression context.

papers.title: Transcriptomic convergence and the female protective effect in autism
papers.abstract: Gene network analysis shows how mutations in diverse genes associated with autism spectrum disorder can converge to exert shared effects, with X-linked transcription factor ZFX emerging as a key protective factor in the female brain.

papers.title: The deep Earth origin of the Great Unconformity
papers.abstract: Continental-scale uplift and subsidence associated with long-wavelength dynamic topography due to mantle convection drove the formation and preservation of the Great Unconformity.

papers.abstract: Twist-angle-dependent studies of moiré bilayer MoTe 2 reveal a transition from fractional topological states to correlated insulators and superconductivity, linking topology, symmetry breaking and magnetism in moiré quantum materials.

papers.abstract: structRFM, a structure-guided RNA foundation model pre-trained on 21 million sequence–structure pairs, learns multimodal representations that improve secondary and tertiary structure prediction, functional inference and zero-shot generalization across diverse RNA families.

papers.abstract: Viral–bacterial synergy accelerates algal bloom collapse by enhancing virus-induced mortality, driven by Alteromonas chemoattraction and co-infection, revealing a previously unrecognized mortality agent that influences oceanic carbon cycling .

papers.abstract: The genomic footprints of 80 years of modern breeding in China are traced using representative cultivars, demonstrating how precision genome editing can be used to reconstruct adaptive modules for climate-resilient crop design.

papers.abstract: A deep single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of human glioblastoma is generated, pairing transcriptomic, epigenomic and genomic profiling, and tracing glioblastoma tumour heterogeneity to a stereotyped and spatially patterned trajectory of cancer cells.

papers.abstract: A new physics-based method combining the use of automatic differentiation to optimize millions of model parameters with a flexible physical model is described for starlight subtraction from real, on-sky coronagraphic images to greatly improve sensitivity.

papers.abstract: RobPicker improves cryo-ET particle picking by correcting noisy labels and reweighting rare species, enabling robust detection of small macromolecules across diverse datasets.
