papers.abstract: Discovering effective perovskite precursor additives is challenging due to the vast chemical space. Here, the authors present a closed-loop active-learning framework that leverages literature knowledge to accelerate perovskite precursor additive discovery, achieving solar cell efficiencies up to 21.32%.

papers.title: Synthesis, ink formulation, and aerosol jet printing of (Nb 0.5 Ta 0.5 )S 2 ternary alloy for additively manufactured electrochemical supercapacitors
papers.abstract: Alloyed 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) hold promise for advanced energy storage, yet their device integration is hindered by the absence of stable, processable inks. Here, the authors develop a ternary TMD alloy ink for aerosol jet printing, achieving significant supercapacitor performance and paving the way for flexible, miniaturized energy solutions.

papers.title: Optical edge computing for speckle sensing interrogation
papers.abstract: Speckle-based sensing exploits the rich environmental information of its high-dimensional spatial intensity patterns. However, the requirement for camera-based acquisition and subsequent electronic digitization introduces significant latency and bandwidth bottlenecks that forbid real-time operation and higher temporal resolutions. Aiming to bypass this imaging processing pipeline, this manuscript presents an optically reconfigurable edge-computing platform for speckle-based sensors that performs task-specific computation directly in the optical domain. This is achieved by projecting output speckle patterns onto a digital micromirror device, using it as a programmable optical layer whose parameters are trained in situ using an evolutionary optimization strategy solely from detector feedback. We demonstrate the concept with a multi-point optical fiber sensing task, where multiple piezoelectric actuators simultaneously perturb the fiber, modifying the speckle pattern. By optimizing a set of masks to decouple these concurrent signals, the system successfully achieves real-time signal separation, achieving a target signal enhancement exceeding 4 dB while suppressing crosstalk leakage below −10 dB. Operating with bandwidths limited only by the photodetector, this approach paves the way for real-time and ultrafast optical sensing via an optical edge computing solution.

papers.title: CD30 ligand promotes skin wound healing through keratinocyte signaling and Vγ6 + γδ T-cell responses
papers.abstract: Skin wound healing depends on coordinated interactions between skin cells and immune cells. CD30 and its ligand CD30L, as members of the tumor necrosis factor (TNF) superfamily, have been implicated in various immune-related disorders. However, the contribution of CD30L in skin wound healing is unclear. Here we show that Cd30l−/− mice exhibited delayed wound closure, as validated by image tracking, along with reduced infiltration of Vγ6+γδ T cells, lower levels of inflammatory cytokines including interleukin (IL)-17A, and impaired angiogenesis in wound tissues, as demonstrated through flow cytometry, immunohistochemistry, RT-qPCR, and ELISA. Furthermore, CD30L deficiency was associated with reduced keratinocyte proliferation, altered nuclear factor (NF)-κB pathway, and lower CCL20 expression in wound-derived keratinocytes, as evidenced by western blot and bulk RNA-seq analysis. These findings support a contributory CD30L-CCL20/CCR6-Vγ6+γδ T-cell axis within the broader multicellular network during skin wound healing.

papers.title: Evolutionary dynamics of adaptive introgression and balancing selection in domestic and wild Capra species
papers.abstract: Genomic analyses reveal a fertile goat–ibex hybrid, uncover ancient introgression among Capra species, and show that balancing selection can mimic introgression signals, highlighting the complexity of interpreting shared genomic variation.

papers.title: A dichotomous family of Cache domain proteins evolved through c-type heme acquisition
papers.abstract: PAS domains often bind cofactors, whereas related Cache domains are thought to function exclusively as ligand-binding modules. We identify and characterize a large family of Cache domains containing covalently bound c-type heme. Sequence, phylogenetic and structual analysis of the DUF3365/Tll0287 family reveals conservation of a canonical CXXCH heme-binding motif, establishing c-type heme binding as a defining feature of this family. Despite previous annotation as PAS-like, these proteins share a distinct heme-binding insertion into a pre-existing Cache scaffold, representing the first documented recruitment of an intact cofactor-binding motif into a bacterial sensor domain. Domain architecture further divides the family into two subclasses: one exhibiting fusions to signaling domains and another comprised of standalone proteins. Spectroscopic analyses indicate that a representative signaling protein acts as a nitric oxide sensor, whereas a stand-alone representative exhibits redox-related properties and weak nitric oxide binding. These findings expand the functional repertoire of Cache domains and reveal a mechanism for the evolution of bacterial sensory systems.

papers.title: Glutathione S transferase assembled gold silver nanoclusters activate cGAS STING immunity in breast cancer
papers.abstract: GST-mediated self-assembly of gold-silver nanoclusters activates cGAS-STING signaling and remodels antitumor immunity, enabling photothermal-immunotherapy to inhibit breast cancer growth, metastasis and recurrence.

papers.title: Time-resolved ligand dynamics revealed in a β-lactamase using room-temperature serial crystallography
papers.abstract: β-Lactamases hydrolyse β-lactam antibiotics and are key antimicrobial resistance determinants in globally important bacterial pathogens. Here, we report on the use of time-resolved room-temperature drop-on-fixed-target serial crystallography, complemented by classical single-crystal crystallography and molecular simulations, to investigate reversible covalent inhibition of the serine β-lactamase CTX-M-15 by the diazabicyclooctane inhibitor avibactam, used to treat infections by β-lactamase producing organisms. A covalent ring-opened avibactam carbamoyl complex is observed in crystal structures 80 ms after mixing, which rearranges on a 1.3 s to 600 s time scale. Together with molecular dynamics simulations and density functional theory calculations based on our experimental structures, our data suggest that in the initially observed species the avibactam N-sulfate nitrogen is poorly positioned to attack the carbamoyl carbon to initiate the 5-exo-trig recyclisation required for inhibitor reformation. This complex then undergoes conformational changes that potentially prime it for this intramolecular reaction. These data reveal the conformational dynamics and stereoelectronic basis of diazobicyclooctane inhibition and demonstrate how the combination of room-temperature serial crystallography and molecular simulations can capture ligand motions in enzyme active sites on millisecond-to-second timescales, delivering mechanistically relevant understanding of the dynamic behaviour of enzyme-bound species.

papers.title: Enhanced sampling enables binding site water reorganization in polarizable absolute binding free energy calculations
papers.abstract: Water molecules shape protein-ligand binding, but their exchange and reorganization within buried binding sites remain difficult to sample in absolute binding free-energy calculations. Here, the authors combine the polarizable AMOEBA force field with Lambda-ABF-OPES to obtain binding free energies across five diverse complexes while capturing persistent hydration motifs, water exchange, and coupled ligand-pocket-solvent relaxation without water-specific collective variables.

papers.title: TARMAC as a taxonomy for robot manipulation in chemistry
papers.abstract: Laboratory automation has made well-defined experimental protocols increasingly executable by machines, yet many physical manipulations remain difficult to generalize, including both those surrounding automated protocols and those not readily accommodated by current automation. Here, the authors propose TARMAC, a taxonomy that organizes these actions into reusable primitives, demonstrating its applicability across various platforms and workflows.

papers.title: Structural and functional insights into the p160 Rho-associated coiled-coil-containing protein kinase ROCK
papers.abstract: Rho-associated protein kinases (ROCK1/2) are critical regulators of fundamental cellular processes and represent promising therapeutic targets for various pathologies, particularly cardiovascular disease. While the terminal globular kinase domain and the PH-C1 tandem (PHn-C1-PHc) are well characterized, the sequence-structure-function relationship of the central amphipathic α-helical segment remains poorly understood. Utilizing an integrative biophysical approach—including multi-angle light scattering (MALS), analytical ultracentrifugation (AUC), small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), negative-stain electron microscopy (EM), X-ray crystallography, and 3D molecular modeling—we elucidate the structural organization of the central coiled-coil region of ROCK1. Notably, the 2.2 Å resolution crystal structure of the homology region 1 (HR1) of ROCK1 reveals a canonical parallel coiled-coil dimer. This structural arrangement diverges significantly from the antiparallel coiled-coil HR1 module found in other Rho effector kinases. Combined with the structural reconstitution of full-length ROCK1, our data demonstrates that the central segment of ROCK1 forms a highly elongated coiled-coil dimer. Furthermore, EM analysis of the isolated full coiled-coil domain uncovers a dynamic oligomerization state, transitioning between a dimer and a tetramer. Together, these biophysical insights establish a foundation that opens avenues for future investigation into ROCK1 regulation, activation, and downstream signaling mechanisms.

papers.title: Phase-binarized auto-oscillation modes in wide nanoconstriction spin Hall nano-oscillators
papers.abstract: Nanoconstriction spin Hall nano-oscillators (SHNOs) are cutting-edge spintronic devices for gigahertz signal generation and neuromorphic computing, offering a CMOS-compatible nanoscale footprint, ultra-wide frequency tunability, and robust synchronization in large networks. Most previous studies have focused on constrictions narrower than 200 nm, where a single dominant spin-wave mode typically emerges. The auto-oscillation dynamics of wide constrictions remain largely unexplored. Here, using micromagnetic simulations, we demonstrate the coexistence of two independently tunable auto-oscillation modes in constrictions wider than 200 nm: a low-frequency in-phase mode and a high-frequency out-of-phase mode, both localized at opposite constriction edges. The out-of-phase mode arises from the interplay of exchange, magnetodipolar coupling, and the antisymmetric Oersted field component, producing strongly edge-localized oscillations with a nearly 180∘ phase difference. We develop an analytical two-mode framework that captures their hybridization and nonlinear competition. Their distinct subharmonic injection-locking responses enable phase-binarized states within a single wide SHNO, opening opportunities for multimode synchronization, unconventional computing, and complex phase locking in SHNO networks.

papers.title: Pain and fifty six subsequent wellbeing and life outcomes in a multicountry longitudinal study
papers.abstract: Macchia et al. use multi-country longitudinal data to explore the longer-term effects of pain across various countries. Authors find that pain is negatively linked to outcomes like flourishing, happiness, life satisfaction, and mental health among others, and positively linked to outcomes such as traumatic distress and anxiety.

papers.title: Facet-dependent molecular adsorption modulates zinc anode work function for the favourable orientation of zinc electrocrystallization
papers.abstract: While additives direct Zn electrocrystallization and impact battery performance, the mechanism remains disputed. Now it has been shown that facet-dependent work function modulation upon additive adsorption governs Fermi-level equilibration and Zn crystallographic texture across 29 additives with 93.1% accuracy, providing an interfacial electronic descriptor for additive screening towards favourable Zn electrodeposition.

papers.title: Pure-blue quantum-dot light-emitting diodes with minimal efficiency roll-off and high brightness
papers.abstract: Quantum-dot light-emitting diodes (QLEDs) are promising candidates for augmented reality, virtual reality and other high-resolution microdisplay applications. For these applications, the QLEDs must sustain high efficiency at high luminance while remaining compatible with device-integration processes. However, blue QLEDs still face pronounced efficiency roll-off and processing-related performance degradation. Here we develop pure-blue-emitting quantum dots based on a CdZnSe core with a compositionally graded ZnSe/ZnSeS/ZnS shell, combined with ZnCl2-assisted surface morphology modulation. This design suppresses surface-trap-related recombination and improves processing robustness. We demonstrate bottom-emission QLEDs at 464 nm with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8% and a 95% external quantum efficiency retention at 50,000 cd m−2 (L95). The top-emission QLEDs reached L95 = 270,000 cd m−2 and a blue index of 586. We also demonstrate patterned QLEDs via photolithography with a resolution of 560 pixels per inch and peak external quantum efficiency of 16.5%. Our results demonstrate pure-blue quantum-dot emitters that combine Rec. 2020-near emission, minimal efficiency roll-off at high brightness, compatibility with direct photolithographic patterning and top-emission device integration for advanced display applications. Quantum dots with compositionally graded shells enhance quantum-dot LED performance, achieving pure-blue emission with a peak external quantum efficiency of 23.8%, 95% of which is retained at a luminance of 50,000 cd m−2.

papers.title: Deaminative nucleophilic substitution of alkyl amines
papers.abstract: Nucleophilic substitution is a fundamental strategy for alkyl functionalization, traditionally relying on alcohols and alkyl halides as alkylating reagents. Now a deaminative nucleophilic substitution strategy that uses alkyl amines as direct alkylation reagents is reported. Harnessing the reactivity of N -alkyl nitroamines, this process enables the efficient construction of diverse alkyl C–halogen, C–C, C–N, C–O and C–S bonds.

papers.title: Wastewater surveillance captures multi-marker responses to short-term examination stress in a university population
papers.abstract: Using wastewater surveillance of an Australian university population, this study reveals examination-period increases in biomarkers of oxidative stress and suggestive rises in antidepressant use, indicating heightened mental health burden during academic stress.

papers.title: Global temperature-related mortality associated with El-Nino Southern Oscillation
papers.abstract: Epidemiological estimates suggest that global heat-related mortality increased by 29% during very strong El Niño years, with the greatest burdens occurring in low- and medium- Human Development Index regions.

papers.title: Perioperative ivonescimab with or without chemotherapy in resectable non-small cell lung cancer: a phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: In a nonrandomized phase 2 trial, patients with resectable non-small cell lung cancer received perioperative ivonescimab as monotherapy or with chemotherapy, leading to encouraging pathological response rates in both cohorts, and sustained circulating tumor DNA negativity throughout neoadjuvant therapy may be predictive of response.

papers.title: Digital cell factories for biomanufacturing
papers.abstract: Metabolism-centric digital cell factories offer a pragmatic route to biomanufacturing optimization by emphasizing predictions of production performance and economic outcomes over biological detail.

papers.title: Digital and hybrid interventions for subacute and chronic low back pain: component network meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Digital and hybrid interventions combining exercise, education, and psychological components are increasingly used for low back pain (LBP), but it remains unclear which components and combinations drive efficacy. We conducted a prospectively registered component network meta-analysis (CNMA) to evaluate their efficacy and safety for non-specific LBP. Six databases and two trial registries were searched to May 2025. Data on disability, pain intensity, and adverse events were analysed using a Bayesian random-effects CNMA. Of 2809 records, 56 reports of 46 studies (6717 participants; 80% chronic low back pain) were included. Hybrid interventions combining digital and in-person exercise with in-person psychological components (MD: –22.21; 95%-CrI: –34.11 to –10.67), digital and in-person exercise (MD: –15.75; 95%-CrI: –22.79 to –8.80), or digital exercise with physiotherapy (MD: –13.17; 95%-CrI: –21.18 to –5.16) reduced disability versus no intervention at short-term (minimal clinically important difference (MCID): 4.92/100 Oswestry Disability Index). Digital and in-person exercise (MD: -1.76; 95%-CrI: -2.62; -0.87) and combined digital exercise training with in-person education (MD: -1.73; 95%-CrI: -2.71; -0.83) improved pain intensity beyond the MCID (0.82/10 numeric pain rating scale). No serious adverse events were noted. Multicomponent hybrid interventions appear safe and may provide clinically meaningful improvements for chronic LBP.

papers.title: Cross-paradigm audit of large language model judges for clinical text evaluation
papers.abstract: Large language models are increasingly being used to evaluate clinical texts, a concept known as LLM-as-a-judge. However, most of the existing evidence focuses on English data and uses pooled agreement metrics that obscure clinically relevant failure modes. This study audited six open-weight models against expert judges on four German clinical datasets covering report and nursing documentation summarization, discharge summary generation, and patient letter generation. The models were evaluated across three paradigms and four prompt configurations. Alignment with experts varied by criterion and corpus, and no configuration proved reliable across paradigms. All judges exhibited position and identity bias. Substituting LLM-as-a-judge for the expert panel shifted 57.2% of pointwise categories, swapped 41.7% of pairwise winners, missed 10.2% of clinical errors, and inverted clinical priorities by overrating the criteria succinct and accurate. Therefore, LLM-as-a-judge is not a safe substitute for experts in German clinical text evaluations, and deployment thresholds should follow decision-impact analysis for LLM-as-a-judge in clinical contexts.

papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: DNA Nanotechnology for Precision Sensing and Diagnostics at the Nanoscale
papers.abstract: Small Methods, EarlyView.

papers.title: Non-invasive oral magnetoelectric vagus nerve neuromodulation for Parkinson’s disease therapy
papers.abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation has shown promising neuroprotective and anti-inflammatory effects in progressive neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson’s disease. However, its invasive nature introduces procedural and device-related risks. Here we introduce a magnetoelectric particulate system for oral delivery and non-invasive vagus nerve stimulation through the gut. The system comprises a magneto-responsive nickel ferrite core and a piezoelectric barium titanate shell, conjugated with capsaicin to specifically target TRPV1 receptors, ensuring effective adherence to the stomach lining after oral administration. Upon magnetic field stimulation, the particles generate electrical pulses that activate vagal afferent fibres, engaging the nucleus tractus solitarius in the brainstem via the gut−brain axis. This activation enhances norepinephrine production in the locus coeruleus and dopamine synthesis in the substantia nigra. Vagal efferent activation triggers the cholinergic anti-inflammatory pathway, mitigating both neuroinflammation and systemic inflammation. This non-invasive approach demonstrates potential for alleviating motor symptoms and non-motor anxiety in Parkinson’s disease, offering valuable insights into its mechanisms and clinical applications. Orally delivered magnetoelectric particles activate vagal afferent fibres in the gut−brain axis and influence neurodegeneration and neuroinflammation in mouse models of Parkinson’s disease.

papers.title: Three-dimensional imaging of individual carbon atoms
papers.abstract: Ptychographic atomic electron tomography determines the 3D positions of 6,648 individual carbon atoms in twisted bilayer graphene with 0.12 Å precision, revealing stacking-dependent corrugations and chiral lattice distortions resembling merons and anti-skyrmions.

papers.title: Rational design of lipid nanoparticles for brain delivery of RNA therapeutics
papers.abstract: Lipid nanoparticles modified with hydroxyzine, an antihistamine compound active in the central nervous system, enable brain delivery of mRNA and gene-editing components in multiple animal models.

papers.title: Head-mounted camera for reconstructing outdoor behavior in freely flying birds
papers.abstract: A head-mounted camera in combination with drone-based mapping of the environment allows reconstruction of the flight trajectory and behavior such as prey capture in freely flying birds such as the Harris’s hawk.

papers.title: Limitations of de novo peptide sequencing in resolving sequence ambiguity
papers.abstract: A benchmark of eight deep learning tools that sequence peptides directly from mass spectra (de novo) shows that their errors mostly stem from incomplete spectra, not model design, calling for tools that flag uncertain regions instead of guessing full sequences.

papers.title: Charge density fluctuations uncover the relevance of electron-phonon coupling in cuprate superconductors
papers.abstract: Electron–phonon coupling (EPC) plays a crucial role in the lattice dynamics and superconducting properties of quantum materials, yet its evolution across phase diagrams in strongly correlated systems remains unclear. Here, the authors use resonant inelastic x-ray scattering to reveal that dynamic charge density fluctuations, rather than static waves, drive phonon renormalization in cuprate superconductors, highlighting EPC’s doping-dependent nature and its impact on superconductivity.

papers.title: Laser-induced delamination of aged silicon photovoltaic modules to achieve >95% selective silver recovery
papers.abstract: End-of-life crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules are difficult to recycle because of strong ethylene-vinyl acetate adhesion and reliance on destructive recycling methods. Here, the authors demonstrate a laser-based delamination strategy for highly selective silver recovery from end-of-life photovoltaic modules.

papers.title: DSIN: dynamic system-empowered implicit neural representation for medical image compression
papers.abstract: Multidimensional/Ultra-high-resolution medical imaging, e.g., Photon-counting computed tomography, multiparametric Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), whole-slide digital pathology drives diagnostic precision but generates massive datasets that strain clinical infrastructure. Current compression methods either sacrifice subvisual diagnostic features to prioritize human perception or lack generalizability across modalities and pathologies. Here, we introduce Dynamic system-empowered implicit neural representation (DSIN), an image compression framework using image-specific implicit neural representations, where a stacked dynamic-system-based compression module further reduces model size while preserving reconstruction quality. When tested across five large-scale clinical datasets (including Computed tomography (CT), MRI, Positron emission tomography (PET), Computed tomography angiography (CTA), and histopathology images), DSIN achieves compression ratios up to 183-fold while maintaining high reconstruction quality, outperforming established and implicit neural representation methods in downstream tasks such as segmentation and classification. Quantitative evaluations reveal superior performance in preserving reconstruction quality, organ boundary fidelity, and metabolic activity delineation in low-dose PET imaging. DSIN provides an effective compression framework for the medical imaging modalities evaluated in this study.

papers.title: Tracing the origin of non-brittle rachis TtBTR1 alleles in wheat
papers.abstract: The evolution of non-brittle rachises, controlled by the TtBTR1 genes, was a key step during wheat domestication. Here, using k-mer-based approaches applied to a large diversity panel, we refine previous estimates of the geographical and temporal origins of the three known Ttbtr1 loss-of-function alleles and show that they emerged in distinct wild emmer subpopulations. For this, we generated a chromosome-scale dika wheat assembly carrying the recently discovered Ttbtr1-Ab allele. Our analyses reveal that the Ttbtr1-A alleles reside on an introgression from the southern judaicum wild emmer population into northern wild emmer wheat, providing an explanation for the long-standing debate about the Ttbtr1-A origin. We further demonstrate that the Ttbtr1-Aa and Ttbtr1-B alleles are already present in wild emmer wheat, with evidence indicating that they arose prior to the advent of agriculture. Together, these findings support a model in which key domestication genes in domesticated crops were selected and combined from standing genetic variation in wild relatives.

papers.title: Predicting discrete traits in evolving systems
papers.abstract: Discrete data are prevalent across biology, from nucleotide base pairs to mating systems or petal count on a flower. Predictions using discrete data are central to imputation, forecasting, and hypothesis testing in biology. How much accuracy and confidence they deliver together, and how this varies across scenarios and taxa, has not been quantified systematically. Here, using accuracy and log loss, we benchmark these models across scenarios varying in tree size, evolutionary rate, and trait coevolution. Against non-phylogenetic baselines, they increase accuracy by 23 percentage points and lower log loss by 92% on average; different Markov implementations perform similarly. Log loss rises as terminal branch lengths elongate, a direct consequence of the Markov process. Last, we provide a tutorial and empirical demonstration for the evolution of unexpected character states (outliers). Our study provides a framework for imputing missing data, reconstructing ancestral traits, and testing evolutionary hypotheses.

papers.title: Genetic insights into foveal morphology and its associations with pigmentation and age-related macular degeneration
papers.abstract: The fovea is the small depression at the neurosensory retina that underlies high-resolution central vision. It is vulnerable to disease and disruption of its architecture can lead to visual disability. Foveal morphology varies substantially across individuals but the molecular causes and functional consequences of this variation remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyse six foveal morphological parameters derived from optical coherence tomography (OCT) images of 39,521 UK Biobank participants. We find marked variation in foveal morphology and identify significant associations with sex and genetic ancestry. Genome-wide association studies identify 162 lead loci across the six foveal morphological parameters, implicating genes involved in pigmentation (including TYR, TSPAN10 and GPR143) and developmental patterning (including FGFR2, CYP26C1 and CYP1A1). Heritability estimates range from 29 to 43%. Foveal pit volume is associated with future risk of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) (hazard ratio 1.09, p = 0.026), a finding supported by Mendelian randomisation. Given the strong correlations among foveal traits, the specificify of this association to pit volume remains unclear. These results establish foveal morphology as a highly heritable trait that is biologically linked to AMD.

papers.title: Early-life adversity induces social anxiety and cognitive deficits alongside neurobiological changes in rats
papers.abstract: Mood disorders such as anxiety often originate early in life, yet rodent models of early-life adversity are typically assessed only in adulthood using a limited array of behavioral assays. Here we show how neonatal isolation affects social behavior, learning and memory, neuron structure, and blood metabolites in Long Evans rats (Rattus norvegicus). Juvenile isolated rats play less with unfamiliar peers but interact typically with cage mates, consistent with a social anxiety-like phenotype. As adults, isolated rats show reduced cooperation and increased aggression, whereas traditional anxiety tests do not reveal increased generalized anxiety. Females show pronounced cognitive and motivational deficits. Isolation is also associated with reduced dendritic spine density in the medial prefrontal cortex, sex-specific neuronal changes in the dorsolateral septum, and shifts in glucose and amino acid metabolism. Together, these findings reveal selective, sex-dependent consequences of early-life social deprivation across behavioral, neural, and metabolic domains.

papers.title: Biofilm selection activates c-di-GMP synthesis by the bifunctional enzyme MbaA
papers.abstract: Biofilms, in which microbes are encased within a self-produced matrix, represent the primary mode of microbial life. Yet, our understanding of the molecular mechanisms governing biofilm formation remains incomplete, limiting the development of targeted interventions against biofilm-associated infections. By selecting for Vibrio cholerae biofilms, we identified mutations in the polyamine-regulated, bifunctional enzyme MbaA that alter its enzymatic activity in metabolizing the conserved second messenger cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP). These mutations occur in both the c-di-GMP-producing GGDEF domain and the c-di-GMP-hydrolyzing EAL domain of MbaA. Mutagenesis and enzyme kinetic analyses revealed regulatory crosstalk between these domains, where mutations in either domain enhanced production of c-di-GMP by MbaA while concurrently reducing its hydrolytic activity. In the wild-type enzyme, c-di-GMP metabolism is post-translationally regulated by specific polyamines. Biofilm-selected mutations not only shift MbaA’s enzymatic activity but also disrupt this regulation, rendering the enzyme insensitive to external polyamine signaling. Our findings illustrate how evolutionary pressure can rewire existing enzymes, promoting a biofilm-associated lifestyle.

papers.title: Nutrient-dependent bet-hedging between reproduction and sporulation in Bacillus subtilis
papers.abstract: To thrive in nature, bacteria must constantly balance growth with long-term survival in response to nutrient availability. Although sporulation in Bacillus subtilis is a classical survival strategy, how the sporulation program is regulated by nutrient conditions during exponential growth remains elusive. Here we show that the Spo0A-mediated sporulation program is strongly modulated during exponential phase across different carbon sources and is accompanied by pronounced population heterogeneity on poor carbons. We further identify the transition-state regulator AbrB as a key modulator that integrates growth and sporulation, promoting growth under favorable conditions while facilitating sporulation under poor nutrients. On good carbon sources, AbrB optimizes cellular resource allocation by directly suppressing the unnecessary expression of adaptive pathways. In contrast, on poor carbon sources, where the Spo0A-signaling pathway is strongly activated, AbrB promotes sporulation by repressing the expression of a plasmid-encoded Rap-family phosphatase gene, which otherwise interferes with the Spo0A signaling pathway. Together, these findings reveal a dual-control strategy that fine-tunes the trade-off between growth and survival and promotes bet-hedging under poor growth conditions, with important implications for both fundamental biology and synthetic biology.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of quiescent epimastigotes as a resource for investigating Trypanosoma cruzi persistence
papers.abstract: Chagas disease is caused by infection with the protozoan parasite Trypanosoma cruzi. Despite triggering a strong immune response, infections are typically life-long and can result in severe cardiac and/or digestive tract pathology. Current drugs have limited efficacy, and treatment failure is a common outcome. Eliminating a non-replicating T. cruzi sub-population that can persist after therapy has been a key challenge for the drug-development community. Here, we describe the transcriptome and proteome profiles of a low-proliferative sub-population of epimastigote forms of the parasite isolated from exponentially growing cultures on the basis of reduced turnover of transiently-induced red fluorescent protein. This partially quiescent sub-population was characterised by down-regulation of genes/proteins involved in translation, transcription, metabolism, mitochondrial function and DNA replication, and by up-regulation of proteins that promote exit from the cell cycle in other organisms. Differential expression was considerably more pronounced at a protein than an RNA level. These data provide a resource that can be exploited to dissect the mechanistic basis of quiescence, as a step towards refining the drug-development screening cascade.

papers.title: Canonical correlation analysis identifies single nucleotide polymorphism combinations and gene expression associated with membranous nephropathy
papers.abstract: In membranous nephropathy (MN), an autoimmune kidney condition, univariate genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified Human Leucocyte Antigen (HLA) and M-type phospholipase A2 receptor (PLA2R1) genetic risk variants. Multivariate-single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) canonical correlation analysis (CCA) with transcriptomics analysis, can uncover additional insights within this context. We applied CCA to our National Unified Renal Translational Research Enterprise (NURTuRE)- chronic kidney disease (CKD) and Salford Kidney Study (SKS) European datasets, identifying 1095 HLA and 46 PLA2R1 SNPs showing significant MN correlation, and single-cell gene enrichment. Top SNP combinations showed greater significance in both MN by multivariate-SNP CCA, and MN and diabetic nephropathy (Type 1) by allele frequency analysis compared to healthy and non-MN groups. ATF6B, C2, CYP21A2, and HLA-DRB1 colocalised with top HLA SNPs and showed significant differential expression in MN (published immune transcriptomics datasets). HLA-DQB1, HLA-DRB5 and RNF5 showed significant differential expression with lead SNP genotype status in MN and CKD. These previously unreported SNP and gene results are candidates for MN and potentially Type 1 diabetic nephropathy risk prediction.

papers.title: Genomic taxonomy reveals distinct evolutionary architectures within the Enterobacter cloacae complex
papers.abstract: The Enterobacter cloacae complex is a major nosocomial pathogen group, yet its taxonomy remains poorly resolved below the species level, obscuring the evolutionary drivers of virulence and antimicrobial resistance. Here we show, by analyzing 254 clinical isolates from Taiwan alongside 6,493 public genomes, that a genome-resolved taxonomic framework corrects taxonomic assignments for 54.9% of public genomes, primarily by resolving Enterobacter hormaechei into its five subspecies. Subspecies-level resolution reveals two distinct evolutionary patterns. Virulence determinants and intrinsic resistance genes are strongly associated with subspecies identity and remain globally conserved, including near-universal carriage of the salmochelin locus in E. hormaechei subsp. steigerwaltii and strict linkage of chromosomal AmpC β-lactamases to specific species. By contrast, acquired carbapenemases show pronounced geographic variation independent of taxonomy. These findings demonstrate that subspecies represent the fundamental biological and epidemiological units within the Enterobacter cloacae complex and highlight the importance of subspecies-resolved genomics for diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and global surveillance.

papers.title: Susceptibility of Achromobacter spp. to bacteriophages and phage/antibiotic combinations
papers.abstract: Achromobacter infections pose significant challenges to people with Cystic Fibrosis (CF). It is a growing problem in people with CF because it is difficult to eliminate with antibiotics, leading to chronic lung infections that increasingly acquire antibiotic resistance. Here we identified a cadre of 26 bacteriophages that target clinical Achromobacter isolates. We tested these phages against a collection of 56 Achromobacter isolates and found that all were susceptible to multiple of these phages. We also evaluated whether we could restore the activity of certain antibiotics by using them as adjunctive therapy to phages in vitro. We found that when meropenem (a beta lactam antibiotic) was added to the phages, improved susceptibility (decreased MICs) was demonstrated in many isolates regardless of whether the Achromobacter was initially susceptible to meropenem. The data presented here suggests that combination therapy using meropenem with an active phage should be considered for treatment of Achromobacter infections regardless of pre-existing antibiotic susceptibility.

papers.title: Structural analysis of the specificity of three neutralising human monoclonal antibodies against poliovirus
papers.abstract: Despite a global eradication programme, pathogenic polioviruses (PVs) still circulate, dictating a need for improved vaccines, therapeutics and diagnostics. Understanding their antigenic properties has been based largely on studies in mice. Here we study three human monoclonal antibodies specific for the native conformation and either PV1, 2 or 3, determining high-resolution structures of complexes with virus-like particles. The anti-PV1 and anti-PV2 Fabs bind around the icosahedral 3-fold axes, whilst the anti-PV3 Fab binds the canyon. We reveal the basis of serotype specificity and discrimination between native and expanded antigenic states. The anti-PV3 antibody partly penetrates the canyon and makes numerous serotype specific interactions on the south canyon face, distinguishing it from a pan-serotype and pan-antigenic state PV antibody. These structures show that human antibodies often span more than one classical antigenic site and can bind deeper crevices than murine antibodies, expanding our understanding of the antigenic landscape of PV capsids and potentially informing the design of better reagents, antivirals and vaccines against PV.

papers.title: Mathematical and experimental models of interactions among subclones and immunity in melanoma
papers.abstract: Mouse and computational models of interactions between heterogeneous melanoma subclones and the immune system are developed that show that initial subclonal ratios and the strength of interactions determine overall sensitivity to immune response.

papers.title: FAK- and TGF-β1-dependent biomechanical alterations in microvascular endothelial cells exposed to fluid shear stress gradients
papers.abstract: Using an impinging flow device, we investigate how spatial shear stress gradients shape microvascular endothelial cell mechanics and collective migration. In response to flow endothelial cells slow down and migrate against the flow, while enhancing their traction and monolayer stresses through distinct FAK- and TGF-β1-dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: Single-file diffusion of charged particles on a devil’s staircase
papers.abstract: Controlling how particles diffuse through low-dimensional materials, where long-range repulsion couples every particle to every other, is central to ionic conductors, intercalation compounds, and many confined transport systems. Yet how such repulsion shapes diffusion at realistic temperatures has remained poorly understood, because the ordered states it stabilizes and the rare hops that govern motion are difficult to treat analytically or to sample numerically. Here we show, by combining large-scale simulations with a theoretical framework, that diffusion is sharply suppressed at a hierarchy of commensurate densities forming a devil’s staircase, most prominently at one-half, one-third, and two-thirds filling, and that random defects destabilize these ordered states and restore transport. To explain this, we represent particle configurations as evenly spaced building blocks whose rearrangements map the complex interacting system onto a simple symmetric exclusion process. Our results provide a unified, quantitative account of diffusion suppression in long-range interacting materials.

papers.title: Sub-wavelength mid-infrared imaging of locally driven photocurrents using diamond campanile probes
papers.abstract: Precise and high efficiency concentration of mid-infrared (mid-IR) light into sub-wavelength volumes is essential for probing low-energy excitations and achieving strong field enhancements, which is hindered by absorption losses and coupling inefficiencies at long wavelengths. Here, we introduce a diamond-based metal-insulator-metal campanile probe that adiabatically compresses free-space mid-infrared light (10 μm) into ≈ 0.7 μm domain. Integrated into a scanning photovoltage microscope, the probe enables sub-wavelength mapping of locally driven photocurrents in graphene, resolving polarization-dependent and contact-sensitive responses at energies down to ≈ 0.1 eV. Experiments reveal a photocurrent signal density enhancement of 103, coupling light power efficiencies above 1%, and an 18-fold increase in near-field light flux density, in agreement with numerical simulations. Operation of the probe with quantum cascade and free-electron lasers demonstrates a robust, spectrally tunable platform for high-resolution exploration of low-energy carrier dynamics in atomically thin materials, opening opportunities for mid-IR optoelectronics and quantum photonics.

papers.title: Electrical conductivity structure drives anomalous and potentially time-varying magnetic fields at Uranus and Neptune
papers.abstract: Most planetary magnetic fields, like Earth’s, are closely aligned with the spin axis, but those of Uranus and Neptune are strikingly tilted and off-center for unclear reasons. Dynamo simulations show that the way electrical conductivity varies with depth can produce such fields, which may measurably change in strength and direction over time.

papers.title: A live biotherapeutic product for adult allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients: a partially randomized, placebo-controlled phase 1b trial
papers.abstract: In a phase 1b study that included an open-label and randomized-controlled cohorts of allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation recipients, treatment with the investigational, cultivated, multi-strain bacterial oral live biotherapeutic product, SER-155, was found to have a similar safety profile to placebo and resulted in fewer bloodstream infections, indicating further clinical investigation of this therapeutic is warranted.

papers.title: Hematopoietic loss of KDM6A impairs cardiac recovery in heart failure via epigenetic reprogramming of myeloid cells
papers.abstract: Solomonidis et al. reveal that hematopoietic KDM6A-driven clonal hematopoiesis worsens post-MI cardiac recovery by promoting inflammatory myeloid reprogramming. IL-1β blockade reverses these adverse effects, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Breast milk is an overlooked biofluid for point-of-care biosensing
papers.abstract: Human breast milk composition is responsive and reflects maternal, mammary gland and infant health, yet remains largely inaccessible to point-of-care analysis. Purpose-built biosensors could transform breastfeeding support, enabling precision lactation care and improved outcomes for mothers and infants.

papers.title: RETBind: a patient-level multimodal foundation model for unified cross-modal retinal representation learning
papers.abstract: Medical artificial intelligence (AI) holds considerable promise across a wide range of ophthalmic tasks, offering a practical path to patient-level diagnostic support. Foundation models further extend this potential by learning generalizable representations from large-scale unlabeled data, alleviating the burden of extensive manual annotation. However, existing ophthalmic foundation models largely rely on single-modality or modality-specific encoders, failing to capture patient-level cross-modal correspondence in real-world multimodal clinical workflows. To address these gaps, we propose RETBind, a patient-level multimodal foundation model with a unified encoder that explicitly learns cross-modal correspondence from paired clinical imaging using patient-level paired optical coherence tomography (OCT) and ultra-widefield (UWF) fundus imaging. This patient-level paired pretraining strategy enables the model to learn unified cross-modal representations of complementary information, improv-ing performance and robustness beyond single-modality approaches. Across nine benchmark datasets spanning ocular disease classification and segmentation tasks, RETBind achieved consistent improvements, particularly enhancing AUPR in clinically relevant imbalanced settings. Exploratory analyses further examined the potential of RETBind for systemic disease prediction from retinal imaging, collectively highlighting its ability to learn unified cross-modal representations within a single shared encoder, enabling direct interaction between modalities and supporting transfer across diverse retinal imaging tasks.

papers.title: A multimodal tool-augmented agent for evidence-based clinical decision support in longitudinal AMD follow-up
papers.abstract: Clinical management of age-related macular degeneration (AMD) requires longitudinal decisions on disease activity, treatment response, and anti-VEGF injection intervals. These decisions depend on integrating multimodal retinal imaging findings across visits, yet manual synthesis is time-consuming and may omit relevant information, limiting transparency and consistency in follow-up planning. Large language models (LLMs) have been explored to summarize longitudinal AMD information, but existing approaches may lack explicit quantitative grounding and evidence attribution, reducing their auditability in clinical decision support. To address these limitations, we developed AMDagent, an evidence-grounded clinical agent that integrates quantitative imaging analysis with guideline retrieval to generate structured, clinician-facing decision-support outputs. The system links longitudinal imaging findings to actionable management considerations while preserving traceable evidence sources. In a 20-case proof-of-concept evaluation of curated longitudinal AMD cases, AMDagent was rated clinically appropriate in 92.0% of predefined decision-support units under expert adjudication. In addition, 83.3% of audited major clinical claims were explicitly grounded in tool-derived quantitative measurements and/or retrieved guideline evidence, enabling clinician verification. These preliminary findings suggest that evidence-grounded, clinician-facing agents may support more transparent and auditable longitudinal AMD decision support, although larger prospective multi-center studies are needed to assess generalizability and clinical utility.

papers.title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of digital medicine support models for alcohol use disorder
papers.abstract: Alcohol use disorder (AUD) is a major public health issue yet often under-addressed in primary care. Digital health interventions offer scalable support, but health systems require economic data to guide implementation decision-making. In a randomized clinical trial involving 558 participants registered at clinicaltrials.gov (NCT04011644; July 3, 2019), we compared three support models built on a shared digital medicine platform: self-monitored use (SM), peer-supported use (PS), and clinically integrated use (CI). We estimated delivery costs and effectiveness based on reductions in heavy drinking days. Annualized reductions in heavy drinking days were 42.4, 40.2, and 48.3 days per patient for SM, PS, and CI models, with per-patient costs of $162, $524, and $802, respectively. Average cost-effectiveness was $3.8 (SM), $13.0 (PS), and $16.6 (CI); PS was dominated, and the ICER for CI versus SM was $107.9. When downstream healthcare utilization was included, results suggested that more intensive support may be economically advantageous. Modeling implementation at scale showed that PS becomes cost-efficient for large patient populations. These findings highlight that no single model is universally optimal: health systems may benefit from offering multiple support levels to match patient preferences and organizational capacity.

papers.title: Predicting different dimensions of fatigue from speech data: a longitudinal study in shift workers
papers.abstract: Shift work, or working outside of normal circadian cycles, is associated with both experience of fatigue and poorer long-term physical and mental health. However, current methods for assessing fatigue present several barriers to building understanding of how these risks develop over time within individuals. Here, we explore the potential of momentary speech activity-based fatigue measurement in a large, multi-lingual cohort of shift workers, using an intensive longitudinal study design (twice-daily measurement over two weeks in N = 1197 individuals from six different countries). Paralinguistic speech features were used to predict different aspects of acute and chronic fatigue at each study time-point, with performance assessed in unseen (held-out) data. In the cross-sectional analysis, good (close to or exceeding current state-of-the-art) performance was achieved for both current sleep deprivation and self-reported sleepiness levels. The within-user analysis revealed robust increases in performance, yielding the ability to detect more subjective aspects of fatigue such as pervasive physical and mental exhaustion. These findings offer preliminary support for the utility of using brief momentary speech samples as a low-burden, acceptable, and reliable measure of different aspects of fatigue in high-risk populations such as shift workers.
