Regional differences were most pronounced in integrative and internally oriented areas. Each dimension also related differently to cortical morphology and neurotransmitter receptor density, highlighting diverse neurobiological substrates and supporting multimodal approaches to studying excitability.

papers.title: Kidney-derived mitochondrial extracellular vesicles trigger acute lung injury in sepsis via mtDNA-cGAS-STING in pulmonary endothelium
papers.abstract: Sepsis often leads to multiple organ failure, but how injury in one organ propagates to another remains poorly understood. Here we show that the injured kidney releases mitochondria-rich extracellular vesicles (mitoEVs) into the circulation, which travel to the lung and trigger acute lung injury. In septic mice and cultured renal tubular epithelial cells, sepsis promotes the formation of mitochondrial-derived vesicles by upregulating sorting nexin 9. Blocking this process in kidney tubules reduces the release of mitoEVs and protects against lung injury. Once taken up by lung endothelial cells, the mitochondrial DNA carried by these vesicles activates an innate immune pathway involving cGAS and STING, with ZBP1 serving as a potential cooperative partner for this activation. This leads to endothelial barrier disruption, immune cell recruitment, and respiratory failure. In patients with sepsis, higher levels of circulating mitoEVs associate with lung injury and death. These findings identify a kidney-to-lung signaling axis that may be targeted therapeutically.

papers.title: Analysis of 515 human proteomes defines plasma extracellular vesicle core composition, corona and coisolated networks
papers.abstract: Analyzing 515 clinical proteomes reveals that the plasma extracellular vesicle core is driven by a charge-based corona and physical co-isolation and identifies 8 distinct functional modules, reshaping liquid biopsy biomarker discovery.

papers.title: Artificial humic acids as model systems for resolving key structural controls on humic acid-metal complexation
papers.abstract: The stability of metal-humic associations controls metal mobility and persistence in natural environments, yet remains difficult to predict from functional-group abundance alone. Using artificial humic acids derived from rice straw and soybean straw as controlled models, we identify a precursor-encoded separation between site supply and site state during metal binding. Humification reorganized precursor chemistry into distinct molecular frameworks that regulated donor accessibility and the exchangeability of the resulting coordination state. Integrating 13C NMR, XAFS, FT-ICR MS, and molecular dynamics simulations, we linked precursor carbon domains to molecular organization and local Cd coordination. Soybean-straw humic acid contained more accessible O- and N-bearing donors, resulting in greater Cd uptake and higher intrinsic affinity under single-metal conditions. Rice-straw humic acid showed lower initial affinity but greater resistance to competitive displacement. Molecular association networks revealed a continuous, highly connected framework in rice-straw humic acid, whereas soybean-straw humic acid formed several relatively independent modules. These findings show that metal capture and retention are distinct outcomes governed by donor accessibility and coordination-state exchangeability, respectively. Precursor chemistry, therefore, acts as an upstream control on humic molecular frameworks and offers a basis for designing humic materials for rapid capture or sustained retention.

papers.title: Hybridizing expert descriptors and learned embeddings yields transferable Mat2Vec- * element representations
papers.abstract: Element representations bridge chemical identity and machine-learning models for materials prediction, but handcrafted descriptors, corpus-derived embeddings, and supervised embeddings are typically treated as separate choices. Here we show that handcrafted and supervised representations encode complementary chemical information and that supervised element geometry can be distilled into reusable element tables (Mat2Vec-*). Across eight structure-based MatBench regression tasks, controlled CGCNN and MEGNet benchmarks span 2,240 models over representation mixtures and latent dimensions. The top-performing models define rotation-invariant cosine-distance relations from which we reconstruct Mat2Vec-*. In composition-only model (CrabNet), these tables replace or augment corpus-derived Mat2Vec, with most configurations improving performance across all four MatBench composition tasks. On the Matbench Discovery WBM benchmark, Mat2Vec-* features further reduce errors for several modern structure-based predictors through lightweight residual correction. Together, these results establish Mat2Vec-* as a compact, transferable supervised chemical prior for materials prediction.

papers.title: Acoustically controlled polarization states of resonant γ -photons
papers.abstract: Coherent control of light and its interactions with matter is a key aspect of quantum optics. Nuclear resonant interactions enable coherent manipulation of photons at X-ray and γ-ray energies. One promising approach to manipulating γ-photons emitted by radioactive sources exploits ultrasonically vibrating nuclear resonant absorbers. However, previous studies have focused on unpolarized γ-radiation interacting with isotropic resonant media without exploiting polarization effects. Here, we demonstrate simultaneous temporal control of the waveform and polarization state of γ-photons by combining ultrasonic vibrations of magnetically ordered resonant absorbers with anisotropy in nuclear resonant scattering. This method allows interlinking phase differences of individual resonant interaction paths with their polarization dependence. A particular consequence is the possibility to form double-pulse γ-radiation sequences with tunable time-dependent polarization states. Using the reported method, coherent control of γ-photons can be expanded to polarization-based experiments and related applications in quantum optics can be further explored using a tabletop γ-optical setup.

papers.title: Evaluating the cost-effectiveness of next-generation sequencing strategies for familial hypercholesterolemia cascade screening in Thailand
papers.abstract: Genetic cascade screening of familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) effectively prevents cardiovascular complications, but it remains unclear how health systems should roll out genetic testing over time. We developed a policy-relevant, forward-looking framework for stepwise economic evaluation on genetic testing, using FH cascade testing in Thailand as a case study. We constructed a decision tree-Markov hybrid model for a cohort of 35-year-old probands with low-density lipoprotein cholesterol above 4.9 mmol/L and their first- and second-degree relatives. We performed stepwise evaluations on conventional three-gene panel testing, whole-exome sequencing (WES), and onward to emerging long-read sequencing (LRS), compared with standard of care from a societal perspective. Conventional economic evaluation compared panel testing and WES using currently available evidence, while early economic evaluation was applied to LRS to identify target product profiles and explore uncertainties. The analyses show that panel- and WES-based cascade screening are cost-effective versus standard of care, with incremental cost-effectiveness ratios (ICERs) of Thai baht (THB) 81,494 (€2,146/$2,371) and THB 74,641 (€1,966/$2,172) per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY), respectively. Compared with panel testing, WES generates 0.055 incremental QALYs at an ICER of THB 50,703 (€1,335/$1,475)/QALY. LRS is also cost-effective versus standard of care under target costs and yields 0.04 incremental QALYs/person versus WES, but requires cost reductions of 16.33% to THB 33,468/proband and 46.05% to THB 21,580/proband to surpass WES and dominate the market, respectively. This forward-looking, stepwise evaluation demonstrates that next-generation sequencing for FH cascade testing can be economically viable in Thailand while advancing precision health under universal healthcare. Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is an inherited condition that causes very high cholesterol levels and increases the risk of early heart disease and stroke. Many people with FH are not diagnosed. Testing the relatives of someone with FH can help identify affected family members early so they can receive treatment. In this study, we evaluated different genetic testing methods for conducting FH cascade testing in middle-income countries with universal health coverage, such as Thailand. Our results suggest that whole-exome sequencing provides greater health benefits with good value for money compared to standard of care and conventional three-gene panel, while emerging long-read sequencing may offer even greater benefits in the future with expected cost reductions. These findings support cost-effective stepwise implementation of next-generation sequencing to improve precision health in Thailand and similar health systems.

papers.title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe 2
papers.abstract: Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe 2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

papers.title: Multiparticle quantum walks in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model
papers.abstract: Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

papers.title: Automated inverse design of metainterfaces with tailored friction laws
papers.abstract: Understanding friction between contacting surfaces is important to improve device performance. Now a method is shown to discover materials that offer on-demand frictional behaviour using inverse design based on genetic algorithms.

papers.title: Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules
papers.abstract: Microtubules are bound by active motors and passively diffusing proteins. Now it is shown that this mixture of active and passive molecules is a realization of rectified Brownian motion in active matter.

papers.title: Low-voltage avalanche heterojunction phototransistor for infrared-to-visible upconversion
papers.abstract: Researchers demonstrate infrared-to-visible upconversion using an InGaAs/InP avalanche heterojunction phototransistor. Intrinsic positive feedback provides the photocurrent for amber LED operation, producing visible emission 17,000 times brighter than incident infrared light with a breakdown voltage as low as 1.4 V.

papers.title: Automatic on-chip separation of partially coherent light into its mutually incoherent components
papers.abstract: Partial coherence often limits imaging and optical information processing. Researchers demonstrate a photonic chip that separates partially coherent light into its coherence modes, enabling scalable coherence analysis with resources that scale linearly with mode rank.

papers.title: Light-switch for nerve cells
Optical control stabilizes cold-atom comagnetometry
papers.abstract: The use of tailored laser fields improves the coherence times of two co-trapped ytterbium isotopes, resulting in the rejection of magnetic-field noise by more than thirty-thousand-fold, opening the way to improved comagnetometry.

papers.title: Measuring hard X-ray attosecond pulses
papers.abstract: The generation and characterization of high-power X-ray attosecond pulses is a challenging research frontier in free-electron laser science. Now, researchers at the Linac Coherent Light Source have demonstrated experimental confirmation and measurement of hard X-ray pulses reaching 100-attosecond durations.

papers.title: Enhanced neutral seawater photoelectrolysis by fast hydrogen pumping at subnanometre triple interfaces
papers.abstract: Atomically dispersed Cr(OH) x on Pt/GaN creates subnanometre triple interfaces that couple water activation, hydrogen transfer and Pt–H formation across adjacent interfaces for fast hydrogen pumping in photoelectrochemical seawater splitting. This overcomes hydrogen-utilization limitations in single-interface catalysis and enables high-current outputs under neutral seawater photoelectrolysis in low-bias and bias-free devices.

papers.title: Sustainable photoelectrochemical lithium extraction mediated by self-regulated potential
papers.abstract: A solar-powered electrochemical system achieves selective lithium extraction from seawater and low-grade brine enabled by a self-regulated electrode potential, providing a simplified membrane-free approach to sustainable resource recovery.

papers.title: Durable reactive CO 2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts
papers.abstract: Reactive CO 2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. Here the authors show that pH-swing-driven acidification accelerates catalyst demetallation and develop a cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst that suppresses metal loss, sustaining efficient CO production for 1,000 h.

papers.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
papers.abstract: Power grids on five continents show frequency oscillations with a period of exactly 1 min. The authors trace this to clock-synchronized software in devices such as uninterruptible power supplies that creates coherent, repeating demand peaks.

papers.title: Selective blockade of microRNA-31-5p−calcitonin receptor interaction reverses established atrial fibrosis and atrial arrhythmia burden
papers.abstract: Trompf, Cox, Hulsurkar et al. show that the selective disruption of the miR-31-5p−CTR interaction in atrial fibrillation reverses established atrial fibrosis and reduces atrial fibrillation susceptibility, highlighting a promising RNA-based therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Electronically active polymers from the outside to the inside
papers.abstract: Electronically active polymers provide a natural interface between the human body and machines, where precise control down to the molecular level enables the multifaceted properties required for applications outside and inside the body. The next leap might come from materials that integrate with innate biological processes, coupled with a deeper understanding of their downstream effects.

papers.title: Accuracy and impact of an AI safety system for missed specialist referrals in primary care
papers.abstract: Missed specialist referrals in primary care pose substantial health and medico-legal risks, yet remain poorly understood. We developed an AI-supported safety system (MR-AI) to identify missed referrals from consultation notes, evaluated in a quasi-experimental study across seven primary care clinics in Singapore. MR-AI scanned ~25,000 notes weekly for referral intent without a corresponding order, achieving an estimated sevenfold increase in weekly missed referral detection (4.7 percentage point level increase; 95% CI 0.024–0.069; p < 0.001). Of 428 cases flagged, 225 were clinician-verified, alongside 31 patient-reported cases, yielding 256 total detections. MR-AI demonstrated 99.9% specificity and 48.8% sensitivity. In a blinded one-week comparison against seven physician reviewers, MR-AI achieved a PPV of 61.8% versus a human confirmation rate of 51.8% across 83 flagged cases, while requiring approximately 41 fewer projected staff-hours. AI-enabled surveillance substantially assisted in missed referral detection, though sustainable improvement will require complementary preventive workflow changes and future cost-effectiveness assessment.

papers.title: Interpretable graph learning of spatial TME patterns in digital pathology for gastric cancer prognosis
papers.abstract: Current gastric cancer (GC) risk stratification, based on TNM staging and molecular subtypes, often fails to capture intratumoral heterogeneity driving variable outcomes. Although the tumor microenvironment (TME) spatial architecture within histopathological images holds critical prognostic value, quantifying these interactions remains challenging. We present the Graph-based Tumor Microenvironment Aggregation (GTMA) framework, an interpretable deep learning approach modeling whole-slide images as spatial graphs to decipher tissue interactions. Validated in a large cohort (n = 1871) and TCGA-STAD dataset (n = 213), the GTMA-derived Risk Score (RS) provided prognostic information complementary to TNM staging and clinical models. Notably, the RS stratified patients into distinct risk groups within identical TNM stages and molecular subtypes, identifying high-risk patients traditionally overlooked. Integrative analysis revealed high-RS tumors feature a fibroblast-dominant, immune-excluded phenotype and distinct stromal spatial patterns. By linking digital pathology to biological TME patterns, GTMA offers a robust, interpretable AI tool for individualized prognostic risk stratification and precision oncology in GC.

papers.title: Implementation strategies for digital relapse prevention in schizophrenia identified during a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Digital mental health technologies hold promise, yet their integration into routine care remains challenging. This study reports findings from an implementation workshop conducted midway through an ongoing multi-site randomized controlled trial (RCT) evaluating a smartphone-based relapse prevention app for patients with schizophrenia and schizoaffective disorder. Sixteen stakeholders, including developers, researchers, and clinicians, discussed experiences and barriers using a semi-structured agenda, incorporating prior feedback from three focus groups with people with lived experience, and analyzed the discussions using an adopted R(E)-AIM framework (Reach, Adoption, Implementation, and Maintenance). Findings highlight the need for structural, technical, and personnel adjustments to support sustainable implementation. Key recommendations include integrating digital tools into discharge planning, enhancing interdisciplinary collaboration, delegating digital responsibilities, and streamlining technical workflows to facilitate seamless adoption. These insights inform feasibility considerations and strategic requirements for digital interventions in severe mental illness, offering guidance for future RCTs and practice-oriented integration of digital therapeutics in psychiatric care.

papers.title: Platform evaluation and lessons learned with IT-supported patient recruitment
papers.abstract: Recruiting participants for clinical trials is a challenge, often limited by inefficient methods for identifying eligible candidates. Clinical trial recruitment support systems (CTRSS) can enhance recruitment efficiency by leveraging data from electronic health records (EHR). We evaluated two CTRSS—recruIT and KAS+—to quantify their real-world impact on enrollment. Within the German MIRACUM consortium, we conducted a multicenter segmented interrupted time-series (ITS) evaluation across six university hospitals. Twenty-nine trials contributed 814 observation weeks spanning a control phase (usual practice) and an intervention phase (CTRSS active). Weekly enrollments were compared using segmented negative binomial mixed models estimating level and slope changes at implementation, complemented by Wilcoxon signed-rank tests. A criteria revision covariate captured iterative refinement of computable cohort definitions. In pooled ITS analyses, we observed neither a statistically significant immediate level change nor a statistically significant post-implementation slope change in weekly enrollments. Effects were highly heterogeneous across trials and specialties; implemented eligibility logic most often relied on diagnosis, age, and visit data, while laboratory values and structured observations were seldom available. Higher values of the criteria revision covariate were associated with higher recruitment in some settings, with the most exploratory signal observed at the single KAS+ site. Despite the potential benefits of CTRSS, their effectiveness depends on careful customization and implementation. Overall, our findings suggest that CTRSS impact is context-dependent and that measurable benefit is more likely driven by iterative computable phenotyping and local workflow fit rather than a simple “switch-on” effect. Context-specific adaptation and continual revision of eligibility logic appear critical to realizing benefit. Future studies should reduce trial heterogeneity, strengthen compliance incentives, and employ granular outcomes, such as identification-to-enrollment latency, to better capture workflow-mediated effects.

papers.title: AnySleep: a channel-agnostic deep learning system for high-resolution sleep staging in multi-center cohorts
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for health, yet studying its dynamics requires manual sleep staging, a labor-intensive step in research and clinical care. Across centers, polysomnography (PSG) recordings are traditionally scored in 30-s epochs for pragmatic, not physiological, reasons and vary in electrode count, montage, and subject characteristics. These constraints challenge harmonized multi-center studies and the discovery of robust biomarkers on shorter timescales. We present AnySleep, a deep neural network that scores sleep from any electroencephalography (EEG) or electrooculography (EOG) data at adjustable temporal resolutions. We trained and validated the model on over 20,000 overnight recordings (>200,000 h of EEG and EOG) from 28 datasets across multiple clinics to promote robust generalization across sites. The model attains state-of-the-art performance and surpasses or equals established baselines at 30-s epochs. Performance improves with more channels, yet remains strong when EOG is absent, or only EOG or single EEG derivations (frontal, central, or occipital) are available. On sub-30-s timescales, the model captures short wake intrusions consistent with arousals and improves the prediction of pathophysiological conditions (obstructive sleep apnea, narcolepsy type 1, insomnia) over 30-s scoring. We make the model publicly available to facilitate large-scale studies with heterogeneous electrode setups and accelerate biomarker discovery in sleep.

papers.title: Optimal closed-loop feedback control of blood flow after spinal cord injury with norepinephrine
papers.abstract: A closed-loop control strategy regulates spinal cord blood flow by adjusting norepinephrine infusion using real-time flow measurements, enabling direct flow targeting after acute injury.

papers.title: Topological control of polaritonic flatbands in anisotropic van der Waals metasurfaces
papers.abstract: Photonic metasurfaces patterned in anisotropic ReS 2 create robust, spectrally scalable directional photonic flatbands, enabling the topological control of polarization-resolved exciton–polaritons and enhanced light–matter coupling.

papers.title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
papers.abstract: The electron-beam-assisted subtraction method enables the controllable fabrication of free-standing metal oxide monolayers, along with lateral heterostructures and twisted bilayers, expanding the material space of 2D quantum systems.

papers.title: Electric-field-controlled spin transport in a vertical organic spin–field device for room-temperature spin logic
papers.abstract: A vertical organic spin–field device based on an organic semiconductor/ferromagnet interface can be used to continuously modulate spin polarization from 0% to 100% at room temperature.

papers.title: Foundation model for particle collision data analysis
papers.abstract: Hsu et al. present EVENET, a foundation model pretrained on simulated particle collisions using both self-supervised learning and physics labels, which transfers across many analysis tasks and works on real collider data.

papers.title: Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations
papers.abstract: This Article presents a large-scale analysis of self-supervised learning methods for high-content morphological profiling.

papers.title: Enhanced cfDNA methylation profiling by detection and correction of jagged ends
papers.abstract: The computational tool JEEPERS detects and corrects jagged-end-induced errors in cell-free DNA methylation analysis, demonstrating improved performance in multiple applications, such as cancer detection and monitoring.

papers.title: 3D-printable and cytocompatible hydrogel from Acinetobacter baylyi ADP1 extracellular matrix
papers.abstract: Multicomponent hydrogels that mimic natural extracellular matrices remain underexplored due to their complex design requirements. Here, the authors introduce a bacterial-derived multicomponent hydrogel with photocrosslinking, bioprinting, injectable, and cytocompatible properties for biofabrication applications.

papers.title: Epitaxial superconductor/semiconductor/metal nitride heterostructure for single-photon detection
papers.abstract: Single-photon detectors are central to emerging quantum and photonic technologies, but material inhomogeneity in conventional superconducting nanowire devices can limit performance and scalability. Here, the authors demonstrate an all-epitaxial superconducting nanowire single-photon detector platform that delivers wafer-scale uniformity and ~90% broadband detection efficiency near the 1550 nm telecommunication wavelength, enabling scalable detector arrays and wavelength-division multiplexing applications.

papers.title: Atomistic islet amyloid polypeptide fibril simulations reveal interplay of amyloid kinetic and mechanical stability
papers.abstract: Human islet amyloid polypeptide aggregation is a hallmark of type 2 diabetes. Here, the authors developed a molecular dynamics framework to reveal how mechanical forces govern amyloid fibril stability and breakage.

papers.title: Biomimetic functional materials, devices, and systems: integrating nature-inspired design across flexible electronic scales
papers.abstract: Biological systems maintain resilience through structured and adaptive integration across materials, architectures, and feedback networks, yet flexible electronics arising from this often remain component-driven. In this perspective, we propose a system-level framework for biomimetic and bioinspired flexible electronics, linking nature-inspired materials, functional interfaces, and closed-loop architectures. Advances in tactile sensing, mechanotransduction, biointerfaces, and energy-aware computation provide promising routes toward autonomous, resilient, and biologically integrated electronic systems.

papers.title: Circuit plasticity coordinates action selection and temporal compression during operant conditioning in Aplysia
papers.abstract: A central challenge in neuroscience is to explain how reinforcement jointly shapes action selection and the temporal structure of action execution to optimize behavioral efficiency. Using an ex vivo operant conditioning paradigm in the Aplysia feeding circuit, we found that reinforcement biases selection toward ingestive motor programs and shortens their duration by advancing the transition from protraction to retraction phases of the feeding movements. Temporal compression reflected coordinated plasticity of phase-switch elements. Operant conditioning reduced the intrinsic electrical excitability of neuron B52 and thereby weakened B52-mediated inhibition of the retraction-initiating interneuron B64, while also lowering the threshold for triggering the B64 plateau potential. Phase-restricted co-manipulation of B52 and B64 activity reproduced protraction shortening. These results provide a circuit-level framework for how reinforcement coordinates motor-pattern selection with temporal structure within identified circuitry, a form of circuit plasticity that may contribute to the efficiency of action execution.

papers.title: M6A demethylation of IRF9 by ALKBH5 promotes intervertebral disc degeneration via nucleus pulposus cell necroptosis
papers.abstract: Necroptosis drives disc degeneration. ALKBH5 demethylates IRF9 mRNA, blocking YTHDF2-mediated decay; IRF9 then activates RIPK1/RIPK3/MLKL, driving nucleus pulposus cell necroptosis. Targeting this axis alleviates disc degeneration in rats.

papers.title: BdCDPK5 is an essential regulator of Babesia divergens intraerythrocytic progression
papers.abstract: Calcium-dependent protein kinases (CDPKs) are central regulators of developmental transitions in apicomplexan parasites, yet their roles in tick-borne pathogen Babesia remain largely uncharacterized. Using Babesia divergens, a zoonotic parasite of growing medical and veterinary concern, we identify BdCDPK5 as an essential enzyme controlling intraerythrocytic parasite replication. Through comprehensive transcriptional profiling of the bdcdpk repertoire across synchronized blood-stages, combined with an animal-free Ixodes ricinus membrane feeding infection model, we show that bdcdpk5 is dominantly expressed during vector tissue colonization and significantly upregulated upon erythrocyte invasion. Genetic disruption of BdCDPK5 caused long-term growth arrest and pronounced morphological defects, whereas its ectopic expression promoted parasite replication. Localization analyses further revealed BdCDPK5 to be diffusely distributed throughout the parasite cytoplasm and associated with vesicle-like structures within infected erythrocytes. Together, these findings establish BdCDPK5 as a molecular determinant of B. divergens intraerythrocytic infection and highlight it as a promising target for selective therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Myristic acid promotes in vitro maturation and developmental competence of porcine oocytes
papers.abstract: The present study examined how antral follicle size influences oocyte meiotic maturation and developmental competence from a metabolic perspective and explored strategies to improve the meiotic maturation and quality of oocytes derived from small antral follicles. Untargeted metabolomics revealed dynamic metabolic changes during porcine antral follicle development, with increased fatty acid synthesis and enhanced activities of related enzymes in oocytes from larger follicles. In vitro, myristic acid (MA) improved meiotic maturation (polar body extrusion, spindle morphology, chromosome dynamics) and survival of oocytes from small follicles by reducing Annexin V expression and ROS levels. MA also enhanced their developmental competence after parthenogenetic activation. Molecular and cytochemical analyses showed that MA altered the transcriptional profile, increased lipid storage, and boosted mitochondrial number and function. Finally, MA upregulated SIRT1, activated PPARα, and increased CPT2 expression, suggesting a potential mechanism underlying its effects on these oocytes.

papers.title: Omega-3 PUFA supplementation promotes arthritis resolution by modulating joint cell phenotype involving E-series resolvins
papers.abstract: The cellular mechanisms of omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acid (ω3 PUFA) supplementation were investigated in inflammatory arthritis. Mice fed a prophylactic ω3 PUFA-enriched diet displayed reduced arthritis and paw oedema, with a discrete regulation of innate and stromal cell phenotypes in arthritic joints. Non-classical monocytes and VCAM-1+ synovial fibroblasts were lower at peak arthritis while pro-resolution MerTK+CD206+ macrophages were increased at resolution onset. Lipid mediator profiling of arthritic paws identified a distinct repertoire of molecules in ω3-fed mice, with elevated EPA-derived resolvin E2 (RvE2) and RvE4, compared with increased TXB2 and PGF2α with a normal diet. Pharmacological treatment of mice with RvE2 and RvE4 concomitant with arthritis induction, attenuated arthritis and increased MerTK+CD206+ macrophages in arthritic joints. Synovial explant treatment revealed reduced pro-inflammatory mediator and enzyme release including IL-6, CCL2 and MMP-9. In arthritic patient blood, RvE2 and RvE4 (100 nM) lowered monocyte ICAM-1 expression. Collectively, these data identify cellular and molecular determinants of an ω3 diet in pre-clinical and human settings, highlighting therapeutic potential.

papers.title: Structure-function tethering of human locus coeruleus connectivity reveals a noradrenergic cortical hierarchy
papers.abstract: The locus coeruleus (LC) is the primary source of cerebral norepinephrine and plays a broad role in cognition. Here, we show the macroscale organization of human LC connectivity using 7 T diffusion and resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Structural and functional connectivity exhibit a dominant rostral-caudal gradient, with structure-function tethering lowest in the intermediate LC and increasing toward its rostral and caudal portions. In the neocortex, this pattern is expressed as steeply increasing tethering from the central sulcus toward anterior and posterior regions. Allen Mouse Brain Connectivity Atlas tracing further reveals preferential LC projections to somatomotor cortex. The cortical expression of LC structure-function tethering exhibits a network-level hierarchy and aligns with a behavioral axis. Additionally, this cortical expression shows significant spatial covariance with norepinephrine transporter concentration, fiber length, and gray matter volume. Together, these findings provide MRI-based evidence for a hierarchical macroscale organization of human LC connectivity linking structural and functional architecture to cortical and behavioral variation.

papers.title: OVOL1/2 regulate trophectoderm differentiation during the morula-to-blastocyst transition
papers.abstract: Blastocyst formation failure is a major challenge in preimplantation development. We identify OVOL1/2 as regulators of the morula-to-blastocyst transition that promote trophectoderm differentiation through ARPC1B-mediated cytoskeletal remodeling.

papers.title: Microbiology Galaxy Lab: a community-driven gateway for reproducible and FAIR analysis of microbiological data
papers.abstract: Microbiology Galaxy Lab provides a community-driven, democratized ecosystem of tools, workflows, training, and computational infrastructure enabling accessible and reproducible microbial research across health, environmental, agricultural, food, and One Health domains.

papers.title: Metabolic sensor Gpr35 links dietary lipids to itch mediating neural circuits
papers.abstract: Using cell physiology, bioinformatics, pharmacology, mouse genetics and behaviour, we uncover metabolic-neuronal pathways for itch. We show that the linoleic acid metabolite EKODE acts via Gpr35 to trigger inflammation and itch in skin conditions.

papers.title: TOC159 receptors use a galactolipid-specific bipartite signal for chloroplast targeting in Arabidopsis thaliana
papers.abstract: Chloroplast biogenesis and function depend on the recognition and import of nucleus-encoded preproteins by the translocon at the outer envelope membrane of chloroplasts (TOC), yet the mechanism by which TOC159 receptors, key components of the TOC complex, are targeted and inserted remains only partially understood. Here we show the C-terminus of TOC159 from Arabidopsis thaliana contains a highly conserved bipartite chloroplast targeting signal, composed of a canonical β-signal and “reverse transit peptide-like” extension that shares canonical chloroplast transit peptide characteristics in reverse orientation. Using chloroplast targeting assays in planta and peptide-lipid interaction assays in vitro, we demonstrate that the β-signal is required for targeting, whereas the reverse transit peptide-like extension is not required, but contributes significantly to targeting fidelity through interactions with galactolipids enriched in plastid membranes. These findings support an evolutionary adaptation in TOC159 targeting, combining β-signal-driven insertion with galactolipid-specific recognition that couples TOC159 targeting to TOC complex assembly and provides a mechanism for organelle discrimination in plant cells.

papers.title: Developmental and genetic modulation of evidence integration dynamics in zebrafish sensorimotor decision-making
papers.abstract: Animals integrate information over time and maintain persistent internal representations of cues to guide decision-making. How the underlying behavioral algorithms of individual animals depend on factors such as experience, developmental stage, or genotype remains poorly understood. Drift-diffusion models provide a powerful theoretical framework to describe and predict performance metrics across a wide range of species. The stochastic nature of these models and the typically limited throughput of most experimental designs challenge the automatic inference of latent variables. Here, we combine high-throughput behavioral assays in larval zebrafish with drift-diffusion modeling, revealing that larvae progressively develop more persistent, self-reinforcing integration dynamics during early development. This effect is reduced in fish carrying mutations in genes linked to human epilepsy and schizophrenia. Our results show that behavior-based drift-diffusion modeling can offer a scalable, automated approach to generate experimentally testable hypotheses about the algorithmic implementation of sensorimotor integration in health and disease.

papers.title: Imaging hot-electron Thomson cooling beyond the Boltzmann–Onsager framework
papers.abstract: Classical Thomson cooling is inefficient. Now non-equilibrium energy dissipation with a breakdown of the Boltzmann–Onsager limit is demonstrated by imaging hot electrons in HgTe and HgCdTe quantum wells.

papers.title: Ligand-engineered CsEuI 3 nanocrystals for efficient single-component white electroluminescence
papers.abstract: Ligand-engineered CsEuI 3 nanocrystals enable efficient single-component white electroluminescence with a peak external quantum efficiency of 8.3% and integration into active-matrix full-colour displays.

papers.title: Liquid-phase growth of dense ceramic films
papers.abstract: By decoupling ceramic-film densification from high-temperature sintering, molten-salt-mediated liquid-phase growth enables a dense, compositionally uniform proton-conducting thin film to form at 800 °C, despite its melting point exceeding 2,700 °C. This strategy opens opportunities for low-temperature ceramic fabrication and on-demand materials design.

papers.title: Chemical-linkage-regulated single-phase crystallization and uniform gallium alloying for efficient solution-processed chalcopyrite solar cells
papers.abstract: Controlling phase evolution and composition homogeneity are challenging for chalcopyrites. Ma, Wu, Liu, Yan et al. use acetate anions to build complex networks in precursor solution, achieving single-phase crystallization and an 18.53% efficient Cu(In,Ga)Se 2 solar cell.

papers.title: Perovskite lattice compliance enables efficient and stable bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Bifacial perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells are promising for high area-normalized power output, but factors governing the photothermal stability of perovskite absorbers remains unclear. Xu et al. identify lattice compliance as a descriptor when screening stable perovskites.

papers.title: The SDGs need a subjective well-being reality check
papers.abstract: The Sustainable Development Goals aim to improve lives, but it is unclear whether progress on Sustainable Development Goal indicators translates into greater subjective well-being over time. A study of 42 countries found associations in levels, but weak links with year-to-year changes in life evaluations.

papers.title: Global socio-economic resilience to disasters
papers.abstract: Disaster risk assessments often overlook how damages affect well-being and recovery across populations. A global analysis now shows that well-being losses from disasters are much higher than asset damages, with the poorest suffering disproportionately.

papers.title: 5-year outcomes of chemotherapy de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and exploratory circulating tumor DNA analyses from the randomized phase 2 PHERGain trial
papers.abstract: A 5-year secondary analysis of the phase 2 PHERGain trial supports the clinical utility of a PET-guided adaptive strategy for treatment de-escalation in HER2-positive early breast cancer and provides circulating tumor DNA insights that could inform further treatment approaches.

papers.title: A clinical multimodal vision language foundation model with fine-grain explainability
papers.abstract: A multimodal vision language foundation model, EVLF-FM, integrates extensive clinical data and advanced training techniques, achieving superior diagnostic accuracy and explainability across diverse imaging modalities, enhancing clinical decision-making through robust reasoning and interpretability.

papers.title: Insights into early-onset colorectal cancer from a single-nucleus RNA-seq atlas of colorectal cancer across the age continuum
papers.abstract: A high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas of 189 colorectal tumors from patients aged 20–90+ years uncovers age-associated features of colorectal cancer.

papers.title: Temporal proteomics maps concealed-stage remodeling and reveals early mitochondrial alteration as an intervention target in a model of PKP2-arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy
papers.abstract: Achter, Svenningsen, Mulvey, Bertoli et al. use an inducible cardiomyocyte-specific Pkp2 knockout model to map the spatiotemporal proteomic changes underlying arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy. They identify early mitochondrial remodeling preceding overt disease and show that honokiol attenuates pathological protein network alterations.

papers.title: Switchable Chlorine Atom Transfer Radical Reactions
papers.abstract: Atom transfer radical reactions—encompassing atom transfer radical addition (ATRA)1 and atom transfer radical polymerization (ATRP)2—provide a versatile route to synthesize functionalized small molecules and polymers. Using readily available unactivated alkyl chlorides3 instead of activated organohalides represents the state-of-the-art in this field, as this requires cleaving stronger C–Cl bonds in the substrates while preserving weaker ones in the products. Here we describe a dual-copper relay catalytic strategy to overcome this limitation. A dinuclear copper complex selectively activates the robust C–Cl bond of unactivated alkyl chlorides, while a mononuclear copper catalyst mediates controllable C–Cl bond reconstruction. The reaction pathway can be switched between ATRA and ATRP-type reactions in the presence or absence of the mononuclear copper partner, thus providing a switchable platform for chlorine atom transfer radical reactions. This protocol can not only enable synthesis of structurally diverse ATRA products and α-end-functionalized polyacrylates, but allow for direct modification of poly(vinyl chloride) (PVC) under mild reaction conditions. It demonstrates the successful utility of unactivated organochlorides in organic synthesis and polymer science.

papers.title: Stone and water governed early human settlement of the desert
papers.abstract: A geoarchaeological survey of the Rub’ al Khali (the Empty Quarter of Arabia) and spatial modelling of the Arabian Peninsula suggest that human settlement tracked the co-occurrence of water and stone suitable for making tools, rather than water alone.

papers.title: Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin targets CD9 to drive NEC and brain injury
papers.abstract: A subset of necrotizing enterocolitis in infants is mediated specifically by the Clostridium perfringens Delta toxin.

papers.title: Tandem repeat variation shapes immune cell type-specific gene expression
papers.abstract: Whole-genome sequencing and cell-level gene expression measurements show that length variation in tandem repeats in the human genome contributes to cell type-specific differences in gene regulation and expression, as well as the architecture of complex traits.

papers.title: Delayed electron–hole recombination in a pseudo-direct semiconductor
papers.abstract: Pseudo-direct bandgap character in bismuth sulfide retards bimolecular electron–hole recombination while preserving strong light absorption.

papers.title: Perinatal elimination of genetically aberrant human cortical neurons
papers.abstract: Single-neuron sequencing shows that widespread genomic abnormalities are common prenatally but largely eliminated around birth, indicating developmental genome quality control in human neurons.

papers.title: Connectome simulations identify a central pattern generator for fly walking
papers.abstract: Computational simulations of a neural network based on fly connectomes identify a three-neuron circuit that is organized to produce leg motor rhythms for walking.

papers.title: Narrow carbon pentaheptite nanoribbon as a covalent metal
papers.abstract: Planar carbon pentaheptite nanoribbons are synthesized by laterally fusing polypentalene chains transformed from pre-synthesized polycyclooctadiene chains, suggesting a possible route towards carbon quantum wires.

papers.title: Subcycle videography of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene
papers.abstract: An experimental concept enabling attosecond-precision, subcycle band-structure videography covering the entire first Brillouin zone is demonstrated and used to visualize the lightwave-driven electron motion of Landau–Zener–Majorana transitions in graphene.

papers.title: Diet at disease onset determines tissue inflammatory memory
papers.abstract: Dietary state during a narrow temporal window can durably reprogram disease trajectory.

papers.title: T and B cells recognize splicing-derived neutrophil neoantigens in lupus
papers.abstract: In systemic lupus erythematosus, aberrant splicing in neutrophils generates novel peptides that are presented on MHC I, driving CD4 + and CD8 + T cell activation, clonal expansion and IgG autoantibody responses, establishing neoantigen-driven autoimmune immunity.

papers.title: Rare and common genetic variants shape single-cell immune gene expression
papers.abstract: Phase 1 of TenK10K takes single-cell RNA sequencing and matched whole-genome sequencing data from 1,925 individuals, enabling detection of associations for common and rare genetic variants, the latter of which have been uncharacterized in their impact on cell-specific gene expression.

papers.title: Tracing the spread of Germanic languages using ancient genomics
papers.abstract: Analysis of newly sequenced and previously published ancient human genomes identifies migrations associated with the spread of the Germanic language group, from its arrival in Scandinavia 4,000 years ago, through to its diversification during the historical period.

papers.title: Altermagnetic signatures and topological textures in ultrathin multiferroic BiFeO 3
papers.abstract: Epitaxial strain and a metallic SrRuO 3 bottom electrode are used to stablilize a monoclinic phase in four-unit-cell BiFeO 3 thin films. A broad suite of measurements are used to support the presence of both ferroelectricity and d -wave altermagnetism in these ultrathin films.

papers.title: Cellular-resolution three-photon ultra-deep imaging (TrUDI) of neuronal population activity at 2-mm depth in the mammalian brain
papers.abstract: TrUDI is an optimized three-photon imaging approach that allows structural and functional imaging of neuroactivity up to a depth of 2 mm in the mouse brain.

papers.title: Aptamer-mediated multivalent endogenous ADAR1 recruitment for highly efficient RNA editing
papers.abstract: The multivalent ADAR1-recruiting RNA editing system (MARRS) is an RNA editing platform that efficiently recruits endogenous ADAR1 to achieve precise adenosine-to-inosine editing. MARRS enables up to 100% editing in vitro and 84% in vivo with high specificity across diverse RNA targets.

papers.title: An engineered, compact Cas12m variant for multiplexed gene activation in vivo
papers.abstract: smCRISPRa is a compact platform for high-efficiency multiplexed gene activation in mouse models.

papers.title: An mRNA–lipid nanoparticle vaccine against H5N1 influenza virus protects lactating dairy cows from infection
papers.abstract: Dairy cows are protected from H5N1 influenza by an mRNA vaccine.

papers.title: A coordination-ligand reorientation mechanism for ferroelectricity in Mn(II) hybrid complex and its utility for memory application
papers.abstract: Addressing the limitations of classical models in molecular ferroelectrics, the authors introduce a ligand-tilting design using asymmetric isothiocyanate ligands. This approach enables room-temperature ferroelectricity and neuromorphic capabilities in devices, with implications for memory and brain-inspired computing, as demonstrated by their integration into ferroelectric field-effect transistors.

papers.title: An integrated NMR field probe using rapid non-adiabatic field switch-off for (ultra) low field MRI
papers.abstract: Pavel Povolni and colleagues report an integrated NMR field probe for low-field MRI based on rapid non-adiabatic switch-off of a pre-polarization field using controlled avalanche breakdown in SiC transistors. The probe measures Larmor frequencies without prior field knowledge from 1 to 45 mT, covering field strengths relevant to ultra-low- and low-field MRI.

papers.title: A review of ring-type rotational MEMS traveling-wave ultrasonic micromotors: design, detection, control, and application validation
papers.abstract: The ring-type rotational microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) traveling-wave ultrasonic micromotor has emerged as an important candidate for micro- and small-scale precision rotary actuation because of its thin-film structure, low driving voltage, less electromagnetic interference, and strong potential for system-level integration. In recent years, continuous advances in MEMS wafer processing, lead zirconate titanate (PZT) thin-film deposition and etching, and multi-layer interconnect packaging have driven substantial progress in micro-stator design, output performance, online sensing, motion control, and application validation of ring-type rotational MEMS traveling-wave ultrasonic micromotors (R-MTWUMs). Centered on the framework of design, detection, control, and application, this review systematically summarizes the development of R-MTWUMs. It first outlines their operating principles and representative fabrication processes, and then critically reviews the evolution of micro-stator configurations from substrate supported structures to nodal circle anchored and flexibly supported structures, and further to stator teeth and ball-amplified structures. Key performance metrics, including quality factor, driving voltage, torque, and rotation speed, are comparatively analyzed. On this basis, the review further summarizes the main detection methods used for R-MTWUMs, discusses recent progress in angular position sensing, driving and control, feedback electrode-based mode monitoring, and closed-loop control, and assesses their application potential through the application validation. Finally, this review summarizes major development trends, discusses the remaining challenges in fabrication, mechanism, evaluation, on-chip sensing, and closed-loop control, and outlines future research directions to accelerate the transition of R-MTWUMs from laboratory prototypes to practical engineering systems.

papers.title: CRISPR knockout screen identifies MYD88/IRAK4 signaling as a mediator of deoxynivalenol-induced oxidative damage
papers.abstract: Deoxynivalenol (DON) is a prevalent mycotoxin that poses serious risks to food and feed safety, particularly affecting pigs. However, the primary host factors mediating DON cytotoxicity remain poorly understood. Here, we perform a genome-wide CRISPR knockout (KO) screen in porcine intestinal epithelial IPI-2I cells and identify MYD88 and IRAK4 as the top-ranked genes conferring resilience to DON-induced cell death. DON treatment activates the MYD88/IRAK4/NF-κB signaling axis, leading to pronounced upregulation of pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1β, IL-6, and TNFα. Concomitantly, DON suppresses the expression of multiple antioxidant genes (e.g., GPX4, SOD1, NQO1, GCLC) and promotes accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS) and oxidized protein. Genetic KO of MYD88 or IRAK4 markedly reduces IL-1β expression, partially restores antioxidant protein levels, attenuates ROS and oxidized protein accumulation, and significantly improves cell viability upon DON exposure. Our findings establish the MYD88/IRAK4 signaling cascade as a critical driver of DON-triggered inflammatory and oxidative damage, revealing potential therapeutic targets for mitigating mycotoxin toxicity in livestock.

papers.title: PDE10A identified by cross-hemisphere visual cortex proteomics restores adult ocular dominance plasticity involving cAMP/CREB signaling
papers.abstract: Ocular dominance plasticity (ODP) is robust during the critical period but is restricted in adulthood. The molecular programs that distinguish this permissive state and whether they can be pharmacologically engaged in adulthood remain unclear. Here, using quantitative proteomics of the left and right visual cortices from monocularly deprived (MD) juvenile mice, we identify phosphodiesterase 10 A (PDE10A) and the cAMP signaling pathway as molecular signatures of juvenile ODP. Juvenile MD is associated with reduced PDE10A and increased phosphorylated CREB (pCREB) in the visual cortex contralateral to the deprived eye, whereas adult mice show no comparable response. In adult mice, systemic administration of the selective PDE10A inhibitor TAK-063 during MD reinstates an experience-dependent ocular dominance shift and reduces visual acuity in the deprived eye. This is accompanied by increased cortical cAMP and pPKA, an inverted-U pCREB response peaking at 0.3 mg/kg, and upregulation of plasticity-related synaptic proteins. TAK-063 does not alter basal visual function, retinal electrophysiology, or locomotor behavior in non-deprived adults, excluding nonspecific sensory/motor confounds. These findings identify PDE10A as a candidate molecular regulator of visual cortical plasticity and support its pharmacological inhibition as a strategy to facilitate experience-dependent plasticity in the adult visual cortex.

papers.title: Mercury contamination impairs the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal axis of a neotropical caiman
papers.abstract: Reduced physiological stress response is associated with elevated mercury from environmental contamination in wild caimans, supporting a conserved mechanism of endocrine disruption with implications for wildlife resilience.

papers.title: Nucleophilic defluorination of PFAS under mild conditions
papers.abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are globally significant water contaminants because of their persistence and associated environmental and health risks. Because PFAS stability and toxicity are closely linked to their fluorinated structures, complete defluorination represents a critical strategy for detoxification. Yet near-complete defluorination of structurally diverse PFAS, particularly short-chain compounds, under mild conditions remains challenging. Here, we report a nucleophile-driven approach for effective PFAS defluorination in DMSO at relatively mild temperatures around 100 °C, yielding free fluoride ions. Five nucleophiles, methanethiolate, ethanethiolate, methoxide, ethoxide, and amide, were evaluated. Under optimized conditions, complete defluorination, as verified by nearly quantitative fluoride recovery, was achieved for a broad range of perfluoroalkyl carboxylic acids and fluoropolymers, including short- and ultrashort-chain compounds such as PFPrA and TFA, which are typically resistant to other defluorination methods. Partial degradation of PFOS was also achieved under the same conditions. This approach provides an effective route to PFAS defluorination under comparatively mild reaction conditions.

papers.title: Hierarchical structure of primary and hybridization-induced superconducting correlations in bilayer nickelates
papers.abstract: The discovery of high-pressure superconductivity in the bilayer nickelate La3Ni2O7, with a transition temperature approaching 80 K, has stimulated intense debate regarding its microscopic origin. Although an s± gap symmetry has been widely proposed, the electronic degrees of freedom responsible for pairing remain unsettled. Here we investigate a bilayer two-orbital Hubbard model using the variational Monte Carlo method and reveal a hierarchical pairing structure in bilayer nickelates. The primary pairing tendency originates from the bonding–antibonding splitting of the Ni $$3{d}_{{z}^{2}}$$ orbitals, while orbital hybridization redistributes superconducting correlations to the $${d}_{{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}}$$ channel despite its weak intrinsic pairing tendency. This distinction between the origin of pairing and the resulting superconducting correlations explains why the two orbital channels exhibit comparable long-range correlations. The resulting s± state is robust against changes in Fermi-surface topology. These results reconcile apparently competing theoretical scenarios and provide a comprehensive understanding, highlighting the distinctive role of orbital hybridization in multilayer correlated superconductors.

papers.title: Digital home-based monitoring for patients with hypertension and type 2 diabetes in Ghana
papers.abstract: van Andel, Aovare et al. test a smartphone-based home monitoring system for adults with hypertension and type 2 diabetes in Accra, Ghana. The system is feasible and improves long-term blood pressure control, while modestly reducing blood glucose in those with high baseline levels.

papers.title: AI-guided discovery of self-assembled monolayers combining synthetic accessibility and interfacial stability for perovskite solar cells
papers.abstract: Using an artificial intelligence-guided framework combining retrosynthetic prediction, high-throughput DFT screening and chemical expertise, a readily synthesizable self-assembled monolayer for perovskite photovoltaics is identified. The top candidate delivers 27.2% efficiency and retains >95% of its initial efficiency after 2,000 h at 65 °C under maximum-power-point tracking.

papers.title: Carbonation of silicate minerals contributes to atmospheric CO 2 drawdown in glacier-fed streams
papers.abstract: Geochemical analyses of 170 glacier-fed streams reveal widespread CO 2 undersaturation, with 69% of sites below atmospheric equilibrium. Combined streamwater and sediment analyses identify silicate carbonation and secondary Mg-rich carbonate formation as a pathway that can contribute to atmospheric CO 2 uptake and transient inorganic carbon storage under favourable geochemical conditions.

papers.title: Solar-operated interlayer electrothermal evaporator enabling instant high-flux freshwater production across multiple scenarios
papers.abstract: An interlayer evaporator integrating electrothermal and photothermal effects achieves efficient freshwater production from diverse water sources, enabled by reduced heat loss and improved heat utilization.

papers.title: A decade of machine learning for materials development
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, machine learning for materials has expanded from property prediction to generative design and experimental discovery. The next challenge is to understand how materials evolve and function across scales under real operating conditions, and to translate that understanding into reliable materials development.

papers.title: Mitochondrial-targeted strategies for advancing ovarian cryopreservation: enhancing follicular survival and reproductive health
papers.abstract: Global fertility rates are in decline, underscoring the importance of effective fertility preservation strategies. Ovarian tissue cryopreservation and transplantation (OTCT) shows great promise but faces challenges like oxidative stress, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and poor follicle survival due to burn out. Protecting and preserving a greater number of primordial follicles remains pivotal to the success of this technology. While current strategies predominantly rely on antioxidants, their efficacy is constrained by non-specificity and the inability to achieve sustained release at the transplantation site. In this study, we explored the potential of elamipretide (SS31), a novel mitochondrial-targeted antioxidant peptide, to address these limitations. By combining SS31 with a recombinant human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (rhGM-CSF) gel, we achieved localized and sustained release of SS31 at the transplantation site in rabbits. This combination demonstrated synergistic effects by reducing oxidative stress, improving mitochondrial function, and enhancing follicular survival. Notably, reproductive endocrine function was restored 8 weeks post-transplantation. Proteomics and metabolomics analyses revealed that these improvements were primarily attributed to the activation of energy metabolism pathway. Our findings suggest improved transplantation outcomes in preclinical settings, highlighting the potential of this strategy to serve as an efficient and precise approach for women requiring urgent fertility preservation in the future.

papers.title: A physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin for personalized estimation of arterial stiffness
papers.abstract: Arterial stiffness, commonly assessed by pulse wave velocity (PWV), is an important biomarker of cardiovascular risk, yet conventional PWV measurements require dual-site recordings that limit scalability in clinical settings. Here we introduce a physics-informed peripheral hemodynamic digital twin framework for estimating central-brachial arterial stiffness from a single brachial pressure waveform. Using our laboratory-developed cuff device, high-resolution brachial pulse waveforms were collected in a cohort of 118 subjects. The digital twin then personalizes a reduced-order wave propagation model through PDE-constrained optimization, generating a compact parameter space that encodes ventricular–vascular characteristics relevant to stiffness. Incorporating digital-twin-derived parameters improved PWV estimation on a blind test cohort (r = 0.67, RMSE = 1.12 m/s) compared with a baseline model using only age and blood pressure (r = 0.22, RMSE = 1.90 m/s). These results indicate that physics-informed digital twins can enable scalable, noninvasive assessment of vascular aging from accessible peripheral waveforms.

papers.title: Cartilage-binding coacervate with therapeutic payload delivery and biomimetic lubrication alleviates osteoarthritis by reducing joint friction and inflammation
papers.abstract: Polyzwitterionic coacervates with therapeutic payload delivery, mimicking physiological lubrication and cartilage-binding functionalities, reduce joint friction and inflammation in rat and mini-pig osteoarthritis models.

papers.title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
papers.abstract: The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.

papers.title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
papers.abstract: Intrinsic electric polarization in III-nitride semiconductors is an advantage for large-scale optoelectronic devices but remains largely unexplored in sensory-memristive devices. Polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers at the interfaces of III-nitride heterostructures enables efficient and scalable in-sensor computing at room temperature.

papers.title: An open dataset of gas adsorption in deformable metal–organic frameworks for direct air capture
papers.abstract: Direct air capture needs better sorbents, but screening the vast space of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) demands accurate, scalable models. The Open DAC 2025 dataset provides nearly 60 million DFT calculations of CO 2 , H 2 O, N 2 and O 2 adsorption across approximately 15,000 MOFs, with machine-learned potentials enabling high-resolution MOF screening.

papers.title: From footsteps to wireless events: infrastructure-native battery-free interfaces for human–environment interactions
papers.abstract: Future intelligent environments require infrastructure-native interfaces that can sense human activities and directly generate wireless communication events using standard protocols. Achieving this remains challenging because human footsteps are transient, irregular, and often low-force, whereas standard wireless protocols such as Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) require substantial energy consumption. In this work, we present a self-powered floor interface that addresses this challenge through coordinated material, structural, and circuit design. The system integrates a high-performance PMN–PZT ceramic with a piezoelectric charge constant of d33 = 962 pC/N for efficient energy transduction, a carefully engineered metallic substrate for enhanced stress transfer and recoverability, a threshold-regulated energy management circuit that regulates transient outputs into a usable burst-power window, and an ultra-low-power BLE interface for protocol-compatible transmission. With a 4.7 μF storage capacitor, the circuit provides 22.84 μJ of releasable energy, exceeding the approximately 17 μJ required for BLE cold start. Despite a footprint of only 30 mm, sub-millimeter thickness, and a prototype-level unit cost below $5, the system enables direct wireless triggering from a light actuation of approximately 12 N. Across 100 footstep trials involving 10 participants, the system achieved an average of 2.39 BLE packets per actuation, with up to 4 packets generated per event, and successfully delivered at least one wireless transmission in 97% of the trials. The proposed system directly translates irregular footsteps into reliable protocol-compatible wireless events and enables infrastructure-integrated human-environment interactions, including smart-home control, indoor localization, digital-twin interaction, and transportation-safety alerting. These results establish a practical route toward compact infrastructure-native battery-free interaction systems for future intelligent environments.

papers.title: SQSTM1/p62-LC3A–mediated autophagic clearance of stress granules prevents apoptosis under hyperosmotic stress
papers.abstract: Stress granules (SGs) are transient, membraneless assemblies that form in response to cellular stress and typically disassemble when stress resolves. Their persistence has been linked to neurodegenerative disease. Here we show that LC3A has a selective role in the autophagic clearance of SGs formed during hyperosmotic stress. LC3A, but not LC3B or LC3C, associates with SGs, and depletion of LC3A impairs their removal. LC3A also promotes clearance of pathogenic inclusions containing TDP-43 or poly(GR) dipeptides from C9orf72 expansions. Proteomic analysis reveals enrichment of the autophagy receptor SQSTM1/p62 in SGs, supporting its role in SG degradation. SGs are also enriched in mitochondrial and apoptosis-related proteins, consistent with an anti-apoptotic function potentially linked to mitochondrial proximity. However, prolonged stress activates CASP3 and promotes apoptosis, which is exacerbated by defective SG clearance. These findings highlight the critical role of the SQSTM1–LC3A axis in SG turnover and cell survival under chronic stress.

papers.title: Exceptional preservation in cherts reveals complex cuticular architecture in one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoans
papers.abstract: Ecdysozoans, animals characterized by a periodically moulted cuticle, became major components of Cambrian marine ecosystems, yet the structural organization of their earliest non-mineralized cuticles remains poorly documented. Here we report Spinosoma reticulatus gen. et sp. nov., a millimeter-scale ecdysozoan from Fortunian cherts on two paleogeographic blocks: the Liuchapo Formation, South China, and the Yurtus Formation, Tarim Block, dating to ca. 538 Ma. This occurrence represents one of the earliest Cambrian ecdysozoan body-fossil records and may predate the classic Kuanchuanpu scalidophoran assemblages. The material preserves a terminal mouth with large circumoral spines and abundant cuticular fragments. Its cuticle comprises a fibrous mesh, short upright plate-like structures, and hollow ridged spines. Morphological and Raman data support an ecdysozoan affinity, whereas scalidophoran placement remains tentative. Spinosoma reveals a previously undocumented cuticular architecture, suggesting that early ecdysozoan ecological breadth and integument diversity are underestimated in the earliest phase of the Cambrian Explosion.

papers.title: Genetic interaction between Adgrg6 and Sox9 reveals a feedforward mechanism for postnatal spinal stability
papers.abstract: Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis (AIS) is the most common pediatric spinal disorder and is best understood as a complex polygenic condition. Genome-wide association studies have identified AIS risk loci, including regions near ADGRG6 and SOX9, yet the mechanisms underlying its heritability remain poorly defined. Here we use spatial transcriptomics to characterize gene expression in the spine of a conditional Adgrg6 mutant mouse model, revealing reduced expression of Sox9 and several extracellular matrix genes in the intervertebral disc. We demonstrate a strong genetic interaction between conditional loss of Adgrg6 and a hypomorphic Sox9 allele that increases the penetrance and severity of scoliosis. We further show that SOX9 occupies open chromatin within the Adgrg6 locus in SOX9+ cells isolated from the mouse disc tissue, consistent with direct transcriptional regulation, and provide evidence for SOX9-dependent and SOX9-independent regulation across a variety of spinal tissues. Together, these findings support a self-reinforcing feedforward circuit in which Adgrg6 and Sox9 are co-regulated to maintain extracellular matrix gene expression in the annulus fibrosus and paraspinal tissues. These results provide mechanistic insight into genes implicated by AIS-associated loci and establish combined Adgrg6–Sox9 insufficiency in mice as a tractable model of polygenic scoliosis susceptibility.

papers.title: AI-assisted image-based screening identifies TFEB agonists that restore adipose angiogenesis and reduce adipose fibrosis
papers.abstract: Adipose tissue expansion in obesity frequently outpaces vascularization, triggering hypoxia, fibrosis, and metabolic dysfunction. The molecular mechanisms coordinating adaptive angiogenesis during this expansion remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that myeloid deletion of Transcription Factor EB (Tfeb) in high-fat diet-fed mice exacerbates epididymal white adipose tissue (eWAT) dysfunction, manifesting as profound hypoxia, fibrosis, and systemic insulin resistance. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing and chromatin immunoprecipitation assays reveal a novel TFEB-VEGFA axis: TFEB directly activates Vegfa transcription in macrophages, and its absence impairs angiogenic compensation under hypoxic stress. To translate these findings, we established an AI-driven, high-content screening platform to quantify TFEB nuclear translocation. We identified and validated Tetrandrine and Pacritinib as potent TFEB agonists. Notably, Tetrandrine acts via an mTOR-independent mechanism. Pharmacological activation of TFEB with these compounds restored adipose angiogenesis, resolved fibrosis, and improved insulin sensitivity in obese mice. These findings establish macrophage TFEB as a critical regulator of healthy adipose remodeling and validate the TFEB-VEGFA axis as a therapeutic target for metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Lactate drives the emergence of tumor cells with centrosome amplification through CP110 lactylation
papers.abstract: Centrosome ampllification is a frequent feature of cancer cells, whose origin is still under investigation. The present study shows that high lactate levels present in cancer cells can induce centrosome amplification via the the lactylation of the centrosomal protein CP110

papers.title: Automated and noninvasive in vivo mapping of brain functions in the human cortex
papers.abstract: Mapping forms the basis for understanding the functional organization of the brain and for developing targeted interventions in neurological and psychiatric disorders. Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a non-invasive tool that allows causal mapping of cortical functions involved in motor control, speech, and connectivity. Since manual mapping procedures limit standardization, we present an automated cortical mapping method that integrates electronically controlled multi-locus TMS with a Bayesian optimization algorithm for identifying stimulation targets efficiently and objectively through a closed-loop framework. We localized individual motor representation area peaks with high accuracy (average 2.4 mm and 5° deviation from the optimum) in only approximately 4 minutes. This represents a substantial advancement over current mapping approaches, providing the means to greatly accelerate and standardize both research and clinical protocols while maintaining high reliability. We anticipate that our approach can further extend to map other cortical functions that cannot be easily analyzed online by a human operator.

papers.title: Crocin alleviates renal fibrosis through inhibiting mitochondrial dysfunction via regulating HOXD8/PGC‑1α pathways
papers.abstract: Crocin, a key bioactive compound derived from saffron (Crocus sativus L.), a traditional Chinese medicinal and edible herb, exhibits renoprotective effects against fibrosis, but the mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that homeobox D8 (HOXD8) and PGC1-α are downregulated, while reactive oxygen species levels, mitochondrial dysfunction, and fibrosis are increased in kidney fibrosis models. HOXD8 overexpression increases PGC1-α expression, reduces reactive oxygen species, restores mitochondrial function, and suppresses profibrotic genes. Crocin upregulates HOXD8 and mitigates mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis. Mechanistically, HOXD8 binds the PGC1-α promoter and enhances its transcription. DNMT1-mediated promoter hypermethylation drives HOXD8 downregulation, and crocin reduces DNMT1 enrichment and activity at this promoter. Molecular docking and cellular thermal shift assay support a potential interaction between crocin and HOXD8, and crocin reduces HOXD8 ubiquitination. These findings suggest that crocin upregulates HOXD8 by inhibiting both its promoter hypermethylation and protein ubiquitination, thereby ameliorating mitochondrial dysfunction and fibrosis in chronic kidney disease (CKD).

papers.title: Anisotropic light-electron-phonon coupling and ultrafast carrier separation in ferroelectric BaTiO 3
papers.abstract: Ferroelectric materials with built-in electric fields are useful for ultrafast electronics and conversion of light into electrical energy, yet the interaction of carrier motion with ultrafast relaxation processes remains nontrivial. Combining ultrafast electron diffraction with electron microscopy of electromagnetic fields, we capture ultrafast lattice dynamics and nanometer-scale carrier transport in ferroelectric BaTiO3. We demonstrated that BaTiO3 reacts to light with an anisotropic electron-phonon coupling that depends on the optical polarization of the excitation light. Excited electrons relax two times faster into phonons when the optical electric field aligns to the ferroelectric symmetry break. Furthermore, ultrafast electron electrometry captures the motion and separation of photo-excited electron-hole pairs in presence of the ferroelectric field. These combined results provide insight into the tangled and anisotropic interaction of photons with phonons and the ferroelectric field, producing phonons and voltages in a stepwise reaction path.

papers.title: Reconstruction of SARS-CoV-2 transmissibility within households in the UK Virus Watch Study
papers.abstract: Households provide an ideal setting to study SARS-CoV-2 transmission modes due to the close proximity and extended exposure among members. Understanding the patterns of who infects whom during infectious disease outbreaks is crucial for implementing effective control measures globally. Combining genomic data with epidemiological insights can help clarify and infer pathways of viral spread. We analyse SARS-CoV-2 whole genome sequences from 237 subjects across 162 households recruited to the Virus Watch Prospective Community Cohort Study (n = 372 total participants). We consider minority variants as an indicator of within-host genomic diversity and incorporate these into a phylogenetic model to reconstruct the relationships between genomes, leading to a more accurate reconstruction of transmission than if only the consensus variation were used. Here we show that of the 73 households with multiple infected participants, both consensus and within-host phylogenetic analyses identify eight households in which one or more secondary cases appear to arise from separate community introductions rather than within-household transmission. These households are excluded from the bottleneck and within-host transmission analyses. For the remaining 65 households, including minority variants when reconstructing phylogeny allows us to infer transmission chains that are otherwise uncertain with consensus variants only. Integrating within-host genetic diversity into a phylogenetic model alongside epidemiological data provides a robust approach to accurately identify true household transmission events, assess risk factors for infection acquisition and spread, and improve the estimation of the secondary attack rate When people in the same household get COVID-19, working out who infected whom is difficult using standard genetic testing, because the virus does not always change enough between people to leave clues. In this study, we used a more detailed type of analysis that looks at small, subtle differences in the virus within each person. By combining this with information about who lived together, we were able to identify household transmission events more accurately. We also examined how many virus particles typically pass from one person to another during transmission and found that transmission is usually established by a very small number of virus particles. This work helps improve our understanding of how respiratory viruses spread within families and could support future outbreak investigations.

papers.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
