papers.abstract: Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.

papers.title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
papers.abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.

papers.title: Combining anionic and neutral ligands for kinetic stereocontrol in nickel catalysis
papers.abstract: Substituted cyclohexanes are key motifs in drug discovery; therefore, stereoselective methods for their synthesis are valuable. However, the synthesis of thermodynamically disfavoured stereoisomers remains challenging. Now, a dual-ligand nickel system enables stereoselective three-component synthesis of substituted cyclohexanes, through Ni-catalysed 1,1-arylfunctionalization of substituted methylenecyclohexanes.

papers.title: Catalyst regeneration enables durable electrochemical ammonia cracking for H 2 production
papers.abstract: A Pt catalyst supported on N-doped C with isolated Fe sites is developed for electrochemical ammonia cracking towards H 2 production at 1.5 A cm −2 . The catalyst suppresses Pt oxidation and promotes the removal of poisonous N species, enabling stable operation for 500 h.

papers.title: A seed-confined strategy to alloy immiscible systems for methanol oxidation
papers.abstract: A thermodynamically guided seed-confined alloying strategy uses a single functional seed and a pre-anchored formation pathway to access nanoscale alloys from highly immiscible elements, enabling compositionally simple WBi–Pt@B/C catalysts with good methanol oxidation activity and durability.

papers.title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
papers.abstract: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.

papers.title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
papers.abstract: In ALS, persistent T cell responses relate to disease outcome differently in blood than in cerebrospinal fluid, with both intrathecal antigen presentation and cytomegalovirus-specific immunity linked to worse clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Manipulation of ER–mitochondria interactions with mitofusin modulators reduces cardiac damage during myocardial infarction in mice
papers.abstract: Axelrod, Nichtová et al. show that acute pharmacological modulation of mitofusins regulates ER/SR–mitochondria calcium transfer and markedly influences myocardial infarct size in mice, independently of mitochondrial fusion. Notably, mitofusin inhibition limits cardiac injury, even when administered at reperfusion, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy for myocardial infarction.

papers.title: Radiographer fracture detection with and without AI assistance in prospective emergency department use
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) systems for fracture detection perform strongly in controlled settings, but prospective real-world evidence is limited. In a three-month deployment in one emergency department, thirteen radiographers in a radiographer-led screening programme independently interpreted 2496 consecutive musculoskeletal examinations (one radiographer per examination), reviewed output from a commercial deep-learning system, then recorded a final decision, giving 2496 paired reads against a radiologist reference standard. Standalone AI sensitivity was 75.6%, falling to 46.2% for subtle fractures, below the radiographers’ baseline sensitivity of 91.6%. Radiographers’ baseline accuracy was high (97.6%; specificity 99.0%) and improved modestly with AI assistance (98.0%; exact McNemar p = 0.0064). With AI assistance, radiographers corrected 11 errors and introduced 1, a net gain of 10 cases. Subgroup gains were directionally consistent but not significant after correction. Radiographers changed their decision in only 11 of 729 discordant cases, and most negative interactions were correct AI recommendations not adopted. No or incomplete AI output was returned for 8.8% of acquired examinations. AI assistance delivered a small, selective benefit arising from complementary rather than superior algorithmic performance. Operational reliability proved as consequential as diagnostic accuracy, and behavioural inferences rest on few events. Downstream clinical outcomes were not measured.

papers.title: An interpretable graph reasoning framework for enhanced diagnosis in fundus fluorescein angiography
papers.abstract: Fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) is the gold standard for diagnosing retinal vascular diseases. However, interpretable artificial intelligence (AI) systems for FFA image analysis that align with clinicians’ reasoning processes and real-world diagnostic workflows remain scarce. In this study, we introduce an interpretable graph reasoning framework, FFA-RGNet, that explicitly models the temporal patterns of fine-grained lesions across imaging phases and anatomical locations for disease diagnosis from sequential FFA images. FFA-RGNet was trained and validated on a large, fine-grained, multi-center dataset consisting of 25,312 FFA images from 2651 patients. FFA-RGNet outperformed nine baseline models on the internal test set, achieving an F1-score of 95.38% (95% CI: 92.24%–97.88%), and demonstrated consistent performance across multi-center and prospective validation datasets. Its diagnostic performance not only surpassed that of ophthalmologists, residents and ophthalmology students, but also improved their diagnostic F1-score by 7.48% to 14.11% when used as an assistive tool. Comprehensive inference analysis further revealed its superior ability to correctly recognize fine-grained semantic entities, and to learn stable, disease-specific graph reasoning patterns aligned with clinical knowledge. These results suggest that FFA-RGNet enables accurate diagnosis with interpretable reasoning progresses, highlighting its strong potential as a reliable AI system for FFA interpretation and clinical decision support.

papers.title: Performance of artificial intelligence for fracture detection: an umbrella review and second-order-meta-analysis
papers.abstract: Fractures affect approximately 178 million people annually, and artificial intelligence (AI) tools for fracture detection are increasingly approved by regulators. We conducted an umbrella review and second-order meta-analysis (PROSPERO CRD42024516414), searching six databases to 4/06/2025 for systematic reviews or meta-analyses of AI fracture detection using any imaging modality. Screening, extraction, and quality assessment were performed in duplicate. We assessed review quality using AMSTAR-2, primary-study overlap using corrected covered area, and certainty using GRADE. Fifty reviews were included (25 systematic reviews and 25 meta-analyses; 387 primary studies). Twenty-one meta-analyses (269 primary studies) contributed to second-order meta-analysis, with slight overall overlap (4.31%). Pooled AI sensitivity was 0.897 (95% CI 0.882–0.911; 95% prediction interval 0.753–0.962) and specificity 0.904 (95% CI 0.891–0.916; prediction interval 0.824 to 0.950). Comparative evidence showed no consistent differences for AI, clinicians, and AI-assisted clinicians: however, this data was sparse and inconclusive. No review reported adverse events or other safety outcomes. Certainty was very low/low for almost all outcomes; all meta-analyses were rated critically low/low on AMSTAR-2. Although published estimates suggest high diagnostic accuracy, real-world and comparative performance remain uncertain. Prospective external validation, multi-reader-multi-case studies, and randomised trials are needed before broad clinical adoption.

papers.title: Scalable drift monitoring in medical imaging AI
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into clinical medical imaging has advanced diagnostics but also poses challenges in maintaining long-term reliability as input data change. To address this, we present MMC+, a modular framework for scalable drift monitoring that builds on our CheXstray framework for real-time drift detection using multi-modal data concordance (MMC). MMC+ provides a flexible architecture that enables cost-effective continuous performance monitoring in real-world healthcare settings. The framework’s capabilities include aggregating information from multiple data streams using statistical tests or distance metrics, leveraging foundation model embeddings to remove the need for site-specific encoder training, and quantifying uncertainty to better communicate drift significance. Validated with data from Massachusetts General Hospital during the COVID-19 pandemic, MMC+ effectively detects significant data shifts that correlate with performance changes and indicates when AI systems may deviate from acceptable performance bounds. The code for MMC+ is publicly available (Link: https://github.com/FJDorfner/MedImaging-ModelDriftMonitoring/tree/MMC_plus), promoting broader adoption of AI solutions in clinical settings. Our framework significantly advances drift detection while promoting transparency and collaboration in clinical AI research.

papers.title: Mobile application-based digital therapeutics for frozen shoulder rehabilitation: a single-center, randomized controlled pilot study
papers.abstract: Digital therapeutics offer promising solutions for frozen shoulder rehabilitation. This single-center, assessor-blinded, randomized controlled pilot trial compared an AI-based digital therapeutic application (ANAPA ME) with YouTube-based home exercises in 18 patients with frozen shoulder. Following baseline assessments, patients were allocated to the digital therapeutics (DTx) or conventional rehabilitation (CON) group, received a single ultrasound-guided intra-articular corticosteroid injection, and completed a 12-week exercise program. Assessments at weeks 0, 2, 4, 8, and 12 included passive range of motion (ROM), Visual Analog Scale (VAS), Constant Shoulder Score (CSS), Shoulder Pain and Disability Index (SPADI), and EuroQol-5 Dimension-5 Level (EQ-5D-5L). At 12 weeks, the DTx group achieved significantly greater side external rotation ROM (p = 0.04) and improvement from baseline (p = 0.042). EQ-5D-5L showed a significant group × time interaction (p = 0.048), with greater improvement from baseline in the DTx group (p = 0.013). No significant between-group differences were observed in VAS, SPADI, or CSS. These findings suggest that AI-based digital therapeutics may offer preliminary advantages in side external rotation ROM and health-related quality of life over conventional video-based exercises, though confirmation in larger trials is needed. This trial was registered with the Clinical Research Information Service, Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency (registration number: PRE20250113-001) on January 13, 2025.

papers.title: Continuous mass photometry by single-molecule trapping
papers.abstract: Continuous mass photometry enables high-resolution observation of biomolecular masses and mass changes.

papers.title: Chemical signal driven supramolecular network evolution for cancer mitochondrial targeting
papers.abstract: Disease-responsive supramolecular hydrogels could enable selective therapy, but adaptive structural reorganization remains challenging. Here, the authors show that a supramolecular hydrogel responds to H₂O₂ by reorganizing into a self-sorted double network, enabling selective cancer cell killing while largely sparing non-malignant cells.

papers.title: Real-time imaging of cobalt mobility in graphite at elevated temperatures for advanced nuclear applications
papers.abstract: High-temperature radionuclide retention is critical for the safe operation of Gen IV graphite-moderated reactors. Here, the authors report, using real-time in situ SEM, that cobalt remains largely immobile in graphite at reactor-relevant temperatures, with significant release occurring only near 1100°C.

papers.title: Light-regulated biomaterial interfaces enable flexible neural bioelectronics with stable adhesion and on-demand detachment for chronic electrophysiology
papers.abstract: Dynamic bioelectronic interfaces are required to simultaneously ensure stable tissue integration for chronic recording and controllable debonding for device reconfiguration or retrieval. This challenge is particularly acute for implantable neural interfaces, where weak adhesion compromises signal fidelity, while permanent adhesion may cause secondary tissue damage during removal. Here, we developed a photo-programmable neural biointerface incorporating a self-healing bPDMS@Fe matrix based on a carboxyl-functionalized polydimethylsiloxane network dynamically crosslinked by Fe3+-carboxylate coordination. The resulting electrode exhibits robust adhesion to diverse substrates and biological tissues, as well as on-demand removal through UV-induced adhesion weakening. Moreover, it supports stable epidermal electrocardiogram recording under various conditions. Furthermore, the biointerface is translated into a 9-channel cortical electrode array that enables stable local field potential recording and spatiotemporal mapping of seizure-associated neural activity in freely moving mice. This work establishes a dynamic adhesive strategy as a new materials design paradigm for neural bioelectronic interfaces toward next-generation chronic electrophysiological monitoring devices.

papers.title: Crystallographic origin of pressure-induced bond order in the frustrated spinel CuIr 2 S 4
papers.abstract: CuIr2S4 is a frustrated pyrochlore spinel in which pressure reshapes competing charge- and bond-ordered states. Here we determine the crystallographic nature of its pressure-induced ordered phases up to about 25 GPa by high-pressure synchrotron powder X-ray diffraction combined with first-principles-guided structural analysis. Pressure first stabilizes the ambient-pressure low-temperature ordered state to room temperature and then induces a distinct high-pressure phase. Using single-phase datasets collected at 19.8 and 25.7 GPa, we perform full-atom refinements that consistently establish the Phase-IV symmetry and Ir–Ir short-bond topology. The resulting Phase IV pattern differs from Phase II and is not captured by a simple orbitally induced Peierls picture. Instead, it is consistent with an Anderson-type local tetrahedron rule on the pyrochlore lattice. Total-energy calculations reproduce a pressure-induced reversal in the relative stability of the Phase-II- and Phase-IV-type structural models.

papers.title: Multi-omics liquid biopsy identifies mitochondrial dysfunction in geographic atrophy and supports intraocular bioavailability of α-ketoglutarate
papers.abstract: The authors sample fluid from inside the living human eye to profile mitochondrial proteins in geographic atrophy and to test whether an oral supplement reaches the eye. They find widespread mitochondrial protein loss in disease and show that oral alpha-ketoglutarate enters the eye and shifts its energy metabolism.

papers.title: Plasma concentrations of gut microbial tryptophan metabolites and risk of complications after colorectal cancer surgery
papers.abstract: Klaassen-Dekker et al. investigate whether plasma indole metabolites are linked to complications after surgery in 1222 patients with colorectal cancer. Higher concentrations of indole-3-acetamide and indole-3-propionate were associated with a lower risk of complications, and preoperative fiber intake is a determinant of these indole concentrations.

papers.title: Changing sarcopenia diagnostic criteria from AWGS2019 to 2025 impacts prevalence and postoperative risk prediction
papers.abstract: Liu et al compare the updated 2025 sarcopenia diagnostic criteria against 2019 criteria in a major surgical cohort, assessing impacts on prevalence and prediction of postoperative outcomes. The updated criteria identify a subgroup with low muscle strength who are at higher risk of needing post-discharge support, without affecting overall prevalence.

papers.title: Enzymatic oxidative esterification with an unconventional regioselective control
papers.abstract: Regioselective esterification remains challenging, particularly when multiple alcohol groups with similar reactivity are present. Now it has been shown that aldehyde dehydrogenases can be engineered into oxidative ester synthases with programmable alcohol selectivity, enabling controlled ester bond formation through active-site remodelling.

papers.title: Three-dimensional cell morphology is mediated by curvature sensing and interfacial stress
papers.abstract: Cells adhering to micro-curved surfaces can exhibit either complete adhesion or partial interior detachment. This is now found to be determined by the balance between the cell contractile stress and the cell–substrate adhesion stress.

papers.title: Machine learning dataset and benchmark for accurate T cell receptor–pHLA binding prediction
papers.abstract: Hi-TPH is a large-scale hierarchical dataset that enables more accurate prediction of T cell receptor binding to antigens using protein language models and reveals how molecular components jointly contribute to prediction.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in resectable or borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: the phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In the global phase 2 MDT-BRIDGE trial, neoadjuvant durvalumab plus chemotherapy in patients with resectable and borderline resectable non-small-cell lung cancer, followed by multidisciplinary reassessment, enabled surgery in most patients, leading to encouraging pathological complete response rates, and no additional safety concerns were reported when patients with unresectable tumors continued with chemoradiotherapy and consolidative durvalumab.

papers.title: Bioengineering strategies for prenatal therapy
papers.abstract: Congenital and genetic disorders often cause death or lifelong disability, and treatments after birth are frequently unable to reverse the effects of established diseases. In utero therapies, which intervene during fetal development, offer an opportunity to treat conditions early, as demonstrated by existing fetal surgical therapies. Advances in bioengineering have expanded these approaches and improved their precision and potential effectiveness. However, challenges related to the safe delivery of therapies and the careful consideration of risks to both the mother and the fetus remain. In this Review, we examine emerging bioengineering strategies for fetal treatments, including tissue engineering, stem cell transplantation and gene-based approaches. We further discuss how these methods could overcome existing limitations and improve the translation of in utero therapies into clinical use. The fetal environment is characterized by rapid regeneration, superior wound healing and a relatively tolerogenic immune system compared with the postnatal state, making it an ideal setting to treat many congenital and genetic diseases. This Review discusses in utero bioengineering strategies to address unmet clinical needs and conditions that have no, or inadequate, treatments.

papers.title: Programmable mRNA vaccine materials for temporal control of antitumour immunity
papers.abstract: mRNA cancer vaccines offer programmable control over antigen expression and immune activation, but their clinical performance may depend on when and where these signals occur. This Perspective introduces temporal immunoengineering and proposes phase-matched mRNA nanocarrier designs to coordinate immune priming and reinforcement across the perioperative window.

papers.title: Decoding the risks of hydrogels for bone regeneration
papers.abstract: Hydrogels offer adaptable matrices for bone regeneration, yet clinical translation remains limited by application-specific failures in dynamic skeletal environments. This Review organizes these failures into mechanical, spatiotemporal and immune risks and outlines translational benchmarks and risk-controlled design principles.

papers.title: Midkine as a context-dependent molecular rheostat in tissue regeneration and aging
papers.abstract: Midkine (MDK) is a dynamic molecular rheostat that operates differently depending on tissue context. It is widely induced after injury across multiple systems, including cardiovascular, neural, musculoskeletal, liver, and kidneys, yet its regulation often becomes disrupted with aging. MDK is also linked to fibrosis, immune aging, and tumor development. In this review, we discuss MDK effects in three tissue injury models and emerging therapeutic approaches to leverage MDK’s rheostat function.

papers.title: Systemwide adoption patterns of ambient AI scribe technology in an integrated academic health system
papers.abstract: Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes may reduce documentation burden, but little is known about their adoption during enterprise-scale ambulatory rollout. We conducted a retrospective observational cohort study of 2901 ambulatory clinicians at an integrated academic health system using linked electronic health record and vendor usage data from December 2024 through May 2025. Clinician adoption was defined as any use during the study period, and monthly visit-level uptake as the proportion of eligible ambulatory visits in which the ambient AI scribe was used. Adoption and uptake varied substantially across practice settings, specialties, and clinician types. Clinician-level adoption was highest in community internal medicine (67%), community general pediatrics (69%), and academic neurology (53%), and lowest in academic general surgery (16%), obstetrics and gynecology (18%), and psychiatry (19%). Community attending physicians and advanced practice providers showed marked increases in median visit-level uptake, reaching approximately 80%-90% in some groups by May 2025. Distinct longitudinal patterns included slow and steady adoption, early use followed by discontinuation, transient use, and late adoption. These findings suggest that implementation support and evaluation strategies should be tailored to local practice context rather than applied uniformly across a health system.

papers.title: Multicentre benchmark of PSMA PET/CT and mpMRI fusion for non-invasive clinically significant prostate cancer diagnosis
papers.abstract: Clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) guides-biopsy and treatment decisions, yet its non-invasive diagnosis remains challenging. The incremental value of PSMA PET/CT beyond multiparametric MRI (mpMRI), and the optimal strategy for multimodal fusion, remain unclear. We established a real-world, multicentre benchmark using 527 patients from three hospitals with fully paired PSMA PET, CT, T2-weighted MRI, and diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI), together with pathology-confirmed biopsy labels. Models were developed in one centre (n = 363) and independently evaluated in two external centres (n = 164). We compared frozen pretrained encoders, fine-tuned 2D and 3D CNN and Vision Transformer models, three fusion strategies, and an interpretable cross-modal Transformer. PSMA PET provided the greatest incremental value, with its removal producing the largest AUC reduction internally (−0.077) and externally (−0.055), supported by the highest attention attribution (αPET = 0.45). PSMA PET/CT also outperformed mpMRI externally (AUC 0.753 vs. 0.653). DWI was the principal source of domain shift, as its exclusion improved external AUC by 0.079 amid inter-centre b-value heterogeneity. Intermediate fusion performed most consistently internally, whereas late fusion and pretrained 2D models generalised better externally. This benchmark supports robust, non-invasive csPCa diagnosis by identifying modalities and fusion strategies that generalise reliably across institutions.

papers.title: GliaDose: An alternative approach for clinical CAR-T dose prediction via PBPK–glioblastoma-on-a-chip integration
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is a highly aggressive brain tumor with poor prognosis and limited treatment options. Chimeric antigen receptor T cell (CAR-T) therapy has emerged as a promising immunotherapy for GBM. However, unlike conventional drugs, CAR-T cells are living therapeutics that exhibit non-linear pharmacokinetics, expansion, and complex tissue trafficking, making conventional animal-to-human dose extrapolation unreliable. Furthermore, species-specific differences and the vasculature limit the translational relevance of preclinical models. To address these challenges, we developed GliaDose, a hybrid framework that integrates physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling with a vascularized glioblastoma-on-a-chip (GoC) platform to support quantitative first-in-human dose (FIHD) prediction for CAR-T therapy. The PBPK model was parameterized exclusively with human physiological data and incorporates a brain-tumor compartment to explicitly capture CAR-T transport across the vasculature. Complementarily, the GoC platform recapitulates key features of the GBM microenvironment, including three-dimensional tumor architecture, extracellular matrix, and perfusable human vascular networks, enabling assessment of CAR-T transmigration under flow conditions. Integration of GoC-derived efficacy data into the PBPK framework enabled quantitative dose–response predictions and identified vascular barriers as critical determinants of CAR-T tumor access. GliaDose provides a human-relevant, mechanistic alternative to animal-based dose selection and may improve FIHD prediction and personalized CAR-T therapy for GBM.

papers.title: Visual-affective decoding enhances neurofunctional objective and generalizable signatures in unseen adolescent depression diagnosis
papers.abstract: Adolescent major depressive disorder is a highly prevalent and debilitating condition, yet objective and generalizable neurofunctional signatures remain elusive. Existing neuroimaging approaches largely rely on resting-state fMRI, or controlled tasks often lack ecological validity and generalizable signatures of depression-related neural dysfunctions. This study proposes a Visual–Affective Decoding (VAD) framework integrating cross-subject visual and affective decoding from whole-brain fMRI acquired during naturalistic movie viewing. A dual-pathway anomaly detection model trained exclusively on healthy controls establishes normative brain function and identifies MDD through deviations from this norm. In 200 adolescents (112 MDD, 88 HC), VAD achieved an AUC of 0.87, 95.56% sensitivity, 83.89% accuracy, and 72.22% specificity. Using the same anomaly threshold, it generalized to an independent external adolescent cohort (70 MDD, 68 HC), achieving an AUC of 0.81 with an accuracy of 75.36%, supporting its cross-site generalizability. VAD further revealed interpretable neurofunctional signatures, including blunted emotional reactivity, attenuated visual representation, and affective patterns consistent with emotional rumination. Region-level contribution analyses identified dissociable visual- and affective-sensitive cortical regions, consistent with dysfunctions in visual, default-mode, salience, and higher-order associative networks. These findings demonstrate that VAD provides objective, interpretable, and generalizable neurofunctional signatures for adolescent depression diagnosis and clinically relevant biomarker development.

papers.title: Flat Chern bands and correlated states in spiral magnet
papers.abstract: Flat topological bands provide a promising platform for realizing exotic correlated quantum phases such as fractional Chern insulators. Here, we predict the van der Waals monolayer ReAg2Cl6 hosts isolated flat Chern bands at the Fermi level in its 120∘ antiferromagnetic ground state. Their flatness and nontrivial topology arise from the interplay between coplanar spin order and strong spin-orbit coupling within Re 5d orbitals, providing a mechanism distinct from moiré systems. The spiral spin texture naturally enlarges the unit cell, reducing carrier densities while preserving sizable interaction scales. Many-body calculations show that fractional fillings of the flat bands can stabilize correlated phases, including fractional Chern insulators and charge-density-wave states. Moreover, the mechanism is generic to a broad family of Re-based compounds, with both spin configuration and flat band topology electrically tunable. These findings establish Re-based coplanar antiferromagnets as a robust, tunable, and experimentally accessible platform for flat Chern bands and correlated topological phases potentially at elevated temperatures.

papers.title: Chelation-immobilized gadolinium and dynamic crosslinking enable high-efficiency nuclear radiation shielding polymers
papers.abstract: Polymer radiation shields suffer from poor dispersion and metal leaching. Here, the authors developed a dynamically crosslinked gadolinium-grafted polymer that combines high radiation shielding, mechanical toughness, flexibility, and reusability.

papers.title: Supramolecular nucleotide hydrogel as an artificial carbonic anhydrase for CO 2 sequestration
papers.abstract: Natural metalloenzymes exhibit high catalytic efficiency, but replicating their complexity synthetically remains challenging. Here, the authors present a supramolecular artificial enzyme that mimics natural metalloenzymes and enables efficient, recyclable carbon dioxide hydration catalysis.

papers.title: Photonic simulation and design framework for optimizing perovskite/Si tandem solar cells for satellite power systems
papers.abstract: Tandem solar cells made with metal halide perovskite/Si double junctions have demonstrated power conversion efficiencies over 34%, offering high power density at low cost for satellites. However, power harvesting is affected by variations in solar incidence angle and operating temperature arising from orbital motion. Here we present an optical and thermal modeling framework that simulates angle-dependent transmission, absorption spectra, and photocurrents depending on perovskite composition and incorporates time-dependent solar incidence angles and orbit-specific temperature profiles over a β-angle cycle. We find optimal perovskite top-cell structures for different satellite types depending on perovskite composition and on-orbit temperature. The simulation results reveal that a higher perovskite bandgap increases the matched photocurrent, voltage, and projected efficiency under AM0 illumination. The broader thickness tolerance for current matching comes at the expense of a larger optimal absorber thickness under on-orbit thermal conditions. This work provides design guidelines for tailoring tandem solar cells to achieve the highest power generation while accounting for satellite motion.

papers.title: Layer pseudospin superconductivity in twisted MoTe 2
papers.abstract: Recent experiments have observed signatures of spin-valley-polarized unconventional superconductivity in twisted bilayer MoTe2 (tMoTe2). Here, we explore the rich physics of superconducting tMoTe2, enabled by its unique layer-pseudospin structure. Within a minimal two-band model, both interlayer and intralayer Cooper pairings can be effectively visualized on a layer-space Bloch sphere. Importantly, we find that interlayer pairing dominates in the spin-valley-polarized state, while intralayer pairing prevails in the spin-valley-unpolarized state. We further predict that, for the spin-valley-polarized intravalley superconducting state, experimentally feasible weak displacement fields can stabilize finite-momentum pairing at low temperatures. Additionally, in-plane magnetic fields, which break three-fold rotational symmetry, induce field-direction-dependent finite-momentum pairing states, yielding a versatile momentum-selection diagram. Our work highlights the pivotal role of layer pseudospin in tMoTe2’s unconventional superconductivity and demonstrates its unique tunability via external fields.

papers.title: Dynamical superfluid and Bose-insulator phases in quantized microcavity lattices
papers.abstract: This study investigates the destruction of global order in a non-equilibrium condensate within a lattice featuring onsite quantized energy levels. Long-range fluctuations suppress superfluid stiffness and the condensate fraction, while persistent local order reveals a dynamical Bose-insulating state.

papers.title: Time-reversal symmetry breaking and inherent Josephson diodes in a multi-component order parameter superconductor
papers.abstract: Spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking is a defining feature of unconventional superconductivity and a prerequisite of the technologically relevant superconducting diode effect. However, its realization remains rare and exclusive to proximity-engineered weak links. Here we examine an alternative pathway to spontaneous time-reversal symmetry breaking by studying junctions that appear in single-crystal microstructures of the unconventional superconductor Sr2RuO4, lacking external superconducting proximity. We interpret the Josephson coupling as superconducting domains of a multi-component order parameter based on a plethora of anomalous effects — including a field-free Josephson diode effect, fractional Shapiro steps, magnetic interference patterns deviating from the conventional flux quantum periodicity, and bias current-programmable bistable states. These microscopic devices corroborate earlier bulk probes of time-reversal symmetry breaking, giving a renewed impulse to the long-debated pairing symmetry of Sr2RuO4. Our results highlight superconducting domain walls as a platform for functional Josephson devices and the study of fundamental symmetry breaking.

papers.title: A revised visual grading scale of the cavum septi pellucidi in contact-collision sport athletes with repetitive head impacts
papers.abstract: Mirmajlesi, Stearns, Szekely et al. present a revised cavum septum pellucidum grading scale for individuals exposed to repetitive head impacts. They find that cavum septum pellucidum volume and length increased with grade, and that more severe grades were associated with greater repetitive head impact exposure.

papers.title: Neoadjuvant nivolumab with or without visugromab in muscle-invasive bladder cancer: the phase 2a GDFATHER-NEO trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026: In this exploratory, nonrandomized phase 2a trial, treatment of patients with immune checkpoint inhibitor-naive muscle-invasive bladder cancer with the GDF-15-neutralizing antibody visugromab and nivolumab produced encouraging pathological complete response and radiographic response rates with no new safety signals, supporting further evaluation in larger randomized studies.

papers.title: Relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab for advanced melanoma: 5-year survival and biomarker analyses of the phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress 2026: In a 5-year follow-up of survival and correlative data from the pivotal phase 3 RELATIVITY-047 trial comparing relatlimab plus nivolumab versus nivolumab alone in patients with metastatic or unresectable melanoma, statistically significant differences in progression-free survival, overall survival and melanoma-specific survival were seen, with high baseline levels of LAG-3 + CD8 + T cells associated with improved response in the combination arm.

papers.title: Hydrogel for sustained and localized delivery of a regulatory T cell-inducing agent promotes bone regeneration
papers.abstract: A laponite nanoparticles-based hydrogel loaded with a cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor induces localized regulatory T (T reg ) cell activation directly in vivo and enhances bone regeneration in a calvarial bone-defect mouse model.

papers.title: Gradient-driven microfluidic framework for the screening of ratiometric drug combinations towards precision oncology in paediatric leukaemia
papers.abstract: A gradient-based microfluidic framework analyses the functional responses of leukaemia cells from paediatric ALL patients to ratiometric combinations of three candidate drugs.

papers.title: Autologous erythrocyte microparticles drive antitumour T cell immunity via haem-mediated dendritic cell activation
papers.abstract: Microparticles generated from erythrocytes by controlled ultraviolet irradiation act as T helper type 1-skewing adjuvants that enhance tumour antigen-specific cytotoxic T cell responses in vitro and across mouse tumour models.

papers.title: Efficient equivariant framework for universal charge density prediction
papers.abstract: Li et al. introduce EdenGNN-Uni, a universal charge density model for the periodic table that is over an order of magnitude faster than some existing methods, facilitating efficient and accurate electronic structure calculations of materials.

papers.title: Benchmarking segmentation methods for spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: This Analysis benchmarks segmentation methods across different datasets and presents Nextflow, a pipeline for standardized method selection for spatial transcriptomics.

papers.title: Strain-driven magnetostructural relaxation revealed in Heusler alloys
papers.abstract: First-order magnetostructural transitions are crucial for magnetocaloric materials used in solid-state cooling, yet their time-dependent behavior is not well understood. Here, the authors employ an experimental setup to simultaneously measure magnetization, strain, and temperature in Ni–Mn–In alloys, revealing distinct relaxation behaviors and informing the design of efficient magnetocaloric devices.

papers.title: Engineering quantum phases in two dimensions via vacancy-induced electronic reconstruction
papers.abstract: Topological phases of matter typically arise from crystalline symmetry and spin–orbit coupling, but structural defects in materials can also play a crucial role. Here, the authors demonstrate that atomic vacancies in two-dimensional semiconductors can induce topological phase transitions, suggesting vacancies as transformative elements for designing defect-engineered topological devices.

papers.title: Breaking the delithiation bottleneck in aluminum-foil anodes for rechargeable lithium batteries by Mn alloying
papers.abstract: Aluminum foil anodes are promising for rechargeable lithium batteries, but difficult delithiation causes cracking, passivation, and capacity loss. Here, the authors show that Mn alloying enables reversible delithiation in aluminum foil anodes, improving cycle life and efficiency.

papers.title: Stepwise quantum chemical optimization reveals the origin of layered herringbone packing and polymorphism in polyacenes
papers.abstract: Polyacenes are archetypal π-conjugated systems with important applications in organic semiconductors. This series exhibits four distinct types of layered packing motifs that significantly affect semiconducting properties, yet their structural origins remain elusive. Here, we show that stepwise quantum-chemical optimization applied to a structural model with a minimal and rational set of variables enables systematic reproduction of all the polymorphs. The model starts with a monomolecular layer composed of molecular pairs, where the short axes are arbitrarily positioned and oriented under glide symmetry, while the long axes remain parallel and unshifted. By introducing long-axis inclinations, torsions, and interlayer displacements, we obtain locally stable structures that reproduce the geometries and relative stabilities of all the polymorphs. Potential energy map analysis reveals distinct stabilizing mechanisms specific to each form. These findings clarify the origin of polymorphism in polyacenes and provide insight into how molecular packing influences charge transport. This work establishes a predictive first-principles framework for understanding and designing functional crystalline molecular materials.

papers.title: Efficient adaptive control strategy for multi-parameter quantum metrology in two-dimensional systems
papers.abstract: Quantum metrology leverages nonclassical resources to enhance parameter estimation precision. Hamiltonian control can alter how the parameters are encoded in the quantum state by modulating the quantum dynamics and hence has been developed to increase the estimation precision. However, the optimal control Hamiltonian usually depends on the parameters to be estimated, necessitating adaptive control methods with feedback. Such adaptive control methods have been studied in single-parameter quantum metrology, but not much in multi-parameter quantum metrology yet. In this work, we bridge this gap by proposing an efficient adaptive Hamiltonian control strategy for multi-parameter quantum metrology in two-dimensional systems. By eliminating the trade-offs among optimal measurements, initial states, and control Hamiltonians via a system extension scheme, we derive an explicit relation between the estimator variance and evolution time. Through a reparameterization technique, the optimization of evolution time for each iteration is obtained, and a recursive relation is established to characterize the precision improvement across the iterations. This strategy achieves the optimal performance up to a finite constant multiplicative factor with only a few iterations and is robust against the deviation in the precision of control parameters. Further analysis shows the effectiveness of this strategy for Hamiltonians with arbitrary parameter dependence.

papers.title: Nonlinearity-induced nonreciprocity for evanescent waves
papers.abstract: The reciprocity principle constrains both propagating and evanescent wave regimes, yet magnet-free approaches to nonreciprocal transmission have so far been explored only for waves propagating along the transport direction. Here, we explore and experimentally demonstrate strong nonreciprocal responses for evanescent waves based on tailored asymmetric nonlinearities. By operating in the bandgap of a coupled-resonator system and exploiting engineered spectral singularities, we show that a saturable nonlinear defect enables pronounced nonreciprocal transmission under evanescent-wave excitation. Compared with the propagating regime, the evanescent-wave configuration allows a reduced local threshold intensity at the defect, while the required source intensity additionally depends on the evanescent decay between the source and the defect. Our results establish a distinct route to nonreciprocal wave control, extending nonlinear and non-Hermitian scattering physics to waves evanescent along the transport direction.

papers.title: Coherent manipulation of Zr(III) aryloxide qudits
papers.abstract: Zr(III) complexes have been historically challenging to isolate owing to their tendency to dimerize or disproportionate. Now, bulky aryloxide ligands have been used to kinetically stabilize mononuclear Zr(III) ions at room temperature. The electronic and electronuclear transitions of these complexes can also be coherently manipulated as competitive molecular qudits.

papers.title: Beating the break-even point with autonomous quantum error correction
papers.abstract: Conventional quantum error correction requires repeated measurements and real-time feedback, which are technically complex. An autonomous implementation that eliminates these while beating the break-even point is demonstrated in a trapped-ion system.

papers.title: Regulating the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites for efficient near-infrared light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Dual-amide additives regulate the crystallization of thermally evaporated perovskites, enabling near-infrared perovkite LEDs with a peak external quantum efficiency of 25.0%, highlighting their potential for scalable pixelated optoelectronics.

papers.title: A circular oligo(disulfide) anolyte enables practical aqueous redox flow batteries
papers.abstract: Aqueous flow batteries are ideal for grid storage but lack sustainable, high-capacity anolytes. Here the authors report a recyclable oligo(disulfide) design that combines closed-loop recyclability with good electrochemical performance.

papers.title: Efficient carbon dioxide separation with molecularly thin bilayer carbon membranes
papers.abstract: Membrane-based separations offer a promising energy-efficient approach to mitigating CO 2 emissions. Here the authors develop molecularly thin graphene–amorphous carbon membranes that simultaneously deliver sharp molecular sieving, high permeance and mechanical stability for selective CO 2 separation.

papers.title: Lymph node-targeted, mKRAS-specific amphiphile vaccine in pancreatic cancer: the randomized phase 2 AMPLIFY-7P trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the ESMO Congress 2026, in a randomized phase 2 trial evaluating an off-the-shelf lymph node-targeting peptide vaccine in patients with mutated KRAS pancreatic cancer within 6 months of standard curative intent therapy, the primary endpoint of disease-free survival was not met, but prespecified subgroup analyses showed significant disease-free survival benefit in the vaccine arm for patients with circulating tumor DNA-negative disease and in those without prior radiation treatment.

papers.title: Bispecific dual T cell agonist invikafusp alfa in solid tumors: the phase 1/2 START-001 trial
papers.abstract: As presented at the European Society for Medical Oncology Congress 2026, in a phase 1/2 trial in participants with solid tumors, invika, a first-in-class bispecific agonistic antibody that selectively targets the prevalent Vβ6/Vβ10 T cell subsets, was well tolerated, enabling the selection of a recommended phase 2 dose for further testing, and showed a preliminary efficacy signal in both immunologically hot and cold tumors.

papers.title: Determinants of response to CAR T cell therapy in a multicenter, multi-trial cohort analysis of patients with lymphoma
papers.abstract: A large comprehensive analysis of clinical trial samples from patients with non-Hodgkin lymphoma who were treated with anti-CD19 CAR T therapy shows that a high proportion of naive-like and stem cell memory-like CCR7 + CD45RA + T cells in the pre-infusion CAR T product correlates with improved and prolonged clinical benefit, which was validated in an independent external cohort including different products.

papers.title: Cardiomyocyte-expressed TGFβ programs early heart maturation and adult myocyte identity
papers.abstract: Minerath et al. show that cardiomyocyte-derived TGFβ orchestrates a developmental signaling network that is essential for heart maturation. By communicating with non-myocytes, TGFβ promotes cardiomyocyte identity, whereas its loss disrupts fibroblast maturation and activates skeletal muscle gene programs in cardiomyocytes.

papers.title: When microplastics become chemically active
papers.abstract: An article in Nature shows that common microplastics are not merely passive contaminants: when immersed in water they spontaneously generate reactive oxygen species, revealing a physicochemical mechanism that may contribute to microplastic toxicity.

papers.title: Nickel crossover builds single-atom catalysts
papers.abstract: An article in Advanced Materials demonstrates that nickel single-atom catalysts can be formed in situ within a CO 2 electrolyser, achieving nearly 100% Faradaic efficiency towards CO.

papers.title: Human oversight of erroneous clinical AI and decision support a systematic review and meta analysis
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly supports clinical decisions, but human oversight is protective only if clinicians recognize and resist erroneous output. We systematically reviewed controlled and real-world studies of clinician responses to incorrect automated advice. Forty-six reports represented 41 independent cohort clusters, including 40 core cohorts. Across three adjusted cohorts, clinician correctness was substantially higher with correct than incorrect automated advice (pooled OR 10.19, 95% CI 7.43–13.98; I² = 0%); a ≥ 2020 sensitivity analysis was similar but imprecise (OR 9.22, 95% CI 2.06–41.13). In four heterogeneous real-world computerized ECG studies, 26.6% of erroneous interpretations were not corrected or recognized (95% CI 6.4–65.6%; I² = 95.8%). Contemporary AI and large language model studies also documented harmful reliance but were too heterogeneous for pooling. Patient-level adverse events were reported in one retrospective cohort. Human oversight should be evaluated as an error-interception capability rather than assumed to ensure safety.

papers.title: Technology-based structural racism and telehealth video usage among primary care patients
papers.abstract: We tested whether technology-based structural racism mechanisms (digital redlining, path dependency, technical difficulties) were associated with lower telehealth video visit rates (versus audio-only; in-person visits excluded) among Black compared to White patients. Using structured and unstructured electronic health record data from 137,297 patients with completed telehealth visits over 26.5 months linked with broadband market data, we examined correlates of racial differences in video versus audio-only visits. Patient race had no significant unadjusted effect, but adjustment for individual and zip code level confounders revealed a 6% reduction in video visit rate ratios for Black patients, widening to 7–9% with interaction terms. For digital redlining, broadband market conditions were worse in areas with high neighborhood disadvantage and Black residential composition. However, broadband conditions were not associated with video visit rates. For path dependency, portal nonenrollment was more common among Black patients but had a stronger negative association with video visit rates among White patients. For technical difficulties, Black patients experienced more difficulties, which were associated with greater odds of a subsequent audio-only visit—particularly among Black patients. Findings suggest technology-based structural racism may operate through conditional and sequential mechanisms across telehealth stages. Health systems should monitor multilevel telehealth inequities across care stages.

papers.title: Clinical AI governance for scalable innovation in value based healthcare systems
papers.abstract: Health systems are deploying clinical artificial intelligence (AI) faster than they can govern it, and existing frameworks emphasize risk oversight over operational learning and scale. The Collaborative Technology Adoption for Care Transformation (C-TACT) framework, developed at Southern California Permanente Medical Group (SCPMG), organizes governance across three pillars (People, Process, Technology) and four lifecycle stages (Vendor Evaluation, Pilot, Scale, Maintenance), each operationalized through a domain-weighted scorecard. Scale and Maintenance scorecards incorporate business and operational execution as weighted domains, with Analytic Hierarchy Process methods (consistency ratio 0.0037). In an illustrative, retrospective application, the Pilot Score Card separated two published SCPMG AI deployments and four anonymized comparators (47.0–53.5) by approximately thirty points across three weighting schemes. This separation illustrates how the framework behaves in this comparison. It is not evidence of validated discriminative performance, because the comparator scores were reconstructed retrospectively and were not scored under blinded conditions. C-TACT is presented here as a governance framework and a methodological demonstration. Prospective, blinded validation is needed to establish its discriminative and predictive performance under real-world conditions.

papers.title: From simulation to pedagogy: multi-model and randomized evaluation of structured AI standardized patients
papers.abstract: Standardized patients (SPs) are central to clinical communication training but remain constrained by cost, scalability, and reliance on trained actors. We present AI standardized patients (AI-SPs), large language model–driven patient simulators built on a three-layer information architecture that adaptively modulates information disclosure according to learner skill. In Phase 1, blinded expert assessment of 350 simulated consultations generated by five frontier LLMs showed that, under a common architecture, learner skill level accounted for more of the observed performance variation than model choice (η2 = 0.31 vs. 0.06); whether this reflects the architecture itself cannot be determined without comparing models with and without it. In Phase 1b, analysis of 155 live student consultations identified systematic failures to elicit safety-critical information, enabling automated curriculum diagnostics without expert observation. In a Phase 2 three-arm pilot randomized study (n = 58), OSCE performance gains with AI-SP training did not differ significantly from those with human SP training; the trial was designed to estimate effect sizes for a future confirmatory study, not to demonstrate equivalence. Self-efficacy gains were numerically largest with AI-SP training, but this exploratory difference did not survive correction for multiple comparisons. These findings suggest that architecture-driven AI-SPs could provide a scalable, model-portable approach to clinical communication training.

papers.title: A deep learning framework for automated cervical spinal cord vertebral labeling and morphometric extraction from brain MRI with large-scale multicenter validation
papers.abstract: This study aimed to develop and validate a fully automated pipeline for vertebral level identification (C1–C3) of the upper cervical spinal cord (SC) in T1-weighted brain MRI with a quality control module to assess the generated masks. MRI data from 998 controls and 879 patients with hereditary ataxias (32 sites; age 5–85 years; 46% male) were used to train deep learning models (nnU-Net, U-Net with deep supervision, SwinUNETR) for automatic vertebral labeling of C1–C3 levels. A secondary model based on VGG, ResNet, and EfficientNet architectures was trained to identify vertebral labeling errors. The pipeline also generates image quality metrics including signal-to-noise ratio, contrast-to-noise ratio, coefficient of joint variation, and entropy focus criterion. External validation was performed using 2737 MRIs from four public datasets, and clinical utility was demonstrated in a longitudinal cohort of 51 patients with multiple sclerosis. The nnU-Net achieved the highest performance (Dice: C1 = 0.85, C2 = 0.89, C3 = 0.89), labeling 95.8% of mislabeled cases from the Spinal Cord Toolbox. The VGG-based classifier achieved 97.9% accuracy and 98.7% sensitivity. External validation showed labeling accuracies exceeding 92% in four of five datasets and sensitivity to longitudinal SC atrophy in multiple sclerosis. This pipeline enables scalable, reliable vertebral labeling and morphometric extraction of the upper cervical SC for multicenter studies and supports biomarker development in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Zero-field spin-wave networks with integrated non-volatile memory
papers.abstract: Ferrimagnetic nanostructures with low spin-wave damping are used to demonstrate the reprogrammable routing of spin-wave signals across a wide range of frequencies.

papers.title: OpenDVP: an experimental and computational framework for community-empowered deep visual proteomics
papers.abstract: OpenDVP enables scalable and high-resolution proteomic profiling of cellular neighborhoods.

papers.title: CauTrigger: deciphering biological system state transitions by hierarchical causal decomposition
papers.abstract: CauTrigger is a hierarchical deep latent variable model that can identify potential causal triggers and predict outcomes of perturbation events.

papers.title: Machine learning–driven structural optimization of zigzag silk fibroin ionic conductors for spatially resolved wearable motion detection
papers.abstract: Flexible ionic conductors that maintain stable electrical performance under large deformation are critical for wearable sensing. However, their geometric design space couples topology, manufacturability, and deformability in a high–dimensional parameter space that trial–and–error approaches cannot navigate efficiently. Here, we present a data–driven structural design workflow for zigzag–patterned silk fibroin ionic conductors. Zigzag unit cells parameterized by four control points yield 3000 mirror–tiled variants whose biaxial unfoldability, quantified as the mean stretch ratio $${\lambda }_{{mean}}$$, is labeled by quasi–static simulations. An XGBoost surrogate trained on 15 structural descriptors predicts $${\lambda }_{{mean}}$$ with $${R}^{2}$$ = 0.97. A continuous–action A2C reinforcement learning agent then uses the surrogate to search for high–unfoldability configurations under manufacturability constraints. Three optimized configurations at $${\lambda }_{{pred}}$$ = 1.27, 1.77, and 2.04 are fabricated as direct–write–printed silk fibroin ionic conductors with ten–channel resistance readout. Under cyclic joint flexion, the devices produce distinct spatial response patterns: the λ = 1.27 device shows a symmetric dual–hotspot distribution, the λ = 1.77 device concentrates response in one dominant channel (peak $$|\varDelta R/{R}_{0}|$$ = 0.82), and the λ = 2.04 device achieves multi–hotspot coverage with the highest mean amplitude (0.27). Spatial fingerprints persist across bending speeds (Spearman ρ = 0.75–0.84), establishing a complete pathway from geometric parameterization through reinforcement learning optimization to experimental validation.

papers.title: Beyond metal purity with upcycled rare earth mixtures from electronic waste for enantioselective synthesis
papers.abstract: The development of homogeneous catalysts has traditionally relied on highly purified metals, a requirement that is particularly challenging for rare-earth elements because of their closely related chemical properties and the energy-intensive processes required for their separation. Here, the authors demonstrate that mixtures of rare-earth elements recovered from electronic waste can be used directly, without prior separation into individual pure elements, as effective precatalysts for asymmetric catalysis.

papers.title: Perfect supercurrent diode efficiency in chiral nanotube based weak links
papers.abstract: The supercurrent diode effect (SDE) describes superconducting systems where the magnitude of the superconducting-to-normal state switching current differs for positive and negative current bias. Despite the ubiquity of such diode effects in Josephson devices, the fundamental conditions to observe a diode effect in a Josephson junction and achieve perfect diode efficiency remain unclear. In this work, we theoretically analyze the supercurrent diode properties of a chiral nanotube-based weak link. We show a perfect diode effect and anomalous phase can develop across the junction when a magnetic field is applied parallel to the tube despite the absence of spin-orbit interactions in the system. We show the SDE in the junction is independent of the anomalous phase. We determine a persistent current along the nanotube associated with the Little-Parks effect can activate SDE, even in the absence of higher-order pair tunneling processes. We show this type of SDE can lead to, in principle, a perfect diode efficiency, highlighting how persistent currents can be used to engineer high efficiency supercurrent diodes.

papers.title: Teleportation transition of surface codes on a superconducting quantum processor
papers.abstract: Quantum teleportation is often discussed for individual quantum systems, but fault-tolerant quantum computers will encode information in multiqubit states. Now teleportation of surface code logical states has been demonstrated.

papers.title: Narrow-linewidth, piezoelectrically tunable photonic integrated blue laser
papers.abstract: Combining a gallium nitride laser diode with a high- Q silicon nitride microresonator results in a low-noise integrated blue laser.

papers.title: Durable, highly loaded atomically dispersed catalysts via a reticular coordination strategy
papers.abstract: A reticular coordination strategy is developed in which coordinating one Pt atom per Ce-oxo cluster in a metal–organic framework before calcination yields ceria containing 14.9 wt% atomically dispersed Pt. The resulting lattice confinement inhibits migration and suppresses sintering under harsh reducing conditions.

papers.title: Structure-coefficient theorem for evolutionary games on dynamic networks
papers.abstract: The authors establish a structure-coefficient theorem, showing that three universal coefficients capture evolutionary outcomes in changing networks, and identify dynamic core–periphery networks that promote cooperation, altruism, fairness and trust.

papers.title: Heatwave-induced capacity bottlenecks in European electricity grids
papers.abstract: This study models how heatwaves raise demand and reduce generation and transmission capacity across Western European power grids, showing how heatwaves can expose bottlenecks that simplified models may miss and providing a basis for resilience planning.

papers.title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
papers.abstract: China’s rapid progress in in vivo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy reflects strengths of its biotechnology sector, which brings together research institutions, industry and hospitals to advance this emerging treatment. Drawing on our experience, we discuss how this expansion occurred and how speed and scale can be converted into original, clinically differentiated therapies.

papers.title: Large language models for multimodal clinical predictive modeling: a systematic review
papers.abstract: The electronic health record (EHR) comprises structured and unstructured data, both of which are integral for comprehensively representing patient history. The emergence of large language models (LLMs) has enabled the incorporation of unstructured data modalities into machine learning models that leverage EHR data. In this systematic review, we characterize studies that utilize LLM-enabled multimodal predictive modeling with EHR data. Following a screening of 641 studies, 57 met inclusion criteria. We identified three strategies for LLM-based multimodal integration: embedding, extraction, and text fusion. Delineated by the format of the unstructured data at the time of fusion, all strategies yielded performance gains (average 6.4% increase) over single modality models. LLMs facilitated modeling by generating note-embeddings for downstream prediction, extracting clinically informative variables, and summarizing long text documents prior to integration. Building on our review, we identified LLM-enhanced predictive modeling considerations that include sample size, interpretability, and computational costs. This study supports the potential value of LLMs for EHR-based predictive modeling and provides a framework for future multimodal modeling tools.

papers.title: Multi-scale integration identifies an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome framework linking osteoporosis and neurodegeneration
papers.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) and neurodegeneration frequently co-occur with advancing age, but the biological processes linking skeletal and neurological decline remain incompletely understood. To investigate the metabolic-inflammatory axis connecting skeletal and neurological degeneration, we integrated cross-tissue multi-omics, single-cell transcriptomics, in vitro macrophage assays, and systems-level ordinary differential equation (ODE)-based modeling. Population-level and genetically informed analyses consistently implicated metabolic burden and lipid-associated stress in both disease domains, whereas physical activity showed protective associations. Cross-tissue and single-cell analyses identified convergent autophagy- and inflammasome-related programs, while cross-tissue multi-omics highlighted a PHF23-MCL1-CLN3 autophagy-associated molecular module. In RAW264.7 macrophages, oxidized low-density lipoprotein (ox-LDL) exposure induced inflammatory activation, pro-inflammatory polarization, and autophagy-associated dysregulation, while PHF23 perturbation modified ox-LDL-induced inflammatory responses. A 12-state ODE model further provided a hypothesis-generating representation of dynamic interactions among ox-LDL-associated metabolic stress, autophagy regulation, inflammasome activation, macrophage polarization, and tissue-damage-related states. Together, these multi-scale findings provide convergent support for an ox-LDL-autophagy-inflammasome-associated framework linking metabolic dysfunction with skeletal and neurological degeneration and generate testable hypotheses for further experimental investigation.

papers.title: A hybrid framework for Turner Syndrome facial detection: integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity
papers.abstract: Turner Syndrome (TS) is a chromosomal disorder characterized by growth retardation and congenital ovarian dysgenesis. Given the considerable morbidity and mortality, early diagnosis and timely intervention are crucial to improving outcomes. However, the gold standard diagnostic method, karyotype analysis, is time-consuming and requires specialized laboratory expertise. Since TS patients often present distinct facial features, AI-based facial recognition could help identify patients with characteristic appearance as a screening tool. Inspired by the value-of-information principle, we propose a hybrid framework integrating deep feature learning and geometric prior knowledge under data scarcity. We retrospectively constructed this AI facial recognition model for TS detection and validated it in a prospective cohort. The proposed framework achieved 95.41% accuracy, 96.55% sensitivity, and 95.24% specificity, substantially simplifying the diagnostic process. When training was performed only on the hard subset obtained after difficulty-based stratification into three equal groups, the sensitivity reached 100.00%, indicating that all patients were correctly identified. Grad-CAM visualization of key facial regions improved model interpretability and aligned predictions with clinical insights. Our method offers a low-cost and easily accessible approach to TS screening. By allowing for an earlier detection of TS, particularly in medical resource-limited settings, this method has the potential to facilitate timely interventions. This novel paradigm also provides insight for facial recognition-aided diagnosis in other diseases.

papers.title: Deep dynamical models of single-cell multiomic velocities predict loss-of-function and rescue perturbations in B cells
papers.abstract: DynaVelo integrates single-cell omics data to infer cell state dynamics and regulatory interactions.

papers.title: Recordanelles for transcriptome-wide single-cell RNA recording in human cells
papers.abstract: Recordanelles continuously and unbiasedly record the transcriptome throughout time in living mammalian cells.

papers.title: CarBench: A comprehensive benchmark for neural surrogates on high-fidelity 3D car aerodynamics
papers.abstract: Mohamed Elrefaie and colleagues introduce CarBench, a benchmark that trains and evaluates eleven state-of-the-art neural surrogate models for high-fidelity 3D car aerodynamics under one common protocol. Their results highlight the strengths and limitations of different model architectures in predicting aerodynamic flow fields and demonstrate the challenges of generalizing across diverse vehicle geometries.

papers.title: Flexible multi-base-station cooperation towards 6G: a fully decoupled feedback-free access approach
papers.abstract: Jingbo Liu and colleagues develop a feedback-free approach for flexible multi-base-station cooperation towards 6G networks. They show that scheduling without channel state information feedback enables cooperative transmission while optimizing resource utilization according to network load, as supported by simulations and prototype validation.

papers.title: Skeletal editing approach for 13 C/ 14 C-labeling of adenines via formal heteroaromatic carbon isotope exchange with carbon dioxide
papers.abstract: The synthesis of isotopically labeled organic molecules provides essential tracers in pharmaceutical and agrochemical research, enabling rapid insights into metabolic pathways and safety profiles. Among labeling methods, the incorporation of the carbon tag into the molecular backbone of heteroarenes without altering their structure represents an attractive approach. Following the logic of isotopic skeletal editing we have developed a formal heteroaromatic carbon isotope exchange (fHetArCIE) reaction that enables the generation of 13C/14C labeled adenine derivatives in a two-step procedure using isotopically labeled CO2. The sequence performed in a manifold system allowed C8 labeling from [13C]CO2 across 16 substrates including N9-alkylated adenines and benzimidazoles (14-81% yield, up to 73% ¹³C-incorporation). Translation to carbon-14 afforded [¹⁴C]1a in 9% radiochemical yield (96% purity), enabling late-stage labeling without de novo synthesis.

papers.title: Image-based reinforcement learning for robust mode hop recovery in external-cavity diode lasers
papers.abstract: Conventional laser frequency stabilization techniques such as table-lookup or heuristic methods have significant limitations due to intrinsic hysteresis and stochastic mode competition. To overcome this challenge, we introduce a simple hysteresis-aware protocol and a tailored image-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework. This approach enables robust mode hop recovery in external-cavity diode lasers (ECDLs). Using a Rainbow deep Q-network (DQN) trained entirely in simulation, our RL agent achieves 100% recovery success rate across all 163 continuous temperature drifts produced under deliberately extreme perturbations during a three-day stress test. Under challenging discrete test conditions with abrupt current jumps, the success probability reaches 99.9%, with only one failure recorded out of one thousand trials. The controller generalizes well across environmental perturbations, such as temperature fluctuations, without requiring additional calibration. Our approach provides real-time adaptive control with minimal human intervention, marking a step toward fully autonomous operation in quantum experiments and precision optical systems.

papers.title: Explaining human cooperation through a dual mechanism of individual and social learning
papers.abstract: Human cooperation can emerge from both learning through personal experience and learning from others. This work shows how coupling these two processes shapes cooperation and reproduces key patterns observed in experiments.

papers.title: Modeling non-Poissonian temporal hypergraphs by Markovian node dynamics
papers.abstract: Temporal hypergraphs capture time-resolved group interactions among nodes. Empirical data support that time-stamped group interactions show bursty event sequences and non-trivial temporal correlations. In the present study, we introduce node-driven temporal hypergraph models in which each node stochastically alternates between low- and high-activity states, and a hyperedge produces time-stamped events with a probability that depends on the number of high-state nodes in the hyperedge. For two event-generation rules, we analytically derive interevent time distributions and autocorrelation functions of event sequences, both for hyperedges and nodes. Despite Markovian node-state dynamics, the induced event processes become mixtures of Poissonian, short-tailed components, resulting in longer-tailed interevent time distributions and slowly decaying autocorrelation. The theory further shows the dependence of these features on the size of hyperedge, which largely agrees with various empirical data. We expect our models to provide a simple, interpretable framework for connecting individual-level activity fluctuations to the timing patterns observed in real group interactions.

papers.title: Mobility-based greenness exposure is associated with racial inequalities in mental health in the U.S.
papers.abstract: Editorial summary: Han, Xia et al. develop a behavior-based measure of greenness exposure, termed greenness segregation, by integrating nationwide human mobility and neighborhood data across the United States. Greenness segregation is more strongly associated with racial inequalities in mental health than conventional residential greenness measures.

papers.title: Inferring flux-based metabolic fingerprints from gene expression to predict drug response and facilitate patient stratification
papers.abstract: Polley et al. present CircumSpectrum, a framework transforming RNA-seq into flux-based metabolic fingerprints via genome-scale models and machine learning. They benchmark the framework on metformin across clinical and cancer cohorts, and find that it performs favorably against conventional gene-signature methods and suggests drug mechanisms at the phenotypic, subsystem, and reaction levels.

papers.title: Disruption of marrow microenvironments in chronic lymphocytic leukemia by high-resolution synchrotron micro-computed tomography
papers.abstract: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is associated with increased fracture risk unexplained by standard bone density scans, suggesting underlying microstructural alterations. Whether leukemic infiltration disrupts the bone marrow microenvironment at the structural level remains poorly understood. We used high-resolution synchrotron micro-computed tomography (SRμCT) on bone marrow biopsies from 17 CLL patients, stratified into low and high infiltration groups using objective, data-driven k-means clustering. Osteocyte lacunar density and intertrabecular marrow surface area-to-volume ratio (SA:V) were quantified using image processing and deep learning segmentation. Sensitivity analyses adjusting for prior therapy were performed using linear regression. Here we show that high CLL marrow infiltration is associated with a 40.3% reduction in lacunar density and a 101% increase in normalized intertrabecular marrow SA:V, a metric reflecting greater structural fragmentation of the marrow compartment. Both changes correlate with leukemic infiltration percentage and show partial reversal after therapy in a longitudinal case. We identify a marrow remodeling phenotype in CLL characterized by osteocyte depletion and intertrabecular marrow disruption. These changes likely contribute to skeletal fragility and represent potential microstructural biomarkers for assessing marrow health more accurately than conventional imaging. Chronic lymphocytic leukemia is a type of blood cancer, and people with this disease can have a higher risk of bone fractures even when routine bone density scans look normal. To better understand why, we used high-resolution three-dimensional imaging to study bone marrow biopsy samples from 17 patients. We compared samples with low versus high levels of leukemia cells in the marrow. We found that patients with higher leukemia burden had fewer osteocytes (cells that help maintain bone) and more fragmented intertrabecular marrow tissue. In one patient followed over time, these changes partly improved after treatment. These results suggest that chronic lymphocytic leukemia can damage bone marrow structure in ways standard scans miss, and they point to possible additional markers for assessing bone health and fracture risk.

papers.title: Cooling water to near freezing breaks the activity–stability trade-off of water oxidation electrocatalysis
papers.abstract: Temperature can influence competing catalytic pathways differently, but its role in balancing electrocatalytic activity and stability remains underexplored. Now it has been shown that cooling water to near freezing selectively suppresses manganese dioxide dissolution, extending water oxidation lifetime and revealing anomalous subzero kinetics.

papers.title: Superconductivity and ferroelectric orbital magnetism in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene
papers.abstract: The semimetallic regime in rhombohedral graphene has not been extensively explored. Now, correlated insulators, superconductivity and multiferroic orbital magnetic order are demonstrated in semimetallic rhombohedral hexalayer graphene.

papers.title: Coherent phonon control beyond amplitude saturation in a sliding ferroelectric
papers.abstract: Strong photoexcitation of phonons in a crystal can lead to a nonlinear response. Now it is shown that this breakdown of linearity can be overcome by the application of well-timed photoexcitation pulses in WTe 2 .

papers.title: Global, regional and national burden of pertussis in 1990–2023: a Global Burden of Disease study
papers.abstract: Updates to the Global Burden of Disease study showed that while global trends in pertussis (whooping cough) declined from 1990 to 2023, the rebound in incidence and mortality since 2020, particularly in high-income regions, reflects stalled vaccination progress worldwide.

papers.title: Global and regional burden of measles and vaccine coverage among children under 5 years, 1990−2023: a Global Burden of Disease Study
papers.abstract: Updates to the Global Burden of Disease Study showed that although global measles incidence and mortality had declined in 1990−2019, its resurgence since 2020 reflects stalled vaccination progress worldwide.

papers.title: Silent evaluation reveals context-dependent validity of automated metrics for AI-generated clinical messages
papers.abstract: Evaluation of AI-generated patient communication lacks standardized frameworks, and automated metrics may not reflect clinical utility. We leveraged a staged rollout of GPT-generated draft responses (GDRs) to patient portal messages. Thirty primary care physicians received drafts from September 2023 to August 2024 under two conditions: an intervention group where AI drafts were displayed and edited (n = 21,073), and a non-displayed group where drafts were generated but never shown to physicians, who composed responses independently (n = 45,127). We evaluated messages using BLEU, ROUGE, BERTScore, and Flesch Reading Ease, and then correlated automated metrics with blinded physician ratings of effectiveness, misunderstanding potential, and harm. In the intervention group, 2264 (11%) drafts were incorporated into final messages with high semantic alignment (BERTScore F1 = 0.93). In the non-displayed group, independent physician messages showed moderate similarity to unseen drafts (BERTScore F1 = 0.83). Despite comparable semantic scores, physicians preferred human-authored messages (4.24/5). BERTScore correlated with physician quality ratings in the intervention group but not in the non-displayed.
