Automated metrics demonstrated context-dependent validity; they assessed editing fidelity but failed to evaluate whether AI-generated content matches independent human performance. Rigorous evaluation of clinical generative AI requires validation of metric meaning within specific use contexts.

papers.title: A Generative AI-powered navigation system for precision CBCT-guided lung biopsies: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Lung puncture biopsy is the gold standard for the qualitative diagnosis of lung nodules. Cone Beam CT (CBCT) is commonly used for guiding punctures to locate lung nodules. However, the poor quality of CBCT images and the limited intelligence of surgical guidance systems have lowered the efficiency of puncture procedures, particularly for small and complex lesions. This study developed and validated a robust and accurate Generative AI-Powered Puncture Surgery Navigation System for lung punctures (GPS-Lung), demonstrating clinical applicability through a multicenter randomized controlled trial (Registration number: NCT06762613). The clinical results showed significant improvements in surgeon performance with the assistance of the integrated GPS-Lung system. Specifically, the system facilitated a more standardized and efficient operational process, reducing number of punctures (2.0 ± 1.2 vs. 2.5 ± 1.7, P = 0.005), shortening operative time (20.4 ± 5.6 min vs. 23.2 ± 6.3 min, P = 0.001), decreasing radiation exposure (4357.4 ± 3427.3 μGy·m2 vs. 5570.9 ± 4846.7 μGy·m2, P = 0.033), and reducing pneumothorax complications (12.7% vs. 23.9%, P = 0.033). Taken together, the proposed system demonstrates promising clinical and translational value in lung nodule puncture intervention. (Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613). Clinical Trials Registration: NCT06762613, Registration Date: March 26, 2025. (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06762613?term=NCT06762613&rank=1&tab=history).

papers.title: Multi-site real-world performance of commercial AI for pulmonary and incidental pulmonary embolism detection
papers.abstract: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular mortality, yet the real-world performance of FDA-cleared AI detection models remains incompletely characterized. We retrospectively evaluated two FDA-cleared AI algorithms from a single commercial platform (Aidoc Medical BriefCase)—one for PE triage on dedicated CT pulmonary angiography (CTPA; n = 30,678) and one for incidental PE (iPE) detection on routine contrast-enhanced CTs (n = 37,191), across a 17-facility academic health system. Reference-standard labels were extracted from radiology reports using a validated LLM pipeline (97% accuracy, κ = 0.94). The PE model achieved 86.8% sensitivity and 99.1% specificity, with sensitivity declining from 99.3% for saddle emboli to 72.9% for subsegmental PE, and from 89.7% for acute to 65.3% for non-acute PE. The iPE model achieved 73.5% sensitivity and 99.8% specificity. Both models demonstrated lower sensitivity than FDA-clearance benchmarks while exceeding cleared specificity, with diminishing performance for peripheral and non-acute emboli mirroring known human reader limitations and underscoring the need for standardized post-market surveillance of AI-enabled medical devices.

papers.title: Towards reliable morphological subtyping and cancer detection on Barrett’s esophagus pathology through ensembling foundation models
papers.abstract: The reliability of emergent histopathology foundation models (Histo-FMs) for real-world diagnostic tasks remains unproven. Given the complexity of diagnostic tasks and the challenges inherent in real-world data, we utilized Histo-FMs to investigate their utility for morphological subtyping of Barrett’s esophagus (BE) and detecting esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) across the BE progression spectrum. We benchmarked Histo-FMs on the BarrettNet cohort, spanning diagnostic categories ranging from normal to EAC (N2EAC). The dataset comprised 3528 hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained whole-slide images (WSIs) from 790 patients. A multi-magnification, multi-backbone aggregation of the five most expert-consistent single-scale models yielded incremental performance gains (AUROC of 0.907, F1-score of 0.696, accuracy of 0.795, and κ of 0.651 for morphological subtyping; AUROC of 0.909, F1-score of 0.836, accuracy of 0.959, and κ of 0.673 for EAC detection), with non-uniform gains across single-model comparisons and limited benefit for dysplasia. The findings support the capability of Histo-FMs for BE morphological subtyping and EAC detection in a multicenter clinical cohort, while highlighting persistent challenges in dysplasia assessment and the need for external validation. This study provides a foundation for future clinical validation.

papers.title: Supramolecular chemical ligation of helical polymers
papers.abstract: Chemical ligation of synthetic polymers is achieved via supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation in a process that does not require thermal activation.

papers.title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In 2 Se 3 for ferroelectric homojunctions
papers.abstract: Stacking-controllable 2D In 2 Se 3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. A 2H/3R homojunction memristor achieves an on/off ratio one order of magnitude higher than that of pure-phase devices, offering opportunities for advanced ferroelectric memory applications.

papers.title: Lagrangian–Eulerian learning of flow field and trajectories with TrajectoryFlowNet
papers.abstract: Wan et al. introduce a physics-informed learning model that simultaneously predicts long-range particle paths and flow fields based on very limited trajectory measurements, validated in both simulations and blood-flow experiments.

papers.title: Genetic code expansion enables plant-directed control of bacterial activity
papers.abstract: The noncanonical amino acid O -methyl-L-tyrosine is used as a tool to control microbial protein synthesis across diverse plants.

papers.title: Engineered human Argonaute 2 for targeted C-to-U RNA base editing
papers.abstract: Human Argonaute is repurposed for RNA editing.

papers.title: Flexible active-matrix dual-band electrochromic display based on a Gires-Tournois resonator for human and robotic vision
papers.abstract: Reflective displays have attracted considerable attention owing to their ultralow-power operation and compatibility with flexible and wearable platforms1. Although dynamic optical modulation has been demonstrated in reflective displays, including electrophoretic displays (EPDs), their operation remains confined to the visible spectral range. These spectral limitations restrict their applicability in environments that require reliable and simultaneous delivery of optical information to both human and robotic vision systems under varying illumination conditions2,3. Here, we introduce an electrically tunable dual-band Gires-Tournois (DB-GT) resonator integrated with a conducting polymer, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS), realizing a dual-band active-matrix display platform that achieves simultaneous visible and near-infrared (NIR) modulation within a single active layer. By modulating the complex refractive index of PEDOT:PSS through electrochemical doping within a low-voltage range (−2.0 V to +1.0 V), the system achieves high reflectance contrast across dual bands, yielding a hue variation of ΔHue = 167.2° in the visible range and ΔR = 38% at 1270 nm in the NIR range, with rise time of 88 ms and a fall time of 165 ms. Furthermore, a 4 × 4 active-matrix pixel array fabricated on a flexible thin-film transistor (TFT) backplane demonstrates independent pixel-level control, supported by a high on–off ratio ( ≈ 106), low off current, and high spatial uniformity, collectively suppressing pixel crosstalk. The DB-GT resonator array is validated through visible–NIR dual-band recognition under bright conditions and robust NIR pattern recognition under haze and low-light conditions, demonstrating its potential for visual information delivery to both human and robotic vision systems.

papers.title: Quantitative relationship between coupled structural dynamics and collective order in the original Vicsek model
papers.abstract: We investigate the relationship between structural organization and collective order in the original Vicsek model. We uncover a universal structure–order relationship and develop a phenomenological framework linking microscopic structural statistics to macroscopic order, with velocity incorporated through an effective interaction number.

papers.title: Multi-scale higher-order contagion dynamics in complex networks
papers.abstract: Real-world social contagions exhibit significant multi-scale features, where behavioral adoption is driven by both microscopic synergistic pressure within tight-knit groups and mesoscopic prevalence across diverse social circles, yet existing studies treat these mechanisms in isolation. Here, we propose a unified multi-scale higher-order contagion model integrating micro-local clustering and meso-structural diversity, and develops a dynamic message passing method to accurately analyze system dynamics. We rigorously derive tricritical points defining the topological boundary between second-order and first-order phase transitions, beyond which significant bistability and hysteresis emerge. While the higher-order effects have a limited impact on the forward threshold, they significantly lower the backward threshold, thereby expanding the active region of propagation. Crucially, structural diversity dually regulates contagion through a competition mechanism between single-component size fragmentation and component quantity gain. This leads to a significant non-monotonic U-shaped variation of the steady-state density with the structural diversity, proving the existence of an optimal structural diversity capable of minimizing the infection scale.

papers.title: Fibres and glasses are competing material states in protein condensation
papers.abstract: Fibres are thought to emerge from a dense protein condensate ageing into a glassy state. It is now shown that protein fibres and glassy condensates may result from two competing ageing pathways.

papers.title: Light-induced asymmetric pseudogap below the critical temperature in cuprates
papers.abstract: How superconductivity relates to the pseudogap in cuprates remains unclear. Now, time-resolved photoemission measurements show a light-induced pseudogap-like state below critical temperature, revealing a dynamic interplay with superconductivity.

papers.title: Experimental demonstration of attosecond hard X-ray pulses
papers.abstract: Researchers experimentally demonstrate attosecond pulse generation in the hard X-ray regime with a free-electron laser. The confirmation is enabled via the measurement of amplified spontaneous emission from 3 d transition metals. Pulse durations are in the range of 100 as to 400 as.

papers.title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
papers.abstract: Cathode interlayers play a pivotal role in improving the performance of organic solar cells. Yao, Zhang, Zhang, Wang et al. show a stepwise solvent treatment to achieve a vertically aligned cathode interlayer, enabling a certified efficiency of 20.65% in binary organic solar cells.

papers.title: GUARD-LGG: a glioma upfront AI-driven radiotherapy response decipher for lower-grade glioma
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone in managing lower-grade glioma (LGG), but its response varies widely. Reliable pre-treatment prediction of RT response could facilitate patient management but remains unavailable. Here we present GUARD-LGG, a machine learning model designed to predict early RT response in LGG before treatment. GUARD-LGG was trained on 963 patients from a major center, tested on 187 patients from seven independent institutions, and 328 patients prospectively enrolled in a registered clinical trial. GUARD-LGG achieved AUCs of 0.946 (95% CI: 0.938–0.962), 0.929 (95% CI: 0.894–0.965), 0.882 (95% CI: 0.830–0.934), and 0.913 (95% CI: 0.878–0.949) in the training, internal validation, external, and prospective test sets, respectively. Model interpretation highlighted residual tumor, age, T2-weighted texture roughness and T1-weighted contrast intensity changes as major predictors. Radiogenomic analyses suggested potential associations between predicted unfavorable RT response and enrichment of RT resistance-related pathways. Consistently, patients with predicted unfavorable RT response exhibited shorter overall survival. In conclusion, GUARD-LGG enables individualized prediction of early RT response before therapy, offering a tool for pre-treatment response stratification in LGG.

papers.title: Expertise modulates automation bias and sentinel behavior in human–AI collaborative diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum
papers.abstract: Medical AI is often validated under an additive assumption that algorithmic sensitivity and clinician oversight will combine to improve care. We tested this assumption in the high-stakes diagnosis of neonatal pneumoperitoneum, a time-critical surgical emergency. In a multi-reader crossover study analyzing 1750 interpretation events, clinicians reviewed radiographs aided by either a high-reliability model or a systematically error-injected model. We found that high AI reliability paradoxically induces automation bias in trainees, who accepted 52.0% of incorrect suggestions, while offering limited gains to experts. Conversely, when challenged by flawed AI, the three participating neonatologists exhibited a “sentinel behavior” phenotype, correctly overriding 91.7% of errors (Wilson 95% CI: 83.0–96.0%) consistent with increased deliberation; given the small specialist cohort, this finding is hypothesis-generating and warrants prospective replication. We operationalize systemic resilience as the capacity to maintain diagnostic integrity under algorithmic failure and demonstrate that clinical validity depends on the human–AI team’s adversarial resilience rather than standalone accuracy. To mitigate the risk of deskilling and never-skilling, we release an open-source educational sandbox designed to inoculate clinicians against automated errors.

papers.title: MEDA-PKD: a dynamic, real-time analytics platform for precision care in autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease
papers.abstract: The use of medical real-world data is constrained by fragmented data infrastructures and the absence of tools integrating longitudinal clinical with molecular data at scale. Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), the most common monogenic cause of kidney failure, exemplifies this gap given its phenotypic complexity and the need for individualized treatment decisions. We present MEDA-PKD (MEdical DAta translation service of Polycystic Kidney Disease), an interactive, near-real-time analytics platform that integrates clinical routine with research data from the German AD(H)PKD Tolvaptan Registry (NCT02497521, DRKS00008910) into a harmonized database ( https://doi.org/10.18716/adpkd_registry ). MEDA-PKD provides automated near-real-time analysis and dynamic visualization, replacing traditional static approaches to clinical cohorts. As of March 2026, MEDA-PKD visualized data from 1735 patients (mean follow-up 796 days). eGFR slope analysis of data from patients initiating tolvaptan therapy (332 patients) demonstrates the platform’s capacity to evaluate real-world therapeutic impact in real-time. Other tabs include family history, medication, lifestyle, quality of life and a wide array of lab values (20,894 entries). Besides, MEDA-PKD integrates proteomics data and allows for secure individual patient-level data access. MEDA-PKD represents a paradigm shift by transforming static cohort data into a living, actionable knowledge resource in ADPKD and will serve as a template for other diseases.

papers.title: Bioresorbable metal-free molecular magnets enable untethered organ monitoring
papers.abstract: A bioresorbable, metal-free molecular magnet for wireless deep-tissue sensing is reported that enables continuous cardiac monitoring and injectable organ tracking in vivo before the material safely degrades.

papers.title: Analogue fast Fourier transforms for scalable and efficient signal processing
papers.abstract: The fast Fourier transform can be implemented on analogue in-memory computing accelerators, allowing analogue systems to scale efficiently and accurately to practically useful discrete Fourier transform sizes.

papers.title: Reusability report: multi-sample omics network inference operates in distinct robustness regimes defined by prior knowledge and data availability
papers.abstract: This work studies the reusability of CORNETO, a previously developed framework for learning biological networks from multi-omics data. Robust network inference is found to depend on data availability, prior knowledge, regularization and biological context.

papers.title: Multi-immersion oblique plane microscope (miOPM): a reconfigurable platform for high-resolution light-sheet fluorescence microscopy
papers.abstract: The multi-immersion oblique plane microscope is a flexible and versatile light-sheet microscope that allows imaging of samples ranging from cells in culture to whole organisms or cleared tissue samples.

papers.title: Elevating CO 2 electrolyzer temperature accelerates the viability of chemical electrification
papers.abstract: Unlocking the full potential of CO 2 electroreduction requires looking beyond ambient-temperature operation. By integrating elevated-temperature electrolysis to capture waste heat, this study highlights opportunities for substantial process-wide savings in energy, climate change impacts and cost. Ultimately, this study demonstrates how system-level integration guides the design of scalable, sustainable chemical production.

papers.title: Trustworthy machine learning of diffractograms to prevent silent failure of apparently accurate models
papers.abstract: Machine-learning models can accurately predict outcomes from diffractograms, but differences between images and diffractograms may introduce vulnerabilities. Here, the authors compare neural networks trained on natural images and simulated diffractograms, revealing that physics-driven pre-training enhances model robustness by focusing on relevant features, underscoring the need for domain-specific training in scientific applications.

papers.title: Overcoming MRI data acceleration barriers in functional human brain mapping with physics-driven deep learning
papers.abstract: Ömer Burak Demirel, Luca Vizioli and colleagues developed a self-supervised deep learning method that improves highly accelerated functional MRI reconstruction without requiring fully sampled training data. The approach enables whole-brain fMRI at 20-fold acceleration with reduced noise and aliasing, while preserving image quality and functional activation mapping compared with conventional reconstruction methods.

papers.title: Intelligent generative design framework for semantic driven mechanical design
papers.abstract: Mechanical product design integrates functional reasoning, geometric modelling, assembly planning, and engineering validation, yet remains highly dependent on human expertise. Existing large language models lack the spatial reasoning and physical constraint awareness required for engineering-grade design, whereas task-specific neural networks perform well in localised geometric recognition but are restricted to narrowly defined and repetitive tasks. Here we show an Intelligent Generative Design framework that enables autonomous mechanical design from natural-language requirements through biologically inspired coordination of task-specific agents. Integrating multimodal engineering knowledge, the framework decomposes design tasks, performs engineering analysis, generates dimensionally accurate three-dimensional models, infers assembly constraints, and validates kinematic behaviour. Across diverse mechanical systems, the framework produces mechanically consistent designs and completes multi-component tasks beyond standalone large language models. Intelligent Generative Design establishes a framework for practical AI-assisted mechanical product development, with implications spanning intelligent manufacturing, rapid prototyping, and design space exploration within diverse industrial domains.

papers.title: Towards advanced motion control systems for micro-scale magnetic drillers inside viscoelastic media
papers.abstract: Microrobotic systems have the potential to reach regions of the body with significantly less invasiveness than conventional surgical tools. However, control over clinically relevant workspaces remains challenging due to limitations in magnetic field and robotic trajectory control. Here, we present a planar eight-solenoid magnetic field generator (MFG) that enables programmable velocity and heading of a 250 × 250 × 1250 µm3 microscale driller through continuous field reorientation within a workspace of 20 × 20 × 20 cm3. The microscale driller achieved velocities up to 155 µm/s in 0.6 weight percent agarose gel, which mimics the mechanical properties of brain tissue, and executed turns beyond 90° with angular errors below 3°. These results demonstrate a scalable platform for precise and remote control of magnetically embedded microdevices, and support future development of minimally invasive systems for applications such as targeted therapeutic delivery and microsurgery.

papers.title: Microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric platform for selective single-cell isolation and in situ transfection
papers.abstract: Single-cell transfection technologies hold tremendous promise for precision cell and immunotherapies. However, monolithic integration of cell isolation with targeted intracellular delivery remains technically challenging, especially within complex biological matrices. Herein, we present a microcapillary-assisted acoustoelectric single-cell selective isolation and sonoporative transfection platform (μC-ASSIST), which seamlessly sequences microcapillary-assisted dielectrophoresis (μC-DEP) for deterministic single-cell trapping with high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) for transient membrane poration within a unified workflow. We demonstrate the label-free, high-efficiency extraction of human non-small cell lung cancer (A549) cells from a complex white blood cell (WBC) background with a capture efficiency of 95%. Furthermore, we validate the highly efficient, contact-free intracellular delivery of diverse cargoes ranging from small dyes (PI) to functional small interfering RNA (siRNA) and large plasmid DNA (mRFP-C3), maintaining a high cell viability of 83.7% alongside a 78.1% transfection efficiency. Crucially, the targeted delivery of siBcl-xL significantly suppressed target mRNA expression and profoundly inhibited tumor cell motility. By circumventing off-target effects and cumbersome manual handling, the μC-ASSIST platform establishes a highly versatile, streamlined paradigm for precision single-cell engineering, holding immense potential for advancing functional genomics and next-generation gene therapies.

papers.title: Focusing and weighing microanalytes in liquid enabled by higher-order piezoelectric resonant membranes
papers.abstract: Micro-electromechanical-system (MEMS) resonators have been recognized as powerful tools for precision mass detection. However, achieving both flexible on-chip capture of microanalytes and high-sensitivity liquid-phase sensing remains a technical challenge. We present a fully anchored multi-modal piezoelectric resonant membrane (PRM) that utilizes self-excited bulk acoustic waves to rapidly enrich sparsely dispersed microparticles within milliliter droplets and precisely locate them at the region of highest vibrational amplitude — the most sensitive area for resonance detection. The design of higher-order resonance modes preserves acoustofluidic enrichment performance while enabling reconfigurable particle distribution patterns through modulation of the acoustic field distribution. Experimental results demonstrate that the resonant frequency shift induced by the same mass load increases with the mode order, indicating that the sensing sensitivity is proportional to the resonance order. We systematically characterized the acoustofluidic parameters and electrical measurement performance of transverse modes from (0, 0) to (4, 0). This work shows that extending the integrated actuation-and-sense approach to consider multiple modes of resonances presents a toolbox for designing such miniaturized platforms to address nanogram-level mass analysis in liquid phase.

papers.title: A fabrication-aware vectorized generative representation for topology optimization of path-defined MEMS microstructures
papers.abstract: This work proposes a vectorized generative representation for fabrication-aware heuristic topology optimization of path-defined MEMS microstructures, addressing the trade-off between topological freedom and fabrication feasibility in MEMS inverse design. Pixel-level topology descriptions provide high design freedom and often require additional constraints to suppress disconnected or fabrication-incompatible layouts. Meanwhile, heuristic algorithms are attractive for non-gradient MEMS optimization, yet their efficiency depends critically on the compactness and validity of the design representation. The proposed representation addresses this limitation by mapping low-dimensional continuous design variables into connected, fabrication-compatible physical layouts, with topology evolution, boundary compatibility, linewidth modulation, spacing constraints, and geometric smoothing embedded directly into the generation process. This formulation provides a compact continuous search space in which path topology, spatial deployment, and local linewidth can be jointly explored while the prescribed fabrication constraints are maintained during decoding. Each generated layout is exported as a vector geometry for finite-element electrothermal labeling and rasterized as a morphology image for surrogate-model training, enabling rapid performance prediction during optimization. In a resistive thermal MEMS microheater used as the primary experimental validation case, infrared thermography showed that the measured temperature coefficient of variation decreased from 4.04% to 1.22%, while the ±2 °C effective isothermal area ratio increased from 34.7% to 95.6%. Finite-element results from a compliant micro-spring case demonstrated transferability: in-plane displacement increased by 30.6%, while peak von Mises stress decreased by 16.3% under matched footprint and loading. These results demonstrate the applicability of the proposed representation as a fabrication-compatible optimization interface for path-defined MEMS microstructures under distinct physical objectives.

papers.title: Pervasive electronic nematicity across the doping-tuned phase diagram of Kagome superconductors
papers.abstract: Kagome superconductors AV3Sb5 (A = Cs, K, Rb) host intertwined orders arising from electronic correlations and lattice geometry, but the nature of the high-temperature electronic state from which these phases emerge remains poorly understood. Although numerous experiments have reported rotational symmetry breaking, it is still intensely debated whether this may be a simple consequence of the symmetry of the underlying 2  × 2 charge density wave (CDW) or an entirely different mechanism. Here we use spectroscopic imaging scanning tunneling microscopy to track the evolution of electronic structure in CsV3Sb5 as the CDW is intentionally suppressed through two distinct chemical substitution routes—Sn on the Sb site and Ti on the V site. Across a wide doping range, we uncover persistent electronic rotational-symmetry breaking—referred to here as electronic nematicity—forming nanoscale domains with orientations along three crystalline directions. These results demonstrate that electronic nematicity is a persistent feature of the Kagome phase diagram, distinct from the 2  × 2 CDW.

papers.title: Epilepsy domain adapted large language models enhance epileptogenic zone prediction from seizure semiology
papers.abstract: ED SUM: Yang et al. develop and externally validate EpiSemoLLM, a domain-adapted language model that localizes epileptogenic zones from seizure semiology. The model outperforms evaluated language models and performs comparably to or better than epileptologists across internal and external cohorts.

papers.title: Multi-ancestry genome- and transcriptome-wide association studies expand the susceptibility landscape for breast cancer overall and across subtypes
papers.abstract: Breast cancer genomic studies have been conducted primarily in European-ancestry populations, limiting diversity and statistical power. To address this, this study increases representation of African- and Asian-ancestry women and expands the European-ancestry sample size to better define inherited susceptibility to breast cancer overall and by subtypes. Genetic association summary data were harmonized for 237,817 breast cancer cases and 1,679,059 controls of African, Asian and European ancestry. Fixed-effect meta-analyses were conducted within and across ancestries for overall breast cancer and subtypes. Transcriptome-wide analyses were carried out in European-ancestry populations to identify candidate susceptibility genes. Candidate genes were assessed for pathway enrichment. We identified 415 risk loci and 196 genes associated with breast cancer risk overall or by subtypes. Of these, 207 loci and 81 genes have not been reported previously. Subtype analyses identify 198 loci and 135 genes for estrogen receptor-positive breast cancer, 69 loci and 35 genes for estrogen receptor-negative breast cancer, and 22 loci and eight genes exclusively associated with triple-negative breast cancer, including 11 loci and four genes not reported previously. Associations for 230 loci and 132 genes differ by estrogen receptor status. Risk genes are enriched in pathways related to transcriptional regulation, estrogen response, mitotic spindle processes and repair of genetic damage. These findings expand the landscape of breast cancer susceptibility and subtype-specific genetic architecture, provide insights into breast cancer biology and genetics. Breast cancer is a the most common malignancy diagnosed among women, and genetic factors can affect a woman’s risk. We conducted a large genetic studies including 237,817 women with breast cancer and 1,679,059 women without breast cancer across African, Asian and European ancestry groups. We found 415 genetic regions and 196 genes linked to breast cancer risk, many of which were not reported before. These results provide insights into breast cancer biology and genetics and enhance risk prediction to identify high-risk women for breast cancer prevention.

papers.title: Perivascular spaces are associated with T cell trafficking and may have prognostic relevance in brain metastases
papers.abstract: Perivascular structures, in particular, perivascular spaces (PVS) are emerging key immune modulators in the tumor microenvironment. However, their relationship with immune infiltration, vascular remodeling, and clinical outcomes in brain metastases is unclear. In this retrospective two-center study, we analyzed 56 brain metastases. Perivascular spaces were graded on preoperatively T2-weighted MRI in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale. Tumor immune infiltration, vascular features, and immune cell phenotypes were assessed by immunohistochemistry and spectral flow cytometry and correlated with clinical outcome. Here we show that high PVS burden in the centrum semiovale region, but not in the basal ganglia, were significantly associated with improved overall survival. High PVS are linked to increased presence of tumor-infiltrating cytotoxic T cells—most of which exhibited an activated/exhausted phenotype, indicated by PD-1- and Fas-positivity—was likewise prognostically favorable. Moreover, these cells showed elevated expression of the migration marker CXCR3, as well as Granzyme B/IFNγ consistent with effector polarization. High PVS were additionally associated with a higher M1/M2-like macrophage ratio, which showed similar prognostic relevance as high vascular density, suggesting enhanced blood supply and immune cell recruitment. These findings could establish PVS as a non-invasive imaging marker of anti-tumor immunity and prognosis in patients with brain metastasis, underscoring their potential as biomarkers for immune activity and therapeutic monitoring. Brain metastases are cancer deposits in the brain and are often difficult to treat. In this study, we asked whether small fluid-filled spaces around brain blood vessels, called perivascular spaces, are linked to immune activity in these tumors and to patient survival. We studied brain scans and tumor samples from 56 patients treated at two hospitals. We found that patients with more visible perivascular spaces in one brain region often had more tumor-infiltrating immune cells and lived longer. These immune cells showed signs of an active anti-tumor response. Our findings suggest that perivascular spaces seen on routine brain scans may help identify patients whose tumors show stronger immune activity. Larger studies are needed to confirm this.

papers.title: A liquid-crystal analogue of the skyrmion Hall effect
papers.abstract: Magnetic skyrmions are known to exhibit a Hall effect in the presence of an electric current. Now it is shown that liquid-crystal solitons also exhibit a Hall-like drift under shear flow.

papers.title: Evidence for spin-fluctuation-mediated superconductivity in electron-doped cuprates
papers.abstract: The mechanism for superconductivity in cuprates is still not known. Now, the observation of a relationship between the critical temperature and strength of coupling between electrons and spin fluctuations suggests the latter as a prime candidate.

papers.title: Intrinsic backward emission of coherent Raman photons from homogeneous media
papers.abstract: Backscattered coherent Raman microscopy brings new opportunities.

papers.title: Controllable transient coherent state reproduction in lasers
papers.abstract: By periodically resetting the pump power, a Fourier-domain mode-locked laser achieves a 2.5-kHz linewidth, exploiting the high coherence of a transient initial stabilization state.

papers.title: Stepwise and chemoselective installation of carbon substituents at silicon atoms via monobromination of hydrosilanes
papers.abstract: Heteroleptic organosilanes with four different substituents are prepared by a selective and simple method based on the controlled monobromination of multihydrosilanes. This approach avoids the limitations of conventional methods, tolerates diverse functional groups and enables iterative access to highly substituted silanes in excellent yields.

papers.title: Comparative analysis of selective ion removal in electrochemical technologies reveals the need for a new data representation framework
papers.abstract: An integrative framework is introduced to standardize and visualize selective separations across technologies, including the comparative performance analysis between electrodialysis and membrane capacitive deionization.

papers.title: Molecular predictors of minimal residual disease in newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with quadruplet therapy
papers.abstract: In a multiomic analysis of samples from patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma treated with isatuximab, carfilzomib, lenalidomide and dexamethasone induction therapy followed by consolidation treatment guided by minimal residual disease (MRD) status, baseline genomic, transcriptomic and epigenetic features are associated with MRD status after induction.

papers.title: Cost-driven strategies towards industrially manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics
papers.abstract: As perovskite solar cells advance towards commercialization, the need for competitive manufacturing costs is becoming increasingly important. This Review discusses cost-driven pathways towards industrially manufacturable perovskite photovoltaics, including improving manufacturing yield, reducing material costs and simplifying fabrication, as well as the remaining challenges for their industrial implementation.

papers.title: Water serves as a charge-transfer medium for ultrafast aqueous batteries
papers.abstract: Ultrafast charge storage in aqueous batteries is difficult to reconcile with conventional ion-transport models alone. This Perspective proposes interfacial water as a charge-transfer medium and examines its molecular mechanism, boundary conditions, regulation, characterization and implications for high-power aqueous energy storage.

papers.title: Extending synthetic medical education: generating OSCE cases with LLMs
papers.abstract: Objective Structured Clinical Examinations (OSCEs) are central to competency-based medical education, yet high-quality case development is resource-intensive. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable solution, but comprehensive OSCE case generation, including components such as candidate instructions, standardized patient scripts, and examiner marking schemes, is underexplored. We developed an LLM-based tool to generate complete OSCE stations. Three board-certified internists evaluated 24 generated cases across eight internal medicine diagnoses and three learner levels using a 12-item Likert instrument. Ratings were high across all domains; communication behaviors (4.64/5), EPA alignment (4.62/5), and overall value (4.61/5) performed best; guideline concordance scored lowest (4.24/5) with the greatest rater disagreement. As a feasibility study, these findings establish that whole, schema-validated OSCE stations can be generated from a single structured call at a quality experts rate as acceptable, while also identifying guideline concordance and difficult calibration as the domains most requiring faculty oversight -- providing reproducible infrastructure for, but not yet evidence of, effective EPA-aligned OSCE development.

papers.title: Reinforcement learning for repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation protocol selection in treatment-resistant depression
papers.abstract: Repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS), including intermittent theta-burst stimulation (iTBS), is an established treatment for treatment-resistant depression, but clinicians lack evidence-based guidance for session-level choices among stimulation type, intensity, and laterality. In this study, we investigated whether a reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm trained on routine clinical data could recommend session-level rTMS protocols associated with greater symptom improvement using electronic health record data from 1609 adults treated with rTMS between January 2023 and June 2025 across 19 clinic groups. Among 370 patients from held-out clinics, treatment decisions matching algorithm recommendations were associated with 0.788 points greater next-session Patient Health Questionnaire-9 improvement than treatments that differed (95% CI: 0.634–0.940). Following every recommendation was projected to produce 3.22 points of additional improvement (95% CI: 2.72–3.75). These findings suggest RL can find treatment patterns associated with greater next-session improvement and potentially meaningful improvement accumulated across a treatment episode.

papers.title: A generalizable deep learning model for predicting opioid use disorder using language modeling for cross-EHR data harmonization
papers.abstract: The opioid use disorder (OUD) epidemic in the United States has been a major public health crisis. We developed OUD-REY (OUD Risk Evaluator at 1 Year) - a deep learning model that uses longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data from the All of Us research program to predict risk of OUD at one year for patients with an opioid prescription. On internal validation, OUD-REY achieved an AUROC of 91.2% and AUPRC of 77.0%. We leveraged a pretrained language model to accommodate thousands of unseen, out-of-vocabulary clinical features in a patient’s longitudinal EHR history. We externally validated our model on a new dataset released by All of Us that was temporally separated from our development set and on a dataset containing ~6 million patients from medical centers of the Veterans Affairs (VA) nationwide over a span of 20 years. On external validation, our model had an AUROC and AUPRC of 86.4% and 23.1% (OUD prevalence of 2.9%), respectively, on our temporally separated All of Us validation set. It had an AUROC and AUPRC of 85.5% and 19.5% (OUD prevalence of 3.5%), respectively, on the VA dataset. Our fairness auditing showed that the model was generally fair for patients with different genders, race, and ethnic backgrounds. This model may potentially improve prevention and care of OUD.

papers.title: A reusable strawberry stem based on hot melt adhesives for robotic harvesting applications
papers.abstract: Juan Espejel Flores and colleagues develop a reusable self-healing strawberry stem surrogate based on hot-melt adhesives for repeatable robotic harvesting experiments. The surrogate reproduces the static behavior of real strawberry stems through geometric scaling while enabling repeated cutting, healing, and reuse in a low-cost experimental platform.

papers.title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family
papers.abstract: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti-Mycobacterium activity.

papers.title: Cell-specific proteome profiling reveals altered peripheral immune cell communication in early multiple sclerosis
papers.abstract: Shams et al. use high-resolution proteomics to profile sorted peripheral immune cell populations from individuals with newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve multiple sclerosis. They identify prominent monocyte-associated inflammatory signaling and altered immune cell communication, revealing coordinated immune dysregulation at disease onset.

papers.title: Large language models for depression assessment from brief daily diaries
papers.abstract: Closely tracking changes in depression is important for clinical research and practice. However, intensive longitudinal depression assessment relies on self-report surveys that have major limitations. Scoring depression from natural language with large language models (LLMs) could resolve these shortcomings. This study tested the validity of depression rated by LLMs from daily video diaries. We studied 108 participants selected for mental health treatment status (45% in treatment). Participants completed a clinical interview and 14-21 days of depression surveys and video diaries. Daily depression scores were estimated by LLMs from diary transcripts. LLM ratings converged with self-report depression within-person (r = .45;95% CrI[.40, .49]) and when averaged across days for an overall depression score (r = .61;95% CrI[.43,.75]). Averaged LLM ratings correlated with depression symptom severity ascertained by clinical interview (r = .53;95% CrI[.35, .68]). LLM-rated depression and self-report had similar profiles of associations with daily functioning variables (profile r = .98 within-person; r = .94 between-person). Multivariable regression results showed LLM ratings predicted daily functioning variables (partial $$\beta s$$=|.12 | - | .28 | ) and interview-rated depression (partial $$\beta$$=.33;95% CrI[.07, .58]) over and above self-reports, suggesting LLMs capture clinically-relevant information that self-reports miss. Findings establish a strong foundation for a depression assessment approach that addresses shortcomings of self-reports while satisfying the unique demands of intensive longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: GWDRO-Lung: Gromov–Wasserstein distributionally robust learning for calibrated pulmonary nodule malignancy prediction across imaging cohorts
papers.abstract: Low-dose chest computed tomography (CT) screening detects pulmonary nodules whose malignancy risk must be triaged, yet deep-learning risk models often lose both accuracy and calibration when transferred to a different scanner, protocol, or population. We developed GWDRO-Lung, a chest CT framework that treats cross-cohort transfer as a coupled problem of structural mismatch, distributional instability, and calibration. A weight-shared three-dimensional encoder with embedded acquisition metadata summarizes each cohort as a relation matrix over learned prototypes; cohort geometries are aligned to a shared Gromov–Wasserstein barycenter; and a distributionally robust, calibration-aware risk head estimates malignancy, with the residual alignment error setting a cohort-specific robustness radius. The model was developed on 1842 pulmonary nodules from LIDC-IDRI, organized into three acquisition-defined cohorts, and validated externally on 618 nodules from the independent LNDb cohort, with leave-one-cohort-out, protocol-shift, size-stratified, and decision-curve analyses. Relative to the strongest recent imaging baseline, external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve improved from 0.857 to 0.878, external expected calibration error fell from 0.106 to 0.066, worst-cohort AUC rose from 0.829 to 0.851, and net benefit was higher across triage-relevant thresholds. Prospective, pathology-confirmed validation is required before clinical use.

papers.title: AI-supported first consultation preparation in oncology: a real-world clinical usability study
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) may support clinicians by facilitating information management, but their usability in real-world oncology practice remains understudied. This study evaluated the workflow performance of Artificial Intelligence-based First Consultation Preparation (AI-FCP), generating structured summaries from unstructured clinical documentation, co-created with end users. In a prospective single‑group pre‑post design, nine clinicians completed a person-level baseline, followed by 33 consultations with AI-FCP. Case numbers varied by clinic scheduling and enrollment timing, potentially introducing survivorship bias. Usability was evaluated using validated questionnaires and study-specific instruments. Post AI-FCP, overall perceived workload (NASA-TLX) was 28.9% lower than baseline (Hodges-Lehmann estimate difference −12.3; 95% CI –21.7 to –3.3), with self-reported average time savings of 3.26 min (SD = 2.65) per case. Preparation succeeded in 84.9% of consultations; 63.6% of summaries were complete. These exploratory findings suggest clinicians perceived lower workload and reported improved workflow efficiency with AI-FCP. Further research is needed to determine generalizability.

papers.title: Millisecond phonon lifetimes in piezoelectric nanomechanical resonators
papers.abstract: When defect-mediated losses are mitigated, lithium niobate phononic crystal nanomechanical resonators can have intrinsic phonon lifetimes of up to 21 ms at gigahertz frequencies.

papers.title: Large-scale iontronic skins with neural-hierarchical processing architecture
papers.abstract: Li et al. introduce a neural-hierarchical skin that combines high-density iontronic sensor array, fast readout and data compression, enabling humanoid robots to perceive fine textures, manipulate delicate objects and respond to nociceptive stimuli.

papers.title: AmpliconSuite: an end-to-end workflow for analyzing focal amplifications in cancer genomes
papers.abstract: AmpliconSuite is a toolkit that enables the analysis of focal amplifications from cancer whole-genome sequencing data.

papers.title: Simultaneous antimony recovery from and debromination of flame-retardant electronic-waste plastics
papers.abstract: Isothermal-clamped flash Joule heating enables simultaneous antimony recovery and debromination of flame-retardant electronic-waste plastics. By creating a spatially uniform high-temperature reaction zone within seconds, this ambient-pressure process recovers high-purity antimony and bromine as HBr and suppresses toxic brominated emissions compared with conventional treatment pathways for electronic-waste management.

papers.title: MRI-PHYSIOL-NIRS: an integrated platform to study kidney oxygenation
papers.abstract: Thomas Gladytz and colleagues develop MRI-PHYSIOL-NIRS to improve MR-based assessment of renal oxygenation by integrating MRI with direct oxygen probes and near-infrared spectroscopy in rat kidneys during aortic occlusion and hyperoxia. MRI measures correlate with tissue oxygenation, supporting systematic investigation of additional scenarios toward quantitative MR oximetry.

papers.title: Self-selected motion of overlaid droplets on heterogeneous surfaces via competitive wetting
papers.abstract: Droplets would move following the designed wettability gradient on the surface, toward the position with high surface energy, which is vital for various applications like ink printing, biological detection, and water collection. Anomalously, here we have found that the core of the overlaid droplet shows anti-wettability-gradient movement on the wettability boundary. The core droplet would perform different directional motions after the impact on the same established surface, depending on the impact dynamics and the composition ratio of the overlaid droplet. The macroscopic motion preference of the overlaid droplet is related to the wetting preference of the overlayer on the heterogeneous surface. Competitive wetting/dewetting of different components of the overlayer droplet induces a special shuttle motion of the core droplet. The phenomenon would provide new insight into wetting and droplet control, being promising for broad application scenarios.

papers.title: Beamstop-free small-angle X-ray scattering for multiscale structure measurement of high-energy-density plasma
papers.abstract: The advent of free-electron lasers has enabled in-situ small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) measurements of laser-produced high-energy-density plasma at solid density, with nanometer- and femtosecond-scale resolution. Such plasmas generally exhibit gentle density gradients, which suppress large-angle scattering signals while small-angle scattering components dominate near the direct X-ray beam; the latter signals were hard to access in the conventional SAXS method due to the use of a beamstop. Here, we demonstrate a beamstop-free SAXS system comprising layered metallic filters for optimal attenuation of diffraction signals. It enables continuous acquisition of wide q-range/angular scattering signals with a large dynamic range, including the critical small-angle region containing the direct X-ray beam. This method was applied to a two-dimensional array of submicron columnar plasmas generated by irradiating a high-intensity laser pulse onto an assembly of high-aspect-ratio silicon rods with well-defined sharp edges. We experimentally resolve the microscale and macroscale rarefaction dynamics of bulk electrons driven by the pump-laser pre-pulse and main pulse, revealing the initial plasma scale length as a key parameter governing laser absorption in structured targets. Beamstop-free SAXS enables single-shot multiscale structure measurement and establishes a route toward exploration of stochastic plasma dynamics under high-energy-density conditions, including filamentation instability and turbulence.

papers.title: Temporal trends of dengue exposure among children in coastal Kenya
papers.abstract: Serosurveys suggest widespread dengue virus (DENV) transmission in Africa but there is limited information on the temporal patterns of exposure. Using repeated cross-sectional serosurvey data, we estimated the prevalence and incidence of DENV infections in coastal Kenya over 20 years (1998–2018). Stored sera (n = 8025), collected annually from an open longitudinal cohort of 1834 children aged 15 years and below, were screened for anti-DENV IgG antibodies. We show that, of 8025 samples, 2287 (28.5%, 95% CI 27.5–29.5%) were seropositive for DENV IgG antibodies. Seroprevalence increased with age, from 2% among children aged below 1 year to 40% among those aged 9 to 10 years, and peaked during outbreak years. Among 1343 children who were seronegative at recruitment, the overall incidence (seroconversion) rate was 111.5 DENV infections per 1000 person-years (95% CI 102.5–121.2). The highest incidence occurred in 2013 at 439.7 infections per 1000 person-years (95% CI 375.1–515.5), coinciding with a large outbreak in coastal Kenya. Our findings suggest long-term DENV exposure among children in coastal Kenya and highlight an urgent need for clinical surveillance to determine the associated health burden. Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection, but little is known about how often children in Africa are infected over time. We tested more than 8,000 blood samples collected from children in coastal Kenya between 1998 and 2018. Overall, about 28% of samples had antibodies showing previous dengue infection. The proportion increased with age and was highest during outbreak years. New infections occurred throughout the 20-year study, with the highest rate recorded in 2013 during a major local outbreak. These findings show that children in coastal Kenya have been regularly exposed to dengue for many years. Better clinical surveillance is urgently needed to measure the illness caused by dengue and support effective public health responses.

papers.title: Immune-related gene expression links anxiety, depression, and pain outcomes in adolescence
papers.abstract: Le et al. use longitudinal data to examine whether polymorphisms in the NRF2 gene are associated with affective symptoms and pain. They find that higher levels of anxiety and depression at age 14 predicted increased pain complaints at age 16 and the NRF2 rs6721961 polymorphism is associated with differential vulnerability to pain.

papers.title: Stereochemical preorganization directs triple-helical assembly of Au 4 nanoclusters
papers.abstract: Translating local stereochemical information into higher-order helical architectures is a central challenge in materials design. Now it has been shown that stereochemically preorganized Au 4 nanoclusters assemble into homochiral triple helices through directional aurophilic interactions, providing a design strategy for chiral nanocluster materials with amplified chiroptical responses.

papers.title: Unidirectional rotation in a molecular motor driven by angular-momentum transfer via helical orbitals
papers.abstract: Molecular motors typically rotate by cycling through excitation and relaxation to ground states. Now it has been shown that a molecular motor can be driven by angular-momentum transfer. Circulating positive and negative currents flowing through orbitals of opposite helicity along a carbon–carbon triple bond enable unidirectional rotation.

papers.title: Cavity-less Brillouin strong coupling in a solid-state continuous system
papers.abstract: Strong coupling between light and matter is typically realized in resonators. Now it is shown that this can happen in a cavity-less waveguide scenario in which the light passes through only once.

papers.title: The extraction of work from hidden degrees of freedom
papers.abstract: According to the laws of thermodynamics, information can be converted into energy. An information engine that harnesses environmental memory and exhibits non-Markovian dynamics has now been realized in experiments.

papers.title: Topotactic synthesis of gradient-encoded covalent organic framework membranes
papers.abstract: A diffusion-limited topotactic exchange strategy transforms vertically aligned imine-linked covalent organic framework membranes into gradient-encoded frameworks across multiple linkage chemistries while preserving crystallinity and channel orientation. The built-in chemical asymmetry enables directional ion transport, enhanced osmotic energy conversion and robust operation under strongly acidic conditions.

papers.title: Synthesis of covalent organic frameworks through hydrogen-bonding catalysis
papers.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are typically synthesized under harsh acid- or base-catalysed conditions. Here a hydrogen-bonding catalysis strategy based on reusable benzimidazole enables the rapid and scalable production of COFs with high crystallinity and porosity, offering a general route to imide, imine, hydrazone and sp 2 -carbon-linked COF synthesis.

papers.title: Reversible zinc oxidation as a route to on-demand hydrogen delivery
papers.abstract: Reversible zinc oxidation, enhanced by lactate coordination, enables a self-sustained, circuit-free pathway for high-density hydrogen storage and delivery. By overcoming solubility limits under ambient conditions, this system delivers higher volumetric capacity and safety than existing carriers, providing a robust alternative to high-pressure infrastructure for decentralized, on-demand green hydrogen delivery.

papers.title: Hydrogel-confined environment for aqueous-compatible perovskite crystallization
papers.abstract: Confining water within a polymeric hydrogen-bond network creates a controlled aqueous reaction environment that stabilizes precursors and directs the growth of dense, crack-free perovskite thick films. The resulting X-ray detectors achieve an ultralow detection limit of 19.8 nGy air s −1 .

papers.title: Material circularity implications of battery degradation in shared electric mobility
papers.abstract: Shared mobility aims to save materials, yet intensive use accelerates battery degradation and may alter these savings. This study assesses the implications of shared mobility by coupling fleet projections, battery degradation and dynamic material flow analysis in China.

papers.title: Small-molecule-bound biopolymer networks for sustainable multifunctional composites
papers.abstract: Combining biomaterials of different nature can yield sustainable composites with otherwise inaccessible properties. This study presents a strategy to overcome interfacial mismatch between individual components, enabling efficient structural integration within mechanically strong, multifunctional films.

papers.title: EGFR-targeted antibody−toxin conjugate in recurrent glioma: a phase 1 trial
papers.abstract: Results of a phase 1 trial of the antibody−toxin conjugate D2C7-ATC targeting EGFR/EGFRvIII in patients with recurrent malignant glioma show encouraging safety and efficacy signals, with translational analyses of patient samples indicating intratumoral and systemic immune activation.

papers.title: Real-world, digital-first delivery of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy in women
papers.abstract: At 6 months, a cohort of 8,127 women in the UK initiating GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy via a digital platform showed mean weight reduction comparable to that in randomized clinical trials.

papers.title: Batteries that sense dendrite growth
papers.abstract: An article in Nature Sensors describes a solid electrolyte that converts lithium dendrite penetration into an electrical signal, providing advance warning of impending battery failure.

papers.title: Automated differentiation for parkinsonism using clinical structural MRI: A multicenter study
papers.abstract: Multimodal research-grade magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans show potential for differentiating Parkinson’s disease (PD) from multiple system atrophy (MSA), but clinical translation is limited by cost, acquisition time, and processing burden. Here, we developed a T1-weighted structural MRI-based machine learning model to differentiate Parkinsonism and generalized it to routine anisotropic 2D clinical MRI. Using a multicenter cohort of 969 participants, we employed a hierarchical discovery–verification–translation framework. While a multimodal benchmark model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.98, our streamlined unimodal T1-Top20 model achieved an AUROC of 0.93 for multiclass discrimination (healthy controls, PD, MSA). For PD vs MSA, the frozen T1-Top20 model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.88 in the external research-grade cohort (n = 227) and identified 19 of 25 who phenoconverted from idiopathic rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) to PD. Importantly, the generalized model achieved a pooled AUROC of 0.84 in the clinical-MRI cohort (2D T1, n = 303), supporting its potential for clinical translation.

papers.title: A generalist model for diverse text-guided medical image synthesis
papers.abstract: Deep learning requires extensive data to achieve robust performance. However, data availability is often restricted in medicine due to patient privacy concerns. Synthetic data from medical image generative models present a possible solution to these challenges. Unfortunately, many models are often task-specific or trained on private datasets, limiting scalability and reproducibility. To address this, we introduce MediSyn: an open-access, generalist, text-guided latent diffusion model. MediSyn can generate images across 6 medical specialties and 10 imaging modalities, while being trained exclusively on public data. Our study provides several key contributions using MediSyn. First, we demonstrate that a generalist model can generate images of comparable quality to task-specific models across multiple specialties. Second, we show that this generalist approach is more computationally efficient than a suite of task-specific models. Third, we establish that a generalist model can produce realistic, text-aligned images across visually and medically distinct modalities. Fourth, we empirically demonstrate that these synthetic images are visually distinct from real images used in training. Finally, we show that a generalist model can produce images that improve classifier performance in data-limited settings across multiple specialties. Altogether, our findings highlight the potential of generalist image generative models to accelerate medical algorithmic research and development.

papers.title: A multi-stage validation framework for trustworthy large-scale clinical information extraction using large language models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show promise for extracting clinically meaningful information from unstructured health records, yet real-world deployment is constrained by limited scalable, trustworthy validation approaches. Conventional evaluation relies on annotation-intensive reference standards and incomplete structured data, limiting population-scale use. We propose a multi-stage validation framework for LLM-based clinical information extraction that enables rigorous assessment under weak supervision by integrating complementary validation strategies. The framework combines prompt calibration, rule-based filtering, semantic grounding, judge-LLM evaluation, expert review, and predictive validity analysis to quantify uncertainty without exhaustive manual annotation. We applied this framework to extract substance use disorder (SUD) diagnoses across 11 substance categories from 919,783 clinical notes. Rule-based filtering and semantic grounding removed 14.59% of LLM-positive extractions that were unsupported or structurally implausible. For high-uncertainty cases, the judge LLM showed substantial agreement with subject matter expert. Using judge evaluations as references, the primary LLM achieved an F1 score of 0.80. LLM-extracted SUD diagnoses predicted subsequent engagement in SUD specialty care more accurately than structured-data baselines. By unifying complementary validation strategies, this work presents a generalizable human-in-the-loop framework for establishing the trustworthiness of LLM-based clinical information extraction at scale while minimizing the need for exhaustive manual annotation.

papers.title: Effectiveness of ecological momentary interventions for patients with cancer: a meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
papers.abstract: Symptom burden and impaired quality of life (QoL) are major challenges for patients with cancer. Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) offer real-time, context-sensitive, and personalized support, enabling more precise management of patient needs. To explore the effectiveness of EMIs in improving symptoms and QoL in patients with cancer, a systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted. Following PRISMA 2020, a comprehensive search was conducted in nine databases from inception to December 8, 2025. The RoB 2 tool and GRADE were used to assess risk of bias and certainty of evidence, respectively. The R (version 4.4.1) and the “meta” package were used for statistical analysis. A total of 17 studies involving 4,160 randomized participants were included. The results suggested that EMIs may improve depression in patients with cancer, but were not associated with significant improvements in fatigue, pain severity, pain interference, sleep disturbance, anxiety, or QoL. Given the limited certainty and robustness of the available evidence, further adequately powered, allocation-concealed randomized controlled trials with blinded outcome assessment, where feasible, are needed to strengthen the evidence base for EMIs in oncology care.

papers.title: Postoperative CT habitat fusion model predicts prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer after neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy
papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NAIC) has been widely adopted for non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC); however, reliable tools for postoperative disease-free survival (DFS) risk stratification remain lacking. We developed and validated a habitat radiomics–clinicopathological fusion model, termed the Neoadjuvant Lung Joint Clustering (NeoLung-JC) model, for postoperative DFS stratification and prediction in patients with NSCLC who underwent surgery after NAIC. The model integrates dual-sequence CT-derived tumor habitat heterogeneity scores with key clinicopathological factors. The habitat heterogeneity scores were extracted from the tumor core and peripheral regions using a joint clustering approach. In a multicenter cohort of 508 patients, the NeoLung-JC model showed favorable and consistent predictive performance, achieving a concordance index of 0.750 (95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.680–0.807) in the external validation cohort. The model significantly stratified patients into high-, medium-, and low-risk DFS groups, with clearly separated Kaplan–Meier survival curves across all cohorts (P < 0.0001). Its prognostic performance exceeded that of conventional clinicopathological indicators, including clinical TNM (cTNM) stage, post-treatment pathological TNM (ypTNM) stage, and pathological response. By integrating dual-sequence CT-derived tumor spatial heterogeneity with clinical risk characteristics, the NeoLung-JC model may provide a useful supplementary approach for individualized postoperative prognostic assessment in patients with NSCLC undergoing surgery after NAIC.

papers.title: Structural variant detection across sequencing technologies
papers.abstract: HitSV models the interaction between genomic repetitiveness and signature intensity to improve structural variant detection.

papers.title: Ultrafast laser-engineered hollow TiO 2 Nanoblisters for enhanced flexoelectricity
papers.abstract: This study uses a femtosecond-laser to sculpt hollow nanoblister arrays in TiO2 thin films, creating high-curvature architectures that amplify flexoelectric response. By coupling this with macroscopic substrate bending, devices achieve an output voltage of 0.516 V and a 21.5-fold enhancement over planar TiO2 films.

papers.title: Surface diffusion strategies for chemical vapor deposition of 2D Nb 2 C MXene films
papers.abstract: This paper reports a surface diffusion liquid metal chemical vapor deposition method for synthesizing bare few-layer 2D Nb 2 C MXenes. Single crystalline Nb 2 C flakes with a trigonal structure are obtained in a specific region, and a continuous 2D film can be formed by leveraging the self-assembling process observed during growth.

papers.title: Pixel-segmenting imaging physically exceeds pixel-level sampling constraints via intra-pixel quantum-efficiency measurement enabled by evolutionary algorithms
papers.abstract: Jinchao Liang and colleagues report a physics-driven pixel-segmenting imaging (PSI) method that integrates a custom optical system and evolutionary algorithms to measure intra-pixel quantum efficiency. This approach transcends conventional pixel-level sampling constraints and achieves 4×4 sub-pixel resolution without any hardware modification.

papers.title: A bio-inspired energy-resilient wireless skin
papers.abstract: Soft and conformal wearable wireless systems are promising for healthcare, ambient Internet-of-Things and mission-critical applications, but persistent operation is hindered by mechanical deformation and fluctuating energy availability. Existing wearable systems are typically confined to fixed communication modes, relying on either energy-intensive active radios or low-power but functionally limited passive schemes. Here we present a bio-inspired octopus-like energy-resilient wireless skin (ERWS) with adaptive active–passive communication. The ERWS uses active communication for multimodal sensing and localization when energy is sufficient and switches to low-power backscatter sensing and data transmission when energy is limited. A time–frequency–space co-design enables this operation: undervoltage-lockout-based energy management controls temporal mode switching; dual-band operation assigns Bluetooth communication and radio-frequency (RF) energy harvesting to 2.4 GHz and wake-up/backscatter communication to 915 MHz; and a flexible optically transparent antenna, flexible solar cell and central functional island are vertically integrated. An island–bridge architecture mechanically decouples RF-sensitive components from stretchable interconnects, preserving electromagnetic performance under deformation. Experiments demonstrate autonomous mode switching, reliable active and passive communication, hybrid solar/RF energy harvesting, deformation tolerance and multimodal physiological monitoring, establishing the ERWS as an energy-resilient wearable platform for persistent operation under dynamic conditions.

papers.title: Low-temperature monolithic integration of patterned distributed Bragg reflectors for high-resolution QD-OLED microdisplays
papers.abstract: With the increasing demand for hyper-realistic displays, significant advancements have been reported in high-resolution quantum dot–organic light-emitting diode (QD-OLED) technology owing to its wide color gamut and improved color purity. However, achieving both high color purity and light extraction remains a critical challenge due to significant blue light leakage in high resolution QD-OLED. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating a damage-free, low-temperature ( < 100 °C) monolithic integration of patterned distributed Bragg reflectors (DBRs) directly onto a QD-OLED stack to effectively suppress blue leakage and enhance conversion efficiency. DBRs fabricated from SiNx and SiOx using low-temperature ( < 100 °C) plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition demonstrate high reflectance of 95.9% at 455 nm while effectively suppressing reflectance in the red and green regions. A high-precision, one-step fluorine-based dry etching process achieved a 4 μm pattern size with a near-vertical taper angle of 89°, supporting pixel densities up to 3175 ppi. Compared to the device without DBR, the monolithically integrated architecture exhibits a photon recycling effect, enhancing red and green emission intensities by 19.7% and 10.7%, respectively, while reducing blue leakage by approximately 90%. Furthermore, the integrated device achieved a color gamut of 120.5% relative to the sRGB standard. These findings confirm that monolithically integrated DBRs serve as a robust and scalable solution for next-generation high-resolution QD-OLED displays.

papers.title: Monolithically integrated four-channel optoelectronic wind sensor with a mushroom-shaped sensitive structure
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel wind sensor based on a monolithically integrated four-channel optoelectronic chip and a mushroom-shaped sensitive structure. The four-channel optoelectronic chip consists of a centrally positioned light-emitting diode (LED) surrounded by four symmetrically arranged photodetectors (PDs). By employing monolithic integrated manufacturing technology, the consistency among the four PDs is significantly enhanced, thereby ensuring the overall symmetry of the sensor. In addition, an environmentally robust mushroom-shaped wind-sensitive structure is designed to interact with airflow while packaging the optoelectronic chip, providing reliable protection against outdoor environmental conditions. The manufactured sensor is subsequently installed in a wind tunnel for a series of measurements. The results demonstrate the capability of the sensor to monitor wind speeds ranging from 0 to 18 m/s and wind direction from 0 to 360°. This innovative design paves the way for advancements in wind-sensing devices, positioning it as a promising candidate for practical applications across various fields.

papers.title: Evidence for symmetry-reduction in solid H 2 O above 222 GPa
papers.abstract: Water (H2O), one of the most consequential compounds in the Solar System, governs the structure and dynamics of icy planets, the terrestrial water cycle, and through the pressure-induced transition from hydrogen to ionic bonding, it exhibits marked changes over the pressure range of planetary interiors. While many materials are expected to favour simple, densely packed lattices with increasing compression, as observed in water ice-X, others exhibit unexpected structural complexity at extreme pressures. Here we report experimental evidence that water ice undergoes a transformation from ice-X to a loss of cubic symmetry above 222(12) GPa. Synchrotron X-ray diffraction reveals a distortion of the cubic lattice consistent with either Pbcm or P42/nnm symmetry, the former being strongly favorable by ab initio calculations. This transition marks the onset of a new regime of structural complexity in high-pressure H2O, redefining the upper stability limit of ice-X.

papers.title: Structural control of Fe(II)-based multivalent glycan assemblies enables intramolecular avidity and ultra-high-affinity binding
papers.abstract: Understanding how saccharide spatial arrangement governs multivalent glycan recognition is critical, yet quantitative design principles linking glycan geometry to binding affinity remain poorly defined. Here, the authors engineered atomically precise iron(II)-based glycoassemblies to systematically modulate glycan valency, spacing, and topology and, using monomeric Griffithsin as a model lectin, demonstrate a striking >1000-fold variation in binding affinities arising from controlled glycan presentation.

papers.title: Precision targeting of tumor-associated macrophages via a 6-substituted pyrrolo[2,3- d ]pyrimidine chimeric molecule for enhanced cancer immunotherapy
papers.abstract: The clinical application of small molecule immunomodulators is limited by poor selectivity for tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) and systemic toxicities. Here, the authors develop a folate receptor-beta targeted chimeric molecule, AS-6, which selectively accumulates in TAMs, remodels the tumor microenvironment, and enhances the efficacy of anti-PD-1 therapy while reducing systemic side effects.

papers.title: Capturing attosecond delays in electronic and vibrational dependent photoemission of NO molecules
papers.abstract: Timing the photoionization process reveals electron motion through the molecular potential and the interplay between electronic and nuclear dynamics. Here we show, using attosecond interferometry with high energy resolution, that photoionization delays in nitric oxide depend on the electronic state and vibrational level of the molecular ion. We observe significant delays among channels leading to different electronic states, in agreement with scattering calculations. In contrast, delays among vibrational levels of the ground electronic state are negligible in an energy range without significant resonances. These results attribute this difference to the influence of resonant electronic structures on electron propagation, which establish photoionization delays as a sensitive probe of the molecular potential. Despite averaging over molecular orientations, the agreement between experiment and theory provides a valuable test of the theoretical description and supports the interpretation of electron dynamics in heteronuclear molecules.

papers.title: Design and Monte Carlo simulation of a phase grating moiré neutron interferometer to measure the gravitational constant
papers.abstract: This work uses a Monte Carlo model to design and simulate a neutron phase-grating moiré interferometer experiment to measure Newton’s gravitational constant G. Simulations show G can be measured to 150 parts-per-million with systematics independent of previous experiments, and that lunar gravitation may require corrections to earlier measurements.

papers.title: Reaction–diffusion competition drives anomalous relaxation of vitrimers
papers.abstract: Vitrimers—polymers that form covalent networks—show glassy behaviour with viscosity decoupled from structural relaxation. This decoupling is now found to originate from a competition between chemical exchange reactions and diffusion processes.

papers.title: Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array
papers.abstract: Quantum computers require simultaneous control of multiple qubits, which is challenging to achieve in nanoscale semiconductor devices. Now high-fidelity parallel operations have been demonstrated for five silicon spin qubits.

papers.title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
