papers.abstract: The experimental realization of intrinsic 2D kagome materials with controllable flat bands has remained challenging. Now a van der Waals kagome material family is shown to host an isolated, gate-tunable flat band down to the monolayer limit.

papers.title: Perovskite chiral multiple quantum wells with extended spin lifetime via efficient spin cascade
papers.abstract: Chiral multiple quantum wells enhance spin coherence in perovskites through spin cascade, achieving over 5-ns spin lifetime at room temperature.

papers.title: Quantifying assets for the geopolitics of climate change mitigation
papers.abstract: Climate action reshapes who gains and loses from energy and environmental resources, raising new geopolitical questions. A study now quantifies four climate-related asset types across 169 countries and reveals uneven asset redistribution, with major powers often less affected.

papers.title: Skill and spatial mismatches for sustainable development in Brazil
papers.abstract: Deforestation-reducing development pathways may cut emissions, but it is unclear how workers can adapt given skill and geographic mobility constraints. Modelling job transitions in Brazil reveals that greener pathways benefit workers in high-skill occupations but increase low-skill unemployment, mitigated by mobility policies.

papers.title: Deep learning-enabled assessment of right ventricular size and function is associated with cardiovascular outcomes
papers.abstract: Al-Alusi et al. develop DROID-RV, a deep learning model to assess right ventricular dilation and dysfunction, and show that the model’s predictions are associated with mortality and cardiovascular disease risk.

papers.title: Human iPSC-derived lens organoids recapitulate lens development and morphogenesis in vitro
papers.abstract: The human lens is a transparent, avascular organ essential for focusing light and achieving visual acuity. While animal models have illuminated lens development, direct models of human lens organogenesis remain limited. We present an in vitro platform for lens morphogenesis by combining spatially patterned self-formed ectodermal autonomous multizone (SEAM) differentiation of human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs), with a lens optimised medium (LOM). Lentoids exhibited zone-specific organisation, upregulation of lens crystallins and connexins, and spatial protein localisation reflective of lens epithelial and fiber cells. LOM-treated cultures exhibited enhanced γ-crystallin expression, cadherin-mediated organisation, and capsule basement membrane deposition, alongside ultrastructural features of a maturing lens, including elongated cortical-like fibers, epithelial layering, and intercellular junctions with ball-and-socket-like interdigitations. Lentoids demonstrated self-renewing, preplacodal and presumptive lens ectodermal PAX6⁺/SIX3⁺/SOX2⁺ epithelial-like populations, which formed secondary lentoids, following activation of lens crystallin differentiation transcription factors—PROX1 and SOX1. These findings advance hiPSC-derived lens models and reveal an epithelial plasticity—offering a platform for studying ectodermal pathways, regenerative biology, and cataractogenesis. Lens differentiation requires the highest translational output to generate lifelong structural proteins, alongside a superior protein quality control system, and hiPSC-derived platforms provide a human model to study the limits of cellular differentiation and protein homeostasis.

papers.title: TrajOnco: a multi-agent framework for temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHR for multi-cancer early detection
papers.abstract: Accurate estimation of cancer risk from longitudinal electronic health records (EHRs) could support earlier detection and improved care, but modeling such complex patient trajectories remains challenging. We present TrajOnco, a training-free, multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework designed for scalable multi-cancer early detection. Using a chain-of-agents architecture with long-term memory, TrajOnco performs temporal reasoning over sequential clinical events to generate patient-level summaries, evidence-linked rationales, and predicted risk scores. We evaluated TrajOnco on de-identified Truveta EHR data across 15 cancer types using matched case-control cohorts, predicting risk of cancer diagnosis at 1 year. In zero-shot evaluation, TrajOnco achieved AUROCs of 0.64–0.80, performing comparably to supervised machine learning in a lung cancer benchmark while demonstrating better temporal reasoning than single-agent LLMs. The multi-agent design also enabled effective temporal reasoning with smaller-capacity models such as GPT-4.1-mini. The groundedness of TrajOnco’s output was supported by human evaluation. Furthermore, TrajOnco’s interpretable reasoning outputs can be aggregated to reveal population-level risk patterns that align with established clinical knowledge. These findings highlight the potential of multi-agent LLMs to execute interpretable temporal reasoning over longitudinal EHRs, advancing both scalable multi-cancer early detection and clinical insight generation.

papers.title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
papers.abstract: Phenotyping is fundamental to rare disease diagnosis, but manually curating structured phenotypes from clinical notes is labor intensive and difficult to scale. Existing artificial intelligence (AI) approaches optimize individual components of phenotyping but generally do not operationalize the full workflow of extracting features from clinical text, standardizing them to Human Phenotype Ontology (HPO) terms, and prioritizing rare disease-relevant HPO terms. We developed RARE-PHENIX, an end-to-end AI framework for rare disease phenotyping that integrates large language model-based phenotype extraction, ontology-grounded standardization to HPO terms, and supervised ranking of HPO terms. We trained RARE-PHENIX using data from 2671 patients across 11 Undiagnosed Diseases Network clinical sites, and externally validated it on 16,357 real-world clinical notes from 143 patients at Vanderbilt University Medical Center. Our findings suggest RARE-PHENIX generates structured, prioritized HPO terms highly concordant with clinician curation, demonstrates potential downstream disease-prioritization signal, and may support human-in-the-loop rare disease phenotyping in real-world settings.

papers.title: Characterizing time-of-day physical activity patterns across cognitive trajectories in older adults: a longitudinal cohort study
papers.abstract: Declining cognitive function is a growing health challenge, yet how cognitive decline influences time-of-day physical activity (PA) patterns remains underexplored. Among cognitively unimpaired participants from the Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities Study, we modeled general and domain-specific cognitive trajectories and related them to accelerometry-derived PA a median of 8.2 years later in 811 participants (mean baseline age 73.1 years) using function-on-scalar and multivariable regression. Slower cognitive decline was associated with more favorable midday PA (10 AM–3 PM), including higher movement volume, less sedentary time, fewer interruptions to active periods, and greater activity variability. In adjusted linear regression models, associations with PA patterns derived from a window as short as 11 AM-1 PM were comparable to those with 24-hour measures. The executive function trajectory exhibited the strongest associations with PA patterns, and over the longest period of the day; the language trajectory showed non-linear associations, and the peak association for the memory trajectory with PA occurred in the late morning (10:30–11:30 AM). Associations between cognitive decline and activity variability were stronger than for other PA metrics. Our findings highlight the potential of PA patterns, particularly activity variability, as a non-invasive way to help monitor cognitive decline before clinical impairment emerges.

papers.title: Solving operating room scheduling problems using large language model based multi-agent architecture
papers.abstract: Efficient operating room scheduling is a complex task due to the diversity of surgical types, high patient demand, and limited hospital resources. Since OR operations account for a substantial share of hospital costs, effective scheduling solutions are critical. Large language model (LLM)-based multi-agent systems offer new opportunities to support optimization for this problem. This study evaluates an LLM-based multi-agent framework for generating and refining optimization code for OR scheduling. Leveraging iterative collaboration among specialized agents, the proposed iterative multi-agent (IMA) framework consistently outperformed both single-agent and traditional multi-agent baselines. Across 10 LLMs and 35 scenarios, IMA achieved an average feasible schedule rate of 82.91%, compared with 65.59% and 52.53% for the baselines. Experiments on 1050 synthetic cases and three real OR datasets further showed that IMA-generated code produced solutions close to those of expert-written mixed-integer programming models, while a case study of hospital as-is schedules demonstrated improvements in OR utilization and overtime reduction. These results suggest that LLM-based multi-agent systems can provide a practical and effective approach for OR scheduling optimization.

papers.title: Implementation and effectiveness of a smartphone app targeted at improving physicians adherence to antimicrobial treatment guidelines
papers.abstract: The effectiveness of mHealth interventions for improving antimicrobial guideline adherence remains insufficiently understood in resource-limited settings. This study evaluated a context-adapted smartphone Standard Treatment Guideline (STG) app designed to improve physicians’ adherence to antimicrobial treatment guidelines in Ethiopia. A type 1 hybrid effectiveness–implementation cluster-randomized trial was conducted in 20 hospitals randomized to a smartphone app plus training or paper-based guidelines and retrospectively registered (PACTR202504495116733). The primary outcome was guideline-adherent prescribing, defined as correct antibiotic selection, dose, frequency, and duration when treatment was indicated, or appropriately documented non-prescribing when antibiotics were not indicated across 1433 patient charts. Secondary outcomes included overall antibiotic use and broad-spectrum antibiotic use. Guideline adherence improved by 26.7 percentage points in crude difference-in-differences analysis, and the adjusted intervention-by-endline effect showed higher odds of guideline-adherent prescribing (aOR 3.89; 95% CI: 1.96–7.73). Overall, antibiotic use declined from 96.9% to 82.2% in the intervention arm. In a post-hoc sensitivity analysis using all eligible charts, broad-spectrum antibiotic use declined from 83.9 to 57.5%. These findings support the potential value of a multicomponent intervention combining an offline STG app with training and implementation support for improving guideline-concordant antimicrobial prescribing; however, the independent contribution of the mobile application cannot be determined.

papers.title: SpatialZoomer: multi-scale feature analysis of spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: SpatialZoomer is a spectral graph-based method for analysing spatial transcriptomics data across scales, from single cells to spatially organized domains. The demonstrations highlight the power of studying heterogeneous diseased tissues across scales.

papers.title: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene
papers.abstract: Gate-voltage sweeps drive a first-order sliding transition between Bernal-dominant and rhombohedral–Bernal mixed stacking in marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene, which allows for non-volatile on/off switching of the low-temperature ferromagnetic phase.

papers.title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics
papers.abstract: A scalable cryogenic shock exfoliation method for the fabrication of large and uniform rhombohedral graphene flakes is demonstrated.

papers.title: LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
papers.abstract: LoL-align is a probabilistic, distance-based protein structure alignment algorithm that iteratively optimizes a local log-odds score, achieving higher sensitivity for remote homologs and better alignment quality than available methods.

papers.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
papers.abstract: This Article presents MassNet, a large-scale AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT). Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods.

papers.title: Optical signal enhancement in erbium-doped yttria-stabilized zirconia heterogeneously integrated on silicon nitride waveguides
papers.abstract: Silicon photonics is promising for developing increasingly complex communication systems but faces challenges in integrating key functionalities such as light amplification. Here, the authors demonstrate a heterogeneously integrated photonic device using erbium-doped yttria-stabilized zirconia on silicon nitride waveguides, achieving significant on-chip signal amplification, which advances efficient photonic materials compatible with silicon platforms.

papers.title: Voltage-driven magnetoelectric laminates enabled by interfacial design for energy-saving spintronic actuation
papers.abstract: Reducing power consumption in electronic technologies requires innovative methods to generate magnetic fields without current flow. Here, the authors develop polymer-based magnetoelectric laminated composites that achieve voltage-driven magnetic actuation, significantly lowering power usage by nearly 75% compared to traditional methods, and setting new benchmarks for low-power spintronic applications.

papers.title: Reconfigurable acoustic tweezers based on a programmable droplet array
papers.abstract: Conventional acoustic manipulation relies on either direct acoustic radiation force acting on particles or indirect methods using acoustic streaming generated by acoustic pressure fields to manipulate particles. While acoustic devices generating standing waves can create patterned arrangements of particles and cells, these methods are typically limited to producing regular arrays in static configurations. This study introduces a dynamic acoustic field modulation method to overcome these limitations, significantly enhancing manipulation flexibility. Crucially, the propagation of acoustic energy varies substantially at liquid-solid interfaces or gas-solid interfaces due to differences in acoustic impedance matching. To exploit this, we use a digital microfluidic chip (DMF) to manipulate droplets and generate a programmable droplet array via the electrowetting-on-dielectric effect. By utilizing the programmable droplet array, we dynamically alter the spatial distribution of the acoustic field from a bulk acoustic wave (BAW) device in real time and demonstrate this technique’s capability for capturing and manipulating particles on demand. We believe this is a unique method to create acoustic tweezers with great flexibility and reconfigurability, which holds promising potential for advanced applications in micromanipulation, micro-assembly, and beyond.

papers.title: Magnetized joystick with dual-anisotropy for high-capacity wearable human-machine interactions
papers.abstract: One of the urgent demands for flexible and wearable sensors is to achieve single-channel, less-sensor, and multi-output for effective communications. However, expansion of signal capacity on a single interface often requires sensor arrays, which significantly increases the complexity in electrode layout and multiple device design. In this work, we developed a flexible magnetized joystick (FMJ) with structurally induced eigenfrequency anisotropy by applying laser cutting process to a raw magnetized cubic. Using an eigenfrequency-polarity dual-anisotropy addressing method, we show that single FMJ can achieve four identifiable outputs based on the direction of in-plane mechanical inputs. According to the cantilever beam model, the eigenfrequency library can be expanded by adjusting cutting parameters, dimensions, and material properties, laying the foundation for further expanding signal capacity through the combination of multiple FMJs. The advantages of FMJs in terms of high capacity and multi-functionality are demonstrated through a range of human-machine interaction (HMI) applications, including game control, PowerPoint slides, robot car control, and a fingertip calculator. The increased signal requirement would not impose the complexity of electrical connection thanks to the interference-free parallel design of the electrodes. We expect that the development strategy will provide valuable insights for further advancement of high-capacity wearable HMI.

papers.title: Curvature-driven passive mixing in three-dimensional conical helix micromixers
papers.abstract: Passive microfluidic mixing is fundamentally constrained by the dominance of laminar flow, a limitation commonly addressed using embedded obstacles or surface modifications, often at the cost of increased fabrication complexity and hydraulic resistance. Here, we introduce a conical helix micromixer (CHM) that combines circular and helical microchannel topologies into a monolithic geometry capable of passively generating progressively intensified Dean vortices through continuously varying curvature. This curvature-driven mechanism induces strong transverse transport and achieves  a mixing index (MI) > 95% in the first turn of the CHM across varying flow rates (1–2500 µL min−1) without requiring any internal roughness structures or external energy inputs, as validated by field-based mixing simulations. A central methodological contribution is a reduced-order planar representation of the full three-dimensional (3D) CHM geometry for flow-field analysis and optimization. Direct geometrical validation against the original 3D conical-helix centreline demonstrated projection-induced deviations below 2% across all investigated configurations, with most cases remaining below 1%, confirming that the planar representation preserves the dominant geometric characteristics of the true 3D flow path with negligible loss of fidelity. This reduced-order strategy lowered computational costs by approximately an order of magnitude, while preserving a strong correlation with full 3D field-based calculations across the investigated ranges of Reynolds numbers. Geometric and flow parameters were systematically explored using a Taguchi framework, while gradient-boosted machine-learning models were employed as mechanistic analytical tools to quantify parameter sensitivity. Both analyses consistently identified the inlet curvature radius as the dominant design variable governing Dean vortex onset and mixing-length compression, with tighter curvature significantly accelerating the development of transverse mixing. The results prove that controlled curvature modulation alone can function as an efficient passive mixing engine, providing a compact, fabrication-ready platform for microreactor synthesis, point-of-care diagnostics, and scalable lab-on-a-chip applications.

papers.title: Liouvillian exceptional-point-induced phase transition in a single Kerr-cat qubit
papers.abstract: The authors numerically investigate a driven dissipative Kerr cat qubit and uncover a Liouvillian exceptional point that induces a phase transition. The transition manifests as a sharp change from underdamped oscillations to overdamped relaxation, with the Wigner function negativity serving as a hallmark of genuine quantum coherence.

papers.title: An accurate Lanczos method for the matrix product state representation
papers.abstract: When using matrix product states (MPS) to represent the quantum states, the Lanczos algorithm faces a convergence issue due to the MPS truncation. In this work, we address this incompatibility between the MPS representation and the Lanczos algorithm, significantly improving the convergence of the Lanczos algorithm for the MPS representation.

papers.title: Self-organization and collective migration of active condensates
papers.abstract: The authors use simulations of attractive active Brownian particles to investigate how spatial activity gradients regulate active condensates. They find that condensates migrate toward higher activity and can localize, evaporate, and reassemble through the interplay of attraction and motility.

papers.title: Discovering gut microbiome signatures that predict adverse and reverse cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure
papers.abstract: Yang, Liao, Lin et al. investigate gut microbiome signatures associated with adverse and reverse cardiac remodeling in preclinical heart failure. Gut microbiome profiles predict both remodeling trajectories, with specific bacterial taxa associated with favorable or adverse remodeling.

papers.title: A hierarchical model for forecasting seasonal respiratory epidemics across pathogens and regions
papers.abstract: Since 2021, the seasonal tripledemic composed of COVID-19, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) has threatened healthcare capacity globally. Short-term forecasts can provide public health officials and healthcare leaders time to effectively respond to epidemics, but many forecast approaches are bespoke to specific diseases or localities. We present a Bayesian hierarchical forecast model that flexibly accounts for spatial and seasonal transmission dynamics and test its performance on hospital admissions of COVID-19, influenza, and RSV in the United States over two years. We find the model outcompetes a naive baseline model by 42%, 44%, and 41% for COVID-19, influenza, and RSV, respectively, and it was the top individual forecast model in the 2023-2024 and 2025-2026 CDC FluSight forecast challenges. We use our model’s inferences to quantify the timing and shape for influenza and RSV epidemics and the biannual seasonality of COVID-19. Additionally, we estimate regional disease burden differences across the country, finding higher burden in the South and lower burden in the West and Northeast. Given its flexible nature and robust performance, our model provides a straightforward way to expand forecasting to additional regions and for other seasonal diseases such as Dengue virus or malaria. Short-term forecasts of respiratory diseases can help hospitals and public-health agencies prepare for increases in patients. However, many forecasting models are designed for only one disease or location and therefore cannot easily be used elsewhere. We developed a model that accounts for differences in the timing and severity of seasonal outbreaks across locations. We tested it by forecasting US hospital admissions caused by COVID-19, influenza, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Its forecasts were more than 40% better than simple comparison forecasts, and it was the best-performing individual model in two seasons of the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention’s FluSight forecasting initiative. The model also revealed differences in seasonal timing among the three viruses and in disease burden across US regions. Given its adaptability, this approach provides a scalable framework for expanding outbreak forecasting to other regions and diseases, enhancing global epidemic preparedness.

papers.title: Global inequities and fragmentation in guidelines for endometriosis: a scoping review
papers.abstract: Gete et al. review 47 endometriosis guidelines worldwide to assess their availability, target populations, development methods, and recommendations. The guidelines show regional inequities and variation in inclusivity, methodological rigour, and recommendations, highlighting the need for more standardised and equitable global guidance.

papers.title: Mechanoradical-chain C( sp 3 )–C( sp 2 ) coupling with unactivated arenes
papers.abstract: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C( sp 3 )–C( sp 2 ) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.

papers.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π -extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
papers.abstract: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π -extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

papers.title: Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn 2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
papers.abstract: Atomically ordered CuAuZn 2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH 2 , while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO 2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.

papers.title: HDOCK-Multimer: improved structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating docking and combinatorial assembly
papers.abstract: This study presents HDOCK-Multimer, a general framework for structure prediction of large protein complexes by integrating ab initio docking and combinatorial assembly, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art methods.

papers.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial
papers.abstract: A phase 1 trial shows that treatment of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer with personalized neoantigen vaccines combined with PD-1 blockade was feasible and led to tumor-specific immune responses in many patients and putative mechanisms of resistance related to antigen presentation were identified via cell-free DNA analysis.

papers.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
papers.abstract: In the randomized multicenter phase 2 ZZ-FIRST trial, patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor talazoparib combined with androgen receptor inhibitor enzalutamide had an improved prostate-specific antigen response compared with enzalutamide alone, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of paired biopsies linked AR inhibition-induced suppression of HRR-related programs to proliferation arrest rather than functional HRR deficiency.

papers.title: Pou2f2 enhances retinal ganglion cell survival and axon regeneration after optic nerve injury
papers.abstract: Retinal ganglion cell (RGC) degeneration and the limited regenerative capacity of mammalian central nervous system axons result in irreversible vision loss in optic neuropathies. Identifying intrinsic regulators that promote both neuroprotection and axon regeneration is critical for developing effective therapies. This study identified POU domain class 2 transcription factor 2 (Pou2f2) as a previously unrecognized regulator involved in RGC biology. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of developing mouse and human retinas showed that Pou2f2 is enriched in RGC clusters and suppressed by an RGC fate suppressor in the mouse retinal progenitor cell culture. Pou2f2 protein was detected in mouse RGCs and optic nerves, where its expression decreased following optic nerve crush (ONC). In primary RGC cultures, AAV2-mediated Pou2f2 overexpression enhanced neurite outgrowth, whereas Pou2f2 knockdown reduced neurite length. In vivo, intravitreal injection of Pou2f2 overexpression AAV2s increased axon regeneration, improved RGC survival, and partially preserved RGC function after ONC. Bulk RNA sequencing data revealed early activation of cytoskeletal growth pathways and later upregulation of DNA repair-associated genes, whereas immunostaining and in vitro analyses suggested activation of AKT/mTOR signaling following Pou2f2 overexpression. Together, these findings identify Pou2f2 as a promising molecular target for gene-based therapies for RGC degenerative diseases, including glaucoma and other optic neuropathies.

papers.title: Electronic health record developer adherence to federal AI risk transparency requirements
papers.abstract: We evaluated electronic health record developer compliance with federal transparency requirements for AI-enabled predictive decision support interventions. Developers are required to publicly report on risk analysis, mitigation, governance, and on eight other attributes. Across 35 developers, reporting was inconsistent and often incomplete, with substantial variation in structure and detail, yet all developers were certified as meeting the requirements. Results suggest a need for standardized reporting and more rigorous certification review.

papers.title: From research to clinical practice: Expert consensus on Neuroimaging AI tools for the Memory clinic (Neuro-AIM)
papers.abstract: Although AI tools for neuroimaging show considerable promise in the diagnosis, prognosis, and management of neurodegenerative disorders, their uptake in memory clinics has been limited. A key barrier is lack of consensus on their effective design and implementation. Here we establish expert consensus on the specific goals, usage and challenges of AI tools for neuroimaging in the memory clinic using a Delphi process. Sixteen experts from clinical, academic, and industry backgrounds participated in three rounds of questionnaires, coordinated by the Imaging Working Group of the Deep Dementia Phenotyping (DEMON) network, with support from a patient and public involvement representative. Consensus was reached on eight statements covering four themes: purpose, quality, interactions with clinicians and memory clinics, and privacy and ethics. Implementation of these recommendations will further the adoption of AI neuroimaging tools from research to clinical practice, improving diagnostic and care pathways for patient benefit.

papers.title: FedFound: Federated Foundation Model for GI endoscopy imaging
papers.abstract: Gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy is essential for identifying abnormalities and enabling early diagnosis, thereby improving diagnostic accuracy and facilitating timely clinical intervention. While deep learning has shown promise in supporting GI diagnostics, most models require carefully labeled datasets that are costly to acquire and limited in scope. Foundation models offer a paradigm shift by learning general-purpose representations that can be adapted for diverse tasks, addressing data scarcity and variability. However, training such models on medical imaging data remains challenging due to privacy regulations, security concerns, and fragmented digital infrastructures that prevent centralized data aggregation, even as hospitals collectively generate vast amounts of endoscopic data. To overcome these barriers, we propose a federated learning (FL) framework for GI foundation models, allowing data to remain local while collaboratively training a shared model. We extensively evaluate multiple FL algorithms under both homogeneous and heterogeneous settings across three clinically relevant downstream tasks-classification, detection, and segmentation. We further evaluate our framework with a larger number of clients and across diverse pretraining strategies to assess its scalability and robustness. Our results demonstrate consistent performance gains, underscoring the potential of Federated Foundation Models to enable clinically validated AI applications and support secure, regulation-compliant deployment in real-world gastroendoscopy practice.

papers.title: Sequence models reveal diagnosis accumulation pathways beyond comorbidity burden in population-scale hospital data
papers.abstract: Aging trajectories vary among individuals of similar age and disease burden. Comorbidity indices, e.g. the Elixhauser index, aggregate recorded conditions into a single score, but discard the timing, sequence, and pace of morbidity accumulation. Here we ask whether longitudinal hospital diagnosis histories contain information beyond age, sex, and comorbidity burden, and where it is concentrated. Using 13 years of Austrian inpatient data covering 7.4 million patients, we trained a visit-level contrastive transformer to encode diagnosis sequences and inter-admission timing into patient-history embeddings. In a downstream cohort of 1.7 million individuals, the embedding model improved prediction of in-hospital death over the Elixhauser-based comorbidity model, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.879 versus 0.866 (AUC gain = 0.0132, 95% CI 0.0118–0.0144). Across 130 incident ICD-10 disease-block outcomes, the embedding model had higher AUC for 93 outcomes, with a modest median gain of 0.006. Gains were concentrated in mental, musculoskeletal, nervous system, and metabolic disorders. We then evaluated event-free survival, defined as remaining alive without accumulating a second unrecorded ICD-10 disease block. The embedding model achieved an AUC of 0.726 versus 0.722 for the comorbidity model. However, among patients with similar age, sex, and comorbidity-model risk, those assigned high residual risk had 127–181 fewer event-free days over five years and observed event rates comparable to low-residual-risk patients more than a decade older. Together, these findings link the embedding’s signal to the breadth, recency, and pace of prior disease accumulation.

papers.title: Repurposing adult AI radiograph models for neonatal care through continual learning: an international multicentre study
papers.abstract: Continual learning, a privacy-preserving approach, was shown to be effective in addressing a critical gap in paediatric AI by adapting a deep learning model for adult endotracheal tube assessment to neonatal care.

papers.title: Interpretable AI model reveals spatial codes of cell recruitment in tissues
papers.abstract: A fully interpretable multi-instance learning framework, SPACER, helps elucidate which molecular signals recruit specific cells to their precise locations by decoding gene-level recruitment rules from spatially resolved transcriptomics data.

papers.title: Thermal conductance of atomic-scale glass reaches 40% of quantum limit
papers.abstract: Heat flows coherently through an atom-scale break junction of amorphous silicon dioxide at room temperature, reaching 40% of the quantum limit and revealing that structural disorder does not fundamentally impede atomic-scale phonon transport.

papers.title: An all-in-one foundation model for multimodal medical image restoration and enhancement
papers.abstract: Cao et al. present AMIFound, a foundation model that unifies medical image restoration across seven imaging modalities, delivering robust enhancement across diverse degradations and preserving clinically relevant information for diagnosis.

papers.title: Near-infrared photochromic miniprotein enables photoacoustic molecular imaging of acute inflammation and intracellular antigens
papers.abstract: A small, photoswitchable and genetically encodable protein operating in the near-infrared window is reported for photoacoustic tomography applications.

papers.title: In vivo engineering of CAR natural killer cells for immunotherapy using ligand-directed lipid nanoparticles
papers.abstract: Chimeric antigen receptor natural killer cells to treat autoimmune disease and cancer are generated in vivo.

papers.title: Quantitative investigation of thermally driven interfacial diffusion and front-contact breakdown in organic-inorganic halide perovskites
papers.abstract: Elemental migration critically undermines the stability of organic-inorganic halide perovskites, yet the underlying substrate as a source of extrinsic mobile species remains largely overlooked. This study uses Rutherford Backscattering Spectrometry to quantify elemental depth profiles in methylammonium-lead-triiodide films thermally aged at 45, 65 and 85 °C for 96 hours under nitrogen atmosphere. Aging redistributes lead and iodine and produces unexpected oxygen accumulation at the buried interface. Comparison with a non-annealed control confirms that this oxygen originates not from fabrication but from thermally activated out-diffusion of the indium tin oxide substrate, which shows measurable oxygen loss and surface roughening. To mitigate this, a self-assembled monolayer namely [2-(3,6-Dimethoxy-9H-carbazol-9-yl) ethyl] phosphonic Acid was integrated as an interfacial diffusion barrier, which preserves substrate’s stoichiometry and suppresses oxygen migration into the perovskite stack. Although intrinsic lead and iodine migration persists, suppressing substrate-derived oxygen underscores the necessity of interfacial engineering and validates RBS for quantitative tracking of elemental migration.

papers.title: Chemodivergent photoinitiated radical-polar crossover α - and α , β -C–H bond functionalisation of cyclic amine and ether scaffolds
papers.abstract: Saturated heterocycles with acetal motifs are crucial in synthetic and medicinal chemistry, yet their efficient α - and α , β -functionalisation remains challenging. Here, the authors introduce a photoinitiated chemodivergent radical-polar crossover method using dichloramine-T, enabling selective α -functionalisation and β -chlorination.

papers.title: Non-thermal effects and temperature disparities in uniform supersonic flows
papers.abstract: Over the last 40 years, low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical databases have largely come from CRESU (Cinétique de Réaction en Ecoulement Supersonique Uniforme) experiments, where the flow is described by a single temperature under an assumption of local thermal equilibrium. Here we directly test this assumption using infrared frequency comb spectroscopy, laser-induced fluorescence, Pitot measurements, and computational fluid dynamics in seeded supersonic flows. We observe persistent vibrational excitation in carbonyl sulfide (OCS) and nitrous oxide (N2O) under all conditions examined, despite efficient rotational cooling, demonstrating a breakdown of local thermal equilibrium within the flow. In parallel, we find that conventional Pitot-derived temperatures do not consistently reflect the energetic state of the reacting ensemble. These results show that the reacting ensemble in CRESU flows cannot always be described by a single thermodynamic temperature, particularly for species with low-lying vibrational modes, and that internal-state distributions should be carefully considered when interpreting low-temperature reaction rate coefficients in astrochemical kinetic databases.

papers.title: Cycle holonomy captures higher-order compatibility constraints in remote synchronization
papers.abstract: Higher-order interactions have typically been modeled using hypergraphs or simplicial complexes, where interactions explicitly involve more than two nodes. Here we show that effective higher-order dynamical constraints can also emerge on ordinary graphs when the interaction carries nontrivial topological structure. We study a gauge-coupled phase model in which edge phase lags accumulate around closed loops, producing gauge-invariant mismatches. The associated twisted Laplacian admits a zero mode if and only if all cycle holonomies vanish, linking global compatibility to cycle frustration. We then connect this framework to the symmetric Sakaguchi-Kuramoto model. For cactus graphs, path mismatches induced by the symmetric lag can be represented through associated cycle holonomies, while edge-overlapping cycles require an additional cycle-consistency condition. Our results provide a spectral framework linking frustration to cycle-level constraints and identify cycle holonomy as a local-to-global diagnostic of path incompatibility in synchronization dynamics.

papers.title: Modulating time refraction via collisional plasma-formed photonic time interfaces
papers.abstract: Temporal interfaces created by abrupt refractive-index changes enable frequency conversion and underpin photonic time crystals, but bidirectional control in a single physical system remains difficult. Here we show that collisional plasma provides pressure-controlled bidirectional microwave frequency modulation. We develop a self-consistent framework coupling finite-difference time-domain electrodynamics with particle-in-cell Monte Carlo collision kinetics, avoiding a prescribed Drude permittivity for the transient plasma response. The model predicts that high gas pressure produces a redshift dominated by collisional momentum relaxation, whereas low pressure produces a blueshift driven by rapid ionization and electron-density dispersion. Experiments using a waveguide-loaded gas discharge system reproduce the pressure-dependent shift directions predicted by the simulations. These results identify gas pressure as a control parameter for time refraction in plasma and provide a microscopic framework for designing dynamic temporal photonic systems.

papers.title: Elasticity permeability and buckling of aspirated polyacrylamide microgels
papers.abstract: Soft, porous materials combine elasticity with fluid transport, yet how these properties interact to produce mechanical instabilities remains poorly understood. Here we use polyacrylamide microbeads and microcapsules as model of soft porous materials to investigate this coupling. By combining quantitative micropipette aspiration with scaling analysis, we establish a relationship between elastic modulus E and hydraulic permeability k, showing that both are governed by the network mesh size even in highly heterogeneous gels. In hollow microcapsules, we observe buckling instabilities within well-defined ranges of shell thickness and pipette radius. A model coupling shell elasticity to hydrodynamically driven deswelling accounts for these instabilities and reveals how solvent transport can trigger mechanical collapse. These results establish a direct link between network structure, fluid transport and mechanical instability, providing a framework for understanding similar phenomena in physical gels, biological vesicles and shell-coated condensates, with potential relevance to cellular mechanics, tissue engineering and adaptive materials.

papers.title: Molecular fingerprints linked to graft viability in extended criteria donor livers during normothermic machine perfusion
papers.abstract: Attard et al. investigate metabolic signatures of extended-criteria donor livers undergoing normothermic machine perfusion. Differences were seen in pathways relating to amino acid and energy metabolism between viable and non-viable livers.

papers.title: Blood DNA methylation profiling identifies candidate diabetic kidney disease risk signatures in the PROPHECY Aboriginal Diabetes Study
papers.abstract: Maxwell, Khurana et al. examine blood DNA methylation in the PROPHECY Aboriginal Diabetes Study. The study identifies discovery-level candidate methylation regions and pathways associated with diabetic kidney disease risk for future validation.

papers.title: Parsing altered brain connectivity in neurodevelopmental disorders by integrating graph-based normative modeling and deep generative networks
papers.abstract: Shen et al. introduce a brain imaging framework that builds a reference trajectory of neurotypical connectivity development. In children with autism, it identifies global neurodivergence associated with clinical assessments and regional maps that reveal individual differences.

papers.title: Nonlinear circular dichroism reveals the local Berry curvature
papers.abstract: The nonlinear high harmonic circular dichroism for crystals with broken time-reversal symmetry is found to be directly proportional to the local Berry curvature, and it can be directly probed via ultrafast all-optical measurements.

papers.title: Intermolecular decoupling of C 60 suppresses interfacial recombination in perovskite solar cells
papers.abstract: Interfacial recombination in perovskite solar cells is mitigated through a vapour-phase molecular passivation method using trialkylamines, disrupting C 60 packing. This approach results in a power conversion efficiency of up to 27.2% while maintaining stability.

papers.title: A general synthesis of tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides enabled by a dual-functional directing group
papers.abstract: Tryptophan-crosslinked macrocyclic peptides display interesting therapeutic properties; however, methods for their synthesis are limited. Now a Rh-catalysed process enables their synthesis through the development of a dual-function directing group that promotes C–H activation and C–N bond formation. The method provides access to a range of macrocycles, including pharmacophores of micitide 982 and tryglysin.

papers.title: Synthesis of chiral allylic amines through regio- and enantioselective homologation of enamines using Ni catalysis
papers.abstract: Chiral allylic amines are key building blocks in the synthesis of bioactive molecules. Now a regio- and enantioselective method for their synthesis is reported. The Ni-catalysed process proceeds through homologation of enamines by cross-coupling with alkynes, forming a range of chiral allylic amines in good yield and with excellent enantioselectivity.

papers.title: HIP: Hessian Interatomic Potentials without derivatives
papers.abstract: The authors introduce an extension of machine learning interatomic potentials that predicts molecular Hessians directly, improving accuracy and speed compared in transition-state searches, geometry optimization and vibrational analysis relative to Hessians from automatic differentiation.

papers.title: Human–artificial intelligence collaboration for comanaging epilepsy in real time
papers.abstract: A small epilepsy monitoring study shows that a moderated, large language model-based chat interface lets patients converse with their electroencephalography monitoring in real time, using a smartphone, and patient feedback cut seizure-detector false alarms by about 80% without clinician input.

papers.title: A multiview video–text model detects obstructive coronary stenosis and predicts 1-year cardiovascular events from angiography
papers.abstract: Harrabi et al. develop DeepCORO-CLIP, a multiview video–text model, to interpret coronary angiograms by detecting obstructive stenosis and predict 1-year cardiovascular events.

papers.title: Inhibition of endogenous TGF-β normalizes extracellular matrix deposition in hiPSC-derived fibroblasts
papers.abstract: Fibroblasts are mesenchymal cells with essential functions for connective tissue homeostasis and repair through the production and organization of the extracellular matrix (ECM). Most reconstructed skin models used in research and skin-related applications rely on fibroblasts to produce ECM. Despite their shared functions, human fibroblasts from different origins exhibit heterogeneity in age, morphotype, and localization. Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) offer a promising alternative by providing a consistent and scalable source of fibroblasts, overcoming the challenges of availability and variability. Here, we show that iPSC-derived fibroblasts (F-hiPSC) exhibit enhanced proliferative capacity and substantial functional differences compared to primary fibroblasts. Our aim was thus to comprehensively characterize F-hiPSCs in terms of fibroblast marker expression to benchmark their subtype identity, phenotype and ECM production. Secretome analysis also revealed that both Transforming Growth Factor-beta (TGF-β) abundance and activity were strongly increased in F-hiPSC, thereby enhancing ECM production and collagen I biosynthesis and affecting the maturation and assembly of collagen I fibers. By inhibiting the main TGF-β signaling receptor, we also unraveled the potential of modulating TGF-β signaling to normalize F-hiPSC ECM production.

papers.title: T-regulatory cell protection of progenitor cells from CD4 + T-cell-mediated cytotoxicity is essential for endogenous mouse digit-tip regeneration
papers.abstract: Regeneration of amputated digit tips in humans and mice relies on osteoclast-dependent bone erosion coupled with osteoblast-mediated bone replacement. Currently, little is known of the impact of lymphoid immune cells, i.e., T cells, B cells, and NK cells, on digit-tip regeneration. Using lymphoid-deficient mutant mice, we revealed lymphoid immunity as a net negative regulator of regeneration. CD8+ cells are thought to negatively regulate fracture repair; however, we showed that adoptive cell transfer (ACT) of CD8+ T cells into lymphoid-deficient hosts did not impact regeneration. In contrast, ACT of CD4+ T cells potently inhibited regeneration via osteoclast and osteoblast progenitor-cell cytotoxicity. CD4+ T-cell-mediated inhibition of regeneration was rescued by supplementation with T regulatory cells or recombinant RANKL, a mediator of osteoclast differentiation. ACT of IFN-γ-deficient CD4+ T cells abolished cytotoxic activity and rescued regeneration. Future strategies protecting endogenous progenitor cells could enhance human tissue repair and autologous stem-cell therapies.

papers.title: Development of a scoring system via an interpretable end-to-end neural network for prognostic stratification of patients with advanced melanoma
papers.abstract: We created an interpretable end-to-end neural network (ScoreNet) which can be used to develop an easy-to-implement scoring system for risk stratification. We applied it to data from 2711 patients with advanced melanoma across 5 trials that supported new drug approvals and developed a scoring system for overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). The scoring system was then validated in two separate trials. This score is a weighted summation based on eight baseline features (sum of longest diameter for all target lesions, lactate dehydrogenase, systemic immune inflammation index, hemoglobin, ECOG performance status, liver metastasis, pulse rate, and PD-L1 immunohistochemistry status). Using the score, patients can be classified into low, moderate, or high-risk categories of reduced OS and PFS. Risk stratification was demonstrated for patients treated with PD-1/PD-L1 inhibitors, chemotherapy, CTLA-4 inhibitors, BRAF or MEK inhibitors, and their combinations. ScoreNet-based risk stratification can be a new tool for clinical research/practice.

papers.title: Multidimensional continuous glucose monitoring metrics enable digital risk stratification across the diabetes spectrum
papers.abstract: Although continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) provides high-dimensional data, the usefulness of multimodal and diurnal glycemic profiles for disease characterization and risk stratification remains unknown. Here, in the iCanNet cohort of 90,757 participants, we examined the associations of 48 CGM-derived metrics with prediabetes, T2D, and T1D, compared to normoglycemia. We further employed Gaussian Mixture Model to define glycemic phenotypes and established digital glycemic risk score (DGRS) to quantify complication risks in T2D. Participants with prediabetes, T2D, or T1D exhibited distinct CGM signatures compared to normoglycemic individuals (all P < 0.001). Integration of top five metrics significantly improved diabetes classification, and calibration analyses showed agreement between predicted and observed risks. Four glycemic phenotypes were identified in T2D, with sustained hyperglycemia associated with a 59% increased risk of acute complications, and high glycemic variability associated with 75% and 41% higher risks of acute and chronic complications, respectively. The DGRS identified residual risk among patients achieving time in range ≥70%, reclassifying 25.0% and 22.3% of these individuals to high-risk groups for acute and chronic complications, respectively. In summary, this study revealed distinct CGM-derived signatures across diabetes statuses and established a multimodal framework for identifying high-risk individuals with T2D who may be overlooked by conventional biomarkers.

papers.title: Exploring PET and MRI brain networks across healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, and Alzheimer’s disease
papers.abstract: This study aimed to characterize population-level and individual-level metabolic and radiomics-derived structural brain networks across healthy controls (HC), mild cognitive impairment (MCI), and Alzheimer’s disease (AD) using multimodal PET and MRI. A total of 651 participants with both [18F]FDG PET and MRI were retrospectively included, with an external cohort of 45 participants used for validation. Thirty-two AD-relevant regions of interest were retained as network nodes and characterized using PET standardized uptake value ratios (SUVRs) and a selected MRI radiomics descriptor. Population-level networks were constructed using probability density function-based similarity with Jensen–Shannon divergence, and individualized perturbation networks were derived relative to an HC reference. Network-derived features were evaluated for prediction. Both SUVR-based and radiomics-based networks showed distinct patterns in MCI and AD compared with HC. Fused network features improved discrimination compared with either modality alone, achieving one-vs-rest AUCs of 0.894 [0.868–0.917] for HC, 0.888 [0.862–0.912] for AD, and 0.814 [0.783–0.844] for MCI. These findings indicate graded network disorganization across the HC–MCI–AD spectrum and support multimodal prediction.

papers.title: Model-dependent prompt effects challenge reliable deployment of medical LLMs in traditional Chinese medicine
papers.abstract: Although contemporary large language models (LLMs) have achieved satisfactory results in Western medical knowledge, their performance on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) remains underexplored, and the determinants of performance variation are poorly understood. We evaluated 16 LLMs under seven prompt strategies on 475 questions from the 2025 Taiwan national TCM licensing examination, a public benchmark of TCM knowledge. Without prompt engineering, accuracy ranged from 35.4% to 85.9%, with approximately half passing. Among the evaluated model versions, adjusted accuracy differed substantially when models were grouped by family (for example, Claude-family models, 84% vs. GPT-4, 43%); these family-grouped comparisons were descriptive because only 16 individual models were evaluated. Paired prompt analyses showed modest average absolute effects, ranging from a 2.03-percentage-point decrease with implicit CoT to a 3.04-percentage-point increase with explicit CoT. However, prompt–model interactions produced substantial model-level divergence: prompt optimization reversed failing performance in one model (87.4% vs. 49.7%) while reducing accuracy in others. No single prompt strategy yielded consistent benefits across the evaluated models. Among five selected lower-performing models evaluated under explicit CoT prompting, misunderstanding of foundational TCM concepts was the most frequent error. These findings indicate that reliable LLM deployment in TCM requires empirical validation of both model choice and prompt strategy: model selection strongly shapes baseline capability, while prompt-model interactions can materially alter performance.

papers.title: A “growth mindset of mental health” intervention increases the likelihood of initiating self-help on a mental health app: a randomized controlled trial
papers.abstract: Mental health apps hold potential to improve access to treatment, but engagement remains low. One barrier may be the belief that mental health cannot be meaningfully improved. In a randomized controlled trial (N = 252), we examined whether a brief growth-mindset-of-mental-health intervention—portraying mental health as improvable, not fixed—can initiate mental health app engagement among people with mental health needs. Participants completed baseline well-being measures (stress, anxiety and depression, and positive mental well-being) and were randomly assigned to the growth-mindset-of-mental-health or active control condition. Over the subsequent three months, we tracked whether they re-engaged with the app overall (i.e., completed at least a second self-help feature), and with features categorized as low-, moderate-, and high-intensity. Analyses revealed that participants in the growth-mindset condition (vs. control) with poorer baseline mental well-being (i.e., higher stress, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and lower positive mental well-being) were significantly more likely to show repeat app engagement. Moreover, those with higher anxiety and depressive symptoms were more likely to show repeat engagement with moderate-intensity features, while those experiencing higher stress and lower positive mental well-being were more likely to do so with both low- and moderate-intensity features. Together, these findings demonstrate the benefits of the growth-mindset intervention for successful initiation of self-help on a mental health app. Trial Registration: The trial was registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: NCT07071311) on July 25, 2025.

papers.title: AEGIS: an operational infrastructure for post-market governance of adaptive medical AI under US and EU regulatory frameworks
papers.abstract: Medical AI requires governance preserving safety during continuous improvement. FDA Predetermined Change Control Plans (PCCP) and EU post-market surveillance address iterative updates but lack operational tooling. We present AEGIS, an internal governance and post-market-monitoring infrastructure designed to support the documentation of predetermined governance pathways for PCCP and Medical Devices Regulation alignment. AEGIS comprises dataset assimilation and retraining, model monitoring, and conditional decision-making modules. It utilizes a four-category taxonomy (APPROVE, CONDITIONAL APPROVAL, CLINICAL REVIEW, REJECT) and an independent ALARM signal. Instantiating AEGIS for sepsis prediction (PhysioNet) and brain-tumor segmentation (BraTS) exercised all decision categories, successfully routing failures to the critical REJECT + ALARM state (no deployable model; released model at risk). On real cross-site data, drift detection ROC-AUC rose from 0.82 to 1.00, reliably triggering near 500-patient batches with zero false alarms. This proof-of-concept utilizes illustrative clinical models; drift scoring quantifies covariate shift only, leaving concept drift for future work.

papers.title: Scalable low-thermal-budget fabrication of suspended silicon nanowire devices
papers.abstract: Silicon nanowires (Si NWs) are versatile one-dimensional building blocks for gas and biochemical sensors, MEMS/NEMS physical transduction platforms, and integrated electronic devices because of their high surface-to-volume ratios and compatibility with semiconductor processing. A key limitation of conventional top-down fabrication is its reliance on furnace-based high-temperature steps, such as thermal oxidation and LPCVD, which can induce residual stress and constrain post-CMOS integration because of thermal-budget limits above 400 °C. Here, we present a furnace-free, low-thermal-budget fabrication approach for suspended Si NWs with a maximum process temperature of 180 °C. The process forms suspended Si NWs at the top surface of both bulk Si substrates and SOI substrates with a 2 µm device layer. The method defines a nanoscale Si surface protrusion and uses a conformal Cr sidewall coating to preserve linewidth during DRIE release. The process yields suspended Si NWs with critical dimensions down to 50 nm, aspect ratios of up to 100, and array pitches of 5 µm, while supporting integration into junctionless field-effect transistor architectures. Electrical measurements confirm ohmic behavior in two-terminal NW devices and demonstrate depletion-mode current modulation in side-gated junctionless FETs, with a threshold voltage of 24 V and approximately 40× current modulation. After nominal 2 nm Pd functionalization, single-NW devices exhibit repeatable 1% H2 sensing, producing near-complete current suppression of the p-type NW channel at sub-10 nW operating power. By eliminating furnace-based processing, the approach supports post-CMOS-compatible integration, avoids high-temperature stress-inducing process steps, and establishes a scalable platform for suspended Si NW devices.

papers.title: Enhanced electrochemically-directed oligonucleotide synthesis via porous silica thin-film for DNA data storage
papers.abstract: DNA-based data storage has emerged as a promising alternative for long-term information archiving and its implementation accelerates the development for on-chip large scale oligonucleotide synthesis. Among various technological routes, electrochemically directed synthesis offers exceptional synthesis-site density thanks to its compatibility with semiconductor microfabrication processes. Yet increasing density typically comes at the expense of reduced per-site oligonucleotide yield, compromising the practical utility of these synthesis platforms for reliable data recovery. Here we report a porous silica thin-film strategy in order to address this fundamental trade-off by substantially increasing the effective on-chip synthesis surface area while preserving spatial confinement during electrochemically generated acid-mediated deblocking. The porous thin-film, fabricated via a sacrificial templating approach, forms an interconnected high-surface-area porous network that enables efficient reagent transport and stable electrochemical control. The presented method enables an areal oligonucleotide yield of more than 1821 pmol/cm², which represents more than 11-fold enhancement compared to a planar silica substrate. Moreover, this platform achieves comparable error statistics of deletion, insertion and substitution compared to other laboratory-built DNA data writing systems. Using this platform, we demonstrated parallel synthesis of 121-nt oligonucleotides and successful encoding, writing and error-corrected recovery of digital information. These results establish a scalable strategy for high-yield on-chip DNA synthesis and provide a practical pathway towards integrated molecular data storage systems.

papers.title: Representation choice shapes the interpretation of protein conformational dynamics
papers.abstract: Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations provide detailed trajectories at the atomic level, but extracting interpretable and robust insights from these high-dimensional data remains challenging. Here, the authors introduce a geometrically grounded representation for analyzing protein backbone dynamics in MD simulations, showing that representation choice shapes the conformational organization, similarity relationships, and apparent transitions inferred from identical simulation data.

papers.title: Engineering an AgZnInS@ZnS/g-C₃N₄ hybrid heterostructure for enhanced green hydrogen production
papers.abstract: The engineering of composites based on quantum dots and 2D g-C₃N₄ has garnered increasing attention in catalysis for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Here, the authors report an AZIS@ZnS/g-C₃N₄ (CS QD/gCN) hybrid heterostructure that achieves overpotential and Tafel slope values close to those of Pt/C electrodes.

papers.title: All-optical generation of dense multi-GeV positron beams with longitudinal polarization
papers.abstract: The production of high-yield, high-energy, longitudinally polarized positron beams remains a pivotal challenge in advanced accelerator science. Laser-driven schemes offer an integrated pathway but typically yield only transverse polarization, or require pre-polarized electron beams, and struggle to efficiently accelerate positrons to high energies. Here we show an all-optical scheme that overcomes these limitations by integrating positron generation, acceleration, and spin manipulation into a single, coherent framework. In our design, an ultraintense circularly polarized laser pulse collides head–on with a counterpropagating unpolarized electron beam, initiating a robust Quantum Electrodynamics(QED) cascade. Within this cascade, positrons are generated via the nonlinear Breit–Wheeler(NBW) process directly inside the strong laser field. Although the positrons are born with transverse polarization, their spin orientations are random, resulting in zero net polarization. The same driving laser field accelerates the positrons to multi–GeV energies via direct laser acceleration and, through in-situ spin precession, rotating their initially random transverse polarizations into a common longitudinal direction simultaneously. Our Monte–Carlo simulations confirm that at normalized laser amplitude a0 = 1000 the scheme simultaneously achieves a high positron yield of 25.8, positrons/electrons (e+/e−), a high average longitudinal polarization (47.0%), and multi–GeV energies (up to  ~ 9 GeV), for positrons collected within 30°.

papers.title: Predicting delirium in critically Ill patients with cancer using interpretable machine learning
papers.abstract: Delirium is common in critically ill patients with cancer, but early recognition remains difficult and externally validated prediction tools are limited. We aimed to develop and externally validate interpretable machine learning models and identify clinically meaningful factors associated with delirium. We conducted a retrospective multicohort prediction study involving 20,596 adults with cancer admitted to intensive care: 5,686 patients from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV database were used for model development and internal validation, and 14,910 patients from the eICU Collaborative Research Database were used for external validation. Five machine learning models were evaluated using discrimination, calibration, and decision curve analysis. Predictor contributions were assessed using Shapley additive explanations. Here we show that the tabular foundation model provides the best internal discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.94), whereas extreme gradient boosting demonstrates the strongest external performance (0.93). Propofol exposure is the leading internal predictor, while Glasgow Coma Scale score is most influential externally. Additional predictors include antibiotic use, prolonged mechanical ventilation, greater physiological severity and organ dysfunction, potassium abnormalities, elevated bilirubin, older age, and insurance-related disadvantage. These findings indicate that baseline vulnerability and acute physiological insults jointly characterize delirium risk. Interpretable machine learning accurately identifies patients at increased delirium risk across two independent critical-care cohorts. The models may support earlier risk stratification and highlight potentially modifiable prevention targets, but prospective evaluation and clinical-impact testing are required before routine implementation. Delirium is a sudden state of confusion that often affects people with cancer who are critically ill. This study aimed to identify patients at risk early, so healthcare teams may be able to prevent or reduce its effects. We analyzed electronic health records from 20,596 adults with cancer treated in intensive care units and compared five computer-based prediction models. The models predicted delirium accurately in two large, independent patient databases. Important warning signs included older age, greater illness severity, infection, organ problems, abnormal potassium levels, longer use of breathing machines, and exposure to sedative medicines. These findings may help healthcare professionals recognize high-risk patients sooner and provide personalized monitoring and preventive care.

papers.title: Morphogenesis of a stratified cell mound at a vortex defect
papers.abstract: In cell monolayers with a vortex-like orientation defect, cells converge towards the core of the defect and form a highly organized three-dimensional mound. This mechanism may be relevant for morphogenesis and tumorigenesis.

papers.title: Chip-mediated manipulation of photonic quantum skyrmions
papers.abstract: Although photonic quantum skyrmions can be generated as entangled or single-photon states, a means to switch between the two is required for quantum information processing. Now, entangled skyrmions and their manipulation on chip is realized.

papers.title: Solid-state emissive acceptors enable thermally accessible radiative pathways for efficient organic solar cells
papers.abstract: Solid-state emissive guest acceptors enhance organic solar cells by establishing thermally accessible radiative pathways, significantly reducing non-radiative voltage loss end enabling ternary blend devices with a certified power conversion efficiency of 20.84%.

papers.title: Stable deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes with reduced efficiency roll-off via accelerated exciton utilization
papers.abstract: Deep-blue organic light-emitting diodes leveraging phosphor-assisted TADF-sensitized fluorescence enable accelerated exciton dynamics, resulting in devices with an external quantum efficiency of 35.9% and an LT80 lifetime of 632 h.

papers.title: Photocatalytic tetrapeptides for enantioselective visible light-induced transformations
papers.abstract: Upon irradiation with visible light ( λ = 425 nm), a tetrapeptide with a C-terminal photocatalytic site and an N-terminal site for substrate recognition promotes photochemical deracemization and enantioselective [2 + 2] photocycloaddition reactions. The required spatial proximity of catalyst and substrate is corroborated by NMR spectroscopy studies and molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Scrambling-free synthesis of heteroleptic silylium ions by halide abstraction from halosilanes
papers.abstract: Access to silylium ions with three different substituents has remained elusive owing to substituent scrambling under established synthetic methods. Now, harnessing the Lewis superacidity of halogen-substituted silylium ions, a broadly applicable protocol for synthesizing such heteroleptic silylium ions without substituent redistribution by halide abstraction from readily available halosilanes is reported.

papers.title: One-step skeletal editing of oxetanes to thietanes using thiourea
papers.abstract: Four-membered heterocycles are privileged scaffolds in medicinal chemistry, yet valuable thietanes remain underexplored compared with widely studied oxetanes and azetidines. Now a one-step skeletal editing strategy is reported that directly converts oxetanes into thietanes using thiourea.

papers.title: China’s centralized wastewater treatment system reaches efficiency limits in tackling water scarcity
papers.abstract: This study finds that centralized wastewater treatment systems in China have limited potential to simultaneously achieve cost recovery and reduce water stress.

papers.title: Less can be more for predicting properties with large language models
papers.abstract: Researchers show that large language models cannot learn from spatial coordinates regardless of model or data scale. Specialized geometric neural networks consistently outperform language models for material property prediction.

papers.title: A health-system-scale, episode-resolved multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia
papers.abstract: Using longitudinal data from 52,236 patients with cancer, this study created a multimodal atlas of cancer cachexia, demonstrating that weight loss episodes are linked to systemic serologic signatures and specific tumor genotypes and can be predicted using integrated clinical and molecular data, enabling earlier identification.

papers.title: Population-scale reconstruction of menopause dynamics reveals a physiological cliff at the final menstrual period
papers.abstract: By using a novel computational framework, a cross-sectional analysis on laboratory data from two independent cohorts reveals that the final menstrual period marks an abrupt, multisystem physiological shift, with sex hormone changes beginning more than 10 years before menopause onset.

papers.title: Lung derived extracellular vesicles have distinct pro-repair effects, depending on the age of their source tissue
papers.abstract: Many age-related lung diseases encompass aberrant repair mechanisms. To develop novel treatments for these diseases, it is critical to understand how biology and repair signals are altered in aged lungs. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) carry bioactive signals reflecting their source tissue; therefore, we used precision-cut lung slices (PCLS)-derived EVs as tools to investigate differences in lung biology and repair signals that occur upon ageing and injury. We compared the physicochemical properties and biological content of EVs obtained from uninjured and injured, young and aged mouse PCLS. Treatment with EVs from young, uninjured (YU) PCLS decreased apoptotic cells in both young and aged spatially acid-injured (AIR)-PCLS. YU EVs increased the percentage of alveolar progenitor cells in aged AIR-PCLS, indicating that aged lungs retain the capacity to mount a repair response, if provided with the right biological cues. Small RNA sequencing revealed the miRNA content of each EV group is altered, depending on the physiological conditions of their source tissue. Bioinformatic analysis of the target genes regulated by differentially expressed miRNAs identified enrichment of genes required for lung development and repair. These findings provide mechanistic insight into the content of young versus aged lung EVs, that could be leveraged for regenerative medicine strategies.

papers.title: AI-based hourly prediction of emergency department demand integrating social determinants of health
papers.abstract: Emergency department (ED) crowding is associated with delayed treatment and increased mortality, and proactive staffing requires reliable short-term demand forecasts. Most operational models rely on temporal or weather patterns but may insufficiently capture underlying population vulnerability. We evaluated whether community-level social determinants of health (SDoH) improve the prediction of near-term ED demand compared with weather factors using XGBOOST, and developed an interpretable model to inform resource allocation. The study included 213,138 encounters aggregated into 22,883 hourly observations at a tertiary teaching hospital in Wuhan, China. Neighbourhoods differed markedly in age structure and diagnostic profiles, indicating heterogeneous healthcare needs across the catchment area. Models incorporating dynamic SDoH features consistently outperformed those using weather variables alone. Overall, the composite model achieved the best performance with an RMSE of 3.48 visits per hour, an MAE of 2.62 visits per hour, and an R² of 0.68. Mean absolute prediction errors were approximately 2 to 3 patients per hour across scenarios, suggesting practical utility for short-term staffing and capacity planning. The study indicates that community-level social vulnerability may provide more informative signals than weather conditions for anticipating short-term ED demand. Integrating SDoH-informed forecasts into hospital operations may enable earlier staffing adjustments and help mitigate crowding-related risks.

papers.title: Technology-Enabled Hospital Discharge: Consolidated Framework of Implementation Research-Informed Qualitative Study of Stakeholder Perspectives on Digital Solutions
papers.abstract: Hospital discharge is a complex, time-consuming process that requires coordination across multiple stakeholders. Technology-enabled solutions may improve this process, but their implementation depends on alignment with user needs, workflows, and care contexts. We explored stakeholder perspectives on six candidate digital solutions for hospital discharge as part of a wider service improvement project. We interviewed forty-three purposively sampled healthcare workers, operations staff, patients, and caregivers. We introduced participants to ward-based teleconsultation, smart glasses, AI bots, medication collection boxes, digital discharge documentation, and AI-assisted discharge summary drafting, and explored perceived value, risks and implementation requirements. We analysed the data using a hybrid deductive–inductive approach informed by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR). Participants described discharge as poorly communicated, lacking transparency, and often prolonged. We identified eleven subthemes under the five CFIR domains. Participants viewed technologies more favourably when they could see practical value, when the technology was familiar from other contexts, and when it could integrate with existing workflows while preserving the relational aspects of care. Concerns centred on safety, privacy, equity, workflow disruption, burden, and loss of human interaction. Successful implementation requires a clear value proposition, workflow integration, stakeholder co-design, and early attention to training, governance, accountability, and equity.

papers.title: Photography-based dental plaque detection and report generation among preschool children using PlaqueSAM
papers.abstract: Dental plaque is the primary etiological factor for common oral diseases such as dental caries and gingivitis, particularly affecting susceptible populations including children. Preventing plaque-induced dental diseases in pediatric patients remains a global challenge as certain plaque regions are often missed during daily cleaning. Early detection and removal of plaque are essential but often difficult to achieve consistently. A routine monitoring tool that visualizes plaque accumulation on primary teeth could allow parents to actively track their children’s oral health, enabling timely prevention and intervention for dental caries and periodontal diseases. Inspired by these, we present PlaqueSAM, an automatic plaque detection system using intraoral photographs captured by smartphones. By uploading six images captured with the assistance of alignment overlays, PlaqueSAM can generate a comprehensive plaque detection report with visual references. PlaqueSAM was developed using 3402 prospectively collected intraoral photographs from 567 preschool children across 11 kindergartens in Hong Kong using a three-stage training strategy based on a multi-task learning paradigm. The performance of PlaqueSAM was quantitatively evaluated on 81 children, achieving sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy of 76.58, 82.47, and 79.60%, respectively. These findings suggest that PlaqueSAM may support future plaque screening workflows without requiring disclosing agents or plastic retractors typically used by dental professionals, although home-based use requires further validation under real-world user-operated conditions.
