With further real-world validation, PlaqueSAM may support dynamic monitoring of children’s daily plaque accumulation and cleaning, thereby contributing to the advancement of teledentistry and promoting children’s oral health remotely, conveniently, and at a lower cost.

papers.title: An agentic AI system for multi-framework communication coding
papers.abstract: Clinical communication is central to patient outcomes, yet large-scale annotation of patient–provider conversations remains labor-intensive, inconsistent, and difficult to scale. Existing large language model (LLM)–based approaches typically rely on single-task systems with limited robustness across communication frameworks and clinical domains. In this study, we developed MOSAIC, a Multi-framewOrk Structured Agentic AI system for scalable Clinical Communication coding. MOSAIC combines dynamically few-shot prompting, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and a LangGraph-based multi-agent workflow for planning, annotation, and verification. Performance was evaluated against gold-standard annotations produced by trained human coders. MOSAIC was developed on 54 annotated transcripts and evaluated on 120 transcripts spanning rheumatology and obstetrics/gynecology (OB/GYN). On the evaluation set, MOSAIC achieved an overall weighted F1 score of 95.6%. Performance was highest in rheumatology (F1 = 95.9%) and strongest for bias and patient behaviors categories (F1 = 96.4% and 96.1%, respectively). These results demonstrate the potential of multi-framework AI systems for reliable clinical communication analysis.

papers.title: Macroporosity and Stiffness Tailored Hydrogels Enhance Bone Formation via Inside Out and Outside In Regeneration
papers.abstract: Synthetic hydrogels support bone regeneration, but their nanoporous structure restricts cell infiltration. Here, the authors developed macroporous hydrogels that enhance cell infiltration and bone regeneration.

papers.title: Kinetic retention of an anisotropic lattice response in pure FAPbI 3 by flash infrared annealing
papers.abstract: Far-from-equilibrium crystallization accesses metastable states beyond equilibrium phase diagrams but remains underexplored in halide perovskites. Here, the authors show that sub-second flash-infrared processing enables the kinetic retention of an anisotropic metastable lattice state in pure FAPbI₃, yielding improved photoluminescence and stability.

papers.title: Development and application of a smartphone-based thermal contrast amplification reader for photothermal lateral flow immunoassays
papers.abstract: The high cost and poor portability of external infrared thermal imagers have limited the widespread adoption of photothermal lateral flow immunoassays (PT-LFIAs) in on-site testing. To address this, we developed a smartphone-based handheld Thermal Contrast Amplification (TCA) Reader, eliminating the need for costly external hardware. Compared with existing recent external thermal imager-based PT-LFIA readout, this reader integrates a selected thermal-sensor-equipped smartphone, a motorized laser module, Bluetooth-enabled control, and a fixed 3D-printed holder into a compact device. The reader enables automated thermal signal acquisition with a same-strip measurement CV below 1% and supports multiple PT-LFIA formats. Using Au@Ag core-shell nanoparticles (Au@Ag NPs) as reliable photothermal labels, the handheld TCA reader-based PT-LFIAs (hT-PT-LFIAs) offers higher sensitivity compared to conventional LFIAs. The hT-PT-LFIAs can be used for the multiplex detection of viral antigens (Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2), small molecule drugs (morphine, methamphetamine, ketamine) and nucleic acids (HPV 16/18), demonstrating versatility across various LFIA formats, good clinical performance in training cohort, and high repeatability for small molecule assay. By seamlessly integrating micro-engineering, nanotechnology, and smartphone-based sensing, this work provides a low-cost, portable, and broadly applicable PT-LFIAs detection strategy that bridges a critical technological gap.

papers.title: Supramolecular structuring of nanoparticle ligand shells revealed by liquid-phase AFM
papers.abstract: Polymer grafts on nanocrystal surfaces are crucial for functionalities like biocompatibility, yet their complete structural characterization under realistic conditions remains challenging. Here, the authors employ high-resolution AFM and CG-MD simulations to reveal persistent patchy morphologies in well-solvated grafts, suggesting widespread surface heterogeneity that could influence nanocrystal self-assembly.

papers.title: Mechanism and process optimization of lithium extraction from alkaline solutions using oxybenzone/aliquat 336
papers.abstract: Effective lithium recovery from the mother liquor after lithium precipitation can reduce waste and enhance the supply capacity of lithium resources. Here, the authors report a mixed extraction system based on oxybenzone and Aliquat 336 for lithium recovery from alkaline solutions, demonstrating 99% recovery from mother liquor through a two-stage countercurrent extraction.

papers.title: A targeted ionic iron/platinum-based precatalyst for bias-dependent reconstruction in alkaline water splitting
papers.abstract: Efficient alkaline water splitting requires catalysts for both the oxygen-evolution reaction (OER) and the hydrogen-evolution reaction (HER). Precatalyst reconstruction offers a route to generating active surfaces under operating conditions. Here, we report an ionic iron/platinum-based precatalyst reservoir for alkaline water splitting, prepared by combining anionic iron(III) phthalocyanine-4,4′,4″,4‴-tetrasulfonate (FeTSPc³⁻) with cationic [Pt(NH₃)₄]²⁺ (TP²⁺) species. The resulting FeTSPc/TP ionic solid has limited solubility in alkaline electrolyte and supplies Fe- and Pt-derived species under electrochemical bias. Rather than acting as a persistent molecular bifunctional catalyst, FeTSPc/TP undergoes bias-dependent reconstruction on nickel-foam electrodes. Under anodic conditions, Fe-derived species are associated with the nickel surface, producing a Ni–Fe (oxy)hydroxide-type OER-active layer. Under cathodic conditions, Pt-derived species generate Pt-containing deposits that promote the HER. Compared with bare Ni foam, the FeTSPc/TP system decreases the OER overpotential by approximately 200 mV and the HER overpotential by approximately 80 mV under the tested conditions. The analyses support the formation of distinct catalyst-derived surface deposits at the two electrodes. These results show that a single ionic precatalyst reservoir can deliver different catalyst-forming components to anodic and cathodic surfaces, providing a proof-of-concept strategy for bias-dependent reconstruction during alkaline water splitting.

papers.title: A photoinduced, FeX 3 -catalyzed, stereo- and regio-selective halofunctionalization of olefins with MX n via a radical-polar crossover reaction
papers.abstract: The classical reaction for the halofunctionalization of olefins involves hazardous and highly toxic molecular halogens. Here, the authors report the FeX 3 -catalyzed halofunctionalization of alkenes with MX n at room temperature, under visible-light irradiation, and without strong oxidants.

papers.title: Modular multifunctional 5HP2O linkers for the versatile assembly of protein-oligonucleotide conjugates
papers.abstract: While the demand for advanced biotherapeutics grows, current protein conjugation methods face challenges with stability and complexity. Here, the authors introduce 5-hydroxy-1,5-dihydro-2H-pyrrol-2-ones (5HP2O) as modular, stable, versatile linkers for assembling multi-functional protein-oligonucleotide conjugates, demonstrating enhanced hydrolytic resistance and stability.

papers.title: Priming of human iPSCs with doxorubicin causes genome-wide transcriptional reprogramming and functional impairments in iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes
papers.abstract: How Doxorubicin (Dox) mediated damage to stem cells or cardiomyocytes contributes to cardiotoxicity and cardiac regeneration is unclear. Using a human iPSC-based model together with corresponding iPSC-derived cardiomyocytes (iCMs) revealed that iPSCs are much more sensitive against single short pulse-treatments with Dox than iCMs. Major mitochondrial impairments such as increased mitochondrial fragmentation, loss of mitochondrial membrane potential, reduced ATP levels, and altered mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) organization, yet neither increased ROS formation, nuclear DNA damage response, nor apoptosis were detected in Dox-treated iPSCs. Whole genome transcriptome profiling revealed major differences in the transcriptional response to Dox including downregulation of genes regulating cellular homeostasis and energy metabolism. Dox exposure at the iPSC stage, termed priming here, shifts the global transcriptional landscape of iCMs towards reduced cardiac muscle regeneration, energy metabolism, muscle contraction, and increased fibrosis. Functionally, priming caused iCMs to ‘memorize’ this early Dox treatment resulting in reduced ATP levels, altered mtDNA organization, and in impaired contractility and oscillating Ca2+ handling. We propose that Dox-induced mitochondrial dysfunction and transcriptional priming in stem cells alters durably cardiac and bioenergetic properties of its progeny which may impair the regenerative capacity after differentiation. This may be of particular relevance for children and teenagers undergoing chemotherapy.

papers.title: FHIR-AgentEval: a modular sandbox for benchmarking clinical LLM agents with memory-augmented configurations
papers.abstract: Healthcare data exchange increasingly relies on HL7 FHIR, but FHIR’s implementation complexity creates barriers for clinical workflows. Large language model (LLM) agents could bridge this gap by translating natural language requests into structured FHIR operations, yet their reliability remains unproven. We present FHIR-AgentEval, an extensible evaluation sandbox comprising 43 modular tasks for benchmarking LLM agents on realistic appointment management and genetic testing workflows. Each task executes against a resettable FHIR server with custom deterministic validation of both agent responses and resulting server state. We run an ablation study of five agent configurations, varying access to an on-demand FHIR R4 specifications server and long-term memory trained with or without specification grounding. Across four experimental settings, memory consistently improves task success and reduces strategic failures such as incorrect tool selection and resource-type confusion. On held-out tasks, the best memory configuration improves success by 9.1% over baseline, offering a potential pathway toward more robust clinical deployment.

papers.title: Longitudinal actigraphy reveals healthy maturation of preterm infants in the neonatal intensive care unit
papers.abstract: Approximately one in ten live births is preterm ( < 37 weeks gestational age), placing these infants at elevated risk because of immature physiology. Analysis of movement patterns in the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit (NICU) is essential for detecting complications, yet current monitoring approaches remain limited. Using routine photoplethysmography (PPG), we extracted movement bouts from 65 preterm infants (47 without health complications, 18 with severe neurological conditions) across 50 days using a validated algorithm. Movement actigraphy was summarized using three novel metrics: (1) percent time moving per day across postmenstrual age, (2) daily distributions of movement durations quantified by power law exponents, and (3) ultradian movement cycles across 24 hours. While percent time moving did not change with age, power law exponents scaled linearly with age, indicating longer movements with maturation. Daily movement activity revealed 3-hour ultradian cycles corresponding to NICU feeding schedules, alongside an anticipatory rise in spontaneous motor activity before feeding. Infants with neurological complications, including two individual case studies, showed deviations in activity patterns when compared to uncomplicated infants. These results suggest that longitudinal movement tracking using routine sensors reveals systematic activity patterns and offers a scalable clinical tool for evaluation of health in this high-risk population.

papers.title: VOICE-AE: automated CTCAE scoring from ambient clinical audio using speech recognition and large language models
papers.abstract: Treatment-related adverse event documentation is labor-intensive and subject to inter-observer variability. We developed and evaluated VOICE-AE, a multi-stage pipeline integrating automatic speech recognition, speaker diarization and large language models (LLMs) for automated extraction and grading of Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) toxicities from clinician-patient audio recordings. Encounters of prostate cancer patients undergoing radiotherapy were recorded and processed through VOICE-AE. Six blinded human raters independently graded 10 genitourinary/gastrointestinal toxicities from the same transcripts; hierarchical clustering identified an expert-rater subgroup that established the consensus reference standard. A total of 31 patients (39 encounters) were enrolled, yielding 390 encounter–toxicity assessments, of which 300 (76.9%) carried a reference grade of 0. Six-rater Krippendorff alpha was 0.677 for ordinal grading. Against reference standard, VOICE-AE achieved a mean weighted kappa of 0.717 and Krippendorff alpha of 0.669. Exact CTCAE grade match was 82.6% and within-one-grade accuracy 99.2%; because grade 0 predominated, a trivial classifier always predicting grade 0 would achieve 76.9% and 93.6% respectively. Performance was weaker at the grades that drive clinical action (grade 1 F1 0.58; grade 2 F1 0.57), and binary detection sensitivity was 77.8% with specificity 89.0% and precision 68.0%. In a like-for-like comparison restricted to the three expert-cluster raters, mean weighted kappa between VOICE-AE and those experts (0.666) fell just below agreement among the experts themselves (0.681). VOICE-AE performed within the range of inter-expert agreement, supporting the feasibility of automated, post-encounter AE documentation. Accuracy at grade ≥2 and detection of severe toxicity remain unproven.

papers.title: A bioengineered model of human placental exposure to environmental metals during pregnancy
papers.abstract: A vascularized microphysiological system that mimics the human maternal–fetal interface is used to simulate exposure to environmental metals and investigate the mechanisms of placental toxicity and transport during pregnancy.

papers.title: Light-driven biohybrid microrobots for contact-enhanced photoenzymatic degradation of plastic debris
papers.abstract: Light-driven microrobots enable autonomous pollutant remediation in water. Here, the authors develop light-driven biohybrid microrobots that switch between clustered and motile states, enhancing photoenzymatic degradation of polylactic acid in water.

papers.title: Stem cell-laden rigid-flexible bioscaffold for neural regeneration and functional recovery after spinal cord injury
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury remains a major challenge owing to restricted neural regeneration and complex neuroimmune responses. Here, the authors developed a multifunctional bio scaffold that promotes nerve regeneration, modulates immune responses, and improves recovery after spinal cord injury.

papers.title: Sub-nanosecond structural dynamics of the martensitic transformation in Ni-Mn-Ga
papers.abstract: A time-resolved X-ray diffraction study of a femtosecond laser-induced martensitic transformation in Ni-Mn-Ga reveals a transformation time of approximately 90 ps, an upper limit set by the duration of the synchrotron probe pulse, with the transformation possibly occurring faster.

papers.title: Vacuum-compatible phase engineering enables high-efficiency and color-pure green perovskite light-emitting diodes
papers.abstract: Vacuum deposition offers a scalable, industry-compatible route for perovskite optoelectronics, yet efficient and spectrally stable emission remains limited by uncontrolled crystallization and defect-mediated nonradiative recombination. Here, we incorporate phenethylammonium bromide into a co-evaporated cesium bromide and lead bromide emissive layer for green vacuum-deposited perovskite light-emitting diodes. Phenethylammonium bromide regulates crystallization, modifies the local coordination environment, suppresses excessive grain growth, and improves film uniformity, thereby reducing trap-assisted recombination and enhancing radiative efficiency. The optimized devices achieve a maximum external quantum efficiency of 10.2%, a current efficiency of 36.5 cd A−1, a power efficiency of 35.8 lm W−1, and a luminance above 12,600 cd m−2. The emission peaks at 518 nm with a full width at half maximum of 20 nm and remains spectrally stable under varying drive conditions. The devices exhibit an operational lifetime of 4388 s at an initial luminance of 500 cd m−2.

papers.title: Flexible, stretchable and sustainable paper electronics enabled by ultraviolet laser-induced graphene
papers.abstract: The proliferation of short-lifetime consumer electronics has intensified the global electronic waste challenge. Paper, as an abundant and eco-friendly material, offers an attractive platform for sustainable electronics. Here we report a simple, additive-free, and ambient-condition approach to fabricate paper electronics by directly patterning laser-induced graphene (LIG) circuitry on lignin-rich kraft paper using a 355 nm UV pulsed laser. Under optimized conditions, the porous LIG electrode exhibits a sheet resistance of 147 ± 5 Ω sq−1, a thickness of 43 µm, and an ablation depth of 20–30 µm, while maintaining stable electrical performance after 1000 bending or stretching cycles. We demonstrate paper-based LIG devices including flexible and stretchable electronic circuits, eco-friendly photodetectors, and electrothermal transducers. The compatibility of direct laser writing with roll-to-roll manufacturing provides a pathway toward scalable and low-cost production. These results establish paper-based LIG as a sustainable platform for flexible electronics, disposable sensors, and soft robotic systems.

papers.title: Differentiated skeletal myotubes coupled with bimodal biosensing for dynamic functional evaluation of inflammatory myotube dysfunction
papers.abstract: Inflammatory skeletal muscle atrophy is a growing clinical challenge, driven by chronic inflammatory conditions and life-threatening illnesses that cause progressive muscle loss. This condition leads to premature muscle fatigue and a decline in muscle function, highlighting the necessity for highly sensitive diagnostic methods to detect impairment prior to the occurrence of structural damage. Conventional diagnostic methods, including electromyography, serum biomarker assays, and medical imaging, often fail to detect early and subtle alterations in myotube electrophysiological responsiveness because of limited temporal accuracy and insufficient target specificity. Furthermore, these techniques are limited in resolving dynamic electrophysiological fluctuations as well as characterizing the coupling between electrical signaling and intracellular calcium dynamics. Herein, we have developed an integrated bimodal biosensing platform that combines microelectrode array (MEA)-based electrophysiological recording with high-resolution, fluorescence-based calcium imaging. This platform performs coordinated and real-time tracking of extracellular field potentials and intracellular calcium transients across networks of differentiated C2C12 myotubes. Using an in vitro model of LPS-induced inflammatory skeletal muscle atrophy, LPS exposure progressively disrupted spontaneous electrical firing, field potential amplitude, and intracellular calcium transients in a concentration- and time-dependent manner. Diclofenac, a clinically applied anti-inflammatory agent, effectively maintained both electrophysiological function and calcium homeostasis in myotubes under inflammatory stress. Therefore, our bimodal platform functions as a robust, real-time preclinical tool for the detection of incipient inflammatory myopathy. Its integrated capabilities enable the precise quantification of drug responses and the scalable screening of therapeutic candidates, thereby establishing a versatile, translationally-oriented platform for the investigation of skeletal muscle atrophy mechanisms and interventions.

papers.title: Conformational heterogeneity and vibrational signatures of dAMP in aqueous solution revealed by high-accuracy machine-learning potentials
papers.abstract: Nucleotides are fundamental building blocks of life, but their behavior in water remains underexplored. Here, the authors develop neural network potentials through an active-learning protocol to study the structural and vibrational properties of 2’-deoxyadenosine 5’-monophosphate (dAMP) in aqueous solution, showing that it populates a mixture of conformations and proposing a framework for studying conformational heterogeneity in biomolecules.

papers.title: Unsupervised probing critical transitions in complex systems using generative diffusion models
papers.abstract: Critical transitions can irreversibly change complex systems, making anticipation a fundamental challenge. Machine learning is increasingly used for early warning, but many approaches require transition labels or control information. Probabilistic time-series forecasting models naturally produce predictive uncertainty by generating future trajectories from observations. Here we show that this uncertainty changes with system dynamics near critical transitions. Across three networked systems, uncertainty patterns depend on model architecture and system dynamics. Among the four models, the diffusion model that explicitly estimates the history-dependent endpoint variance of the forward diffusion process consistently exhibits a localized uncertainty collapse across the tested systems. Controlled analyses link the collapse to reduced diversity among generated futures and to transition mechanisms and dynamical regimes represented in training data. Mediterranean Sea data show similar predictive-uncertainty changes near transitions in empirical systems. Beyond quantifying forecast reliability, predictive uncertainty could therefore be further developed as a label-free complement to existing early-warning approaches for tracking dynamical changes in complex systems.

papers.title: Anthropomorphic phantom dosimetry and validation of 150–200 MeV very high-energy electron radiotherapy at CERN
papers.abstract: Very high-energy electrons could treat deep-seated tumours, but simulations are rarely validated above 100 MeV. Here, the authors characterise 150 and 200 MeV beams at CERN and show that simulations reproduce measured 200 MeV dose distributions in an anthropomorphic head-and-neck phantom, with gamma pass rates of 98.7–99.9% using 1%/1 mm criteria.

papers.title: Child health service coverage estimation using routine health data from Ghana’s Eastern Region
papers.abstract: Johnson et al. use data routinely collected by Ghanaian health facilities to estimate vaccination and diarrhoeal service coverage amongst children aged under 1 year. Their findings show that the variability and proportion of implausible estimates increase at the level of individual health facilities as compared to higher administrative levels.

papers.title: Sub-national estimates of visceral leishmaniasis and optimisation of geographical accessibility to treatment centres in Kenya
papers.abstract: Mutono et al. combine nationwide surveillance data, small-area disease mapping, and geospatial accessibility modelling to characterise visceral leishmaniasis burden and treatment access in Kenya. They identify highly localised hotspots and show that strategically locating a small number of additional treatment centres substantially improves access to care.

papers.title: Reversible Sn 4+ /Sn 0 anode for high-energy-density flow batteries
papers.abstract: Tin-based aqueous flow batteries offer high-capacity anodes due to the potential four-electron redox reactions, but irreversible Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ electrochemistry has hindered battery development. Now it has been shown that iodide-mediated intermediate complexes enable reversible Sn 4+ /Sn 2+ conversion and four-electron Sn 4+ /Sn 0 chemistry, yielding a high anolyte energy density and stable long-term operation.

papers.title: Order from chaos with adaptive circuits on quantum hardware
papers.abstract: Controlling quantum chaos requires using measurement and feedback that survive noise and decoherence. Such control is now achieved in a superconducting quantum processor and reveals a critical transition between quantum and classical dynamics.

papers.title: Phase control of interfering stimulated Raman pathways in the XUV regime
papers.abstract: Researchers modulate population transfer from the helium ground state to a metastable state by controlling the relative phase between two interfering stimulated Raman pathways through the continuum, demonstrating phase-coherent control in the extreme ultraviolet.

papers.title: High-entropy molecular contacts enable high-efficiency and stable perovskite solar cells
papers.abstract: High-entropy molecular contacts made by blending self-assembled molecules improve hole transport through diverse packing modes. Solar cells incorporating these contacts achieve a certified power conversion efficiency of 27.31% and negligible loss after 1,300 h of operation at 85 °C.

papers.title: Advancing chemical reaction prediction in data-scarce drug discovery with active and geometric deep learning
papers.abstract: Researchers pair active learning with geometric deep learning to predict the outcome and site selectivity of chemical reactions from scarce data, guiding experiments that accelerate drug discovery and expand accessible chemical space.

papers.title: Limited agricultural gains but high flood risk from global wetland reclamation
papers.abstract: As food demand increases, global wetlands are being reclaimed as croplands; however, these reclaimed croplands are not only less productive, but also face substantially higher flood exposure. This dual vulnerability highlights the urgency of balancing food security with wetland conservation.

papers.title: AI-assisted scoping review of code sharing in clinical prediction model research
papers.abstract: An analysis of code availability in the open-access published literature shows that code sharing in clinical prediction models remains limited and reveals significant variability in practices and documentation quality.

papers.title: Human adult and pediatric multimodal transcriptomic atlas of progression from pressure-loaded to failing right ventricle
papers.abstract: Kuznetsov et al. present a multi-modal transcriptomic atlas of the human right ventricle, revealing a two-phase progression from pressure loading to failure, with erosion of tissue-protective programs preceding focal fibrotic and vascular remodeling.

papers.title: What closed-loop insulin delivery can — and cannot — teach us
papers.abstract: Closed-loop insulin delivery is one of the great success stories of autonomous medicine. Its legacy, however, is not a universal blueprint, but the recognition that each closed-loop system must be designed around the biology, risks and lived realities of each condition.

papers.title: A scoping review of digital health technologies in glycogen storage diseases
papers.abstract: Glycogen storage diseases (GSDs) are rare inherited metabolic disorders requiring complex management. Digital health technologies (DHTs) offer solutions for improving care delivery, yet their implementation remains poorly characterised. This scoping review systematically mapped DHT applications in GSDs following PRISMA-ScR guidelines, searching four databases through June 2026. We identified 44 studies with 662 participants across 17 GSD subtypes, revealing geographic concentration in Europe (48%), focus on hepatic subtypes (59%), and predominant use of continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) (66%). Five themes of DHT in GSD research emerged: intervention evaluation, communication enhancement, clinical monitoring, population surveillance, and technology development. Critical gaps included underrepresentation of muscle subtypes and minimal research in movement behaviour and psychosocial evaluation. Glucose-centric DHT use predominates in research; whilst clinically valuable, this neglects holistic health monitoring. Future research should prioritise comprehensive digital ecosystems integrating metabolic, behavioural, and psychosocial monitoring to optimise care for all individuals with GSDs.

papers.title: Early prediction of prolonged ICU stay in sepsis patients using an explainable hybrid deep learning model
papers.abstract: Sepsis remains a leading cause of intensive care unit (ICU) admission and is frequently associated with prolonged ICU stay, which contributes to increased morbidity, healthcare utilization, and strain on critical care resources. Despite widespread use, existing clinical severity scores inadequately capture the individual risk of prolonged ICU stay in sepsis. We developed a hybrid deep learning (FT-TabNet) model with an adaptive gated fusion framework to predict prolonged ICU stay (>4 days) using 17 routinely collected Sequential Organ Failure Assessment (SOFA)-based features available within the first 24 hours of ICU admission. Model development and internal validation were performed using the MIMIC-IV dataset, with external validation conducted in a single-center cohort from Chungbuk National University Hospital (CBNUH) and Chungnam National University Hospital (CNUH), South Korea. The hybrid model showed strong discriminative performance in internal validation, achieving an AUROC of 0.848, and consistent performance across the external validation cohort, with modest variability, achieving an AUROC of 0.823 in the CBNUH and 0.781 in the CNUH cohort. SHAP-based explainability enabled transparent, patient-level interpretation of key contributors to prolonged ICU stay risk. These findings suggest that an explainable hybrid deep learning approach can help clinicians to identify patients at risk of prolonged ICU stay early in sepsis, using routine clinical data to support clinical decision-making and ICU resource allocation.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence for opportunistic osteoporosis screening on chest radiographs
papers.abstract: We developed an artificial intelligence model (AI-OsRM) to predict osteoporosis and reduced bone mineral density (BMD) from chest radiographs (CXR) and evaluated its performance and clinical utility across three external cohorts. AI-OsRM was developed using 46,478 paired CXR and dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) examinations from 26,757 patients collected at a tertiary referral hospital between 2016 and 2022, using a ResNet-based architecture with masked autoencoder pretraining. External validation was performed in three independent cohorts, including a temporally separated hospital cohort (SNUH; n = 6391) and two large health checkup cohorts (HPC, n = 24,132; YSMC, n = 122,535). In the SNUH cohort, AI-OsRM achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) of 0.88 (95% CI: 0.87–0.89) for both osteoporosis and reduced BMD. In the health checkup cohorts, AUROCs for osteoporosis detection were 0.93 (95% CI: 0.92–0.93) in HPC and 0.92 (95% CI: 0.92–0.92) in YSMC. Simulation analyses demonstrated that AI-OsRM–based prescreening could reduce DXA utilization by approximately 50% while maintaining detection of 98-99% of osteoporosis cases and 80–90% of reduced BMD cases. These findings suggest that AI-OsRM can enable accurate identification of individuals with osteoporosis or reduced BMD and may serve as an effective prescreening tool to optimize DXA utilization.

papers.title: Integrating generative artificial intelligence facilitates faculty interaction network and role transition in a biostatistics curriculum
papers.abstract: In a two-year action-research study within an undergraduate biostatistics curriculum for nursing, pharmacy, and medical biotechnology students, we examined how generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) facilitates educators to design, supervise, and evaluate learning. Students used GenAI first as a technical tutor and then as a partner in knowledge co-creation in case-based statistical problem-solving. Teachers’ reflection records and 4697 LINE messages during the study period were analyzed using qualitative coding, GenAI-assisted semantic analysis, and social network analysis. Teachers’ roles shifted from knowledge transmitters to facilitators of critical inquiry and human–GenAI co-learning. Overall, faculty communication was dense, reciprocal, and decentralized, whereas GenAI-related discourse was more selective and centralized. GenAI-related ties were less likely to form but, once formed, strongly reciprocal and locally clustered. GenAI integration can catalyze new forms of faculty leadership through expertise sharing and collaborative problem-solving. Intentional structures for cross-disciplinary exchange and reflective faculty development are needed.

papers.title: Human-validated LLM-assisted assessment of a large-scale online precision medicine course in diabetes
papers.abstract: Precision medicine increasingly relies on multimodal data and artificial intelligence, creating a need for scalable education and assessment. We developed an online diabetes precision medicine course and conducted an observational single-group pre–post evaluation of knowledge, confidence, and rubric-scored open-ended responses among 435 learners who completed the course. Because manual scoring of open-ended responses is time-consuming and subject to variability and human judgment, we developed a human-validated, large language model (LLM)-assisted scoring workflow. Knowledge, confidence, and open-ended response scores increased by 30.0 percentage points, 1.32 points, and 0.39 points, respectively (all p < 0.001). Across 4350 responses evaluated by the LLM-assisted workflow, only 12 (0.3%) required human review. In a stratified 300-response validation sample, the final LLM consensus score achieved 75.3% exact agreement, 99.3% adjacent agreement, and 0.7% major disagreements (LLM unanimity, 74.0%; human unanimity, 65.7%) with the final human score. Course completion was associated with improvements in knowledge, confidence, and open-ended response scores, while the findings also support human-validated LLM-assisted assessment as a scalable approach for evaluating open-ended responses.

papers.title: The complexity paradox of generalist AI agents in medicine: exploring GPT-5 for real-world multimodal medical diagnosis
papers.abstract: The next generation of medical AI systems that integrate language understanding, web data retrieval, and multi-step reasoning are demonstrating increasing promise as potential diagnostic aids in technical evaluations. However, their real world diagnostic performance, explainability, and reliability remain unclear. We conducted a systematic quantitative analysis of ten GPT-5-based configurations on 161 clinician validated real world cases. Each model was assessed for diagnostic accuracy, reasoning quality, retrieval accuracy, evidence integration, and robustness to low-quality inputs. We found important limitations in these AI systems, including image misinterpretation, inconsistent web search that sometimes degraded performance, and limited transparency in agentic workflows. Yet the models also showed strengths, including effective use of patient history, clear stepwise reasoning, plausible differentials, improved specificity with explicit reasoning, and relevant evidence retrieval. To support clinical deployment and future model development, we recommend prioritizing reasoning-optimized AI models, improving information retrieval mechanisms for reflection and error correction, strengthening visual-textual integration, and establishing practical standards for image quality and clarity. Overall, reliable real world multimodal diagnostic performance depends more on transparent reasoning and high-quality inputs than on aggressive retrieval or complex agentic workflows. Persistent gaps in evidence integration and visual reasoning remain major barriers to safe routine clinical use.

papers.title: Expanding the functional scope of AI-driven rehabilitation exergames: multimodal biofeedback and adaptive safety monitoring
papers.abstract: We extend Tannús and colleagues’ AI-driven rehabilitation exergame by proposing a closed-loop adaptive framework integrating real-time heart rate monitoring for cardiovascular safety. A three-phase validation roadmap is outlined. This commentary provides a technically specified pathway to transform passive motor assessment into responsive, safe home rehabilitation for stroke survivors.

papers.title: Implementing and Scaling Artificial Intelligence in Low-Resourced Radiation Oncology: A Systematic Review of Deployments
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has the potential to address workforce shortages and workflow inefficiencies in radiation oncology, particularly in low-resourced settings where limited specialist capacity constrains access to care. This systematic review evaluated AI deployments in radiation oncology in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) and assessed readiness for safe implementation and scale-up. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, six databases were searched from January 2000 through December 2025. Eligible studies were classified using a radiation oncology-specific integration spectrum (Levels 0-4) and evaluated for workflow integration, validation, deployment, and governance characteristics. Eighteen studies met the inclusion criteria. Two studies (11.1%) focused on readiness or governance without clinical AI deployment (Level 0), nine (50.0%) reported task-level applications (Level 1), six (33.3%) demonstrated clinician-supervised workflow integration (Level 2), and one (5.6%) reported cross-stage workflow orchestration (Level 3). No study provided sufficient evidence for classification as Level 4 operation. Validation was predominantly retrospective, and continuous performance monitoring was not reported. AI deployment in LMIC radiation oncology remains concentrated at early stages of integration. This pattern reflects not a lack of innovation, but constraints in validation, workflow maturity, infrastructure, and governance. Safe and scalable deployment will require coordinated advances across these domains.

papers.title: Development and validation of an objective skills scoring system for robotic inguinal hernia repairs
papers.abstract: Competency-based surgical education requires objective, scalable assessment of technical skill, yet existing rating scales are subjective. Objective performance indicators (OPIs) derived from console kinematics, offer a solution; however, they lack a validated scoring framework. We developed and externally validated an OPI-based scoring system from robotic transabdominal preperitoneal inguinal hernia repairs performed by 6 attendings and 41 trainees at an academic center (2023–2026). Nineteen OPIs across four tasks were grouped into eight domains, reduced by principal component analysis, and integrated into task-specific 0–100 composite scores via ridge logistic regression. Among 2588 tasks from 392 cases, cross-validated AUCs for attending-trainee discrimination were 0.62–0.74, and composite scores increased from postgraduate year 2 to attending (Spearman ρ, 0.94–1.00; P ≤ 0.005). In an independent external cohort (84 observations, 21 cases), the overall AUC was 0.84 (95% CI, 0.69–0.93). This framework enables objective technical skills assessment in robotic hernia repair.

papers.title: Magnetic control of an exciton–polariton condensate in a van der Waals magnet
papers.abstract: Magnetically tunable exciton–polariton condensation is demonstrated in CrSBr, a van der Waals magnet, using microwires embedded in an optical cavity under photoexcitation. The observation may enable ultrafast control of condensate emission through coupling to coherent magnons.

papers.title: Gene-driven self-morphing microtubule-based active matter
papers.abstract: Cell-free gene expression is embedded directly within a microtubule network to generate a genetically programmed active material with complementary biochemical and physical controls.

papers.title: Ultrafast anisotropic valleytronics in SnSe
papers.abstract: Polarization-selective excitation in SnSe reveals anisotropic valley dynamics with distinct channels: one channel with near-unity valley polarization and one channel that rapidly depolarizes through electron–phonon-mediated intervalley scattering.

papers.title: Atomic-scale visualization of three-dimensional magnetization vectors with competing spin Hamiltonian interactions
papers.abstract: A beam-shift-based 4D EMCD method is developed that can map 3D spin vectors across individual atomic planes and reveal how competing spin Hamiltonian interactions drive asymmetric spin rotation in canted antiferromagnetic YFeO 3 .

papers.title: Tangermeme: a toolkit for understanding cis- regulatory logic using deep learning models
papers.abstract: The tangermeme software package is a comprehensive, flexible and efficient Swiss Army knife for deep learning-based cis -regulatory pattern identification and analysis.

papers.title: Symmetry-enabled multisite redox utilization in Cu-Ni cyanide coordination polymer for high-rate long-life aqueous proton batteries
papers.abstract: Aqueous proton batteries offer safe, low-cost energy storage, but achieving high-rate performance and long-term stability remains challenging. Here, the authors report CuNi(CN) 3 , a cyanide-bridged bimetallic coordination polymer with high capacity, rate capability, and cycling stability for aqueous proton batteries.

papers.title: Factorized-gating mixture of experts enables cross-regime turbulence modeling
papers.abstract: Predicting turbulent flows is vital for advancing aerospace, energy, and environmental technologies, yet remains critically limited by the accuracy of turbulence models. While machine learning has led to the widespread development of data-driven turbulence models, existing approaches predominantly rely on monolithic dense networks that struggle to generalize across diverse flow regimes. To address this challenge, we introduce the factorized-gating mixture of experts (FG-MoE) framework, where regime-specific experts are trained and blended via spatially varying probabilities. Crucially, the FG-MoE factorizes the conventional monolithic router into a set of lightweight, physics-guided binary attributes, reducing the high-dimensional gating function to a product-form approximation of low-dimensional binary factor probabilities. This factorized design substantially reduces gating complexity, offers physical interpretability of the gating mechanism, and enables plug-and-play scalability to expand the expert library without retraining the entire model. Through extensive numerical experiments, spanning canonical benchmarks to complex real-world engineering applications, FG-MoE delivers consistently high-fidelity predictions across diverse flow regimes. The FG-MoE framework offers an engineering turbulence-modeling pathway by decomposing complex turbulent flows into distinct physical regimes and leveraging a factorized gating strategy to ensure interpretability, efficiency, and scalability.

papers.title: Converting a conventional fluorescence microscope into a high-performance platform for sub-10-nm single-molecule localization microscopy
papers.abstract: Joaquin Garat and colleagues present a cost-effective strategy to transform standard epifluorescence microscopes into focus-stabilized TIRF platforms for 2D and 3D single-molecule localization microscopy. The system delivers sub-10-nm DNA-PAINT and (d)STORM performance on par with state-of-the-art instruments, broadening access to high-quality nanoscale imaging.

papers.title: Strain-engineered piezo-phototronic interface modulation in flexible GaN/monolayer MoS 2 heterostructures
papers.abstract: A flexible, strain-mediated, and photo-responsive device based on a heterostructure comprising a chemical vapor deposition (CVD)-grown MoS2 monolayer and metal-organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD)-grown GaN films is fabricated. By integrating the distinct piezo-phototronic properties of GaN with the excellent carrier transport characteristics of MoS2, the device exhibits a synergistic response to both mechanical strain and optical excitation. Under compressive and tensile strain, piezo-polarization charges generated in the GaN layer effectively modulate interfacial charge transport at the MoS2 monolayer, leading to significantly enhanced sensing performance. The device achieves ultrahigh gauge factors of 2224 and 3349 at a compressive strain of −0.25% under halogen and UV illumination, respectively, corresponding to ~11.1 and ~11.7 times higher sensitivity than standard metallic stain gauges. Furthermore, it demonstrates rapid electro-opto-mechanical responses, detecting halogen and UV irradiation with response and recovery times of 186/84 ms and 83/53 ms, respectively, under −0.25% compressive strain. These results reveal strong coupling between strain-induced polarization and photoexcited carrier dynamics at the nanoscale interface. This work provides new insights into strain-engineered interfacial charge modulation in low-dimensional heterostructures and establishes a promising platform for multifunctional, self-powered, ultra-sensitive and active flexible optoelectronics.

papers.title: A tongue-controlled FES-robotic exoskeleton restores hand function in users with cervical spinal cord injury
papers.abstract: Hand exoskeletons and functional electrical stimulation (FES) have shown promise in restoring hand function after stroke or cervical spinal cord injury. However, major challenges remain in providing reliable user command input in individuals with severe paralysis and in enabling safe and effective control of hand closing and opening. Here, we present a non-invasive tongue-based control strategy for a hybrid soft hand exoskeleton system combining tongue-controlled independent tendon-driven flexion of five fingers with tongue-triggered FES-induced finger extension. This user-intent-driven hybrid approach supports multiple activities of daily living, such as grasping a bottle or toothbrush, and enables hand opening while mitigating muscle fatigue and reducing system complexity. The system was evaluated in five users with cervical spinal cord injury, demonstrating high task success rates in daily living tasks and user preference due to its wearability and ease of use, as well as consistently low reported levels of discomfort, pain, and fatigue. These findings show that the proposed hybrid system can restore activities of daily living in individuals with cervical tetraplegia, including those with long-term injuries.

papers.title: Highly oxidized products from the atmospheric reaction of hydroxyl radicals with toluene
papers.abstract: Simple aromatics, largely toluene (C7H8) and benzene (C6H6), are emitted into Earth´s atmosphere by different sources. Their degradation initiated by the gas-phase reaction with hydroxyl radicals (OH) forms mainly bicyclic peroxy radicals (BCP) besides phenol-type compounds. The formation of highly oxidized products with at least 6 O atoms (HOMs) starting from BCP is currently controversial. Here, the experimental observation of HOMs and other products is reported for near-atmospheric conditions focusing on OH + toluene. Autoxidation processes starting from BCP generate C7H9O7 and C7H9O9 radicals with molar yields of $${0.25}_{\,-0.13}^{\,+0.25}\, \%$$ and $${0.12}_{\,-0.06}^{\,+0.12}\, \%$$ , respectively. Labeling experiments revealed that the ring H atoms are involved in autoxidation. The atmospherically relevant reaction of C7H9O7 and C7H9O9 with NO almost exclusively forms organic nitrates as HOM products, C7H9O6-8NO2, with a total molar yield ≤ 0.1%. Other HOMs, such as C7H8O8 and C7H8O10, represent only small trace products. Results from OH + benzene confirmed the findings from the toluene system pointing to a minor relevance of both aromatics for HOM generation.

papers.title: Social comparison shapes the evolution of cooperation in structured populations
papers.abstract: Human cooperation unfolds in social environments where individuals influence each other through payoff-based learning and social comparison, the tendency to evaluate fitness relative to others. However, it is still unclear how social comparison and population structure jointly shape cooperation. Here, we incorporate social comparison theory into evolutionary dynamics on structured populations, letting fitness depend on individual and neighbour payoffs weighted by a comparison parameter. Under weak selection, we derive conditions favoring cooperation and find that the proposed comparison nonlinearly reshapes the critical benefit-to-cost ratio. Even one individual applying this protocol can affect the population, especially in heterogeneous networks. When comparison tendencies vary, the full distribution, not just the mean, determines evolutionary outcomes. Using a swarm-intelligence-based framework across typical and empirical networks, we identify cooperation-maximizing patterns: optimal states exhibit heterogeneous comparison tendencies, yet collectively align toward assimilative development. These results provide a basis for designing social incentives that harness comparison to promote collective cooperation in human groups.

papers.title: Direct observational constraint on upstream magnetic field amplification reveals the particle acceleration limit in a supernova remnant
papers.abstract: Exploded stars, called supernova remnants, leave behind shock waves that are thought to accelerate cosmic rays, but how energetic those particles can become depends on the magnetic field ahead of the shock. X-ray hotspots found ahead of the shock of the supernova remnant RX J1713.7-3946 place that field at about 10 microgauss, limiting the particles to well below PeV energies.

papers.title: Shifting mosquito vector ecologies pose new risks for new stakeholders
papers.abstract: Mosquito-borne infectious disease is a major cause of mortality and a significant economic burden worldwide. Variable regional and seasonal patterns make proactive intervention challenging. Here we introduce a machine learning approach trained on satellite and mosquito observational data, improving generalizability to sparse observations while retaining similar positive performance characteristics of models used in standard practice. We provide global estimates for Aedes habitability at high spatial resolution in five-year increments from 1970-2024. Mosquito ecologies appear to be shifting in regionally specific ways. Overall, we demonstrate a decrease in risk near the equator and an increase in risk in historically temperate climates including the United States, the European Union, and China. Despite this decrease in risk relative to historical averages, regions near the equator remain among the highest risk worldwide. Together, these results reflect an overall, marked expansion of the regions of the globe that support Aedes mosquitoes, and we observe an ongoing, linear increase in the global population at risk of contracting mosquito-borne disease. Mosquito-borne diseases, for example, malaria, Zika, and Dengue, remain among the most common causes of death worldwide. The most effective way to prevent these diseases from spreading is to prevent infected mosquitoes from biting people. As mosquitoes migrate around the globe over time, it is difficult to know where resources that prevent mosquito bites should be sent. Here we introduce an approach that can be used to predict where mosquitoes are most likely to live. Using this approach, we find that mosquito habitats are expanding both North and South, and, in particular, within the United States, the European Union, and China. These trends contribute to an increasing risk of mosquito-borne disease worldwide.

papers.title: Time-varying risk prediction for oral potentially malignant disorders using deep learning
papers.abstract: Patients with oral potentially malignant disorders require repeated risk assessment after diagnosis because malignant transformation risk varies across lesions and over time. Existing tools rarely provide individualized, interpretable, time-resolved estimates to guide surveillance. A retrospective multicentre study was conducted with clinicopathologically confirmed oral leukoplakia or oral lichenoid conditions. Hong Kong cohorts from 2003 to 2024 were used for model development and internal testing, and independent United Kingdom and mainland China cohorts for external validation. OCRiskNet integrates demographic, exposure, clinical, treatment and histopathological data in a fixed deep survival pipeline combining probabilistic feature enrichment with an intrinsically interpretable free-knot Kolmogorov-Arnold network. Performance was evaluated using concordance index, area under the curve, Brier score, calibration and decision curve analysis. Interpretability was assessed using symbolic function extraction and feature attribution. Here we show that OCRiskNet provides strong internal discrimination for oral leukoplakia and oral lichenoid conditions, with concordance indices of 0.9209 and 0.9207. External validation supported model generalizability across geographically distinct cohorts. Interpretation analyses identified clinically meaningful contributors to risk. OCRiskNet also demonstrated favorable calibration and clinical utility, with clear stratification of risk groups over time. A web-based interface was further implemented to support practical use of individualized risk estimation in longitudinal management. OCRiskNet provided individualized, time-resolved estimates of malignant transformation risk in OPMDs and demonstrated consistent performance across multicentre cohorts. This framework may support more transparent and risk-adapted surveillance planning in heterogeneous clinical settings, with potential public-health value by enabling risk-adapted surveillance of high-risk patients and more efficient allocation of clinical follow-up resources. Oral potentially malignant disorders (OPMDs) represent an important window for oral cancer prevention. These conditions may persist for years, with malignant transformation risk changing across the disease course, making long-term risk-adapted surveillance essential. Specialist oral medicine services remain limited in many regions, and general dental practitioners may face challenges in determining which patients require closer monitoring. We developed OCRiskNet using longitudinal real-world clinical and histopathological data from multicentre cohorts with extended follow-up. The model estimates how an individual patient’s future cancer risk changes over time using information routinely collected during care. This low-burden approach may help resource-limited settings prioritise surveillance for high-risk patients, use specialist services more efficiently, and strengthen oral cancer prevention.

papers.title: Short-range excitonic correlations and enhanced excitonic susceptibility in 1 T -TiSe 2
papers.abstract: In bulk materials, excitonic condensation is hard to separate from charge-density-wave formation. Now short-range excitonic correlations are revealed above the transition temperature in 1T-TiSe 2 via few-femtosecond extreme-ultraviolet spectroscopy.

papers.title: Modular synthesis of 3,3-diaryloxetanes
papers.abstract: Limited modular access to 3,3-diaryloxetanes restricts their broader use as ketone bioisosteres in drug discovery. Now a two-step method for 3,3-diaryloxetane synthesis from 3-oxetanone is reported. (Hetero)aryl lithium addition and alkoxide trapping form stable oxetanyl tetrafluoropyridyl ethers, which can then be cross-coupled with (hetero)aryl boronates using Ni catalysis, affording 3,3-diaryloxetanes.

papers.title: Anticipatory intelligence in clinical microbiology
papers.abstract: Clinical microbiology needs an artificial intelligence system that predicts pathogen evolution and resistance to enable prevention. Laboratories should connect forecasts to confirmatory experiments and defined actions, then test them prospectively across time and populations, as well as govern false alarms, model updates and inequitable performance as carefully as diagnostic errors.

papers.title: Increased potency of human placental mesenchymal stromal cell-derived extracellular vesicles from scaled-up hollow fiber bioreactor production
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs), and more recently MSC-derived extracellular vesicles (MSC-EVs), have demonstrated translational potential, with the first MSC therapy approved by the FDA in 2024 and multiple clinical trials evaluating MSC-EVs. However, clinical translation of MSC-EVs remains limited by batch-to-batch variability in EV properties. To investigate how culture systems affect EV properties and evaluate early gestation placenta-derived MSCs (PMSCs), PMSCs were cultured in tissue culture flasks or a hollow fiber bioreactor and comparatively assessed for cellular and EV composition and potency. Bioreactor-cultured PMSCs exhibited increased neuroprotective and wound-healing potency while maintaining MSC markers, differentiation potential, and a normal karyotype. Proteomic analysis revealed distinct EV profiles between culture conditions, with bioreactor-derived PMSC-EVs enriched in proteins including neuraminidase 1, dynamin-related protein 1, and matrix metalloproteinases involved in tissue remodeling, apoptosis regulation, and immune modulation. Across independent PMSC donor lines, bioreactor culture consistently enhanced functional efficacy. These findings demonstrate that culture conditions substantially influence PMSC and EV properties and highlight the therapeutic potential of PMSC-EVs for translational development.

papers.title: Infant neurodevelopmental impairment detection via large-scale motion screening with generative learning
papers.abstract: Neurodevelopmental impairments like cerebral palsy are prevalent infant developmental problems in clinical infant healthcare. Early detection of these disorders enables timely intervention and better rehabilitation outcomes. Automated, large-scale screening tools remain scarce, and artificial intelligence offers a promising solution by identifying abnormal infant motion patterns. However, developing a data-driven AI system is challenging due to the scarcity of expert-annotated motion records. To address the challenge, this paper proposed a generative pattern learning method, which achieves sensitive detection of abnormal actions through the training paradigm of temporal auto-regression and reconstruction. We trained and validated the AI model DeepAD with more than 1,300 infant motion videos over a period of 5 years (2019-2024) from three children’s hospitals in China, which contain about 50 infants diagnosed with cerebral palsy. Extensive experiments demonstrate the superior performance of DeepAD over baseline methods and equivalent level to clinical experts, indicating its potential for smart screening of neurodevelopmental disorders.

papers.title: Early epilepsy detection from electronic health records with large language models
papers.abstract: Epilepsy and psychogenic non-epileptic seizures often present with similar seizure-like manifestations but require fundamentally different management strategies. Misdiagnosis is common and can lead to prolonged diagnostic delays, unnecessary treatments, and substantial patient morbidity. Although prolonged video-electroencephalography is the diagnostic gold standard, its high cost and limited accessibility hinder timely diagnosis. Here, we developed a low-cost, effective approach, EpiScreen, for early epilepsy detection by utilizing routinely collected clinical notes from electronic health records. Through fine-tuning large language models on labeled notes, EpiScreen achieved an AUC of up to 0.875 on the MIMIC-IV dataset and 0.980 on a private cohort of the University of Minnesota. In a clinician-AI collaboration setting, EpiScreen-assisted neurologists outperformed unaided experts by up to 14.3%. Overall, this study demonstrates that EpiScreen supports early epilepsy detection, facilitating timely and cost-effective screening that may reduce diagnostic delays and avoid unnecessary interventions, particularly in resource-limited regions.

papers.title: Payment models in pediatric digital health and their implications for innovation, policy, and access
papers.abstract: Investment in pediatric digital health lags behind that in adult care, partly due to the different financial incentives involved. Analyzing 73 PitchBook-identified pediatric digital health companies’ publicly available documentation, we found they often rely on non-insurance revenue, with fewer payment models incorporating publicly insured patients. Financial and regulatory incentives that facilitate capitated revenue streams incorporating public payers and school systems may further enhance access to digitally connected care for children.

papers.title: An audit-ready EHR foundation model for order-time medication-safety auditing across health systems
papers.abstract: Real-time medication-safety auditing requires current laboratory and medication histories, yet electronic health records (EHRs) may contain stale or missing decisive evidence. We present ClinicalGPT, an audit-ready foundation model using Clinical Trajectory Language to encode time, units, provenance, and observability, and workflow-aligned objectives to handle structured missingness. Across seven health systems, we retrospectively evaluated 847,000 eligible high-risk medication orders against a reference vector frozen before final scoring. The primary endpoint was the reference-standard-defined order-time failure-to-alert rate: eligible tier-i/ii reference-positive orders receiving no actionable alert at a system’s frozen operating point, per 1000 eligible orders. This offline process metric did not measure subsequent clinical actions, adverse drug events, or patient harm. ClinicalGPT with hard constraints achieved 3.2 misses per 1000 orders, versus 9.4 for rules only, 6.1 for the original generic LLM comparator, and 4.8 for the strongest observed LLM comparator (RAG + LLM + rules). Its false-alert rate was 33.9 (95% CI, 31.6–36.3), versus 38.7 for rules only. A separate single-site silent prospective assessment evaluated workflow measures without altering care. Matched ablations supported explicit observability modeling; independent de novo labeling of an enriched knowledge-base–independent subset preserved sensitivity ordering but narrowed the ClinicalGPT–RAG gap. These findings support comparative order-time auditing performance but do not establish clinical effectiveness or reduced patient harm.

papers.title: Adaptive heterogeneous graph neural networks for differentiating pulmonary arterial hypertension from left heart disease
papers.abstract: Differentiating pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) from pulmonary hypertension associated with left heart disease (PH-LHD) is clinically important because management differs substantially, but definitive classification requires invasive haemodynamic assessment together with clinical evaluation. We retrospectively studied 905 patients with PAH or PH-LHD treated at Shanghai Pulmonary Hospital and developed an adaptive heterogeneous graph neural network (AHGNN) that integrates contrast-enhanced thoracic CT images with noninvasive clinical variables. The model combines differentiable graph construction using Gumbel-Softmax reparameterization, hierarchical cross-modal attention, and dual-level self-supervised contrastive learning. Across 100 outer test folds from repeated patient-level five-fold cross-validation, AHGNN achieved a mean area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.946 ± 0.023 and a precision–recall AUC of 0.952 ± 0.009. At a fixed probability threshold of 0.50, sensitivity was 0.867 ± 0.070 and specificity was 0.867 ± 0.072. The Brier score was 0.139, although a calibration slope of 3.547 indicated that recalibration may be required. These findings support the potential of multimodal noninvasive data to assist referral and diagnostic triage. Prospective external validation, recalibration, and clinical safety evaluation are required before clinical use or any change to the role of right heart catheterization.

papers.title: Digital Transitional Care Management and Lower Hospital Readmissions in Patients with Cancer: An Allocation Study
papers.abstract: Hospital readmissions are common among patients with cancer, yet scalable transitional care strategies remain limited. We conducted a health system-embedded allocation study evaluating whether a digital transitional care management (DTCM) intervention could reduce readmissions among adults discharged from medical oncology services. Between April and September 2024, 1,713 patients were allocated by medical record number parity to DTCM or usual care. The intervention delivered daily electronic symptom assessments and tailored self-management education for 10 days, with moderate or severe symptoms routed to clinical teams. Usual care involved symptom monitoring at the discretion of the treating oncology team. The primary outcome was 30-day readmission, analyzed using cumulative incidence functions with death as a competing event. Thirty-day readmission was lower with DTCM than usual care (30% versus 37%; P = 0.001), as were 90-day readmission (48% versus 54%; P = 0.004) and 30-day emergency department visits without admission (12% versus 17%; P = 0.007). Among intervention participants, 56.6% completed at least one assessment; among those participants, 46.6% reported at least one severe symptom. These findings suggest that a multifaceted DTCM program may reduce post-discharge acute care utilization in patients with cancer.

papers.title: Critical gaps in health technology assessment guidance for generative AI across six health systems
papers.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in healthcare poses significant challenges for evaluation due to algorithmic complexity and evolving performance. Existing evidence generation guidelines, primarily designed for static medical technologies, may inadequately address the unique characteristics of generative AI. Here, we conducted a comparative analysis of evidence generation guidelines from six countries, examining recommendations for efficacy and effectiveness evaluations, health economic evaluations, social and equity evaluations, and uncertainty management for AI technologies. Across 56 documents, we found a consistent preference for randomised controlled trials and cost-effectiveness analyses, alongside emerging acceptance of alternative study designs and real-world evidence to accommodate the evolving nature of AI technologies. However, current frameworks lack specific guidance for the stochastic, non-deterministic, and adaptive learning properties of generative AI technologies. Moving forward, evidence generation guidelines require methodological and conceptual adaptations in order to improve the value assessment for generative AI technologies.

papers.title: A soft bioelectronic system with a responsive hydrogel neural interface for direct force quantification and real-time intraoperative craniocerebral injury monitoring
papers.abstract: A thermoresponsive hydrogel-based neural interface enables real-time force quantification during surgery, with simultaneous somatosensory evoked potential and electrocorticography recording, and is validated in rabbit brain tumour excision models.

papers.title: Horizontal-up microfluidics for embedded chip cooling with a dielectric fluid
papers.abstract: An embedded two-phase cooling architecture, which features horizontal inlets for liquid supplement and vertical outlets for vapour evacuation, can use a dielectric fluid to achieve a critical heat flux of 1,570 W cm −2 .

papers.title: Genetic encoding and mutagenesis of RNA droplet phenotypes
papers.abstract: This study shows that genetic mutations can generate cellular-like traits in RNA droplets. By encapsulating their DNA templates, the droplets establish a genotype–phenotype link, and low levels of mutagenesis give rise to stable vacuoles that enable cargo storage and micrometer-scale motion.

papers.title: Rare-earth-free regenerator materials for enhanced 4-K cryocooler performance
papers.abstract: Cryogenic cooling technologies, crucial for MRI and quantum computing, face challenges due to reliance on scarce helium and rare-earth elements. Here, the authors design a non-rare-earth regenerator material, MnNb 2-x Ta x O 6 combined with CuFe 1-x AL x O 2 with enhanced cooling capacity at 4.2 K, offering a sustainable alternative to standard cryogenic cooling platforms.

papers.title: Ultrafast X-ray sonography reveals the spatial heterogeneity of the laser-induced magneto-structural phase transition in FeRh
papers.abstract: Phase transitions on the nanoscale are influenced by complex heterogeneities, yet their spatio-temporal dynamics are difficult to capture. Here, the authors combine ultrafast hard-X-ray diffraction with a propagating strain pulse as a universal and non invasive marker to reveal transient spatial phase heterogeneity via phase-specific strain responses, offering insights into the magneto-structural phase transition in FeRh.

papers.title: Boosting structural stability of lead-free Tin-based layered double perovskite nanocrystals with enhanced photoelectrochemical activity
papers.abstract: Quasi-2D lead-free layered double perovskites (Cs₄M(II)M(III)₂Cl₁₂) have gained growing attention. Here, the authors develop Sn(II)-based quasi-2D layered double perovskite nanocrystals, achieving high photoelectrochemical activity and sustained air stability.

papers.title: Operationalizing resilience for sustainable infrastructure governance across the life cycle
papers.abstract: Marco Domaneschi and colleagues develop a decision-oriented framework that integrates recovery-based resilience with life-cycle environmental and economic assessment to evaluate infrastructure adaptation strategies. The framework identifies retrofit options that balance resilience, cost, carbon emissions and service life for ageing infrastructure.

papers.title: Bio-inspired exploration of butterfly wing morphology guides deep reinforcement learning optimization of robotic flight
papers.abstract: How wing morphology shapes flight performance is a central question in functional biology and bio-inspired robotics, yet these relationships are difficult to isolate in living organisms. Here, we use a robotic butterfly with tunable wing geometry to systematically characterize morphology–performance relationships by combining motion capture with morphometric analysis. We then use deep reinforcement learning to search the morphological design space and identify wing designs optimized for aerodynamic performance. The resulting designs increase lift and thrust performance by 339% and 46%, respectively. Physical flight tests validate the learning-derived morphology, with prediction errors remaining below 7%. By integrating controlled robotic experiments with machine learning, this framework provides a means to generate testable hypotheses in functional morphology while guiding the engineering design of bio-inspired robots.

papers.title: BaTiO 3 /ZnO nanocomposite photocatalysts for enhanced degradation of mixed antibiotics and dyes
papers.abstract: Antibiotics and synthetic dyes, which are considered persistent pollutants in wastewater, cannot be removed effectively by conventional wastewater treatments based on mechanical-biological processes. Here, the authors develop composite photocatalysts combining barium titanate and zinc oxide via a simple hydrothermal method, demonstrating their application to the degradation of a mixture of multiple pollutants (ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, methylene blue and methyl orange) in a heterogeneous photocatalytic process, in which photogenerated holes act as the dominant reactive species.

papers.title: Towards parahydrogen-induced polarization of acetoacetate
papers.abstract: Hyperpolarized acetoacetate is a promising probe for detection of redox status inside mitochondria using 13 C MRI. In this pilot study, the authors use parahydrogen-induced polarization by means of a side-arm hydrogenation (PHIP-SAH) approach for the hyperpolarization of [1,3- 13 C 2 ]acetoacetate, expanding PHIP-SAH studies beyond pyruvate to the metabolically relevant acetoacetate probe and identifying the key chemical factors that currently limit direct probe production.

papers.title: The energetics of high temperature oxidation and formation mechanisms in binary lanthanide nitrides ( Ln N)
papers.abstract: Nitride-based compounds present exceptional thermal properties for advanced material applications, but an accurate determination of their thermodynamic properties is critical for their application. Here, the authors use high-temperature oxide melt calorimetry to determine the standard enthalpies of formation (ΔHf°) for all LnN compounds (Ln = La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Lu; excluding Pm), showing that ΔHf° values correlate with the ionic radius of Ln +3 cations, with smaller Ln-bearing nitrides exhibiting more negative values.

papers.title: Active fluctuations drive inertia-free absolute negative mobility in soft and living matter
papers.abstract: Absolute negative mobility (ANM) is one of the most paradoxical transport phenomena in which a setup moves on average in a direction opposite to the applied force. The simplest system exhibiting this effect in minimal one-dimensional dynamics involves an inertial particle subjected to a constant bias while dwelling in a nonlinear, symmetric periodic potential in a nonequilibrium, nonstationary state generated by external driving. The necessity of inertia poses a significant conceptual barrier in predicting the ANM in a microscopic world of soft and living matter such as biological cells. In this work, we solve a two-decade old puzzle and demonstrate that none of the previously thought factors required for this effect are decisive. We show that the ANM may occur in a system composed of an overdamped particle in a piecewise linear symmetric periodic potential in an equilibrium state, provided that it is additionally driven by active fluctuations in the form of white Poisson shot noise. Our result may help to explain exotic transport behavior emerging in biological cells where dynamics is typically overdamped and assisted by active fluctuations derived from various metabolic activities. It can also be exploited for effective separation strategies in a microscopic world, thus transforming fluctuations from a nuisance into a functional resource.

papers.title: 3D articular knee shape drives increased anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) loading in young, active individuals with ACL injury and females
papers.abstract: Pechstein et al. made computer knee models for 168 young, active people, half with torn anterior cruciate ligaments (ACL), to test if 3D knee shape affects ACL loading during a stressful maneuver. They show that 3D knee shape drives greater ACL loading in injured people and in females and provide a mechanical basis for more personalized treatment.

papers.title: Multi-agent AI for liver disease guideline development and maintenance: a proof-of-concept study
papers.abstract: Here the authors develop multi-agent AI that acts like a digital committee to review evidence and flag potential guideline updates. In liver disease benchmarks, it replicated expert consensus and cut early-career clinicians’ guideline errors by half.

papers.title: Paradoxical relationships of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha with methamphetamine use and body mass index
papers.abstract: Blair et al., assess longitudinal associations between methamphetamine (MA) use, body mass index (BMI), and systemic inflammation in 140 men using mixed-effects models across 560 samples. Frequent MA use and higher BMI are each associated with higher IL-6, whereas their combination is associated with lower IL-6 and TNF-α, suggesting a joint influence on inflammatory responses.

papers.title: Comparative evaluation of HIV testing interventions for men who have sex with men in the Netherlands
papers.abstract: New HIV diagnoses among men who have sex with men (MSM) in the Netherlands have declined considerably, but the recent plateau suggests ongoing transmission. In 2024, 29% of new diagnoses among MSM were late stage, showing that the time between infection and diagnosis can still be reduced. In low-incidence settings, infections introduced through immigration are increasingly important in sustaining transmission. We used an agent-based model of HIV transmission among MSM in the Netherlands, incorporating infections acquired domestically and abroad. For 2026 – 2040, we simulated testing interventions focused on immigrants at entry, resident MSM subgroups, and combinations of these. Entry testing of immigrating MSM averts up to 94 (95-th % quantile interval, 95% QI -128 – 328) infections over 15 years if at least 50% take the test. Testing every 7 months in the general MSM population achieves the largest reduction, up to 508 (95% QI 292 – 900) infections averted. The same rate in MSM with more than 5 recent partners results in 340 (95% QI 132–592) infections averted. Combining entry testing with 7-monthly testing in the general resident MSM population results in 534 infections averted (95% QI 308–884). Considering both impact and additional tests per infection averted, combination strategies generally offer the most favourable trade-offs. Increased testing in resident MSM, particularly when combined with entry testing of immigrating MSM, can substantially reduce HIV infections while offering an attractive testing effort. The higher impact of targeting the general MSM population compared with targeting those with high recent partner numbers suggests that the criteria used to identify individuals with undiagnosed HIV need to expand. HIV transmission among men who have sex with men (MSM) in the Netherlands is ongoing. In 2024, 29% of new HIV diagnoses among MSM were late-stage, highlighting the need for earlier diagnosis. We evaluated testing strategies for immigrating and resident MSM. Offering HIV testing to immigrating MSM at entry can avert many infections, but increasing testing rates among resident MSM can avert substantially more. Combining both approaches provided the best balance between impact and testing effort. Our simulations show that some MSM living with undiagnosed HIV do not meet traditional criteria used to identify individuals with undiagnosed HIV. Improved strategies can help reach these individuals earlier, benefiting public and personal health.
